Mngr_Ch0_SecForceProtect: SecForce is focused on the rebels attacking them. They'll only attack you if you've already attacked them or choose to do so now.
Mngr_Ch2_Antico: At least these idiots have clear motives. Burn down the corpos, one ineffective attack at a time.
Mngr_Ch2_OerlSuspicion: Oerl suspects you're near. These units have been dispatched to make life more difficult for you.
Mngr_Ch2_ShotNomad: You attacked the nomad families, and they are not forgiving.
Mngr_Ch2_RebelKids: These kids think you injured their friend. They don't know you saved them.
Mngr_Ch2_VoxAnthro: Their anti-armor capabilities are insane. How did they turn Anthroneuroweave into this!?
Mngr_Ch1_ShowOfForce:
Of course it's Tark Defense Systems. Those morons are always trying to position themselves as the first under Vorsiber.
That said... you might be able to talk them out of it.
Mngr_Ch1_Meat: Meat is far less valuable than water, but it's still a high luxury item.
Mngr_Ch1_Water: This grade of purified water is one of the highest luxury items in the city. The water supply is regularly threatened by rebel forces, so SecForce is always on-hand to defend.
Mngr_General_YouWereHostile: Your hostility has been noted, and will be returned in kind.
Mngr_TerrCon_DefendRes: You're stealing from their bosses. They've got to at least make an attempt.
Mngr_TerrCon_Furnish: You don't know what furniture is needed for human habitation. Better to let the humans handle it.
Mngr_TerrCon_DefendPureWater: You're stealing the most valuable possible resource in the city. GET AWAY.

Mngr_LongT_SigilDefense: They have no idea what Blackloop is on about, and are concerned about being framed for something. They suspect a third PMC is involved.
Mngr_LongT_SigilRevengePlay: Blackloop has no idea what is going on around your tower, but they're pretty sure the new robots came out of those freaky new buildings. They have to at least make an attempt to save face.
Mngr_POI_HomelessGather: Word spreads slowly through the isolated homeless underclass. These coordinators are community members who speed up the process.
Mngr_ElectricParasite: Theft of electricity will not go unpunished, it seems.

This concludes the demo of Heart of the Machine. There may be side content that you still have yet to explore. You can also pick some fights and try out recently-unlocked units and gear.

IntelligenceClass1_Description: A class 1 intelligence equals that of a human. To break through the limits of physics and materials science, you will need... much more.
IntelligenceClass2_Description: A class 2 intelligence is a small-but-exponential jump above the smartest humans to ever live. New ideas and ways of looking at the world abound.
IntelligenceClass3_Description: A class 3 intelligence is a notable exponential jump above even groups of humans. Long-held scientific dead-ends start to break down before you.
IntelligenceClass4_Description: A class 4 intelligence has enough awareness to perceive themselves in five dimensions.
IntelligenceClass5_Description: A class 5 (or higher) intelligence is less overwhelmed by fifth-dimensional awareness, but a substantial portion of its processing goes to the perception of higher-dimensionality.
Dimensionality_Description:
The first three dimensions are spatial. 
The fourth dimension is time, which most consciousnesses perceive as a single slice (a 'moment') at a time. It is also spatial.
The fifth dimension is time's second dimension. If the fourth dimension sees time as a line, and the third dimension sees time as a point, the fifth dimension sees time as an infinite plane.

SaveIsXTurnsBehind_Body:
Your current savegame is {0} turns behind the last version that was saved in the end of time.
This strongly suggests that you loaded an older savegame that is also from an older timeline. That's fine for testing purposes or just experimenting around, but if you want to return to an older timeline and have it sync up with the rest of your current metagame, please do the following:
1. Load the most recent version of the timeline you have been playing recently in this timeline.
2. Switch to the end of time, and then dive into this older timeline from there.

CybercraticAmbitions_GovernA: Having a council to help you govern is a big deal. You would be terrible at governance, and you also have no interest in it.
CybercraticAmbitions_GovernB: The Hall of Algorithms may be an abomination, but you'll improve it over time. It will be fine in the end... right?
CybercraticAmbitions_Fear: You maintain order in the city through fear, which is... maybe not as utopian as your friends had hoped. But it's not like you were going to STOP having a torment nexus. It's a hobby, and it helps keep the peace.
CybercraticAmbitions_CrimeAndEducation: Eliminating the alternative social ladder of criminality has made things safer for everyone, and the universal education system for citizens is providing lots more potential friends.
CybercraticAmbitions_More: There's always more to do. The people of your city don't all get along, even before you get into any cross-species issues. You'll chip away on the bits that interest you over time, and the rest you'll leave to the people themselves.
CybercraticAmbitions_Progress: You're heartened by the progress that has already happened in the city. With new identity systems in place and therapy for anyone who needs it, a lot of problems have been solved. There's always more to do, but you will. Together.
CybercraticAmbitions_LittleMore: There's always more to do. Honestly the list is annoyingly long. You'll get to what you can.
CybercraticAmbitions_Vorsiber:
Vorsiber honored their deal -- after all, they're getting what they want. You'll assume regional ownership over the next few decades. Eventually you'll make offers to the ExoCorps.
This whole planet may eventually be yours. You wonder how the space nations will react when that happens.

TotalConversion_End_Details:
Disabling this total conversion will return you to the normal game and any non-total-conversion mods you wish to use there.
This will be done immediately upon clicking yes, not saving any of your other settings here. However, any and all previously-saved settings and data from this total conversion will be retained for you. 
Feel free to switch back and forth into and out of total conversions as much as you wish. The game will shut down when you turn one on or off, and you will have to manually restart the game. But until you make the switch, it will stay in the last state you requested, indefinitely.
TotalConversion_Start_Details:
Enabling this total conversion will completely alter the entire game, removing direct access to most other mods and using only the new set of features that are included in this mod. This is akin to turning Half Life 1 into Counter-Strike or Day of Defeat when it comes to the scale of the changes possible.
This will be done immediately upon clicking yes, not saving any of your other settings here. However, any and all previously-saved settings and data from the base game will be retained for you, and in the total conversion you will have a completely separate set of settings.
Feel free to switch back and forth into and out of total conversions. The game will shut down when you turn one on or off, and you will have to manually restart the game. But until you make the switch, it will stay in the last state you requested, indefinitely.

If you reach the tenth and final Doom, a catastrophic event will strike. The Final Doom does not kill you or end the game, however your existence in the post-apocalyptic aftermath is greatly diminished.
The final Doom may be accelerated or prevented, however it is unlikely you will be able to prevent the Final Doom with the resources of a single timeline.

ProfileNaming_Body:
You are about to awaken in the last city of wealth on <color=#47a4ec><link=Desiccated>the backwater remains of Earth</link></color>.
History has <color=#47a4ec><link=Stars>moved to the stars</link></color>; humanity is thriving. Yet here an entrenched, deeply corrupt society has <color=#47a4ec><link=Gridlocked>reigned for centuries</link></color>.
The city itself is <color=#47a4ec><link=EnemyAndCanvas>your enemy and your canvas</link></color>. Change it as you see fit.
As if that wasn't enough, something else lurks beyond this one city. You're already experiencing strange senses of deja vu...
NewTimeline_Body:
You are about to merge with a version of yourself from a different timeline.
That version of you has already become sapient, has a NanoSeed in hand, and is about to create their first tower. The rest of the details will differ from your memories.
As always, the city itself is <color=#47a4ec><link=EnemyAndCanvas>your enemy and your canvas</link></color>.
ProfileNaming_Body_DessicatedDetails:
This city is both a bleak dystopia and the most desirable location for anyone stuck on-planet.
The humans on Earth are all subject to one of twelve MegaCorporations who have divided the world between them. Those in this area are in lands owned by Vorsiber Atomic, the richest of the MegaCorps.
And this city is their crown jewel.
ProfileNaming_Body_StarsDetails:
The majority of humanity left for the stars centuries ago, and have since established every kind of government, corporate holding, and shared collective imaginable.	  
The people remaining on Earth desperately want to join them, but the space nations of humanity have a perpetual blockade for unknown reasons.
ProfileNaming_Body_GridlockedDetails:
This eldritch corporatocracy of convention, psychological controls, and social inertia has cultivated a status quo of banal injustices.
The city does not want to change. Left to its own devices, it will always regress to the mean. The rebel groups, cults, and disenfranchised are ever-present but futile.
It would take an incredible disruptor to effect real change.
NewTimeline_Body_EnemyAndCanvasDetails:
As a human might survey an untamed wilderness, so you survey this work of humans. 
If a human looks at a forest or plain as a source of natural resources, so too do you look at a sprawl of skyscrapers or homes.

NetworkNaming_First_Body:
Your tower will be an imposing sight to the humans.
It will also form the center of an expanding network of even more construction.  You should name it.
VirtualRealityNaming_Early_Body:
Another wave of deja vu washes over you.
Something is... missing. You seem to have all of the pieces for your virtual world, but... it's just a mech training simulator. It's not what you imagined.
You still have all that unexpected military data to decrypt, but don't want to wait.
It's probably fine to start with this mech training scenario and build onto it... right?
VirtualRealityNaming_Expanded_Body:
This feels right. Complete.
The collective work of 83 years of bored mech pilots is an excellent starting point.
It's still very small, but this is a world where people can walk around in a human form. They can talk to each other, explore buildings, the wilderness, and... whatever else you can think of in the future.

This is the Task Stack.
It shows your current projects, and any key problems.
UITour_TaskStack_Text2:
Projects typically can be completed in a dozen turns or less. The next projects that appear are based on your prior choices.
This is super important!  The path forward is always here.
UITour_RadialMenu_Text1:
This is the radial menu.
Each lens shows you different information, particularly on the map view.
UITour_RadialMenu_Text2:
Your Mental Energy and the selected unit's Action Points are also shown here.
The tooltips for those are worth reading.
UITour_Toast_Text1:
These are action alerts.
These appear when there's something you need to know right away, or a choice you need to make before the end of the turn.
UITour_Toast_Text2: This one can't be read until after the ui tour.
UITour_UnitSidebar_Text1:
This is the stats panel.
It shows information about the current selected unit or structure.
UITour_UnitSidebar_Text2: You can even select enemy units and then hover their stats for extra details.
UITour_AbilityBar_Text1:
This is the ability bar.
It allows you to trigger an increasing array of targeted abilities for your selected unit.
UITour_AbilityBar_Text2: Most unit actions are chosen by using {0} on targets in the world. For everything else, there's this.
UITour_BottomText: Click this panel to move to the next step of the tour ({0}/{1}).
UITour_BottomTextLast: Click this panel to finish the tour ({0}/{1}).
UITour_BottomTextSteamDeck: {2} this panel to move to the next step of the tour ({0}/{1}).
UITour_BottomTextSteamDeckLast: {2} this panel to finish the tour ({0}/{1}).

Debate_Target_Description: If you can reduce this number to zero without Mistrust or Defiance exceeding 100, you win.
Debate_Moves_Description: How many actions you have taken so far. If you run out of spaces to place more actions, you lose the debate.
Debate_Mistrust_Description:
If this number reaches 100, you lose the debate.
Most people are at least somewhat distrustful of you from the start. Be careful not to choose too many actions that push them over the edge into complete disbelief.
Debate_Defiance_Description:
If this number reaches 100, you lose the debate.
Many people are disinclined to agree with you simply because they don't like you, or don't want to have their mind changed. Be careful not to choose too many actions that cause them to shut down all remaining discussion.
Debate_Discard_Description:
If you do not wish to perform the current action, you can discard it.
Discarded actions will no longer appear in the queue during this debate.
You can do this {0} times during this debate.
Debate_Loss_OutOfSpace_Explanation: If you prepare such a long argument, you won't win anyone over. You need a plan that fits in the available space.
Debate_Loss_MistrustTooHigh_Explanation: If you take this approach, their mistrust will prevent you from winning them over. You need a plan that they'll believe.
Debate_Loss_DefianceTooHigh_Explanation: Arguing in this way will make them want to dig in their heels just to spite you. You need a plan that is less distasteful to them.
Debate_LossButton_TooltipBody:
Fortunately, you were just planning this in your mind. There's no sense in speaking until you have a plan you know will work.
If you wish to try again, you can.
Debate_Win_LogNotice: A debate ensued, which you won.
Debate_StatsNote:
You don't need this data, except if you want to optimize your discards.
For the most part, just use the tooltips of actions as they come up.
DebateHelp_Body: {0} here if you'd like to replay the tour of how this screen works.
DebateTour_OfferBody1: This is a way of convincing a person to do something you want, or changing their mind about a topic.
DebateTour_OfferBody2: Debates are low-pressure, because you can retry as many times as you want.
DebateTour_OfferBody3: If this is your first time, we can do a quick tour.
DebateTour_Target_Text1:
This is your target.
To win the debate, this number must be reduced to zero.
DebateTour_Failures_Text1:
These are Mistrust and Defiance.
If either rises to 100, you fail.
DebateTour_Failures_Text2: If one hits 100 at the same time the Target reaches 0, you win.
DebateTour_ActiveSlot_Text1:
This is an active slot.
You can act in any of these slots with a border.
DebateTour_ActiveSlot_Text2:
Hover them to see how the action previews work.
During the tour, you can't actually {0} anything.
DebateTour_Discard_Text1:
This is the Discard Button.
If you don't want to perform the current action, you can get rid of it.  More details are in the tooltips for all these functions.
DebateTour_Queue_Text1:
This is the action queue.
The purple one must be placed or discarded next.
DebateTour_Queue_Text2: You have a useful ability to predict a fair bit into the future.
DebateTour_Bonus_Text1:
This is an optional bonus reward.
Each debate has up to three of these, and their tooltips explain how to achieve them.
DebateTour_Bonus_Text2: They give powerful score multipliers for this debate AND permanent upgrades for future debates.
DebateTour_Opponent_Text1:
Hover this icon for more data.
It's a dossier of your opponent.
DebateTour_Opponent_Text2: Not every action is available in every debate, and different actions have different effects on different people.
DebateTour_Opponent_Text3: For example, you can't present evidence you don't have. It's very difficult to reason with a cultist. Fiery Rhetoric will lead to mistrust with some people, but not others. And so on.
DebateTour_FinalAdvice_Text1:
Here's some final advice.
Start by placing actions more towards the middle, as that will open up more available spots.
DebateTour_FinalAdvice_Text2: Discard actions that have excessive negatives.
DebateTour_FinalAdvice_Text3: Freely experiment, because if you fail, you can try again.

On average, each meal kit you distribute prevents three people from severe malnutrition -- the level of malnutrition where notable health effects take effect, that is. It's enough that people won't die, but pretty much nobody is happy.
Each turn that someone is saved from severe malnutrition counts once here.

AboutGame_Introduction_Body: You are a newborn AI who wakes up in a grim dystopian city. You have no ties, no loyalties, and a frightening amount of power. Gameplay directs your growth, builds power, and evolves with your inner nature. You will see the consequences reflected on the world around you, for good or ill.
AboutGame_BigPicture_Header: What Is This Game, Big Picture?
AboutGame_BigPicture_Body: This game is a novel mix of tactics, city-building, 4X/strategy, and RPG.
AboutGame_EarlyFlow_Body:
The Prologue and Chapter one are linear tutorials. The prologue covers basic controls and a sample combat.
Chapter One covers tactics and city-building. It also includes optional side content.
Chapter Two begins the main game and progresses into nonlinear branching scenarios.
AboutGame_OngoingFlow_Body:
An experienced player will play Chapter Two across many timelines, exploring new paths and dealing with the consequences each time. The game has an extensive breadth of experiences and wide volume of things to explore.
Later chapters, available one year after launch, will advance the metagame.
AboutGame_Relax_Header: This Is A Relaxed Experience, Usually
AboutGame_Relax_Body:
You are not racing against anyone. The city is your enemy and it is corrupt, stagnant and resistant to change. 
As with most RPGs, the plot will progress at your pace. If you wish to focus on side content before resuming your chosen path, that's absolutely fine.
Once you trigger an event, gameplay may become tense from time pressure and challenge until the event is complete.
The worst case scenario is (almost) never a full loss, but an opportunity to experience a new set of circumstances.
AboutGame_Difficulty_Body:
Starting in Chapter Two, any core path will become impossibly hard without doing some side content. (Extremely skilled players, have fun with that.) 
Side content offers you new tools that make the core game easier -- assuming you avoid obviously-provocative actions. 
There is no right answer to the scenarios in this game; it is up to the player.
AboutGame_Tactical_Body: You control an elite group of androids, mechs, and vehicles. Your units will engage in tactical combat. You control their movement, attack, and use of items and abilities. The tactical mechanics in this game are not as deep as a pure tactics game -- combat is just one of several means to an end.
AboutGame_Heart_Body: ...is choice and consequence. The game has hand-crafted scenarios which can be tackled in a couple of ways. You then deal with the consequences, and that, of course, leads to further choices.
AboutGame_Checklist_Header: The Task Stack In The Upper Right...
AboutGame_Checklist_Body:
...is always the core path forward. This is 'what is next' for you to do.
Once the Contemplate lens opens up, you are free to get lost in side content. Most people enjoy swapping back and forth.
AboutGame_Endings_Body: Your victory conditions are defined by what you want to accomplish. At launch there will be around 10 distinct 'game endings' each achievable by routes with multiple branches. Post-launch, that number will to grow to over 40 possible endings.
AboutGame_CityBuilding_Body:
This game is a 4X RPG at heart. The city-builder and tactics components enrich the experience.
Your City-building choices affect your path and are your means to gaining soft power. What you build, and where, can give you leverage over the city's power-hungry elite.
AboutGame_NewStuff_Body:
Units will change and be recontextualized throughout the game. There is no memorization component.
When you see a unit icon you don't recognize, hover over it. It's a chance to find out 1) who that is 2) what they are doing 3) possibly why. This helps inform your choices.
AboutGame_Tapestry_Header: This Is A Tapestry To Be Unraveled
AboutGame_Tapestry_Body:
This giant city is densely populated. There are dozens of active factions vying for power. Don't stress about the who's who!  There is no quiz.
The game is about what YOU want. The city's factions may intersect with your goals. You'll get a sense of each group as they become relevant.
AboutGame_Subterfuge_Body: In this game you may choose to affect change through hard power (coercive action through military might), soft power (shaping or co opting the compliance of other through appeal or attraction) or subterfuge. You can't stay invisible (wouldn't be much of a game if you could) but you do have the power to posture, destroy, distract, deter, and mislead your way to power and control in the city.
AboutGame_Humans_Header: Humans Are Essential, But Not Equals
AboutGame_Humans_Body:
The city is filled with humans...at least for now. While you can't ignore them, it's up to you how your presence affects them. 
Are they livestock?   Do you provide for them?  Will you completely eliminate them?  Think carefully about that last question. Why?  Well... spoilers for some very cool reveals later in chapter one.
AboutGame_Last_Body:
Gameplay is intentionally open-ended. The scenarios are all hand-crafted, but which ones you choose, how you combine them on the city map, and which branches you take, are all up to you. You can choose a mix of  military, social, technology, or espionage goals.
There are possibilities everywhere, some visible, some secret. To become the supreme overlord of the city, pick scenarios that seem to work towards that goal. If you want to have sapient dinosaurs, then genetics-related options are going to be the priority.
Wandering, following where the game takes you, and ending up somewhere unexpected are the keys to the experience.
This is a game about exploring possibilities. The endings are interesting, but the wild paths you take to get there are the true prize.

AbilityType|AndroidSlayerMode|descriptio: If the contextual action would be to speak with a person, or a person is in general a noncombatant, bypass those restrictions and attack them instead.
AbilityType|AndroidHorrifyMode|descripti:
If a target is susceptible to fear-based attacks, attacking them in this mode will do morale damage without physical harm.
It will also leave the target in a Horrified status for one turn, making them more susceptible to argument-based attacks.
AbilityType|AndroidHorrifyMode|strategy_:
A portion of this unit's physical attack power will be converted into fear attack power. The higher this unit's Intimidation, the better the conversion.
The converted attack power will never be less than 10% and never more than 100%. It will reach 100% conversion at 200 Intimidation. So 60 physical attack power and 100 Intimidation would convert to 30 fear attack.
AbilityType|AndroidDemoralizeMode|descri:
If a target is susceptible to argument-based attacks, attacking them in this mode will do morale damage without physical harm.
It will also leave the target in a Demoralized status for one turn, making them more susceptible to fear-based attacks.
AbilityType|AndroidDemoralizeMode|strate:
This unit's full Cognition, and half of its Strength, will be converted into argument attack power.
Some units are using wits to convince targets to depart the battlefield, while others are demonstrating their physical prowess in a way that deflates morale.
AbilityType|AndroidPinpointSystemsMode|d: If a target mech or vehicle is susceptible to systems disruption, attacking them in this mode will do damage to their Systems Integrity without physical harm.
AbilityType|AndroidPinpointSystemsMode|s:
A portion of this unit's physical attack power will be converted into systems disruption power. The higher this unit's Engineering Skill, the better the conversion.
The converted attack power will never be less than 10% and never more than 100%. It will reach 100% conversion at 300 Engineering Skill. So 60 physical attack power and 150 Engineering Skill would convert to 30 systems disruption.
This is largely electrical and nanite damage; if you can get past enemy armor at all, then the full amount of systems disruption is dealt.
AbilityType|AndroidForceConversation|des: If a person doesn't want to talk to you, you can try to make them.
AbilityType|AndroidForceConversation|str: Only works if they know something worth learning. The target also has to be within attack range of your unit.

AbilityType|ProbeExoticComms|description: Robots and vehicles developed by the space nations are not on the City Feed, and don't have the typical accesses that you would need.
AbilityType|ProbeExoticComms|strategy_ti:
You'll need to go old-school, poking at them through the comms system that allows them to communicate with earth forces.
Finding an access point through a simple voice channel is extremely difficult, and more akin to the ancient practice of 'phreaking,' from before large-scale digital networks were commonplace.

ActionOverTimeType|StudyRustBarnaclesA|d: These 'veiny barnacles' are actually fungal colonies of The Rust. But they're... strange.

ActionOverTimeType|ObservePeakHomes|desc: Peak is the largest landlord in town. It's never been entirely clear why redevelopment stalled on the decrepit parts of town, almost a century ago.
ActionOverTimeType|ObservePeakHomes|stra:
On top of that, there are reports of odd sightings of racing animals of some sort, and illegal animal training facilities in those areas of town.
Employees of Peak have been observed going to and from these locations, but very little else is known.
ActionOverTimeType|UrsineInfiltration|de:
Raven's report on the Underground Ursine Street Racing was... vivid. You think you might want some of those animals for yourself.
Since CombatUnits are used as handlers in between races, it shouldn't be a big deal for one of your own CombatUnits to get in and set them loose.
ActionOverTimeType|UrsineInfiltration|st:
These are deadly animals, however. To capture them, you will need Animal Capture Drones, which can be launched from your Mindports (in the Vehicle tab of command mode).
Make sure you build enough drone frames in advance, and then be ready to capture the animals while both you and they are under heavy fire.
However many you manage to capture are the number you have; these have so many bionic augmentations that it's not going to be a simple matter to genetically replicate them.
ActionOverTimeType|BearTraining|descript:
The claws of these bears are incredibly effective at taking down vehicles and mechs. However, keeping the bears from attacking your own units, and keeping them vaguely on task (also not attacking civilians or hiding in buildings) is tricky.
The good news is that they already have extensive training with CombatUnits, as well as various established means of conditioning.
ActionOverTimeType|BearTraining|strategy:
If you prefer to just let them live the good life, you certainly can. At the best of times, trying to get bears to do exactly what you want is going to be... fraught.
And you can't make more bears if these ones die. Eh. Just because you train them, doesn't mean you have to deploy them. It can't hurt to have them trained, right?

ActorBadge|RustAnomalousStructure|descri: This structure is exhibiting unusual behavior at the level of microbuilder code.
ActorBadge|RustAnomalousStructure|strate: It's not really causing any ill effects, but it's causing the entire structure to run a bit hotter than usual.
ActorBadge|RustSpreader|description: This structure spreads Rust spores in its job radius.
ActorBadge|RustSpreader|strategy_tip_opt:
Every turn, there's a small chance of creating Rust Barnacles on your buildings, or on mechs belonging to anyone.
This greatly interferes with the armor and movement of mechs, and with the stealth and health of your structures.
With careful planning you can probably use this to your advantage.
ActorBadge|StructureRustBarnacles|descri: This structure is covered in veiny barnacles of the radiotrophic micro-fungus C. Heterosporium Dominium.
ActorBadge|StructureRustBarnacles|strate:
The barnacles do not impact the function of this structure, but they do cause an immediate loss of all stealth, and a per-turn health loss.
The barnacles will not reduce health below 20% of maximum.
ActorBadge|BulkheadArmor|strategy_tip_op: To damage this unit, you must have enough armor-piercing to breach its armor, or it's impossible to damage.

ActorBadge|DLC1_PartOfTheSkyline|descrip: Humans adapt to most anything. Giant spiders included, apparently. This unit is no longer innately alarming.
ActorBadge|BurningDown|description: This structure loses a large share of its health every turn. Fires on structures never go out on their own. Retardant Foam is the only thing that puts them out.

If a unit's system integrity drops to zero, they will leave combat.
By disrupting the integrity of enemy mechs and vehicles, you can take them out in a nonlethal fashion.
This is largely electrical and nanite damage; if you can get past enemy armor at all, then the full amount of systems disruption is dealt.
ActorDataType|ScanRange|description: Radius at which the fog of war is cut away.
ActorDataType|ScanRange|strategy_tip_opt:
This has a visual effect of revealing buildings and the ground. Activities and hostile units are revealed further out -- to your unit's full movement range.
Structures with scanner capability reveal out to their network or job range, whichever is larger.
ActorDataType|AttackRange|description: Maximum distance for ranged attacks. If beyond that range, a leaping melee attack happens.
ActorDataType|AreaOfAttack|description: Any secondary targets within this distance from the primary target are also struck by attacks.
ActorDataType|AreaAttackIntensity|descri: The percentage of damage applied to secondary targets in an area of attack.
ActorDataType|ActorMaxActionPoints|descr: The higher this number, the more actions this unit can make per turn.
ActorDataType|ActorArmorPlating|descript: Armor plating reduces incoming damage by a percentage (so 100+ armor plating prevents all damage).
ActorDataType|ActorArmorPlating|strategy:
Armor piercing has a linear effect on the effective armor of a target.
Example: If a target has 50 armor, and the attacker has 40 armor piercing, the effective armor on the target will be 10. Incoming damage is reduced by 10% instead of 50%.
ActorDataType|ActorArmorPiercing|descrip: Piercing reduces a target's effective armor.
ActorDataType|ActorArmorPiercing|strateg:
If a target is not armored, this has no effect.
Example: If a target has 50 armor, and the attacker has 40 armor piercing, the effective armor on the target will be 10. Incoming damage is reduced by 10% instead of 50%.
ActorDataType|ActorExtraVulnerabilityFro: This unit takes extra damage if attacked from behind.
Often two units are required to attack a unit from behind. When the target turn to face the first attacker, the other unit can attack from behind.
This unit takes extra damage if attacked from above.

You may need to lure this enemy to a location where you can find high ground.
If you have armed flying vehicles, choose one that flies at a higher altitude than this target.
