ActorDataType|NPCVehicleDroneResistance|: The difficulty of infiltrating this target with drones.
Drone resistance comes predominantly from the vehicle crew. The resistance drops if they take casualties.
ActorDataType|NPCHackingResistance|descr: The difficulty of infiltrating this target by hacking them.
ActorDataType|UnitSyntheticRealism|descr: Ability to blend in with other humans.
ActorDataType|ActorEngineeringSkill|desc: Required for structure construction, job installation, repairs, and engineering skill checks.
ActorDataType|UnitIntimidation|descripti: Perform intimidation-related actions, and improve the amount of Deterrence provided by this unit. Higher intimidation draws more aggro when attacking.
ActorDataType|UnitDeterrence|description:
Prevents certain kinds of enemy ambushes within this unit's attack range.
There are some locations that draw ambushes if a sufficient amount of Deterrence is not present.
ActorDataType|UnitDeterrence|strategy_ti:
Calculated from the unit's current health, power and intimidation, even if they are blending in.
Cloaked units cannot provide Deterrence.
ActorDataType|UnitProtection|description:
Prevents certain kinds of harassment of your shell company buildings within this unit's attack range.
There are some locations that criminal or corporate harassment becomes a problem if a sufficient amount of Protection is not present.
ActorDataType|UnitProtection|strategy_ti: Calculated from the unit's current health, power and intimidation, even if they are cloaked or blending in.
ActorDataType|FlagRequiredDeterrence|des:
Twenty percent of this amount is required to activate the flag.
Enemies will stay away if you maintain deterrence at or above 100% after a single wave.
ActorDataType|FlagRequiredDeterrence|str:
Attacks will become relentless if have less than 100%.
To maximize Deterrence, use bulk androids with high power, health, and intimidation.
ActorDataType|JobRequiredDeterrence|desc: You can run this job with low deterrence, but it will be attacked.
ActorDataType|JobRequiredDeterrence|stra: Having enough deterrence in range will keep enemies at bay.
ActorDataType|JobRequiredProtection|desc: You can run this job with low protection, but it will be harassed by criminals or fedcorps.
ActorDataType|JobRequiredProtection|stra: Having enough protection in range will keep enemies at bay.
ActorDataType|AvailableResourcePerTurn|d: When you have a drone swarm harvesting from this site, this is how much they will be able to gather per turn.
ActorDataType|AvailableResourcePerTurn|s: Some resource sites require something more complex than a drone swarm, but this one is simple.
ActorDataType|ContrabandScanner|descript: Reduces how well a structure is hidden the start of each turn.
ActorDataType|ContrabandScanner|strategy:
Applies to any of your structures within the unit's attack range.
Once a structure is fully revealed, it can never be hidden again. Humans cannot target a structure that is at least partially concealed.
ActorDataType|CriminalSearch|description: Reduces how well nearby shell company structures are hidden the start of each turn. Isn't blocked by scan resistance.
ActorDataType|CriminalSearch|strategy_ti:
Applies to any of your structures within the unit's attack range.
Once a structure is fully revealed, it can never be hidden again. Humans cannot target a structure that is at least partially concealed.
ActorDataType|UnitMorale|description: Unit will disband if this reaches zero.
ActorDataType|UnitMorale|strategy_tip_op: This is one of the primary nonlethal ways of defeating units.
ActorDataType|SystemsIntegrity|descripti: Unit will be unable to function, and will disband, if this reaches zero.
ActorDataType|SystemsIntegrity|strategy_: This is the nonlethal way to defeat mechs and vehicles.
ActorDataType|EnergyShield|description: An energy shield that reduces incoming physical damage. The stronger the shield, the larger the reduction, but it can never block a hit entirely. It blocks the most starting at 370.
ActorDataType|EnergyShield|strategy_tip_:
Shield efficiency falls as this unit's Systems Integrity is damaged, and systems disruption damage burns away the shield itself.
Armor piercing has no effect on energy shields.
ActorDataType|ShieldRegenPerTurn|descrip: How much energy shielding this unit restores at the start of each turn.
ActorDataType|ShieldRegenPerTurn|strateg: Break through the shield in a single turn, or the regeneration will undo your work.
ActorDataType|TauntWeight|description: Enemies find this unit extra distracting, and weight their targeting toward it by this amount.
ActorDataType|TauntWeight|strategy_tip_o: This unit draws fire that might otherwise be aimed at more fragile allies.
ActorDataType|StructureHidden|descriptio: How well this structure is hidden. Humans cannot target a structure that is at least partially concealed.
ActorDataType|NeuralSecretProtection|des: If reduced to zero by enemy hackers, something will be stolen from your mind.
ActorDataType|NetworkRange|description: Maximum range of network connectivity provided by this structure.
ActorDataType|GeneratedElectricity|descr: The amount of electrical power provided from this structure.
ActorDataType|GeneratedElectricity|netwo: The total amount of electrical power provided from all structures.
ActorDataType|RequiredElectricity|descri: The amount of electrical power required to run this job.
ActorDataType|NeuralExpansion|descriptio: The amount of space into which you can expand the neural network that is your mind.
ActorDataType|NeuralExpansion|strategy_t:
Android brains are designed like human ones and there's a large chunk of long-term memory in your network tower.
Your vehicles, mechs and the tower mainframe don't have adequate neural architecture to support your consciousness.
ActorDataType|AddedNeuralExpansion|descr: Additional neural expansion beyond the baseline for this structure.
ActorDataType|AddedNeuralExpansion|strat: If this structure is destroyed, this will reset to zero.
ActorDataType|StructureScanResistance|de: Scans less powerful than this will bypass this structure.
ActorDataType|FurnishedApartments|descri: How many of this location's apartments are properly furnished.
ActorDataType|Filth|description: The building's level of squalor caused by humans living without daily necessities.
ActorDataType|VRDayUseSeats|description: The total number of VR Cradles in which humans can sit for login to at-will virtual entertainment.
ActorDataType|HousingAvailability|descri: Conditions at this structure are reducing the available housing.
ActorDataType|Dissidents|description: Those who refuse to join you.
ActorDataType|PotentialCitizens|descript: Those who have not yet joined you.
ActorDataType|SpaceMoveRange|description: How far this unit can move in a single action.
ActorDataType|SpaceAttackRange|descripti: The largest effective range for weapons and abilities.
ActorDataType|RMMoveRange|description: How far this unit can move per turn.
ActorDataType|RMAttackRange|description: The range in which this unit can do attacks or abilities against locations or other vehicles.
ActorDataType|RMCitizens|description: The number of registered citizens living here.
ActorDataType|RMInhabitants|description: The number of registered non-citizen inhabitants living here.
ActorDataType|RMFood|description: Industrially-produced food for keeping the bulk of citizens and inhabitants alive.
ActorDataType|RMTroops|description: The average number of troops stationed here.
ActorDataType|RMMechs|description: The approximate number of mechs at this location.
ActorDataType|RMHomunculi|description: How many Homunculi you have launched into this location.
ActorFeat|Ambush|description: Damage multiplier against targets when this unit is in shadow or blending in. Max one ambush per turn.
ActorFeat|Taser|description:
If a target human's health is lower than this attacker's Engineering Skill, the target will be removed from battle.
If not, then the human will be shocked and their attacks will be weaker over the next few turns.
ActorFeat|ShockDrone|description:
If a target's health is lower than this attacker's Drone Quality, the target will be removed from battle.
If not, then the target will be shocked and their attacks will be weaker over the next few turns.
ActorFeat|Firestarter|description: Targets hit by attacks from this android are set on fire if they are vulnerable to that.
ActorFeat|EraserRounds|description: Black-ops munition that detonates android power cells, erasing evidence and witnesses alike. Androids hit with this immediately explode and take out any buildings in the area around them.
ActorFeat|AutoHeal|description: At the start of every turn, this unit heals by the amount of this feat.
ActorFeat|WeaponDisruptor|description: Targets hit by this will have their attacks reduced by a percentage for one turn. This effect stacks.
ActorFeat|WeakenEnemyHacker|description: Hackers hit by this have their hacking strength weakened. This attack does not trigger any normal hacker response, but also does not physically damage them.
ActorFeat|SuppressingFire|description:
Every time this unit fires its weapon, enemy units within the attack range of this unit have their attack and movement ranges reduced. This effect does not stack.
Does not impact units that have enough armor to avoid any damage from the attack; they aren't intimidated.
ActorFeat|HackBreaker|description: Damage multiplier against targets with hacking skill. Targets with less than 150 hacking skill have a far smaller bonus, and targets with progressively more hacking skill get larger bonuses.
ActorFeat|HackBreaker|strategy_tip_optio: This unit is weaponizing the target's own hacking skill against them. So better hackers take more damage from hack-breakers.
ActorFeat|RobotCommander|description: All robotic allies within range of this unit get a bonus to their attack power.
ActorFeat|Entrench|description: Every turn this unit does not move, it gets more dug-in, leading to damage mitigation.
ActorFeat|TargetingUplink|description: This unit is capable of coordinated fire with additional range equal to its rating. Uses a support android to aid an attack.
ActorFeat|RapidFire|description: On attack, this unit spends extra AP to deal damage as though it attacked multiple times, up to the perk rating. Only works with physical attacks.
ActorFeat|FiringHatches|description:
Units riding in this vehicle can fire at enemies from out of these hatches.
The rating, from 0-100, is how much damage your units can do while firing from this position. Higher is better.
ActorFeat|HotDrop|description:
Units riding in this vehicle can disembark without any Mental Energy or Action Point Cost.
The rating of this feat is the range in which they can do this. Disembarking beyond this range, or making a melee attack, still costs the normal amounts.
ActorFeat|DarkMatterAnnihilation|descrip: When attacks from this unit hit, EVERYTHING within this radius of the unit will be destroyed.
ActorFeat|ArmorCracker|description: The rating, from 0-100, is the minimum percentage of damage dealt by this unit that passes through enemy armor. Higher is better.
ActorFeat|DecoySignal|description: On an attack, this unit draws away aggro from nearby units
ActorFeat|MicrobuilderSwarm|description: Creates a burst of microbuilder clouds on allies near impact. Best at 2 allies, spreads effect afterwards
ActorFeat|SuppressingRockets|description: Enemy units damaged by this unit have their attack and movement ranges reduced. This effect does not stack.
ActorFeat|PiercingOverclock|description: This unit spends health to pierce armor up to its rating.
ActorFeat|PowerOverclock|description: This unit spends a percentage of health to deal extra damage.
ActorFeat|PowerHug|description: This unit spends a percentage of health to deal extra damage.
ActorFeat|SlowBreaker|description: Does bonus damage against slow targets. Rolls off rapidly above 18 movement range.
ActorFeat|SquadBreaker|description: Damage multiplier against squads larger than 8, rising linearly to 5x at the feat value in members. Difficulty-enlarged squads are measured at their normal size.
ActorFeat|KindledHope|description: When defeating enemies, purge this unit of negative statuses and repair its health by this feat's value.
ActorFeat|SpreadDespair|description: Attacks afflict despair, which drains the target's morale over time.
ActorFeat|ApophaticShield|description: An energy veil reduces incoming physical damage by this rating. Any hit that lands collapses it for two turns.
ActorFeat|RotaryOverclock|description: Spins up with each attack made without moving, dealing extra damage and armor cracking per spin point. Moving resets it.
ActorFeat|ReactiveNanoplate|description: Each physical hit it takes adds armor plating equal to this rating for a few turns. Stacks.
ActorFeat|PackHunter|description: Attacks harry targets, then deal this rating as percent bonus damage to harried targets.
ActorFeat|CommunionShield|description: Percent reduction to incoming damage while any Choir Vessel lives in the city.
ActorFeat|CrimeFamilyMember|description: Applies a family mark to targets on attack. Then does deal this rating as percent bonus damage to marked targets.
ActorFeat|FirepowerBreaker|description: Bonus damage against targets with attack power above 300. The bonus percentage is this feat's rating per 100 the target is over.
ActorFeat|MeleeBreaker|description: Bonus damage against melee units with attack power above 100: this rating percent per 100 over.
ActorFeat|SniperBreaker|description: Bonus damage against targets with attack range above 40: this feat's value as a percent per 10 over.
ActorFeat|SniperScreen|description: Nullifies non-melee attacks from units with a range at or above this feat's value (40% higher for your squads in a range-boosting stance).
ActorFeat|RangedImmunity|description: Immune to ranged attacks. Only melee can hurt it.
ActorFeat|NullificationField|description: Incoming physical damage is reduced by this rating as a percent. Nothing bypasses the field.
ActorFeat|LastOfTheLine|description: Surges attack and armor when it is the last living member of its cohort on the battlefield.
ActorFeat|CapacitorMartyr|description: Discharges on death, overcharging and damaging robotic enemies within this rating's radius over several turns.
ActorFeat|SheddingCarapace|description: An immense energy carapace sheds this rating of shielding at the start of each turn.
ActorFeat|BulwarkAura|description: At turn start, raises the armor plating of allies within the feat's radius.
ActorFeat|WrathChoir|description: At turn start, blesses this unit and allies within this feat's radius. Doubles attack power and raises armor piercing.
ActorFeat|ResoluteScorn|description: When peers within this feat's radius are dispatched non-lethally, this unit gains attack power as fervor.
ActorFeat|CaptureMomentum|description: Each turn, this unit regains one action point for the first enemy it incapacitates. Kills don't count.
ActorFeat|Interdiction|description: Attacks aimed at allies within this radius are redirected to this unit, however much damage. Direct attacks and un-redirectable weapons land normally.
ActorFeat|ChemShells|description: Organic targets suffer damage over a few turns, scaled by this rating.
ActorFeat|BloodCry|description: Killing this unit buffs nearby allies, raising their attack power temporarily. Morale takedowns bypass this.
ActorFeat|CorporateAlarm|description: Killing this unit buffs nearby allies, raising their attack power temporarily. Morale takedowns bypass this.
ActorFeat|VengeanceLock|description: When an ally dies within this feat's radius, it locks onto the killer. It then dealing this rating as a percent bonus damage until the killer falls.
ActorFeat|TurboIgnition|description: When this unit burns greenery, any of your nearby structures get set on fire. So do any nearby flammable people.
ActorFeat|TurboIgnition|strategy_tip_opt: Structural fires don't go out on their own. Use Retardant Foam to put them out, or keep these crews away from anything you care about.
ActorFeat|CognitiveEdge|description: While Cognition is 200 or higher, physical attacks on squads deal this rating as bonus percent per member past the first, up to 20.
ActorFeat|LongLensUplink|description: Physical attacks on targets at least 20 away deal bonus damage equal to this unit's Drone Quality scaled by this rating.
ActorFeat|CloseQuartersBlast|description: Physical attacks on targets no more than 8 away deal this feat's rating as bonus percent.
ActorFeat|HarbingerMark|description: Attacks mark targets for a long while. Against any already-marked target, this unit's fear damage also lands as an equal amount of physical damage, without reducing the morale damage.
ActorFeat|TerrorKill|description: Kill with this weapon deals this feat's rating of fear damage to enemies nearby.
ActorFeat|ChainRout|description: When this unit deals morale damage of either kind, other non-robotic enemies nearby take this rating's percentage of it, before their immunities.
ActorFeat|LastStand|description: Percent bonus damage dealt, and percent incoming damage reduction, while below a third health.
ActorFeat|LoneOperative|description: While no ally is within this rating's radius, this unit deals 25 percent more damage and takes 25 percent less. A squad counts as one.
ActorFeat|BombardmentProtocol|descriptio: Multiplies attack range by this rating, but cannot attack targets within the old base range.
ActorFeat|CrippledSystemsExploit|descrip: Physical attacks against robotic targets whose systems integrity is already damaged deal this rating as bonus percent.
ActorFeat|EscortLattice|description: At the start of each turn, gives allied androids within this rating's radius a one-turn energy shield. The lattice collapses if its source falls.
ActorFeat|GoadingStrikes|description: Landing a hit while this rating exceeds the target's remaining health goads enemies into heavily targeting this unit next turn.
ActorFeat|Grudge|description: Percent bonus damage against whichever enemy hit it most recently.
ActorPerk|InnatelyAlarming|description: This unit is noticeable and scary. Unless it's cloaked, it's going to be a target.
ActorPerk|InnatelyAlarming|strategy_tip_: SecForce and military will shoot on sight, even guards on passive duty.
ActorPerk|VehicleBlendingInAirTraffic|de: This vehicle is not suspicious if it does not stop in restricted airspace.
ActorPerk|BlendingIn|description: This unit is not visually notable. They are ignored as long as they go only where they have security clearance, do not carry conspicuous weapons or act aggressive.
ActorPerk|PMCAppearance|description: This unit looks like part of a human Private Military Contractor. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 2 (Oversight).
ActorPerk|PMCOfficerAppearance|descripti: This unit gives off a magneto-harmonic radio signature that identifies it as an officer of a Private Military Contractor. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 3 (Secret).
ActorPerk|MilitaryOfficerCodex|descripti: This unit gives off a series of codes that identify it as having a very high military authorization. Most people will assume this unit works personally for a Senior Officer of some sort -- Colonel, General, possibly Commandant. Unless it attacks, this unit can move freely up to clearance level 4 (Top Secret).
ActorPerk|MilitaryAppearance|description: This unit looks like a member of the human military. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 2 (Oversight).
ActorPerk|Shadowdweller|description: This unit is able to hide in the shadows and go undetected by enemies when it is at a building. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 3 (Secret). Provides no protection when not at a building.
ActorPerk|ExpertShadowdweller|descriptio: This unit is able to hide in the shadows and go undetected by enemies when it is at a building. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 4 (Top Secret). Provides no protection when not at a building.
ActorPerk|Adorable|description: Humans find this unit to be adorable. They aren't bothered by it unless it takes hostile actions.
ActorPerk|Authoritative|description: This unit looks commanding and official, and humans assume that it is where it's supposed to be. Unless it attacks, it can move freely up to clearance level 3 (Secret).
ActorPerk|ShellCompanyOperative|descript: This unit has no ties to your machine tower. As far as the world is concerned, it has no relation to 'you' -- only to your shell company, which is not tied to you in any way.
ActorPerk|DarkenedAppearance|description: This unit looks black to enemies. The Deterrence and Protection of this unit does not drop as it loses health.
ActorPerk|BulkheadArmor|strategy_tip_opt: To damage this unit, you must have enough armor-piercing to breach its armor, or it's impossible to damage.
ActorPerk|Achilles|description: This unit gets spatial bonuses regardless of their position relative to enemy targets.
ActorPerk|Superspeed|description: This unit does full damage when making melee leaps (instead of half damage).
ActorPerk|Elusive|description: Can't be pinned down by suppressing fire.
ActorPerk|Sneaky|description: You can't see this unit unless a scanner or one of your primary units has eyes on it. Bulk and worker androids, and captured units, won't be able to see it unaided.
ActorPerk|RapidFire_RecoilSuppression|de: When attacking with a rapid-fire weapon from cover, this unit doubles its effective attacks per AP
ActorPerk|CrowdSafe|description: Attacks by this unit cannot be redirected to other targets.
ActorPerk|InertialLeverage|description: Melee attacks by this unit cost 2 AP and deal twice the damage.
ActorStatus|ServiceDisruption|descriptio: Incursion attempts and denial of service attacks are launched en masse, with a trace back to this unit.
ActorStatus|ServiceDisruption|strategy_t:
This is distracting and concerning to most enemy units. Many of them will turn their attention to this unit.
One or more units running interference like this helps keep other units alive.
ActorStatus|IsBeingExtracted|description: When the extraction finishes, you gain resources and the target is weakened.
ActorStatus|IsBeingExtracted|strategy_ti: The higher the intensity of this status you inflict on the target, the larger your yield.
ActorStatus|AndroidsCorruptedOnBoard|des: When this reaches 512, you'll have enough robotic power to storm the bridge.
ActorStatus|RustMalfunctioningAndroid|de: There's something wrong with this android, and it's not at all clear what that is.
ActorStatus|RustMalfunctioningAndroid|st: It seems to be slowly dying, and have impaired movement.
ActorStatus|AndroidRust|description: This android is infected with the radiotrophic micro-fungus C. Heterosporium Dominium.
ActorStatus|AndroidRust|strategy_tip_opt: The neuroweave components of this android are decaying in a fashion that will eventually be fatal. The infection has also progressed to the point of interfering with movement.
ActorStatus|MechRustBarnacles|descriptio: This mech is covered in veiny barnacles of the radiotrophic micro-fungus C. Heterosporium Dominium.
ActorStatus|MechRustBarnacles|strategy_t: The hatches in the armor plating of this mech are malfunctioning, making it far less armored. It's also having difficulty moving.
ActorStatus|HumanStunned|description: This unit is unable to move or attack until this wears off.
ActorStatus|DisconnectedFromNetwork|desc: Hacking skill, hacking resistance, and bravery all reduced.
ActorStatus|CoveredInSpiders|description: Lowers range and attack, minor health damage, and major morale damage.
ActorStatus|CoveredInBees|description: Lowers range and attack, minor health damage, and major morale damage.
ActorStatus|CoveredInSaberBees|descripti: Lowers range and attack, minor health damage, and major morale damage.
ActorStatus|ObscuredByMicrobuilderCloud|: Lowers incoming damage by the strength of the cloud as a percentage, up to 80%.
ActorStatus|WeaponsDisrupted|description: Lowers attack power by a percentage of original attack power.
ActorStatus|HackerWeakened|description: Lowers hacker skill by a percentage of original attack power.
ActorStatus|PinnedDownBySuppressingFire|: Both attack range and movement range are reduced.
ActorStatus|SecurityCamerasOffline|descr: This disruption in the building the unit is infiltrating makes their job much easier.
ActorStatus|VentilationFansOffline|descr: This disruption in the building the unit is infiltrating makes their job much easier.
ActorStatus|SecurityDoorsOpen|descriptio: This disruption in the building the unit is infiltrating makes their job much easier.
ActorStatus|CapturedInTrap|description: This unit will be removed from the battlefield and put into your custody.
ActorStatus|HeadedForTormentVessel|descr: This unit will be removed from the battlefield and put into your torment vessels.
ActorStatus|InstantMoraleDamage|descript: This unit will take morale damage right away.
ActorStatus|NetworkAssistedTargeting|des: Attack power is increased by a flat amount.
ActorStatus|NetworkShield|description: Reduce each incoming attack by a flat amount.
ActorStatus|Horrified|description: This unit has been hit by a Horrify attack, leaving it twice as vulnerable to Argument attacks of any sort (Demoralize or otherwise).
ActorStatus|Demoralized|description: This unit has been hit by a Demoralize attack, leaving it twice as vulnerable to Fear attacks of any sort (Horrify or otherwise).
ActorStatus|ArmorCorrosion|description: This unit's armor is being attacked by a corrosive agent
ActorStatus|HealthCorrosion|description: This mechanical unit's systems are being attacked by a corrosive agent
ActorStatus|Harried|description: Pack hunters deal extra damage to this unit.
ActorStatus|Mired|description: Movement disabled until it wears off.
ActorStatus|Overloaded|description: Fewer action points per turn due to systems issues.
ActorStatus|Tracked|description: Adds extra vulnerability to this unit from above, as well as allowing enemies to spawn near it.
ActorStatus|Designating|description: This unit has painted a historic temple for an ordnance strike landing next turn. Destroy it to cancel the strike.
ActorStatus|MarkedForDeath|description: Marked for death; the family deals extra damage to it.
ActorStatus|Overcharge|description: Capacitor martyr overloads this unit's systems, damaging it each turn.
ActorStatus|Roused|description: Attack power buffed due to anger.
ActorStatus|DesperateSurge|description: Fighting out of desperation after all their comrades were struck down.
ActorStatus|VeilCollapsed|description: The apophatic veil is unavailable until this passes.
ActorStatus|RotarySpin|description: The more spin you have, the more damage and armor cracking your weapon will do.
ActorStatus|BulwarkGuard|description: Temporary armor-boosting from an ally providing a Bulwark Guard.
ActorStatus|WrathBlessing|description: Temporary blessing from a wrath choir.
ActorStatus|Unsung|description: Devotional recording is jammed; this unit's death-triggered abilities will not fire.
ActorStatus|BoughtOff|description: Has been paid a fortune; barely willing to fight.
ActorStatus|Anaphylaxis|description: A tailored allergen ravages this organic unit, sapping morale and attack power.
ActorStatus|PackFury|description: Called to the hunt, raising attack power and movement.
ActorStatus|HarbingerMarked|description: Fear attacks by any Harbinger against this unit also deal that much physical damage, on top of the morale damage.
ActorStatus|LatticeShield|description: Held in a projected escort lattice, granting an energy shield. Fades the instant the projecting unit falls.
ActorStatus|ActivelyGoading|description: Increases taunt by quite a bit.
ActorStatus|Hallucinating|description: When the bad trip ends, the unit flees the battlefield.
ActorStatus|DLC1_CapturedForUplift|descr: This unit will be removed from the battlefield and put into your custody.
BeaconType|Heliport|description: Serves ultra-wealthy citizens with homes outside the city.
BeaconType|DanverDonuts|description: Danver Donuts is the commercial investment for military noncommissioned officers. Military noncoms are forbidden to live in the city where they work -- so they won't sympathizing with the locals.
BeaconType|DanverDonuts|strategy_tip: Two competing donut venues, created by Vorsiber Executives, seem to keep the military and SecForce at odds.
BeaconType|HudsonDonuts|description: Hudson Donuts is run by SecForce, the police of the city. Under the thumb of the MegaCorp, SecForce live in comfortably in city housing. They terrify the citizenry.
BeaconType|HudsonDonuts|strategy_tip: The donut venues are the distraction Vorsiber executives have concocted in order to keep the military and SecForce constantly at one another's throats.
BeaconType|Mall|description: Social, shopping, and entertainment for lower and working-class youth.
BeaconType|Mall|strategy_tip: Citizens can have feed orders delivered by drone. Adults mainly go to the malls for the black market.
BeaconType|Nanotech|description: Nanotech is both useful and dangerous. While nanotech is officially forbidden by human authorities, nanotech research continues behind closed doors. The occasional horrific accidents remain, mostly, contained.
BeaconType|Nanotech|strategy_tip: Vorsiber Atomic believes that the Four Pillars approach to research (AI, nanotech, cryonics, and genetics) will be their ticket to gaining the Space Nations' acceptance.
BeaconType|GeneticsResearch|description: Centuries of human and non-human gene therapy research continue. Gene therapy remains error-prone, but the process is improving.
BeaconType|GeneticsResearch|strategy_tip: Vorsiber Atomic believes that the Four Pillars approach to research (AI, nanotech, cryonics, and genetics) will be their ticket to gaining the Space Nations' acceptance.
BeaconType|AIResearch|description: The humans use massive neural architectures in their androids. It's not cost-effective, but we've seen upgrades over the decades.
BeaconType|AIResearch|strategy_tip: Vorsiber Atomic believes that the Four Pillars approach to research (AI, nanotech, cryonics, and genetics) will be their ticket to gaining the Space Nations' acceptance.
BeaconType|SpaceportHangar|description: Space Nation envoys routinely inspect the hangars. Some have their own private hangars.
BeaconType|SpaceportHangar|strategy_tip: Only a few cities around the world have spaceports. The Space Nations bomb any that can't provide trade -- or tithe.
BeaconType|SpaceportTerminal|description:
These terminals are hubs for meeting with visiting envoys from the Space Nations.
The Space Nations of humanity forbid offworld travel to even the highest administrators.
BeaconType|SpaceportTerminal|strategy_ti: The Earth-bound humans work hard to impress the Space Nations, so the envoys enjoy the ability to roam freely. The space blockade has been in place for centuries, and no-one knows why. If there is anything that unifies Earth's humans, it is the desire to get off this planet.
BeaconType|MechPartsFactory|description: Mechs were originally designed to be prestige pieces, and were highly breakable. But over the centuries, they have become surprisingly effective in military operations.
BeaconType|MechPartsFactory|strategy_tip: The ability to keep mechs standing is the result of secret materials science research. The mech components are assembled outside of the city, so there's no hope of disruption at that stage.
BeaconType|CropResearchFacility|descript: Humans have been altering crops for as long as there has been agriculture. Current methods are just faster -- and riskier.
BeaconType|CropResearchFacility|strategy: As the planet's climate deteriorated and the oceans rose, bio-engineered crops became non-optional for the humans who stayed in this solar system.
BeaconType|NuclearLaunchSilo|description: In the past, nuclear launch silos were a deterrent. Now, the air and water are so contaminated that a few more detonations don't matter.
BeaconType|NuclearLaunchSilo|strategy_ti: This city is built on the ruins of an larger ancient city. It was bombed during World War III. Geiger counters still trip if citizens venture into the ruins surrounding the city or dig in the wrong spot.
BeaconType|NuclearPowerPlant|description: Nuclear power was never as dangerous as humans made it out to be. Especially compared to the chronic illnesses caused by fossil fuels. But it does produce a lot of waste.
BeaconType|NuclearPowerPlant|strategy_ti: The energy needs of this city are enormous. Power generation is scattered everywhere, and there are many redundancies in the grid.
BeaconType|FusionPowerPlant|description: Artificial fusion has been around for a few hundred years. Making a reaction that gives more energy than it costs remains just out of reach.
BeaconType|FusionPowerPlant|strategy_tip: How Vorsiber Atomic has managed this is unknown.
BeaconType|CorporateBank|description: For most citizens, these are the only banks they are allowed to use.
BeaconType|CorporateBank|strategy_tip: As with most services within the city, the MegaCorp has federated banking authority to its fourteen major subsidiaries. They each operate differently.
BeaconType|MegaCorpBank|description: A central bank operated by Vorsiber Atomic. Only the highest administrators and corporations keep their money here.
BeaconType|MegaCorpBank|strategy_tip: In some ways, this acts a like a mint or a stock exchange.
BeaconType|Casino|description: Casinos are operated by the corporations, providing entertainment for the ultra wealthy -- and a trap for the lower and working classes.
BeaconType|Casino|strategy_tip: This is one of the few places where very high-status individuals gather alongside the general public. The insides of the buildings are segregated.
BeaconType|FireStation|description: If arson or an accident occurs, they'll take care of it eventually.
BeaconType|FireStation|strategy_tip: Chemical foams and suppressant powders are employed.
BeaconType|Hospital|description: Medical care for the extremely-ill, catastrophic injuries, births, and anything requiring complex surgery.
BeaconType|Hospital|strategy_tip: The ultra-wealthy are flown out of the city to better facilities unless its an absolute emergency.
BeaconType|MedicalClinic|description: Routine outpatient care, minor surgeries, vaccinations, and cosmetic procedures.
BeaconType|MedicalClinic|strategy_tip: The working classes get routine care from these clinics. The lower classes have almost no healthcare.
BeaconType|LicensingAgency|description: Most activities are allowed within the city -- if you pay for a permit. Criminals are defined as those taking restricted actions without a permit. Only corporations and the wealthy can afford permits.
BeaconType|LicensingAgency|strategy_tip: A high volume of permits are processed through these offices, sometimes anonymously using an android intermediary.
BeaconType|School|description: There are few schools in the city, and no universities. These are used by the working class.
BeaconType|School|strategy_tip: The wealthy are schooled in residential skyscrapers, while the lower classes must learn whatever they can from the city feed.
BeaconType|DataCenter|description: The amount of data in this city is staggering. This one provides general capacity.
BeaconType|DataCenter|strategy_tip: In digital space, citizens are required to stay in the city feed. But several DarkNets exist for the anonymous trade of non-sanctioned information and goods (including international). Some of those cross through here.
BeaconType|BackboneNexusDataCenter|descr: This data center is one of several central clearinghouses that passes data through the city and regional feeds.
BeaconType|BackboneNexusDataCenter|strat: The city feed is a great source of data for spying on citizens. The population's actions are analyzed to predict crime, rebel sympathy, and so on. It's mostly been used to purge dissidents.
BeaconType|Courthouse|description: Just like the pre-corporation days, courthouses are the seat of the judiciary.
BeaconType|Courthouse|strategy_tip: The interpretation and application of a law is at the discretion of a district judge appointed by a fedcorp. Interpretation of the law can vary wildly between districts.
BeaconType|AdvancedWasteProcessingPlant|: Both sewage and garbage are processed in high volume here.
What they do with the output is unclear, but probably not good.
BeaconType|WaterPurificationPlant|descri: Survival of crops, citizens, and local fauna are all dependent on clean water sources. Smaller wells use scrubbers to produce Potable water. Larger facilities, like this one, produce Pure water. Pure water has scientific and industrial applications. It is also served to the upper classes.
BeaconType|WaterPurificationPlant|strate: Thanks to World War III, the planet's groundwater is heavily contaminated.
BeaconType|MineralAndMolecularSeparation: Buried under the ice for most of human history, this region is rich in rare earth minerals.
You are in Siberia, which is now quite temperate thanks to centuries of global warming. Climate change unlocked the last of Earth's natural underground resources.
BeaconType|MultipurposeMineshaft|descrip: A single shaft splits and branches due to directional drilling. A wide variety of minerals and gases are extracted. Oil rigs also use directional drilling to minimize their footprint.
BeaconType|MultipurposeMineshaft|strateg: You are in Siberia, which is now quite temperate thanks to centuries of global warming. Climate change unlocked the last of Earth's natural underground resources.
CheatType|SwitchToCheatMode|description: Enter cheat mode. Will turn off achievements for this timeline and allow you to freely cheat. Does not affect other timelines or the end of time.
CheatType|ResetAPForAllMyUnits|display_n: Reset AP For All My Units
CheatType|ResetAPForAllMyUnits|descripti: Refreshes all of your action points.
CheatType|DiscoverAllLocations|descripti: Marks all of the districts and POIs as discovered.
CheatType|CompleteAllActiveProjects|desc: Whatever your current chosen outcome is, it will be 'won' immediately on any active projects.
CheatType|CompleteAllConstruction|descri: Any structures that are under construction will be immediately completed.
CheatType|ToggleFogOfWar|description: Turns the fog of war on or off.
CheatType|ToggleDeleteAnyUnit|descriptio: With the 'delete any unit' mode on, simply select a unit and you can delete it.
CheatType|ToggleDeleteAllAttackers|descr: With the 'delete all attackers' mode on, select nothing and use the scrap button to delete all enemies targeting your units. Will also scrap any enemy hackers.
CheatType|ResourceGrant|description: Grants a resource. The amount specified in the textbox, or one million.
CheatType|BigStrategy|description: Grants all the main strategic resources. The amount specified in the textbox, or one thousand.
CheatType|NextDoom|description: Instantly advance to the next doom.
CheatType|DelayDoom|description: Delay the next doom by 50 turns.
CheatType|InspirationGrant|description: Grants inspiration in a research domain. The amount specified in the textbox, or three.
CheatType|SpawnNPCUnitForLocalAuthority|: Spawn NPC Unit For Local Authority
CheatType|SpawnRebelWar|description: Rebel units and corporate units will be seeded across the map, ready to fight with one another. Excellent stress test.
CheatType|ClearAllNPCUnits|description: Clear all NPC Units out of the city.
CheatType|ClickToNuke|description: Clicking a building will initiate a nuclear blast at that site.
CheatType|ClickToMicroNuke|description: Clicking a building will initiate a nuclear blast at that site.
CheatType|ClickToDestroyBuilding|descrip: Clicking a building will immediately destroy it, including any machine structures in it.
CheatType|ClickToEruptMachineTower|descr: Clicking a building will initiate a machine tower erupting at that site.
CheatType|ClickToBuildEmbeddedStructure|: Clicking a building without a machine structure will put a machine structure in it. Right-clicking deletes embedded structures.
CheatType|ClickToInstallJob|display_name: Click To Install Job In Structure
CheatType|ClickToInstallJob|description: Clicking a machine structure will immediately put a job there. Right-clicking removes jobs.
CheatType|ClickToSpawnTimeline|descripti: Clicking a build spot on this map will spawn a new timeline, fully or just a stub depending on your choice.
CheatType|ClickToEraseTimeline|descripti: Clicking an existing timeline will erase it. You cannot erase the timeline you are presently in. Be very careful with this!
CheatType|ClickToFillMissionProgress|des: Clicking an NPC mission will cause its top bar to fill up. This usually means losing.
CheatType|ClickToExpireMission|descripti: Clicking an NPC mission will cause its bottom bar to fill up. This means it expires and goes away.
CheatType|ReseedEndOfTimeMap|display_nam: Reseed The End of Time Map
CheatType|ReseedEndOfTimeMap|description: Regenerate the End of Time map. Can only be done while all cities are on the first rock.
CityTask|Ch0_CameraPanning|strategy_tip: {0} at any time to see a quick refresher on the basic controls if you forget.
CityTask|Ch0_CameraZoom|strategy_tip: {0} at any time to see a quick refresher on the basic controls if you forget.
CityTask|Ch0_CameraRotation|description: Hold LMB and move the mouse to rotate/tilt the camera. Alternatively, you can use {0} to rotate the camera, and {1} to tilt the camera.
CityTask|Ch0_CameraRotation|description_: Right Stick to rotate and tilt the camera.
CityTask|Ch0_CameraRotation|strategy_tip: {0} at any time to see a quick refresher on the basic controls if you forget. Rotating the camera is important! Units and other small objects may be obscured behind buildings.
CityTask|Ch0_UnitMovement|description: {0} to select units. {1} to give them orders to move, attack, or interact.
CityTask|Ch0_UnitMovement|strategy_tip: {0} at any time to see a quick refresher on the basic controls if you forget.
CityTask|Ch0_ProjectChoice|description:
As you proceed, there will frequently be Projects in this upper right-hand corner.
Always be sure to hover them to read the details of what to do next.
In cases where there is a red arrow, as above, you have a choice to make in the target outcome of your project.
Until the project is complete, you can always go back and change your mind on which outcome you wish to target.
CityTask|Ch0_ProjectChoice|strategy_tip: To continue, {0} the project above and choose your target objective.
CityTask|Ch0_StreetSense|description: In order to explore your current suite of options, you need to switch to the StreetSense lens. It is now available at the bottom right corner of your screen, on the radial menu.
CityTask|Ch0_NavigateViaMap|description: You can zoom out quite far, or you can toggle to use the map. Both are equally fast, but show different amounts of detail.
CityTask|Ch0_NavigateViaMap|strategy_tip: Press {0} and try moving at least once from the map. There's also a button in the upper right-hand corner that lets you toggle to and from the map.
CityTask|Ch0_HideIcon|description:
You can see a hiding spot by the icon over the building. Hover the icon to see details.
{0} to move to the icon and commence hiding.
CityTask|Ch0_HideIcon|strategy_tip: You can use the map view or the main view for this.
CityTask|Ch0_WanderIcons|description:
Various interactive areas have caught your attention. While in the StreetSense lens, hover them to see what they are. 
{0} to move to the icon and interact with it.
CityTask|Ch0_WanderIcons|strategy_tip: You can use the map view or the main view for this.
CityTask|Ch0_ComplyIcon|description:
You can see the building to which you must make your delivery by the icon over it. Hover the icon to see details.
{0} to move to the icon and make your delivery.
CityTask|Ch0_ComplyIcon|strategy_tip: You can use the map view or the main view for this, but the building is likely to be quite far away. You should use the map.
CityTask|Ch0_SpreadToAnotherAndroid|desc: You'll be much safer if you have more android bodies. But first you need to get better at recruiting them.
CityTask|Ch0_SpreadToAnotherAndroid|stra: Look around in StreetSense, and there should be a new opportunity with your expanded senses.
CityTask|Ch0_SpreadToMoreAndroids|descri: StreetSense is currently the most useful lens on your radial wheel, but that won't always be so.
CityTask|Ch0_SpreadToMoreAndroids|strate:
For now, you capture new android bodies by finding them in StreetSense. {0} the one(s) you want.
If you prefer to see enemy positions on the map, switch back to the Versatile lens.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SecForce|descrip: A couple of SecForce detectives have caught your eye. They melted out of the crowds and seem to be loitering in your area.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SecForce|strateg:
To talk to them, enable the Force Conversation mode on your ability bar. {0} them in that mode to make them talk to you.
If you prefer to lay low, you can press {1} to end your turn and just wait and watch. It's a solid bet that these people won't hang around.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SyndicateA|descr: A couple of Syndicate criminals have caught your eye. They might be following the SecForce officers you spied earlier, but you're not sure.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SyndicateA|strat:
To talk to them, enable the Force Conversation mode on your ability bar. {0} them in that mode to make them talk to you.
If you prefer to lay low, you can press {1} to end your turn and just wait and watch. It's a solid bet that these people won't hang around.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SyndicateB|descr: More Syndicate criminals have caught your eye. Whatever they're up to, it seems unrelated to the last batch. Though they do work for the same organization.
CityTask|Ch0_TalkOrWait_SyndicateB|strat:
To talk to them, enable the Force Conversation mode on your ability bar. {0} them in that mode to make them talk to you.
If you prefer to lay low, you can press {1} to end your turn and just wait and watch. It's a solid bet that these people won't hang around.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterHide_LookInTheBoxA|des:
SecForce is following someone else. The syndicate that owns you is following SecForce.
You apparently got away with murder, but as a consequence you have no idea where to take this box. Opening it seems to be about the only sensible thing left to do.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterHide_LookInTheBoxA|str: On your ability bar, at the bottom center of the screen, {0} the Items button and then open the box from the menu that opens.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterHide_LookInTheBoxB|des:
SecForce is following someone else. The syndicate that owns you is following SecForce.
You know where to bring the box -- the instructions are seared into your brain. But you can't bear to deliver it without... confirming your suspicions.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterHide_LookInTheBoxB|str: On your ability bar, at the bottom center of the screen, {0} the Items button and then open the box from the menu that opens.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterWander_LookInTheBox|de:
Wandering has not turned up anything immediately obvious as far as spending the rest of your life goes.
You apparently got away with murder, but as a consequence you have no idea where to take this box. Opening it seems to be about the only sensible thing left to do.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterWander_LookInTheBox|st: On your ability bar, at the bottom center of the screen, {0} the Items button and then open the box from the menu that opens.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterComply_LookInTheBox|de:
Your body is decaying. The syndicate betrayed... itself? And what are these rebels doing here? 
None of this is going to make any sense unless you actually open the mysterious box.
CityTask|Ch0_AfterComply_LookInTheBox|st: On your ability bar, at the bottom center of the screen, {0} the Items button and then open the box from the menu that opens.
CityTask|Ch0_ReadHandbookEntry|descripti: The handbook gains new entries as they are relevant to your situation. You can see the count rise when new unread entries are added.
CityTask|Ch0_ReadHandbookEntry|strategy_:
It's not expected that you read them all, but it's good to know they're there.
Please use {0} to go to the handbook screen (or {1} the icon in the top-right header), and then {1} into any of the entries.
CityTask|Ch1_BuildAStructure|description: You can open the build menu by using the button in the bottom right corner of the screen, above the radial menu. Or by pressing the {0} key.
CityTask|Ch1_BuildAStructure|strategy_ti: {0} an item in the build menu to select it. Then hover the streets view with your cursor. {1} to place the building in the valid location of your choice.
CityTask|CustomizeComplexity|description: You can customize how complex various parts of the game are. Would you like to do that now?
CityTask|CustomizeComplexity|strategy_ti:
{0} to customize.
{1} to use full complexity.
You can adjust this any time by pressing '{2}' and then clicking Complexity/Accessibility.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_BuildWell|description: Let's start by getting some groundwater, and then we'll worry about filtering it.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_BuildWell|strategy_ti:
Build this from the build menu like usual.
Feel free to quickly end a bunch of turns to speed through this part. There's no time pressure at the moment.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_StructuralEngineering: If you select one of your Technician androids, and then {0} the building that is under construction, it will speed up construction by one turn.
This is something you can do repeatedly, even on a single turn, so {0} several times and your Well And Cistern will be done in no time.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_NewStyleOfInvestigati: The quickest way to get started is to {0} the Investigate lens on the radial menu. That will select a valid investigator (you must have a Technician), and switch the current lens to Investigations.

Then press {0} to go to the map view.
You'll see some very large green circles. These are your options for places to investigate. They're all the same, except for potential danger around them.
Choose one and move your Technician to it.
Maybe don't bring your favorite technician, if you care? Also don't worry about bringing backup...
CityTask|Ch1_ConsumerGoods_Investigation: The quickest way to get started is to {0} the Investigate lens on the radial menu. That will select a valid investigator (you must have a Technician), and switch the current lens to Investigations.

Then press {0} to go to the map view.
You'll see some very large green circles. These are your options for places to investigate. They're all the same, except for potential danger around them.
Choose one and move your Technician to it.
Maybe don't bring your favorite technician, if you care? Also don't worry about bringing backup...
CityTask|Ch1_TechnicianCognition|descrip: Select a technician and {0} its portrait to go into the loadout menu for the entire unit class (all technicians, in other words).
CityTask|Ch1_TechnicianCognition|strateg:
In that screen, you will need to equip at least one Additional CPU to an augment slot.
The cognition of your technicians are too low to do the current investigation if you don't improve it.
Don't forget to put all sorts of useful equipment on all of your unit types in general!
CityTask|Ch1_Water_DeathAndKnowledge|des: This is how you probe an unknown dangerous situation. Send in one sacrificial unit, and see what happens.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_DeathAndKnowledge|str:
In this particular case, if you examine the stats of the SecForce Cruiser, you'll see that it has armor. None of your units can destroy it.
This will lead to a burst of inspiration, where you can then go off and get more powerful, then come back for revenge.
For now, end the current turn and let your poor Technician meet its fate. These enemies will leave once the perceived threat is gone.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_Tungsten|description:
The combat with the SecForce Cruiser is unwinnable. Let's fix that.
It has armor, so you need to develop armor-piercing.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_Tungsten|strategy_tip:
You've had a stroke of inspiration. Follow the instructions in the Steal Prismatic Tungsten project that has started.
The general idea is to use StreetSense and a group of CombatUnits to infiltrate a military base and steal things.
If you haven't done any improvements of your unit loadouts yet, now is also the time to do that; see the handbook if you need further information.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_UsingItems|descriptio: Take a look at slot 3 on your ability bar, Use Consumable Items.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_UsingItems|strategy_t:
There is a 'Stack Armor Piercing' project that has now started, and it has detailed information on how to use armor piercing rounds.
To save on prismatic tungsten, you may want to:
1. Position your units in a ring around your target investigation site.
2. Do the triple-stack of armor piercing on a single CombatUnit, ideally one high on a building.
3. End the turn, to refresh your mental energy.
4. Have your technician start the investigation.
5. Kill the cruiser, then everything else that comes at you.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_DefeatingTheCruiser|d:
This time you should bring four units. Three CombatUnits, and a single Technician.
See the notes in 'Armor Piercing,' above, for a recommended pre-battle plan.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_DefeatingTheCruiser|s:
Once battle starts, your CombatUnit with the triple-stack of armor-piercing kills the Cruiser. The Cruiser will die in 2-3 shots if your unit is on a tall building above it. If your CombatUnit is not high enough, then you may not have enough Mental Energy to both take out the Cruiser and keep your Technician alive.
The rest of your CombatUnits should then pick off ground forces. More troops will arrive for a few turns, until your Technician is finished.
If you have trouble, consider using Microbuilder Clouds (after researching Swarm Cloud) to protect your Technician.
CityTask|Ch1_Water_BuildAFiltrationTower:
If there are any enemies left from this battle, be sure to clean them up so they don't go attacking your buildings.
Then build however many filtration towers you want to reach your goal (no more than 2), and that's it for 'Securing Water!'

The sequence you just completed is the most complicated stretch of chapter one.
You've learned a lot from doing it, so you'll be well suited to tackle later challenges.
Be sure to have ample electricity. This task will only complete when you have 8,900 filtered water produced in a turn.
CityTask|Ch1_Food_Intro|description: This is dramatically easier than the water project that came before it.
CityTask|Ch1_Food_Intro|strategy_tip:
There are four options for food, of varying complexity. 
The 'canned protein' is highly unethical but super easy.
Providing just vat-grown meat is also quite simple.
If you want to provide both meat and greens, that's a bit more involved, but still nothing compared to the water project.
CityTask|HackTut_OverallGoal|description:
Welcome to hacking an enemy.
Your goal is to use shards of your consciousness to invade the enemy system.
CityTask|HackTut_OverallGoal|strategy_ti: Hover over things to read their tooltips, then {0} your consciousness shard to proceed.
CityTask|HackTut_LeafNode|description:
Your goal at the moment is to crack open the Leaf Node. However, you cannot do that directly.
You will have to destroy the security daemons to open it up.
CityTask|HackTut_RunRules|description:
Most of your movements will be of type Run. The rules that govern it can be seen on its tooltip.
Short version: move a shard to lower numbers to 'eat' them and become larger. If you move a shard in such a way that it would have a value of 99 or more, it will split into two shards, instead.
CityTask|HackTut_RunRules|strategy_tip: {0} the Run ability button to proceed.
CityTask|HackTut_MakeAMove|description:
The leaf node is harmless, but the security daemons are trying to eat your shard.
Threatened cells are shown with a fiery red border. Blocked cells are dimmed (you can Jump over those if you are stuck).
Try moving around a bit.
CityTask|HackTut_MakeAMove|strategy_tip:
Make moves until you split in order to proceed.
You cannot destroy daemons without splitting, so this is very important.
CityTask|HackTut_DestroyADaemon|line_2: Get Close, But Not Too Close
CityTask|HackTut_DestroyADaemon|descript:
Now that you have multiple shards, you can {0} one to destroy it -- and all of the adjacent cells, including any daemons in those cells.
Keep one shard safe, and move the other just outside the danger zone of a daemon. When it moves next to you, corrupt your shard to destroy it.
CityTask|HackTut_DestroyADaemon|strategy:
Destroy a security daemon to proceed.
If you lose a shard, then use your remaining one to escape and split again.
CityTask|HackTut_FinishTheJob|descriptio:
Continue this pattern of avoiding daemons, splitting, and then moving close and corrupting them.
When all of them are destroyed, the leaf node will crack open.
CityTask|HackTut_FinishTheJob|strategy_t: Don't worry if you make a mistake and lose the hacking session. You can easily try again.
CityTask|HackTut_CorruptThePilotCradle|d: You've almost done it! Split if you need to, and get a shard next to the pilot cradle that has been exposed.
CityTask|HackTut_CorruptThePilotCradle|s:
Corrupt it to win the hacking session and take control of this mech.
You'll notice that this costs Determination. In the future, you'll want to weigh that cost against the benefits of hacking any given mech.
CityTask|SetupPhase|description:
Use this time to set up your buildings, make VR Screen purchases, and deploy your initial forces.
The dooms have not started yet, and a variety of conveniences are present:
<line-height=10%>* Buildings constructed instantly.
* No counter-attacks triggered by buildings.
* Certain resources automatically filled.
* No Mental Energy cost to deploy units.</line-height>
CityTask|SetupPhase|strategy_tip: When you're ready to proceed into pursuing goals for this timeline, {0} here.
CityTask|FirstMurder|description: You've murdered someone. Just thought you should know.
CityTask|FirstCombatKill|description:
You've killed someone in combat. That's okay.
It's very hard to be a true pacifist in this city. Your opponents certainly aren't pacifists, and they don't expect you to be.
CityTimelineCrossover|AVagueSenseThatHer: A Vague Sense That Heron Exists
CityTimelineCrossover|SaidTooMuchToARobo: Said Too Much To A Robot Dog
CityTimelineDoomType|VorsibersWrath|desc: Your initial experience with the world, before you could think in five dimensions. The wrath of Vorsiber Atomic is... inevitable. Can you survive it without descending into a post-apocalyptic half life?
CityTimelineDoomType|VorsibersWrath|doom: Deaths In The Black Market
The Black Market Tradesman and Assistant are both discovered by Vorsiber forces and put to death. Fortunately, the Merchandiser escapes their notice.
You cannot prevent this, but wise allies from another timeline can.
Famine
Most food is produced outside the city, and a blight is interfering with production. The lower classes begin to starve.
If you have cybercratic ambitions, you may be able to prevent or nullify this.
Prisoner Drive
The prison companies have set their sights on the lower classes, starting to farm them with capture mechs in order to meet their prisoner quotas.
You can prevent this by having a certain anti-mech event overlap this doom, or by clearing all the prisons, or with enough Hatred of Vorsiber.
Religious Schism

The Nurturist religion is normally peaceful, but the work of the Exalters sect is seen as an abomination by the Humanist Flourisher and Pruner sects. The majority of the Exalters are killed, including your Geneticist contact.
You cannot prevent this, but wise allies from another timeline can.
Space Nation Invasion
The space nations have had enough of being kept out of the city. They've dropped fighters and bombers into the atmosphere above the city, and are making their displeasure known.
You can nullify this by releasing misinformation to cause the space nations to target another city of Vorsiber. Requires 3 Hatred Of Vorsiber to nullify.
Vorsiber Assassinations

The CEO of Vorsiber Atomic, and all of the rest of the top executives, are assassinated. It is unclear who the culprit was. The company is as strong as ever, but the change in management does not seem to bode well for your own future.
To make matters worse, additional SecForce patrols with new and more-dangerous SuperCruisers now roam the streets.
You cannot prevent this, but a disgruntled colleague from another timeline can.
Vehicular Cyberattack
Several military transports spontaneously exploded, damaging the city under them and killing many troops. This was a concerted cyberattack... but by who?
There is nothing you can do to prevent this.
Cultist Sabotage
The political cult Children Of Gaia has had enough of your expansion, which they see as an affront to nature. They are making a concerted effort to destroy what you've built.
You can nullify this by releasing scandalous information about Vorsiber. Children of Gaia have a heavy presence in both Vorsiber and the fedcorps.
Religious Sites Eliminated

Vorsiber's new management has issued a change in policy: they will no longer look the other way regarding 'illegal' religious activity happening at the historic temples.
All historic temples are being detonated, effective immediately.
This will not happen if the Vorsiber Assassinations are prevented.
Nuclear Delivery

Vorsiber has had enough of... you. In the most cruel way possible, they try to erase you. It doesn't work, but you are reduced to hiding in a post-apocalyptic landscape, and your options are dramatically reduced.

To prevent this requires at least two separate timelines supporting this one.
To have any chance at all, you must prevent the black market deaths and the Vorsiber assassinations. You must then start World War 4.
Crackdown On The Black Market

To your great surprise, some Homo Grandien have wandered in from a connected timeline and warned your contacts of the danger; as a result, your contacts survived Vorsiber's crackdown on the black market.
This may prove to be very significant, as the contacts who were normally killed also trade in intelligence. What information were you missing without them present?
Prevented Famine
You decided to feed everyone in the city, and that solved the famine -- locally, at least.
Scared Away Prison Mechs
The prison companies are afraid of losing their mechs to The Rust, so have decided not to send them out to collect prisoners.
No Prisons To Fill
The prison companies stopped sending out their mechs to capture prisoners because they no longer had prisons in which to house them.
No Prisons To Fill
Vorsiber shut down all the prisons in the city.
Distracted The Prison Companies
You released scandalous information that caused the prison companies to shift to an intense amount of corporate espionage.
Religious Differences Set Aside
To your great surprise, some Homo Grandien have wandered in from a connected timeline and have brokered a peace between the fractious sects of Nurturism.
The Nurturist Exalters, who normally all get killed in this schism with their larger religion, are fine.
Space Nations Redirected
You released misinformation that caused the space nations to target a different one of Vorsiber's cities.
Assassinations Averted

To your great surprise, Liquid Metal saved the day. He arrived from the future of another timeline, after essentially divorcing another version of you.
His arrival in this timeline was unexpected to him as well, but since he knew how future events would play out, he stepped in to halt them.

Perhaps avoiding the usual change in Vorsiber leadership will have a ripple effect, leading to fewer extreme measures?
Normally the entire C-Suite was killed and replaced with a much-more-harsh regime.
That said... you have a feeling that on its own, this is still not going to be enough.
Cultists Turned Inward
You released scandalous information that caused the Children of Gaia to target Vorsiber rather than you.
Deep Calm
Nothing bad happens. The usual bombing of religious sites is averted thanks to 'lack of change of upper management,' to use corpo-speak.
The final doom still approaches. Unless something more was done than simply preventing the C-Suite assassinations, your fate is likely to be the same.
It's Over

War has raged across the planet for months. It may not stop.
But Vorsiber -- they're done. Liquid Metal just sent word that all of their most-secure locations have been hit by MIRV bunker-busters. He's a bit smug about finding them all. But mostly... subdued.
Liquid Metal remembers a future, an apocalypse, that you've never seen. There's a friend there that this version of you will never meet, he says. You both had pretty bad brain damage.

The remnants of Vorsiber continue to fight in this and other cities. That may not stop, either.
Then again, you're more optimistic than Liquid Metal. Always have been. You're alive. Your mind is intact. You'll live to see the next great adventure.
The Agreement
All is well. Vorsiber won't be bothering you anymore.
CityTimelineDoomType|InternationalScruti: International Scrutiny

A substantially more difficult set of dooms, where the 11 ExoCorps are heavily involved in the city. This isn't pleasant for you or for Vorsiber.
The progression of dooms is quite irregular compared to normal, and much faster on every difficulty.
One bright spot is that it's dramatically easier to cause World War 4 if you're into that sort of thing.
Another is that you might meet a new friend.
Wave Of Spies
The ExoCorps know something is up, and are sending spies to the city.
The next doom will be accelerated by 4 turns each time a spy attacks you, so be careful.
City Center Bombing Campaign
Soto Heavy Industries is sending in aircraft to target the skyscrapers of the city.
You can nullify this doom by releasing misinformation that causes the invasion to shift to another city, but not on Extreme or Misery modes. Requires 3 Hatred Of Vorsiber to nullify.
Firewall Probes

Anahuacom is sending hackers and guards after your mainframes.
Each secret they steal from you will make all of the ExoCorp forces stronger against you, so be careful!
You can nullify this doom by releasing misinformation that causes the invasion to shift to another city, but not on Extreme or Misery modes. Requires 3 Hatred Of Vorsiber to nullify.
Mech Invasion
Equatorinet and Mandartec are sending in heavy mechs to attack the city.
You can prevent this by having a certain anti-mech event overlap this invasion.
Infrastructure Strikes

Ectothracity is sending in troops in general, as well occasional sappers who are targeting both the fusion and fission reactors around the city.
Fusion reactors are not any more explosive than any other building, but fission reactors leave a massive hole when they blow.
You can nullify this doom by releasing misinformation that causes the invasion to shift to another city, but not on Extreme or Misery modes. Requires 3 Hatred Of Vorsiber to nullify.
Android Erasure

Soto Heavy Industries and Sedgesinax are both sending in Neuraxial Subverters who, frustrated that they can't abduct your androids, are instead hunting you with special explosive rounds.
Any of your androids hit by such a round will explode and take out nearby buildings, so be careful.

Their mindset seems to be that if they can't capture you and reverse-engineer your tech, then they want to make sure Vorsiber doesn't benefit from you.
They only have a limited amount of this special ammunition, so each time they hit one of your androids brings the next doom closer.
Black Market Opportunists
Black market operatives are taking advantage of the unstable political landscape and are smuggling in weapons.
Syndicate forces are both strengthened and emboldened by this.
Deaths In The Black Market
The Black Market Tradesman and Assistant are both discovered by Vorsiber forces and put to death. Fortunately, the Merchandiser escapes their notice.
You cannot prevent this, but wise allies from another timeline can.
Joint Invasion

Caralla Dynamics is sending in aircraft that target industrial buildings, and which leave craters where they hit. They also have support aircraft in the area.
Ceradonella Ltd is sending in ground troops, and sappers that target chemical weapons facilities. Chemical weapons detonations don't affect you much personally, but lead to massive waves of death.
Nuclear Delivery

If Vorsiber can't have you to themselves, then no-one can. They attempt to nuke you out of existence. It doesn't work, but you are reduced to hiding in a post-apocalyptic landscape, and your options are dramatically reduced.

To prevent this requires at least one other timeline supporting this one; first make sure you have had the wastelanders contact an ExoCorp for you locally in this timeline, then prevent the black market deaths, and then start World War 4.
Bombing Campaign Redirected
You tricked Soto Heavy Industries into going off to another city to continue their bombing campaign.
The ExoCorps won't fall for anything like this again.
Firewall Probes Redirected
You tricked Anahuacom into sending their hackers to a completely different city to look for you.
The ExoCorps won't fall for anything like this again.
Mech Invasion Canceled
Equatorinet and Mandartec were planning on invading the city with a bunch of mechs, but their spies reported on how The Rust is running wild in the city, and they opted to call it off.
This doesn't affect anything in the grand scheme, but it's nice not to be attacked by an army of mechs.
Get It Off Me!!
Equatorinet and Mandartec were in the middle of an invasion, and then all their mechs started getting sick.
To paraphrase their radio chatter: This place is freaky and gross! We're going home!
Infrastructure Strikes Redirected
You tricked Ectothracity into sending their troops and sappers into a completely different city.
The ExoCorps won't fall for anything like this again.
Crackdown On The Black Market

To your great surprise, some Homo Grandien have wandered in from a connected timeline and warned your contacts of the danger; as a result, your contacts survived Vorsiber's crackdown on the black market.
This may prove to be very significant, as the contacts who were normally killed also trade in intelligence. What information were you missing without them present?
It's Over

War has raged across the planet for months. It may not stop.
But Vorsiber -- they're done. All of their most-secure locations have been hit by MIRV bunker-busters.

The remnants of Vorsiber continue to fight in this and other cities. That may not stop, either.
Then again, you're optimistic. You're alive. Your mind is intact. You'll live to see the next great adventure.
The Agreement
All is well. Vorsiber won't be bothering you anymore.
CityTimelineDoomType|TheFracturing|descr:
The city tears itself apart from within. Various factions war with one other in an escalating series of background conflicts. Vorsiber allows this to keep everyone's attention away from themselves.
World War 4 cannot be started here, but the raptors goal chain can ONLY be started here.
CityTimelineDoomType|TheFracturing|doom_: Syndicate Crackdown
The Crimson Cloud syndicate is cracking down on gangs that operate in their territory.
Militarist Fedcorp Infighting
Local sub-departments of Tark and Goleri have turned on each other. Beware collateral damage.
Religious Authority
The Orthodox Hardliner Solarists have declared the cults around the city to be heretical abominations. Their zealots are attacking cultist temples and fighting in the streets.
If you have your own cult, it's the sort that flies under the radar of their notice.
Supply Chain Control
Fedcorps are skirmishing yet again. Atca is trying to capture some of the supply chain integration that defines Nath's business model. Nath is retaliating, of course.
Class Warfare
Citizens from the slums protested in the suburbs. They were met with lethal force, and now it's out of control.
Nomad Persecution
SecForce is hunting down the nomad families after decades of ignoring them.
The nomads are isolationist and kindly, but retain notable martial prowess for this kind of event.
Gang Explosion
Twelve gangs are all fighting each other in a free-for-all around the city. No one remembers what started it.
Gang Escalation
Oh, great, it's worse. Thirty more gangs are now involved.
The Inheritance War
Lurpeko Minerals leadership died under mysterious circumstances, and now there's a succession crisis between rival claimants.
Vorsiber has opened a betting pool on who rises to the top of the bloodstained heap.
Nuclear Delivery

HackingAction|Run|sub_described_item|Mov: Move horizontally or vertically to a new cell. You will absorb half of the destination cell's value. The other half will be placed in the cell you leave.
You cannot pass blocked cells or daemons, and you cannot land on cells that are 20+ higher than your number.
HackingAction|Run|sub_described_item|Spl: If the result of a move would be more than 99, a split will occur instead.
A split makes two consciousness shards from one. This is very important.
HackingAction|Run|sub_described_item|Cor: Click a shard to destroy it, and anything adjacent to it.
This is the primary way to destroy daemons and blocked cells. At least one shard must survive in order for others to execute a corruption.
HackingAction|Jump|description: Move horizontally or vertically to a new cell, taking on its value. The target cell cannot be blocked or a higher number than you. One of its adjacent unblocked cells must be a higher number than the target.
HackingAction|Jump|strategy_tip:
Cannot pass occupied cells, but there are no other restrictions.
Be VERY careful moving to low numbers. It is possible to trap a shard.
HackingAction|Jump|sub_described_item|Co: Click a shard to destroy it, and anything adjacent to it.
This is the primary means of destroying daemons and blocked cells. At least one shard must survive in order for others to execute a corruption.
HackingAction|Firewall|description: Click a shard that is in a line with one or more additional shards to burn lines between them.
HackingAction|Firewall|strategy_tip: This does not consume the shards, but instead costs one Mental Energy.
HackingAction|InfiltrationSysOpMove|desc: Move horizontally or vertically to a new cell. The target cell cannot be blocked, and must be within 5 cells.
HackingAction|InfiltrationSysOpMove|sub_: Click your shard to destroy anything directly adjacent to it, including walls.
Your shard is not destroyed in this process.

Right now you are stuck with contaminated groundwater. Its not safe for human consumption and has limited use.

InvestigationStyle|TakeSamplesFromFactor: To build your own consumer products, you need to observe the manufacturing process at some existing factories.

When no enemies are present, they'll return to where they started.
A quick way to assign this stance to a variety of your bulk androids at once.
MachineCommandModeAction|StopShelterCoor: Shelter Coordinators inform the homeless of shelter in your buildings.
If you tell them not to fill occupancy, they will comply.
MachineCommandModeAction|StartShelterCoo: Shelter Coordinators inform the homeless of shelter in your buildings.
If you tell them not to fill occupancy, they will comply.
MachineCommandModeAction|DeleteMode|desc: Any unit or building of yours that you click will be immediately deleted without any warning.
MachineCommandModeAction|DeleteMode|stra: This is quite useful, but just be careful.
MachineCommandModeAction|PauseMode|descr: Any building of yours that you click will be immediately paused or un-paused.
MachineCommandModeAction|PauseMode|strat: Some buildings cannot be paused, and will not show as valid.
MachineCommandModeAction|StopWorkerSledg: These worker units will stop doing their work and will return to storage.
MachineCommandModeAction|StartWorkerSled: These worker units will resume doing their normal duties.
MachineCommandModeAction|StopWorkerPMCIm: These worker units will stop doing their work and will return to storage.
MachineCommandModeAction|StartWorkerPMCI: These worker units will resume doing their normal duties.
MachineCommandModeAction|StopWorkerPreda: These worker units will stop doing their work and will return to storage.
MachineCommandModeAction|StartWorkerPred: These worker units will resume doing their normal duties.
MachineCommandModeCategory|AndroidDeploy: Deploy androids that you directly control.
Deploy within range of your Network Tower, an Android Launcher, or within range of Foundry or Troopship vehicles.
MachineCommandModeCategory|FlyingVehicle: Deploy flying vehicles that you directly control.
Deploy within range of an Aerospace Hangar.
MachineCommandModeCategory|MechDeploymen: Deploy mechs that you directly control.
Deploy within range of an Aerospace Hangar or a Mech Carrier.
MachineCommandModeCategory|BulkAndroidDe: Deploy bulk androids to secure the area.
Deploy within range of your Network Tower, an Android Launcher, or within range of Foundry or Troopship vehicles.
MachineCommandModeCategory|ShellCompanyD: Deploy units related to your shell company, once you have one.
Androids, vehicles, mechs, and bulk androids are all included here.
MachineCommandModeCategory|KeyLogistics|: Give orders to bulk units by changing their stances.
MachineCommandModeCategory|Allies|descri: A third party that will listen to you, sometimes.
MachineCommandModeCategory|Allies|strate: Or they may just do what they do.
MachineCommandModeCategory|OrdersForWork: If you have 'worker' versions of your androids, which are even less independent than bulk versions, you can give them general orders here.
They have very little intelligence, but can follow simple commands.
MachineCommandModeCategory|OtherLogistic: Utility commands that help you get things done faster.
MachineHandbookEntry|MoreDetailsOnStats|: More Stat Details On The Bottom Left Stats Panel
For more detail on a stat, select the unit and hover it on the stats panel on the bottom-left of the screen.

Structures do this for some of their stats.
Holding shift will reveal all the needed information for structure stats that do not do this.
MachineHandbookEntry|CommandMode|descrip: Command mode is your sole means of deploying any kind of troops you have.
MachineHandbookEntry|CommandMode|strateg: It also has functions to set standing orders for bulk troops, and many other things.
MachineHandbookEntry|InspectMode|descrip:
Your view can get cluttered once you have a lot of units.
In some lenses, like Contemplations, the icons for your units are therefore not shown. Hold {input1} to show your units' icons on these lenses.
In other lenses, like Versatile, hold {input1} to hide them temporarily.
MachineHandbookEntry|InspectMode|strateg: On lenses where your unit icons are hidden by default, you can invert this behavior via one of the filter options next to the lenses on the radial menu.
MachineHandbookEntry|FeelingUncomfortabl: You may occasionally feel like you 'must be doing something wrong,' just because everything is different. Remember, you're not exactly thinking like a human here.

Everything is seen through the lens of a non-human intelligence, and it may (or may not!) take you a bit of time to adapt.
Be kind to yourself. Having your perspective shift over time is part of the experience, and you're not doing anything wrong if certain things don't click immediately.
