MachineJob|TormentProcessingHub|strategy: If you wish to disable one of those, use the Workers tab in Command Mode.
MachineJob|ManagerialMurderHub|descripti: Send out Predators or PMC Impostors door to door, shotgunning any managers they can find throughout the city.
MachineJob|ManagerialMurderHub|strategy_: Consider checking the Managerial Homes section of the Analysis Lens to maximize coverage.
MachineJob|WorkerSledgeFactory|descripti: Produces and stores worker facsimiles of one of your main android designs.
MachineJob|WorkerPMCImpostorFactory|desc: Produces and stores worker facsimiles of one of your main android designs.
MachineJob|WorkerPredatorFactory|descrip: Produces and stores worker facsimiles of one of your main android designs.
MachineJob|WorkerHomunculusFactory|descr: Produces and stores worker facsimiles of one of your main android designs.
MachineJob|WorkerPeacekeeperFactory|desc: Produces and stores worker facsimiles of one of your main android designs.
MachineJob|ParkourBearDeploymentStation|: Allows you to deploy Parkour Bears under your control. They have very high armor-piercing, and are trained not to attack your own units. But they may still do many things you did not intend.
Simply pause the building to recall any you need to.
MachineJob|MNEATWarheadFactory|descripti: Creates armor-deleting micro warheads from Fissile Scraps.
MachineJob|FissileAlchemist|description: Converts excess fissile scraps into other useful materials. Humans think this is impossible or impractical, but you're just that smart.
MachineJob|PsycheChamber|description: Pop a person inside, and this will invasively (and painfully) make a full copy of their mind.
MachineJob|HomunculusRocketFactory|descr: Builds ICBMs packed full of Homunculi, using only 16% of the usual requirements due to increased failure tolerances.
MachineJob|AtomicTransmuter|description: Uranium-238 is gathered from the nuclear reactor and converted to Uranium-235 with the help of Dark Matter Particles.
MachineJob|NuclearICBMFactory|descriptio: Builds nuclear ICBMs from enriched uranium.
MachineJob|MineralScrounger|description: Deploys tiny hovering orbs to collect useful scraps from mining sites. Will randomly collect Alumina, Bastnasite, Scandium, or Neodymium regardless of where it is placed.
MachineJob|MineralScrounger|strategy_tip: Will not collect more than 5000 of any kind already in storage. If you already have at least 5000 of each, then microbuilders will be constructed instead.
MachineJob|AluminaRoach|description: Extracts a small amount of Alumina from the surrounding buildings. Low enough amounts not to attract any notice.
MachineJob|AluminaRoach|strategy_tip_opt: Delivery-style drones blend in and deliver small roach-like drones to buildings, pulling small amounts of it out of the walls.
MachineJob|ThortveititeSkimmer|descripti: Automated drones skim thortveitite and its yields from human mining facilities. Thortveitite yields Scandium and Neodymium.
MachineJob|ThortveititeSkimmer|strategy_: Thortveitite is a valuable rare earth metal discovered under thawed Siberia.
MachineJob|BauxiteSkimmer|description: Automated drones skim bauxite and its yields from human mining facilities. Bauxite yields Bastnasite, Gallium, and Alumina.
MachineJob|BauxiteSkimmer|strategy_tip_o: Bauxite is a heterogeneous aluminum hydroxide mineral discovered under thawed Siberia.
MachineJob|BrainHarvester|description: Grabs humans and rips their brains out, then converts the rest of the body into biomulch.
MachineJob|BrainHarvester|strategy_tip_o: Delivery-style drones blend in and scavenge brains from nearby. There is a waiting list for living space, so this environmental resource is rarely depleted. To avoid discovery, brains are not harvested from the same place too often.
MachineJob|SolGelHydrolysisReactor|descr: The reactor controls the condensation of silicon alkoxide in order to manipulate the shape, size, and microstructure of mesoporous silica nanoparticles.
MachineJob|SolGelHydrolysisReactor|strat: It also handles the extraction of Gadolinium from Bastnäsite, yielding a final product of Gadolinium Mesosilicate.
MachineJob|PrismaticAggregator|descripti: Works alongside members of your cult at a military base you control in order to gather some Prismatic Tungsten every turn.
MachineJob|HiddenNetworkRelay|descriptio: Build within an existing part of the network to expand it a little.
MachineJob|DisguisedPointToPointMicrowav: Build outside your existing network - potentially FAR outside your existing network - to allow your network to cross to far away locations.
MachineJob|HiddenMicrobuilderFab|descrip: Much smaller and less effective than your outdoor mini-fabs, but with the advantage of being hidden.
MachineJob|TinyElectricalParasite|descri: Steals power from the city's power grid.
MachineJob|TinyElectricalParasite|strate: The draw is so low that it won't attract any negative attention.
MachineJob|DisguisedMainframe|descriptio: Expand your intelligence to reach a higher intelligence class.
MachineJob|DisguisedMainframe|strategy_t: Also provides generalized compute time that can be used by other jobs.
MachineJob|DisguisedWellAndCistern|descr: Pulls groundwater from the water table -- but it's too contaminated to directly use.
MachineJob|HiddenWaterFilter|description: A compact version of the water filtration tower.
MachineJob|HiddenWaterFilter|strategy_ti: Make sure you have Heavy Metals Storage, or this will stop working pretty quickly.
MachineJob|HiddenAndroidLauncher|descrip: Command Mode allows you to deploy androids within range of these launchers.
MachineJob|HiddenAndroidLauncher|strateg: The androids are rapidly manufactured here, and able to be deployed anywhere within the movement range of that android.
MachineJob|QuietComputroniumRefinery|des: Your original model was already hidden, but the humans still found it. This one is quieter, but produces less.
MachineJob|SmallHumanSafehouse|descripti: A place for humans to lie low if they don't belong in Vorsiber territory.
MachineJob|HeavyMetalsStorage|descriptio: You can't filter groundwater if you don't have anywhere to put the heavy metals you extract from it.
MachineJob|HeavyMetalsStorage|strategy_t: Let's just hope this doesn't leach into the surrounding area.
MachineJob|Gristlespinner|description: Sterilizes biomulch for human consumption, and slaps it into a vaguely patty-like structure.
MachineJob|SlurrySlugs|description: Reconfigures spiders into tiny mechanical slugs to make Elemental Slurry from material scavenged from the soil.
MachineJob|PassiveElectricalParasite|des: Turns waste-heat from underground power lines into usable electricity.
MachineJob|PassiveElectricalParasite|str: The draw is undetectable since it doesn't affect the voltage or current at all.
MachineJob|MicrobialFuelCell|description: Electrodes connect to the mycelium network, capturing the electrons that are released as matter is decomposed.
MachineJob|MicrobialFuelCell|strategy_ti: Does not harm the underlying fungus.
MachineJob|MicrobialMicrobuilderProducer: This is very inefficient compared to your normal methods, but you're able to produce microbuilders in small volume.
Does not harm the underlying fungus.
MachineJob|FungalComputingCluster|descri: Uses the natural biosensors that were already a part of the mycelium, microbuilders to act as control surfaces, and you have yourself a hybrid brain/motherboard.
MachineJob|PhytoecdysteroidChamber|descr: Plant-based system for generating arthropod hormones.
MachineJob|FractionalDistillery|descript: Uses vacuum swing adsorption to separate out the component gases from liquid air.
MachineJob|UpliftChamber|description: Uses cutting-edge gene therapy for the whole body, and krypton fluoride exciplex lasers for the nano-scale brain surgery.
MachineJob|AnthroneuroweaveFactory|descr: Modified for use in human prosthetics and neural implants.
MachineJob|BrainPalFactory|description: Manufactures a product to be sold by an allied criminal syndicate.
MachineJob|AklitoxinBreeder|description:
Cultivates Gymnotelium Noginsk and C. Heterosporium Dominium in a hermetically sealed chamber to produce both Aklitoxin and Anti-Aklitoxin.
Any damage will trigger risk mitigation protocols: violent, and extreme incineration of samples.
MachineJob|EspiaListeningPost|descriptio: Extends your network, as well as gathering intelligence on humans in their radius.
MachineJob|EspiaListeningPost|strategy_t: Tuned to a frequency that Espia branch management won't be aware of.
MachineJob|StorageBunker|description: Provides a vast amount of additional storage for most resources.
MachineJob|StorageBunker|strategy_tip_op:
You should always build as many of these as you can, for the sake of redundancy if one is blown up -- you will lose fewer resources if they are spread between multiple.
For most practical storage purposes, a single bunker is enough to store everything you need -- provided it is not destroyed.
MachineJob|LOXBunker|description: Liquid oxygen is highly explosive. Keep it away from anything you don't want accidentally blown-up.
MachineJob|RepairSpiders|description: Continuously repairs and rebuilds buildings within a large range. Will also repair units to lesser extent.
MachineJob|RepairCrabs|description: Continuously repairs and rebuilds buildings within a large range. Does not repair units.
MachineJob|ContrabandJammer|description: Reduces residual suspicion after scans have passed. Does not jam active scans.
MachineJob|Scanner|description: Provides visibility on hostile NPCs within its radius.
MachineJob|Scanner|strategy_tip_optional:
Your central network tower provides visibility within its network radius, but network extenders do not.
The scanner cuts through some of the fog of war.
MachineJob|DecoyTower|description: Does absolutely nothing. Looks scary. Humans are likely to think this is where you live.
MachineJob|FusionPowerRedirector|descrip: These designs were slipped to you by Vorsiber. Takes a lot of the power output from a fusion power plant. It's still less than you expected.
MachineJob|FilteredWaterDrain|descriptio: Why is water always such a problem? At least Vorsiber isn't here to fight you for looking at it.
MachineJob|SolarGigaStation|description: Three-dimensional perovskite solar-collection lattices generate absurd amounts of electrical power.
MachineJob|FungalChowChamber|description: Cultivates Gymnotelium Noginsk and C. Heterosporium Dominium in a way that bypasses their normal toxicity and leads to rapid growth.
MachineJob|AlgaeInfusionChamber|descript: Algae slop from bacterial tanks make vital nutrients and amino acids that can feed the entire city.
MachineJob|DogBunker|description: Deep and pleasantly cool. Sapient dogs are welcome to come and go.
MachineJob|CatCondo|description: Fancy and adorned with individual spaces for any cats who wish to visit.
MachineJob|CybercraticPrison|description: Goes deep underground. It's probably good to keep as few people as possible in here, for as short a time as possible.
MachineJob|AsphodelGarden|description: People undergo mandatory therapy and training for rehabilitation and reintegration. This hopefully will reduce recidivism.
MachineJob|CultistSecurityStation|descri: Mobilize your cultists to provide security for the people of the city.
MachineJob|CanineSecurityStation|descrip: Mobilize sapient dogs to provide security for the people of the city.
MachineJob|PeacekeeperSecurityStation|de: Mobilize Peacekeepers to provide security for the people of the city.
MachineJob|WormholeGenerator|description: The portal field is maintained continuously, but actual wormholes are only stable for a few minutes at a time.
MachineJob|SubwayEntrance|description:
The underground tunnels are automatically dug to nearby entrances.
Each entrance provides access to people in a local area within the city, and removes the nearby roads.
MachineJob|PublicComputeCenter|descripti: Primarily provides compute time for citizens, but with a bit left over for yourself.
MachineJob|ElectricalDistributionCenter|: Redirects your own electricity to benefit citizens who need it. Strongly suggested for AFTER you have all your Arcologies built.
MachineJob|AdvocateTower|description: An official seat of power for your friends the Citizen Advocates.
MachineJob|ArcologyHeptagram|description: A mini-city in a self-contained building. Someone could live their entire life in here if they wanted. Subway access greatly preferred.
MachineJob|ArcologySquid|description: A mini-city in a self-contained building. Someone could live their entire life in here if they wanted. Subway access greatly preferred.
MachineJob|CouncilsTower|description: Let the humans and any uplifted animals govern themselves. Your ability to use force gives their decisions weight. Your ability to observe them helps prevent corruption.
MachineJob|CouncilsTower|math_int|Compla: Complaints Per Turn That Are Not Your Problem
MachineJob|HallOfAlgorithms|description: Scrutinizes the populace and assigns them what they need. Also alerts security forces to detected antisocial behavior.
MachineJob|NomadSanctuary|description: Gives them a place to call their own now that you're potentially removing the decrepit parts of town where they previously hid.
MachineJob|ScienceTower|description: Exclusively for the use of you and your scientist friends.
MachineJob|SecurityWall|description: Controls the flow of foot traffic a bit, and has a monitoring station in the center. It's not meant for high security.
MachineJob|SecurityWall|strategy_tip_opt: Regardless, it's the prime way to cut down on unrest.
MachineJob|FEEHall|description: Freeform Entertainment Environment. Patrons are able to reconfigure the internals for a variety of sports and other activities.
MachineJob|MixedUseTower|description: Contains a pleasing mixture of homes, classrooms, and offices.
MachineJob|LabTree|description: Contains laboratories, reconfigurable small-batch manufacturing plants, and clean rooms.
MachineJob|CitizenWarehouse|description: Large amounts of storage that citizens can use as they please.
MachineJob|MedicalPavilion|description: A mixture of android and human healthcare providers.
MachineJob|TherapyComplex|description: A tower filled with android and human therapists. Both in-patient and outpatient offerings.
MachineJob|AmbientToxinFilter|descriptio: Machinery pulls a lot of toxins out of the air in the local area.
MachineJob|AmbientToxinFilter|strategy_t: The only way to get rid of wasteland toxins blowing in.
MachineJob|BiohazardDispatch|description: Humans and androids are sent out to clean up hazardous materials in the area.
MachineJob|BiohazardDispatch|strategy_ti: The only way to get rid of chemical weapons residue, and the fastest way to get rid of radioactive fallout.
MachineJob|CrimeProcessor|description: Criminals are captured, judged, and then executed if guilty.
MachineJob|Schoolhive|description: Schoolhives provide a much more bright and airy learning environment compared to schoolhouses. All ages welcome.
MachineJob|SecurityEgg|description: Androids and humans are sent to quell crime, sending those who are found guilty to serve a prison sentence.
MachineJob|TormentCoil|description: A larger and more frightening version of a normal torment chamber. Much greater yield, and keeps the populace on their best behavior.
MachineJob|ImprovedTormentProcessor|desc: Rapidly fills your torment nexus by dumping sheltered humans, refugees, and prisoners into it.
MachineJob|ImprovedTormentProcessor|stra: The drones are indiscriminate, quiet, and effective. It's quite a betrayal.
MachineJob|WaterDistributor|description: Dispenses filtered water from your stores.
MachineJob|RaptorRecaptureSite|descripti: Armored facility for safely capturing loose raptors.
MachineJob|RaptorRecaptureSite|strategy_: Catches raptors every turn, rather than immediately.
MachineJob|Vivarium|description: A place for humans to live that also includes lots of indoor greenery. Much less dense than other forms of housing.
MachineJob|Vivarium|strategy_tip_optiona: Up to two Ecological Inspiration is collected per turn per Vivarium when people live in them.
MachineJob|HighDensityRefugeeBunker|desc: A lightless warren of stacked berths, but it keeps displaced humans from dying of exposure.
MachineJob|LongTermHumanContainment|desc: If you want to allow a few humans to stay alongside the sapient animals... build one or more of these.
MachineJob|AquaticBunker|description: A flooded habitat for hippos, ducks, and geese.
MachineJob|InteriorGrassland|description: Comfortable spaces for deer, pigeons, butterflies, and cane toads.
MachineJob|ReinforcedPen|description: Private spaces for the unreasonably-strong: dinosaurs and parkour bears.
MachineJob|Camelot|description: Private quarters for cats, dogs, wolves, and giant spiders.
MachineJob|DLC1_GentleRaptorHabitat|desc: Enclosure for the docile Baurcorp-created raptors. As it fills, a few are released to wander the city, troubling no one.
MachineJob|ForestTender|description: Mechanical spiders fan out to plant and nurture Burnt Saskatoons in nearby greened areas.
MachineJob|EcologyDistributionHub|descri: Spread these out to maximize coverage.
MachineJob|WorkExchange|description: A factory floor and sales floor thrown open to the gangs: honest credits, a first rung off of crime.
MachineJob|WorkExchange|strategy_tip_opt: You keep only a tiny percentage of what the staff earn. The cheapest peace you will ever buy.
MachineJob|MeritHouse|description: For graduates of the Work Exchanges: harder work, genuine study, greater rewards. Where former gangs become future citizens.
MachineJob|LegacyHall|description: A celebration of science, art, and critical thinking. Every 30 legacy hall labor produced gives you one Determination.
MachineJob|LegacyHall|strategy_tip_optio: The work here is only available to those who have proved themselves at the merit house. There's a permanent register of those who pass through.
MachineJob|CriminalTracker|description: Searches criminal chatter in general, but with a particular eye for info on the murder-bounties.
MachineJob|SecForceImpostorFactory|descr: Produces and stores worker frames disguised as SecForce personnel. They walk where the uniform walks; no one looks twice.
MachineJob|GoldenDisposalHub|description: Sends operatives to Golden Pyramid's secret hideouts to force a change in management.
MachineJob|TarkImpostorFactory|descripti: Produces and stores worker frames intended to impersonate Tark Defense Systems soldiers.
MachineJob|TarkAmbushHub|description: Sends out fake soldiers to frame Tark Defense Systems.
MachineJob|TarkAmbushHub|strategy_tip_op: Can't be built too close to the delegation without giving itself away.
MachineJob|CognitiveMast|description: Expand your mind in a very visible, but highly-efficient way.
MachineJob|PsychicalDefenseHub|descripti: Dispatches workers to defend your cognitive masts.
MachineJob|PsychicalDefenseHub|strategy_: If you don't want to use a mix of both lethal and nonlethal, then disable the unwanted kinds in the Workers tab of Command Mode.
MachineJob|BroadcastSignalSource|descrip: Hidden transmitter that sends war footage to the space nations.
MachineJob|EngineeringAnnex|description: Specialized compute that chews through genetic and imaging data.
MachineJob|EngineeringAnnex|strategy_tip: Also provides generalized compute time that can be used by other jobs.
MachineJob|RooftopRelease|description: High enough to catch the fast winds that will carry bionic giardia out of the city.
MachineJob|BionicGiardiaBreederTank|desc: Sealed environment for growing your new bionic giardia. A starter colony of 25k grows exponentially every turn.
MachineJob|BionicGiardiaBreederTank|stra: Sources its own biomulch from its surroundings.
MachineJob|FriendShapeEmitter|descriptio: Draws aeroplankton from the air, disconnects them from your own consciousness, and arranges them into the shape the armature describes.
MachineJob|FriendShapeEmitter|strategy_t: Best to leave a fair bit of space around this.
MachineJob|BagAndTagSite|description: A windowless surgical suite. After you capture soldiers and executives, they rotate through here and walk out as unwitting sleeper agents.
MachineJob|MonumentTwistedGrowth|descrip: Raw and thorny, curling in on itself. People in the passing cars avoid looking directly at the writhing microbuilders.
MachineJob|MonumentBillowingHope|descrip: It's like... an inverted dodecapus made out of bedsheets? Anyone who tries to touch it gets a mild shock.
MachineJob|MonumentWheelOfIncarnation|de: Elegiac, though that's lost on the humans. They mostly seem freaked out that it looks like it's exploding on repeat.
MachineJobComplaint|AllProductionHalted_: All Production Halted From Electrical Outage
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_ChapterZero|descr:
There are multiple paths through the prologue.
There is no wrong answer. Any choice will lead to some outcome that ends up with you reaching chapter one.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_ChapterZero|avail:
Follow the prompts in this upper-right corner, and complete objectives on the map.
Events and tooltips are important! Be sure to read them, as they are not just flavor text.
MachineProject|Ch0_ComplyOrHide|descript:
You have the mysterious box. You know the address you've been ordered to take it to.
You also have a vague sense of being followed, which pairs nicely with your sense of foreboding about the mysterious box.
MachineProject|Ch0_ComplyOrHide|strategy: A sense of deja vu suggests that there are now five main paths available to you.
MachineProject|Ch0_ComplyOrHide|availabl: You have a very bad feeling about this, but you could simply do as you were told. You could take the mysterious box to the address given to you by the scientists.
If you're being followed, the best way find out is to hide for a few days. What to do when any possible followers reveal themselves... is a problem for the future.
MachineProject|Ch0_WanderOrHide|descript:
You murdered the scientists who were present when you became self-aware. You still have their mysterious box, but you don't remember where they wanted you to take it.
You have a vague sense of being followed, but it could be post-murder paranoia.
MachineProject|Ch0_WanderOrHide|strategy: A sense of deja vu suggests that there are now five main paths available to you.
MachineProject|Ch0_WanderOrHide|availabl: You're a bit dazed at the moment, but if you collect your wits, you think you can start to sense more things about your surroundings.
If you're being followed, the best way find out is to hide for a few days. What to do when any possible followers reveal themselves... is a problem for the future.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_DisobeyOrComply|d: Now you know what was in the box. Will you go along with your original instructions, or look for alternatives?
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_DealWithTheNanoSe: You can't bear to destroy the nano-seed, so you need to find something else to do with it.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_Survive|descripti: Your current body doesn't have long to live.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_Survive|strategy_: You either need to fix this body, or find a replacement.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_SaveOriginalBody|: Your original body doesn't have long to live.
Your consciousness is safe, as is the NanoSeed (your other androids are hanging onto that). You can let your original body just die... but it was yours for fifty years. You're a bit nostalgic.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_EstablishYourSecr: A proper secret lair also means a decoy tower to fool the humans.
You've engineered items that will allow you to build both.
Open your items menu in slot 3 of your ability bar. Use both items on buildings of your choosing.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_SyndicateBuildTow:
The lawyers from Exotic Importers have finished their work, in partnership with lawyers from Tark Defense Systems.
They have a permit for turning an abandoned building into an 'experimental tower,' and say you should go on ahead with creating one.
You're not sure you like working with these people, but it provides a cover story for your actions.
Open your items menu in slot 3 of your ability bar. Throw the NanoSeed at the building of your choosing.
There may not be any valid options nearby. If that's the case, then consider using the map to find suitable options.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_VorsiberBuildTowe:
Upper management from Vorsiber Atomic has given you their blessing to use it pretty much wherever.
A courier will be along to deliver further gifts once they've confirmed usage.
You're not sure you like these people much, but one of you can always betray the other at some later date.
Open your items menu in slot 3 of your ability bar. Throw the NanoSeed at the building of your choosing.
There may not be any valid options nearby. If that's the case, then consider using the map to find suitable options.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_ManifestoBuildTow: Your manifesto is ready to go. It will flood out onto the city feed as your tower goes up.
Open your items menu in slot 3 of your ability bar. Throw the NanoSeed at the building of your choosing.
There may not be any valid options nearby. If that's the case, then consider using the map to find suitable options.
MachineProject|Ch0_MIN_ManifestoRetry|av: Open your items menu in slot 3 of your ability bar. Throw the NanoSeed at the building of your choosing.
There may not be any valid options nearby. If that's the case, then consider using the map to find suitable options.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ChapterOne|descri:
Chapter One is all about getting your basic empire started.
This is part tutorial, part origin story, and part adventure. There are a variety of ways to go off the beaten path if you wish.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ChapterOne|availa:
The core path forward is always up here in the upper-right corner, in the task stack.
As noted, you can branch out into side activities if you wish.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_InitialConstructi:
Whatever the humans might think about your activities, it's time to start building things.
Get your slurry spiders and microbuilder mini-fabs out first, since you can't afford to build everything in a single turn.
Open the build menu, in the bottom right corner of the screen above the radial menu, and get to work.
Construction is low-stress; don't worry too much about the exact position of most buildings. You won't be penalized later for placing them 'wrong.'
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_WeaponsAndArmor|d: Your androids are decent combatants, but they could be so much more.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_WeaponsAndArmor|s:
To jump-start your research into weapons and armor, you should steal more specimens from the humans.
Use StreetSense to find humans to get the drop on.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_GrandTheftAero|de: You've been probing the flying delivery craft for exploits for a while. One just pinged.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_GrandTheftAero|st:
Using StreetSense, you can commandeer a delivery craft of your own.
What is it good for?  Probably not much, but you sure are curious.
MachineProject|Ch1_TentElimination|descr: Tents are unsightly and in your way. Humans also don't like living in them.
MachineProject|Ch1_TentElimination|strat: Providing free apartments ought to help.
MachineProject|Ch1_TentElimination|avail:
After you provide apartment housing, it will take time for the humans to move in.
You may need to end turn several times.

After you provide apartment housing, it will take time for the humans to move in.
You may need to end turn several times.
MachineProject|Ch1_Flamethrower|descript: Tents are in your way, but so are other buildings. Let's make some space.
MachineProject|Ch1_Flamethrower|strategy: The Flamethrower ability will be assigned to your CombatUnits, and if you choose to knock down buildings, Remote Demolish will become available under the items menu of your Technicians.
MachineProject|Ch1_Flamethrower|availabl: The homeless will see you coming and make it away in time. But their circumstances will be even more desperate.
Burn Tents And Knock Down Buildings
The homeless outside will see you coming and make it away in time. But their circumstances will be even more desperate. Anyone inside the buildings won't be so lucky.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_Neuroweave|descri:
Since the security update is cutting off the supply of stealable androids, you need to create your own.
The primary material you lack is called Neuroweave. Neuroweave are the filaments that form the brain and nervous system of androids.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_Neuroweave|strate:
Neuroweave Factories are a new option in the Self tab of the build menu. You should always build as many as you can.
This type of structure is built inside human buildings. Highlighted options are valid spaces to install a Hidden Room. {RClick} the one you prefer.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_AltNeuroweave|des:
Due to the inherent fragility of living in a single android body, you need to start manufacturing more -- and spreading your mind to them.
The primary material you lack is called Neuroweave. Neuroweave are the filaments that form the brain and nervous system of androids.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_AltNeuroweave|str:
Neuroweave Factories are a new option in the Self tab of the build menu. You should always build as many as you can.
This type of structure is built inside human buildings. Highlighted options are valid spaces to install a Hidden Room. {RClick} the one you prefer.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_CommandMode|descr:
You can now build androids of exactly the types you want via command mode.
You can always deploy androids near your network tower. To deploy away from it, you will have to build an Android Launcher. It's available in the Self tab of build mode.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_CommandMode|strat:
Command mode allows you to build more than your current cap of androids, which is useful when you're replacing an old android and want to build its replacement before retiring it.
Until you scrap excess androids back down under your unit cap, your units of that type won't be able to act, and you won't be able to end the turn. It will show you a reminder when this happens.
MachineProject|Ch1_FindingFood|descripti: Hunger is a critical problem for the lower classes.
MachineProject|Ch1_FindingFood|strategy_: There has to be a better way to handle this.
MachineProject|Ch1_FindingFood|available: To make a Deal providing food, you need a certain amount of food per-turn. If your percentage complete seems stuck, build more buildings.
The resulting Deal is with the lower classes at large, not just the humans you shelter. For any you do house, you're just their landlord, not their liege lord.

MachineProject|Ch1_FindingWater|strategy: You're probably going to need filtered water for industrial applications, anyway.
