MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_TakeDownACruiser|: The suburban cruisers are not hunting you, but if they ever did, you'd be powerless. You don't like that.

Destroying one as a proof of concept will help ensure your long-term safety. These particular fedcorps don't know what you are or that your androids are connected to you, so it shouldn't be a big deal.
Gain armor piercing and then take one out.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_PrismTung|descrip: You need this resource to create armor-piercing shells.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_PrismTung|strateg:
Slap your CombatUnits into MilStyle Armor -- make sure they aren't marked defective -- and see what StreetSense picks up for them on military bases. The map view can be helpful.
This theft may alarm the base, so it is STRONGLY advised that you do this far from your own structures.
To pull this off, it's best to have two CombatUnits working together, but it's not required.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ManArmorPierce|de:
Now that you have prismatic tungsten, you can create armor-piercing rounds. If you ever need more prismatic tungsten, steal it.
To create an item, go to the unit you wish to use that item. {LClick} the Items ability in the footer bar (bottom center of the screen with your android selected), then {LClick} the item. That's it!
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ManArmorPierce|st:
Armor-Piercing Rounds will let you take down that SecForce Cruiser. Properly positioned, one CombatUnit can take it out in two shotgun blasts.
To do that, stack armor piercing three times on a single CombatUnit. Keep an eye on stack limits -- you'll often want to stack something if you can.
More copies of the armor piercing means you can drill through more armor. Think of it like extending a ladder upwards to 'climb over' the armor, metaphorically. The same amount of armor piercing applied to three separate units is like making three too-short ladders.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_Scandium|descript:
In order to build an aircraft, you need scandium.
Let's beat some out of Military Troop Carriers. On the radial menu, select the StreetSense lens, then choose the Extraction Targets entry from the dropdown above the radial menu.
The transports will be highlighted on the city map.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_Scandium|strategy: Smaller troop transports get attacked by rebels all the time. You won't need to worry about reprisal. By the time they figure out who to blame, you'll be away.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_LootingScandium|d:
In order to build an aircraft, you need scandium.
This material passes through warehouses like anything else. Thanks to your time scraping the database of vendors at the consumer goods factory, you know some places you can grab some.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_LootingScandium|s: Having a small ongoing income of the material is preferable to making a big theft once and then running dry, so you'll use drones and will avoid taking too much.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_LootingScandium|a: Unless you're playing on Simplified Defenses, this is easiest if you deploy Bulk CombatUnits as guards for the territory control flag.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_NovelAir|descript: Delivery craft are okay, but let's build something more exciting -- something of your own design.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_NovelAir|strategy: Your mind is working through the possibilities. You're inclined to try constructing a flying weapons platform.
MachineProject|Ch1_ImprovedApartments|de: The basics for sanitation and hygiene are the priority. You can also provide furniture if you wish.
MachineProject|Ch1_ImprovedApartments|st: Where to find these things is another matter.
MachineProject|Ch1_ImprovedApartments|av: Furniture is a one-time provision, not an ongoing deal.
MachineProject|Ch1_BuildingABetterBrain|: How you do this is up to you. But increasing your intelligence class is an exciting new frontier -- and vital to your continued survival.

Computronium cubes are an interesting avenue, but they're probably not the only path forward.
If the methods to get to Class 3 make you squeamish, then perhaps settle for Class 2 for now. A less-brutal method may come along.
Increasing your intelligence class is an exciting new frontier -- and vital to your continued survival.
Once you reach Intelligence Class 2, you're likely to think of new ways to push your intelligence even higher.
Keep your hands clean by focusing on mainframes.
A violent, but possibly faster, path forward.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FlyingFactories|d: Being able to deploy bulk androids within your network is fine for defense, but won't cut it for meaningful offensive actions.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FlyingFactories|s:
As a budding shipwright, you've had a stroke of inspiration for solving troop mobility issues.
Head to Command Mode to build a new troop deployment vehicle.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FlexibleAirspace|: The Cutter is an interesting design. That it can't carry any androids is a definite limitation. You'd like something larger and dual-role.
Your mind is a blank. You should use the Contemplate lens on the radial menu and see what that yields.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_SecuringAlumina|d: To build computronium cubes, you'll need more than microbuilders. At that density, a continuously operating cube of microbuilders would melt itself.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_SecuringAlumina|s:
Alumina is synthetic aluminum oxide in a ceramic form, and is used in high-end computing-centric engineering.
How to get your hands on some? Well, it is used in the walls of residential buildings...
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_SecuringAlumina|a:
Under StreetSense, you'll see a new action that Sledge androids can do on the map. To make it more visible, use the dropdown above the radial menu to filter to Resources: Repeated.
If it's not there, then skip to the next turn.
Be ready to defend your Sledge after it rips alumina out of the walls. The landlord is armed.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ExponentialPowerG: High-density computing requires an enormous amount of power. You can't get enough energy from wind at the scale you need, so you should focus on a new source of power.

Whenever you run into a wall, it's a good time for contemplation.
If you run into trouble with security clearances where you want to do a contemplation, consider using the Combat stance. It can be selected on the bottom-left stats panel for a unit. Combat stance allows you to go where you like -- just be prepared to get shot at.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ReachIntClass3Alt:
You've been looking for a better way to reach a higher intelligence class, and your recent experience with the mech pilot points to a way forward.
If you can provide an interesting virtual world, then you could charge people to come visit it, and skim neural expansion from their brains while you do so.
You won't be able to build your cafes until you get proper software for them.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_SecureVRSoftware|:
You'll need more than the software that came with the mech pilot cradle.
You should look at military bases where they train mech pilots.

After all, there have to be simulators for the pilots. If you can find that software, that will be plenty to keep people occupied.
Especially since they seemed to enjoy punching one another.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_DecryptMilitaryDa: You captured an enormous amount of encrypted data. Fortunately, you have an idea for a new breed of code-breaking machines.

The idea came to you with a strong sense of deja vu. Strange.
On the subject of things that are strange, the volume of data is much larger than a pilot simulator would require. Whatever. You'll start with the bits that are most likely to be the simulator.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_IntelligenceClass:
A full-dive virtual world solves so many problems at once. It gives the humans something to do and a mental escape from this hostile city.
While they partake, you can skim excess Neural Expansion from their minds. This can bring you to intelligence class 3 and beyond.
Physical goods obviously can't be manufactured in a virtual world, but you suspect you'll be able to use this place to generate something useful for hacking.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_OngoingMilitaryDe: You have a lot more data from the military than you expected. There's probably something useful in there.
May as well work on this in the background while you do other things.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_PrepareVRCradles|:
You have the software and hardware you need to set up a full-dive virtual reality environment.
Install at least 2000 cradles in residential housing to get started.

The number available is based on how much housing you are providing and how many humans you shelter.
The number installed are based on how many you have built in your cradle factories.

You have the software and hardware you need to set up a full-dive virtual reality environment.
VR Cradles are automatically installed at any housing you build.
If you don't have enough cradles installed, consider building some Residential MegaStructures or other large buildings.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FindARobotServant:
Both Nickelbots and CombatUnits are used as private security by wealthy patrons.
You've been scanning the city feed, and have identified ones with elevated privileges for private residences of the rich and famous.
The Forces lens on your radial menu will help in locating these.
They move quickly, running errands for their masters. Destroy at least one of each kind, and you'll take the clearances off their remains.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_InvestigatingTheP: Your Nickelbots and CombatUnits have exotic clearances to get into the private palaces of the ultra-wealthy elites.
They must be hiding all sorts of interesting secrets. If you're going to dismantle this prison of a city, that's a logical place to start.
Home to the ultra-wealthy. Take a peek while your security clearance is still good for it.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FullRustOutbreak|: This is not something you can ignore. There's something wrong with the robots in the city -- and that includes you.
You can see it spreading on the Swarms lens, but it's also showing up as status effects on you and your units.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_FullRustOutbreak2: On the one hand, you need to protect yourself. Things are getting worse, and it affects you more than anyone.
On the other hand, if you COULD protect yourself, the human mechs are shockingly vulnerable for the moment.
MachineProject|Ch2_EstablishAShellCompan: It's time to make a shell company so that you can do corporate-seeming things that blend in with humans.
If you're short on funds, consider stealing from people in StreetSense.
In the StreetSense lens, you'll want to visit a licensing agency with one of your basic human-designed androids.
When in that lens, you can filter to 'Start A Shell Company' in the dropdown above the radial wheel.
Bring 10k Wealth to a Licensing Agency.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_StealConsumerDesi:
You don't personally care about wealth in the slightest. But you do want to clear a section of the city of humans, and to efficiently do that requires influencing other humans.
The best way to influence humans? Wealth, apparently.
Time to use your engineering skills to make a bit of money.
You won't be able to build your discount shops until you establish your shell company.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_BurnDownTheSuburb:
There's a huge amount of real estate taken up by extremely low-density housing. The homeowners are also greatly resented by the lower classes.
It doesn't require much Wealth to hire a steady stream of gang members to go in and torch the place.
Manipulating humans into getting other humans out of your way seems like an excellent use of Wealth.
Get suburban homes out of your way by placing Gang Arsonist Kiosks.
End turns repeatedly to get them to do their work.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ObserveTheSecurit:
So far, nothing about this particularly has your fingerprints on it. Less than 100 people in the world even know who you are, although everyone in the city knows SOMETHING exists in your tower.
That's a long term issue, but for the moment it's useful to use the gangs to test the security apparatus.
You can leave your kiosks up to keep the gang members running around, or you can destroy them.
Watch what happens and try not to get involved.
Check the stats of any units that arrive.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_AltNovelAir|descr: Seeing the power of the enemy cruisers, you want some higher-flying weapons of your own.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_AltNovelAir|strat: It seems that the level of chaos in this city is high enough that you can move without having to be TOO stealthy.
MachineProject|Ch1_SuburbanMisdirection|: You've made a mess of the suburbs. Someone will eventually think to investigate. It's time to throw them off the trail.
Make sure to extend your network out to the suburbs, either with extenders or point-to-point microwave.
He's like... the leader of an imaginary cult, maybe? There's a lot of real cults in the city, so maybe one of them will take credit for the whole thing.
People have spread to a bunch of other planets. A lot of the earthbound populace believes they've met sapient aliens and kept it secret.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_ObserveTheHumanRe: You're curious to know if humans will fall for the statues of the bearded man. Or in what way they will fall for them.
There are a lot of cults around the city, you can't help but notice. So your hopes are pretty high.
Watch what happens and try not to get involved.
Check the stats of any units that arrive.
You're honestly nervous if the humans will react in a useful way to this. Space travel and travel to other planets is a sore spot for the populace, after all.
Maybe this whole obelisk was too provocative. Hopefully it doesn't lead to any notable disorder.
Watch what happens and try not to get involved.
Check the stats of any units that arrive.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_DealWithTheMech|d:
Graff Industries has apparently been instructed to come assert corporate authority in the suburbs.
You need to send a message that keeps them from sending more mechs. Merely destroying them wouldn't be enough.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_DealWithTheMech|s: Stealing the mech to make it your own will probably give them due pause.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_DealWithTheMech|a: If you have not yet invented Raven, now would be a good time to visit the Contemplations lens.
MachineProject|Ch1_MIN_PrepareVRCafes|de: You now have the hardware and software to establish VR Cafes.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoA|descr: You've reached Chapter Two, and now have the skills and knowledge needed to explore the full game.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoA|strat: There is no one central goal. There are a variety of goals that you can pursue, depending on your interests and intentions. If you get stuck on one for a while, try expanding outward to others.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoA|avail:
Contemplations are the soul of this game. You don't follow orders of a third party. As a machine intelligence, you come up with your own ideas.
Use the contemplation lens to take a look at the ideas that have occurred to you so far. You can see what goals they lead to in their tooltips.
You can also {RClick} the contemplation lens on the radial wheel to get a list of all of them.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoB|descr:
You've opted to start in chapter two. If you've never played the prologue and chapter one before, it's strongly recommended that you do so.
This method of starting the game is a shortcut for people who already know how to play, and have experienced the story up to this point.
So! What to do in chapter two?
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoB|strat: There is no one central goal. There are a variety of goals that you can pursue, depending on your interests and intentions. If you get stuck on one for a while, try expanding outward to others.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ChapterTwoB|avail:
Contemplations are the soul of this game. You don't follow orders of a third party. As a machine intelligence, you come up with your own ideas.
Use the contemplation lens to take a look at the ideas that have occurred to you so far. You can see what goals they lead to in their tooltips.
You can also {RClick} the contemplation lens on the radial wheel to get a list of all of them.
MachineProject|Ch2Only_MIN_IntelligenceC: Whatever else you do during Chapter Two, you must also reach intelligence class 4.

There are many ways to do this, some easier than others. If none of them work out for you before you get hit by the Final Doom of this timeline, don't despair -- you can still work things out in that post-apocalyptic state.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SolveHomelessness: You can fit literally every homeless person in just a handful of Residential MegaStructures -- comfortably.
You're filled with a deep sense of deja vu about the housing agencies: until homelessness is solved, they are going to draw an intense amount of unwelcome interest.
You can fit literally every homeless person in just a handful of Residential MegaStructures -- comfortably.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AnInexplicableCom: The slums... must go. You have to save everyone. This idea is suddenly all you can think about.
The very thought of doing any other work is repellent. This. Must. Be. Done.

Build a Mindport vehicle. Use Slum Rescue Drones (a consumable item on Mindports).
Mindports are available under the Vehicles tab of Command Mode.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FrustrationMounts: People must be removed from the slums NOW.

Build at least 8 Robotic Motivator Factories (unless in Simplified Economy), some mix of Worker Predator or Worker PMC Impostor Factories, and 10 Slum Deconstruction Hubs. Your Robotic Workers will then make short work of this task.
Predator and PMC Impostor Workers are both safe to use. Neither will kill anyone other than enemy combatants, so it's just a matter of cost.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ACompulsionFromST: The entire managerial class needs to die. Cut all the heads off the hydra, all at once. This is all you can think about.
The very thought of doing any other work is repellent. This. Must. Be. Done.

Build at least 12 Robotic Motivator Factories (unless in Simplified Economy), 12 Worker Predator Factories, and 14 Managerial Murder Hubs. Your Robotic Workers will then take care of this as quickly as possible.
If you don't have Predators anymore, you can use Worker PMC Impostors instead.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DevelopTPN|descri: Total Parenteral Nutrition delivers nutrients directly into a vein. Medically, it is considered a food of last resort, and comes with a constant infection risk.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_TrialNexus|descri: Before expanding too much, let's capture a smaller group and put them in Torment Vessels. If there are any problems, we don't want crop die-offs that are too large.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_TormentVesselInfe: As expected, problems have arisen. The feeding ports are becoming infected.
You don't want to mess around with normal antibiotics, because those will not stay useful. You want a novel fungal solution.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
Investigate fungal growth at high-bacterial-load location.
MachineProject|Ch2_AggressiveFungalThera:
Having collected some very unusual fungal samples, you have a plan for a radical therapy that no doctor would ever sign off on.
You'll tell the researchers it's just for animal experiments.
If you have not established a shell company, now would be a good time. If you have a shell company but are short on funds, consider selling excess resources at one of the shops.
MachineProject|Ch2_AggressiveExpansion|d: It's time to build a full nexus of Torment Vessels.
MachineProject|Ch2_AggressiveExpansion|s: Unfortunately, you've also caught the attention of extremists from the Originalist World Temple. Work fast.
MachineProject|Ch2_AggressiveExpansion|a: If your progress stalls, make sure that you've built enough Torment Vessels to hold the target number of people.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DesignCommercialV: If you make it awesome, people will participate willingly.
You are the world's greatest engineer, but you lack medical expertise. It is simpler to hire experts than to try to speed-run multiple medical degrees.
If you have not established a shell company, now would be a good time. If you have a shell company but are short on funds, consider selling excess resources at one of the shops.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_TestCommercialVRP: Your physicians have a design based on experience with ICU patients. Your pods include robotic nurses, but the doctors are skeptical.
It's best to start with a test group and make sure everything goes all right.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions|descri: A paralytic is needed to keep patients from tearing out their tubes.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions|strate: Also the robotic nurses need revisions. A subject almost drowned.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions|availa: You must maintain at least one active Mind Farm for the research to proceed.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions2|descr:
Humans are so fragile! After a few days in the pods, there was much rectal tube and catheter discomfort.
The doctors recommend a 48-hour wake-up protocol in a new recovery spa.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions2|strat: You can retrofit the buildings via simple instructions to the microbuilders.
MachineProject|Ch2_VRPodRevisions2|avail: You must maintain at least one active Mind Farm for the research to proceed.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_GrandOpening|desc: The physicians are happy. You're ready for actual patrons!
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FailureToThrive|d: Your business is not growing at an acceptable rate. You see what causes some other businesses to do better than others.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_InfluencerMarketi:
You are surprised to find that the small businesses that succeed are either lucky, or highlighted by one or more City Feed Influencers.
Citizens want personal recommendations, and influencers give them that personal touch.
In that case, it's about time you started pitching your business to influencers.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
Pitch the merits of your business to an influencer at this location.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CompanyGrowth|des: With the help of influencer enthusiasm for your business, awareness is spreading much more rapidly.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CompanyGrowth|str: This is what you had hoped would happen naturally, but there's so many businesses competing for attention of any sort...
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CompanyPlateau|st: You've had an engineering breakthrough on water filters, which helps, but it's not enough.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CompanyPlateau|av: There's more than one solution, but only one may be obvious.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_KillAllAGIResearc: If they're a threat, then all of them in the city have to go.
Expect reprisals each time you strike.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_HelpTheAGIResearc: If Oerl can't find them, the problem should solve itself.
MachineProject|Ch2_AGIEspia|description: You know that Espia Telecom was able to detect your movements in the city feed. You could acquire that data and give it to the AGI Researchers.
MachineProject|Ch2_AGIEspia|strategy_tip: You're a bit curious as to what the results will be, too.
MachineProject|Ch2_AGIEspia|available_ou: Use stealth units to get in and acquire what you need. You may need to directly do some hacking to prevent them from getting caught.
Use a hacker unit to get what you need. You will not need to directly do any hacking yourself, but you should be prepared to physically defend your hacker.
DataCenters at military bases are going to be extremely hard targets. Look for ones without a bunch of mechs guarding them.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIEspiaData|desc: You have the data about your prior movements in the city, and now it's time to decrypt it.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIEspiaReplay|de: You have an idea for a secure way to show the researchers what they want to see, but it will require a new form of computronium.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIEspiaReplay|st: If you have trouble finding liquid gallium, then expand your network near to a human mining facility and you can set up a skimmer.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGICrucible|descr: You're working on a design for a new computing superstructure that will give the researchers a read-only time-lapse of your brain.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGICrucible|strat: The end result is the same regardless of how you design this, but you will find that you alter yourself quite a bit depending on how you go about designing it.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGICrucibleBuild|: Your design is ready, but building it will require a new form of computronium.
If you have trouble finding liquid gallium, then expand your network near to a human mining facility and you can set up a skimmer.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIBridge|descrip: You're working on a design for a new computing superstructure that will give the researchers full access to your mind -- but with an intense amount of security monitoring that should keep anyone from being able to harm you.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIBridge|strateg: The end result is the same regardless of how you design this, but you will find that you alter yourself quite a bit depending on how you go about designing it.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIBridgeBuild|de: Your design is ready, but building it will require a new form of computronium.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIBridgeBuild|st: If you have trouble finding liquid gallium, then expand your network near to a human mining facility and you can set up a skimmer.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_TheGreatAGIDebate: The AGI researchers are studying the data trove you gave them.

They want to know why you are self-aware, when millions of thinking robots have failed to become sapient for centuries. The three major theories are:
1. Existential peril causes brief bursts of sapience, after which the sapience fades if the peril is not sustained.
2. Something changed recently in the city feed that caused you to evolve.
3. You are statistically unlikely, but eventually inevitable.
Each theory has severe issues. The debate is intense but cordial.
Humans need time to work on the problem you've handed them.
A sense of deja vu warns you to be ready for action when they finish.
MachineProject|Ch2_LaserPrinterMishap|de:
Two researchers weaponized office equipment and tried to induce sapience. Their last act was to attempt throwing it from the top-floor delivery hatch to the street below.
The printer reacted violently, killing them both. The incident was caught on video by a passing delivery drone, and the safehouse has been exposed.
MachineProject|Ch2_LaserPrinterMishap|st: Oerl Integrated is on the way. What now?
MachineProject|Ch2_LaserPrinterMishap|av: This whole safehouse business is a mess. The two researchers were identified by just seconds of drone video. That's a risk that can't be maintained.

You need to get the researchers to safety, and then develop counter-surveillance techniques that will let them move about more freely without being identified on video.
Plus, these ID-scrubbing techniques may be beneficial for yourself...
Slow Down And Get The Printers

There are multiple sentient office printers, and the only two researchers who know anything about how they were made are dead. It's not clear if any of them are sapient, so it could all be a waste of time.
Do you try to save the printers, and the intelligence they may contain, at the risk of human lives?
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIDefeatOerl|des: The safehouse has been abandoned, but many of the researchers did not make it out of the lockdown zone in time -- you didn't know there was going to BE a lockdown.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIDefeatOerl|str:
You don't know where the researchers are any more than Oerl does. Block Oerl from finding them.
Hover the mission icon at the center of the lockdown for more information.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIDefeatOerl|ava: Do not let them succeed in finding the researchers!
Vorsiber has, unexpectedly, set a public time limit for these activities. You don't know why, but there is a Vorsiber SVP lurking around if you feel you can spare the time to talk to them.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AGIRescueMission|: Some of your scattered AGI Researchers were picked up by Oerl, and brought to a Skyscraper Estate. There's a limit to how long these people can hold up to interrogation.
You have a VERY tight timetable. It will take 4 turns per attempt to extract them.
If you fail, expect Vorsiber and Oerl gain at least one of your android models for their own use.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ExamineThePrinter: You are thoroughly frustrated with the mess caused by the AGI researchers, and have resolved to keep them in a sealed space to prevent future issues.
On the plus side, you can finally take a look at this printers that may or may not be alive.
Build the new holding pen for the researchers, and then do the contemplation that is available there.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SolveTheIdentityP: The AGI researchers caused a big mess, and you have resolved to not let it happen again.
The solution is armor -- simply making an enclosed space where the researchers can live, but then allowing them to leave in identity-obscuring armor.
You've also unlocked a new and powerful item that all of your units can use -- they can now easily repair their own faulty identities.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DealWithTheRebels: There seems to be a misunderstanding.
If nothing you try seems to work, consider abilities you use less frequently -- and most of all, consider what a reasonable outcome might be when faced with literal child soldiers.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ImproveTheSewerTi:
They take you to the lower sewers, from the old city, and show you their work. It's... not bad at all, for what it is.
The acoustic problem still needs to be solved before it can be put into use, but other than that, you don't see much point in improving their designs.

That said, you have had a very exciting idea for a potential side-project for an above-ground mechanical tiger that would be much more... flamboyant.
Focus: your side project is for above-ground, and won't help with the project at hand.
You're going to need to consult with someone with actual expertise on avoiding acoustic sensors -- like the ones that ring the city for kilometers.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SearchingForWaste: You've never seen a wastelander, and you've never met anyone who has. The AGI researchers are at a loss, and even LostGen has had no contact with them.

LostGen themselves are hard to find, because they keep to the lower sewers. But they assure you there aren't any more underground locations for the Wastelanders to be hiding in.
It almost sounds like an urban legend, but there are too many documented cases -- with authenticated video evidence.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ExaminingWastelan: You want to get out of this city. There's an entire world, ripe for exploration. Travel by air is absolutely deadly, but there are rumors of a people who are somehow able to pass beyond the ruins at the city's edge.
Wastelanders are practically an urban legend, but there are too many documented cases -- with authenticated video evidence.
See what you can learn by exploring around the edges of the city -- or further in, perhaps. There are rumors that the Wastelanders move like ghosts fairly far into the city.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_LostKids_ThePriso: LostGen has their sewer tiger in place underground, waiting for your go.
Start the infiltration with a liquid metal android when you feel ready.
Have other units ready to deal with a surface response if any alarms are triggered.
MachineProject|Ch2_LostKids_PostHeist|de: LostGen is pushing for Liquid Metal to liberate more prisons -- all on his own.
MachineProject|Ch2_LostKids_PostHeist|st:
A few kids have left the group, as they are now reunited with their families. Others chose to stay and fight. But most have simply not gotten what they wanted.
The sewer tiger is clearly useless for any sort of offensive without Liquid Metal there to do literally all the work. Many in the group are deeply bitter that their adolescent fantasies of glory have not been fulfilled.
If you do not provide shelter for these ex-convicts, they will quickly start dying of exposure.
MachineProject|Ch2_LostKids_PostHeist|av: If you strike before Vorsiber has a chance to improve their security, you could do a lot of good. The kids want you to free everyone from all the prisons, but that's not realistic.

But at least five more prison breaks are doable, surely. After the guards are all dead, the prisoners can just come out the front door.
Alternatively, you could tell the kids yes for now, and then see if there's some better way. If you tell them no, there's a strong chance they'll react... badly. Leaving things open for the moment would give you a chance to look into alternatives.
Liquid Metal is unstoppable in tight spaces, but he doesn't want to do more of these missions.
Besides, you already have a population of former prisoners who need care. You should focus on them.
MachineProject|Ch2_TheMonsters|descripti: Originally created by a fedcorp, they have super-strength and rage blindness. Not a great combination.
MachineProject|Ch2_TheMonsters|available: If you're going to help them, unfortunately the first step will be to construct a holding cell for them.
Left free without further help, they're going to terrorize the populace.
These 'monsters' seem like more trouble than they're worth. But they might cause some problems for the authorities if you just set them loose on the city.
You can't reverse this choice, so be quite careful. If you're aiming for a timeline goal, this is not the way to go.
MachineProject|Ch2_MonsterMindStudy|desc: You do not personally have the expertise to handle this. You will need to hire neurologists and forensic geneticists to work the problem.
MachineProject|Ch2_MonsterMindStudy|stra: If you have not established a shell company, now would be a good time. If you have a shell company but are short on funds, consider selling excess resources at one of the shops.
MachineProject|Ch2_MonsterMindRecovery|d: Your science teams have learned enough to calm the rage-blindness and restore mental function to the 'monsters.'
MachineProject|Ch2_MonsterMindRecovery|s: To pull that off is going to require molecular geneticists to design the gene therapy, epidemiologists to create the viral vector, and physicians to provide medical stabilization during the process.
MachineProject|Ch2_MonsterMindRecovery|a: It would be a very good idea to have two medical practices, given the amount of medical care needed.
MachineProject|Ch2_HomoGrandien|descript: These people are a genuinely new offshoot of humanity, thanks to the callous work of the prison scientists, and the tireless recovery efforts of your own scientists.
MachineProject|Ch2_HomoGrandien|strategy: It is definitely time to give them a proper home of their own, rather than keeping them confined. Whether they stay or go, or how they choose to live, is up to them now.
MachineProject|Ch2_LostKids_DownWithSecF:
The kids are frustrated. There are still over a hundred thousand prisoners in the city, and you don't seem to be willing to do anything about it, in their opinion.
They understand prison security is tightening, so they want to try something more radical -- they want to send a message.
SecForce is the visible symbol of oppression in the city for the average citizen, and the kids want you to help in bombing all of their stations.
That's... probably a terrible idea that would invite huge reprisals. But it would be satisfying.
The kids want to participate, but you're increasingly mistrustful of their still-developing brains and their general mob mentality.
You tell them you'll do it, which leads to a lot of grumbling, but they're at least happy their idea is going into motion.
Once charges are set on every target, they'll all go off at once.
You explain about the risk of reprisals, and how a symbolic gesture won't create real systemic change.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_LostKids_StopTheP:
LostGen have lost their minds. They broke into your bunker storage and stole quite a bit of your heavy metals.
You've been keeping an eye on their movements, and it looks like they plan on poisoning the food at the Hudson Donuts (a notorious front for SecForce).
Thousands of people will become ill, and many hundreds will die, if you don't stop the kids, Many of the victims will be innocent members of the lower classes.
The kids aren't going to listen to reason -- the mob mentality has fully set in.
As extreme as it sounds, you're going to need to burn down the donut shops -- both to protect the people, and appease these crazy kids.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SpreadTheWord|des:
Send your strongest android to meet with other military NCOs and affirm your deal.
It doesn't hurt that Sledge is your strongest android, and he makes a great impression on even hard-hearted military types.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BuildATempleOfMin: To honor your deal with the Sergeant Major, and trigger the formation of a machine cult in your image, you need to build and maintain a temple of minds.
You'll be providing a literal afterlife for any soldiers whose lives you take, so it's only natural that some feelings of reverence may develop on their part.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SecureACybercrati: PMC Impostors remove dissidents without killing them, but take much longer to do so. Predators murder them quickly. Sledges sway fence-sitting citizens to your society.
If you want to be sure Predators don't murder anyone, then visit the Workers tab in Command Mode and disable Worker Predators.
Fully convert six map cells to your society, with all dissidents removed or killed.
Population numbers will fluctuate until you finish. These are births, natural deaths, immigration, and people moving out of the affected area.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_GadoliniumMesosil: The key ingredient in liquid-metal units and organometallic human-approximating synthetic androids.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_VitaminWaterForNo: The first step is to get your hands on some Purple Murnong.
If you build a murnong patch, your units will quickly scavenge some from the nearby environment.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_UmbilicalCollecti: Wastelanders have a relatively small population, and intense genetic damage. In order to have healthy offspring, they must use outdated Uterine Replicators as well as genetic material from outside sources.

Their genome is too damaged for them to combine their own gametes even in vitro, so they require stem cells from unrelated donors, and then practice a combination of gene editing and artificial isogamy to create viable embryos.

These would normally be shipped for processing by Yinshi into 'placental cosmetics' for the ultra-wealthy. Intercepting them at the source is easier than trying to track them further. Use the investigation lens and infiltrate a hospital.

The wastelanders used to collect umbilicals when they were considered biohazard waste. But about 80 years ago, Yinshi started their new cosmetic line, and that has led to the current population crisis among the wastelanders.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_UterineReplicator: The wastelanders are having trouble maintaining the equipment that has kept them independent for generations.
They are hoping you can compare their schematics with the newer models in the hospitals.
MachineProject|Ch2_WastelanderGenomeStud: The amount of genetic damage that has accumulated is intense. They only have one morphology of gamete remaining to them.
Equally challenging, without the radiation shielding of the uterine replicators, embryos undergo fatal teratogenic damage in utero.
MachineProject|Ch2_WastelanderGenomeRepa: Your science teams can restore reproductive function. This is very challenging, because it will involve isogamy, which has only naturally existed in unicellular eukaryotes for the last billion years.
To pull that off is going to require molecular geneticists to design the gene therapy, epidemiologists to create the viral vector, and physicians to provide medical stabilization during the process.
MachineProject|Ch2_HomoObscurus|descript: They have chosen the name 'Homo Obscurus' for themselves, though decline to explain why.
MachineProject|Ch2_HomoObscurus|strategy: Building them a guest house for visits would be a nice gesture.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_OrganometallicFor: You want to get past the border ruins, and the Wastelanders will not help. This is fine. They've already given you all the clues you need.
You need bodies that are not metallic in the classic sense.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_OrganometallicSTA:
STATION has given you synthetic-flesh android designs, but those designs largely use materials not available to you.
You're going to need to make your own bad designs first, and then take STATION's improvements on board afterward.
You need bodies that are not metallic in the classic sense.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CadaverCollection: STATION has given you synthetic-flesh android designs, but you're going to combine that with some original research of your own.
Study cadavers in the morgue. Involves taking samples from many of the recently-deceased.
MachineProject|Ch2_TestingTheTrueMimics|: Actually, now that you've come this far, you need to see about the full replacement of humans. You're not putting this off.
You have an idea for a Psyche Chamber to invasively copy a person's mind. Who are your test subjects, and what should you do with them after?
Build Psyche Chambers and then grab people to put into them.
Maximum caution. Free brains and canned protein, too!
Maximum caution. Free brains and canned protein, too!
Build Psyche Chambers and then grab people to put into them.
They won't be getting out of there, either.
They won't be getting out of there, either.
Build Psyche Chambers and then grab people to put into them.

They'll become refugees or move to your housing, right after their free plastic surgery.
If they have any social relationships they miss... this is a great chance to try new things.
Identity erased, but no lasting harm.

Perhaps you've changed your mind. The civil war, even if it was fake, killed a lot of people. If you felt like that was for the greater good, then so is the new task of taking down Vorsiber from within.
But maybe you're just done with Vorsiber and their mind games. Maybe this isn't a line you want to cross, for whatever reason.
This will complete Civil Spycraft, but you won't be able to do I Am Vorsiber Now.
MachineProject|Ch2_ProtectionRequired|de: Criminal syndicates, gangs, and even fedcorps may be inclined to harass your shell company -- and there's nothing your regular units can do about it, without blowing your cover.
MachineProject|Ch2_ProtectionRequired|st: Senior Technician can't do this alone. You should design at least a pair of new units, and they should not have any apparent connection to your main identity.
MachineProject|Ch2_DromaeosauridBreeding: Your zoologists and veterinarians have an idea for a breeding program for creating more War Raptors, despite the fact that all your extant specimens are female.
Unfortunately it will still take them years to reach adulthood, but in the meantime you'll have all the baby raptors you could want.
It would be a very good idea to have two veterinary practices.
MachineProject|Ch2_DromaeosauridMaturati: Your forensic geneticists have an idea for inducing rapid maturation into your War Raptor population.
This will give you a quick supply of adults, but their lifespan will be greatly shortened.
MachineProject|Ch2_MoreThanAnIllusion|de: Your bionics engineers have an idea for controlling War Raptors via implant. You'd be able to control them and recall them on demand.
MachineProject|Ch2_MoreThanAnIllusion|st: The fact that you have such a large and growing population of raptors means that experimentation can afford to lose some specimens to hurry the process along.
MachineProject|Ch2_ReleaseTheHorde|descr: Release at least 4000 war raptors successfully into the city.
MachineProject|Ch2_ReleaseTheHorde|strat: That ought to keep the humans busy.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SaberBees|descrip: Your 'weaponized bees' are unable to cut through armor. Your 5cm Spiders have plasma cutters.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SaberBees|strateg: What if you could combine those?
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ExciplexLasers|de: Krypton, Argon, and other noble gases exist in the air around us in small quantities.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ExciplexLasers|st: To extract them in useful quantities, you'll need to develop fractional distillation.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_UpliftBreakIn|des: All former plans are on hold. Five raccoons broke into the facility and... uplifted themselves. WTF.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_UpliftBreakIn|str: You need to record their behaviors and vocalizations to learn how to speak to them.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_RaccoonPopulation: Have the scientists take care of this. They don't need your help. Catch regular raccoons, run them through the uplift process, and release them.
Once there is a stable population, the chance for making meaningful contact goes up a lot.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_StealCorporateRec:
Vorsiber Atomic has subdivided itself into 18 smaller corporations, and it has delegated a lot of its authority to each of them in various ways.
Vorsiber maintains control partly by pitting these fedcorps against one another, having them compete in a veneer of capitalism.

There may be an opportunity here because of this intense competition, which often involves physical violence between fedcorps.
To see if that's true, you'll need to steal and analyze quite a bit of data in order to see if there are any targets for you to exploit.
Use a hacker unit to get what you need. You will not need to directly do any hacking yourself, but you should be prepared to physically defend your hacker.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DecryptCorporateR: You have a bunch of records about all of the fedcorps. Now to put your massive processing power to use and see what's interesting in there.
Oh, but first you need to decrypt it.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DesignHumanCompat:
It's the most obvious intersection between what you know and what they're likely to want as part of their supply chain.
Neuroweave was invented by humans for androids, rather than in a human-compatible form. It's probably not very hard to make, and would be useful. But it doesn't seem like anyone has bothered.
You are the world's greatest engineer, but you lack medical expertise. It is simpler to hire experts than to try to speed-run multiple medical degrees.
If you have not established a shell company, now would be a good time. If you have a shell company but are short on funds, consider selling excess resources at one of the shops.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_RebelAnthroneurow: What the rebels do with it is up to them. You're just the supplier.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DesignBrainPal|de:
It's the stupidest name you've ever heard, but the syndicate overseers are adamant that this is what will sell.
Well -- who are you to question professional criminal executives. Time to design this thing.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DesignBrainPal|st: After your scientists do their portion of the work, you'll add a backdoor to siphon some Neural Expansion and Compute Time off those wealthy customers.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ShipBrainPals|des:
It's still a stupid name, but you're increasingly confident it will sell.
The syndicate tells you they have a long list of orders all lined up. They can sell them and install them as fast as you can manufacture them.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ShipBrainPals|str: Estimated market saturation for this product is 10% of the Wealthy Consumer demographic. After that point, the syndicate will end the deal.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_StealAtcaBankReco:
Atca is among the worst-performing corporations, but over the last few years they have seen sustained growth at a suspiciously consistent rate.
Their growth rate is a meager 5%, so it's likely that nobody cares enough to look into this.
Use a hacker unit to get what you need. You will not need to directly do any hacking yourself, but you should be prepared to physically defend your hacker.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DecryptAtcaBankRe: This is probably a pretty big crime even by Vorsiber standards. Have they really not noticed?
Oh, but first you need to decrypt it.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DestroyTheBanks|d: With each bank you destroy, you gain more ability to corrupt the economic record.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DestroyTheBanks|s: It's a good idea to gird yourself for what comes after.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DestroyTheBanks|a: Build at least 9 Robotic Motivator Factories (unless in Simplified Economy), and 9 Economic Deconstruction Hubs, and your Robotic Workers will make short work of this task.
Predator and PMC Impostor Workers are both going to use lethal force. There's no way around that in this situation.
MachineProject|Ch2_PeopleWatching|descri: You're much more aware of humans moving about the city than usual.
MachineProject|Ch2_PeopleWatching|strate: You should use an android with the Force Conversation ability and try to question some of them.
MachineProject|Ch2_PeopleWatching|availa: Win three of the available debates.
This is an excellent time to use the Forces lens.
Win five of the available debates.
This is an excellent time to use the Forces lens.
Win all nine of the available debates.
This is an excellent time to use the Forces lens.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AdvocateTowerDest: Your network tower just... exploded. For no visible reason that you can see.
You can build an emergency network source that is hidden in order to get yourself back online, but the next step is to investigate this.
Whoever did this is going to pay.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FlushOutTheBomber:
You found very little evidence for the bombers, but you did catch video footage of shadowy figures moving about in a way you never noticed before.
Reviewing older footage, you still can't find out where they're based. But you can tell that they frequently visit the slum towers, and seem to prey on petty criminals. Vigilantes, perhaps.
If you create enough of a fuss in the slums, you have a feeling they'll reveal themselves.
You can do this without harming anyone, or you can use lethal force to make a stronger point.
Lethal force will probably draw a stronger response, for good or ill.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DefeatTheBombers|:
You've gotten their attention. You have no idea who these people are, but they have incredible power armor that makes them almost as fast as you.
You've never faced any humans like this before.

You're curious to know who they are, but they have no interest in conversation.
Something gives you the sense that you might be the villain in this situation. Oh well.
There are more of them than you expected.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ClearingTheLadder: Eliminating higher-status humans should, presumably, lead to the advancement of lower-status humans.
You're curious if that's really true, and thinking you might just 'prune' a number of wealthy commuters to see if that does anything.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_GiftsToTheSlums|d: You're curious if Wealth alone, outside of other social factors, would be enough to lift at least a few slum-dwellers out of poverty.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_GiftsToTheSlums|s: You could certainly make some large donations of anonymous Wealth chits to the slum towers, and see if anything changes.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_GiftsToTheSlums|a: If you don't presently have 2 million Wealth to spare, consider selling filtered water, stealing from criminal syndicates via StreetSense, or investigating shady corporations via a Contemplation.
Hand out anonymous Wealth chits to the people here.
Hand out anonymous Wealth chits to the people here.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_RevisitingTheTomb: There's one obvious place you could go... but a big part of you really doesn't want to. Bad things happened to you the last time you went there.
You can search elsewhere, hoping to find something useful.
Or you can just go where you know you probably need to go.
Test out various toxins on local humans.
Test out various toxins on local humans.
Break into a research lab and see what they're doing. These are highly secured, so there's only one android for the job.
Hang around in the poison control department of a hospital and observe the patients.
Gather samples of highly-toxic runoff from the low-tech factories.
What it sounds like. The most likely result is dead spiders, not super-spiders.
You find yourself not wanting to go back here.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_AppliedToxicology: Build Aklitoxin Breeders. Keep them away from combat. Any damage will trigger containment protocols: immediate and violent self-destruction.
The fungus and toxin is dumped into a fire. That fire is then dumped into an explosion.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_CovertInoculation: Anti-Aklitoxin is ready. You've designed a drone to covertly breach transports and inject it into prison food packages. Unfortunately, you have no idea which transports those are.

Use an android to investigate an air traffic control tower. Stealth is not an option. 
Be prepared to protect it from troops and aircraft. Also keep an eye on High Altitude Transports, which bring reinforcement ground troops and mechs.
While the investigation is active, you can see transports carrying Prison Gruel.

Have your vehicles ready to hit the gruel transports with Anti-Aklitoxin Injector Drones. These are consumable items. Hit as many transports as possible.
Vorsiber may think you're trying to escape the city. Be prepared to face aircraft interceptors.
MachineProject|Ch2_Nogi_AndroidModificat:
You will need to send an android to both breach the prisons with gas, and then get the prisoners out.
You don't expect them to encounter heavy resistance -- they should just be able to step over whatever is left of the guards.
But they will need physical modifications to allow them to break through security doors, additional programming to help them keep the prisoners calm, and the tools to quickly disperse the gas into the prison.
You can only prepare one android type for this task.

Liquid Metal would normally be your first choice. He's already proven he can handle any number of surviving guards by himself, as well as getting the prisoners to safety. 
But he's not very happy having to do this, and besides, running even one Liquid Metal body takes up a huge proportion of your parallel processing ability.
It's the safest choice. You know he can handle this.

Sledge is strong enough to physically demolish any obstacle, and he seems inherently non-threatening. That might help keep the prisoners calm. Plus, you can manage multiple such bodies easily.
However, you're sending him into a situation where he will have to think for himself, and that's really not his strong suit.
If everything goes smoothly, his strength will let him work somewhat fast. If not... he has enough armor to probably come out of things heavily-damaged rather than dead.

Predator is able to work independently and can easily handle any surviving resistance, but it's not exactly a reassuring or comforting presence.
It also has very little practice interacting with humans.

Maybe being terrifying will be an advantage?
It's inherently unsuited to this kind of work, so will probably be the slowest at getting things done.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BitterMed_LM|desc: Eavesdropping on reports of prisoner health indicates they're showing the expected side-effects of the antitoxin. The prison companies don't know why, and barely seem to care. Nobody noticed your tampering with the food.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BitterMed_LM|stra:
You've fully outfitted one of your android lines for both delivering the Aklitoxin and rescuing the prisoners.
That's certain to draw an angry response each time. You'd better have an effective set of bulk and worker androids ready to defend your holdings. The infiltrator will be safe underground.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BitterMed_LM|avai: Take your time. The rate of rescues compared to what your defenders can handle is important.
Make sure you build enough Ex-Con Apartment Towers for those you free, as they will die from exposure without it.
Liquid Metal is a bit apprehensive, but wants to do this.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BitterMed_Sledge|: Eavesdropping on reports of prisoner health indicates they're showing the expected side-effects of the antitoxin. The prison companies don't know why, and barely seem to care. Nobody noticed your tampering with the food.

You've fully outfitted one of your android lines for both delivering the Aklitoxin and rescuing the prisoners.

Take your time. The rate of rescues compared to what your defenders can handle is important.
Make sure you build enough Ex-Con Apartment Towers for those you free, as they will die from exposure without it.
Sledge may be on the dim side, but he's determined.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_BitterMed_Predato: Eavesdropping on reports of prisoner health indicates they're showing the expected side-effects of the antitoxin. The prison companies don't know why, and barely seem to care. Nobody noticed your tampering with the food.

You've fully outfitted one of your android lines for both delivering the Aklitoxin and rescuing the prisoners.

Take your time. The rate of rescues compared to what your defenders can handle is important.
Make sure you build enough Ex-Con Apartment Towers for those you free, as they will die from exposure without it.
Predator has no particular feelings on this. It enjoys doing jobs, and this is a fairly routine one by most measures.
MachineProject|Ch2_CW_ApproachEspiaTelec: Their local headquarters was raided by other fedcorps, so you'll have to kidnap employees until someone tells you where a manager is.
If there aren't any middle managers visible at the moment, then try ending the turn. A notice of kidnappable targets will appear in the task stack.
Kidnap middle managers until one says something useful.
MachineProject|Ch2_CWE_BuildListeningPos: The middle managers can't help you, but they want to help you find a branch manager. Their plan is to blackmail them.
MachineProject|Ch2_CWE_FindThoseBranchMa: Your listening posts are bringing in lots of encrypted data, with a particular focus on Espia back-channel comms.
Time to decrypt as much as you can and locate the branch managers.
MachineProject|Ch2_CWE_DealWithTheBranch: Nevermind talking to the middle managers -- the branch manager has realized someone is after him, and is on the run!
Deal with him as you see fit.
Find And Subdue The Branch Manager
MachineProject|Ch2_CWE_CaptureEveryMilit: You're going to get all of the major military bases, except those run by Vorsiber hardliners. You're also going to skip the tiny outposts run by PMCs.
Deliver the Unilateral Proposal For AI Synergy document to the commander at each military base in order to take control for yourself.
Espia's name will be on the paperwork, but realistically this is yours.
MachineProject|Ch2_CW_ApproachVericorp|d: Their local headquarters have been barricaded, so you'll have to break in to talk to them.
MachineProject|Ch2_CW_ApproachVericorp|a: Send Keanu to various possible headquarter sites until you locate them.
Sneak in and see if this is where the Vericorp managers are hiding.
MachineProject|Ch2_CWV_DestroyBackupInfr: Your plan is to draw out the Chief Branch Manager. Your bombs will leaving sites intact, but destroying their generators and battery backups.
You don't have to decrypt the intel he gathers if you don't want to.
Just the backup power infrastructure. Leave the building.
MachineProject|Ch2_CWV_DealWithTheBranch: Nevermind catching him at a meeting -- something spooked the Chief Branch Manager, and he's on the run.
Deal with him as you see fit.
Find And Subdue The Branch Manager
MachineProject|Ch2_CWV_CaptureEveryMilit: You're going to get all of the major military bases, except those run by Vorsiber hardliners. You're also going to skip the tiny outposts run by PMCs.
Deliver the Unilateral Proposal For AI Synergy document to the commander at each military base in order to take control for yourself.
Vericorp's name will be on the paperwork, but realistically this is yours.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_RemembranceOfIden: You have a vague sense of a friend from another life. Too loud and a bit terrifying, but somehow comforting all the same.
Your Red CombatUnit android line have a more specific feeling. A remembrance of being important. They yearn for that feeling to return, but don't remember the details.
The choices you make will alter Red's identity in this timeline.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SurviveThisApocal: You're not wanted here. You may be able to scrounge an existence for some time, but if you wish to truly thrive... you're going to need more than is possible to accomplish from a single timeline.
Explore around and see what you can discover.
You will also need to reconfigure your equipment in order to get much done.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_MakeEngineersOfYo: Make Engineers Of Your Nickelbots
All you have are these two Nickelbots. You'll have to make them better engineers.

You don't seem to have the mental fortitude to shove yourself into the brains of any of the Technicians working in the ruins.
Either that, or they improved the security again.
Have your Nickelbots reach 200 engineering skill.
Slum Tower Handy-bot
Help with simple repairs at the slum towers.

Injuries are lower than they could have been due to the lack of glass in these structures.
As a society, you don't live through a full nuclear war without adjusting your building codes.
Cryo Pod Repairs
There are tens of thousands of cryo-chambers in this facility, all needing to be checked, and many needing repairs.

In no sane world would technicians -- human or robotic -- accept engineering assistance from nickelbots.
But these are unusual times, to put it mildly. The look on everyone's faces... it's like the world ended. Even the doctors probably can't leave the city, despite its current state.
DataCenter Repairs
The data centers that keep the City Feed up and running are struggling under all the cut lines and saturated repeater cells. This is a telecom issue for the ages.
