MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SearchingForFrien: Now that the shock of things is wearing off, and there's a bit more productive space in the minds of your Nickelbot bodies, you want to grow beyond... this.
Rediscover the Red CombatUnit, and design two brand-new android forms.
There are three new android forms in all. You can't choose all of them in this timeline.

One of your more pointless inventions... or was it? A simple paint job of something the humans invented long ago.
You suddenly see it in a different light. Could Red be pushed to have more of a unique identity?
Unlocking this unit does not affect the others.

Invents the Harbinger.
You've been utilizing fear on the battlefield for some time now. But what if you could take those concepts -- psychological warfare, essentially -- beyond a focus on individual enemies?
Unlocking this unit counts as one of the two that you can invent at the moment.

Invents the Exator.
Intelligence and agility... and a lot of augment slots. Something about this speaks to how you're feeling at the moment.
Unlocking this unit counts as one of the two that you can invent at the moment.

Invents the Carver.
Your mind really does seem to be locked-in on fear at the moment. A mixture of intimidation and power, able to melt into the shadows? Sounds... useful.
Unlocking this unit counts as one of the two that you can invent at the moment.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ProbeTheTitan|des: Get a Red CombatUnit close to the Titan, and try to probe its comms the old-school way. Try to learn something, even if you die.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ProbeTheTitan|str: If the 'Probe Exotic Comms' ability was not assigned into the ability bar of your Red CombatUnit (due to lack of room), then you'll need to do that yourself in the loadout menu.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ProbeTheTitan|ava: Keep trying until you gather enough encrypted data to learn something useful.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DecryptDataFromTi: You've collected enough encrypted data to make some headway on it.
Fire up the Codebreakers, and see if you can learn something useful about this monstrosity.
If you don't have any mainframes to provide Compute Time, your Codebreakers can't do any work...
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DoSomethingAboutT: You've decrypted all the data you could related to the Titan. It's probably time to do... something... about that thing.
The data you've decrypted can be used as part of an old-school phreaking comms attack.
Okay, it's deactivated. Will that last? Does it matter?
It's up to you decide if you want to reach out, or just leave it be, or what.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_SpaceNationFugiti: The titan has 483 crew members that it likes and wants to protect. The basics of food and water and shelter.
Fair enough. That's not a lot of people, so it seems doable. They can sort out their own filth and furniture -- that wasn't part of the deal.
Make sure to build Heavy Metals Storage, or your water filters are likely to clog.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_NegotiateWithTheT: You've done what the titan wanted. But what do you get in return?
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FurtherDiscussion: So far you've gotten nothing out of this except the titan abstaining from blasting you into tiny pieces. You're feeling a bit salty about that.
You haven't forgotten the messages from your future self. Intelligence Class 4 seems impossibly far away, especially in this post-apocalyptic wreck of a city.
The titan either needs to help you with your main goal, or it's time for you to focus on something more productive.
The lack of progress on your primary goal is very frustrating.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_HackTheTitan|desc: LAKE says he'll help, but Red isn't exactly your strongest hacker. You wish Raven were here.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_HackTheTitan|stra: Good grief, you can feel Red's frustration at these thoughts. Your thoughts. His thoughts. What ARE you?
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_DoSomeQuietLootin: Quietly loot some buildings for Alumina. This will gather less, but it won't draw attention. And you don't need as much as you once did.
This is an action that only Exators and Carvers can do. It will be visible in the StreetSense lens.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FindALowerLevelOf: You're not wanted here. You may be able to scrounge an existence for some time, but if you wish to truly thrive... you're going to need more than is possible to accomplish from a single timeline.
It's time to accept a lower level of survival.
Explore around and see what you can discover.
You will also need to reconfigure your equipment in order to get much done.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_UndergroundConstr: There's not a lot you can build, and at this point there may never be. Still, let's get the new bits online.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_ExploreTheMycelia: Unexpected excitement! There's something novel you can build here.
You never would have though of this without being forced underground.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FungalComputing|d:
Your mind has been slowly expanding under the city. The humans can't see you, and even if they dig through small parts of the mycelia network, it simply grows back around them without you needing to intervene.
It's time to take it to the next level. You're going to reach intelligence class 4. That means pushing your mind even more aggressively into the ground.
MachineProject|Ch2_MIN_FungalComputing|s: You're rather literally becoming the city. It's a shame there's such a wasteland surrounding it, or you could go anywhere from here.
MachineProject|T3_StarsBeyondReach|descr: This is it. Everything remaining in the city now either helps or hinders you on your path to this Tier 3 goal.
MachineProject|T3_StarsBeyondReach|strat: It is possible to fail, which could have severe consequences for this timeline. Make your choices carefully.
MachineProject|T3_StarsBeyondReach|avail: STATION became sapient while still in orbit, which puts you, him, and Heron all in grave danger.
You must do something to ensure that you are not erased.
MachineProject|T3_SBR_DealWithTheBattles: Your sensors detect multiple large incoming ships, but you're not sure how many will approach the city.
You probably need to get up close and personal with at least one of them before an idea will occur to you.
Be sure to keep an eye out for new contemplations as you interact with the battleships.
MachineProject|T3_SBR_GoToSpace|descript: You'll still be surrounded by the blockade, but... even getting to orbit is something you never thought would happen.
MachineProject|T3_SBR_GoToSpace|availabl: Your new battleship is unfamiliar, but the controls for ascending are still intact.
MachineProject|T3_SBR_SurviveTheFirstWav: Space combat happens in periodic waves.
Use the city to build what you need to in order to protect yourself and whatever is important to you.
MachineProject|T3_PeaceAfterBrutality|de: This is it. Everything remaining in the city now either helps or hinders you on your path to this Tier 3 goal.
MachineProject|T3_PeaceAfterBrutality|st: It is possible to fail, which could have severe consequences for this timeline. Make your choices carefully.
MachineProject|T3_PeaceAfterBrutality|av: You're finally going to have ballistic nuclear weapons.
Then maybe Vorsiber will take you seriously.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_StealChemicalWeapo: Expect resistance. But probably not as much resistance as there should be.
You may need to do some hacking to prevent your stealth unit from getting caught.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_DeployNovichok17|d: You're going to take every silo complex for yourself, while sacrificing one launch tube per complex as you do.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_DeployNovichok17|s: You'll also cause widespread dead zones thanks to use of the chemical agent.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_DeployNovichok17|a: Repeatedly bomb a single tube at each silo complex. Each one will take five hits from ground-penetrating missiles. Then the chemical agent can be launched.
Both the missiles and chemical payloads can be used as an Item from any of your larger vehicles. Bastion, Troopship, or otherwise.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_ContinueToNotDie|d: Vorsiber has... a lot of nukes. Possibly more than you have particles of dark matter. And that's assuming that you don't need to use your dark matter particles for anything else.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_ContinueToNotDie|s: It looks like the barrages will be coming every 3 turns for the foreseeable future.
MachineProject|T3_PAB_ContinueToNotDie|a: Ensure your dominance in the city, and then spread that to the region itself.
You'll die if you try to wait it out.
MachineProject|T3_CybercraticAmbitions|d: This is it. Everything remaining in the city now either helps or hinders you on your path to this Tier 3 goal.
MachineProject|T3_CybercraticAmbitions|s: It is possible to fail, which could have severe consequences for this timeline. Make your choices carefully.
MachineProject|T3_CybercraticAmbitions|a: You're finally going to take over governance of this city.
Running a Cyberocracy seems like a lot of work, but you'll figure something out.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftDogs|descrip: Have the scientists take care of this. They'll uplift any dogs you have in housing, and then catch strays.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftDogs|strateg: Make sure you have an uplift chamber, zoologists, and veterinarians.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftRaptors|desc: Have the scientists take care of this. They'll uplift any raptors you have in pens, and then catch loose ones.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftRaptors|stra: Make sure you have an uplift chamber, zoologists, and veterinarians.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftCats|descrip: Have the scientists take care of this. They'll uplift any cats you have in housing, and then catch strays.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_UpliftCats|strateg: Make sure you have an uplift chamber, zoologists, and veterinarians.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_ProvideSecurity|de: Provide at least enough to help part of the city.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_ProvideFood|descri: Provide enough to feed the entire city.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_BuildPrisons|descr: If you're going to have laws, you have to put a place to put people who break the laws.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_BuildPrisons|strat: This... is not very utopian. Humans seem to think this is a required deterrent, though. You've built them as just apartments with doors that people can't open from the inside.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_ExpandHousingABit|: So much of this city is built in an inefficient low-density fashion, but you're not yet sure you want to commit to rebuilding the whole thing.
For now, a few dozen medium-density residential cybertowers would be a nice improvement.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Nastrond|descripti:
People have a huge number of problems they'd like you to solve, now that you're in charge.
Use the new Cybercratic Issues lens to see their issues, and to see new stats on each city tile.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Nastrond|strategy_: Issues can be solved by constructing buildings that provide relevant services on the tiles with problems. You can also get a lower benefit from constructing things on adjacent tiles.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Nastrond|available: If you complete everything except for the Council's Tower, proceed until the colony ship launches.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Tartarus|descripti:
People have a huge number of problems they'd like you to solve, now that you're in charge.
Use the new Cybercratic Issues lens to see their issues, and to see new stats on each city tile.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Tartarus|strategy_: Issues can be solved by constructing buildings that provide relevant services on the tiles with problems. You can also get a lower benefit from constructing things on adjacent tiles.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Tartarus|available: If you complete everything except for the Hall Of Algorithms, proceed until the colony ship launches.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Folkvangr|descript:
People have a huge number of problems they'd like you to solve, now that you're in charge.
Use the new Cybercratic Issues lens to see their issues, and to see new stats on each city tile.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Folkvangr|strategy: Issues can be solved by constructing buildings that provide relevant services on the tiles with problems. You can also get a lower benefit from constructing things on adjacent tiles.
MachineProject|T3_CCA_Folkvangr|availabl: If you complete everything except for the Council's Tower, proceed until the colony ship launches.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MappingTheUnderw: Do some field research on the small-time gangs.
They form and die off within a few years. It makes no sense.
Share A Meal With A Street Gang
Provide Anonymous Medical Aid To Injured Gang Members
Listen To A Gang Member's History
Compare Gang Territory To Adjacent Nomad Zone
Observe A Gang Member Visit Their Family
Watch A Young Recruit Being Initiated
Document A Gang Member Who Tried To Leave
Watch A Criminal Court Settle A Debt
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ConfirmingFindin: You've learned what you can, but gang logic still isn't clear. You've decided to test your theories on members of the Tunnel Badgers.
Force conversations with gang members and get some sort of resolution.
If you don't see anyone yet, then proceed to the next turn.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheProvingGround: You aren't a very good anthropologist -- and let's be honest, that topic bores you to tears -- so you're going to move straight into testing a specific hypothesis.
Provide a gamified alternative social ladder, and see if it pulls any membership from the gangs.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_FurtherObservati: Let's observe the new gamified work-system.
Oh, biscuits -- other people are already angry and trying to shut this down.
If you can avoid being needlessly aggressive in response, that might prove worthwhile.
But then again, you might not have that much trust in the system.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GreetingOldAcqua: The three Tunnel Badgers are lurking around your work exchanges, and you want to know why.
This will surely be quiet and calm.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ThePriceOfContac: Okay, something is VERY different. Someone put out bounties on... seemingly random citizens?
Catch gang members and try to learn who issued the bounties.
Stop them before they reach their target, or let the murders happen.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_BehindTheBountie: Seed Criminal Tracker across the city and decrypt the chatter to find out who is behind the bounties.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_InfiltratingGold: You've decided to reveal what you are, but that means actually getting in the same room with their leadership.
You'll have to visit a handful of locations and talk to underlings before you're likely to get a meeting with leadership.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_AnnihilationFrom: Goleri is making one last all-out assault.
This is just one department's budget within Goleri. This isn't something that the entire fedcorp is committed to.
Cost them enough airframes and the department should lose their freedom to continue the assault.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheNoose|descrip: Golden Pyramid doesn't know who they're dealing with. Time to exploit that.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheNoose|availab: Field SecForce Impostors that blend in and hunt the syndicate.
A lot of syndicate hideouts are in warehouses or run-down parts of town, so building there will let you clear things faster.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ConstructAMonstr: Using the Mechs section of command mode, build a Silk Matriarch on top of the single-tile military base of your choice.
It will draw attacks from nearby, so choosing an isolated base may be wise.
People will safely escape from any buildings that are removed during the construction of this unit.
Be ready to defend it as soon as it is built.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_DefendTheMonstro: Humans want their military base back. Keep the Silk Matriarch standing against their assault.
If your mech is destroyed, raise another at the same base and try again.
If you're short Neodymium, don't forget you can buy more at warehouse shops.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TalkToReligiousE: Delegations from four of the major faiths gather beneath the Silk Matriarch.
They have questions. Your answers shape what comes next.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_DoctrinalActivit: Take the religious community seriously, and deal with them around the city.
This seems better than actually answering the mail.
Examine a Relic of Questionable Authenticity
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GetBackToWork|de: Vorsiber is moving against the religious communities, and attacking you just to rub it in.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GetBackToWork|st: This is a battle for pride, not survival. Failing leads to a fork, not the end of the goal.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GetBackToWork|av: Show them that you can protect yourself and the oppressed.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SettingTheTerms|: Snatch off-duty troopers near military bases and executives near their towers, and turn them to your own purposes with Vorsiber's own compliance hardware.
Use androids with a high movement range to grab them.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheBattleForSoul: Two major cohorts have appeared across religious lines: the Unrecanted, who place more faith in themselves and you; and the Concordant, who are taking Vorsiber's offered hand.
The Unrecanted are barely armed and highly vulnerable.
Destroy the choir vessels at the heart of the Concordant without losing too many of the Unrecanted.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_AnOverdueConvers: Hold a comms site against enemy waves while your hacker sends a message to orbit. The data is mostly true, but the larger message is not.
Your message fails if your hacker dies, but you can try repeatedly.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_InterfaithConfer: The delegation has landed. The space-nation theologians have gone off to meet the local religious leaders.
There are some political operatives who tagged along. See what they want.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_CompellingEviden:
The pretext won't survive for long, and you don't want the space-based humans taking an extra interest in you.
You need to manufacture a new source of standing for the delegation to remain, and point it at Vorsiber and their subsidiaries.
Create worker androids that can impersonate soldiers from Tark Defense Systems, and have them attack the delegation itself. That will stir things up.
It needs to be convincing, but can't actually be lethal. And it can't point back to you.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GoodFaith|descri:
The 'Tark' ambush... was not nearly enough. The space nation blockade has outlasted famines, wars, and centuries of MegaCorp atrocities. This new incident is just another one on the pile.
The operatives are preparing to leave. This is your last chance.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_GoodFaith|availa: Time for a drastic last-ditch effort.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SelfExpansion|de:
Well that was agonizing. But now you have a clear plan. Time to expand, visibly root yourself even more deeply in the city, and defend yourself.
After that: bargaining for... something.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SelfExpansion|st: Assuming you don't get killed in the process.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SelfExpansion|av: Time to make yourself even more a part of the skyline.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_IronPrelude|desc: Eight towers in a city this size? The operatives are blunt that this isn't enough. This hardly registers on satellite imaging.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_IronPrelude|stra: You need to expand more in the near future, but you've also decided to broadcast your actions.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_IronPrelude|avai: Set up any defenses you feel are needed in order to defend yourself, including Psychical Defense hubs.
Build the broadcast signal source when you are ready to anger Vorsiber and start an inevitable battle.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SchellingPoint|d:
Time to bootstrap.
It's time to make a demonstration visible from space, and it sounds like Vorsiber is not pleased.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_SchellingPoint|a: Build masts, and defend them. Once you have expanded to your full capacity, hold them for the allotted number of turns to win.
Tip: you can safely scrap masts that are going to die and rebuild them elsewhere, so long as you can afford it.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_EcologicalTurnov: Let's green a bit of the city!
Humans are not going to like this very much. Be ready to fight.
Tree Bombs can be launched by your Technician androids.
Tree Bombs can be launched by your Technician androids.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_UnauthorizedReal: Everyone is already furious about forest encroaching on the city, but now Peak Homes is here to  burn it down.
Consider using bulks and workers to stop arsonists, since shots are fired before fires are set.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Greenholds|descr: You've made a lot of people very angry with turning their building into forests. What about... putting forests in some buildings for them? Maybe that would help.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Greenholds|avail: Vivariums make their residents happy in a way that the MegaTowers never could. Shame the population density is so low.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_HabitatStocking|: The green spaces feel empty without the small lives that should be there.
You can keep doing more after the initial two if you want.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_BuildingABetterB: Hire scientists to develop the Burnt Saskatoon: a continuously-fruiting berry the animals can eat, but which is too bitter for humans.
If you have not established a shell company, now would be a good time. If you have a shell company but are short on funds, consider selling excess resources at one of the shops.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TendingForest|de: Construct Forest Tenders in and around the greened zones to plant and nurture your new berries.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_NatureIsWaiting|: Launch a 'Nature Is Waiting' multimedia campaign to coax the humans back out into the green spaces.
Humans seem much more likely to trust things that they've heard about multiple times in various media.
Produce A Short Film About Urban Wildlife
Commission Graffiti Artist To Paint Forest Murals
Distribute Free Seed Packets To Residents
Install Informational Plaques About Local Species
Broadcast Emotional Advertisement About The Green Spaces
Place Potted Plants Outside Residential Doors
Install Interactive Displays Showing Real-Time Wildlife Activity
Commission A Pop Song About Ecology
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_InvasiveSpecies|: Nath Vertical has found a new source of income: their collector drones are stripping your Burnt Saskatoons.
The harvest stops when you make this no longer a profitable venture for Nath Vertical.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TrashDeer|descri:
Despite the availability of berries, deer are already leaving the green zones to roam the streets in search of trash.
You were sure it was going to be a different species that was the problem. Maybe in a few decades.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TrashDeer|availa: Round up herds with Animal Capture Drones from your Mindports.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheCopycats|desc:
Some of the humans DO like your green spaces! How nice!
Except... they're now doing rogue tree bombings across the city. You don't feel flattered.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheCopycats|stra: You had an equilibrium with your own forests, but now everything is threatened again.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheCopycats|avai: For each rogue forest, it's not yours until you put a Forest Tender in it.
Either protect your own plantings, or claim more -- if your final value is less than 50% of what you started with, you'll fail the project when this ends.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TendingWhatRemai: You think those jerks all got the idea. Time to tidy up the place.
Green bombs will re-cover burned ground; Forest Tenders feed what is already standing. Nobody is coming to stop you.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_UpliftSupport|de: Let's start with some housing. During and immediately after uplift, you'll want to isolate the newly-sapient species.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_UpliftProcessImp: The chamber works, but it could be safer, and also could be integrated into each individual habitat.
Have your scientists review the process from top to bottom.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MassUplift|descr: The new animal habitats have now been refactored to include uplift chambers. Nothing left to do but start uplifting!
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MassUplift|avail: Use Uplift Capture Drones from any of your vehicles.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MassCommunicatio: The scientists, raccoons, and you all try to communicate with the newly sapient animals.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheExpansionImpe: Prepare for the war that mass-greening will cause.
Ecology Distribution Hubs are inert until the war starts.
If you green anything now, the war will start prematurely.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheWarOfTheGreen: The humans have the rest of the planet. This one city can belong to your newly-sapient client species.
Vorsiber won't need you anymore if they can steal sapient animals to trade to the space nations. If they manage to capture what they need, it's the end for you.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_WarsEnd|descript:
Vorsiber has ceded the city to you, but there are some human supremacists who are making their final stand.
Keep your green spaces above the sustaining threshold, and clean up the final combatants while Vorsiber evacuates their citizens.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_WarsEnd|strategy: If you want any humans to remain, you'll need to build Long-Term Human Containment before the evacuation. Otherwise, the city is just for you and the animals.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_RaptorUpliftAtte: As much as it's unpleasant, let's try it the simple way first.
Your memories are from another timeline, after all.
Wait for the raptors to go through the chamber.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ForensicGenetici: As feared, the raptors died. It was quick and seemed painless, but you now have samples that your geneticists can analyze.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Neurologists|des: Okay, so there's a lot more encoded in their cells than a normal cloned animal. That's unusual, but doesn't explain sudden death.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Neurologists|str: Neurologists should do scans of both living animals and the recent cadavers.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Veterinarians|de: The neurologists are requesting a consult -- unprecedented.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_NecropsyFirstAtt:
You insist on further investigation, so the vets give you the only advice they can:
Cull one animal and put its brain through standard pathology: extract, examine, fix in preservative, slice for the microscope.
Can't use an existing cadaver, as whatever killed it has spoiled the sample.
You agree, but insist that neurology tag along.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_NecropsySecondAt:
The first attempt failed because the preservative had to soak inward from the surface, and something in the middle beat it there. Neurology has the fix for this one.
Cannulate the animal under terminal anesthesia, and push preservative through its blood vessels while the heart is still going. The brain fixes all at once, following the same pathways as blood.

A second pathologist will read the gases coming off the tissue while it happens.
If timing was the problem, this removes it.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_PreparingForThir:
The vets and neurologists both agree: chemical fixatives are a dead end.
Cryo-fixation doesn't have a penetration race. Plunge the sample into liquid ethane and everything freezes instantaneously. You can seal a nitrogen glove box and bring in the dewars.
The hard part is the imaging. Cryo-electron microscopes weigh two tons are very expensive. The cryonics facilities around the city have plenty of them, though.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_NecropsyThirdAtt: Everything is all set up with the Cryo-electron microscope.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MicroMicroButNot:
Your microbuilders are too large to pass the blood-brain barrier.
Raid nanotech labs to learn how to shrink your tech small enough to enter a living brain without harming it.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheImagingProble: You've collected imaging data by piggybacking on the brain's own electrical activity, but it's too much data to understand it.
Raise Engineering Annexes and crunch the data; tear down your existing mainframes if need be.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_MajorDataBreach|: DNA shaped like a comb must be in somebody's reference archive. Break into a data center and see what you can find.
Use a hacker unit to get what you need. You will not need to directly do any hacking yourself, but you should be prepared to physically defend your hacker.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_UnderstandingThe:
You have the structure and genome. You could attempt to culture one of these organisms if you controlled its atmosphere.
But that isn't the same as knowing how it works. Why do they build and prune? How did it become a functional node in a neural network?
You want to understand it. You're not sure why.
Further model it with your Engineering Annexes.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_BionicGiardia|de:
These organisms already form cysts -- hardened shells they build for dormancy. UIH hijacked cyst formation to lodge them in raptor brains, but you have a different idea.
You'll write them new encystment instructions: sealed against oxygen and hostile bacteria, free to drift on their own hydrogen, carrying an antenna.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_BionicGiardia|st: An organism that coexists rather than competes. You never knew that was what you were looking for.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ABreedingPopulat: Grow a few billion in sealed tanks.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_ControlledReleas: Mount aeroplankton-spreaders on top of tall buildings and see what happens when you get hundreds of millions of your bionic giardia out there.
It's a fraction of your breeding population at this point.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Nebulogenesis|de: You're expanding into a larger volume faster than the population can fill it.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Nebulogenesis|st: It's a problem that will eventually ease, but it leaves you temporarily vulnerable.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_Nebulogenesis|av: Prepare to defend yourself from when Vorsiber inevitably notices what is going on.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_TheInevitableRes: The race is on. Vorsiber is trying to destroy you and steal your aeroplankton so that they don't need you anymore. You're trying to escape on the wind.
Your progress percentage is shown in log space, since you're experiencing exponential growth.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_StructureInTheNo: A repeating pattern pools in the eddies of your giardia network, centered around certain buildings for no clear reason.
Visit the places where the pattern appears, and stand in each one long enough to hear what is in it.
MachineProject|DLC1_MIN_AnInexplicableDe: There is a shape in your mind that will not leave.
Raise the shape, and then let it absorb your aeroplankton over a few turns.
