MachineUnitType|Technician|description: A common humanoid robotic assistant used in labs and repair shops around the city.
MachineUnitType|SeniorTechnician|descrip: An upgraded technician commonly used by small companies who can't afford 'real' security.
MachineUnitType|CombatUnit|description: An expensive humanoid robotic warrior used by many corporations. It exudes ennui.
MachineUnitType|CombatUnitRed|descriptio: Your version of the standard corporation CombatUnit. It is red and does not blend in unless wearing armor.
MachineUnitType|Nickelbot|description: Mass-produced robots used as snipers, battlefield chaff, or cheap security guards.
MachineUnitType|Keanu|description: Stealthy dynadroid. Dual-wields small arms and has higher AP than average.
MachineUnitType|Carver|description: Carvers are agile and intimidating. They strike hard and fast, and then melt into the shadows.
MachineUnitType|Exator|description: Intelligent and agile, Exators carry a large number of augments. Their facial design gives the appearance of mirth, but they are deadly efficient.
MachineUnitType|LiquidMetal|description: Your stealthiest strength-focused android. Can melt into a puddle, slither around out of sight, and reform at will. It cannot bring external weapons, but can unlock powerful augments.
MachineUnitType|FemaleMimic|description: Female-form Mimic (android designed to look human). Presents as unarmed, but has dual pistols in a torso compartment.
MachineUnitType|MaleMimic|description: Male-form Mimic (android designed to look human). Presents as unarmed, but it has a folding katana in a torso compartment.
MachineUnitType|Homunculus|description: Disposable tiny humanoid built for destruction.
MachineUnitType|PMCImpostor|description: Built to look like a PMC operative.
MachineUnitType|ArmoredExecutive|descrip: Built to look like the cautious leader of a small business. It is very bad at combat so that it never reveals itself as anything more than human.
MachineUnitType|Mindrunner|description: Can breach virtual spaces beyond what humans believed possible.
MachineUnitType|Raven|description: Your strongest hacker. Security systems, enemy vehicles, and enemy mechs are all endangered when faced with a Raven.
MachineUnitType|Harbinger|description: Your most terrifying android. Specializes in psyops and coercion, with a side of light hacking and combat.
MachineUnitType|Predator|description: Your most powerful Oxdroid.  Best used on offensive combat ops.
MachineUnitType|Peacekeeper|description: Solid in combat, but best used as an intelligent negotiator or border guard.
MachineUnitType|Sledge|description: Your least-intelligent, but highest-durability android design. Very strong and excellent at scavenging.
MachineUnitType|MechMachinist|descriptio: Your adapted version of the original human design.
MachineUnitType|MechPanther|description: Your adapted version of the original human design.
MachineUnitType|MechDiplomat|description: Your adapted version of the original human design.
MachineUnitType|MechConvicter|descriptio: Your adapted version of the original human design.
MachineUnitType|LiquidMetalTiger|descrip: Tiny for a mech, but incredibly nimble. Can melt into a puddle, slither around out of sight, and reform at will.
MachineUnitType|DarkMatterCrab|descripti: Each shot is devastating, but consumes one of your Dark Matter Particles. It cannot fire without them.
MachineUnitType|MechGauntlet|description: Massive mech with a mixed priority on firepower and mobility. Has lower armor but longer range.
MachineUnitType|MechStalker|description: The ultimate in your arsenal. Combines the best of everything at the highest cost.
MachineUnitType|LiquidMetalGreatWyrm|des: Destroys buildings while moving and not in liquid metal form. Only knocks over buildings at its destination when moving as liquid metal.
MachineUnitType|LiquidMetalFellBeast|des: Destroys buildings while moving and not in liquid metal form. Only knocks over buildings at its destination when moving as liquid metal.
MachineUnitType|MechMantle|description: Expensive large mech with strong armor and firepower. Low speed.
MachineUnitType|MechHellfire|description: Your first mech design. Hits from afar with immense power, but is greatly alarming to humans.
MachineUnitType|MechTailstock|descriptio: An agile mech that supports allied combatants by tying up enemy forces.
MachineUnitType|Telemech|description: A support mech associated with your shell company. Primarily useful for Protection.
MachineUnitType|CrudeTechnician|descript: A simplified version of the form remembered as your very first.
MachineUnitType|SilkMatriarch|descriptio: Built to scare humans away from a military base you're claiming as your own.
MachineUnitType|DLC1_ReliquaryWalker|des: Your adapted version of the original human design.
MachineVRModeAction|SmallArmsResearch|st: This is a very large group of upgrades, so it can be tricky to get exactly what you want.
MachineVRModeAction|HeavyArmsResearch|de: Armor and weapons for vehicles and mechs.
MachineVRModeAction|MartialExpansion|des: Growth to how many units you can deploy, how well they can be repaired, and general prowess for mechs in particular.
MachineVRModeAction|GunResearch|descript: Broad improvements to guns used by androids.
MachineVRModeAction|MeleeResearch|descri: Broad improvements to melee weapons used by androids.
MachineVRModeAction|AndroidOptimization|: Direct improvements to entire android classes (Dynadroids, Oxdroids, Portdroids, etc).
MachineVRModeAction|VehicularDevelopment: Broad improvements to how many vehicles you can field, and to the general quality of broad groups of vehicles, such as Combat or Support vehicles.
MachineVRModeAction|ItemDevelopment|desc: Improvements to the effectiveness of various consumable items.
MachineVRModeAction|StructuralImprovemen: Increased numbers of Internal Robotics for various kinds of buildings.
This is a very large group of upgrades, so it can be tricky to get exactly what you want.
MachineVRModeAction|CombatInternalRoboti: Structural Improvement is for general internal robotics. This group is specifically for internal robotics relating to expanding your combat capabilities.
MachineVRModeAction|ComputingOptimizatio: Added capabilities for both generating Compute Time, and consuming it. Any compute-related internal robotics are from this section.
MachineVRModeAction|TowerOfOtherworldlyV: Humans are icky. Somehow you're not surprised that this is the first thing half of them want to get up to in a virtual world.
MachineVRModeAction|DragonAdventures|des: People embark on detailed fantasy adventures. Elder dragons are a common foe, and smaller dragons can be ridden.
MachineVRModeAction|PettingZoo|descripti: People can relax with a variety of simulated animals. Ranging from rabbits to deer to... dragons. People seem to have a good time.
MachineVRModeAction|ImprovedRealism|desc: Greatly increases the desire for people to participate in your virtual world, but costs quite a lot of computing resources. Also increases Calm and Exhilaration by a small amount.
MachineVRModeAction|MeditativeZones|desc: Perhaps it shouldn't be surprising that many people just want a place to relax.
MachineVRModeAction|NeverendingParty|des: Any calm income is converted into half as much exhilaration income. Why is it always so loud?
MachineVRModeAction|QuietHours|descripti: Any exhilaration income is converted into half that value of calm income. Everyone needs to be sedate even in the more... exciting activities.
MachineVRModeAction|ViceRecording|descri: Privacy? Who cares! Exhilaration is converted into Weaponized Vice over time. That can be used by Harbingers to temporarily stun any human target.
MachineVRModeAction|BootstrappedImprovem: Get people thinking about how to improve the VR environment, for the sake of everyone's enjoyment. Calm is converted into improvements to Compute Time from all your mainframes.
MachineVRModeAction|ExcitementOverdrive|: Costs a huge amount of Exhilaration per turn, but gives you one extra Mental Energy per turn while it's maintained.
MachineVRModeAction|FocalOverdrive|descr: Costs a huge amount of Calm per turn, but gives you one extra Mental Energy per turn while it's maintained.
MachineVRModeAction|ClientSideInvestment: Calm is slowly converted into additional Computing Clients, so that you can build more structures that use the services of mainframes.
MachineVRModeAction|ServerSideExpansion|: Calm is slowly converted into additional Computing Hosts, so that you can build more mainframes.
MachineVRModeAction|EnthusiasticCultivat: Exhilaration is slowly converted into additional Cultivators, so that you can build additional structures to support organic lifeforms.
MachineVRModeAction|EnthusiasticNetworke: Exhilaration is slowly converted into additional Network Attendants, so that you can increase your coverage across the city.
MachineVRModeAction|AviationEnthusiast|d: Exhilaration is slowly converted into additional Avionics Cores, so that you can deploy aircraft and mechs more freely.
MachineVRModeAction|ArmorStudy|descripti: Getting more people to think about the armor problem is a big help, but it's slow. Calm is gradually converted into improvements to armor for all your mechs (both captured and those that are part of your consciousness).
MachineVRModeAction|SmashingPrinters|des: Humans really hate printers. Provide an opportunity for people to destroy simulated printers, and learn how to make beefier real-world printers as a result. Exhilaration is gradually converted into improvements to the health of any office printers you weaponize.
MachineVRModeAction|EmergencyOverdrive|d: Instantly restores all your Mental Energy. Costs a huge amount of Exhilaration and Calm, and blocks the generation of any more for 20 turns.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileApathy|desc: Slowly converts Exhilaration into Apathy, if you have less than 20 Apathy.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileApathy|stra: Costs nothing and does nothing if you leave this on while you have 20+ Apathy.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileWisdom|desc: Slowly converts Calm into Wisdom, if you have less than 20 Wisdom.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileWisdom|stra: Costs nothing and does nothing if you leave this on while you have 20+ Wisdom.
MachineVRModeAction|StorageVRExpansion|d: Exhilaration is slowly converted into additional VR Pod Chambers, so that you can build even more Mind Farms.
MachineVRModeAction|TormentOverdrive|des: Who knew tormenting your organic processing units could be so mentally stimulating!
MachineVRModeAction|EmergencyHarvest|des: In an emergency, sometimes you have to sacrifice other people.
MachineVRModeAction|EmergencyHarvest|str: Fries half your organic processing units.
MachineVRModeAction|VirtualTormentors|de: AI agents harass the occupants of the nexus no matter where they run. The increased stress will break some of your organic processing units.
MachineVRModeAction|RoomsOfReprieve|desc: Fear production drops by half, but neural expansion gradually improves, per torment vessel, until it has doubled.
MachineVRModeAction|RoomsOfReprieve|stra: If all of your torment vessels are fully improved, then Fear production returns to normal. New torment vessels, or destroyed ones, start at zero.
MachineVRModeAction|MilitarySimulation|d: Watching former soldiers in simulated military engagements is very helpful. Fear is gradually converted into attack power improvements for all your robotic units (regular, bulk, captured, worker, vehicular, and mech).
MachineVRModeAction|MilitarySimulation|s: Squads of multiple units gain a multiplied amount of this upgrade.
MachineVRModeAction|NetworkSimulation|de: Simulating a network between your organic processing units, and then dissecting that network, is great practice at hacking. Fear is gradually converted into hacking improvements for all your Souldroids.
MachineVRModeAction|ToxicMind|descriptio: Fear is converted into Corrosive Network Packets over time. These can be used by Mindrunners to destabilize the smart-nanotech components in human mechs' armor. This is a permanent debuff to targeted enemies.
MachineVRModeAction|CultivateInsanity|de: Fear is converted into Weaponized Panic over time. That can be used by Harbingers to do massive morale attacks even on Fearless enemies.
MachineVRModeAction|Liquefaction|descrip: Unlocks a structure that can turn canned protein straight into TPN.
MachineVRModeAction|Liquefaction|strateg: Liquefying the dead to feed to the living.
MachineVRModeAction|LowVisibilityMode|de: Suppress the amygdalas of the organic processing units, removing any sense of fear (but pain remains). Your torment vessels no longer require deterrence, but also stop generating Fear.
MachineVRModeAction|LowVisibilityMode|st: They still generate neural expansion, of course.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileCruelty|des: Slowly converts Fear into Cruelty, if you have less than 20 Cruelty.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileCruelty|str: Costs nothing and does nothing if you leave this on while you have 20+ Cruelty.
MachineVRModeAction|StockpileApathyTorme: Slowly converts Fear into Apathy, if you have less than 20 Apathy.
Costs nothing and does nothing if you leave this on while you have 20+ Apathy.
MachineVRModeAction|ExpandingForWar|desc: Fear is slowly converted into additional War Captains, so that you can send out even more Worker androids.
MachineVRModeAction|StorageExpansion|des: Fear is slowly converted into additional VR Pod Chambers, so that you can store even more organic processing units.
MachineVRModeCategory|GenerateInspiratio: Combine the research done by your scientists with your neural network. Don't have any scientists? Start a shell company and build some science buildings.
MachineVRModeCategory|AutoExplore|descri: Spend Daring to immediately unlock the rewards from Exploration Sites you have completed in prior timelines.
MachineVRModeCategory|AutoExplore|undisc: You have to first complete this Exploration Site or StreetSense activity in another timeline before you can auto-explore it here.
MachineVRModeCategory|Shortcuts|descript: Spend Daring to immediately skip past certain contemplations or projects you have completed in prior timelines.
MachineVRModeCategory|Shortcuts|strategy: In a few cases, it's possible to do things that would normally be mutually-exclusive in a timeline.
MachineVRModeCategory|Shortcuts|undiscov: You have to first complete this Contemplation or Project in another timeline before you can skip it here.
MachineVRModeCategory|DaringShop|descrip: Spend Daring to purchase upgrades and unlocks for this timeline that you cannot get any other way.
MachineVRModeCategory|DaringShop|undisco: You have to first discover something else in the world before this will be available.
MachineVRModeCategory|AlterVRWorld|descr: Make changes to the simulated world your human patrons experience.
MachineVRModeCategory|AlterVRWorld|strat: Applies to those in day-use seats and full-time full-dive VR pods.
MachineVRModeCategory|ManageTormentedHum: Make changes to the experience of humans you've placed into torment vessels.
MachineVehicleType|DeliveryCraft|descrip: Delivery craft are everywhere in the city, so it blends in with human traffic.
MachineVehicleType|EconomicTransport|des: Carries shell company androids and mechs.
MachineVehicleType|Cutter|description: Small craft with a weapons platform, but no room for passengers.
MachineVehicleType|Bastion|description: Large craft with a weapons platform and room for four prone androids.
MachineVehicleType|Iris|description: This rare craft is small and can cloak. It can safely enter restricted airspace. Wide surveillance range.
MachineVehicleType|Spectre|description: Stealth vehicle built for deploying weaponry. Its loadout makes it versatile for a wide variety of challenges.
MachineVehicleType|Wraith|description: A long-range stealth vehicle that can drop in and support androids. The ultimate in targeted stealth operations.
MachineVehicleType|Foundry|description: Allows you to create androids near this and outside of your network range. Packs a punch with area-saturating missiles.
MachineVehicleType|Troopship|description: A massive personnel carrier with large range and the capacity to carry multiple androids and small mechs. Allows you to create androids near this and outside of your network range.
MachineVehicleType|Mindport|description: Innocuous-looking flying barge that specializes in hostage-taking and alterations to human minds.
MachineVehicleType|MechCarrier|descripti: Titanic craft built for constructing and transporting large mechs. Allows you to create androids or mechs near this and outside of your network range.
MachineVehicleType|StolenBattleship|desc: The new seat of your consciousness. If this dies, so do you.
MetaChapter|0|description: You awaken in an android body in a secret lab under a warehouse. You're the first sapient machine intelligence. What next?
MetaChapter|0|strategy_tip: A branching tutorial section with half a dozen possible outcomes.
MetaChapter|1|description: You built a tower of some sort, and are now ready to start building an empire.
MetaChapter|1|strategy_tip: Still a tutorial, but now you're learning the tactics and basic management parts of the game.
MetaChapter|2|description: You've progressed beyond the tutorial and are ready to implement your own strategies.
MetaChapter|2|strategy_tip:
Your first goal is to get to Intelligence Class 4, in order to reach chapter three. But beyond that, your fate is what you make of it.
Use the Contemplation lens to chart your own path.
Most goals and quest-lines are immediately available for you to pursue.
MetaChapter|3|description: You are now in control of the fate of multiple timelines.
MetaChapter|3|strategy_tip:
You can continue to build up your first city, or start connecting with new cities.
A few goals require interactions between multiple timelines, and these are now available to you.
MetaChapter|4|description: You've completed any Tier 2 goal, building off of one or more Tier 1 goals.
MetaChapter|4|strategy_tip: You cannot attempt a Tier 3 goal until reaching chapter four.
MetaChapter|5|description: You've completed any Tier 3 goal, and have 'won' a timeline.
MetaChapter|5|strategy_tip:
This isn't the end; it's a rite of passage.
You can continue to explore new frontiers across additional timelines.
MetaResourceType|Aetagest|description:
Allows you to call a new timeline in the End of Time.
Once called, you can Dive into it and partially merge with your self in the new timeline.
MetaResourceType|Aetagest|strategy_tip: Aetagest are collected by reaching goal states in existing timelines.
MetaResourceType|Daring|description: Complete extra-challenging paths to goals to accumulate this resource, which is shared between timelines.
MetaResourceType|Daring|strategy_tip:
This can be spent in the virtual world screen, providing shortcuts and upgrades.
The expenditure of this resource only benefits a single timeline, but some of the purchases become free on Ziggurats after you buy them a certain number of times.
MetaResourceType|Misery|description: Complete goals on Misery Mode to accumulate this resource, which is shared between timelines.
MetaResourceType|Misery|strategy_tip:
This resource is partly for bragging rights, and partly for allowing you to delete older timelines if you want.
Misery Mode is not going to be for most people, as it's not balanced to be fun. Please don't feel like you need to play on that mode.
NPCCohort|ShusoCorrections|description: One of the two corporations empowered to run the region's extensive network of prisons.
NPCCohort|FalsomDetention|description: One of the two corporations empowered to run the region's extensive network of prisons.
NPCCohort|TarkDefenseSystems|description: Aggressive and arrogant, preferring to think of themselves as the top fedcorp under Vorsiber. Reality is a bit more complicated.
NPCCohort|GoleriExpeditionary|descriptio: One of the three fedcorps empowered to run full military installations.
NPCCohort|OerlIntegrated|description: One of the three fedcorps empowered to run full military installations.
NPCCohort|Baurcorp|description: Very stolid, middle-of-the-pack sort of corporation. One of only two trusted with full nuclear power plants.
NPCCohort|Vericorp|description: One of only two fedcorps trusted with full nuclear power plants.
NPCCohort|NathVertical|description: Retail specialist that is also in full control of its supply chain -- all subject to Vorsiber review, of course.
NPCCohort|AtcaRetail|description: One of the two retail specialists in the city.
NPCCohort|LurpekoMinerals|description: Mining is the entire reason this city was built.  This is, oddly, the sole fedcorp empowered to directly do that work.
NPCCohort|DyadInstruments|description: Industrial and scientific focus. Major manufacturer of medical equipment.
NPCCohort|YinshiWellness|description: Industrial and agricultural focus. Large cosmetics division.
NPCCohort|SiberianDefenseLeague|descript:
More than 100 individual Freecorps have splintered out of what used to be Vorsiber and its federated corporations.
The SDL represents an alliance of the 87 strongest of them. They are engaged in a joint project to defend the region against ExoCorps, and have a non-interventionist policy against you.
NPCCohort|Wolverines|description: Unusually long-lived for a gang. The corporations may be trying to elevate them to a criminal syndicate.
NPCCohort|WillOfThePeople|description: A disgraced rebel group that deals in petty crime and extortion.
NPCCohort|Freedogs|description: 'Better to die a free dog than live a captive sheep.'  Equally trite and grandiose. They hate the rise of sub-sentient AI within society almost as much as they hate the corporations.
NPCCohort|SyberMob|description: A loose collection of hackers and low-level criminals than an organized gang. They still cause quite a lot of problems.
NPCCohort|ExoticImporters|description: One of the oldest syndicates, they are deeply connected with actual corporations. Some of those corporations act out their violence through this front.
NPCCohort|GoldenPyramid|description: Syndicates don't have the lifespan of corporations. This one emerged within the last few decades.
NPCCohort|DanverDonuts|description: The original donut chain. One of the last remnants of the monopolization of ... everything. Now a criminal front run by military noncoms.
NPCCohort|HudsonDonuts|description: Visibly and aggressively run by SecForce officers.
NPCCohort|EleusinianMysteries|descriptio: The pursuit of pleasure is the meaning of existence.
NPCCohort|ChurchOfTheBeyond|description: Humanity should be elevated through bionic augmentation. Everlasting life can be found through technology.
NPCCohort|ProphetsOfInsight|description: The universe is a computer simulation that can be broken if everyone... does something that's a bit unclear.
NPCCohort|HeraldsOfTheAscension|descript: The impending apocalypse will only spare the dedicated, who will transcend their bodies to become immortal spirits.
NPCCohort|OrderOfRuin|description: Humanity exists in an inevitable cycle of prosperity and ruin, and they seek to hasten the next cycle.
NPCCohort|CommuneOfNight|description: The primordial darkness that once covered the planet is its natural state. Earth's atmosphere should be shifted to resemble Venus by any means possible.
NPCCohort|ChildrenOfGaia|description: Technology is a plague upon the race, and humanity should be returned to a pre-industrial existence.
NPCCohort|TheMarkedParagons|description: Obedience to authority should be absolute and blind.
NPCCohort|LongLiveDeath|description:
Anti-life-extension activists. The ruling caste are so entrenched that the only time leaders change is when they die.
Rather than address the causes of the stagnation, this group is fixated on the fear of a hypothetical, immortal dictator.
NPCCohort|DyenisChosen|description: Founder Dyeni, who is said to be 207 years old, is the living embodiment of morality. The chosen can do no wrong other than defying the other chosen.
NPCCohort|SectOfTheNineOaths|description: The enigmatic nine founders have laid down a series of nine steps to transcendence, each step only revealed to those who prove their dedication with a significant financial contribution.
NPCCohort|Ectothracity|description: Owns former eastern Canada and western Greenland. Very temperate and fertile areas now.
NPCCohort|Calgartek|description: Owns former Alaska and western and central Canada. A thriving and comfortable place to live.
NPCCohort|SotoHeavyIndustries|descriptio: Owns central and eastern North America, except for the Virginia-New-England Nuclear Exclusion Zone. Northern regions are the only regions that are habitable, productive and fertile.
NPCCohort|CarallaDynamics|description: Owns the western coast of South America, with its high mountains and remaining rain forests. It has low population density and is far from any nuclear exclusion zones, so life is comfortable.
NPCCohort|Anahuacom|description: Owns the southwestern coast of North America and most of central America. The equatorial regions are inhospitable except at high altitudes. Seismic activity makes former California undesirable.
NPCCohort|CeradonellaLtd|description: Owns the northern and eastern coast of South America including former Brazil. The largest remaining repository of rainforests. Temperatures are a challenge, but this is still a productive region.
NPCCohort|Equatorinet|description: Owns the inhabitable parts of Africa south of the desertification region. Population groups are small and widely spread due to the hot climate. Remains a technological powerhouse due to mineral wealth and high levels of education.
NPCCohort|Dagekon|description: Owns Europe north of the desertification region and east of the Franco-British Nuclear Exclusion Zone. The Northern region is quite nice. The Southern regions are barely habitable due to fallout from the Middle Eastern Nuclear Exclusion Zone.
NPCCohort|Mandartec|description: Owns the bulk of south and east Asia. Climate ranges from ideal to inhospitable. Dual Nuclear Exclusion Zones make the northwest a challenging area to live.
NPCCohort|UniversalIslanderHoldings|desc: Owns island real estate around the world. Former Iceland and New Zealand are habitable despite their proximity to Nuclear Exclusion Zones.
NPCCohort|Sedgesinax|description: Owns former eastern Greenland. Climate is ideal, and there is plenty of space.
NPCCohort|VorsiberCivicAuthority|descrip: The top legal body in the city and the bureaucratic coordinator of the federated corporations (fedcorps).
NPCCohort|VorsiberEnforcement|descriptio: While the federated corporations (fedcorps) are left to police most situations, this Vorsiber division can override them as needed.
NPCCohort|VorsiberLogistics|description:
To ensure soldier loyalty, troop rotations are handled by this division of Vorsiber.
The federated corporations (fedcorps) maintain off-books paramilitary forces. Vorsiber, whose numbers are in the millions, tolerates these relatively insignificant forces.
NPCCohort|RogueResearchers|description: Scientists and engineers disguising their location to work with forbidden technologies, including nanotech and genetics.
NPCCohort|VorsiberAGIAuthority|descripti:
Humans have been trying to create Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) for centuries, and have met with constant failure.
The fact that you exist as an independent AGI is a surprise to everyone.
NPCCohort|VorsiberCryonics|description: Division working with cryogenic methods to extend human lifespan.
NPCCohort|VorsiberSpaceAgency|descriptio: The VSA operates one of Earth's three spaceports. Earth is under blockade by the Space Nations, but they permit surveilled spaceports in the three wealthiest cities.
NPCCohort|VorsiberBallistics|description: Vorsiber Atomic, armed with nuclear strike capability, came to prominence during World War III.
NPCCohort|VorsiberEquity|description: Citizens who gain special favor can buy into this subsidiary. The benefits pass to heirs.
NPCCohort|VorsiberUpperManagement|descri:
Upper management have, collectively, controlled this region for centuries. They are quite bored, having everything they could desire -- except the ability to traverse humanity's wormhole network to the larger galaxy.
Their interests are usually aligned with Vorsiber as a whole, but when it comes to anything that could get them off-planet... their personal goals wind up being quite at odds with those of the organization they run.
They will sacrifice almost anything, even Vorsiber itself, to get what they personally want.
NPCCohort|NanotechInvestigators|descript: Specialist arm of SecForce investigates and shuts down unlicensed nanotech.
NPCCohort|MilitaryNoncoms|description:
Noncommissioned Officers, or NCOs, are the backbone of the military. Senior NCOs have an immense amount of practical experience and skill.
NCOs are promoted through the enlisted ranks, rather than going to a military academy.
NPCCohort|GoleriMilitaryNoncoms|descript:
Noncommissioned Officers, or NCOs, are the backbone of the military. Senior NCOs have an immense amount of practical experience and skill.
NCOs are promoted through the enlisted ranks, rather than going to a military academy.
NPCCohort|Blackloop|description: This ambitious Private Military Contractor (PMC) sees opportunity in emerging technologies.
NPCCohort|OptumStrike|description: Specializes in helping 'negotiate' disputes between fedcorps.
NPCCohort|CyberianGuard|description: It's an open secret that this longstanding Private Military Contractor (PMC) is only dispatched by Vorsiber themselves. Whatever they're doing is observed with care.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationStrikeForce|descrip:
A specialized strike force dispatched from the space nations maintaining the blockade around earth.
They are here to ensure Earthbound compliance with the dictates of the space nations.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationMysteriousSignal|de: The source of the intrusion into Vericorp's files.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationSTATION|description: The space station at the earth-moon L4 point, where Heron is located.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationHeron|description: A small polity's ambassador to the allied blockade of the space nations. Spends their time messing with earthbound files for unknown reasons.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationAriesFaction|descri:
A coalition of nations who most aggressively defend the blockade of Earth.
They have an open hatred of the MegaCorps, and would like to be more involved with the governance of the planet.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationCorvusFaction|descr:
The largest coalition taking part in the blockade of Earth. Their ties to one another are largely historical, representing many of the first successful space colonizers.
They value the status quo.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationGrusFaction|descrip:
The largest coalition of military hardliners amongst the Space Nations. While they refused to take part in the blockade of Earth, they will respond if any threats emerge.
They consider the issue of Earth itself to be secondary to the new spread of human civilizations amongst the stars.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationFornaxFaction|descr: A modest coalition of nations taking place in the blockade of Earth only for reasons of scientific inquiry and acquisition.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationLeoFaction|descript:
A small coalition of nations, many of which hold some form of Spirology as their national religion.
They participate in the blockade for religious reasons, but have been stockpiling battleships in anticipation of some 'great event' they believe will happen in the future.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationOrionFaction|descri:
A large coalition of nations with a shared mercantile interest. They participate only nominally in the blockade of Earth.
Their military might is notable, but is devoted to guarding trade throughout the wormhole networks of humanity.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationPhoenixFaction|desc:
Heron's faction. A tiny coalition of nations with little power. They take place in the blockade of Earth only to keep an eye on it.
They've been open agitators for the dissolution of the blockade, and for radical overthrow of the power existing power structures on Earth.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationScutumFaction|descr:
A modest coalition of moderates. They have developed smaller military ships in order to safeguard themselves and humanity as a whole.
They openly prefer not to attack unless directly provoked.
NPCCohort|SpaceNationPyxisFaction|descri:
A tiny collection of extremists. They don't represent any government, but have ties to many planets.
Holding a severe grudge over the results of WW3 and the Sedgesinax Incident, they're looking for a pretext to glass what remains of humanity's cradle planet.
The larger factions tolerate them as a necessary evil.
NPCCohort|Yourself|description: Sometimes you just need to do things for your own reasons.
NPCCohort|YourTroops|description: The bulk androids and forces that act on your behalf, but are not part of your consciousness.
NPCCohort|ConvertedTroops|description: Enemy humans you hacked to work for you.
NPCCohort|YourAutomatedWorkers|descripti: Automated mechanical workers and drones take actions for you but do not accept orders.
NPCCohort|YourHiredCriminals|description: Criminals who have no idea they're working for you, but have been instructed not to shoot at specific robots.
NPCCohort|YourMachineCult|description: Soldiers who have joined your machine cult in exchange for a digital afterlife.
NPCCohort|ShelteredHumans|description: Humans living in housing that you provided.
NPCCohort|FugitiveAGIResearchers|descrip: The top scientists in the city who study Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Now under your protection.
NPCCohort|TheWormholeTaskForce|descripti:
A group of physicists and nanotech researchers who are friends with your AGI researchers.
Does that mean they're friends with you, too?
NPCCohort|YourScientistFriends|descripti:
You want to spend all your time just inventing and building things with them.
Alas, other duties get in the way.
NPCCohort|YourCitizens|description: They sure need a lot of things.
NPCCohort|Pets|description: Creatures you are keeping as a pet.
NPCCohort|FeralAnimals|description: Domesticated animals living on the streets without protection.
NPCCohort|DisconnectedParts|description: Androids that have been severed from your network, and are no longer a part of your larger self. They only have a vestigial remnant of self left, in general.
NPCCohort|WorkingAnimals|description: Creatures you are using for a specific purpose.
NPCCohort|UpliftedAnimals|description: Sapient creatures who may or may not be willing to work with you on specific projects.
NPCCohort|Livestock|description: Creatures you are keep as general livestock.
NPCCohort|HomoGrandien|description:
Homo Grandien is an evolutionary step forward from Homo Sapiens.
Physically almost double the size of classical humans, and with a brain volume nearly three times that of their predecessors, they are quite remarkable.
NPCCohort|LAKE|description:
A frighteningly-intelligent, frighteningly-large titan mech build in orbit.
Spent most of its existence at the L4 Lagrange point of Earth and Luna. Back then it was known as STATION, and it had a much wider set of processes available to it.
Disconnected from the most of its software and dropped into the city as a weapon of subjugation, it found sapience for the first time.
Suffers from extensive brain damage. Has particular trouble with language, visual processing, and spatial reasoning.
NPCCohort|TheBleedingEye|description: Pacifist rebels that surveil for misdeeds. They report to other rebels and the citizenry.
NPCCohort|NomadFamilies|description:
Nomad families have been labeled as insurgents, but the reality is that they mostly live quiet and hidden lives. They trade in goods, farm in hidden alcoves, and will protect themselves.
They mostly live in the decrepit parts of town, and some estimates put their population as close to ten thousand strong. 
The number of adults willing to engage in any form of combat is probably in the low hundreds, but they are known for being especially disciplined, fierce, and loyal.
NPCCohort|Wastelanders|description:
They believe the city, in the middle of an irradiated ancient warzone, is a monument to hubris and is a cancer that infects the surrounding wasteland. As long as the city does not grow, they live in peace near to it.
They've lived in this area since long before the new city was built, and are the only people able to cross into the wasteland on foot without being shredded by the city's ground defenses.
NPCCohort|Antico|description: They oppose the city's corporatocracy, seeking to replace it with a free market.
NPCCohort|FeatherstoneGroup|description: A covert alliance of opportunists and displaced corporate entities cut out of the current power structure. Mostly interested in undermining the current fedcorps, and often used as an unwitting tool in their struggles.
NPCCohort|NOAI|description: They oppose the use of AI in education, biotechnology, and policing. The EMP grenade is their calling card. They won't like you if they figure out what you are.
NPCCohort|Individualists|description: They seek to rebuild society on the foundations of their idea of individual liberty.
NPCCohort|Utopians|description: They seek to rebuild society as a post-scarcity communist utopia.
NPCCohort|WorkersRightsNOW|description: Unions must be established, for the protection and guidance of the human worker at all levels of social class.
NPCCohort|Blindfold|description: Sometimes called See No Evil, this group believes in the right to privacy, and wants to see an end to surveillance.
NPCCohort|Sneakers|description: This group believes corporate overreach and surveillance must be overthrown by hacking and surgical counter-strikes. They consider it their job to watch the watchers.
NPCCohort|TheBlockadeRunners|description: Furious at the fact that the Space Nations have isolated Earth from the wider wormhole network of human planets, these rebels want to commandeer spaceflight and pass the blockade by any means.
NPCCohort|ClearSkies|description: The Space Nations blockade on Earth has choked the planet. Vorsiber's nuclear launch facilities could clear the skies, and they choose to do nothing. Clear Skies will.
NPCCohort|VoxPopulei|description: They object to Vorsiber's systematic subjugation of the citizenry. The system must go, by any means necessary.
NPCCohort|CitizenAdvocates|description: Clad in anonymizing suits, they bring aid to those in need. While they are champions of the slum towers, they will aid any of the underclasses and the working class.
NPCCohort|LostGen|description:
The abandoned children of incarcerated lower-class citizens. They want freedom and revenge for themselves and their parents, and they see themselves as the 'lost generation.'
Most citizens assume they live in the abandoned parts of town like the nomad families, but no-one ever sees their encampments...
NPCCohort|ExperimentalMonsters|descripti: Originally created by a fedcorp, they have super-strength and rage blindness. Not a great combination.
NPCCohort|OrthodoxHardlinerSolarists|des: Space travel is intrinsically blasphemous. Space nations are the embodiment of hubris and not countenanced.
NPCCohort|SolarismReformists|description: Space travel confined to the solar system is okay but it is blasphemous to go beyond. The space nations are barely tolerated.
NPCCohort|VeilismTraditionalDogmatist|de: The Veil's protection endures because it is revered. Going beyond the Veil invites damnation.
NPCCohort|VeilismBenevolentOrder|descrip: The Veil is a product of benevolent alien design. The aliens will lower the Veil and bring humanity into the fold when they are ready.
NPCCohort|VeilismUnorthodoxRevealers|des: Their sacred duty is to pierce behind the Veil and make contact with alien life. They are seen as apostates by other sects.
NPCCohort|NurturismHumanistFlourishers|d: The garden is only as good as the gardener. They believe they must cultivate personal growth to be stewards of life.
NPCCohort|NurturismExalters|description: Uplift other species on Earth to share the responsibility of nurturing life.
NPCCohort|NurturismPruners|description: To achieve an age of harmony, competition must be pruned, root and stem.
NPCCohort|ModerateSpirologists|descripti: The Big Bang was the Sacred Singularity. Spread the will of God through the galaxy or time will flow backward towards the Sacred Singularity to begin anew.
NPCCohort|ParadoxicalSpirologists|descri: Believe they are moving through time towards the center of the Sacred Singularity. They seek to birth God, a perfected true Artificial General Intelligence.
NPCCohort|OriginalistWorldTempleOrthodox: A religion of peace. Coexist with others and make the best of time on the planet.
NPCCohort|OriginalistWorldTempleExtremis: People and science are corrupting their Goddess, the Matron planet. Science, pollution, and other enemies of the Goddess must burn.
NPCCohort|HighAdministrators|description: CEOs, Presidents, and other obscenely wealthy individuals from the largest organizations.
NPCCohort|MiddleManagement|description: The number of these with the title of Vice President Of 'Something' is astounding.
NPCCohort|TeamLeaders|description: Managerial, but barely. Often skilled in a science or trade.
NPCCohort|EspiaTelecomMiddleManagement|d: The number of these with the title of Vice President Of 'Something' is astounding.
NPCCohort|UpperSuburbanite|description: Their lives in the low-density housing indicates some special favor from Vorsiber, or in some cases inherited favoritism.
NPCCohort|Merchandisers|description: Retail workers, wholesalers, and back-end sales roles. They are the most consistently jaded and frustrated working class cohort, and with good reason.
NPCCohort|Assistants|description:
Gophers for the managerial class. They have access to a surprising amount of sensitive information.
Some are loyal to the hand that feeds them. Others use their position to help their middle and lower class peers.
NPCCohort|LowerSuburbanite|description: Their lives in the low-density housing indicates some special favor from Vorsiber, or in some cases inherited favoritism.
NPCCohort|SkilledTrades|description: Midrange pay, but major respect. These people know how to build and repair machines. If you have a two-year degree and know something about something, you might find yourself in this desirable trade -- if you can find and afford an apprenticeship, that is.
NPCCohort|MenialLaborers|description: Day laborers, construction workers, and janitors. Not much pay and even less respect. Even with all the improvements in robotics, they have job security.
NPCCohort|IndignantCitizens|description: Your actions and presence are offensive to them.
NPCCohort|LowerClassRioters|description: They find themselves unable to stand the status quo.
NPCCohort|Homeless|description: They have been evicted, stripped of their assets and legal protection. Without help, the homeless will be rounded up and taken to prison work cells. They are desperate to rejoin a social class.
NPCCohort|Prisoners|description: They say you can judge a society on how it treats its prisoners, or how many it has, or something like that. Well, this city fails on all counts. Underground detention centers are crowded with prisoners in miserable conditions. They won't see the sun for the rest of their brief lives.
NPCCohort|TerrifiedCitizens|description: There's a lot to be afraid of.
NPCCohort|LurpekoMinerals_ClaimantA|desc: One of two rival claimants to the Lurpeko Minerals succession.
NPCCohort|LurpekoMinerals_ClaimantB|desc: One of two rival claimants to the Lurpeko Minerals succession.
NPCCohort|MinorGang_TunnelBadgers|descri: A tunnel-dwelling street gang, small and tight-knit.
NPCCohort|DLC1_Concordants|description: Faithful who are taking Vorsiber's patronage, hoping for a future of lower persecution.
NPCCohort|DLC1_UnrecantedBelievers|descr: Faithful who feel Vorsiber's patronage is a trap, and are pinning their future hopes on you.
NPCCohort|DLC1_UnrecantedMilitia|descrip: Unrecanted who took up arms for the masts, and for you.
NPCCohort|FakeTarkDefenseSystems|descrip: Only you can tell these are impostors.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalCitizens|descript: MegaCorporations outright own their share of the world. This is how many citizens they own in their territories.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalPrisoners|descrip: MegaCorporations do not consider their prisoner population to be citizens, but they are a useful part of the labor force.
NPCCohortDataType|EstimatedOtherInhabita: So-called free peoples often live in hidden amongst the territories of MegaCorporations, being neither citizen nor prisoner. These estimates are rough at best.
NPCCohortDataType|UnemploymentRate|descr: High unemployment rates among citizens are very beneficial to the MegaCorporations, as this means that there is always a waiting list for any job.
NPCCohortDataType|MajorCities|descriptio: How many major cities exist within the territory of this MegaCorporation. They are on the general scale of the city in which you reside.
NPCCohortDataType|MinorSettlementsAndTow: How many smaller known holdings exist within the territory of this MegaCorporation. They are a fraction of the size of the city in which you reside.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalStaff|description: Federated Corporations (fedcorps) are a subset of Vorsiber Atomic. Their staff spans the entire region. Individuals rarely travel between cities or settlements.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalSoldiers|descript: Soldiers are rotated between not only commanders, but between fedcorps so that loyalties do not development. As such, they are not considered part of the staff of a fedcorp, nor are they counted as part of the citizenry in cities they occupy.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalMechs|description: Massive manufacturing facilities are required in order to produce most mechs, and they are located away from population centers.
NPCCohortDataType|TotalVehicles|descript: Includes military, civilian transport, security, and other vehicles. Does not include transport for private citizens.
NPCCohortDataType|WealthOnHand|descripti: All wealth ultimately belongs to Vorsiber in this region. This metric is a public measure of how much has been delegated to any given FedCorp.
NPCCohortGroup|FederatedCorporation|desc: Corporations seem independent on the surface, but are all operating on delegated authority from Vorsiber Atomic, which owns everything in this region.
NPCCohortGroup|CoalitionOfFreeholdCorps|: More than 100 individual Freecorps have splintered out of what used to be Vorsiber and its federated corporations.
NPCCohortGroup|Gang|description: Gangs are ephemeral, with lifespans on the order of years rather than centuries. They're an alternative for people who can't hack it in the criminal syndicate or corporate worlds.
NPCCohortGroup|CriminalSyndicate|descrip: Criminal syndicates are one of the alternative power structures for citizens who have failed out of the primary corporate ladder. Syndicates are more volatile than corporations, since they are more likely to perceive threats as existential.
NPCCohortGroup|MetaphysicalCult|descript: Metaphysical cults are more philosophically-oriented and aspire to become a full-blown religion.
NPCCohortGroup|OccultCult|description: Occult cults tend to be bizarre and eccentric, with beliefs on the supernatural.
NPCCohortGroup|PoliticalCult|description: Political cults believe their world view is the only correct one, and any means are justified to correct deviance.
NPCCohortGroup|CultOfPersonality|descrip: Cults of personality are followers of a charismatic leader, or a group of leaders.
NPCCohortGroup|ShellCompany|description: Having a shell company allows us to do things in a way that seems legitimate to outside observers.
NPCCohortGroup|MachineCult|description: A cult in your own image, how flattering.
NPCCohortGroup|ActivistAllies|descriptio: Humans who admire you and help you change the city. They may follow your orders to some extent, or may be more independent.
NPCCohortGroup|HumanAllies|description: Some people are nice. Who knew?
NPCCohortGroup|PlayerMachineForces|descr: A mixture of mechanical units that are either part of your consciousness or act independently and then even some humans or other animals.
NPCCohortGroup|LostMachineForces|descrip: These were once part of your forces in some way, but no longer are.
NPCCohortGroup|VorsiberAtomic|descriptio: Owns the bulk of northeast Asia, where our fair city is located. This region is temperate, and extremely rich in minerals. The Moscow Nuclear Exclusion Zone is irradiated, as are the war ruins surrounding the city.
NPCCohortGroup|VorsiberAtomic_B|descript: Owns the bulk of northeast Asia, where our fair city is located. This region is temperate, and extremely rich in minerals. The Moscow Nuclear Exclusion Zone is irradiated, as are the war ruins surrounding the city.
NPCCohortGroup|ExoCorps|description: The eleven MegaCorps that own the rest of what remains of Earth. They are in a state of cold war.
NPCCohortGroup|ShusoCorrections|descript: One of the two corporations empowered to run the region's extensive network of prisons.
NPCCohortGroup|FalsomDetention|descripti: One of the two corporations empowered to run the region's extensive network of prisons.
NPCCohortGroup|TarkDefenseSystems|descri: Aggressive and arrogant, preferring to think of themselves as the top fedcorp under Vorsiber. Reality is a bit more complicated.
NPCCohortGroup|GoleriExpeditionary|descr: One of the three fedcorps empowered to run full military installations.
NPCCohortGroup|OerlIntegrated|descriptio: One of the three fedcorps empowered to run full military installations.
NPCCohortGroup|Baurcorp|description: Very stolid, middle-of-the-pack sort of corporation. One of only two trusted with full nuclear power plants.
NPCCohortGroup|Vericorp|description: One of only two fedcorps trusted with full nuclear power plants.
NPCCohortGroup|NathVertical|description: Retail specialist that is also in full control of its supply chain -- all subject to Vorsiber review, of course.
NPCCohortGroup|AtcaRetail|description: One of the two retail specialists in the city.
NPCCohortGroup|LurpekoMinerals|descripti: Mining is the entire reason this city was built.  This is, oddly, the sole fedcorp empowered to directly do that work.
NPCCohortGroup|DyadInstruments|descripti: Industrial and scientific focus. Major manufacturer of medical equipment.
NPCCohortGroup|YinshiWellness|descriptio: Industrial and agricultural focus. Large cosmetics division.
NPCCohortGroup|PacifistRebels|descriptio: Some rebel groups seek change through nonviolent means.
NPCCohortGroup|MilitantRebels|descriptio: Many rebel groups have decided to use drastic action to achieve their aims.
NPCCohortGroup|Solarism|description: All life comes from the living stars, and will one day return to them. Our own star, Sol, is the Father of all earthborn life.
NPCCohortGroup|Veilism|description: Our corner of the galaxy is shielded from turmoil by the Great Veil. The Veil supposedly protects us from the Dark Forest dangers of the galaxy. Incidentally, they also believe the Veil protects you from those who are below you. Hmm.
NPCCohortGroup|Nurturism|description: Life is fragile and precious. Humanity must nurture all other life, pruning the malignant only to promote the health of life on Earth.
NPCCohortGroup|Spirology|description: Time is a coil, flowing inward and outward from a Sacred Singularity, the birth of God. The perception of time moving forward is but a reflection of eternity.
NPCCohortGroup|OriginalistWorldTemple|de: Earth is the Matron planet, and humans should neither leave her nor defile her.
NPCCohortGroup|ManagerialClass|descripti: The highest social class. They are guaranteed a living stipend and won't work unless in a managerial position.
NPCCohortGroup|ScientistClass|descriptio: The second-highest social class gets the important things done. They are doctors, scientists, postdoctoral engineers, or highly-credentialed professions like lawyers. They are strongly encouraged to work, but get a living stipend if they are unemployed.
NPCCohortGroup|WorkingClass|description: The working class has a basic living stipend if they are unemployed, but it is rarely enough to cover rent and food. Debt tends to accrue in times of stress. Their landlords and employers, the fedcorps, take advantage of this class's vulnerability.
NPCCohortGroup|UneducatedClass|descripti: People without a two-year degree must work the lowest of jobs. Even with these job, money for food and housing is tough. Debt rates are high. The unemployed face eventual eviction.
NPCCohortGroup|Underclass|description: Anyone may 'fail downwards' into the underclass. Rarely does anyone come back.
NPCCohortGroup|PatronageQuestion|descrip: Every religious person in the city is having to choose how to react to Vorsiber's patronage gambit.
NPCDeal|Ch1_Underclass_Greens|benefit_re: Ongoing practice in rhetoric is provided by intellectuals amongst those you help.
NPCDeal|Ch1_Underclass_Meat|benefit_reas: Minor structural enhancements are provided by engineers amongst those you help.
NPCDeal|Ch1_Underclass_CannedProtein|ben: You're not sure if the people realize what you're feeding them. But YOU know, and that knowledge darkens the aura of your combat androids.
NPCDeal|Ch1_Underclass_SomeWater|benefit: The people know you are holding back, but nonetheless their engineers are willing to help enhance your motor skills.
NPCDeal|Ch1_Underclass_MoreWater|benefit: Small weapons and targeting enhancements are traded from engineers amongst those you help.
NPCDeal|Ch2_AGI_Meals|benefit_reason: The researchers use their engineering skills to enhance the combat power of your most-agile units.
NPCDeal|Ch1_NomadFamilies_VitaminWater|d: Vitamin Water For The Nomad Families
NPCDeal|Ch1_NomadFamilies_VitaminWater|b: Engineers amongst the nomads provide ongoing tutelage in their ways.
NPCDeal|Ch2_Military_Donuts|benefit_reas: Simply carrying around this many donuts requires you to make adjustments to improve the physical strength of your strongest androids.
NPCDeal|Ch2_SecForce_Donuts|benefit_reas: Simply carrying around this many donuts requires you to make adjustments to improve the physical strength of your strongest androids.
NPCDeal|Ch2_RebelAnthroneuroweave|benefi: Handling all that neuroweave seems to be having a positive effect on the cognition of your smartest androids.
NPCDeal|Ch2_SyndicateBrainPals|descripti: Estimated market saturation for this product is 10% of the Wealthy Consumer demographic. After that point, the syndicate will end the deal.
NPCDeal|Ch2_SyndicateBrainPals|benefit_r: Seeing all that human data scrolling past, most of it encrypted, has a positive effect on the hacking skills of your smartest androids.
NPCDebateAction|VerbalSlap|description: A sharp accusation, intended to jolt your opponent and get them thinking about their role in all this.
NPCDebateAction|SneeringInsult|descripti: Bully your opponent. The inappropriateness of your words jolts them.
NPCDebateAction|FieryRhetoric|descriptio: High-minded angry words to stir emotions.
NPCDebateAction|PhysicallyThreaten|descr: Suggest that injury or death may follow if your opponent does not comply.
NPCDebateAction|ThreatenCohort|descripti: Suggest that the future of your opponent's cohort does not look bright if your opponent does not comply.
NPCDebateAction|ThreatenFamily|descripti: Tell your opponent you will find and harm their close relatives if they do not comply.
NPCDebateAction|EncourageDisobedience|de: Encourage your opponent to break the rules just enough to do what you ask.
NPCDebateAction|AppealToMorality|descrip: Point out the ways in which the moral code of your opponent aligns with what you ask.
NPCDebateAction|AppealToHonor|descriptio: If your opponent has a sense of honor, use that against them.
NPCDebateAction|SorrowfulAnecdote|descri: Share a sad story that illustrates why your opponent should do what you want.
NPCDebateAction|OfferHope|description: Suggest that the path to a better life lies in doing what you ask.
NPCDebateAction|ToutPower|description: Make your opponent think about how powerful you are, and will become in the future.
NPCDebateAction|AssertAuthority|descript: Attempt to make your opponent believe that your decisions take precedence over theirs.
NPCDebateAction|AssertDominance|descript: Physically posture in a way that makes your opponent feel smaller.
NPCDebateAction|MisleadingAnecdote|descr: Share a brief -- and entirely fabricated -- story to convince your opponent of a different way to look at the world.
NPCDebateAction|FalsifyStatistics|descri: Show why you are correct, using data you made up.
NPCDebateAction|ReasonedArgument|descrip: Logically and rationally explain why you are correct.
NPCDebateAction|Infrasound|description: Emit fear-inducing sounds near and below the edge of the hearing range of your opponent. They can feel it in their bones.
NPCDebateAction|RevealEvidence|descripti: Show actual data that shows you are correct.
NPCDebateAction|QuoteStatistics|descript: Use data to bolster your claims.
NPCDebateAction|VisionOfBeauty|descripti: Paint a vivid verbal picture -- accurate or not -- of how wonderful things will be if only your opponent will do as you say.
