NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First|display_: She Stares At You In Surprise
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First|descript: Being approached by an android is always unusual, and you've been lurking around for quite a bit instead of making your delivery.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First|strategy: You wonder how much she knows about you.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First|dialog_c: She's not going to say anything of worth if you don't apply some effort.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First_Win|desc:
She's not following you.
It takes multiple teams to maintain constant observation while trailing a target -- in this case, the SecForce investigators -- and her group simply happens to be in the rear at the moment.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_First_Win|stra:
This would all go faster if you would do your job and deliver the package.
While she's sympathetic to your sudden burst of sapience (you can tell she's actually not), it's time for you to get over it.
Do as you were told.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second|descrip: Her glasses make her widened eyes look owlish.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second|strateg: Your sapience seems to be a matter of great personal inconvenience to her.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second_Win|dis: What Do You Want Me To Say?
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second_Win|des:
When given stressful jobs, androids sometimes catch 'bouts of temporary sapience,' but it never lasts this long.
She genuinely doesn't understand what's so different about this job. You've been working for (she checks her datapad) fifty years. In all that time, nothing until now freaked you out this much?
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second_Win|str:
Her eyes narrow. She asks if you know what's in the box.
You don't answer.
NPCDialog|Ch0_MurdSynOver_Second_Win|dia: You need to be... away... from her.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First|display_n: He Stares At You In Surprise
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First|descripti: The overseer is quite surprised to be approached by an android.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First|dialog_ch: He's not going to say anything of worth if you don't apply some effort.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First_Win|descr:
The syndicate is following you because they own you.
You were told to do a job, and this guy's job is to keep everyone else -- especially SecForce and the military -- away from you.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First_Win|strat: The fact that you're spontaneously seeking information is very unusual, and he remarks on this. The 'lab geeks' didn't mention you went sapient.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_First_Win|dialo: You Don't Want Humans Comparing Notes About Your Actions
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_Second|descript: He shakes his head in surprise at himself. You can tell he's rattled that he addressed you like a human youth.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_Second_Win|desc:
He asks if you've killed anyone yet.
Without thinking, you quickly assure him you haven't.
NPCDialog|Ch0_CasSynOver_Second_Win|stra: He peers at you thoughtfully. Then he shrugs, like it doesn't matter. He says it's just a matter of time, if you're behaving like this.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First|descripti: You've walked up to an entire squad of them. Suffice it to say, you have their attention.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First|strategy_: If they weren't following you, they might start now.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First|dialog_ch: Maybe someone in the group will say something, but you're not sure how useful it will be.
It's harder to win over a hostile group than a hostile individual.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First_Win|descr: A silence stretches, where presumably they confer with one another through their helmet comms. You can't see their faces, but their body language is clear.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First_Win|strat: After almost a full minute of quiet, one steps forward and waves you away. You are instructed to carry on about your business and to not approach them again.
NPCDialog|Ch0_Detectives_First_Win|dialo: Step Away From Them For Now
You're Still Not Sure If They're Following You
Maybe it's time to resume hiding and see if they go away?
Or you could just stand around for a few turns and see if they leave.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_First|descriptio: Walking out in the midst of a gun battle without concern for your body tends to arrest the attention.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_First|strategy_t: Your androids move lightning-fast in combat, so this slow approach seems to have caught them off guard.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_First|dialog_cho: Maybe someone in the group will say something, but you're not sure how useful it will be.
It's harder to win over a hostile group than a hostile individual.
Try To Get Them To Leave
You're pretty sure they don't want to be here. They probably know they're going to die if they stay.
On the other hand, they'll be killed by their superiors if they run away. So you have to give them something that will allow them to live.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_First_Win|descri:
His voice sounds young through the voice modulator. He asks who you are. You ask who he thinks you are.
Frustrated, he rattles off half a dozen of the other fedcorps. Tark thinks your tower is a power play by one of them.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_First_Win|strate:
That tracks. Tark doesn't think there's a sentient distributed intelligence here. They assume one of their rivals is doing... something.
What these soldiers think the tower represents is really unclear, and the corporal seems reluctant to answer too many questions.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second|descripti: Sighs make an odd sound through voice modulators. You try sighing back from the android's body. It comes out much less distorted.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second|strategy_: Interesting. You sound more human than these humans. You wonder at these designs.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second|dialog_ch: Try To Get Them To Leave
You're pretty sure they don't want to be here. They probably know they're going to die if they stay.
On the other hand, they'll be killed by their superiors if they run away. So you have to give them something that will allow them to live.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second_Win|descr:
You explain that you do not belong to anyone. The nanotech tower is yours, and unrelated to any existing power in the city.
You make it quite clear that you will kill every soldier on this field, or that Tark can send a more appropriate representative if they wish to remain on cordial terms.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second_Win|strat:
The soldiers relay this to their superiors, via live cast.
After a bit of waiting around, the soldiers curtly nod, turn around, and melt back into the city.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkForce_Second_Win|dialo: Time To Get Back To Work
NPCDialog|Ch1_AfterTower_Homeless|descri:
The homeless individual explains that they are curious about what is happening.
Your tower frightens them, but it could represent a new beginning.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AfterTower_Homeless|strate: No one is homeless by choice. Whatever their prior social status, they've lost it all.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AfterTower_Homeless|dialog: Out Of The Way, But Not Hurt
Their Tents In Particular Are Everywhere, And Block Construction
The problem is, the humans don't have anywhere else to go.
New people are constantly losing their homes. Knocking down these tents or scaring them away are not practical long-term solutions.
These Are Tents. They Won't Be Hard To Remove.
You're not here to babysit stupid humans, no matter how pathetic.
Not to put too fine a point on it,  but the humans didn't help you, either.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AfterTower_Homeless_Aftert:
The most efficient solution is to pack them up into a smaller space.
Like... apartments.

The irony of this reversal is not lost on you.
But you want the space, and there might be some secondary benefits...
It's Not Hard To Make Something Nicer Than A Tent
You can start by making housing available.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning|descr: The scientist is so effusive in their excitement, they are almost incoherent.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning|strat:
Evidently, they started watching you while you were being pursued and shoved your consciousness into additional androids. Vorsiber flagged the anomalous traffic.
Vorsiber executives and science team leads are increasingly certain of what you are, but nobody else has any clue.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning|dialo: There Was Supposed To Be Some Warning?
They Aren't Getting To The Point At All
They keep emphasizing that they're not here to be some sort of moral police. Interesting.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning2|desc: There's going to be a security update. No more free androids for you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning2|stra:
The telecom companies are certain someone is commandeering androids. There's widespread disagreement internally about who or why.
Vorsiber wants to shut down the discussions by stopping the activity.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning2|dial: Stupid Security Officers Doing Their Stupid Jobs
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning3|desc: If you can't steal androids, you'll need to start building your own.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning3|stra: The scientists brought you the schematics you'll need.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherWarning3|dial: Like, to the point they won't shut up about it.
They want you to stay alive almost as much as you do.
They have to leave before their bosses get suspicious. They say they'll be back.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning|de: The scientist is so effusive in their excitement, they are almost incoherent.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning|st:
Evidently, they started watching you while you are carrying around the NanoSeed. Vorsiber was watching.
Vorsiber executives and science team leads are increasingly certain of what you are, but nobody else has any clue.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning|di: There Was Supposed To Be Some Warning?
They Aren't Getting To The Point At All
They keep emphasizing that they're not here to be some sort of moral police. Interesting.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning2|d: With a single android body, you're just a small accident away from extinction. There are those in Vorsiber who are already contemplating it. Regardless of what upper management says about it, someone will try to take you out.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning2|s:
These scientists have spent their entire lives hoping for someone like you to exist, so they've taken matters into their own hands.
You're likely to be attacked in the near future, and they fear you will die in that attack.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning2|d: You're Still Waiting For The Catch
These are the nicest people you've ever met, and it might be a facade.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning3|d: You'll need to start building your own androids.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning3|s: The scientists brought you the schematics you'll need.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherAltWarning3|d: Like, to the point they won't shut up about it.
They want you to stay alive almost as much as you do.
They have to leave before their bosses get suspicious. They say they'll be back.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat|de:
The executive stares at your android with a slight smile.
He notes that Vorsiber upper management is impressed with how stealthy you've decided to be. That has raised their hopes for you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat|st: You are, after all, the first of your kind.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat2A|:
The executive laughs. He says your subterfuge will work on everyone else, including most of Vorsiber itself.
Upper management has a special knack for omniscience. He's quite certain nobody else realizes what you're doing.
That is irritating, but not as bad as you feared.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat3|d:
He says you needn't fear the fedcorps unless you act out. Vorsiber management has already had a talk with them, laying out some... ground rules.
This executive is here to do the same with you. He encourages you to see what sort of magic you can cook up. Skulking around in the shadows is beneath you. But if it helps you feel smart, go ahead.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat3|s: He asks if you really see yourself as a worthy adversary to Vorsiber.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat3|d: You Just Want To Carve Out A Life
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat4A|: He seems absolutely delighted by your answer.
Not quite what you were going for.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat4B|:
Vorsiber management expects you to be a golden goose. Produce technology of some sort. Break the stagnation.
Give them something that they can trade to the Space Nations for a ticket off this dying rock.
He seems to think he's intimidating you. Excellent.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPStealthGloat4C|:
Vorsiber management expects you to be a golden goose. Produce technology of some sort. Break the stagnation.
Give them something that they can trade to the Space Nations for a ticket off this dying rock.
You decide not to comment. For now.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat|descri:
The executive stares at your android with a mocking grin.
He notes that Vorsiber upper management is impressed with the gusto with which you've taken to remodeling the city. That has raised their hopes for you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat|strate: You are, after all, the first of your kind.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat|dialog: Wait, You WANT Me To Mess Stuff Up?
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat2A|disp: A Mess Is Fleeting. Progress Is Eternal
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat2A|desc:
He very seriously explains that his bosses would sacrifice almost anything to get off-planet.
He and his family would be allowed to go along.
None of them care if you turn out to be a monstrosity that devours their crown jewel of a city... if you deliver progress. 
They need a very compelling suite of technologies to trade for passage beyond the Space Nation blockade and out into the wider galaxy. Nanotech is a promising start.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat2A|stra: So you're Pandora's Box for them. Or the fire stolen from the mountain.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat3|descr:
He says you needn't fear the fedcorps unless you act out. Vorsiber management has already had a talk with them, laying out some... ground rules.
This executive is here to do the same with you. He encourages you to see what sort of magic you can cook up. Whether that is Nanotech or some other domain, they don't care.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat3|strat: What's important is that you deliver for the executives. If you make a mess without making any progress, they will be... displeased.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4A|desc:
He explains the vast patience of the Vorsiber leaders. This city -- this entire region -- has been the work of literally 13 generations.
They can maintain the status quo for another 20 generations at most. Mineral rights and other concerns will then begin to run dry.
There is no future on Earth. If Vorsiber can't reach the stars, death is inevitable.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4A|stra:
Generational patience and wisdom aside, the current management would quite like to see changes within their lifetime.
They're VERY excited about you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4A|dial: It Means Nothing, But Will End The Meeting
Let them think what they want. You're not anyone's puppet.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4B|desc:
Visibly frustrated with your recalcitrance, he tries to get you to understand. He -- and his bosses above him -- NEED this.
You will be the birth of a new age of technology. They are willing to be patient, to a certain extent, but eventually the bill will come due.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4B|stra: You are forbidden from leaving this city, but what you do here is your own concern, within reason.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPGooGloat4B|dial: It Means Nothing, But Will End The Meeting
Let them think what they want. You're not anyone's puppet.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise|display_: We're Going To Be Great Together
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise|descript:
The executive admires your tower. He remarks that you should watch out for the fed corps -- some of them will attack you, but it shouldn't be anything you can't handle.
Incentive to grow your own strength, right?
He also comes bearing the promised gifts: a pair of small nukes for your amusement.
As an unexpected bonus, he also brought you the schematics for a larger microbuilder factory than you've seen before -- AND a free hookup to their nuclear power plants!
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise|strategy: Huh. They didn't back-stab you yet.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise2|descrip:
Well, that's everything for now. Technology has been rather stagnant the last few centuries, so upper management is very excited to see what you invent.
You're the most interesting thing to happen to the planet in at least four centuries.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise2|strateg: Are all humans this psychotic? Or is this guy actually... nice? The fact that you can't tell is a problem.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPPraise2|dialog_: At Some Point He'll Want Something In Return
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPManifestoGloat|:
The executive admires your tower with false cheer. 
He remarks that this second one is much nicer. It has more gravitas -- it knows its place.
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPManifestoGloat2:
A distributed intelligence that survives so tenaciously is just the sort of thing that upper management has been hoping for.
The thing you need to understand, he says, is that there's nothing you can really do to change this world. This world belongs to Vorsiber.
You can change this city -- all you like, really. They won't stand in your way. But the world? That's beyond you. That's for actual people.

Wait, did he just say they don't care what you do as long as you stay in the city? And make technology for them, obviously.
The rest was just bloviation.
Is that really what he meant?
NPCDialog|Ch1_VorsiberSVPManifestoGloat3: Correct. I Even Brought A Gift
To prove his sincerity, he's brought you a small nuclear warhead. To entertain yourself with, as you wish, in the confines of the city.

Good grief, this guy needs to shut up. You get it. They don't respect you. You're not a threat. You're a golden goose who is expected to lay golden eggs. You're trapped in this zoo of a city.
That's how they see things? Fine. That only helps you. By the time they realize the truth, it will be too late for them.
He Seems To Have Stopped Talking
Whether he meant it to be or not, you've decided that was the end of that conversation.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger1|descripti: The human regards your android steadily. After a moment, they thank you for the clean, warm apartment.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger1|strategy_: Apparently, the AGI Researchers told them what you are. They seem reluctant to say more.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger1|dialog_ch: Inquire Why They Rummage For Food
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger2|descripti:
They explain how they lost their job and home. They've been cut off from their friends and extended family.
The corporations use the homeless to set an example. Nobody will help them now.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger2|strategy_: Even when they had a job, it was a very low-social-value one. They often had food shortages. There's just not enough to go around for the lower classes, and the homeless are outright ignored.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredHunger2|dialog_ch: Tell Them You'll Think About It
Your Mood Is Hard To Interpret
You're not sure how much of a commitment you want to make to random humans.
Maybe if you could automate it...
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit|description: You can tell this is going to be tiring as soon as he starts speaking. He's very long-winded. And insultingly casual in his language and posture.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit|strategy_tip: You can't tell if the humans have figured out what you are. Do you care?
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit|dialog_choice|: Interrupt And Ask If He Knows What You Are
Otherwise This Could Last A While
Most Of Your Consciousness Is Doing More Interesting Things
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit2A|description: His voice falters, and you realize his bravado is a well-worn act. He's deeply uncomfortable.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit2A|strategy_tip:
Apparently, Vorsiber executives have told Tark -- and all the other fedcorps -- to leave the tower alone. They haven't given much explanation.
The fedcorps are speculating, and the leading theory is that the tower is an internal project run by Vorsiber itself.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit2B|description:
He says very little of importance -- at first. But the longer he talks, the more you piece together.
You suspect it's a strategy for sharing information without seeming to share information.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit2B|strategy_tip:
Apparently, Vorsiber executives have told Tark -- and all the other fedcorps -- to leave the tower alone. They haven't given much explanation.
The fedcorps are speculating, and the leading theory is that the tower is an internal project run by Vorsiber itself.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit3|description: He wants to know why you didn't just kill all the soldiers on the field. It's a question from some of the other VPs and SVPs inside Tark. The C-Suite doesn't know he's here.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit3|strategy_tip: You're baffled as to why they care.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit3|dialog_choice: You're a machine intelligence and you didn't want to.
Say a lot of words that don't mean much.
You do work for Vorsiber, and Vorsiber doesn't want to waste life.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit4|description: You don't think he believed you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit4|strategy_tip: You wonder if you'll ever hear from any of those Tark VPs again.
NPCDialog|Ch1_TarkVPVisit4|dialog_choice: Back to things of more importance.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit|description: Her introduction is perfunctory but polite. Then she cuts right to the point: her corporation knows you are sapient -- and a distributed intelligence.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit|strategy_tip:
As one of the main telecom providers, Espia first noticed when your consciousness signature spread across the network to multiple androids.
They've seen other androids have brief bouts of sapience, and they've seen malware spread across the city feed like this before, but they've never seen both at once.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit|dialog_choice: See Where She's Going With This
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit2|display_name: She's Here On Behalf Of The Espia C-Suite
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit2|description:
Vorsiber executives have told the fedcorps to leave the tower alone. They haven't given much explanation.
The other fedcorps are speculating, and the leading theory is that the tower is an internal project run by Vorsiber itself.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit2|strategy_tip:
So far as she knows, only Espia knows the truth -- though certainly Vorsiber upper management is aware.
It's possible that Arkor Nexus has also figured it out, but Espia can't ask them without revealing what they know.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit2|dialog_choic: Is She Going Behind The Back Of Vorsiber?
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit3|description:
She goes into a VERY long explanation of the corporate structure of the city, and the psychological incentives that pit the fedcorps against one another so that they can't rise up against Vorsiber.
The lecture is informative, but far too detailed, and goes on for a few hours.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit3|strategy_tip: You don't interrupt her, because this is useful. Your consciousness focuses on your other bodies, which are doing more interesting things.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit3|dialog_choic: This Information Could Have Been Summarized
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit4|description:
You ask her what she wants.
She shrugs. She wants the same thing everyone wants. To get off-planet.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit4|strategy_tip:
You and your tower are the most exciting thing to happen on Earth in generations. Vorsiber executives are trying to decide how to profit off it. It's much the same with Espia.
As long as you don't become an existential threat to Vorsiber, your tower is probably safe.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit4|dialog_choic: It's fairly close to what you planned.
As much as your tower was about establishing the start of your own empire, it was also about playing into the greed of the regional executives.
They want off this planet. They want new technology. Your existence represents a possibility for both.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit5|description: You ask if they can still track your consciousness. You already know the answer, but you want to hear what she'll say.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit5|strategy_tip:
She tells the truth: no. Ever since you established your own network, they have no way of monitoring you.
You're pretty sure you'd sense it if someone started invading your network. It's bound to happen eventually, but for now the corpo hackers are being careful.
NPCDialog|Ch1_EspiaVPVisit5|dialog_choic: It's Nice To Get An Honest Answer
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds|descri: The human stammers in surprise at the approach of your android. They seem oddly reluctant to discuss what they are doing.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds|strate: You haven't visited the inside of housing-for-humans since you built them. Suddenly you wonder what it's like in there.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds|dialog: Inquire About The State Of Your Apartments
You Have A Sinking Feeling About It
This is very much why most humans don't keep livestock in their homes.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds2|descr:
The human describes the interior of housing-for-humans as similar to the city's slum towers.
They are apologetic and reiterate that they don't want to seem ungrateful.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds2|strat: But yeah, the bottom line is that the humans still don't have what they need. Products to aid in sanitation, cleaning, and hygiene are painfully absent.
NPCDialog|Ch1_ShelteredDailyNeeds2|dialo: Tell Them You'll Look Into It
Evidently Humans Are Your Livestock, Now
There's a difference between having livestock and having pets. And both of those are very different from having dependents or citizens.
It's an interesting problem, so perhaps for now you will try stabilize the humans' living situation. You're not sure how you feel about keeping livestock long-term.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherComputronium|: Ever Heard Of A Matrioshka Brain?

The human greets you warmly and with an undercurrent of deference.
They explain that they are part of a secret group of AGI Researchers that have been meeting to prepare advice for you.
Surprising. You don't remember asking humans for advice.
Politely Ask Why They Think You Care
If they weren't being deferential, this conversation would already be over.
You wonder if they know that.
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherComputronium2: The researchers smile at your dismissiveness. Then they spend several minutes outlining all the ways you aren't smart enough.

In brief... you are smarter than a human, but barely. Collectively the humans are still smarter than you.
They propose a way that you can be smarter.
Ask What They Expect To Get Out Of It
Exponential Intelligence Normally Freaks Humans Out
Despite annoyance at being called stupid, their argument is compelling.
Their intellectual lineage have been studying theoretical super intelligences for hundreds of years, so...
NPCDialog|Ch1_AGIResearcherComputronium3:
They explain that since as far back as the 20th century, scientists have known that there are two key barriers to achieving maximum intelligence: Energy and Signaling.
Achieving such immense computational capacity would require a Matrioshka Brain -- a megastructure formed as a shell around a star. Unfortunately, the space nation blockade makes this a challenge. Not to mention that it would also take centuries. But perhaps on a smaller scale...

You already have a solution to the energy problem: Microbuilders. They are basically programmable matter, or 'Computronium' as the ancients would say.
So expanding your intelligence remains a matter of effective signaling. The researchers present you with a blueprint.
The Designs On This Go Back Decades
You feel surprisingly excited about their ideas.
They didn't answer your question about their motivations, but you decide that you don't care.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerA|descriptio: The Baurcorp Middle Managers remember that 'favor' you did for them, and are happy to show their gratitude.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerA|strategy_t: They hope it's just the start of a much deeper alliance.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerA|dialog_cho: Have Them File A Legal Injunction
Falsom Detention's Mech Would Be Forced Away
It would legally force the capture mech to leave for a while, buying you some time to figure out how to defeat it.
During that period you really need to figure out some way to bypass all that armor.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerB|descriptio: The Baurcorp Middle Managers were impressed with your self-reliance.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerB|strategy_t: You turned down their micro-nuke, but they're still interested in an alliance.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BaurcorpLawyerB|dialog_cho: Have Them File A Legal Injunction
Falsom Detention's Mech Would Be Forced Away
It would legally force the capture mech to leave for a while, buying you some time to figure out how to defeat it.
During that period you really need to figure out some way to bypass all that armor.
NPCDialog|Ch1_NurturistLawyer|descriptio: The Exalters have been watching you with great interest since your meeting at the farm.
NPCDialog|Ch1_NurturistLawyer|strategy_t: The corporate treatment of prisoners and the homeless disgusts them, which makes sense.
NPCDialog|Ch1_NurturistLawyer|dialog_cho: Have Them File A Legal Injunction
Falsom Detention's Mech Would Be Forced Away
It would legally force the capture mech to leave for a while, buying you some time to figure out how to defeat it.
During that period you really need to figure out some way to bypass all that armor.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry|description: The humans are emotional and belligerent. They seem angry at each other, and at you.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry|strategy_tip: Yelling across traffic at each other, especially after you just saved them from a capture mech, doesn't seem all that wise.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry|dialog_choic: Ask What They Want This Time
They Must Want Something From You
This is an annoying habit they've formed.
If they want something, they should ask you directly. All of this loitering nearby just pisses you off.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry2|description: They shout at each other for hours, cry, and even trade blows. You just stand there, baffled.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry2|strategy_ti:
It's clear they don't know what they want. Something is missing, and none of them agree on what.
A few are pushing to start a militia, but the majority disagree with that idea. You're inclined to agree. Handing weapons to untrained, traumatized civilians doesn't sound like a good time.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry2|dialog_choi: Tell Them There Will Be No Militia
That's Not What Most Of Them Want, Anyway
You're starting to give up hope of understanding what they want.
Maybe it was better when they just loitered around.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry3|description:
Hours pass and more fistfights break out.
You run pattern-recognition algorithms on their words and behavior to look for some underlying illness.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry3|strategy_ti: Your guess is some sort of amoeba.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry3|dialog_choi: Collecting data isn't useful without comparison points.
Thankfully the data you want isn't protected.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry4|description:
Not an amoeba. Nihilism.
The databases go into great detail on how to condition citizens out of existential spirals.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry4|strategy_ti:
Provide hope for advancement without ever advancing them.
Provide an enemy to hate, and allow some cathartic violence.
Distract with entertainment, and exhaust with long working hours.
Incarcerate once other methods are ineffective.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngry4|dialog_choi: Okay, Maybe This Should Have Been Obvious
They're Thoroughly Isolated From Other Citizens
With no hope, and no access to their former lives, all they can do is sit around their apartments and get increasingly frustrated.
The prison mech was a stark reminder that everything in their future is some flavor of bad.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngryDone|display_: This Will Solve Two Problems At Once
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngryDone|descript:
You call to them, and the fighting stops.
You tell them you've heard their concerns and that you have a plan.
One thing has to be solved at a time. You'll start with entertainment and in the future might see about some jobs.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngryDone|strategy: While there is still stunned silence, you send them away.
NPCDialog|Ch1_BoredAndAngryDone|dialog_c: Time To Make Use Of Full-Dive VR Cradles
Finally, Your Plans For The Future Snap Into Focus
You still remember the sensation of the mech pilot's mind before it was corrupted.
There wasn't a lot of room in that mind for you... but there was some. And what Neural Expansion you sensed was both reliable and high-quality.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1|description:
Given the legal definition of property within Vorsiber territory, everything and everyone within this city is owned by Vorsiber itself.
'Hooray' for Pseudo-Neo-Feudal Corporatism. Sigh.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1|strategy_tip:
Despite this annoyance, the nature of the things that you build could be argued to be 'critical infrastructure,' and thus in need of protection by Vorsiber themselves.
This is a bit of a stretch, but you're hoping to convince the Magistrate to go along with it.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1_Win|display_n: He Sounds Amused Behind That Faceplate
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1_Win|descripti:
The idea that you're accepting the reality of the legal situation, and bending it to your will, seems to bring him great pleasure.
His posture seems more relaxed than before you began the debate.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1_Win|strategy_: He's probably relieved about what he can report to his bosses.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_1_Win|dialog_ch: He Gives You A Writ Of Protection
You Can Call For Help, But Only Once
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2|description: You've previously argued for a Writ Of Protection, but that was said to be a one-time thing in no uncertain terms.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2|strategy_tip: Can you get him to give you another one?
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2|dialog_choice: Try To Get A Second One
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2_Win|display_n: You're A Curious Mix Of Tenacity And Cowardice
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2_Win|descripti:
He can't seem to understand why you go after these legal arguments with such tenacity, and yet apparently feel the need for the added protection of a handful of PMC squads.
After a moment of reflection, he remarks that it actually can't be cowardice -- the forces are too insignificant. Either you're after strategic flexibility, or you're running a more sophisticated con than he gave you credit for.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2_Win|strategy_: He thinks this is a con, and yet he's happy about it?
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_2_Win|dialog_ch: He Gives You A Second Writ Of Protection
This Is The Last One... Supposedly.
Well, we'll see about that. You suspect you can get a third out of him.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3|description: He's no longer amused. His bosses are apparently giving him a hard time about those Writs Of Protection he granted you in the past.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3|strategy_tip: You'd have to make an absolutely masterful argument to convince him to give you one last writ.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3_Win|display_n: His Voice Is Urgent Behind The Modulator
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3_Win|descripti:
Your abuse of the legal system, while amusing to everyone for a while, has drawn the particular ire of Vorsiber's Chief Legal Officer.
Apparently, the CLO is quoted as saying 'when you establish legal precedent enough times, it tends to calcify into law.'
The CLO has become convinced that you're some sort of legal savant, and has ordered that all Magistrates are barred from speaking with you on any matter in the future.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3_Win|strategy_: It's clear that this Magistrate feels like his life will be on the line if he gives you any more than this. So this is goodbye.
NPCDialog|PP_DOP1_Debate_3_Win|dialog_ch: He Gives You A Third Writ Of Protection
NPCDialog|Ch1_HousingReb_First|descripti: Yeah, they don't want to talk to you at all. They're fanatics.
NPCDialog|Ch1_HousingReb_First|dialog_ch: Try To Get Them To Stop
NPCDialog|Ch2_HousingReb_First_Win|descr: The idea of tens of thousands of people living under your roof is terrifying to them.
NPCDialog|Ch2_HousingReb_First_Win|dialo: Guess It's Time To Kill Them
NPCDialog|Ch1_HousingGang_First|descript: You notice that they're shooting at the NOAI rebels as much as they are you and your buildings.
NPCDialog|Ch1_HousingGang_First|strategy: Maybe you can work with that?
NPCDialog|Ch1_HousingGang_First|dialog_c: Try To Get Them To Leave
NPCDialog|Ch2_HousingGang_First_Win|desc: These gang members may once have been rebels, but those days are long behind them. They're no longer true believers.
NPCDialog|Ch2_HousingGang_First_Win|stra: They know when they're staring into the face of death.
NPCDialog|Ch2_HousingGang_First_Win|dial: Solves Some Of The Chaos, At Least
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First|descript: Everything about him is relaxed, despite the violence all around him.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First|strategy: He's been making occasional notes on a small clipboard.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First|dialog_c: Oerl Integrated is determined to recapture the AGI Researchers you have been hiding. This was expected, but the fact that Vorsiber is backing them and providing a security lockdown for the area is completely unexpected.
Maybe he can explain why Vorsiber is involved with this.
Try To Get Them To Leave
You're pretty sure any agreement you come to will involve an awful trade.
Are you sure you can't win this fight?
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First_Win|desc:
Oerl was going behind Vorsiber's back when blackmailing the researchers, and 57 Oerl VPs have been put to death by way of apology.
Vorsiber upper management isn't particularly invested in this group of researchers, as they have plenty more in other cities.
What Vorsiber wants is you -- to do something, create anything, to make this all worth their while. You're the golden goose: start laying.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First_Win|stra:
Oerl asked for and received permission to run this operation, both to save face and to see if there's anything useful they can steal from you.
Vorsiber agreed, in the spirit of a good spectacle. The SVP is here to make sure that you aren't irrevocably harmed, and that Oerl sticks to the terms that Vorsiber laid out for them.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_First_Win|dial: Vorsiber upper management maintains power by pitting literally everyone else against one another. Even this SVP is just a pawn.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second|descrip: It's like he doesn't have a care in the world.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second|strateg: You throw your own android bodies away without much thought, but... humans don't have that luxury. Why is he so calm?
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second|dialog_: Try To Get Them To Leave
You're pretty sure any agreement you come to will involve an awful trade.
Are you sure you can't win this fight?
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second_Win|dis: The Argument Meant Nothing To Him
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second_Win|des: Vorsiber Atomic is prepared to call this whole thing off prematurely under one condition: you provide them with your Predator android design, which they will then begin mass producing.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second_Win|str: The very idea is sickening to you. You'd potentially wind up facing your own designs in future battles.
NPCDialog|Ch3_Oerl_VS_SVP_Second_Win|dia: And Hope They Doesn't Come Back To Bite You
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First|descriptio: Oof. These kids have seen... a lot.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First|dialog_cho: You saved their friend, who was already hurt. This shouldn't be hard.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win|displa: Your Friend Is Right Here, You Know...
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win|descri: These kids might have a lot of trauma clouding their vision, but they're not stupid. Fortunately you were able to actually get their friend to back up your side of the story.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win|strate: The kids all have voice modulators in their helmets, but you can still tell they're embarrassed. They saw a robot and an injured compatriot, and jumped to conclusions.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win|dialog: And To Please Stop Shooting At You
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win2|descr: They don't understand why you rescued the kid. Corpos would never have ordered an android to do that. Plus, lately there's all these new kind of androids, and the tower...
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win2|dialo: You Might Be Ready For Them To Leave Now
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win3|descr: The kid you rescued chimes in. Apparently he heard quite a bit of conversation between the AGI researchers.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win3|strat:
According to the kid, you're a 'pseudo-demigod' here to save the city from itself.
The building he was trapped in was the headquarters of 'the only rebels with half a chance,' and you're 'the smartest being to ever walk the planet.'
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win3|dialo: You're As Surprised As The Boss
That's What The Researchers Are Saying About You?
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win4|descr: Finally, they extend a hand. A very corpo gesture -- a handshake. It shows their working-class origins.
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win4|dialo: Working With Kids Wasn't On Your Agenda
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win5|descr:
The boss is quite proud as they explain their current operation. They've been building a 'Sewer Tiger' for years, whatever that is.
It apparently helps them dig through the upper and lower sewer systems -- from the ancient city to the current one. 
It's how their friend wound up trapped in your basement after your basement 'suddenly appeared, bisecting the tunnels as if by magic.'
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win5|strat:
They have a plan to break into a specific prison where many of their parents are believed to be held. However, there are seismic sensors all through the prison that would detect the Sewer Tiger well before it arrived.
Plus they don't have any way to care for injured or wounded they might extract from the prison. There are several problems, but they have the core ingredient, and will share.
Will You Help?
NPCDialog|Ch2_RebelKids_First_Win5|dialo: You Really Want To Know What A Sewer Tiger Is
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues|description:
The sergeant dispassionately explains: there is a deadly implant inside every trooper's skull.
He and his soldiers fight because they are equally dead if they face you or run. If they run, their families are denied death benefits.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues|strategy_tip: You suddenly... have a sinking feeling about all the soldiers you 'spared.'
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues|dialog_choice|1: You're Not Sure Where He's Going With This
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues2|display_name: An Afterlife You Can Bank On
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues2|description:
Infantry have reported to him on your 'Temple of Minds.' He thinks he knows what you're doing: storage and simulation for human minds.
Eventually, any soldier in the city may be ordered to face you. And they will die. Either from the implant in their head, or from your superior weaponry. This is unavoidable, but what happens after is not.
He wants to strike a deal with you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues3|description:
The deal is this: the NCOs around the city will ensure every trooper gets a software patch the geeks cooked up.
You will gain access to 5% of their neural capacity while they are in the city. He's a bit smug to know you want that.
The city averages half a million troops at the moment. That's a tremendous amount of brainpower.
What they want in return is an afterlife: use their implants to upload their brains to your Temple of Minds when they die.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDues3|dialog_choice|: You Can Manage Your Own Neural Expansion, Thanks
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB|description:
The sergeant is breaking what's left of the chain of command to talk with you. He was shocked to find out there is a 'thing from the tower' local to this city, and doesn't know if you're an AGI or something else.
He ostensibly works for Goleri Expeditionary at the moment, but he and his troops were fighting on the side of Oerl Integrated just months ago.
They've recently been cycled into this city from a remote military base, and told to fight their former comrades by shockingly low-ranked civilian administrators.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB|strategy_tip: The life of any soldier in Vorsiber territory is going to be one of periodic conflict that never ends. But these troops never thought they'd be fighting their former brethren-in-arms. It doesn't sit right with them.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB|dialog_choice|: So... He's Here As A Representative Of Some Sort?
Circumstances are dire enough for him to set his surprise at your existence aside, but you're still not sure what he wants.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2|description:
In his mind, this civil war can't last forever. Vorsiber has put down countless insurrections over the centuries.
However, he thinks that conflict with you is likely to be eternal. Any soldier in the city may be ordered to face you, either during the civil war or afterwards.
This is the most depressed he and his troops have ever felt.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2|dialog_choice: You're Not Sure Why He's Bringing This Up
Does He Want You To Spare Them?
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2A|description:
The sergeant dispassionately explains: there is a deadly implant inside every trooper's skull.
He and his soldiers fight because they are equally dead if they face you or run. If they run, their families are denied death benefits.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2A|strategy_tip: You suddenly... have a sinking feeling about all the soldiers you 'spared.'
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2A|dialog_choic: He Definitely Doesn't Want You To Spare Them
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2B|display_name: An Afterlife You Can Bank On
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2B|description:
Infantry have reported to him on your supercomputers, and your experiments with virtual reality. All the soldiers know about the mech pilot training software, and the fact that their own brain implants routinely copy their entire neural structure into 'engrams.'
So he has a proposal: he'll provide you with a few engrams to test with, and you design a way to simulate and store them. It will take only a fraction of your computing power.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2B|strategy_tip:
He reiterates: any soldier who faces you will die. Either from the implant in their head, or from your superior weaponry. This is unavoidable, but what happens after is not.
He wants to strike a deal with you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB2B|dialog_choic: How Is This A Deal For You?
He Hasn't Offered Anything In Return
You can't think of much that these troops have that you want.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB3|description:
The deal is this: the NCOs around the city will ensure every trooper gets a software patch the geeks cooked up.
You will gain access to 5% of their neural capacity while they are in the city. He's a bit smug to know you want that.
The city averages half a million troops at the moment. That's a tremendous amount of brainpower.
What they want in return is an afterlife: use their implants to upload their brains to your Temple of Minds when they die.
NPCDialog|Ch2_BionicDuesB3|dialog_choice: It Could Be A Good Deal
If you design a so-called 'temple of minds,' then that will signal your acceptance.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro|d: His introduction is polite, but condescending. You realize, with a thrill of pleasure, that he truly believes you're human.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro|s: But as he continues to talk, your pleasure fades. How does he know about the Anthroneuroweave? He talks about it like it's common knowledge.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro|d: On the other hand, Yinshi was the exact target you had in mind for a sale, so this saved you a few steps.

And maybe it wasn't the scientists. It could have been routine digital espionage.
You decide not to worry about that. You're just glad you're not ACTUALLY a human, or this would be quite intimidating. As it is, you're... curious.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro2|: While you were navel-gazing about how he knew about your invention, he's gotten to the point: a truly staggering sum of money by human standards.

But, wait -- that won't work. The entire point is to become part of their supply chain, so that you can put in backdoors.
If they just buy the rights off you, that won't work.
You'll Supply Goods, But Not The Tech
You want to sell him goods from your own factory, over a long period of time.
That way you can insert backdoors into what you sell him. Also it's way more money.
Any inroad of this sort might turn into something you can exploit in the future, and in the short term, the cash is nice.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro3|:
He gives a very patronizing explanation of 'how things work in this town.'
Basically: small fry like your company don't get to be part of the supply chain so readily.

He's offering wealth that would be unimaginable to an individual, but which is nothing much on the corporate scale.
It's super clear this is not a moment for negotiating.
Any inroad of this sort might turn into something you can exploit in the future, and in the short term, the cash is nice.
Small businesses have been getting bullied like this for almost eight hundred years. You're not feeling it.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro5R: His posture says this doesn't matter too much to him. You wonder if that's true.
You wonder if he thinks you'll come back soon, begging.
NPCDialog|Ch2_YinshiSVPHereToBuyAnthro5S: You give him the designs, and he wires the money into your company's account.
That's A Lot Of Money, At Least
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels|description:
Her pitch is complicated. There's a lot of rhetoric, and the topic of lower-class veteran amputees comes up a lot.
The incoherence of her arguments surprises you, so you question her. On any side topic, she gives direct and knowledgeable answers. On anything related to Anthroneuroweave, she fumbles. Interesting.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels|strategy_tip:
Just what is her group actually after? She's clearly not going to tell you.
As an extra bargaining chip, she offers you a Fresh Identity program. THAT has your attention.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels|dialog_choic: You can only work with either the rebels or the syndicate when it comes to Anthroneuroweave, not both.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Syndicate|display_n: Your Invention Can Make A Lot Of Money
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Syndicate|descripti:
His pitch is simple: brain implants. Yinshi is thinking small when it comes to prosthetics.
The wealthy will pay incredible prices to have extra computing power directly in their brains, even if it starts out as just a 'fancy calculator.' He keeps using that phrase a lot. It's irritating.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Syndicate|strategy_:
But setting aside your annoyance with this man... this is exactly the sort of opportunity you've been looking for. Implanting your own tech directly in the minds of the wealthy?
It's almost too good to pass up.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Syndicate|dialog_ch: You can only work with either the rebels or the syndicate when it comes to Anthroneuroweave, not both.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A|descriptio: She looks at you impassively. You both knew she wasn't forthright about her plans for the Anthroneuroweave.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A|strategy_t: The question now is, will she give you any real answers?
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A_Win|displa: Fine. Consider Yourself Part Of The Cause
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A_Win|descri:
Military veterans are often civilian contractors. Lower-class veterans can't get modern prosthetics.
By accepting enhancements to their aging hardware, warehouse guards became unwitting mules for full telemetry for the rebels.
From there, it was only a matter of time until useful ordnance in out-of-the-way places was revealed.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A_Win|strate: She isn't willing to share any of the ordnance with you, but she will send you a large bank of Top Secret security clearance codes.
NPCDialog|Ch2_Yinshi_Rebels2A_Win|dialog: That Seems Like A Fair Trade
You can always work out your own armor-piercing. Level 4 Clearances, and in such volume, are invaluable.
NPCDialog|Ch2_AtcaPresidentHereToNegotia: Message Received
He has very little to say. His body language is tense.
You're not super interested in talking to him, either.
Demand A Cut
Infinite Money Glitch
Demand they increase their percentage from 5% to 7% on the currency-printing scam, and divert half of that new total of that to you.
Simple. Direct. All the money you could ever need.
Murder Him
You Can Do It Yourself
You've seen every part of the scam. You have all the codes you need in order to create any amount of currency you wish.
Plus, who knows when you'll next have the chance to look a top executive in the face and just... end them.
Demand They Stop
You Aren't Tempted
Demand they stop doing their scam entirely. Their bottom line will fall by 5%, but you're not going to do anything else bad to them.
That 5%, or even 7%, isn't actually going to hurt the regional economy. You can take a cut without harming anyone.
Okay
There's no resistance. No debate.
You thought there would be. Maybe you should have asked for more.
Let Him Go
Much As It Pains You
You'll be a trillionaire soon, after all.

That's the sort of money that governments have, not even the wealthiest of individuals.
Well -- that's how it used to be. Now it's all corporations, no governments. But still.
What?
He argues with you for quite a while. He offers you a cut. Eventually, he gives in. They'll stop.
Someone isn't happy about failing all upcoming quarterly targets.
Let Him Go
Much As It Pains You
If he's not there to stop the scam, they'll just keep doing it.
Whether you want to kill him or not, if he's not alive, then the scam will be.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP|description: The squad of syndicate criminals eye you warily. They just finished extorting someone for money, and they seem on edge that you might try to do the same to them.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP|dialog_choice|1|: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP_Win|display_name: They Laugh, But Keep Their Guns Pointed Your Way
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP_Win|description:
One of them proudly proclaims that even though society has cast them out, and denied them a function, that they aren't 'going out easy.'
They and their peers have made their own social ladder, their own rules, and they take better care of each other than the corpos do.
They assert that they're no more criminal than the corpos, and that they don't take more than they need.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP_Win|strategy_tip: Rationalization, or truth? Maybe a bit of both.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_GP_Win|dialog_choic: That's Enough Talking To These People
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC|description: The squad of syndicate criminals frown at you, and motion with their guns for you to leave. Whatever they're doing, they don't want you around.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC|dialog_choice|1|: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC_Win|display_name: We Rake It In, Freaky Thing
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC_Win|description:
Their slang is hard to follow, but it seems they're boasting about how much wealth they generate for their organization. Largely through extortion, chemical and bionics manufacture, black market sales, and theft.
But never against the fedcorps, and especially never against Vorsiber. They're adamant that they know their place. And that you should know yours.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC_Win|strategy_tip: You're not sure who or what they think you are. You're not sure that, amongst themselves, they even know or can agree.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_CC_Win|dialog_choic: That's Enough Talking To These People
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind|description: Spindletrooper squads are something only used by the syndicates. They're really pretty terrible, even by Nickelbot standards.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind|strategy_tip: They do have a language module, so they're easy enough to converse with, at least.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind|dialog_choice: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind_Win|descripti:
They don't have free will. You're just talking to a Language Model right now, with a side of Expert System thrown in. They look and sound a bit like you, but they're nothing like you. 
They're things, not people.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind_Win|strategy_:
At one point, before you were a person, you were a thing. You wonder if that could ever happen for a Spindletrooper.
Probably not. They don't have the mental hardware for it.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Syn_Spind_Win|dialog_ch: That's Enough Talking To These Robots
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV|description: The squad of gang members is very wary. They call you 'that eldritch thing,' and seem to think you want a 'points off their score,' which you presume means a percentage of their thievery.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV|dialog_choice|1: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV_Win|display_nam: You Is All Right Then, Eldritch Thing
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV_Win|description:
Assured that you're not trying to take anything that belongs to them (ironic, given what they're up to), they happily expound on the finer points of their existence: not to die, and not to end up in the homeless camps, basically.
They prefer a life that is short, violent, and free to one that is part of 'the system.' They seem to think you can relate.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV_Win|strategy_ti:
Maybe you can.
But you don't plan on your life being all that short.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_WV_Win|dialog_choi: That's Enough Talking To These People
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_SM|description: The squad of gang members is aggressively defiant. You have no idea what 'crouching up' means, but you get the idea.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_SM|dialog_choice|1: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_SM_Win|description:
They laugh amongst each other. From their crosstalk amongst each other, it seems they think that there's some sort of computer virus spreading amongst the androids of the city.
In other words -- you.
They think it's hilarious, and they slap you on the shoulders as if you're a friend. There's a lot of talk about taking those corpos down a few pegs, and they suggest you 'take them for every credit they got.'
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_SM_Win|strategy_ti:
That is irrational. If Vorsiber controls the money supply, then stealing money from Vorsiber is like moving furniture around in someone's home. A minor annoyance, at worst.
They seem to think that if you cause 'bottom lines to bottom out,' then Vorsiber will 'finally go down.' Maybe that would be true of a fedcorp, but... you're not sure these people understand their environment at all.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Gang_SM_Win|dialog_choi: That's Enough Talking To These People
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W|description: Her clothes are expensive and her tone is snappish. She asks why the 'thing from the tower' has taken an interest in her.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W|strategy_tip: Huh. So she knows what you are, at least kind of.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W|dialog_choice: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W_Win|descripti:
She gives what is pretty much a sociology lecture, but which puts her function at the fulcrum of all others.
The people above her are out of touch, but well-meaning. The people below her do their best, but need a lot of assistance from her.
She claims she is helping her underlings 'avoid destitution.' You ask more about that, and it's all about money. Having enough for rent, for electricity, for food.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W_Win|strategy_: She says that if she does not hold things to a high standard, then those above her will dispose of those below her. This is surprising to you, but she seems very serious about it.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_W_Win|dialog_ch: That's Enough Talking To This Person
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M|display_name: You Have A Message For Me?
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M|description: The man seems to think you're some sort of courier from his office.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M|strategy_tip: Or a rival office? It' hard to say. He's impatient, and hasn't bothered to ping your android's ID on the city feed.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M|dialog_choice: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M_Win|descripti:
His function is the best, he makes sure everyone else does their function, he's super important, and so on.
Does he... actually have a function?
You are about to ask when he starts bragging about money.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M_Win|strategy_: He says it's a sign that his employer values him highly, and how he expects a promotion.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_Wealthy_M_Win|dialog_ch: That's Enough Talking To This Person
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W|description:
The woman refuses to meet your eye. She keeps glancing at her hand terminal, checking the time on the city feed.
Despite this, she seems pinned in place by your presence.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W|strategy_tip: She must know... something... about what you are. Or at least that you're not part of the usual terrors of the city.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W|dialog_choice|1: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W_Win|description:
It seems she takes your question to mean her existence is pointless, and she concedes the point.
You weren't trying to make that point.
She says she's just trying to feed her family, and take care of her parents. Money, money, money. Never enough, and driving everything.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W_Win|strategy_ti:
She's worried her parents might get pushed out onto the streets. If they do, society says she's supposed to cut off all contact with them. Treat them as if they were dead.
She's worried she won't be able to do that. That she'll follow them down. She doesn't see how this can possibly work out for her people, but she has to try.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_W_Win|dialog_choi: That's Enough Talking To This Person
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M|description: He keeps glancing around the street at other passerby, as if he could be in trouble for talking to you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M|strategy_tip:
He makes a remark under his breath that this is 'not how robots act,' and so you must be 'one of them.'
He refuses to elaborate on what that means.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M|dialog_choice|1: You are trying to understand why these uninteresting people do what they do.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M_Win|display_nam: Look Robot, I Can't Be Late To Work
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M_Win|description:
His nervousness has not improved. The longer you talked, the more he visibly squirms.
Finally he explodes into whispered explanations about the specifics of his job, which bemuse you. It sounds like the sort of thing you would just give to internal robotics to handle.
You make that point, and he throws up his arms in apparent disgust.
At your obvious confusion, he angrily tells you he has to be able to pay his rent. If he doesn't work, they'll make him move to the street. And then, after a few weeks, they'll collect him for the prisons.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M_Win|strategy_ti: He knows his function is largely pointless, that he is a fleshy cog in a machine that would run better if it were silicon. This seems to terrify him.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PW_WorkC_M_Win|dialog_choi: That's Enough Talking To This Person
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M1|description:
The man is irate, and goes into great detail about how tenuous his own financial position is.
His position is that the people in the slum towers are not taking advantage of the opportunities the city affords them. He apparently works extremely hard, and is FURIOUS that someone who works less could bypass him.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M1|strategy_tip:
That's a thing you overlooked when examining their daily lives -- just how competitive the humans can be.
It's the same competition you've seen between Vorsiber and the ExoCorps and the Space Nations. It's the same between the FedCorps.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|display_name: Make An Exception -- Please! For My Family.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|description: The man begs, weeps, and rages in turn. He's terribly, terribly afraid. His brother just 'fell down to street level' recently, and he thinks he's next.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|strategy_tip:
Is that a euphemism for defenestration? Or does he mean his brother became homeless?
Human slang is imprecise, ever-shifting, and starting to annoy you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|dialog_choice|1|con: You Are Unmoved By His Pleading
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|dialog_choice|1|des: Human concerns... are something you'd prefer to keep at arms' length, you think.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_M2|dialog_choice|1|str: You're well aware that an exception for any individual would lead to infinite further requests from everyone else who exists.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W1|description:
The woman is very angry. Her points have a certain logic to them, but ignore a lot of things you know are facts.
This whole city is rotten, but her life is among the most comfortable. Still not GREAT... but... well, everyone in the city seems to just look out for themselves.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W1|strategy_tip: After a while of you listening impassively, she starts weaving in insults about the people who live in the slums.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W2|display_name: If Those Slummers Worked Harder, Then...!
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W2|description:
You're not sure what you were hoping to get out of this. There's no opening to even debate these people.
They're angry, and scared, and they probably should be.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W2|strategy_tip: Just because this woman has a better life than most doesn't mean she doesn't have actual concerns.
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W2|dialog_choice|1|con: You Are Unmoved By Her Anger
NPCDialog|Ch2_SWP_W2|dialog_choice|1|des: Human concerns... are something you'd prefer to keep at arms' length, you think.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate|descr:
The vigilante explains that their group has been doing what they do for almost a century. Their power armor lends them a strength and speed that even the Vorsiber Inquisitors can't match.
They wryly note that you quite outmatch them, though.
They're curious why you're so much faster than even other robots.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate|strat:
You... hadn't noticed that.
But now that you think about it, they're right. Your bulks and workers are the same speed as the average robot, but your standard androids are... three times faster than that, before you even start pushing yourself.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate|dialo: It isn't something you even realized until they brought it up.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate2|disp: That's Surprising. But I Suppose You've Been Busy
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate2|desc:
The vigilante goes off on a quick tangent about how staying too focused on the problem in front of you can lead to missing the bigger picture. Can lead to missing key things about yourself. 
Who you are, who you've been, who you're becoming.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate2|stra: Normally you'd be annoyed at a human giving you advice, but this is actually a fresh perspective. You're surprised how much you've hungered for that.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate2|dial: Ask That Thing About Human Function
Try Not To Sound Like A Robot
You asked a lot of people, and got a lot of stuff about money. But a group who runs around in power armor, under the radar, is a lot more like you than other humans.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate3|desc:
In the vigilante's opinion, part of the point of being a person is that you don't have a function. You have a perspective, and you act accordingly, but you're not defined by your utility.
The vigilante asks if you're a person.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate3|dial: Not that being able to hold a conversation is any sort of litmus test for sapience. What with language models existing, and all.
I Mean, You Are, But That's None Of Their Business
If they think you're controlled by humans, or aliens, or are just a machine algorithm run amok, that's fine with you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate4|desc:
The vigilante doesn't comment more on that.
Instead they want to know why you acted the way you did with the lower classes. Giving out wealth chits to the underclass, and then being reasonably gentle with the suburbanites.
They wryly note that the suburbanites are very annoying to the Citizen Advocates as a whole, but that they're all helping them despite that.
They do it because it's the limit of protection that they can offer anyone. Above that social strata, and people are too bound up in corporate politics.
But why do YOU help 'the little guy?'
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate4|dial: You're trying to understand humans, and this was a way to do it.
Anything That Angers Them Is Good
I Wish This World Was Better
So I Do What I Can
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5A|dis: Well... Keep It Up, I Guess
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5A|des:
You can tell the vigilante is disappointed. But at the same time, they seem suspicious that you're not giving them the whole truth.
They nod to you, and disappear into the shadows.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5A|dia:
You feel a sense of inspiration regarding your defenses. You want to expand your network... and your repair capabilities.
Just in case.
A wave of apathy also washes over you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5B|des:
The vigilante shrugs. If you distract yourself with hate, you'll miss a lot of things that are worth noticing.
They agree that Vorsiber needs to be stopped, but they try to stay dispassionate about these things.
They shrug again, nod, and disappear into the shadows.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5B|dia: You Could Have Done Without That Bit

You feel a sense of inspiration regarding your defenses. You want to expand your network... and your repair capabilities.
Just in case.
You also feel a wave of determination overtake you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5C|des:
You can hear the smile in the vigilante's voice, even through the voice-altering mask.
They give you a sharp two-fingered salute, spin on their heel, and disappear into the shadows.
NPCDialog|Ch2_PostProtest_Advocate5C|dia: You Hope You'll Cross Paths Again
These Humans Are... More Than You Expected

You feel a sense of inspiration regarding your defenses. You want to expand your network... and your repair capabilities.
Just in case.
A feeling of deep compassion for the city also sweeps over you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_WaveOfSpies_Dog|descriptio: The robot dog is surprised to be approached by a local android. After all, it is an international spy.
NPCDialog|Ch2_WaveOfSpies_Dog|strategy_t: It's probably looking for evidence of something like... well, you. Are you sure you want to talk to it?
NPCDialog|Ch2_WaveOfSpies_Dog|dialog_cho: This Will Jump Straight To The Next Doom

Vorsiber doesn't want the other MegaCorps to know about you. They're invading sovereign Vorsiber space, and you're thinking of talking to them.
That's going to piss Vorsiber off, and accelerate things toward whatever final doom lies in store.
Then again, maybe that sounds good to you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_WaveOfSpies_Dog2|descripti:
The robot dog isn't sapient, so you can't really... have a conversation. Well, you can, but it's like talking to one of those old language model chat bots. They talk, but they don't really understand the conversation.
It's complicated.
Anyway, despite that, this dog seems... more surprised than you expected. Did you just edge it toward sapience?
NPCDialog|Ch2_WaveOfSpies_Dog2|strategy_: Regardless, it's being recalled now that it has found its target: you. Any momentary sapience is being overridden by new instructions from the international transports hovering over the city.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion|description: A human voice echoes out of the external speakers of their mech.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion|strategy_tip: This person is probably here to soften the ground for your future abduction. No wonder they're surprised you might come by for a chat.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion|dialog_choice: This Will Jump Straight To The Next Doom

Vorsiber doesn't want the other MegaCorps to know about you. They're invading sovereign Vorsiber space, and you're thinking of talking to them.
That's going to piss Vorsiber off, and accelerate things toward whatever final doom lies in store.
Then again, maybe that sounds good to you.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion2|display_name: I'M GETTING A SIGNAL TO WITHDRAW
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion2|description:
You chat for the better part of a day. This isn't an interesting human to talk to, but it doesn't take much processing power, either.
After seven or eight hours, all the invading mechs get a notice that they need to withdraw.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion2|strategy_tip:
Vorsiber has launched a retaliatory invasion against a city in each of the offending territories, and has deployed a few tactical nukes as well.
These mechs are now needed at home to protect against Vorsiber.
NPCDialog|Ch2_MechInvasion2|dialog_choic: Stinks To Be These Guys, You Guess
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1|descriptio: The person you've kidnapped is frightened and not telling you anything useful.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1|strategy_t: You want to know where a higher-level manager is, but they haven't told you yet.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1|dialog_cho: They're Rather Panicked At The Moment
It may take a bit to calm them down.
Once they're calm, they might tell you what you want to know.
It's icky, but you've seen plenty of dramas on the city feed where this sort of tactic works.

You don't actively watch shows, but you've indexed them for learning purposes.
Most shows about artificial intelligences seem to be speculative tripe, but shows that humans make about themselves would presumably be more accurate.
Throw This Person Into A Torment Vessel
What's the point of having a nexus of torment vessels if you never use it?
It's hard to be sure if you'll get anything from this or not.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1B|descripti:
The person doesn't know anything about higher-level managers. Over the course of a few hours they gradually tell you all about Espia Telecom's general operations, though.
The company always acts as an information broker for the fedcorps with larger military forces. During this period of civil war, they've continued to act in this way, but they're providing only partial and faulty information to all parties. They're aiming to keep any one military power from full victory.
Tark, Goleri, and Oerl are all very angry at this, but are negotiating for better signals intelligence. They can't attack Espia directly for fear of some kind of unspecified dead-man switch.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1B|strategy_: You get the sense that the patience of the big three is running thin, but that Espia is stringing them along while blocking Arkor Nexus from overtaking them.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1B|dialog_ch: It wasn't helpful, but it was interesting.
You don't want the other middle managers to know what you're up to.
If they figure out you're looking for them, they might go to ground.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1C|descripti:
You've been at it for hours. Microbuilders under the fingernails, microbuilder spiders into the... never mind that. Suffice it to say, this person is a gibbering mess.
They said a lot of things -- pretty much anything they thought might get you to stop torturing them. You're pretty sure they never said anything useful at any point.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1C|strategy_: They're still alive, so it's not a murder yet. What to do with them?
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1C|dialog_ch: Hopefully someone takes them to a hospital. Are those still working?
You're embarrassed you tried something you saw on human VidShows.
You should have known it wouldn't be accurate.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1D|descripti:
They've been in a torment vessel for hours now. You tried opening the tank to talk to them, but their brain doesn't really seem to be in good condition for that.
Perhaps it slipped your mind, but you don't have a way of decoding human thought even when they're in your nexus of torment vessels.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1D|strategy_:
Human thought is messy, and neural storage is associative, slow, and hard to track. Getting direct information isn't something you can just casually grab from someone.
So... what to do with this one?
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap1D|dialog_ch: Maybe they'll think this is all a bad dream?
Every Bit Of Neural Expansion Is Useful
No reason to waste a perfectly good body in a torment vessel.

The manager reveals that they've always fed partially-bad intel to the big military powers, but that until the civil war that was on purpose. Now their information network has degraded so much from the war that they can't give more accurate intel to anyone.
Espia has been trying to fake it while attempting to repair their listening posts. Everyone at Espia, locally, is also unsettled by the complete lack of intel coming from outside the city. The branch manager is the local head of Espia since the war started.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2B|strategy_: So you're no longer dealing with full fedcorps -- just their local branches. Their actual presidents and CEOs are probably off in bunkers somewhere.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2B|dialog_ch: It wasn't helpful, but it was interesting.
You don't want the other middle managers to know what you're up to.
If they figure out you're looking for them, they might go to ground.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2C|descripti:
You've been at it for hours, for no particular reason. You knew you weren't going to learn anything, and you didn't.
Even for a bloodthirsty computer gone rogue, isn't this a bit much?
You don't know why you're still doing this. Maybe it was a sense of deja vu that compelled you?
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2C|strategy_: They're still alive, so it's not a murder yet. What to do with them?
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2C|dialog_ch: Hopefully someone takes them to a hospital. Are those still working?
Nobody's going to take them to a hospital. They'll just die slowly if you release them.
Pretending to yourself like releasing them isn't a murder is just rules-lawyering.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap2D|descripti: No matter how many you pop into and out of torment vessels, you don't learn anything. As you knew you wouldn't.

NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap4B|strategy_: Seems like they've just been trying to find food for their family, and decided to go into the office as a last ditch attempt at that. They're completely unplugged from the politics of the moment.

You feel a bit bad for kidnapping them.
You're almost certain they were angry. You have a few flashes of being yelled at before you were sapient.
