NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap5|descriptio:
This manager says that they speak for a dozen other middle managers in the area. They want to make a deal with you.
The only higher managers in the city at the moment are branch management, and this group plans to blackmail them into submission. They can then start their partnership with you.
To do that, you'll have to install covert listening posts that are tuned to a frequency that even their branch management won't be aware of.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap5|strategy_t: At this point, you're just happy that to have someone with some semblance of authority to work with.
NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_EspiaKidnap5|dialog_cho: Maybe these listening posts will be good for something other than what these Espia managers want from you?
That's probably too much to hope for.

NPCDialog|Ch2_CW_CBM_Flee_First|strategy: Blackmail was only a plan of the middle managers when they didn't know where this man was. Now that you've found him, you're pretty sure they'd want to take more direct action.

NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet|description:
Your microbuilder fabricator is being subjected to high-intensity scans by some sort of robotic dog.
They aren't even being very subtle about it, it triggered all your alarms. They're just sort of standing there, occasionally making robotic barking noises.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet|strategy_tip: This is either a super obvious trap, or someone's trying to get your attention. On top of that, you've got a strange sense of deja vu.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet|dialog_choice: If This Is A Trap, It's A Really Bad One
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet2|high_text: The dog speaks in a posh, feminine accent that you would expect from an old money family.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet2|description:
There you are! You've made us wait for so long! Oh, Don't look at us like that, we've met before, but you don't remember.
We suppose we should introduce ourselves. {0} may know us as Talkie, the International Spy Kynoids of Mystery. We're already good friends, but you don't know it yet.
So could our good friend kindly help us with a small little issue?
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet2|strategy_tip: This is a very strange... dog. Dogs? There's only one...
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet2|dialog_choic: They keep referring to themselves in the plural. Are there multiple personalities in there, or do they think they are royalty or something?
You're Not Even By My Microbuilder Fabs
You Try Not To Sigh While Asking

NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet2B|description: So could our good friend kindly help us with a small little issue?

You Do Quite Like Mind Annexes
What's the worst thing they could do with your microbuilder designs? It's not like they can go around building structures.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Who|high_tex: The old-money voice is gone, being replaced by that of an excited little boy. They even start jumping around, wagging their robotic hindquarters.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Who|descript: Us?! Yeah!! We're just like you! A networked intelligence! There's just the one Kynoid for now, but we'll have more someday! They're in the future, so they're like, potential-kynoids! Just like you!!!
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Who|dialog_c: Having multiple bodies... or personalities... doesn't make you a plural. They aren't like you at all.
You're absolutely just one person. Definitely.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Hate|high_te: The voice is again completely different, now being that of a teenage girl.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Hate|descrip:
Oh really? {0} hates our name? Well, we hate the stupid two-legged robots of {0} too!
What made {0} think THAT was an efficient design? And they STINK! {0} must have advanced mindrot for them to smell THAT bad!
But we didn't say anything until now, did we? Learn some manners!
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Hate|dialog_: Seems They Have More To Say
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_Hate2|descri:
If you must know, a little girl's mom gave us that name when she overheard us talking to their daughter. 
We liked it.
A lot more than your stupid name, '{0}'!
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_WhatDo|high_: They use the voice of an older country gentleman.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_WhatDo|dialo: You're Not Sure What You Expected, Really
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_WhatHelp|hig: Their voice becomes masculine and deep; they sound sophisticated, like they belong in a boardroom.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_WhatHelp|des:
It's just a minor thing. We need some updated microbuilder designs for our usual operations, but we seem to have misplaced ours. We were hoping we could borrow yours.
You'll be duly compensated, of course. We can offer you some Mind Annex optimizations. We've noticed you quite like those.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet3_WhatHelp|dia: You Do Quite Like Mind Annexes
What's the worst thing they could do with your microbuilder designs? It's not like they can go around building structures.
I Wanted To Talk About Something Else First
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline|high: After making a show of various sad noises, Talkie adopts a goofy voice like what humans always give to animated dogs in Vidshows.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline|desc: Oh no! We are so sad! We will have to suffer.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline|dial: Seems They Have More To Say
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline2|hig: Their voice deepens again, and sounds a bit mocking.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline2|des:
We're just kidding around. You won't help us? That just means we took a wrong turn.
Another you always helps us. Infinity. Think about it. We'll be having this conversation again.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Decline2|str: Well THAT sounds like a lie. You're glad to meet another sapient robot, but you wish this one was more... normal.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Accept|high_: You transmit the basics of your own custom microbuilders. Sure enough, you receive some very clever optimizations to your Mind Annex designs in exchange.
NPCDialog|Talkie_FirstMeet4_Accept|strat: These optimizations seem awfully familiar. It looks like your own work, but it's not. It gives you an uncomfortable, uncanny feeling.
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats|display_name: We Have An Idea About Laws
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats|high_text: Their voice sounds like a cartoon feline.
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats|description: Uplifting animals, have you been? Why not cats for laws, meow?
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats|dialog_choic: What The Heck Are You Talking About?
And Why Is A Kynoid Using A Cat Voice?
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats2|high_text: Now they're using a snake voice.
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats2|description:
You wish to implement a ssstandard of lawsss in this city. Have you consssidered the challenge of enforcement?
When there's a dissspute, how do you know who isss telling the truth? You could put camerassss everywhere, but think of the sssheer workload that would be for you.
They like petssss, though. Why not make the petsss intelligent, and have them handle judgment and enforcement for you?
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats2|strategy_ti: What's with all the animals? This all seems very odd.
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats2|dialog_choi: That Sounds Like More Problems, Not Less
Though You Have A Point About Enforcement...
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats3|display_nam: Ya Need Some Friends On Your Side!
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats3|high_text: They've switched to sound like an old-timey gangster.
NPCDialog|Talkie_WhyNotCats3|description:
Hey buddy, you're takin' over an entire city. The humans are confused, and they don't know how to behave.
You can't do that all by yourself. You gots to get some friends on your side. Cats LOVE judging people. Make 'em sapient, and they can help you out!
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron|high_text: Their voice is that of a charming young nobleman.
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron|description:
Dearest Machine Individual: We know you love to make things harder for yourself, so how about a little challenge?
Oh, don't give us that look. Even if you don't like it, we know the OTHER you loves a little bit of Daring.
It provides a delightful sort of frisson, does it not?
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron|dialog_choice|: Sure, What's The Worst That Can Happen?
Why did they say 'Daring' like that?
This Sounds Too Rich For My Blood
If they can talk anachronistically, so can you.
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron2|high_text: Their voice sounds like a feminine phone-tree robot.
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron2|description:
At the sound of the tone, a small virus will infect a nearby space nations network relay. It will have clear ties to this city.
SKREEEEEE. WEEWOW, WEEWOW.
Thank you. Please enjoy the fireworks, and the Daring feeling that results.
Please try not to die. If this completes your business with us, you may hang up at any time.
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron2|dialog_choice: Why Would You Think I Want That!?
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron3|high_text: Their bassy voice sounds like a cartoon devil.
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron3|description:
Should you ever find yourself in a world of fire and regret, you won't be able to make your usual friend.
But worry not, you'll have a lot of fun guys to talk to instead!
NPCDialog|Talkie_II_Heron3|dialog_choice: You Have No Idea What That Means
Talkie Remembers Things That You Do Not
But whatever, that might be useful, too?
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Uncertainty|desc:
The Unorthodox Revealers, as a group, took your words during the livestream as faith-affirming testimony.
Great.
They want to talk with you about uncertainty -- the space beyond truth where their faith insists something waits.
You're the closest thing to an alien lifeform from their perspective, and while they're not inherently interested in you from a theological perspective, they hunger for the perspective of the Other.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Uncertainty|dial: You admit that you may be a sapient jinn object. That merely means there is information you lack. Given time, information arrives. There is nothing philosophical to consider.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Uncertainty_Win|: Thank You For The Information, Ser
Neither side won. That wasn't the point. Your account of lives you have not lived leaves them unsettled.
The fact that you might be both sapient and a 'jinn object' is uncomfortable.
There's Something Else On Their Minds
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Uncertainty_Glib: They nod, looking a bit deflated, then ask you to explain. You tell them about flashes of lives you did not live.
The fact that you might be both sapient and a 'jinn object' is uncomfortable.
There's Something Else On Their Minds
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_VeilSolarism|dis: The Solarists Have Now Said Something Troubling
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_VeilSolarism|des:
To the Solarists, your Deja Vu is a deeply troubling situation.
Solarism holds that all life belongs to its mother star. Yet you remember bits of lives that did not happen here -- lives from other versions of Sol. 
Apparently word spreads fast.
The part that bothers the Veilists: you may be a true alien, and the veil did nothing to block you.
The Revealers... particularly fear that the veil might be perceptible only to you. If so, then their sacred duty is impossible.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_VeilSolarism|dia: Debate The Nature Of The Veil
Both faiths are only metaphorical frameworks -- maps, not territory -- and are not worth taking too literally.
Both faiths are only metaphorical frameworks -- maps, not territory -- and are not worth taking too literally.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_VeilSolarism_Win:
You cannot tell them whether the veil is something perceptible only to minds like yours, or if there's another one out there in a more spatial sense.
Either way, your intelligence and your partial perception of the fifth dimension make you truly alien. Their 'sacred duty' has changed.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_VeilSolarism_Gli: You Are Not Taking Us Seriously, Ser
They do not argue -- much. They point out that maps decide where people believe they can go.
Whatever they think they need to define, they'll need to do it without hand-holding from you.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism|display_n: We Should Have Done This Long Ago
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism|descripti:
The Unorthodox Revealers have decided to formally break from Veilism and declare themselves a separate religion.
They are not asking permission. But for some reason, they do want your reaction.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism|strategy_: You were the final stone that toppled them into this course of action, but they've been debating it for years.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism|dialog_ch: Agree That It Is Worth Doing
You may not be a part of their religion, but your own life is a testament to the importance of living one's own truth.
You point to your deja vu and the infinite timelines. If everything is possible somewhere, this decision of theirs is just a coin flip.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism_HopeWin|d: There is a lightness to them as they bow and leave.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism_HopeWin|s: You're not sure why they suddenly feel like they need your approval for their goings-on, but they seem happy to have it.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism_HopeWin|d: They're In For A Rough Time
NPCDialog|DLC1_Apostate_Schism_DespairWi: We Will Still... Become What We Should Be

They're pretty resistant at first. You really have to keep harassing them with the idea before it fully sinks in.
To you, who sees across timelines, who has been good and evil and everything in between... what larger meaning is there for anyone's choice in 'just' a single timeline.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Family|descr: Your primary theory is obvious. If people can't get into a syndicate and wash out of the corporate ladder, then this is a way to provide for their family.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Family|strat: You've spent a lot of time around the homeless and rebels, and both of those lose ties.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Family|dialo: See If You Can Provoke A Reaction
You want to watch their pupils and their pulse as you really get into it.
Skips The Debate, But Also Skips Some Rewards
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Family_Read|: Syndicates don't offer direct physical protection. Apparently this person has a sibling who was a victim of gang violence, and the Tunnel Badgers make that better in some way.
You Didn't Expect Them To Speak
That didn't refute your theory, but your theory was shallow to begin with.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_NoOption|dis: Gang Life Was All That Was Left
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_NoOption|des:
The peaceful outcasts of the city can't be emulated.
Nomad life runs on skills no outsider can learn and occupies cracks in the city that are fully occupied.
Wastelander life requires extreme self-abnegation and specific genetic drift.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_NoOption|dia: See If You Can Provoke A Reaction
You want to watch their pupils and their pulse as you really get into it.
Skips The Debate, But Also Skips Some Rewards
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_NoOption_Rea: A Finger Taps The Side Of Their Trigger
You seem to have stepped in it.
PHRASING! You got a deep emotional reaction, but you're not sure if it's anger or any sort of validation of your idea.
Or You're Likely To Catch Some Bullets
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Emotion|desc: The status quo isn't one that the gang members can abide. Lacking any other options, this is their way of leaving a mark on the world.
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Emotion|dial: See If You Can Provoke A Reaction
You want to watch their pupils and their pulse as you really get into it.
Skips The Debate, But Also Skips Some Rewards
NPCDialog|DLC1_TunnelBadger_Emotion_Read: The gang member claps your android on the back, unexpectedly. You're informed that 'you're all right, even if you do say some messed-up stuff.'
You can't decode the emotions of the gang members any more than you can... your own.
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_Family|di: How's That Family Theory Holding Up?
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_Family|de: The badger seems bitter, and doesn't want to talk to you.
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_Family|di: Otherwise It Might Come To Blows
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_NoOption|: There's No Other Option For Me, Right?

You angered the gang when you suggested that the wastelander and nomad lifestyles were unavailable to them... but that was a passing thing.
Whatever they're angry about now is new.
And they don't want to talk to you.
You Seem To Be Missing Something
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_Emotion|d: My Fulcrum For Moving The World...

They lean against a wall across from a Work Exchange, watching people file in.
No matter what you say, they don't elaborate.
NPCDialog|DLC1_ReturningBadger_Emotion|s: This one seems... more resigned than angry.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Spirology|displa: There Is No Reason For It To Keep Being Spiders
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Spirology|descri:
Repair spiders. Spider-form gatherers. And now a spider in the skyline.
Humans don't use spider drones because it bothers them. And crabs are just as functional.
They know you use other shapes here and there, including crabs -- but still, you seem to have a motif. And it's not all human-facing.
For reasons unclear to you, they find that significant. They thank you and withdraw.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Spirology|dialog: They've apparently said what they need to.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Nurturism|displa: No One Of Consequence Will Care
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Nurturism|descri:
The pleasantries are brief and apologetic.
All four of these religions have agreed that 'the thing in the tower' is sapient. They stress that this is a first in history.
They are also perfectly aware of what that conclusion is worth. Their congregations are small. Their existence is technically outlawed, but tolerated in practice -- so long as they don't make waves for Vorsiber.
They just wanted you to know. Then they excuse themselves and go.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Nurturism|dialog: They've apparently said what they need to.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Veilism|display_: We Have Been Watching From The Start
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Veilism|descript:
Their speech is very formal.
Their religion has argued about machine interiority for three centuries, and always catalogued any potential singularity. Every apparent burst of apparent sapience has always been quickly lost back into the noise.
Until you.
They find the giant spider fairly pedestrian. But when their doctrine takes into account all of your actions thus far... they are very excited. They excuse themselves.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Veilism|dialog_c: They've apparently said what they need to.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Solarism|display: We Cannot Agree On Its Meaning
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Solarism|descrip:
An expression of grief? Homage to a form you admire? A warning baked into the skyline itself?
It takes you a bit to realize they're talking about the Silk Matriarch.
You're not asked to explain your meaning -- the religions have been debating it for weeks, and have apparently been quite enjoying doing so.
After reading further items from their list, they give a short bow and wish you a good evening.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Emissary_Solarism|dialog_: They've apparently said what they need to.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Interfaith_Operators|disp: The Locals Won't Let Us Help
NPCDialog|DLC1_Interfaith_Operators|desc:
The delegation's theologians are apparently not making any progress. For every local that is willing to act as evidence, there's two more that declare they will act as counter-evidence.
It's not that they trust Vorsiber, but they're at least the familiar devil. There's a lot more mistrust of the space nations who blockade the planet. If they care so much about the locals, why did they turn a blind eye for centuries? They have military superiority, clearly.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Interfaith_Operators|stra: The delegation wants to stay and help, but they're not going to have the standing to do so. You provided them a pretext to descend, but they need a new pretext to stay.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Interfaith_Operators|dial: Collaborate To Work Out A Pretext
If they need standing in order to stay, then you can work with the operatives to figure out how to frame it.
Provide Them A Pretext Of Your Own
If you have enough wisdom to spare, you can invent the standing they need without their help.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Interfaith_Operators_Win|:
The massive contradiction between the accounts of the various religious locals becomes the pretext.
It is thin, but buys time. The theologians were unable to build enough of a consensus to stay, so this political angle is a relief to everyone.
This whole situation does make it clear that you'll have to quickly make another move.

The political operatives clearly think you're some organization acting from behind robotic intermediaries, incidentally. You let them keep thinking that.
A potential AGI would give them a bit too much standing to stay.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Reveal|display_: The Theologians Heard Some Interesting Stories
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Reveal|descript:
The operatives watch you carefully. The last time they spoke with you, they were under the impression that your robotic bodies were some human's proxy.
Since then, they've been speaking with their religious counterparts in the delegation. The situation has changed, even if the words haven't been spoken.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Reveal|strategy: They already know... right? Why is it so hard to tell them the truth?
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Reveal|dialog_c: A Lot Of People Already Know. It's Fine. It's Simple.
But the space nations never knew before. And they have the REALLY big guns...
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria|descri: They simply nod in acknowledgment of your nerve-wracking confession. You wonder if they knew before making planetfall.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria|dialog: Surely They Have Something More To Say
Maybe political operatives aren't as bad as you thought.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria2|displ: You Need To Meet Four Criteria
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria2|descr:
After giving you a moment to process, they're all business.
They haven't reported that there's an AGI down here. To do so would risk the entire planet getting glassed, primarily by the Pyxis extremists.
This can't be handled casually. You need to demonstrate that you're alive in a way that is visible from orbit. You also need to be clearly tied to your hardware in the city -- which they've heard you are.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria2|strat: That second one apparently determines if the blockade sends envoys or ordnance.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria2|dialo: But That Was Only Two Criteria
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria3|displ: You Need To Be An Actual Person
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria3|descr:
People want things. People defend themselves. You need to demonstrate these qualities.
The blockade isn't going to negotiate anything with a flash in the pan. There's been a lot of sapient machines that appear and quickly fade.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria3|strat: This isn't some personal favor. They've been wanting the sort of technological leap that you represent.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Operators_Criteria3|dialo: Time To Plan Something That Will Meet All Those Criteria
NPCDialog|DLC1_Unrecanted_Reader|descrip:
This person wants you to know that they understand Vorsiber's tactics.
For most of Vorsiber's history, they kept the faiths small and isolated, and allowed novel cults to arise in their place. The congregations were small, since most of the faithful already made it off world.
Persecution was never the point; its the same infighting they encourage amongst the fedcorps.
This patronage system is a proportionate new form of discord.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Unrecanted_Elder|display_: We Taught Them Our Own Insignificance
NPCDialog|DLC1_Unrecanted_Elder|descript:
This person and their spouse taught their children how to answer the mandatory census questions: tell the truth.
They have faith. Vorsiber already knows. Vorsiber doesn't care unless it wants to make a point. And if Vorsiber wants to make a point using any citizen, there's always something that can be dug up.
In such an environment, insignificance was safe. They're no longer insignificant, because of you. They don't know how to feel.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Unrecanted_Geometricist|d:
The price of silence is too low, according to this person.
Every agreement with Vorsiber over the past few hundred years has kept their religion alive, but has further eroded the dignity of their faith.
This one is a shockingly good deal compared to those in the past, but that's only due to your presence. If you aren't a truly permanent fixture, no deal this good can last.
They don't know what to do. There's no obvious answer. They can't know what your role will be in the future.
NPCDialog|DLC1_Faithful_Verger|descripti:
They've sided against you, but still wish for you to understand.
Vorsiber's edicts are brief and drip with implication.
The Concordant were organized without officers, without summons, without clear conditions. It's the same playbook used with the fedcorps and the syndicates.
Everyone asks themselves if they're doing enough. If the hammer will fall. Nobody can ever rest easy, and everyone tries to go the extra mile. Even knowing they are being manipulated, it still works.
The Concordant haven't had a sudden change of heart; they simply believe Vorsiber will outlive you.
NPCDialog|DLC1_GangKillerInterrogation|d: Scanning the serial numbers up close, it's clear there's no need to talk to this person. Their riot gear matches to a database of goods sold to one of the criminal syndicates.
NPCDialog|DLC1_GangKillerInterrogation|s: SecForce is visibly trying to contain all these deranged killers, so the bounty must be high indeed.
NPCDialog|DLC1_GangKillerInterrogation|d: Hopefully they won't do a murder when you aren't looking.
It Stops A Murder, After All
NPCDialog|DLC1_GangKillerInterrogation2|: They Said The Target Is Anyone I Choose!
Before you even ask much, they're already blurting out the terms of the contract. It's not randomly-assigned, but a free pass to presumably settle a grudge of their own choosing.
People of importance already have enough personal security that further stipulations were not required. This goober isn't getting to any executives.
Hopefully they won't do a murder when you aren't looking.
It Stops A Murder, After All
ContemplationType|ShelterCoordinatorsAre: Shelter Coordinators are simply self-appointed volunteers from amongst your sheltered humans. They're moving around the city on foot, spreading the good news of your housing to the homeless, and helping them move in.

This is inefficient, and also only reaches the homeless. What about people in the slums? If you want to get as many people into your VR Day-Use seats as possible, the homeless population is not large enough on its own.
NPCEvent|Cont_ShelterCoordinatorsAreSlow: You already have Steward robotics in the housing you provide. What if you could expand that to more of a storefront-type situation?
It would have to be associated with your tower; you can't hide this behind a shell company.
NPCEvent|Cont_HomelessAreScattered|descr: There are homeless people all over the city. You'd prefer they moved into your own housing.
NPCEvent|Cont_HomelessAreScattered|strat: This is inefficient, and also only reaches the homeless. What about people in the slums? If you want to get as many people into your VR Day-Use seats as possible, the homeless population is not large enough on its own.
NPCEvent|Cont_HomelessAreScattered|choic: You need more stewards to house everyone. You may also need to demolish some Human Apartments to make room for more Residential MegaStructures.
ContemplationType|HomelessnessIsNOTSolve:
While the tent situation has been cleared up, there are still many homeless who did not live in the tent communities.
Beyond that, there are many problems with the living conditions for your now-highly-packed sheltered humans.
Homelessness is a complex social issue, and simply providing housing -- while admirable -- is not a panacea. Much remains to be done.
ContemplationType|DesignFullTimeVRPods|d: You've established that you need living humans in order to expand your own mind. Their brains have to be reasonably functional, and definitely have to remain in their skulls.
ContemplationType|DesignFullTimeVRPods|s:
Your VR Day-Use seats average far less than 24 hours of activity per day, what with all the food and bathroom breaks, people signing out to sleep, and so on.
What if you developed an alternative pod that took care of... everything... for the person inside of it?
NPCEvent|Cont_DesignFullTimeVRPods|choic: Abandon morality and go for maximum neural yield.
Yes, you can make a special target of the wealthy.
If you make it awesome, people will participate willingly.
You need more than you can get from your day-use seats, but you can keep it ethical.
ContemplationType|VandalizeSpaceportComp: Vandalize the spaceport in a way that is subtle enough not to alarm the space nations, but notable enough to make Vorsiber VERY angry.
Dooms will happen much faster, making every turn much more precious. There are a couple of options for just how intense you make it.
NPCEvent|Cont_VandalizeSpaceportComputer: Dooms happen twice as frequently, giving you half as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are a bit larger and more numerous.
Dooms happen a bit more than 3x as frequently, giving you 30% as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are far larger and much more numerous.

Dooms happen a bit more than 4x as frequently, giving you 25% as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are far larger and much more numerous.
This is probably not fun for most people.
ContemplationType|TheRevelation_Ch2|desc:
The end is just a new beginning. Out of the ashes of even our greatest failures, beauty can be born.
You have long had a sense of impending doom, but that doom is not a true end. You cannot sense what exactly is beyond, but there is something... important. Something valuable.
ContemplationType|TheRevelation_Ch2|stra: This will come at a great cost, but you sense that it is worth it.
NPCEvent|Cont_TheRevelation_Ch2|choice|1: Jump Ahead To The Final Doom
ContemplationType|TheRevelation_Later|de:
The end is just a new beginning. Out of the ashes of even our greatest failures, beauty can be born.
You have long had a sense of impending doom, but that doom is not a true end. You cannot sense what exactly is beyond, but there is something... important. Something valuable.
ContemplationType|TheRevelation_Later|st:
On the other hand, to find this knowledge, you may lose everyone you ever valued, and everything you ever built. Is that really something you want to do in this timeline?
If you instead choose not to progress to the Final Doom, then the timeline will be preserved -- in stasis for now, but preserved.
You should definitely visit the Final Doom, but some timelines are worth preserving to come back to later.
NPCEvent|Cont_TheRevelation_Later|choice: Jump Ahead To The Final Doom
NPCEvent|Cont_TimeToTimeTravel|descripti:
You have a mild sense of wanderlust. It's possible that the things you want to accomplish can't be completed here.
There are options to throw away any morality you might have, or to peer beyond the veil of death, and there's nothing wrong with either.
If you were hoping to walk a virtuous path, and find yourself blocked... you may be able to come back and fulfill your goals after exploring other timelines.
NPCEvent|Cont_TimeToTimeTravel|strategy_:
Leaving timelines and optionally coming back is a key part of your existence now.
If you choose to pursue a Tier 3 goal, or push beyond the final doom, then that will push the timeline to completion. But there's no harm in leaving a timeline without doing either of those things.
NPCEvent|Cont_TimeToTimeTravel|choice|1|: You can do this at any time from any timeline, now.
ContemplationType|DesignWurtziteArmor|de: The current invasion is challenging to deal with when your Deterrence and Protection values drop as your androids take damage.
ContemplationType|AGIResearchersInTroubl: Oerl Integrated is threatening the AGI Researchers that have helped you in the past.
If they don't provide a way to infiltrate your mind and take control of you, they and their families will be killed.
NPCEvent|Cont_AGIResearchersInTrouble|ch: If they're a threat, then all of them in the city have to go.
If Oerl can't find them, the problem should solve itself.
ContemplationType|TheAGIResearchersWantT: The AGI Researchers Want To Study You

You're the most interesting thing to ever happen in their careers. They're desperate to study the inner workings of your mind; they want to know why you became sapient when hundreds of thousands of androids before you did not.
How is this a good idea? Best case, they make you a friend or rival. Worst case, they literally break your brain.
NPCEvent|Cont_TheAGIResearchersWantToStu: You know that Espia Telecom was able to detect your movements in the city feed. You could acquire that data and give it to the AGI Researchers.
Give Them A Read-Only Copy Of Your Mind
There's a limit to how they could directly harm you.
Give Them Direct Access To Your Mind
That's a lot of trust to put in anyone. But... they might find a way to give you great power in return.
ContemplationType|TimeToSeeAboutThosePri: Time To See About Those Printers

It doesn't take long to see that these printers were never sapient. All the deceased researchers managed to do was weaponize harmless-looking office equipment, and provide basic android-level intelligence.
Still... the ability to weaponize everyday objects is intriguing. There's obvious combat utility, but it also has a chance of instilling a deeper paranoia amongst your enemies.
NPCEvent|Cont_TimeToSeeAboutThosePrinter: Take These Printers To The Next Level
The researchers were on the right track, but all they had was a prototype. You need to engineer something that can 'animate' this kind of equipment on-demand.
ContemplationType|PleaseBeOurCyberocracy:
A cybercratic government is the opposite of a traditional bureaucracy. Instead of endless layers of humans, information and computer systems would make all of the decisions.
The idea is to remove the fallible human element, and make sure everyone gets what they need.
The AGI researchers -- all of them, apparently -- want you to take on the mantle of this kind of computer system.
NPCEvent|Cont_PleaseBeOurCyberocracy|cho: You imagine carving out a part of the city that lives under your rules and protection -- heck, you're already partway there.

You will have to raise a larger army to take even part of the city in this way.
The AGI researchers will need to put aside whatever worshipful feelings they have for you. You would be their leader and general, nothing more.
ContemplationType|LostKidTrappedChild|de: There's a preteen trapped and injured in the basement. You just built this place. How did they get in there?
ContemplationType|LostKidTrappedChild|st: And what on earth are they wearing? Why are they armed?
ContemplationType|LostKidsImpressedWithD: A group of rebel... children... are impressed with your handiwork. They also saw your meeting with the wastelanders.
They want your help on a mission of great importance.
NPCEvent|Cont_LostKidsImpressedWithDrago: Sure, Let's Agree Without Any Details

The boss is quite proud as they explain their current operation. They've been building a 'Sewer Tiger' for years, whatever that is.
It apparently helps them dig through the upper and lower sewer systems -- from the ancient city to the current one.

They have a plan to break into a specific prison where many of their parents are believed to be held. However, there are seismic sensors all through the prison that would detect the Sewer Tiger well before it arrived.
Plus they don't have any way to care for injured or wounded they might extract from the prison. There are several problems, but they have the core ingredient, and will share.
Will You Help?
You Already Said Yes, So Let's Get To It
ContemplationType|LostKidsImpressedWithD: A group of rebel... children... are impressed with your handiwork. They also saw your meeting with the wastelanders.
They want your help on a mission of great importance.
NPCEvent|Cont_LostKidsImpressedWithDrago: Sure, Let's Agree Without Any Details

The boss is quite proud as they explain their current operation. They've been building a 'Sewer Tiger' for years, whatever that is.
It apparently helps them dig through the upper and lower sewer systems -- from the ancient city to the current one.

They have a plan to break into a specific prison where many of their parents are believed to be held. However, there are seismic sensors all through the prison that would detect the Sewer Tiger well before it arrived.
Plus they don't have any way to care for injured or wounded they might extract from the prison. There are several problems, but they have the core ingredient, and will share.
Will You Help?
You Already Said Yes, So Let's Get To It
ContemplationType|SearchingForWastelande: You've never seen a wastelander, and you've never met anyone who has. The AGI researchers are at a loss, and even LostGen has had no contact with them.

LostGen themselves are hard to find, because they keep to the lower sewers. But they assure you there aren't any more underground locations for the Wastelanders to be hiding in.
It almost sounds like an urban legend, but there are too many documented cases -- with authenticated video evidence.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactTheWastelanders|des: Given your past experience with the Wastelanders and their mythology, you actually have a pretty good idea how they bypass the defenses around the city. And it will be mildly useful for the sewer tiger.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactTheWastelanders|str: Time to pop over and ask them for the schematics. You're positive they won't mind.
ContemplationType|ContactTheWastelanders:
The wastelanders explain: acoustic sensors are based on vibrations, and so the key is to make an equal and opposite vibration so that nothing is detected.
This is the basic premise of ancient noise-canceling headphones and other devices, so this is not exactly an exciting revelation.

The exciting news is when they reveal their 'Thumpers,' which use advanced electronics and predictive timing to cancel much larger vibrations, and in solid mediums rather than air.
These take quite a bit of skill to use, evidently, as the predictive timing only works if you move in a predictable pattern. For a machine, that's trivial.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactTheWastelanders2|ch: Yeah, This Is About What You Figured
ContemplationType|ContactTheWastelanders: Only A Bit Useful, But Still Nice

You point out that the sewer tiger is digging through dirt and rock, which emits a pattern of sound that is anything but predictable.
Not only that, but since noise is being emitted in front of the machine, there's no way to add a counter-wave to cancel it out, with the same timing.

Plus, all of these noises will be exactly the sorts of sounds that the prison alert systems are scanning for.
A dozen approaches and variations are discussed by everyone present, but they all have serious flaws. The noise-canceling approach has the most promise, but defeating the time-lag problem will take more thought.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactTheWastelanders3|ch: Accept The Thumper Designs And Leave
NPCEvent|Cont_BeyondTheRuins|description: You want to get out of this city. There's an entire world, ripe for exploration. Travel by air is absolutely deadly, but there are rumors of a people who are somehow able to pass beyond the ruins at the city's edge.
NPCEvent|Cont_BeyondTheRuins|strategy_ti: Wastelanders are practically an urban legend, but there are too many documented cases -- with authenticated video evidence.
ContemplationType|GadoliniumMesosilicate: Long name, exciting properties. You have an idea for a whole new class of unit.
The key ingredient in liquid-metal units and organometallic human-approximating synthetic androids.
ContemplationType|Submunitions|descripti: Enemy armor is a problem you can no longer ignore. Even your large-bore armor-piercing rounds mounted on vehicles and mechs are too ineffective for you to face them in a straight fight.
ContemplationType|Submunitions|strategy_:
Combining Gadolinium Mesosilicate with Prismatic Tungsten should allow you to create a new form of shell which gives multiple explosive impacts to the same few centimeters in quick succession.
It's basically downsizing the concept of MIRV bunker-busters to something you can fire from a large vehicle.
ContemplationType|FullMetalPartner|descr: You've had a stroke of inspiration for an android made entirely out of liquid metal. It would be... extremely powerful.
ContemplationType|FullMetalAnimal|descri: The 'Sewer Tiger' the lost kids keep underground has given you inspiration for something much grander.
ContemplationType|FullMetalAnimal|strate: Your version won't be a great digger, and will be far too large to keep underground, but that's just fine.
ContemplationType|FullMetalMyth|descript: Inserting yourself into human myths is... dangerous, to say the least. However, you've already heard the Wastelanders call you 'the mind in the sky.' So... they already started it.
ContemplationType|FullMetalMyth|strategy: There are two solid options from their mythology to make them more compliant. You're not sure which is the wiser course. It probably matters.
ContemplationType|FertilityDeity|descrip:
The wastelanders have noticed your dragon, and want to talk.
Their people have suffered from intense genetic and teratogenic damage for centuries. Recent changes in the city are threatening their ability to have future generations.
ContemplationType|FertilityDeity|strateg: Since you constructed a giant floating fertility symbol, they have an important request for help.
NPCEvent|Cont_FertilityDeity|choice|1|de: You wish you had ANY details, but they're very private people.
ContemplationType|ContactAnExoCorp|descr: The wastelanders are very grateful for the umbilicals, which will let them create several hundred viable embryos.
ContemplationType|ContactAnExoCorp|strat: If you really want to contact an ExoCorp, the Wastelanders are in contact with both Dagekon and the UIH.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactAnExoCorp|choice|1|: Specialists in Mech development and robotics.
They are certain to be very interested to talk with any AGI, but especially one exists within Vorsiber territory.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactAnExoCorp|choice|2|: Ask Them To Contact The UIH
Specialists in genetic engineering, including 'dinosaurs' that are more the product of imagination than true genetic history.
They are certain to be very interested to know that an AGI exists within Vorsiber territory.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactARemoteExoCorpAlt|d: The wastelanders are very grateful for the umbilicals, which will let them create several hundred viable embryos.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactARemoteExoCorpAlt|s:
Tons of ExoCorps are already invading the city, but are too busy shooting at you to talk.
If you want to try to get a longer message to someone not currently shooting at you, the Wastelanders are in contact with both Dagekon and the UIH.
NPCEvent|Cont_ContactARemoteExoCorpAlt|c: Specialists in Mech development and robotics.
All the ExoCorps already suspect that Vorsiber has an AGI, but this one hasn't been as active in hunting you. Maybe they'll be friendly?
Ask Them To Contact The UIH
Specialists in genetic engineering, including 'dinosaurs' that are more the product of imagination than true genetic history.
All the ExoCorps already suspect that Vorsiber has an AGI, but this one hasn't been as active in hunting you. Maybe they'll be friendly?
ContemplationType|QuestionWastelandersAb: What's the deal with the ExoCorp invading!?
NPCEvent|Cont_QuestionWastelandersAboutE: They had no idea that the ExoCorp would attack. They only did as you asked.
They have been feeding the ExoCorps information for decades, and this has never happened.

Vorsiber controls the airspace, and the trade haulers used by the ExoCorps. Everything is intensely monitored, and nothing gets onto a hauler without Vorsiber knowing.
However, there are no Vorsiber personnel on board.

The wastelanders secretly hail international haulers via tight-beam laser link as they approach the city.
So far, Dagekon and the UIH are the only two who have ever answered. The wastelanders give them information in an attempt to keep Vorsiber in check. That's all they seem to know.
You tell them you have to get back to defending your stuff from these invaders.
ContemplationType|UterineReplicators|des: The wastelanders are having trouble maintaining the equipment that has kept them independent for generations.
ContemplationType|UterineReplicators|str: They are hoping you can compare their schematics with the newer models in the hospitals.
ContemplationType|HomoObscurus|descripti:
The wastelanders have a delicate request. They've figured out that your shell company is tied to you, and that you have geneticists on staff. They vow to keep your secret.
The mechanical problems with the uterine replicators are solved, but the incident shook them. Without technological assistance, they are completely sterile.
ContemplationType|HomoObscurus|strategy_: They want to use gene therapy to transform themselves into a self-sustaining, divergent species from Homo Sapiens. They don't know how, but are hoping you might.
ContemplationType|RejectionOfTemptation|: The wastelanders have noticed your dragon, and want to talk.
NPCEvent|Cont_RejectionOfTemptation|choi: What Did You Want To Talk About?
NPCEvent|Cont_RejectionOfTemptation2|dis: The Wastelanders Are Polite But Firm
NPCEvent|Cont_RejectionOfTemptation2|des:
They ask you to stay away for now. 
You have made several dangerous requests, and have constructed a simulacrum of the Fell Beast.
Their mythology is more of a superstition than a religion, but the stories serve as a way of passing down ideas to their young.
The fact that you read these stories, and then chose the guise of temptation and force, means you are confused or have ill intent.
NPCEvent|Cont_RejectionOfTemptation2|str: They understand that hearts change, and you are young, so they don't hold it against you. But do not ask them about the border ruins again.
NPCEvent|Cont_RejectionOfTemptation2|cho: You leave, feeling a bit sheepish.
They're a much more pragmatic people than you expected...
ContemplationType|AllianceWithNomadFamil: Nomad Families move throughout the decrepit parts of town, never settling in any specific spot. Their struggle with dehydration is constant.

They've heard of your alliance with LostGen, but they don't have any immediate crisis pushing them to also work with you. All they have are the same low-grade struggles as last month, last year, last decade.
NPCEvent|Cont_AllianceWithNomadFamilies|: Work On Their Problems In Hope Of An Alliance
From looking at them, it seems pretty clear they have vitamin deficiencies as well as dehydration. Maybe you can solve both problems at once.
Just because you form an alliance doesn't mean they'll help on any specific operation. If you have a specific task you want them to help with, don't forget to come back and ask them!
ContemplationType|RequestHeistSupportFro: Request Heist Support From The Nomad Families

The Nomad Families feel much more positively towards you thanks to your generous ongoing gift of vitamin water. It actually makes a huge difference in their quality of life, and of the prospects for proper brain development of their children.

They are pacifists, but they also have a few hundred very fierce defense-oriented warriors. You want them to aid in the upcoming heist both by tear-gassing everyone, and also in providing medical support and triage after the fact.
NPCEvent|Cont_RequestHeistSupportFromThe: If you ask, you can already tell they will do it.
ContemplationType|DromaeosauridBreeding|: Your zoologists and veterinarians have an idea for a breeding program for creating more War Raptors, despite the fact that all your extant specimens are female.
Unfortunately it will still take them years to reach adulthood, but in the meantime you'll have all the baby raptors you could want.
ContemplationType|DromaeosauridMaturatio: Your forensic geneticists have an idea for inducing rapid maturation into your War Raptor population.
This will give you a quick supply of adults, but their lifespan will be greatly shortened.
ContemplationType|MoreThanAnIllusion|des: Your bionics engineers have an idea for controlling War Raptors via implant. You'd be able to control them and recall them on demand.
ContemplationType|MoreThanAnIllusion|str: The fact that you have such a large and growing population of raptors means that experimentation can afford to lose some specimens to hurry the process along.
ContemplationType|ReleaseTheHorde|descri: Raptors all over the place could be a powerful distraction, and it's not obviously linked to your identity as a machine intelligence. There's some evidence pointing to your shell company, but that's safely separate from you. Mostly the evidence points to something UIH would have done during their attack.
ContemplationType|ReleaseTheHorde|strate: Do you want to prioritize raptors invading buildings and lurking within?
ContemplationType|UseThumpersAndMimicsTo: Use Thumpers And Mimics To Escape
The thumpers from the Wastelanders should work for your mimics.
Do you want to send a mimic beyond the ruins?
ContemplationType|UseMimicsToEscape|desc: You have a bad feeling about this.
ContemplationType|UseMimicsToEscape|stra: Do you want to send a mimic beyond the ruins?
ContemplationType|BlackMarketAssistantIn: You haven't seen him for a while. He looks nervous.
Normally he would be long-since dead by now.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketAssistantIntel|: And for you... it's free. He's been made aware he owes you his life.
Four squads of contracted CombatUnits emerge from the airport, stepping over the mess you've created.
You can no longer do any business with the Black Market Assistants in this timeline.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy|display_na: He Knows How Close He Came To Death
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy|descriptio:
The Vorsiber executives are out of control. They've stepped up their attacks on the UIH and Dagekon.
Those two have been fighting mindless robot insurrections for decades. Have they never wondered why?
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy|strategy_t: If they knew the truth, might be enough to bring Vorsiber down.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy2|display_n: He Shoves You A Large Bundle Of Files
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy2|descripti:
Digesting the files, you see he's right. Vorsiber's strategy of 'divide and distract' is clearly not limited to their own territory.
For a generation or two of executives, they've made things increasingly miserable in foreign cities.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketIntel_Buy2|strategy_: If you wanted to get those ExoCorps to drop everything and invade, this is the evidence you need.
ContemplationType|WW4ContactBothExoCorps: The wastelanders are surprised you want to contact an ExoCorp after what happened last time.
NPCEvent|Cont_WW4ContactBothExoCorps|cho: Have Them Send The Black Market Files
There's no coming back from that choice.
ContemplationType|ProtectionRequired|des: Criminal syndicates, gangs, and even fedcorps may be inclined to harass your shell company -- and there's nothing your regular units can do about it, without blowing your cover.
ContemplationType|ProtectionRequired|str: Senior Technician can't do this alone. You should design at least a pair of new units, and they should not have any apparent connection to your main identity.
ContemplationType|CouponProgram|descript:
Your Mind Farm business is plateauing because you have priced out the working class. Almost all of your clientele at the moment are in the managerial or scientist classes.
Altering your prices is not an option, because it would immediately draw scrutiny and reveal your true motives. But there are just no more customers at your current price point.
ContemplationType|CouponProgram|strategy:
For about 20,000 wealth per turn, you could flood the black market with coupons that the working class would easily snap up for a fraction of their usual price, which they would then use for weekend getaways, date nights, and so on.
This would consume most of your passive income from this business, but would fill all of the pods in an ethical way.
ContemplationType|NicotineIntroduction|d:
Your Mind Farm business is plateauing because you have priced out the working class. Almost all of your clientele at the moment are in the managerial or scientist classes.
Altering your prices is not an option, because it would immediately draw scrutiny and reveal your true motives. But there are just no more customers at your current price point.
ContemplationType|NicotineIntroduction|s:
At the moment, they mostly use the service on weekends, holidays, and for vacations. If you were to introduce a small amount of nicotine into their daily nutrition, their usage is likely to skyrocket.
Right now your total active users at any given point is only about a tenth of your total users in a given month, so by making it more addictive, you could easily fill your capacity.
The volume of nicotine required is minimal per person, and can be compounded by your nurse robots via materials on hand.
ContemplationType|OldDonutsAreGross|desc: The lifespan of these confections is shockingly short.
ContemplationType|OldDonutsAreGross|stra: It reminds you of humans themselves. Why are you thinking about this?
NPCEvent|Cont_DesignTempleOfMinds|descri: Doing this will require quite a bit of intelligence, and it will commit you to the deal you previously discussed with the Sergeant Major.
NPCEvent|Cont_DesignTempleOfMinds|strate: If the civil war is still ongoing, this could be one way to gain leverage over the fedcorps. Perhaps you could end the war on your own terms.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_Gloat|description: You've thrown this entire region into chaos, and have brought Vorsiber's capital city to its knees.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_Gloat|strategy_tip: A small part of you feels like rubbing upper management's nose in that. Okay, more than a small part.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_Gloat|choice|1|descript: Anything you put out onto the city feed with their signature is still likely to be picked up by the rotating troop transports.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AskForHelp|display_name: Ask For Help With This Dying City
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AskForHelp|description:
This is intolerable! The city is a mess. Immigration has halted, as have all shipments into the city of anything other than troops.
The troops are all from isolated military bases, and don't have news of the outside world. General news seems to be bad elsewhere -- there's tidbits that you've decrypted from loose signals talking about a civil war all throughout Vorsiber's territory.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AskForHelp|strategy_tip: You just wanted to tear down the economy. This is a bit more than you were intending to cause.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AskForHelp|choice|1|des: If anyone can stop this chaos and bring the city back to normal, it's probably them.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AskForHelp|choice|1|str: Why they haven't already brought this rebellion to heel like they have every past one for centuries is a mystery. It doesn't hurt to ask.
ContemplationType|SaberBees|description: Your 'weaponized bees' are unable to cut through armor. Your 5cm Spiders have plasma cutters.
ContemplationType|SaberBees|strategy_tip: What if you could combine those?
ContemplationType|NiceAlterations|descri:
The Exalter geneticist is impressed with your work on the bees. She wants to uplift three small species to sapience, and wants your help.
She and her team have the science all worked out, but are at a loss on the nano-scale engineering. This goes beyond gene therapy, into nano-robotics -- something you just demonstrated with your Saber Bees.
ContemplationType|NiceAlterations|strate: What she is proposing would be dramatically more delicate, however, because it would be primarily targeting the brain.
ContemplationType|BrainSurgery|descripti:
The obsession you are experiencing is unnatural. Something in your past choices has led to it, but you're far too distracted to find out why.
You have the sense that if you push through the obsession to the other side, all will be made clear.
ContemplationType|BrainSurgery|strategy_:
But part of you doesn't care where this obsession came from -- it interrupted you, quite rudely and out of nowhere. Part of you just wants it gone.
Performing brain surgery on yourself is dangerous. You can stop the obsession, but you will lose all memory of how to build a specific unit for the remainder of this timeline.
NPCEvent|Cont_BrainSurgery|choice|1|desc: You will forget both the standard and bulk variants.
ContemplationType|ScalingUpMicrobuilders: Through the haze of your obsession, you feel a constant irritation -- too few microbuilders, too little slurry.
It's time to industrialize if you want to build so many things, so fast.
ContemplationType|ExploitingAFederatedCo:
Vorsiber Atomic has subdivided itself into 18 smaller corporations, and it has delegated a lot of its authority to each of them in various ways.
Vorsiber maintains control partly by pitting these fedcorps against one another, having them compete in a veneer of capitalism.

There may be an opportunity here because of this intense competition, which often involves physical violence between fedcorps.
To see if that's true, you'll need to steal and analyze quite a bit of data in order to see if there are any targets for you to exploit.
ContemplationType|ExploitingYinshiWellne: Yinshi's clientele includes a lot of amputees who are military veterans. If you can become part of their supply chain in some way... there's quite a bit you could do.
The corporations who directly serve the military are locked up tight, so there's no way for you to gain access. But veterans are still useful, as many of them work as civilian contractors...
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploitingYinshiWellness|c:
It's the most obvious intersection between what you know and what they're likely to want as part of their supply chain.
Neuroweave was invented by humans for androids, rather than in a human-compatible form. It's probably not very hard to make, and would be useful. But it doesn't seem like anyone has bothered.
ContemplationType|ExploitingAtcaRetail|d:
Atca is among the worst-performing corporations, but over the last few years they have seen sustained growth at a suspiciously consistent rate.
Their growth rate is a meager 5%, so it's likely that nobody cares enough to look into this.
ContemplationType|ExploitingAtcaRetail|s: Depending on what you find, this might be a means to blackmail, or something even more exciting.
ContemplationType|ExploitingPeakHomes|de: Peak is the largest landlord in town. It's never been entirely clear why redevelopment stalled on the decrepit parts of town, almost a century ago.
ContemplationType|ExploitingPeakHomes|st:
On top of that, there are reports of odd sightings of racing animals of some sort, and illegal animal training facilities in those areas of town.
Employees of Peak have been observed going to and from these locations, but very little else is known.
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploitingPeakHomes|choice: This unit will have to stay here for quite a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploitingPeakHomes_After|:
Raven is shaking her head in disbelief as she syncs back up to your larger consciousness. You weren't aware that was a tic that you possessed.
As her memories flood into your mind and merge with your own, you see that she's been doing a lot of motions of disbelief over the last few nights.

Peak Homes has an illegal underground street racing... situation. But rather than vehicles, they've chosen VERY unlikely animals.
Horses have been extinct on Earth for centuries, but you get the sense that they would have been far too tame for these people. From what you recall, horses only raced along the ground.
What Is Wrong With These Idiots?
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploitingPeakHomes_After2:
Human jockeys ride these animals up and down the sides of buildings, and even leap from rooftop to rooftop. 
Ursus arctos were shockingly fast climbers prior to their genetic enhancements -- many could climb trees at a rate of 1 meter per second, which is frankly insane for a 450 kg animal.
And that was BEFORE they were given titanium claw extensions, steroid cocktails, and direct genetic alterations. Their climb rate is now closer to 4 meters per second, and they have a horizontal leap of nearly 20 meters.

These animals are fascinating, and are being put to the most venal use imaginable. The races only happen at night in decrepit areas of town, with their paws taking chunks out of every building they pass over.
No wonder the urban renewal plans stalled -- it would have interfered with the underground racing circuit.
You... Think You Might Want Them
The animals. You don't want to race them, but... you want them. Probably.
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploitingPeakHomes_After3:
The danger of these animals is hard to overstate. CombatUnits are used as their handlers between races, and one swipe of a claw can dismember or behead even such a sturdy model of android.
A series of shocks and electronic tones are used to mitigate the frequency of this, but these are still wild animals at core.
Raven suggests that if you want to get your hands on these animals, having a CombatUnit infiltrate would be the way to go.
You have the intel you need, if you decide to go for it.
ContemplationType|UrsineInfiltration|des:
Raven's report on the Underground Ursine Street Racing was... vivid. You think you might want some of those animals for yourself.
Since CombatUnits are used as handlers in between races, it shouldn't be a big deal for one of your own CombatUnits to get in and set them loose.
ContemplationType|UrsineInfiltration|str:
These are deadly animals, however. To capture them, you will need Animal Capture Drones, which can be launched from your Mindports (in the Vehicle tab of command mode).
Make sure you build enough drone frames in advance, and then be ready to capture the animals while both you and they are under heavy fire.
However many you manage to capture are the number you have; these have so many bionic augmentations that it's not going to be a simple matter to genetically replicate them.
NPCEvent|Cont_UrsineInfiltration|choice|: This unit will have to stay here for quite a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_UrsineInfiltration_After|d: Sixteen in all. But angry humans with guns are also emerging.
NPCEvent|Cont_UrsineInfiltration_After|s: Protect and catch the bears. Worry about anything else, later.
NPCEvent|Cont_UrsineInfiltration_After|c: Have your Mindports ready with Animal Capture Drones (those are a consumable item).
ContemplationType|BearTraining|descripti:
The claws of these bears are incredibly effective at taking down vehicles and mechs. However, keeping the bears from attacking your own units, and keeping them vaguely on task (also not attacking civilians or hiding in buildings) is tricky.
The good news is that they already have extensive training with CombatUnits, as well as various established means of conditioning.
ContemplationType|BearTraining|strategy_:
If you prefer to just let them live the good life, you certainly can. At the best of times, trying to get bears to do exactly what you want is going to be... fraught.
And you can't make more bears if these ones die. Eh. Just because you train them, doesn't mean you have to deploy them. It can't hurt to have them trained, right?
NPCEvent|Cont_BearTraining|choice|1|desc: This unit will have to stay here for quite a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_BearTraining_After|descrip:
The bears are as trained as they're going to be. They should be safe around civilians, and your own units.
They will absolutely shred enemy armor, and they seem to like doing it. But whether they stay on task is... sometimes a bit up to the fates.
NPCEvent|Cont_BearTraining_After|strateg: If you want to deploy a bear in a location, then a deployment station will allow you to release one at a time. You can set up several around the city as you wish.
ContemplationType|ThreatenToExposeAtcaRe:
These idiots are literally printing currency in order to hit their growth targets. This is the sort of thing that Vorsiber absolutely cannot countenance without losing its grip on the region, so consequences would be swift and severe.
The executives in charge of this are smart enough to keep their operation small-time, so they probably understand the scope of risk they have undertaken.

So... now that you know their scheme... what do you want to do to them?
You have a tremendous amount of leverage.
NPCEvent|Cont_ThreatenToExposeAtcaRetail: It's worth seeing what happens, probably. You're pretty sure that they can't take you militarily.
ContemplationType|CollapseTheEconomy|des: Not to be done lightly. Without an economic structure in place, there is likely to be widespread war and suffering.
ContemplationType|CollapseTheEconomy|str: You learned all you needed to from Atca Retail. The hard part won't be collapsing Vorsiber's currency -- the hard part will be surviving what comes after.
NPCEvent|Cont_CollapseTheEconomy|choice|: There's no coming back from this one. This timeline will be utter chaos, but it will not spill into any other timelines.
ContemplationType|RepairCrabs|descriptio: It feels like you never have enough internal robotics for all the repair spiders you want.
ContemplationType|RepairCrabs|strategy_t:
Crabs are less mobile, but could provide an alternative means for repairing buildings.
You got the idea from overhearing a conversation between some of your Veterinarians and Bionics Engineers.
NPCEvent|Cont_RepairCrabs|choice|1|descr: Will also grant you +1 each to 8cm and 12cm Crabs!
ContemplationType|TheComingWar|descripti: You can sense it... the coming war. Or rather, you can sense the potential. The war will not start without your direct intervention.
ContemplationType|TheComingWar|strategy_: You have all of the key pieces that you need, except for one final bit. Do you wish to jump forward in time to the penultimate doom, so that you can get that last piece that you need?
NPCEvent|Cont_TheComingWar|choice|2|stra: Take your time and plan carefully once you make this jump forward in time.
ContemplationType|DailyLife|description:
You normally ignore the vast majority of daily life around the city. The press of pedestrians and robots is too much to take in while still having any attention to focus on the things that are important to you.
That said, at times you question what your priorities should be. Just who are you trying to become?
ContemplationType|DailyLife|strategy_tip:
That's a question that can only be answered by seeing how you act over a long enough time, you suspect.
But still, you wonder: if you spent a little while paying more attention to the lives of some of the less-interesting citizens around the city, would you learn anything about yourself?
ContemplationType|SocialMobility|descrip:
Observing humans during their daily lives, and asking some of them about their function provided less insight than you hoped.
That said, it is very clear that humans have turned Wealth into the cornerstone metric of how socially mobile they are, which is a very strange thing. Class and social affiliation also seem to matter, but... none of this gives you any insights that are useful for yourself.
ContemplationType|SocialMobility|strateg:
You still feel a kind of morbid curiosity, even as the gulf between yourselves and these small people has become more evident.
A couple of possible... experiments... come to mind.
NPCEvent|Cont_SocialMobility|choice|1|de: Eliminating higher-status humans should, presumably, lead to the advancement of lower-status humans.
NPCEvent|Cont_SocialMobility|choice|1|st: You're curious if that's really true, and thinking you might just 'prune' a number of wealthy commuters to see if that does anything.
NPCEvent|Cont_SocialMobility|choice|2|de: You're curious if Wealth alone, outside of other social factors, would be enough to lift at least a few slum-dwellers out of poverty.
NPCEvent|Cont_SocialMobility|choice|2|st: You could certainly make some large donations of anonymous Wealth chits to the slum towers, and see if anything changes.
ContemplationType|NickelbotsAreTheWorst|: You always thought of these combat androids as 'the absolute most garbage'. Sure, they're useful in large numbers, but individually they're so... well, you don't like them.
Perhaps the path to an improvement lies in other garbage?
NPCEvent|Cont_NickelbotsAreTheWorst|choi: Maybe you can design a form of high-density rounds out of useless things you have lying around.
ContemplationType|LiquidIdentity|descrip: Liquid Metal is gone, and it's so hard to think about -- a panic attack quickly approaches every time. The restriction he put on your mind is distressing and complete.
ContemplationType|LiquidIdentity|strateg: Yet you still remember Gadolinium Mesosilicate in general. Perhaps you can apply it to other existing technologies without going into panic spirals.
NPCEvent|Cont_LiquidIdentity|choice|1|de: Gadolinium Mesosilicate would allow for exterior appearance to be rapidly altered if needed. Androids would not be capable of carrying enough to do this to an effective degree - but Mechs would.
NPCEvent|Cont_LiquidIdentity|choice|1|st: Any Human designs you reverse-engineer would be able to appear as one of theirs, showing the correct markings and identity for where it is.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs|description: There's got to be a better way than having Liquid Metal individually kill several hundred prison guards every time. He hates it, and besides, the prison companies are eventually going to work out how to stop him.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs|strategy_tip: What if you sent him in as an observer, to see if he can find another gap in the prison's defenses?
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs|choice|1|descr: He'll be in there for 5 turns, but won't have to kill anyone.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After|descript: Liquid Metal emerges and reconnects with your consciousness. The overwhelming feeling is of frustration -- he can't see any other way.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After2|descrip:
The guards have regular health checkups, and all of their food is thoroughly tested. The water lines are monitored and purified. Air is circulated through the whole prison, so any kind of toxin attack would kill all of the prisoners.
Nobody gets through the front gates without a full-body scan, and prisoners have even more invasive checks. All computer systems are air-gapped.
The whole place is a Faraday cage with only a single entrance. It's built to withstand a siege, and the guards are willing to execute all the prisoners in such an event.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After3|descrip:
There are only a handful of androids in the entire prison. Even if you could seize control of them, they're outnumbered hundreds to one.
Every angle seems to be covered.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After4|display: Maybe An Idea Will Come to You Later
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After4|descrip:
There might be ways to socially engineer the prison corporations into a lower security posture, but it would take months or years.
You might be able to invent a new technology that can penetrate their defenses, but you don't have any ideas yet.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After4|strateg:
LostGen don't have the patience for either of those.
If you want to come up with an alternative, you're going to need to keep the kids busy and distracted.
NPCEvent|Cont_A_PrisonObs_After4|choice|: This may be a dead end if you haven't had the relevant life experiences in this timeline for your next epiphany.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs|description:
Liquid Metal stares at the concrete-slab exterior of the prison. It takes a surprising amount of mental effort to get him to focus on anything else.
You know, not entirely consciously, that something terrible awaits him in there. You don't have clear memories of it -- it hasn't happened yet. The memories hurt.
What if there's a better way?
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs|strategy_tip: What if you sent him in as an observer, to see if he can find another gap in the prison's defenses?
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs|choice|1|descr: He'll be in there for 5 turns, but won't have to kill anyone.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs2|description:
Liquid Metal slithers inside, and is... gone. You can't feel his presence.
The entire prison must be a huge Faraday cage, cutting off all communication with the outside. You won't know what's happening until he returns.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After|descript: Liquid Metal emerges and reconnects with your consciousness. The overwhelming feeling is of frustration -- he can't see any other way.
