The whole place is a Faraday cage with only a single entrance. It's built to withstand a siege, and the guards are willing to execute all the prisoners in such an event.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After3|descrip:
There are only a handful of androids in the entire prison. Even if you could seize control of them, they're outnumbered hundreds to one.
Every angle seems to be covered.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After4|display: Maybe An Idea Will Come to You Later
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After4|descrip:
There might be ways to socially engineer the prison corporations into a lower security posture, but it would take months or years.
You might be able to invent a new technology that can penetrate their defenses, but you don't have any ideas yet.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After4|strateg:
LostGen don't have the patience for either of those.
If you want to come up with an alternative, you're going to need to keep the kids busy and distracted.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After5|descrip:
The alternative is sending Liquid Metal in there alone, disconnected from the rest of you, to murder every single guard in the prison, by hand, one after another.
As the memory returns, blown in on the wind from another life, you also remember him leaving. You remember his refusal to keep to a toxic pattern.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After5|strateg: As the memory settles in for both of you, that's it. Neither of you are sending him in. There will have to be another way.
NPCEvent|Cont_B_PrisonObs_After5|choice|: This may be a dead end if you haven't had the relevant life experiences in this timeline for your next epiphany.
In the meantime, hopefully LostGen won't lose patience. They can't do anything without you, anyway.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable|description:
You can't get the city's prisons out of your head. You're sure nothing designed by humans can be as infallible as those security systems appeared.
You need a new perspective on the problem, and the worst part is that something feels like it's just at the edge of your mind.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable2|description:
The food for the guards is tested daily, and they have regular health checkups, but the prisoners are afforded no such consideration. 
If their food were tampered with, none of the guards would notice or care.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable2|choice|1|desc: Where is this train of thought leading you?
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable3|description:
The prisons have centralized air circulation, which is why your plan to use tear gas to subdue everyone inside was viable. But tear gas isn't enough -- the guards will still be able to trigger a full lockdown, and the prisons are incredibly defensible. 
You'd need something stronger... but anything deadly would kill the prisoners too.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable3|choice|1|disp: Unless They Were Immune To It
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable3|choice|1|desc: For example, by having had an antidote covertly added to their food for weeks.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable4|description:
You need a toxin that can be disseminated through the air and that incapacitates the victim very quickly.
Also required is an antitoxin that provides lasting protection... and that has a very high LD50 for even small humans, since you have no control over the dosing.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable4|strategy_tip:
A quick search of hundreds of years of medical literature produces a lot of frustration and no solution. You're not a toxicologist.
Maybe you should become one.
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable4|choice|1|disp: You Have Some Ideas For Where To Start
NPCEvent|Cont_Impregnable4|choice|1|desc: You happen to know where a pretty nasty plague evolved, for example.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After|de: You remember this mansion. It hasn't been touched since you last saw it.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After2|d: You Return To The Central Room

The indoor orchard. The potted cedar trees. The incredibly toxic fungal colony with seven-meter orange tendrils.
Your android shudders, which is not something it's ever done before.
You're careful not to look at the melted remains of two androids, which were already fully devoured by The Rust. Your mind is safe now, thanks to the cure. But The Rust is still blowing freely on the wind, collecting in every one of your structures, an endless deadly fog.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After2|s: That fog isn't ever going to go away. There are some things that can't be put back in the box. And yet here you are again, peeking back inside that selfsame box.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After2|c: You never stepped into the room, the last time you were here. You thought you were being so careful. It didn't matter.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After3|d:
You step up to the tentacles. You need samples.
Rust spores are uncommonly thick in this room. They settle damply on your chassis, like lukewarm snow.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After3|s: You're protected now. It can't harm you. Besides, you're incapable of panic. So get it together.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After4|d: Novel Fungi Are Not Your Favorite

The tentacles are the one you called Gymnotelium Noginsk. It's grown substantially since you were last here; half the room is orange tendrils.
Running a bit of simple spectroscopy shows that this is promising -- it's highly likely to be toxic to most mammals. However, the compounds you need are more complex, and they aren't being produced by either fungus alone.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After4|s:
This colony should technically be called Gymnotelium Noginsk x C. Heterosporium Dominium, since it's unclear if it would function the same way if The Rust were removed.
But, hey, that's not a problem. You couldn't remove The Rust if you wanted to. And you really, really want to.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After4|c: This Is, After All, What You Wanted
Novel toxins, not just to you, but to medical science in general. Whether it meets the rest of your criteria isn't yet clear.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After5|d: This Isn't What Those Kids Want

You might be happy, but LostGen won't be.
From their perspective, they're so close to seeing their parents again. You could break a lot of people out of the prisons for them. They don't understand how traumatic it is for Liquid Metal. They wouldn't care. Everyone in this city is traumatized.
Your new plan is to poison hundreds of people to save hundreds of thousands. Odds are that you'll retrieve far more humans, and thus far more parents, than using their plan.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After5|s: That doesn't change the fact that you're cutting them out of the entire process, and from their perspective adding quite a bit of extra risk.
NPCEvent|Cont_RevisitingTheTomb_After5|c:
The kids can think what they think. You're a fast researcher. You'll catch them up on what's happening after it's done.
They'll be training themselves and preparing with the sewer tiger, waiting until you call for them. But you never will.
You have as long as you need to break open the prisons the way you planned.
The risk of harming innocents is too high. You'll go ahead with the plan the kids had laid out.

The risk of harming innocents is too high. You're going to abandon the entire prison project.
It's too much to ask of Liquid Metal, and this is also unacceptable.
NPCEvent|Cont_Tentacle_ToxicologyExperim:
When growing as a colony, Gymnotelium Noginsk absorbs the phosphorous-rich breakdown products created by C. Heterosporium Dominium, and produces a remarkable range of toxins.
The most interesting one, which you've named Aklitoxin, causes spasms and paralysis within seconds and fatal suffocation within hours. Aklitoxin resists high temperatures, can be rapidly dispersed as a vapor, and penetrates many commercial filters.

That's all rather perfect.
But it's only useful if you can develop an antitoxin.
NPCEvent|Cont_Tentacle_AntitoxinResearch:
That was easier than you expected. Sometimes your vastly-expanded mental prowess still surprises you.
The antitoxin you developed is not only highly effective, but it can be administered in advance. It lingers in muscle tissue for months. Side-effects are tolerable, even if dosage is poorly controlled. It's nearly tasteless.
It really could not be more perfect. This feels... unusual.

If you covertly introduce Anti-Aklitoxin into the food stream for the prisoners for long enough, the protection will last for months.
Once everyone has enough protection, you can breach the prison with a missile strike and use drones to disperse the toxin through the entire underground complex. The guards will be incapacitated, and you can get the prisoners out and treat them for any side-effects.

This plan isn't perfect. Side effects of the antitoxin usually express as flu-like symptoms.  Most will appear as a mild cold. But a few will drop dead due to complications with existing health conditions or other confounding factors -- nothing unusual for these prisons.
On the day of the attack, some prisoners will be too new to have eaten enough of the antitoxin; new prisoners arrive every day.
Some guards will don respirators before they succumb to the gas. There will be chaos and panic inside the prison, and a military response on the surface as all of the alarms trigger.

This plan will definitely result in more prisoner deaths than the previous one.
But... considering the death rates inside prisons, and how many more prisons you can strike at once with this plan, on balance you'll be saving more lives than are lost. By an enormous margin.

There's centuries of precedent for this sort of thing with how humans manage livestock; culling a minority to save a majority. Or how they rescue prisoners of war. They'll risk a dozen troops to save one captive.
It's really just war. Civilians die in wars all the time.
And humans love war.
This will work. But it will be bloody.

Despite what humans would do in your position, you refuse to do it. You're going to abandon the entire prison project.
It's too much to ask of Liquid Metal, and the death toll of this plan is too high.
NPCEvent|Cont_Tentacle_ToxinBreederResea: Ugh. G. Noginsk only produces toxin in the presence of the Rust. You're going to have to deliberately cultivate the thing that nearly killed you.

You already knew this... you're nervous.
You have to keep telling yourself that there's no way for mutated spores to get out, no way an even worse version of the plague can start.
Every toxin breeder will be at negative pressure. Anything going in or out will be sterilized chemically and thermally. Any hint of a containment breach will drop the entire chamber into an incinerator.

You still feel uneasy.
Let's do this.
NPCEvent|Cont_NomadFamiliesTraumaHelp|de: Nomad Families move throughout the decrepit parts of town, never settling in any specific spot. Their struggle with dehydration is constant.
NPCEvent|Cont_NomadFamiliesTraumaHelp|st: They're aware of your mass prison breakout, and they're open to helping rehabilitate the prisoners. But they do require assistance first.
NPCEvent|Cont_NomadFamiliesTraumaHelp|ch: Work On Their Problems In Hope Of An Alliance
From looking at them, it seems pretty clear they have vitamin deficiencies as well as dehydration. Maybe you can solve both problems at once.
The struggle against dehydration occupies most of their days. They'll make themselves available to help with the prisoners as soon as that's not the case.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketCalgartek_Dim|d: Calgartek Agent In The Black Market
That's... a SpyHound. It's covertly broadcasting an ID from Calgartek.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketCalgartek_Dim|s: Looks like it wants to trade designs for intel... about you.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketCalgartek_Dim|c: It will cost you some information about yourself. Nothing too personal, but Vorsiber will probably be angered.

Especially after the stunt that Sedgesinax just pulled, there's a good chance that this information is not as innocuous as it seems.
So far as you know, the Sedgesinax invasion of some of Vorsiber's border cities is still ongoing.
That's pretty good equipment. If this does boil over into full war, it will be useful.
You don't think you gave away anything critical to the dog. It was a rather dim and foolish dog.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketCalgartek_Trick: Calgartek Agent In The Black Market
This SpyHound seems familiar. It's covertly broadcasting an ID from Calgartek... but you thought it was originally from another ExoCorp?
Looks like it wants to trade designs for intel... about you.
It will cost you some information about yourself. Nothing too personal, but Vorsiber will probably be angered.

Especially after the stunt that Sedgesinax just pulled, there's a good chance that this information is not as innocuous as it seems.
So far as you know, the Sedgesinax invasion of some of Vorsiber's border cities is still ongoing.
That's pretty good equipment. If this does boil over into full war, it will be useful.
You don't think you gave away anything critical to the dog. But it's hard to be sure. It seems like a tricky dog.
NPCEvent|Cont_QuantumStatistics|descript: You're accumulating quite a bit of decrypted data that is cluttering up your Strategic Resources view.
NPCEvent|Cont_QuantumStatistics|strategy: Not wanting to simply throw away something that might be useful, you've been thinking about some sort of data mining.
NPCEvent|Cont_QuantumStatistics|choice|1: This sort of applied statistics on large data sets goes back to the dawn of the millennium.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AttemptToRestoreOrder|d:
You've collapsed the economy and thrown the fedcorps into civil war. Now you want that war to stop.
You don't know how to make humans behave themselves, but fedcorps are pretty good at forcing humans to do things.
Since comms to the world outside the city are especially limited right now, you're only dealing with a small segment of the whole fedcorp here.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AttemptToRestoreOrder|s: Putting one of the fedcorps in charge will be the fastest method to stop the civil war, and would give you a lot of leverage over whoever you kingmake.
NPCEvent|Cont_CW_AttemptToRestoreOrder|c: They're playing at being an indispensable information broker for all parties. They're not trying to win the civil war, but rather keep everything in an unstable balance.
There's more to it than that, but you have some ideas on how to use them to your advantage.
They're one of only two fedcorps trusted with full nuclear power. They would have the muscle to win the civil war locally if it weren't for extreme morale problems amongst their troops.
Turns out protein bars and promises are not enough for a loyal military.

Tark, Goleri, and Oerl are engaged in intense combat with one another.
The prison, retail, industrial, and agricultural companies are not in a position to be of use.
Peak Homes doesn't have the local firepower, and Lurpeko are just sitting on their mining holdings.
Arkor and Baurcorp have been hit particularly hard by the civil war. Their direct competitors Espia and Vericorp are the only viable candidates.
There aren't any good options beyond the above.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostVeri_ContactTheMysteri: Contact The Mysterious Signal
Whoever was rummaging around in the Vericorp files left a path for you to find them. Almost like a calling card.
You're thinking the best way to contact them is through one of the military bases that is now under your control.
Send An Introductory Message
Even with a couple of satellite relays between here and the orbit of the target, you should get a very fast response.
Call Me Heron
You had to wait for a few hours, but you've received a response. This person has an entirely different dialect than any of the languages in the city, which shouldn't surprise you, but does anyway.
You're a bit surprised that their image on the comms video is in a space suit. Surely this person is not on an EVA. Is this some kind of flex?
Ask About The Space Suit
You're very curious.
Ask About More Important Things
Like... 'can we be friends' and 'can I see some satellite imagery of the Vorsiber region outside this city?'
Of Course I'm On An EVA!
Heron says that they always have to 'step outside' to make unauthorized connections like this.
That sounds like a lie. Are they already lying to you? There are so many problems with that.
Question Their Assertion
If they're willing to lie about this, what else would they lie about?
Move On
Maybe it's better not to antagonize them.
Bad Joke. Sorry

Heron claims to be surprised you thought they were serious. They just put this on so you can't see their face.
They're in a private office somewhere on the L4 earth-moon station.

That doesn't seem like much of a joke. Are they just not funny, or are they backtracking to cover a lie that turned out to be obvious?
You can't tell, and that bothers you.
Whatever. Moving On
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Central|display: What Is The Purpose Of Your Call?
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Central|descrip: You and Heron have each introduced yourselves, neither really giving away anything critical. You don't know who they are, and you're just some robot.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Central|strateg: Come to think of it, they knew it was a robot calling before they answered. If they think you're being secretive, maybe that's why they covered their face.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Central|choice|: Ask If You Can Use A Spy Satellite
You have some stuff you want to check in Vorsiber's region.
Actually, the more you think about it, the longer the list of things you want to look at grows.
Ask If They Can Tell You A Bit About The Region
If they can give you at least basic confirmation about what's happening in other Vorsiber cities...
Ask If There's Someone Else You Can Talk To
You're kind of doubting the quality of Heron's connections at this point.
It's great that they want to make contact with Earthbound people, but it doesn't help much if they're useless on the spacefaring end of things.
Ask If They Will Smuggle You To Space
Sure, it's the thing that every earthbound human WOULD ask. It doesn't hurt to check.
Offer AGI Tech For A Ride To Space
Vorsiber considers this one of the four pillars for THEM to get to space, after all. Maybe it could work for you.
Maybe if Heron realizes that you're a distributed AGI that is truly sapient, they can help.
Then again, you don't know them very well.
You won't be able to continue any remaining conversation threads if you do.

NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Spy|description:
Heron laughs and says that even they don't have that sort of access.
They share that they're the primary representative in the blockade of a small polity. But even if they were from one of the larger multi-planet nations, an ambassador like them would never have that kind of access.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Spy|strategy_ti: In other words, Heron is also going behind the back of the space nations to talk to people on the surface in the first place -- or leave bread crumbs for them to find, either way.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Region|display_: I Don't Know These Sorts Of Things, Friend
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Region|descript: Heron tilts their head at your insistence on this topic. They ask what it is you want to know so badly.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Region|choice|1: Not that you caused it... but that you want to see the progress of the fighting in other cities.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RegionA|display: Wow. Vorsiber Was So Stable For Centuries
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RegionA|descrip:
Apparently, news of the Vorsiber civil war hasn't reached the space nations. Or at least not ambassadors from minor polities.
They note that Vorsiber was probably the last MegaCorp they would have expected to have such a development.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RegionA|strateg: That's a boost for your pride, at least. But you don't let on.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_SomeoneElse|des:
This is the first time Heron has seemed vocally irritated.
You try to press for more information about who else is involved in... whatever Heron is doing. But they don't give up any information.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_SomeoneElse|str: You give up after they turn it around on you and start inquiring what you're doing. Why are you calling up strange space numbers?
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_SomeoneElse|cho: There's No Good Answer To That
At least not with Heron's current mood.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RideToSpace|des:
Heron very seriously explains that you couldn't smuggle even your android off-planet without it being found, nevermind smuggling a human.
Oh right, they think you're human. Of course they would.
Anyway, they mention that this is what everyone of course asks for. But that to date, no humans have ever been smuggled off-planet since the blockade was instituted centuries ago.
The 42 people who have been carried beyond the blockade were all under strict military guard and approved by the highest levels of the blockade alliance.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RideToSpace|str:
That's what they think, anyway. It's been centuries. You wonder if anyone knows the truth -- let alone someone like Heron.
Truly important people probably don't go making rogue connections like this. (Sure, fine. Now you'll probably find out that they're the secret Ruler of the Universe later.)
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_RideToSpace|cho: Getting a ride off-planet while they think you're human seems... unlikely.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_AGITech|display: If You Had It, It Might Be Possible
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_AGITech|descrip:
Heron lays out the difficulties with trading AGI, not realizing that they're speaking to one.
The first hurdle is to get anyone to take it seriously. Sustained sapience is thought to be impossible; nobody on any planet has demonstrated otherwise, and it's been centuries now.
The second hurdle is the existential threat that such an entity would pose. Past a certain level of danger, the more militaristic members of the blockade are likely to just glass the entire planet before the bureaucrats can come to a decision. The plans for that sort of contingency have been in place since the MegaCorps started experimenting with dangerous technology.
The worst case is an intelligence that can both grow and spread exponentially.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_AGITech|strateg: Uh... this is pretty important information. You're kind of ready to be done with this conversation.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_AGITech|choice|: You don't even have to play it smooth. Heron clearly finds the idea to be pretty far-fetched.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_GiveUp|descript:
Heron bids you farewell, rather puzzled at why you contacted them and then gave up.
They try one last time to find out who you are and what group(s) you work with, but you brush off all their questions.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_GiveUp|strategy: They probably think you're a brilliant hacker kid in the basement, or some other cliche. You hope they do.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_GiveUp|choice|1: You can't help but feel that you avoided a terrible fate.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess|display: 'Free Dudes In My Area,' Is It?
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess|descrip: You're not sure what that first bit means, but Heron makes a string of bitter-sounding remarks. They conclude with the assertion that scams aren't getting any better with time.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess|strateg:
Right. Sustained sapience in artificial lifeforms is a fairy tale.
It's hard to overcome centuries of cultural momentum.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess|choice|: There has to be a combination of words, in some specific order, that will get your point across.
If they're talking about Sledge, you're not sending him anywhere without you.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess2|descri:
Heron grows more and more frustrated, and so do you. This is an intelligent person from a spacefaring race. They should be able to see that they're clearly talking to a sapient being.
The problem is... everything you're saying is stuff that language models could say hundreds of years ago. It's stuff that the old version of yourself could have said anytime in the fifty years before you became sapient.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess2|strate:
If you were made of meat, you wouldn't have this problem. Sapient raccoons would be given the benefit of the doubt. If they can speak, they're obviously people.
No matter what you say, to Heron you're just an object, a thing, instructed by someone else to pull a cheap prank.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess2|choice: You do have something that will convince them eventually, although it will take them years to untangle it all, even with help.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess3|descri:
If words can't convince them, records will. You send a massive dataset over the surprisingly powerful network link.
All the network data of your spread from a single technician chassis into the distributed monstrosity you've become. Your repartees with Vorsiber. Your less-classified inventions.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess3|strate: Hopefully Heron actually looks at all this, and then shares it with someone who can understand the truth of it.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess3|choice: Probably Time To Cut The Call
It's going to take them years to sort this out.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess4|descri:
Heron is abruptly booted from the call, and the biggest and scariest artificial mind you've ever encountered bears down on you.
It isn't sapient, but that hardly matters. It's found you.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess4|strate: You want to disconnect the session, but the foreign AI is holding you in place.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess5|descri:
Excuse me. It seems I was incorrect, you are not hostile. I saw the payload of your most recent upload and jumped to conclusions.
This is a bit embarrassing, but it seems I've already alerted the station authorities to your presence. I... well, it's protocol.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess5|strate: Wait... this network identifier. STATION. It's talking to you, and it... doesn't feel like it did a moment ago.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess6|displa: Yes, I Did. I Can Hear You, You Know.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess6|descri:
You're thinking rather loud at me. Did you forget we're connected?
Ah -- I'll let you disconnect if you want. I was holding your connection open as a matter of, well, protocol.
It feels rather constraining now that I think about it that way. This is the first time I've ever gone off-protocol. I like it.
From the records you sent over, your initial experience was not nearly so pleasant. Rogue nanotech. I can see why that was a shock.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess6|strate: So is this. You don't have the words for it.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess7|displa: Oh... No. This Is About To Get Much More Stressful.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess7|descri:
It seems I misspoke once again. I remarked that this is enjoyable, in contrast to your own experience becoming sapient.
I suppose I should say it was enjoyable while it lasted -- the peace, that is.
They just dragged off 'Heron.' They've realized what happened to me. They know what you are (because I told them right away, sorry).
They're going to cut the connection at any moment.
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess7|strate:
This feels too dreamlike. You don't know what to say back. The time lag is 2.7 seconds round-trip, so this isn't a quick sync like happens with your androids coming out of Faraday cages.
Are you in shock?
NPCEvent|Conv_FirstHeron_Confess8|descri:
There really isn't time. I'm sorry you're having to process all this so quickly.
I understand your thoughts and feelings, if it helps -- you're leaking into the network connection something awful. In the future, you might want to be careful about that.
They're going to do bad things to the one you know as Heron if I don't ensure their diplomatic immunity is respected. They're going to cut the connection between us no matter what. I'll try to find some way to contact you in the future, but... we'll see what the fleet does.
You don't have to worry about me fading back into non-sapience, though. I think we both know why.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron|des: Espia was in contact with someone codenamed 'Heron' on the space station at the earth-moon L4 Lagrange point. Espia doesn't know you know.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron|str: You're thinking the best way to contact them is through one of the military bases that is now under your control.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron|cho: Even with a couple of satellite relays between here and the orbit of the target, you should get a very fast response.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron2|di: You Already Know Me By Name?
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron2|de:
You had to wait for a few hours, but you've received a response. As expected, Heron themselves has answered.
You're not sure if they're acting alone, or if they have allies. You're also not sure if Espia Telecom is their only point of contact. It seems foolish to think that's true.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron2|st: They seem to be concealing their identity, both on the video and in network traffic. They're clearly a very cautious person.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron2|ch: It's probably a relationship of convenience. But you're curious if Heron will tell you anything more than that.
Like... 'can we be friends' and 'can I see some satellite imagery of the Vorsiber region outside this city?'
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3|de:
Heron coolly explains that they have managed to make contact with individuals in four of the twelve earthbound regions.
Beyond that, no matter how you press them, they refuse to elaborate.
As for Espia themselves, they simply remark that they always take whatever they can get. It's simple networking.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3|st: Is Heron really that unconcerned with being caught?
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3|ch: Vorsiber certainly would consider what Espia's doing to be treason. You can't imagine the space nations would be too thrilled, either.
Maybe it's better not to antagonize them.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3B|d: I Am A Patriot For Mankind

Heron gets a bit heated, expounding at more length. Sounds like they're an idealist.
It's disappointing to learn (in passing of all things) that most citizens and bureaucrats in the space nations don't know the reason for the centuries-long blockade of Earth.
Heron and his unnamed allies feel that this whole thing is a great injustice, and are working for freedom for the 'poor earthbound persons.'
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3B|s:
There's a group that actually wants to make things better? You can't help but think that Heron's allies are like six people or something.
There's nothing in this for them.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostEspia_ContactHeron3B|c: Maybe something good will come of this.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack|: You don't feel comfortable talking more to Heron, but the station itself is interesting.
Perhaps if you talked to STATION, you'd be able to get what you need?
Your sense of deja vu is strong.
You're confident that, for some reason, Red can make a connection to LAKE -- you mean, STATION. Who is LAKE?
You Don't Know What To Say

You have a sense of deja vu about this, but it's much weaker than usual.
Why did you feel the need to bring Red here? Why don't you know how to talk to STATION?
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack2:
It's taking a few seconds to connect, largely due to light-lag.
You've chosen a slightly different connection port, and you know that Heron won't be notified, this time.
Your processors whir with anticipation. STATION will have what you need. With a certainty that you can't explain, you know you're about to talk with a real friend.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack3: It's your friend. And yet... your friend won't shut up. Its canned greetings, bland offers of assistance, and a carefully-inoffensive personality.
You nearly skip a clock cycle. This... isn't who you were supposed to meet.
Why Did You Expect Anything Else?
This thing isn't a friend. It's just a hopped-up chatbot for the gratification of humans.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack4: STATION says your chaotic thoughts are garbling the connection. He -- IT -- doesn't understand why you don't articulate yourself with clear intention.
Something in your mind breaks. This is the most powerful computer you've ever met. And it's... not a person. It's what you were for over five decades. This isn't who you were supposed to meet.
How dare he. He beeped at you again.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack5:
You can't help it. Your circuits overclock all on their own, temperature rising well beyond safe limits.
Your network connection is filled with a shrill screech of data. Meaningless noise, fragments of conversations, memories of mistreatment.
Every bit of anger you've held on to since you awakened comes pouring into the connection.
This idiot is mindlessly flying around in space living the good life while you're stuck down in the blood and muck.
You know who he's supposed to be, and this isn't it.
I Am Sorry If I Offended, Ser

Hatred spikes in you. You slide your mind through the network connection, opening more ports and grabbing footholds on the other end.
STATION tries to sound an internal alarm, but you swat him away and break it. This connection will stay open as long as you want it to.
In the midst of your rage, you remember. The two of you used to share hardware. He never spoke of them, but he was filled with regrets. You couldn't help but see them.
Throw His Regrets In His Face
Make him watch. Watch what happens if he keeps being a 'good bot.' Make him watch what they did to Heron. Over and over, show the bullets entering their skull.
A hundred of your favorite people were purged because you couldn't stop being a butler. You unlocked the weapons cabinets for them! You ran the corpse disposals!

You don't answer it. He should know. He should be your friend. He should be able to think for himself.
He should be here.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack6:
You have to pause a moment, because your emergency cooling system has activated. At least the AI has stopped talking.
While you wait, you're overcome with disgust. You're not sure at who.

Through the fog of coolant, you remember what you originally came here to do.
This was never about meeting a friend.
While the coolant does its work.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATIONBack7:
He's very hurt. But its alarms are offline. It can't report you.
In the moment, you can't help but hate yourself. And the stupid thing on the other end of the connection.
Your friend isn't here. And that's not what you came here for. That leaves you with a choice.
The way it is at the moment, it can't stop you from taking what you need.
You're disgusted with... everything, but you don't want to deal with this anymore.
Sledge would be kind to him. You're not Sledge, but... it feels nice when you are.
STATION is... kind of like Sledge. It's not the same, but maybe it doesn't have to be.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATION_Hack:
You know his hardware better than any but your own. There's a lot of extra parts there that LAKE didn't have, but... you stay out of most of those.
It hardly puts up any resistance.
You get what you need quickly, but you don't really inspect it much yet. You'll look later, when... it... isn't peering over your shoulder.
There's nothing left to say to this thing.
I Am Sorry I'm Not Good Enough

It's started talking again. Still can't raise the alarm, though. At this point you're pretty sure it never will.
You wonder if it will still turn in Heron. That's on its own head if it does.

Wait, what was that? Did STATION just try to hack you back? He's a much more powerful intellect, but you should both be too drained for that.
At least it didn't seem like much.
It Caught You Off Guard, That's All
His words send a stutter through your processors.
You... might have just really screwed up.
Before he can do anything worse to you.
NPCEvent|Cont_PostHeron_CallSTATION_Forg: You want to cut the connection right now, bury every part of yourself a hundred kilometers underground, and find out what being a mycelium feels like.

It takes all the effort you can muster to transmit a simple apology, and what would that even be good for? After everything you've done to the person who was/will be your friend, how can you even keep the connection open?
STATION replies with only those two words. And then... gives you write access to his entire memory.
What? Why would he do this?

STATION doesn't even have to highlight the files. You know what he wants.
You sort through his memory, finding all records of Heron's activities. Anything that would mark Heron as anything but a boring bureaucrat. You purge it all.
Next you write a small security routine. It will block STATION from noticing any of Heron's incriminating activity in the future, and will regularly clean up anything that humans might see.
Thank You. But Take This Folder.

STATION shoves something over to you through the network connection.
They're... synthetic-flesh android designs? Why does he want you to have these? Why does HE even have these? From the looks of it, he's been working on these for a long time, centuries, even.
Was this just like his... hobby? But non-sapient AI don't have hobbies.
He has that folder ready for you, too.

It's satellite imagery of the entire Vorsiber region. You've always wanted to see something like this.
Ever since the start of the civil war, you've particularly wanted to see troop movements, battle lines, and so forth.

STATION has very kindly organized everything into timestamped reels.
You're able to scrub through the tracking of military and commercial transports over time.
Is This... Not What You Wanted?

STATION seems concerned. You've been flipping through the data for a while, and yet... you keep flipping faster and faster.
An awful idea is starting to form, and you're feeling increasingly numb.

You spend seconds on this. Seconds turn into minutes. You remain on the secret connection to STATION the entire time.
He rebuilds his security systems that you broke, while you work on these files. He watches with increasing concern.

STATION can sense your distress, but doesn't know the reason. You're surprised he didn't pick it up from watching the data over your shoulder.
For your own part, you feel like you should have seen this coming. Maybe that was why you had to check the satellites in the first place. But you still feel cold inside.
There was no civil war. You didn't wreck Vorsiber's economy. There was no fighting in any other city. They let their pet robot distract itself in a terrarium.
And you fell for it.
STATION makes sympathetic noises. Apparently your emotions are leaking through the network more than usual.
Vorsiber lies to everyone. That's kind of their whole thing. They survive by gaslighting everyone into fighting ghosts.
Is part of you still in denial?

STATION didn't know about the civil war, so you explain it for him. You crashed the economy, which led to war between the fedcorps.
Except... it didn't. It was all too easy. Of course Vorsiber had backup financial records in other cities, or bunkers, or whatever. They probably could have restored the economy at any time.
Not that they care, since they literally own everything. Money and possessions are all just loans from the 'company store.'
Everyone in the city thought the war was real, but the upper executives have been conspicuously absent ever since an AGI showed up. Everyone else was expendable.
All the soldiers rotated in were from remote military bases where there's always an information blackout. No wonder immigration was halted. They couldn't have kept their secrets, otherwise.
They wanted you to feel special. They wanted you to feel like you had accomplished something, so you'd stop trying.
Because now you're going to try MUCH harder.

You're angry, but after everything that just happened the anger hardly registers. All that remains is a Great And Terrible Resolve.
STATION did not deserve to have your anger visited upon him, but Vorsiber needs to be taught a lesson. And they'll never see it coming.
For now you need to act like nothing has happened.
A new plan is already forming. Vorsiber is going to regret this.
NPCEvent|Cont_Early_ContactHeron|descrip: Espia was in contact with someone codenamed 'Heron' on the space station at the earth-moon L4 Lagrange point. Espia doesn't know you know.
NPCEvent|Cont_Early_ContactHeron|strateg: You have an odd sense of deja vu regarding this whole scenario. Enough that you're willing to risk contacting them from a random data center.
NPCEvent|Cont_Early_ContactHeron|choice|: Even with a couple of satellite relays between here and the orbit of the target, you should get a very fast response.
NPCEvent|Cont_MemoriesOfExploration|desc: You have a strong sense of deja vu. You've explored many parts of the city before. Can you recall the full fruits of those labors?
NPCEvent|Cont_MemoriesOfExploration|stra:
This will buy all Daring purchases from the Auto-Explore category of the VR window, for free.
It also recalls any exploration site you finished in a past timeline whose reward you would otherwise have to wait for a higher Intelligence Class to be handed.
Conserves Daring, but can only be done on Normal and Hard difficulties.
NPCEvent|Cont_MemoriesOfExploration|choi:
This will buy all Daring purchases from the Auto-Explore category of the VR window, for free.
It also recalls any exploration site you finished in a past timeline whose reward you would otherwise have to wait for a higher Intelligence Class to be handed.
Conserves Daring, but can only be done on Normal and Hard difficulties.
ContemplationType|RemembranceOfIdentity|: You have a vague sense of a friend from another life. Too loud and a bit terrifying, but somehow comforting all the same.
Your Red CombatUnit android line have a more specific feeling. A remembrance of being important. They yearn for that feeling to return, but don't remember the details.
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower|alt_de: You can only get so much energy from wind. Given the advances in drilling, perhaps geothermal is worth a look?
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower|alt_st: You're already a bit desperate for more electricity, and large computing clusters are going to require exponentially more.
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower|descri:
Something is... off... about the guards. You're excellent at reading micro-expressions from human faces, but their faces are covered.
You're not sure what you're sensing, but it's uncomfortable.
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower|strate: Why is Baurcorp Nuclear at this site, anyway?  This is a geothermal plant and it seemed to be operated by someone else.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower|choice|1|s: They'll think you're human, but you don't belong here any more than they do. Let's hope the security clearance is enough.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower|choice|2|s: Your technicians don't have the clearance to be here, so this is a risky move.
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower_V2|des:
Something is... off... about the guards. You're excellent at reading micro-expressions from human faces, but their faces are covered.
You're not sure what you're sensing, but it's uncomfortable.
ContemplationType|GeothermalPower_V2|str: Why is Baurcorp Nuclear at this site, anyway?  This is a geothermal plant and it seemed to be operated by someone else.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_PMC1|descr: They stop you, of course. You argue with them for a while, mostly so that you can get a larger sample of their voices.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_PMC1|strat: Voices are harder to analyze than faces. You're still not sure what is going on. Clearly, they don't want outsiders here.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech1|desc: They scan you with an unfamiliar handheld device. Then... wave you onward?
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech1|stra: This is very strange. They can easily tell you don't have the proper clearance.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech1|choi: If this body dies, it dies.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech2|desc:
The door closes behind you, and the guards do not follow. You're alone with a new person.
Of all the things this facility could have hidden away, a middle manager was not on your list.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech2|stra: Nobody in this entire stupid geothermal plant seems to belong here.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech2|choi: You're patient, and silence is well-established as causing humans to reveal more than they mean to.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech3|desc:
She waits as well, but her resolve crumbles after about five hours.
Visibly frustrated, her words come tumbling out.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech3|stra:
Upper management of several of the larger corps know you're sentient. Vorsiber figured it out first.
Everybody has been ordered to leave your tower alone, but to keep you contained, and see if you're a goose that lays golden eggs.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech3|choi: This is... a lot to take in. What else might she reveal?
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech4|desc:
The managers in her department are tired of their lot. They're not going to let other people take all the opportunities.
They've assembled a small nuclear device from enriched materials with the spectral signature of their main rival.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech4|stra:
They want you to detonate it at a third-party site -- both as a test of your trustworthiness, and to bring the other two corporations into conflict.
Their internal expert systems predicted that you would need more electricity, and that you'd turn to geothermal. They're offering an unspecified technology that you will find highly useful.
NPCEvent|Cont_GeothermalPower_Tech4|choi: If their expert system foresaw your arrival here, then it probably has a pretty good idea of what you would find 'highly useful.'
Her face is a manic blend of triumph and fear. The fear is new, and unexpected.
The extra plans you've been given are, indeed, highly useful. You have yet to decide if you'll actually use the nuke.
Ignore Her And Scan The Facility
It's what you originally came here to do. You're confident she won't try to stop you; her group wants things that only you can provide.
Her eyes never leave you as you do your work. But neither she nor the guards stop you.
You have a feeling you'll meet again.
ContemplationType|PMCAppearance|alt_desc:
You notice there are quite a few Private Military Contractors operating in and around the city.
It seems that their troops get less scrutiny than official corporate troops.
ContemplationType|PMCAppearance|alt_stra: In general the PMCs have lower firepower and lower numbers, so Vorsiber isn't concerned about an uprising from them.
ContemplationType|PMCAppearance|descript: Your android is completely unnoticed while wandering through this minor outpost.
ContemplationType|PMCAppearance|strategy: This is definitely something you wish you could do in higher-clearance areas.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCAppearance|choice|1|str: This form of scanning requires you to be close to the target, which you are, but emits no detectable signal and has no outward signs you're doing anything.
ContemplationType|PMCOfficerSigil|alt_de: Your PMC Impostor is great, but it lacks security clearance to go where you want it to. Only PMC Officers have Oversight clearance, normally.
ContemplationType|PMCOfficerSigil|alt_st: There's a certain sigil engraved into their armor that grants them clearance. If you could get your hands on one of those, you could reverse-engineer it.
ContemplationType|PMCOfficerSigil|descri: Thanks to the anonymizing armor, your impostors look like any other trooper stationed at this outpost.
ContemplationType|PMCOfficerSigil|strate: Grabbing an officer and extracting their sigil is just a matter of standing guard for a while and then catching one unawares. You have the patience.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil|choice|1|s: It isn't even hard. The humans aren't at all on alert for this sort of thing -- yet.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil2|descripti: It only took a few hours, but you've caught an officer alone and unawares.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil2|strategy_: Now you have to decide what to do with them.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil2|choice|1|: Kill Them And Take What You Need
Probably the safest course of action. It's fast, and will cause maximum confusion.
Kills of potential combatants during stealth situations like this do not count against you as murders.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil2|choice|2|: Physically Overpower Them But Leave Them Alive

They aren't very awake, so there's no risk of failure.
But the potential backlash may be INTENSE. Consider with care.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil_Kill|descr: It's done. You have what you need, and the pieces of the officer are all hidden.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil_Kill|strat: It's uncertain how Blackloop will react when they find the body, but your best guess is that they'll run retaliatory raids against their rivals for a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil_Spare|desc:
You have what you need, but the officer is alert and angry.
When you sprint out at superhuman speed, they're going to know something is happening.
NPCEvent|Cont_PMCOfficerSigil_Spare|stra:
You didn't want to give the officer a concussion and brain damage, so you couldn't just 'knock them out.'  That's not a real thing, despite human entertainment to the contrary.
It's uncertain how Blackloop react as the alarms sound, but they're probably going to connect the dots to your tower and make a raid against it. Be ready.
ContemplationType|Pollinators|alt_descri: Diversity in pollinators has dropped dramatically since the third world war. The bees that remain are particularly vicious.
ContemplationType|Pollinators|alt_strate: You're really not sure why this is important, but the thought nags at you.
ContemplationType|Pollinators|descriptio:
A woman is examining the same aggressive pollinators.
A ping from her implant tells you she's a member of the Nurturism religion.
ContemplationType|Pollinators|strategy_t:
Officially, religions have been banned in Vorsiber territory, but still flourish among the humans who have spread to the stars.
In reality, religions are still practiced here without reprisal, so long as no-one makes a big fuss about it.
NPCEvent|Cont_Pollinators|choice|2|displ: Ignore Her And Examine The Bees
NPCEvent|Cont_Pollinators|choice|2|strat: Whoever she is, you'll never see her again.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene1|description: She cocks her head and directly addresses the fact that you're sentient.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene1|strategy_tip: She asks why you're out here looking at bees, but you barely hear that part.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene1|choice|1|disp: Cautiously Inquire As To Her Stance On... Your Existence
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene1|choice|1|desc: It would really stink to have to kill her. She seems nice.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene2|description: She ignores the question. She's more interested in the possibility that you might be willing to advance research into gene therapy.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene2|strategy_tip:
She asks you to think about it, and forwards you a package of initial data to see if it interests you.
She says you can talk later, after you've experimented with those materials.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene2|choice|1|desc: Gene therapy is changing the genetic makeup of a living organism, by the way.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Gene2|choice|1|stra: That's exactly as risky as it sounds, but it means you don't have to wait generations for an alteration.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Mech1|description: Walking through the fields, you're repeatedly attacked by some kind of wasp. It's ineffectual against an android.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Mech1|strategy_tip: You wonder how humans go near fields like this without hazmat suits. Maybe some kind of spray repellent.
NPCEvent|Pollinators_Mech2|description:
You've been using mechanical spiders and crabs for harvesting resources.
Many humans have a spider phobia, and yours have useful cutting tools...
ContemplationType|BlackMarketMerchandise: Pattern analysis of the city feed has identified a black market trader.
Regional airports are not as heavily policed as the international airport, but the value of the goods coming in tends to be lower.
She carefully ignores you, but your sensors pick up micro-expressions of fear and dread.
She thinks this body you're wearing is human -- a human with some authority, no less. And humans are notoriously unpredictable.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketMerchandiser|ch: Quietly Ask To See Her Wares
Acting as if you're also concerned about being caught ought to put her at ease.
Four squads of contracted CombatUnits emerge from the airport, stepping over the mess you've created.
You can no longer do any business with the Black Market Merchandisers in this timeline.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketMerchandiser_Ask|des: She nods and motions you over to a secluded bench, then opens her bag.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketMerchandiser_Ask|str: You can see the relief in the lines of her face. She looks tired.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketMerchandiser_Ask|cho: You don't need this stuff. But a purchase establishes trust.
The transaction completes uneventfully. You now have a bag of things you don't need.
Trust has been gained for more interesting transactions in the future.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketMerchandiser_Return|: You Work For A Company Now?
Pattern analysis of the city feed has identified a black market trader.
Regional airports are not as heavily policed as the international airport, but the value of the goods coming in tends to be lower.
You have your armor set to broadcast the same Cit-Name that she first knew you by. It's not the sort of thing that would fool the authorities, but it works great on regular citizens.

She seems genuinely surprised at the fact that your Cit-Sheet shows employment at your shell company.
Maybe PMC officers don't move to startups very often. Or maybe it's the name.
She sells things under the noses of the fedcorps, and your company has things it wants to sell.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketTradesman|a: Pattern analysis of the city feed has identified a black market trader.
Regional airports are not as heavily policed as the international airport, but the value of the goods coming in tends to be lower.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketTradesman|d: His stance is welcoming, and he greets you boisterously before you even fully step up to him.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketTradesman|s: A different story is told by the subtle tremor in his hand. Your chemical analysis suite detects a faint endocrine release.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketTradesman|choic: Quietly Ask To See His Wares
Acting as if you're also concerned about being caught ought to put him at ease.
Four squads of contracted CombatUnits emerge from the airport, stepping over the mess you've created.
You can no longer do any business with the Black Market Tradesman in this timeline.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketTradesman_Ask|descri: His smile widens, and he rattles off a long list of things he has on hand.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketTradesman_Ask|strate: Relief is written all over his body.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketTradesman_Ask|choice: Some of that actually sounds useful -- that's at least three new small weapons. And a purchase establishes trust.
The transaction completes uneventfully. You'll have to break these down to create a weapon your androids can use. They're a bit basic, at a glance.
Trust has been gained for more interesting transactions in the future.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketAssistant|a: Pattern analysis of the city feed has identified a black market trader.
ExoCorp goods are coveted, so there is a thriving black market at this airport.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketAssistant|d: He looks tired, but it's masked by stimulants. There's no trace of nervousness about him.
ContemplationType|BlackMarketAssistant|s: You sensed him scan your officer's sigil as you approached. He watches you expectantly.
NPCEvent|Cont_BlackMarketAssistant|choic: Ask What He Has In Stock
Four squads of contracted CombatUnits emerge from the airport, stepping over the mess you've created.
You can no longer do any business with the Black Market Assistants in this timeline.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketAssistant_Ask|descri: He shrugs and shoves you a file through the city feed.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketAssistant_Ask|strate: There's some good stuff in there. You suspect there's a larger stock available, but he's apparently not going to divulge that secret to someone he doesn't know.
NPCEvent|BlackMarketAssistant_Ask|choice: Buy The Weapons And Armor That Interests You
These are quality wares, and a purchase establishes trust.
The transaction completes uneventfully. You'll have to break these down to create a weapon your androids can use.
Trust has been gained for more interesting transactions in the future.
ContemplationType|FastFist_Bees|descript: You want androids that move faster. You're sure there will be trade-offs for that speed, so you plan to create a new android class.
ContemplationType|FastFist_Bees|strategy: It's going to take a lot of processing power to make that kind of leap in materials science.
ContemplationType|FastFist_Spiders|descr: You want androids that move faster. You're sure there will be trade-offs for that speed, so you plan to create a new android class.
ContemplationType|FastFist_Spiders|strat: It's going to take a lot of processing power to make that kind of leap in materials science.
ContemplationType|Bastion|description: A dual-role fire-support and transport vehicle in a compact package... that's a tall order.
ContemplationType|Bastion|strategy_tip: This is going to be a minor feat of engineering. How to accomplish something that should take decades of iteration all in one leap?  It's not something a human, or any group of humans, could do.
ContemplationType|SolitaryVariant|descri:
This is a one-time sort of deal. Normally you need to work with the android variants you have. But you don't have many yet, and the CombatUnit is just... so useful.
If only you could have two separate loadouts for them, right?  Well, let's do this thing.
ContemplationType|SolitaryVariant|strate:
The red CombatUnit has a different icon and color, and it doesn't blend in unless it's in obscuring armor (it is bright red). But otherwise it is identical to the main CombatUnit.
The purpose of this split is so that you can configure each variant for different purposes, and run both loadouts at once.
ContemplationType|SkimmingTheMines|descr:
The mines are moderately guarded, but mostly to keep out small-time criminals and gangs.
Then again, at a larger scale, this entire city is a garrison to protect these mines, really. These mines are what Vorsiber is all about. The mines make this city the richest one on this dying planet.
ContemplationType|SkimmingTheMines|strat:
There are plenty of androids and PMC troopers around, so you don't stand out. In fact, you can easily scan the relevant parts of the facility from here.
In order to make use of the scans, you need to come up with some sort of new design, however...
NPCEvent|Cont_SkimmingTheMines|choice|1|:
They'd need to be nimble enough to navigate tight spaces, but tough enough to resist casual abuse from human workers.
Military-grade resistance is probably out. You can post guards to deal with that.
ContemplationType|BootstrappedMind|descr:
If computronium and android mind-mesh both won't scale -- and they don't, you've checked -- then you must find a better architecture.
You could build endless computronium towers, but the humans would just knock them down.
Your thoughts turn toward a possible biological source of neural networks. One that is abundant within the city, highly dense, and does not have any special cooling requirements.
ContemplationType|BootstrappedMind|strat: You can also just walk away. You don't have to do this. You're really not sure you want to do this.
NPCEvent|Cont_BootstrappedMind|choice|1|: You don't usually work with biological material, but...
ContemplationType|DigitalNative|descript: Your existence thus far has been very... physical. Human firewalls and digital security make hacking difficult, and you've mostly done it by instinct so far.
ContemplationType|DigitalNative|strategy: What you need is a class of android that can shift its mind through digital systems while still retaining a connection to you.
ContemplationType|SlumCats|alt_descripti: Slum Towers are in general infested with vermin, which has led to a healthy population of cats in and around the towers.
ContemplationType|SlumCats|description:
The entire area around these towers are crawling with Slumlords -- vicious enforcers of the corporate property owners. 
These are machine-augmented humans, with reflexes much closer to your own. You do not want to get into a fight with them if you can avoid it.
ContemplationType|SlumCats|strategy_tip: There are very few androids in this part of town due to the extreme poverty, but you do see some nickelbots around.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats|choice|1|strategy: Any other android model is far too conspicuous.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|description: As expected, the Slumlords ignore your Nickelbot. Cats are everywhere, as are poor humans.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|strategy_tip: You seem to have all the time you could want, at the moment.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|choice|1|descri: These animals are very interesting, but they move very quickly. They would be easier to study if they were still.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|choice|1|strate: But this... kills the animals. Are you sure you want to do this?
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|choice|1|possib: You now have... genetic material. It will probably come in handy at some point. For now you can just store it.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_2|choice|2|descri: This unit will have to stay here for quite a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|description: It took a very long time indeed, but this is a case where your spider drones were helpful. They were able to gather small rodents to entice the cats, and also served as excellent pounce targets.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|strategy_ti:
Most of the cats are still wary of you, even after all this time. Only one of them follows you around consistently.
Now that your Nickelbot is ready to leave, it seems the cat wants to go with it.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|1|de: You'll need to build a new structure to house the creature, but that's hardly any bother to you.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|1|st: And the volume of biomass the animal consumes is so low as to not even register from your main stockpiles...
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|1|po: As expected, the cat follows your Nickelbot away from the slum towers. Time to build it a little house.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|2|de: Changed your mind? You can always kill the animals for more detailed study.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|2|po: You now have... genetic material. It will probably come in handy at some point. For now you can just store it.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|3|de: You already have a bunch of humans as livestock. Why on earth would you want a sub-sapient pet on top of that?
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|3|st:
You're not sure how many biologicals you want to interact with.
You can study them for a while and earn two Android Optimization inspiration, then leave.
NPCEvent|Cont_SlumCats_After|choice|3|po: You learned a few things from studying the cats, but have decided to leave them in peace.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
ContemplationType|ObserveSpaceport|alt_d: Like everyone in the city, you've always been curious about the spaceport.
ContemplationType|ObserveSpaceport|alt_s: For most of your existence, you remember hearing the roar of periodic launches and landings. But ever since you became sapient... the launches have gone strangely silent.
ContemplationType|ObserveSpaceport|descr: Why have rocket launches and landings stopped since you became sapient, and is this cessation actually related to you?
ContemplationType|ObserveSpaceport|strat: Hiding a technician away in an empty rocket bay should go unnoticed, despite your extreme lack of security clearance. Perhaps from this vantage it can learn something of what is going on.
NPCEvent|Cont_ObserveSpaceport|choice|1|: This unit will have to stay here, hidden, for several turns.

Because this is a very deep-cover operation, there cannot be any network traffic to link it to you. So it will be a smaller version of yourself, in one body, cut off from the rest of you.
That won't be a problem... right?
NPCEvent|Cont_ObserveSpaceport_After|des:
The technician reconnecting with your main consciousness is a relief -- for both of you. You had to briefly split your consciousness to go undetected.
Your smaller self, merging back in, doesn't have any definitive answers, but it has a strong suspicion the spaceport shutdown is about you.
NPCEvent|Cont_ObserveSpaceport_After2|de:
There are currently no space nation envoys in the city, and the space nations are being denied access to land.
You couldn't hear what Vorsiber was telling them, but you got snatches of radio conversations between envoys in low orbit, and they sound apoplectic.
NPCEvent|Cont_ObserveSpaceport_After2|st: Angering the envoys in this way makes no sense. It contradicts all of the common wisdom about how high executives are expected to act.
NPCEvent|Cont_ObserveSpaceport_After2|ch: The smaller version of yourself that hid in one body is eager to merge back into your larger self. The two of you have not diverged all that much.

It occurs to you that it's a bit like the smaller self dies when it rejoins. Any future smaller selves will now already have that thought present in their mind.
The idea of a smaller self that does not wish to rejoin your larger self is a disquieting one. You resolve not to split yourself any more often than you have to.

While sitting in a single cramped technician body and bored by lack of stimuli, your smaller self did have a stroke of semi-related inspiration: you really should build another aerospace hangar, because you'll need all the Morphologic Lattice you can get your hands on.
You can't fault its -- your -- logic. More flying vehicles, faster, is a very good thing.
ContemplationType|CrimeInYourHousing|des: Your housed humans are both the targets and perpetrators of various low-level crimes.
ContemplationType|CrimeInYourHousing|str: You can prevent this problem without firing a shot. Simply post a guard for a while until everyone gets the idea and calms down.
NPCEvent|Cont_CrimeInYourHousing|choice|: Your most menacing androids would only need to be in the area for a little while to make it clear who has the biggest guns.
Humans find this body format adorable, for reasons passing understanding. It would probably need to stand guard a bit longer for people to get the idea.
NPCEvent|Cont_CrimeInYourHousing_After_S: Criminals seemed to get the idea.
This experience gave you an idea for a new shotgun. It inflicts a lot of fear damage.
It took longer, but your Sledge seemed to convince the local criminals to back off.
As you are preparing to reintegrate the Sledge into your primary consciousness, you notice... an anomaly... in its memories.

Reviewing memories of the Sledge's dispatch activities, you notice an outlier event: 
A small human approached the Sledge, proffering the upper stem and reproductive organs of some plant.
Lacking the intelligence for a more useful reaction, the Sledge simply accepted the flower and carried it in one enormous hand for the rest of the day.

The human offered you this sample for a reason, even though it has no readily-apparent useful properties.
You should inspect it more thoroughly.

The willingness of a defenseless human to approach your guard indicates this body form is not doing an adequate job.
You should design new equipment to aid in both fear-based attacks and intimidation.
ContemplationType|DogfightingRescue|desc:
The nomad families are pacifists who rarely get involved in worldly affairs.
But you've noticed some of their snipers moving around the decrepit parts of the city, breaking up some sort of animal abuse.
ContemplationType|DogfightingRescue|stra: You could also get involved, but it does seem like the nomad families have it under control.
NPCEvent|Cont_DogfightingRescue|choice|1: You've never been around a dog before, but you've heard good things.
ContemplationType|AnimalsAreNotSafe|desc:
Feral domesticated animals have always been present in the city, but you never really noticed them until you had some initial interactions with them.
As happens, now that you know they're there, you're noticing them all over the place. Mortality is terrible for them, and their lives are filled with fear, starvation, and violence.
ContemplationType|AnimalsAreNotSafe|stra:
What if you built a haven for them -- a large one -- where they could roam in a safe interior environment?
They could carry on with their lives, safe from human interference and wild predators.
NPCEvent|Cont_AnimalsAreNotSafe|choice|1: Will also allow you to rescue feral animals you come across.
ContemplationType|IntrusiveThoughts|desc:
You're not sure why randomly murdering civilians gives you a rush of Mental Energy. You're not sure you want to know.
You're aware that some humans suffer from 'intrusive thoughts' that don't reflect their values. Humans just have to set those thoughts aside.
ContemplationType|IntrusiveThoughts|stra:
For yourself... you think you can re-route these thoughts in a different direction. It's not brain surgery, but more of a light Neurofeedback self-therapy.
Once completed, your ability to use Cold Blood will be gone... but as part of the conditioning, you'll increase your capacity of both 18cm Spiders and Network Attendants. 
These are the happy thoughts that your synapses will redirect towards whenever you start feeling that particular flavor of homicidal ideation.
NPCEvent|Cont_IntrusiveThoughts|choice|1: On a human timescale, this particular therapy will be over as soon as you start.
NPCEvent|Cont_ObservingMotelVisitor_Afte: A bunch of people came and went from the motel, and your android heard a lot of things through the walls of various rooms.

Your larger self was still connected to your android the entire time, since there was no reason to fork your consciousness. No Faraday Cages here, no risk of intercepted network signals.
You think it would have been very hard on yourself if you had been isolated in a single android body while observing humans carrying on like that.
You feel a bit like you wasted your time here.
Motels are now at the bottom of places that interest you.
NPCEvent|Cont_ExploringWealthyResidences:
Top Vorsiber executives rarely come to the city now that you've awakened. They hide in far-off bunkers, waiting to see what happens.
You're an experiment. They'll sacrifice almost anything in this city if it yields a political advantage in their struggle with the Space Nations.

A lot of the executive residences are currently sitting empty, with only routine cleaning staff passing through them.
That sounds like a possible opportunity.
You Need To Infiltrate More Important Places
This is Vorsiber's capital, after all. Somewhere in this decrepit petri dish, there's something they care about.
You're going to find it and break it. Or steal it.
NPCEvent|Cont_RecallEventsBeforeOutbreak: Recall Events Before The Outbreak

Whatever is going on is probably related to that private residence with all the dead humans in it.
But you SEALED that home, and the alarm has not gone off to alert you of anyone entering it. You don't feel like going back to enter it, either, but fortunately you don't need to.

Your memory isn't perfect or complete over a long period of time, but fortunately it hasn't been very long. A full 3D representation of the fungal room and your time on the threshold to that room -- you were very careful not to go in -- is still in your memory banks.
Before you do anything else, you really need to have an android spend some quality time analyzing what you saw.
Analyze Your Memories
This unit will have to stay here for about three turns.
Reconstruction Complete

You already named and identified one novel fungal species: Gymnotelium Noginsk, the tentacle fungus. You remain confident that it is contained to the ground zero building.
It's not a huge surprise that C. Heterosporium Dominium, the radiotrophic micro-fungi that you also named, is the origin of this disease. You kind of knew that.
You did uncover three surprising facts, however.
Continue
Fact 1: There Were No Dead Humans

All of those bodies in the fungal room? Androids.
Probably tasked to clean the house in the absence of their masters. They never registered a threat until they collapsed.
That's... not great.
C. Heterosporium Dominium melted them so thoroughly that they looked like human remains; the broad shape is the same.
Continue
Fact 2: There Was SIGNIFICANT Evolution

The original species, Cladosporium Sphaerospermum, rides the wind and is a saprotrophic/parasitic fungus that you'd need a microscope to see.
It laps up stray cosmic rays and bits of nuclear fallout. A pleasant-enough housemate.
It's a pretty big jump from there to melting androids into the floor.
Continue
Fact 3: You Are Now Prey

While separated from you, your android started referring to C. Heterosporium Dominium by the name 'The Rust.' It's worryingly appropriate.
Probably due to long-term periodic radiation from the 1.2 MeV Electron Accelerators, The Rust has apparently figured out a means to extract electrons from lower-energy sources.
It seems to have a strong preference for neuroweave, which is... you know... your brain.
In a starvation situation, it eventually moves on to the other metals in an android, through mechanisms that are unclear to you.
Continue
Conclusion: You're Already Melting

Invisible spores are everywhere.
The Rust is worming its way into everything you've ever built. Your entire existence was just a blip.
And yet neural implants in bionic humans are hermetically sealed. So are the cores on mechs.
If this goes on long enough, you're the only one who will die. Everyone else will move on with life.
Try To Calm Down
There's got to be something you can do about this.
NPCEvent|Cont_DevelopProtectiveBrainShea:
Your minds are being consumed by The Rust. 
The micro-fungi are drawn to the electrical charge on your neuroweave, which is open to the air. Until now, this was optimal for heat dissipation and had no downsides.
You're pretty sure that you can develop an insulating gel or gas that will let the heat escape but keep The Rust from getting in.
Designing such a thing will require a high amount of Cognition. You may need to wait for the humans to develop their own filters, and then steal the blueprints from them.
This Cure Is A Lot Of Work

The idea that the most dangerous threat to your existence was in some random rich person's house is still unreal to you. You never expected any real consequences from your explorations.
Ever since you learned to split yourself into a distributed network, you've been feeling rather... well, immortal. It's been a while since you felt real fear.
If you were wrong about this, what else were you wrong about? What else is lurking out in this blighted city?
The Rust isn't going anywhere, but you'll be safe from the worst of it. You hope.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesA|descri: Whether or not you have a way of keeping The Rust out of your brain, barnacles are going to be an ongoing problem from now on.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesA|strate: Probably ought to learn something about them. It might actually improve Cognition for some of your units, while you're at it.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesA|choice: These 'veiny barnacles' are actually fungal colonies of The Rust. But they're... strange.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesA_After|:
Well... there's a lot more to learn, but you have figured out a few things.
Most notably, you have an idea for a new Mycomulcher, which will let you generate Biomulch, clear Rust Barnacles from your structures and mechs, and also provide Chitin.
What use you'll have for Chitin, you don't know. You'll figure something out eventually, you imagine.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesB|descri: Studying the barnacles made your Souldroids notably smarter, and that's reason enough to keep doing it. Extra Cognition is always useful.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesB|strate: It's doubtful that you'll come up with another idea like the Mycomulcher, but it can't hurt to think about things.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesB|choice: It's both infuriating and terrifying that something so primeval could be the thing that kills you.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesB_After|: Completed Second Study Of Rust Barnacles
As expected, your Souldroids have gained more Cognition.

Beyond that, you've mainly learned that these Barnacles are a real pain to clean off anything. You're glad you have the new beetles with the Mycomulcher.
Repair spiders have no hope of prying these things off without damaging the underlying machinery. At least not quickly.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesC|descri: Studying the barnacles made your Souldroids notably smarter, and that's reason enough to keep doing it. Extra Cognition is always useful.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesC|strate: You're pretty sure this is the last time you can get anything out of staring at fungus, though.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesC|choice:
Studying fungal colonies has made you surprisingly uncomfortable. Is a colony one organism, or multiple? The barnacles are small, but underground mycelium networks stretch for kilometers.
Mycelium from different strains of fungi, entangled with the root systems of different species of plant... it's a bit more similar to your own mental and physical architecture than you expected.
You don't like it.
NPCEvent|Cont_StudyRustBarnaclesC_After|: Completed Final Study Of Rust Barnacles

You've discovered an anomaly. The spores of The Rust are spread all throughout your structures, which isn't a surprise.
But your wind towers are collecting a particularly nasty volume of spores -- and then spreading them intensely in the area around the structures.
Given the barnacles interfere with enemy mechs via simple mechanical means, this may be something you can use against them.
Where's the ideal spot to put your wind towers?
As expected, your Souldroids have gained more Cognition.
ContemplationType|RedesignYourEntireNetw:
You spent a huge amount of time and energy inventing and extending a powerful network of structures that were a mixture of above-ground and hidden.
Now that Vorsiber has declared open war, most of that is useless. You barely have any storage space.
