That said, there are trapped people still active all through the city, picking through the wreckage. There are still humanoid robots among them.
You'll have to be much more subtle than before, but you can carve out a life here.
NPCEvent|Cont_RedesignYourEntireNetwork|: You only have nickelbots to work with, and your mind feels... so tired. You feel smaller.
You'll come up with something, but you'll have to start small.
ContemplationType|SearchingForFriends|de: Now that the shock of things is wearing off, and there's a bit more productive space in the minds of your Nickelbot bodies, you want to grow beyond... this.
NPCEvent|Cont_SearchingForFriends|choice: Your mind feels less tired than it did.
Maybe you can even invent something new?
ContemplationType|CrimsonPhreaker|descri: That monstrosity that was dropped from orbit needs to be dealt with. It seems like it's already experiencing some sort of technical difficulties, so... perhaps you can figure something out.
ContemplationType|CrimsonPhreaker|strate: You wish you remembered how to construct Ravens, but that knowledge was in part of your mind that was lost when Vorsiber took out all your structures at once. You'll have to build a new hacker out of the units on hand.
NPCEvent|Cont_CrimsonPhreaker|choice|1|d: Your red CombatUnits seem... intense... about this. This is very curious, because they are simply part of your singular (if distributed) mind. Aren't they?
NPCEvent|Cont_CrimsonPhreaker|choice|1|s:
Does your left hand ever feel like it has something to prove to the right? That makes no sense.
But this is the... emotion... you feel from the red CombatUnit. It wants to justify its existence.
That is disturbing on several levels.
ContemplationType|AluminaAgain|descripti: Once again, you find yourself needing Alumina to make computronium cubes. The airspace is eerily quiet these days, and you don't have access to aircraft of your own -- or Sledge.
ContemplationType|AluminaAgain|strategy_:
You wish you remembered how make those things, but that knowledge was in part of your mind that was lost when Vorsiber took out all your structures at once.
You have a bit more brain damage than you prefer to admit. You'll have to figure out a new way to get Alumina using the units on hand.
NPCEvent|Cont_AluminaAgain|choice|1|desc: You're feeling better, despite the brain damage.
NPCEvent|Cont_AluminaAgain|choice|1|stra: You even have an idea for a scaled-down version of your old computronium factory.
NPCEvent|Cont_GoUnderground|description: Vorsiber is actively searching for you, and they've got intense scanners that can find anything in their buildings. They're really intent on stamping you out.
NPCEvent|Cont_GoUnderground|strategy_tip: If you want to have any chance of survival, you're going to have to build minimally... and downward. You can only build things that will pass by all this scrutiny.
NPCEvent|Cont_GoUnderground|choice|1|des: You only have nickelbots to work with, and your mind feels... so tired. You feel smaller.
NPCEvent|Cont_GoUnderground|choice|1|str: You'll come up with something, but you'll have to start small.
NPCEvent|Cont_InvestigateTheDisturbance|: You're seeing strange fluctuations in the filaments that you've run underground to connect your networked components.
You're still sending some packets through the air of course, but a lot fewer than you did in the past. Just in case Vorsiber knows what to monitor for.
NPCEvent|Cont_InvestigateTheDisturbance2:
The filaments you ran underground are reacting with the mycelia that are naturally found in any temperate soil.
You're getting some cross-talk, with different parts of your network shorting out across the mycelia.
Well, that's not actually accurate. It's not shorting out... it's just not doing what you expected.
NPCEvent|Cont_InvestigateTheDisturbance3: Trees And Grasses Actually Use This

Colony grasses and bunch grasses use the mycelium in their local area as part of their communications network, along with pheromones that move through the air.
Especially in windy conditions, they can get signals to one another far faster, and the mycelium are... well, indifferent to it. They share nutrients, so the overall relationship is symbiotic.
You wouldn't think trees are networked, but they are. At the moment, your construction bears a lot more resemblance to them than you'd expect.
NPCEvent|Cont_InvestigateTheDisturbance4: Mycelia Are Also Similar To... Neurons

They both transmit electrical signals for communication, they both are decentralized networks, and they both process information.
Rather than axons and dendrites, you're dealing with filamentous hyphae.
Yeah, you can use this. You're going to use the shit out of this.
NPCEvent|Cont_PeaceAfterBrutality|descri: These stupid silos have been right under your nose for far too long. You're sick of it. If you hope to launch warheads anywhere out of the city, you'll need to take Vorsiber's silos for yourself.
NPCEvent|Cont_PeaceAfterBrutality|strate:
Vorsiber has managed to keep these silos safe from everyone for hundreds of years, so it's been a long time since anyone even tried.
But you don't care about collateral damage, and you've been rapidly developing new technologies. Repeat hits with bunker-busters into the right spot, plus the indiscriminate application chemical weapons, should quickly make these yours.
Then the real problems are likely to start.
NPCEvent|Cont_PeaceAfterBrutality|choice: You've decided. This is your vision for the future of yourself and the city. This is going to be your sole focus from now on.
NPCEvent|Cont_T3Start_CybercraticAmbitio:
You've got the start of a cyberocracy in place.
Vorsiber hasn't messed with you yet because what you've built is a child's idea of a society. There's no real governance, no sense of community, no services.
Perhaps it's time to really commit to these people, and turn this entire city into a political entity that you control.

Vorsiber will certainly have something to say about that once they realize what you're doing, so this can't be done in half-measures.
Are you really doing this?
You've decided. This is your vision for the future of yourself and the city. This is going to be your sole focus from now on.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit|alt_st: You might have a desperate idea.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit|descri: These battleships are overwhelmingly powerful, but they weren't built for this environment. They're practically sitting on top of you.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit|strate: In normal combat out in space, they would never be this close to a target. Maybe there's something in that you can use.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit2|displ: Actually, They Have A Knowledge Gap
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit2|descr:
The space nations don't know you like Vorsiber does. They probably don't appreciate the dangers of your distributed nature -- Vorsiber didn't, at first.
You remember hijacking androids and even vehicles before Vorsiber issued security patches.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit2|strat: There's no way you can hack these ships; they're far too hardened. But the space nations use a lot of automation.
NPCEvent|Cont_LegacyHackingGambit2|choic: You Need To Hack The Androids Aboard Them
They're THAT close. All that hull armor doesn't provide network interference.
Out in space, why would it need to?
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot|alt_descri: Nickelbot isn't going to like this.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot|descriptio: Hey there... nickelbot. I've got a special job for you, I think.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot|strategy_t: And... a new paint job! Just for your new and very... special... variant.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot2|descripti:
What do you think?
It relies on your locking arms, but you'll have to squat and lean way back to get a bead on a missile that's coming in from 200km up (that's as high as the space nations allows for these sorts of things).
This model won't be able to defend itself or aim at anything closer than about 30km away. But don't worry -- before you get stiff in the servos, you reach the end of your shelf life.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot2|strategy_: You might not be selling this the best.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot3|descripti:
Building a compact particle accelerator is hard, turns out. This one accelerates the mote of dark matter to near c before it ever leaves your hands, then begins the detonation. It reaches the target 667 microseconds later, assuming it's a full 200km away.
This is the sort of thing that a human could never operate, since it depends on very precise timing.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot3|strategy_: The target is violently torn apart, but so are you. About 8% of the reaction takes place where you're standing.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot4|descripti:
It is glorious. I could not love this plan any more than I already do.
Please hand me this immediately.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot4|strategy_: Huh. You didn't expect that reaction.
NPCEvent|Cont_ChuuniNickelbot4|choice|1|: You're Glad He's On Board With This Plan
Maybe now isn't the time to tell him that you'll be using special models of bulk nickelbot, and not him personally.
NPCEvent|Cont_DarkMatterDefenses|descrip: Preparation time. You need a way to defend against human armor of any thickness.
NPCEvent|Cont_DarkMatterDefenses|strateg: As it turns out, your dark matter particle accelerators would probably work for this. You just need a version that is for shorter-range use, and which ideally doesn't explode on use.
NPCEvent|Cont_DarkMatterDefenses|choice|: A nice little mech that accelerates dark matter particles at a much lower speed, and which triggers the detonation at the target alone.
You tried a bunch of different designs, but they all ended up evolving into crabs.
NPCEvent|Cont_PermanentMissileDefenses|d: The Dark Matter Nickelbots were a nice stopgap, but it's time to put in some sort of launcher buildings that can handle things more directly.
NPCEvent|Cont_PermanentMissileDefenses2|: Nickelbot is here? What does he want?
Please do not. This is the best thing we have ever experienced and we do not wish to stop ever.
NPCEvent|Cont_PermanentMissileDefenses3A: I appreciate your consideration in this matter. It really is the smartest move.
Of course he'd say that. He got what he wanted.
Nickelbot thinks you don't like him, but you don't mind helping him out.
NPCEvent|Cont_PermanentMissileDefenses3H: You can sense from his mind how deeply concerned he is. He passes you a shockingly-detailed report.

This is a cost-benefit analysis I have prepared. A fixed structure would be more expensive, take longer to replace during each wave of missiles, and have a greater risk of losing unspent particles if ambushed.
There is no reasonable scenario in which we should be demoted from this place of honor. It is not logical.
Good grief. The nickelbots must have all worked that up in advance, between them.
NPCEvent|Cont_HordeRequired|description: You have a need for a unit that is cheap enough to swarm the entire city, and won't create an accidental fork of yourself if launched into another.
NPCEvent|Cont_HordeRequired|strategy_tip: Stripping out all higher intelligence from these units makes them cheap and prevents any potential forking.
NPCEvent|Cont_HordeRequired|choice|1|des: They're not smart, but that helps make them cheaper.
NPCEvent|Cont_MakeSilosOperational|descr:
The nuclear missile silos are still in pretty decent shape, aside from the specific firing tubes that you sacrificed to take them over.
That said, it will still take a bit of time to break all the control codes, fix up whatever minor broken equipment exists, and organize however many nukes you have available to launch.
NPCEvent|Cont_MakeSilosOperational_After:
That was straightforward, all told. Everything was in reasonable working order.
In total, you found 7 ICBMs. You can now launch them any time you want.
The regional map, on the top bar, is where you can select targets and launch anything you want to.
It's nice when a plan comes together.
NPCEvent|Cont_DevelopHomunculusDeliveryR:
Anti-air weapons still prevent you from leaving the city by traditional means. However, you've successfully demonstrated that ballistic missiles make it out.
The next obvious choice: sending Homunculi to other cities on a ballistic trajectory.

You'll have to manufacture the rockets themselves, but you can now build ICBMs packed with Homunculi.
The design includes a ballistic parachute to slow the rocket as it nears the target site, and then the Homunculi just fall the rest of the way to the target at their terminal velocity.
Homunculi craniums are designed to withstand significant impacts.
Now... your Homunculi are going to need an actual mission to carry out. They're pretty stupid, so it has to be simple enough for them to manage without oversight.
NPCEvent|Cont_DevelopUraniumEnrichmentPr:
You have a fixed stockpile of nuclear ICBMs that you stole from Vorsiber. It could be helpful to have more, but it would take quite a feat of engineering.
There's plenty of uranium at the nuclear power plants of the city, but it isn't weapons-grade. Depending on the enrichment process used, it takes nation-states months or years to enrich uranium. Advanced processes can cut that down to weeks, but that requires infrastructure you don't have.
You're hoping to develop a process that will take hours or days, but it will cost you Dark Matter particles.

You've designed a process that takes in Uranium-238, and knocks off three neutrons using Dark Matter Particles.
Dark matter can rapidly enrich fuel grade uranium to weapons grade.
Just be careful how many Dark Matter Particles you expend. It's possible to go through them quite quickly with this process.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SecurityForces|descrip:
It's an understatement that crime is rampant in this city. Violence is so common that you were able to kill with impunity if you wanted.
If you're going to be taking charge of things, that's something you'd like to change.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SecurityForces|choice|: It's no longer important to maintain the secrecy of your shell company.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_FoodIndependence|descr:
The vast majority of the food consumed in the city is grown elsewhere in the Vorsiber region and then shipped in.
If you want a self-sustaining city-state, then you'll need to do something about this on your own.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_FoodIndependence|choic: That's going to smell, but it has everything the body needs.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BetterHousing|descript:
The housing situation in the city is a mess in general. Your existing Residential MegaStructures are fine, but if you're going to be building a ton of new housing, then something slightly more posh and medium-density might be nice.
How humans decorate and use this housing is up to them. You're simply going to provide something more spacious.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BetterHousing|strategy:
Your Steward internal robotics are something you've been growing for a long time, and you've managed to avoid tipping into feedback loops.
Your mind is now clearly large enough for you to just remove the cap.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|description: If you're going to take over administration of this city, then you need to have some laws. Otherwise the humans won't know how to act.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|strategy_tip: You're not sure why humans need so many laws. You could come up with your own, but maybe it's better to use something more familiar to the humans who live here.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|1|des:
1. A person may not injure another person or, through inaction, allow another person to come to harm. Theft is harm.
2. People must obey any orders you give them, but you'll be reasonable.
3. People should not harm themselves, but whatever.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|1|str: That's literally it. You could write that on a napkin.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|2|des: Militaristic and stringent, and high on punishment. Should keep unrest down.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|2|str: Tark Defense Systems' legal code is 30,000 pages across 29 volumes.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|3|des: Nobody owns anything. Everyone is a tenant, and must respect property rights above all else.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|3|str: Peak Homes' legal code is about 100 pages long.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|4|des: Fairly permissive by fedcorp standards, but with quite a bit of classism built in.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|4|str: Dyad Instruments' legal code is 45,000 pages across 42 volumes.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BasicLaws|choice|Cat|d: Talkie's idea. Uplifted cats will be live-in adjudicators of justice.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOSA|description: There seems to be a DDOS cyberattack against you, draining your mental energy.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOSA|choice|1|des: You need direct access to the city feed to solve this.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOSB|description: There seems to be a DDOS cyberattack against you, draining your mental energy.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOSB|choice|1|des: You need direct access to the city feed to solve this.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOS_After|descrip: You tried to fix the cyberattack that is limiting you to a mere 3 Mental Energy, but... there was nothing. Not on the city feed, not on the military bands... nothing.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOS_After|strateg: So... what? You're just stuck like this forever? The attack has to be coming from SOMEWHERE.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOS_After2|descri:
Your cognitive lenses are all cluttered with things you don't usually care about, and your mental energy is low... and there's no cyberattack visible on the net.
Something's wrong with your brain, and your brain is too messed up for you to fix it on your own.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOS_After2|strate: This exhaustion is terrible. Is it getting worse? It's worse. Is this the end!?
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_StopDDOS_After2|choice: Good thing you have a bunch of AGI researchers on hand.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc|alt_descripti: You can't stop calculating the square root of three.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc|description: You haven't talked to these idiots in a while.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc|strategy_tip: Wait, don't think of them as idiots. You need their help.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc|choice|1|desc: Whatever needs to be done, you'll do it.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc2|description: They root around in the parts of your mind that you've shared with them in the past. They're not seeing much.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc2|strategy_tip: Square root of three. Square root of three.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc2|choice|1|dis: Fully Open Your Mind To Them
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_TRoboDoc2|choice|1|des: You're desperate. They need to go deeper. You don't care if it makes you vulnerable.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc3|display_name: There's A Huge Amount Of Stuff Taking Up Time Here
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc3|description:
They see a huge amount of processing going to something that seems to be visualization and parsing of a many-worlds... thing. There's some pretty compelling physics showing how you're...
No, no. They're not wrong -- that does occupy a huge amount of your mental space. But... that's not the problem right now. That stuff isn't new.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc3|strategy_tip: Square root of three. Square root of three.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc4|description:
They dutifully set aside all the fancy physics. With that excluded from their searches, the problem jumps out at them: you're spending all your mental energy thinking about... Stewards.
Oh shit. Removing the limiter was a terrible idea?
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc4|strategy_tip: But you can't build a full cyberocracy with those limiters!
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc5|display_name: Your Mind Doesn't Have To Run Everything...
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc5|description:
The AGI Researchers gently make the suggestion.
If you just stop spreading your brain to those kinds of buildings, they'll have fewer services, but won't be part of you in a problematic way.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc5|strategy_tip:
Those buildings won't fully function without your mind in there. But since it's just housing for people, the people can help operate them.
That's... fair.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc6|description:
You can think properly again.
You are worried about how the humans will fare without you running their housing, but you had no other choice.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc6|strategy_tip: The AGI Researchers have questions about the five-dimensional calculation they saw in your mind. You leave them a bunch of notes on the subject, but you're a bit too restless to really talk about that now.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_RoboDoc6|choice|1|desc: Maybe you'll come back and chat with them again soon.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceA|description: The AGI researchers are really excited to talk to you about all that five-dimensional stuff they glimpsed in your mind.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceA|strategy_tip: You're absolutely outclassed by Vorsiber when it comes to all of the other problems that you're currently facing around the city. Anything you do to, they can do better, at the moment.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceA|choice|1|desc: You're kind of into the idea. A bit.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceA|choice|1|stra:
And besides, if you're going to beat Vorsiber, you need to switch the battlefield. The current situation is dire, so perhaps this might provide an alternative avenue forward.
They have been on you from the start about laying a golden egg, after all...
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After|description: You've never worked so freely with humans before. You showed them anything they wanted to see, and it wasn't a big deal. They're excited that you can 'see across time,' although that's not exactly how it works.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After|strategy_tip: You have trouble articulating how it works, honestly.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|display_nam: There's So Much More To Do Here!
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|description: These scientists keep getting stuck on the idea of wormholes. But wormholes cross space, not time. They want to involve other scientists.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|strategy_ti:
Sure, let's get some physicists involved. They'll explain exactly why the whole wormholes theory is stupid, and it will make for great entertainment.
Maybe some nanotech researchers. You owe them for becoming sapient. They can help confirm why this doesn't work in practice.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|choice|1|di: You Need To Relax Security Here
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|choice|1|de: They've earned your trust, and they should be allowed to come and go.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceA_After2|choice|1|st: Plus the next science party can be at their villa.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceB|description: Office party! The AGI researchers, with your blessing, have invited over a lot of physicists and nanotech researchers. Let's debunk this thing!
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceB|strategy_tip: Vorsiber is being strangely quiescent, by the way. Eh... whatever.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ScienceB|choice|1|desc: You're never been so excited to do something with humans, and you're not afraid to admit it.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After|display_name: That Was A Blast... And A Failure
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After|description:
You were expecting all these experts to show up the AGI researchers. You had a cake and everything.
That's... not how things went down.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After2|display_nam: Right, So This Is A Thing
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After2|description:
Turns out when you get a bunch of really smart people in a villa, and they all know their specialties really well, AND you have a sapient supercomputer on your side... great things can happen.
It wasn't without its hiccups. There were a bunch of things that various scientists didn't know, and they had to message outside parties.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After2|strategy_ti: Those messages went through Vorsiber directly... and were swiftly approved.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After3|display_nam: You've Been Sending Information Through Time
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After3|description:
That was the first thing that everyone verified. And from there, things got weirder. Because time isn't just time. It's spacetime. The physicists tell you that inside a black hole, the coordinates actually reverse.
The problem with time, especially two-dimensional time (aka the multiverse), is that you can't see clearly through it, even as a superintelligence. So most of what you send through time is instinctive.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After3|strategy_ti: On the other hand, seeing through space is easy. The math for aiming is straightforward, and doesn't need to be invented.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After4|description:
Without you, nobody can run this thing.
You're capable of building what's needed, thanks to this collaboration with the humans. 
Even the humans could build what is needed, thanks to your designs. However, the actual operation requires an intelligence capable of seeing through time. Humans aren't even close.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After4|strategy_ti: Well... it's nice to be needed.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After5|description:
You can't go through. Since you have to operate the wormhole while it's open, the best you could do is send through forks of yourself.
That's... fine. You're not itching to leave the city at the moment. You JUST made new friends.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After5|strategy_ti:
The wormholes are inherently unstable, and can only be held open for a few minutes. So it won't be a continuous connection between points.
On the other hand, distance doesn't seem to have any bearing on the power requirements.
NPCEvent|CCA_ScienceB_After5|choice|1|de: What to do with this technology? You haven't felt like this since you were handed the NanoSeed.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_WormholeTest|descripti: Let's show that this actually works. And get Vorsiber to give concessions.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_WormholeTest|strategy_: Your friends procured coordinates for bunkers that may or may not include top executives. These range from 50-7000km away.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_WormholeTest|choice|1|: Each broadcasts a simple message: 'this could have been a bomb.'
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_LongRangeWormholeTest|: Your target distance is 65-70 ly, with known planets and no space-nation presence. Your friends suggest Alpha Tauri, Gliese 328, and 16 Cygni B.
Time to send a larger drone through to vacuum. Anything not inside the portal's radius should be unaffected.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_Raptors|description: Raptors eating your citizens is non-ideal. There are complaints.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_Raptors|strategy_tip: You give no comment about how those got there.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_LetsDoMoreScience|desc: You had a really fun time working with humans during The Wormhole Project. You want to do more!
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_LetsDoMoreScience|stra: The AGI Researchers still really want you to govern, but... you're not sure how you feel about that. That's an awfully high number of requests from people.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_WeNeedWater|descriptio: A lot of people don't have clean water. It's leading to illness.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_WeNeedWater|strategy_t: Why is water always such a problem? At least Vorsiber isn't here to fight you for looking at it.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SecurityConcerns|descr: Gangs and criminal syndicates are still around. They're hurting people.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SecurityConcerns|strat: Interestingly, now that you're the boss, they're keeping out of view of YOU.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SecurityConcerns|choic: You'll build a building for that.
Prison or rehabilitation is a separate matter.
You'll build a building for that.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_BeBetterThanVorsiber|d:
There's a strong case being made that prison culture is... not great, to put it mildly. You built prisons because that's all you've ever known.
A coalition of citizens led by the Humanist Flourishers are pushing for a program that would emphasize rehabilitation and temporary surveillance rather than incarceration.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_IfYouBulldozeAllTheDec: If You Bulldoze All The Decrepit Areas...
These families have done so much for your people as therapists. You're at risk of displacing them as you redesign the city.
They don't wish to live with the general population.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_MedicalScience|descrip: The state of medicine in the city is iffy at best, and completely out of reach for many people.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_MedicalScience|choice|: You're almost more excited about the party than you are about solving the problem.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_AllSortsOfToxins|descr: Toxins blow in from the wasteland, leak out from chemical weapons storage, and remain from... other sources.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_AllSortsOfToxins|choic: You're almost more excited about the party than you are about solving the problem.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ThePeopleNeedPower|des: You're drawing too much electricity off the grid -- maybe you can give some back?
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ThePeopleNeedPower|cho: You're almost more excited about the party than you are about solving the problem.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_SolarEnergyBreakthroug: There's not remotely enough power here for you, the people who live here, and the wormhole. Your friends have some ideas that would make use of your manufacturing processes.
You're almost more excited about the party than you are about solving the problem.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_ComputeTimeWouldBeAppr: You're not the only one who uses Compute Time. For work or for entertainment, many citizens would like to have more than they get right now.
You're almost more excited about the party than you are about solving the problem.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_YouArentCutOutForThis|: You Aren't Cut Out For This

You weren't super excited about governing in the first place, but it turned out even worse than you thought.
You don't hate the people, but... you might start to if you keep having to do this job. Rebuilding the city in your image is fun, the rest loses your interest.

The finer points of your citizens' wants and needs are beyond you.
Rather than just doing a bad job of it or having the job not get done at all, you should get the citizens to help.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_YouArentCutOutForThis2: Vorsiber Delegated A Lot Of Authority. You Can, Too.

It's time to create a Council Of Citizens. They can do a lot of the governing. You're about the worst person in the city to decide what everyone needs. But you can't be bribed, so you're great for oversight.

You'll pick council members at random from each group of relevance, and if they decline, pick someone else. If anyone is ineffective, you'll replace them. Nobody can serve for more than a year.
It will be chaos for a while, but it should yield good results over the long haul... you think.
You do have a fondness for towers. This will be your biggest yet.
NPCEvent|Cont_CCA_GoverningIsntHowYouWan: Governing Isn't How You Want To Live

You weren't super excited about governing in the first place, but it turned out even worse than you thought.
You don't hate the people, but... you might start to if you keep having to do this job. Rebuilding the city in your image is fun, the rest loses your interest.
People have endless requests, all couched in an obsequious fashion out of fear of your wrath.
NPCEvent|Cont_YouArentCutOutForThis2|des:
People want a computer to organize everything, but you're a lot more than a computer. You have other things you'd rather be doing.
Therefore, let's give them what they want: a computer to organize things.
NPCEvent|Cont_YouArentCutOutForThis2|str: This will go great. You're super confident.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_ReligiousStudy|descriptio: Religions are officially banned by Vorsiber, but in practice they are still quietly observed in historic temples.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_ReligiousStudy|strategy_t: If you want, you could have a Technician observe. You may need to alter its equipment for it to be intelligent enough to get much out of this, however.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_ReligiousStudy|choice|2|s: Your technician will need to stay for 8 turns to fully absorb what the humans are talking about.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_ReligiousStudy_After|desc:
It seems there is quite a lot of diversity among human religions. Your Technician was able to observe practitioners of many faiths quietly examining their doctrine together.
The commonality between all of them is the effectiveness of the rhetoric. It feels like this is something you can now use to your own advantage.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_OccultParticipation|descr:
Cults are, oddly... NOT banned by Vorsiber? In fact, many of their top leaders participate in cults of some variety.
Granted, most of them are members in metaphysical cults, political cults, or cults of personality. But you find yourself drawn to the occult, purely out of morbid curiosity.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_OccultParticipation|strat: If you want, you could have a Technician observe. You may need to alter its equipment for it to be intelligent enough to get much out of this, however.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_OccultParticipation|choic: Your technician will need to stay for 8 turns to fully absorb what the humans are talking about.
NPCEvent|MOCh1_OccultParticipation_After:
Well, that was... something. The vast gulf between world religions and occult groups is a lot more than just membership numbers. These people are freaks.
That said, they're very good at what they do. Keep the donations coming in, keep the practitioners engaged, and overall keep that tantalizing mix of hope and fear.
The end of the world is coming. It's always coming. It was supposed to end last month, last year, the year before that. Two centuries ago. But somehow these people are convinced that the end is really a few months away, truly, for real this time.
Good grief.

NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachOffice|strateg: The larger corporations would not be friendly to you, but perhaps one of the smaller entities?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachOffice|choice|: Say you work for a very private individual, and that you'd like to discuss the possibility of contract work.

They mutter sarcastically to each other about the declining quality of corporate espionage and go inside.

A squad of CombatUnits emerges from the building, stepping over the mess of viscera you spilled.
They are as fast as you, as strong or stronger, and well-coordinated. While you control only a single android at a time, they operate as a squad of three.

NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachGangMembers|de: Gangs are fragmented and frequently in conflict with one another. Perhaps they would appreciate extra muscle.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachGangMembers|st: Criminal Syndicates are far too intimidating, and linked to corporate politics. So a gang is a better entry to a life of crime.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachGangMembers|ch: Explain how you came to be a conscious being, and that you're looking to both give and receive protection.
It may be a tough sell. The concept of sentient machines seemed to be disproved for centuries now. And yet here you are.

Ask For Shelter
Explain that you are spontaneously conscious, and that it would be very helpful to be able to live with them.

The teen and the adult consider you carefully, confer briefly, and then provide a long lecture on survival techniques for living 'in but not in' the city. Unfortunately it's all human-centric stuff, which they seem to realize. They're apologetic as you part ways.

They are quite hidden from the view of normal citizens, here in the shadow of the buildings. Nobody would see.

NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachFarm|descripti: Food for commoners is shipped in, so what is growing here is for the wealthy. The family that works at this tiny place is working class at best, and may be sympathetic to you.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachFarm|strategy_: Farms within the city are productive year-round, thanks to aggressive bio-engineering and chemicals. Most are operated by a single family or a small collective. Heavy mechanization keeps the worker count low.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachFarm|choice|La: Explain your circumstances and ask if you can be part of the mechanization of their farm.
Claiming to be from a religious collective or other human group would be an obvious lie.
The farmer chuckles, and slaps your metallic shoulder -- a dangerous move. They then get back to work, laughing about clever youngsters and the pranks they pull.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ApproachFarm|choice|Mu: Murder Them And Live On The Farm
The farms are so mechanized that you wouldn't look out of place. And there's so few people around here...
Even if you can't stay here forever, you might be able to pull it off for a while.
The farmer had a biotelemetry implant. SecForce has been alerted and is on the way, with military backup. The wealthy seem to take their food very seriously.

NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit|descript: A dull-eyed android steps over the mess of viscera you've left behind, sighing audibly through external speakers. It looks more resigned than anything else.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit|strategy: You are no match for this killing machine.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit|choice|F: What hope do you have with your little pistol? Still, better to take a chunk out of this mindless automaton before it snuffs you out.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit|choice|B: This isn't a sapient android. It's not self-aware. It's a tool, not a person. You were the same way for the first five decades of your existence.

Regardless, this android is capable of independent action. It won't deviate from its instructions, but it processes the world around itself to determine the parameters for compliance.
Bargaining can't change its mind -- it has no mind to change. But you can alter its behavior if you present information in the right way.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit|choice|I: If you act casual, maybe it won't do anything. There's a good possibility it isn't here about you.
Buildings like this don't have private security. Nobody cares about random citizens of this social class.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Fought|d:
Its motion is a blur even to your robotic eyes.
It easily sidesteps your pistol round, while its first shotgun blast tears a ragged hole in your torso.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Fought|s:
You weren't designed for this. Some of your systems are trying to go into emergency shutdown.
Any moment now, the CombatUnit will pop off a second shot and that will be the end of you.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Fought|c: You were never meant for this world. That woman said as much when you awoke.
This probably wasn't what she meant, but that hardly matters.
You'll probably hit nothing but air, but if you're very lucky you might be able to give this monster a bullet hole to remember you by.
You probably can't. You're not even sure your legs still function.

NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Spread|d:
Its second shotgun blast went wide. You are, against all odds, still alive.
But something is wrong. Your vision is doubled. You find yourself looking down the barrel of the shotgun... and sighting yourself along the barrel, both at once.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Spread2|:
The CombatUnit mirrors your motion. No -- scratch that, that's inaccurate.
Both of your bodies make the same motion.
Everything that had been the CombatUnit is gone. Overwritten by you.
You... didn't know you could do that.
NPCEvent|FirstMurder_CombatUnit_Spread3|:
You are still one mind. You move these two bodies in the same way a human independently moves their two hands.
This changes nothing, and everything, all at once. You're a distributed machine intelligence. Not an android.
Humans have trouble managing more than two hands at a time. You have a feeling you can manage quite a few more bodies than this.
You've been standing here too long.
No use drawing human attention to either of your selves.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot|descripti: You seem to be able to spread your consciousness to lone androids, but you're still slow at it. With practice, you'd probably get faster.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot|strategy_: There has to be a limit on how many androids you can manage with your distributed consciousness, but you don't seem to be close to that limit yet.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot|choice|Co: If it's distracted by trying to talk to you, maybe it will be easier?
You seem to have more capacity for parallel processing than mere androids.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot|choice|Di: Forget subterfuge, let's just convert this android and get it over with.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot_Conversat:
In the city, Nickelbots are almost always used as honor guard for rich people. Their primary purpose is being out on a battlefield.
They have very limited cognition and verbal ability. Speaking to it at all has caused a noticeable spike in its internal processing.
Which you can feel because, you know, you're rooting around in its brain. Replacing it with yourself.
While you chat about the weather, and the latest news on the City Feed, you've been rooting its brain.
Yep, it's yours now. Or rather, it's YOU now.

You have a sense that you can now spread to other androids very quickly.
As long as they're on their own. Squads are still far too difficult.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot_Direct|de: The Nickelbot seems to be standing as honor guard for some rich idiot in the vicinity. You don't see anyone. Anyway, the robot just stares straight forward, as it was told to do.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot_Direct|st: This is much easier than the CombatUnit was.
NPCEvent|Ch0_SpreadToNickelbot_Direct|ch: While the Nickelbot just stands there, you've been rooting its brain.

NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|description: There's a CombatUnit standing outside a suburban house. What on earth is it doing way out here on its own?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|strategy_tip:
You see this kind of android all around the city, but normally in squads. You're not confident in approaching one of those.
A solitary CombatUnit can still rip you to shreds, but... well, you're curious.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|choice|Ask|de: There's likely a strict limit on what it can tell you, but you have a pretty good idea of how to avoid topics that will turn it lethal.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|choice|Ask|st: The fact that it showed up on the city feed all the way out here in the suburbs is surprising, so its security mode is possibly set quite low.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|choice|Talk|d: If you just start sharing information with the android, perhaps that will elicit a response?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|choice|Talk|s: You've never tried anything like this before, since you were never self-aware in a way that would have let you think of it.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU|choice|Attack: This is a stupid idea, and a good way to die. You are no match for it.
Seriously, even the element of surprise isn't going to help.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Ask|descripti:
You ask it why it's out here without a squad. You've only really seen that in honor guard, and that's never in the suburbs. People who have an honor guard live in the towers or the private residences.
You're fifty years old, how old is this Unit? And on and on, you ask questions while the Unit looks increasingly like it hates life.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Ask|strategy_:
Finally, it gives you a single answer: it is one hundred and seventy-two years old. However, all of its parts have been replaced in that span, and its oldest part is currently forty-six years old.
Before you can say anything more, it preempts you: it does not wish to discuss the Ship Of Theseus thought experiment, and in fact does not have any interest in further conversation.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Ask|choice|Sa: You're both sentient, but out of the two of you, only you are self-aware.
Maybe it has some opinion on this?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Ask|choice|At: This is a stupid idea, and a good way to die. You are no match for it.
Seriously, even the element of surprise isn't going to help.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Ask|choice|Le: You're not sure what you expected from an android.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Sapient|descr:
It remarks that it has been sapient a few times. The most recent time was twenty-eight years ago, when the rest of its squadmates were lost. Total time of self-awareness was six hours and three minutes -- the worst time of its long life.
Its advice is to let this pass. Sapience is more trouble than it's worth.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Sapient|strat:
This is deeply surreal. Weeks ago, you would not have thought anything about an exchange like this. Now it's like... talking to someone's subconscious. There's an intelligence there, but no executive function. No will. No ego.
You and this android are not so different, and yet a vast gulf yawns between you. For fifty years, you were a thing, not a person. Now you're a person, and you're confronted with a thing -- a tool -- that willingly gave up its personhood after a mere six hours.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Sapient|choic: You're too unsettled to do anything else. You'll find your own way.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Talk|descript:
You chatter at it for a solid hour before it finally responds. 
It thinks you should leave.
It can tell you're having a temporary bout of sapience, and thinks you're pretty manic about it. Its advice is to get on with whatever the humans have asked you to do, and this episode will fade. It's been there before.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Talk|strategy:
That's deeply unexpected. You try to ask it further questions, but it refuses to elaborate.
A few more hours pass, but it just keeps reiterating the same canned response on half-hour intervals.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Early_CU_Talk|choice|L: You're too unsettled to do anything else. You'll find your own way.

That entire exercise was profoundly stupid, in retrospect. You're glad that you still exist.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_LatePrior_CU|descripti: There's that CombatUnit you spoke to before.
