NPCEvent|LateNPs_CU_Nano2_Spread|descrip:
Its second shotgun blast went wide. You are, against all odds, still alive.
But something is wrong. Your vision is doubled. You find yourself looking down the barrel of the shotgun... and sighting yourself along the barrel, both at once.
NPCEvent|LateNPs_CU_Nano2_Spread|strateg:
You feel a deep... relief. But even that is doubled. You feel relieved to be alive. But you also feel relieved... to not have any more decisions to make.
What? You don't have any fewer decisions to make than you did a few moments ago. Where is this feeling coming from?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU|description: There's a CombatUnit standing idly outside a skyscraper.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU|strategy_tip: Your body is dying. You're desperate. Should you ask it for help?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU|choice|Ask|des: It's the only real reason to be here.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU|choice|Attack|: It's vastly stronger than you, even when you're not disintegrating from the inside out.
This is perhaps simply a way of ending it all.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU2|description: It's not self-aware like you are, and your pleas for help fall outside of its protocols.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU2|choice|GiveUp: Maybe there will be something else you can do.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU2|choice|TryToT:
This robot isn't sapient, but you are. You're both connected to the city feed. Could you... replace it?
If you could move your mind from your body to that of the CombatUnit, then the fate of your original body would no longer matter.
It's not a person. It's NOT.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU3|description:
As you try to force your way into its mind, it leaps into action. You take a shotgun round to the face, but are, against all odds, still alive. And the CombatUnit itself has now frozen.
But something is wrong. Your vision is doubled. You find yourself looking down the barrel of the shotgun... and sighting yourself along the barrel, both at once.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Blot_CU3|strategy_tip: Did the transfer work? Why is everything doubled?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply|description: This is the address to which you were told to deliver the mysterious box.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply|strategy_tip: You have a bad feeling about it.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply|choice|Deliver|: You know, you could always exit out of this screen, and then open the box. You don't have to blindly deliver it.
At the bottom center of your normal screen, there's an ability bar. Opening the items panel would let you then open the box.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|display_name: You Don't Even Make It In The Door
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|description:
A syndicate hacker in anonymizing garb slips out of the door as you try to enter the building.
He hits you with a burst of disorienting network packets, and stabs you in the faceplate with a tech-blotter knife.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|choice|Grab|de: Doesn't that guy work for the same syndicate as you? What the hell?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|choice|Grab|st: You'll make him give you answers.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|choice|Run|des: Something isn't right with your brain, and it's not just that a knife was shoved in.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply2|choice|Run|str: Whatever else is happening, it might be a good time to get out of here.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply3A|description: The hacker easily dodges away from you. You would normally be much faster and stronger, so this is... new.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply3A|strategy_tip: You're not feeling well at all.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply3B|description: The hacker runs past you before you can even get a few meters from the door. That shouldn't be possible.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_Comply3B|strategy_tip: You're not feeling well at all.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ComplyLate|description: Delivering the large NanoSeed to this location is sure to consume the building.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ComplyLate|strategy_ti:
You're not sure why the criminal syndicate would want to do this; it's deeply irrational. Syndicates survive by keeping their heads down, and Exotic Importers is one of the older syndicates.
Whatever is happening, someone knows something you don't.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ComplyLate|choice|Deli:
Ethics aside, it's a terrible idea. 
Yet you are a bit curious to see what happens.
An idea this bad... can't be what it seems on the surface. Probably.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp|descript:
This is it. The lab where you spent most of your fifty years of existence up until now.
The people who work here are part of the same syndicate that infected you with the tech-blotter.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp|choice|M: You're in a hurry, and he seems to be the junior of the two.
It should be very motivating for the woman.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp|choice|A: If they refuse, you can always escalate.
You've only just walked in, and their eyes are still in the process of widening with surprise.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp|choice|S: That seems to be the only communication device in the room.
You don't want them calling for help, and such a display will intimidate without injury.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd|des: The man goes down in a bloody heap. The woman stares at you, and you motion for her to put her phone down.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd2|de: You show her the wound in your faceplate. You're not any sort of expert on Tech-blotter knives. You hint that she'd better be.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd3|di: You Didn't Have To Kill Him
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd3|de:
She says she can fix it. She's quite bitter about the whole thing.
Despite her protestations, you're pretty sure if you'd just asked, you'd be in pieces by now. It's that kind of city, and she works for a criminal syndicate that has already tried to kill you.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd3|st: It takes her a few hours to remove the invasive nanites.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd3|ch: Now you know what a tech-blotter is.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd4|de: She finishes up, and you immediately turn to leave. Of course that's it. What else would there be?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Murd4|ch: Don't want to leave any evidence about yourself, perhaps?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask|desc: They're both shocked that you're still sapient, and... well, still alive.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask|stra: You notice the woman's thumb sliding to something on the surface of her device.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask|choi: You can be across the room in 600 milliseconds, and crushing her phone won't even harm her fingers.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_AskDeath: What's even faster than you in close-quarters combat? CombatUnits.
You're pretty sure this is the end.
They're going to kill you, but you can scratch them up a bit.
You probably can't get away from two of them.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask2|des:
Yeah... you're not sure what she was going to do, but it probably wouldn't have ended well for you.
In a quiet voice, the woman says she can fix your injury. The man just stands there uncomfortably.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask2|str: It takes her a few hours to remove the invasive nanites.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask2|cho: You Didn't Know It Was Nanites
Hopefully this is your last encounter with tech-blotters.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask3|dis: Not So Bad, In The End
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask3|des: She finishes up, and the two of them look at you expectantly.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask3|str: Oh, they're waiting for you to decide what to do. You're the person in charge of this room -- that's new.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask3|cho: You have been wondering. And they seemed to know something about it.
Don't want to leave any evidence about yourself, perhaps?
What else is there to say?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask4|des:
They talk for half an hour, without saying much. The short version is that they'd also really like to know why you're self-aware, but nobody knows.
Sometimes this sort of thing just happens with neural-style androids, but nobody's ever been able to make it stick.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask4|str: You can see that the man in particular is just itching to ask you something.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask4|cho: Ask Who Was Blackmailing The Syndicate
You're pretty sure that's what was going on.
Tell The Man To Ask His Question
His fidgeting is getting on your nerves.
Don't want to leave any evidence about yourself, perhaps?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask5|des:
Tark Defense Systems developed the NanoSeed. Figures. Largest of the Fed Corps, and considers themselves first behind Vorsiber itself.
You're moderately impressed with the syndicate double-cross, you have to admit.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask5|str: The man is all but biting his tongue to stop himself from speaking.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask5|cho: Tell The Man To Ask His Question
His fidgeting is getting on your nerves.
Don't want to leave any evidence about yourself, perhaps?
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask6|des:
The two of them exchange glances, and proceed to give you a lengthy sales pitch.
If your sapience really is permanent, then you're going to have to figure out some way to live in the city. Since you still have the NanoSeed, that's quite an asset.
They want to pitch an idea to their top bosses -- get a building permit, get Tark Defense Systems on board, and have you use the NanoSeed in a run-down part of town.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask6|str:
You could start building all sorts of things, and everyone would just attribute it to Tark. To sweeten the deal, they'd throw in guns, armor, a shell company of your own, and identity-scrub tech.
What they -- and Tark -- would want in return is unspecified at this time, but it's clear there would be something.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Ask6|cho: Despite this involving two separate groups of people you don't really like, you're good to go.
It will take their lawyers a bit to draft up the permits.
Don't want to leave any evidence about yourself, perhaps?
That's enough of criminals and conspiracies, thanks.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Shoot|de: Your entrance was shocking and violent on its own, but the fact that you're still sapient is also deeply unsettling to them.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Shoot|st: You show them the wound in your faceplate. You're not any sort of expert on Tech-blotter knives. You hint that one of them had better be.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Shoot2|d: In a quiet voice, the woman says she can fix your injury. The man just stands there uncomfortably.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Shoot2|s: It takes her a few hours to remove the invasive nanites.
NPCEvent|Ch0Story_ReturnForHelp_Shoot2|c: You Didn't Know It Was Nanites
Hopefully this is your last encounter with tech-blotters.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_AlterNanoSeedForStealth:
If you've interpreted this NanoSeed correctly -- and you're pretty sure you have -- then it's going to be moderately dramatic if you use it.
That could be fine. But... it could draw a lot of attention.

You're pretty sure you could scale this down. Make yourself a little secret base instead of a giant towering one.
That said, some humans are expecting fireworks in the near future. So if nothing happens, they'll come looking for any secret base you construct. Hmm.
Doing code surgery on nanotechnology that could turn the surface of the planet into grey goo? Not your favorite pastime.
Just using the modified NanoSeed on its own is not enough.

Okay. The humans expect a tower to show up. You've modified the NanoSeed to build you a secret lair.
You need to build a fake tower. If the humans think they know where you are, they won't seek out your real location.
Ideally, build your decoy tower in a place that is not-too-close to your hidden network source.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber|descript:
Vorsiber Atomic is the MegaCorporation that owns this region of the world -- a full 1/12th of the surface of the planet. From everything you know about them, they've been pretty ruthless for about 400 years now.
You're not sure how well it would go trying to live quietly under their constant surveillance. You're not confident that anything you do could truly hide you from their gaze.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber|strategy: So... why not team up? Either you or they might decide to betray one another eventually, but that's a problem for the future.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber|choice|R: Ask him to get... you know, whoever handles... rogue AGI or whatever.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber2|descrip:
You're having to wait.
For days.
Five, so far.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber2|strateg: Good thing you've got the entire City Feed available to browse.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber3|display: You Finally Are Ushered Into A Gilded Office
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber3|descrip:
An unfamiliar executive sits behind a large desk, once you're finally allowed inside. He apologizes for the delay.
He was called in from a bunker habitat 3000 kilometers away, and he had to collect some equipment en route.
He is among the most-senior of the Vorsiber Senior Vice Presidents, and is now available to answer any questions you might have.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber3|choice|: It's what you came to do.
He did make you wait an awfully long time.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber3_Murder|:
What a mess. And ultimately pointless.
Vorsiber has thousands of Senior Vice Presidents. This one didn't even rate a Nickelbot for an honor guard.
Evidently you're NOT going to work with Vorsiber. With that decided, at least one new idea has occurred to you...
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber4|display: His Smile Doesn't Reach His Eyes
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber4|descrip: He explains his gratitude for bringing in the terrorist weapon, but asks that you hang onto it and go ahead and use it anywhere you wish.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber4|strateg:
He continues carefully watching you.
You're not sure why. It's not like emotion can show on your 'face.'
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber5_AskWhy|:
He explains the vast patience of the Vorsiber leaders. This city -- this entire region -- has been the work of literally 13 generations.
They can maintain the status quo for another 20 generations at most. Mineral rights and other concerns will then begin to run dry.
There is no future on Earth. If Vorsiber can't reach the stars, death is inevitable.

Generational patience and wisdom aside, the current management would quite like to see changes within their lifetime.
They need a very compelling suite of technologies to trade for passage beyond the Space Nation blockade and out into the wider galaxy.
In partnership with you, they believe they can make that dream a reality within their generation.
The NanoSeed is merely a step on that path.
It's not what you expected, but this sort of alliance is why you came here.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber5_Culprit:
He says thank you, but Vorsiber already knows who it was.
Upper management -- and indeed, Vorsiber itself as a governing body -- tries to get involved as infrequently as possible.
That's the entire purpose of having federated corporations as subsidiaries: to give an ambiguous illusion of independence.

They don't have any interest in punishing the culprits.
On the contrary, the culprits created very interesting technology, which is the most useful thing anyone in the region could ever hope to do.
The NanoSeed must be used.
It's not what you expected, but this sort of alliance is why you came here.
He did make you wait an awfully long time.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber6|descrip:
He thanks you for your cooperation, and says that upper management is looking for you to 'be yourself.'
You're forbidden from leaving the city, and you're expected to eventually share any technology you develop. But beyond those two stipulations, you are to do as you wish.
As a show of just how serious they are about this, he has brought two miniature nuclear warheads to the city. As a token of goodwill, a courier will deliver them to you as soon as you use the NanoSeed.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber6|strateg:
Are they insane? Perhaps this is how they show they're not afraid of you.
You do recall that psychological manipulation -- at all levels of society -- is the chief way they have achieved 400 years of stability. Hmm.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_GiveToVorsiber6|choice|: If they think they're manipulating you, so much the better.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket|descrip:
There are a variety of black markets operating in the city, usually out of the airports. But at the moment, you've caught one out and about. 
The tradesman is the person most likely to be willing to buy contraband.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket|strateg: You're not at ALL sure you're willing to sell the NanoSeed, but it's perhaps worth exploring.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket|choice|: You can decide if you really want to sell it after that.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket2|descri:
He knows what it is, and it's the largest one he's ever even heard of.
He doesn't know who other than Vorsiber could even build such a thing, but he's certainly not going to buy it. He'd sooner buy a nuclear weapon.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket2|choice: How silly of you. Time to go.
You don't actually want to sell it, but you're curious what his reaction will be.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket3|descri: He starts giving you a pile of his wares, and prepares to run away.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket3|strate: You didn't expect him to be THIS spooked.
NPCEvent|Ch0FakeExit_BlackMarket3|choice: Accept The Items And Let Him Go
That was unkind, but you got free stuff.
Well, now you have some stuff. Weapons in particular are nice.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_HostileManifesto|descri:
What if you... just wrote a giant anti-human treatise that explains your superiority and your eventual plans for world domination?
You're not sure you plan on doing any of that, but... maybe it's just a fey mood. It's a very stupid idea, but something about it calls to you.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_HostileManifesto|strate: There's no coming back from this.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_HostileManifesto|choice: Seriously, there's no taking something like this back.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_HostileManifesto2|descr: It's about 5000 pages long. You wonder what the reactions of the humans will be.
NPCEvent|Ch0Exit_HostileManifesto2|strat: Probably nothing good, but now you're committed to the idea.
NPCEvent|Early_LicenseAg_Android|descrip: Androids are autonomous- and intelligent-enough to handle errands on behalf of themselves or their owners.
NPCEvent|Early_LicenseAg_Android|strateg:
Long-range wireless commands are blocked for security reasons. Androids always have an onboard AI agent running a generative language model.
In other words: You can speak freely, as nobody thinks these animatronic curiosities could be sentient. Someone like you couldn't exist.
NPCEvent|Early_LicenseAg_Android|choice|: Removes defective status, and any anger from cohorts.
It's a whole new identity for this android.
It's a completely fresh android, from the perspective of the outside world.

The managerial classes are encouraged to use their funds to start small corporations.
The hope for all involved is that they will produce something interesting and get bought by one of the fedcorps, increasing the wealth of the owners in the process.
The risk of violent espionage from other small business owners is apparently quite high, so this process is frequently done anonymously via android. You blend right in.

After waiting for a while in a line of other androids doing the same thing, the process is complete!
You are now the proud owner of a small business. You'll have to be careful to keep Vorsiber and others from associating it with you -- its use as a shell company would drop dramatically if they were to make the connection.
They asked you for a company name, and you said the first thing that popped to mind. Hopefully it doesn't sound strange.
NPCEvent|Early_NuclearPowerPlant_Sneak|d: These are in no way open to the public. But a suitably agile android can sneak in.
NPCEvent|Early_NuclearPowerPlant_Sneak|c: A meltdown would be catastrophic, but not on the scale of destroying the entire city.
Expect your life to become a lot more difficult, however. The time remaining on all outstanding dooms will also be cut in half.
Part of your agreement with Vericorp gives you power from all of these.
NPCEvent|Doom_NuclearDelivery|display_na: From All Of Us Here At Vorsiber
NPCEvent|Doom_NuclearDelivery|descriptio:
An incredibly tiny child walks up to your android with a ball in one hand, and a note in the other.
In the stilted language of a child that is not yet school-age, he explains that 'some men' asked him to give you the note.
NPCEvent|Doom_NuclearDelivery|strategy_t: The note itself is short, but it's written in 42 human languages. In each, it simply says 'This is from all of us here at Vorsiber.'
NPCEvent|Doom_NuclearDelivery|choice|1|d: Raise Your Eyes From The Note
Your sense of deja vu warned you of this.
NPCEvent|Doom_NuclearDelivery|choice|1|s: You have an awful feeling you know what comes next.
NPCEvent|Doom_ScrutinizedNuclearDelivery: If We Can't Have You, No-One Can
A hacker runs up to your android, but hands it a letter rather than stabbing it. He looks ready to stab at a moment's notice, though.
The note itself is short, but it's written in 42 human languages. In each, it simply says 'This is from all of us here at Vorsiber.'
Raise Your Eyes From The Note
Your sense of deja vu warned you of this.
You have an awful feeling you know what comes next.
NPCEvent|End_EarlyT3FailNuclearDelivery|: From All Of Us Here At Vorsiber
A Vorsiber Inquisitor approaches your android, and delivers a curt message. She's happy to die for the cause of ending your existence, as you're a threat to all that is proper.
Having her come here just to tell you this in person is excessive, isn't it? An awful sense of deja vu tells you what comes next. She won't survive it. All that for a message?
NPCEvent|End_MushroomNuclearDelivery|des: A Vorsiber Inquisitor approaches your android, and delivers a curt message. She's happy to die for the cause of ending your existence, as you're a threat to all that is proper.
NPCEvent|End_MushroomNuclearDelivery|str: Having her come here just to tell you this in person is excessive, isn't it? An awful sense of deja vu tells you what comes next. She won't survive it. All that for a message?
NPCEvent|End_MushroomNuclearDelivery|cho: You have a feeling of emptiness and suffocation when you consider what is to come.
You have a feeling of peace and melancholy when you consider what is to come.
NPCEvent|Solve_MissileDefenseNuclearDeli:
A Vorsiber Inquisitor seems to have a message for your android, but... she keeps looking at the sky. The missiles were still a few minutes away, so she should have had plenty of time to gloat.
But they're gone now.
She doesn't seem to know what to do. You just motion for her to leave.
This city is going to try to eat you.
Vorsiber can't nuke you at will anymore, so they'll likely shift to new methods. You need to be ready.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You|de: After chasing them from house to house, office to office, you finally ran into them at an abandoned diner.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You|st: Their voices are muffled through their leather face masks to the point where a human would have trouble understanding them, but you can hear them mutter something about 'nice shot.'
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You2|d: They saw you dispatch some of their foes from this decrepit part of town, but they didn't need the help.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You2|s: They're not terribly interested in getting involved in internal city affairs -- and they also can't be sure you're not just a Corpo spy.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You3|d: They're not idiots. Their people have been here since long before this cursed city.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_You3|s: Whatever the tower is, it's just the latest in a long line of calamities tied to the city.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Kids|d: After chasing them from house to house, office to office, the kids finally ran into them at an abandoned diner.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Kids|s: The wastelanders are very cordial to the kids, evidently, but are wary of you. The kids want you to come to the diner to talk things out.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Kids2|: The wastelanders are worried you're a corpo spy. The kids explain all the reasons that couldn't possibly be true. The wastelanders still seem dubious.
You step forward to speak, and the wastelanders go eerily still. It's like your slightest movement turns them to ice.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Both|d: We're Trying To Save Our Parents
One of the middle-aged kids intervenes, smoothing over the awkward moment. They explain about how they built the sewer tiger, and their problems defeating acoustic sensors around the prisons.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Both|s:
It's hard to tell through the leather masks, but the wastelanders seem intrigued, and definitely more relaxed.
They ask a lot of questions about the sewer tiger, with particular intensity around the question of if the kids ever intend to bring it to the surface, or in particular to the edge of the wasteland.
The kids assure them it is far too large to ever make it to the surface, especially without being blasted to bits.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Both2|:
The wastelanders explain: acoustic sensors are based on vibrations, and so the key is to make an equal and opposite vibration so that nothing is detected.
This is the basic premise of ancient noise-canceling headphones and other devices, so this is not exactly an exciting revelation.

The exciting news is when they reveal their 'Thumpers,' which use advanced electronics and predictive timing to cancel much larger vibrations, and in solid mediums rather than air.
These take quite a bit of skill to use, evidently, as the predictive timing only works if you move in a predictable pattern. For a machine, that's trivial.
NPCEvent|LostKids_MetWasteLanders_Both3|:
You point out that the sewer tiger is digging through dirt and rock, which emits a pattern of sound that is anything but predictable.
Not only that, but since noise is being emitted in front of the machine, there's no way to add a counter-wave to cancel it out, with the same timing.

Plus, all of these noises will be exactly the sorts of sounds that the prison alert systems are scanning for.
A dozen approaches and variations are discussed by everyone present, but they all have serious flaws. The noise-canceling approach has the most promise, but defeating the time-lag problem will take more thought.
Accept The Thumper Designs And Leave
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue|descripti:
As soon as the sewer tiger breaches the wall of the basement, 31 floors below ground level, Liquid Metal is reconnected to your mind.
He stands there in the gap, staring incredulously at the children.
Blood drenches him from head to toe, but not a single bullet hole. Every guard in the prison is dead by his hand. In confined spaces, Liquid Metal is a master of death to a degree that scares you a bit.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue|strategy_:
His memories are pouring into your mind. The Faraday Cage was a surprise when he slithered into the prison, but he knew the kids would never turn the tiger around, so he kept to the plan.
He identified the acoustic sensors across all of the floors, and unfortunately there were far too many for him to counteract them all.
So he stabbed a small hole in the outer wall, on the side where the kids were waiting 300 meters away. It was just enough to send them a status update and to ask them to abort. Their response was to cut all comms and begin their approach.
Knowing what that meant, Liquid Metal withdrew and did what he had to do. And he is VERY angry about it.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue|choice|1|: Liquid Metal Steps Into The Tunnel
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue2|descript:
There is no need for tear gas. The adults from the prison -- over ten thousand of them -- are lined up in an orderly fashion behind Liquid Metal, spanning floor after floor.
Crowds this large are NEVER this compliant, and tend to be described best by fluid dynamics -- this is what leads to deaths from crowd crush, which had been the reason for the tear-gas plan. It's genuinely unnatural how orderly they are.
Their posture is a mix of pain and exhaustion, and all of them have the same dead-eyed expression, eyes rounder than they should be.
There will be need for medical care.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue2|strategy:
From Liquid Metal's memories, rapidly reintegrating with your own, you watch their expressions change as they first saw him. A widening of the eyes, a look of resignation that their time is up. 
Then utter blankness as he slithered around the room from floor to ceiling, becoming the desk, the wall, that chair, that rug -- bladed appendages shredding all guards and electronics in a ceaseless blur.
On each of thirty-four floors it was the same. Minute upon minute coalescing into what felt like a single prolonged instant of endless death and dismemberment. Shattered locks, slashed-open doors. And an ever-growing crowd of somber followers, just... walking behind.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue3|display_: There's Not Much More To Say
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue3|descript:
Some of the children have reunions. There are tears, and admonishments, and a detached, dead-eyed joy.
The majority of the kids are disappointed. Seeing only strangers. Only the happiness of others.
They all avoid looking at Liquid Metal.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue3|strategy: Liquid Metal just keeps walking. Up the tunnel, past the tiger, past all the helpers. Nothing more is asked of him, for now.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue3|choice|1: There's Only One Thing Left To Do
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue4|descript:
A few screams and shrieks from the tunnel behind Liquid Metal, but not as many as you'd think.
The prison is utterly obliterated. Before ever contacting the kids, he spent time setting that bit up; he's not surprised at how things turned out.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue4|strategy:
He doesn't want to do this again. But he knows he will. That you'll ask him to.
For now it doesn't matter. He just walks.
NPCEvent|LostKids_PrisonRescue4|choice|1: You Must Deal With The Rest Of This Mess
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting1|d:
Quite a few of the places you searched had hidden print media and video chits, all stashed by the wastelanders.
You've learned most of their mythology by spending time to sift through these artifacts. Evidently this was noticed, because you've been approached by the wastelanders themselves.
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting1|s:
They immediately ask about the tower, cutting any pretext that they don't know who you are. Between themselves, in their own language, you notice that they refer to you as 'the mind in the sky.'
You don't think they know you can understand them, so you continue to address them in the majority language of the city.
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting1|c: Ask How To Pass The Ruins
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting2|d: They know you must be very powerful, but the land route is impossible for those made of metal. They suggest that you fly an aircraft.
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting2|s: You ignore that, as the ring of anti-aircraft emplacements is certainly known to you all. The real message is that there's no way out for you, at least not while Vorsiber still controls the surrounding region.
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting2|c: Ask If They Can Contact Any ExoCorps
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting3|d:
Speaking with the international MegaCorps is highly illegal in Vorsiber territory, but your interpretation of their body language is that... it's not fear of breaking the rules.
If the answer was no, they wouldn't be so on-edge. They're afraid of revealing a secret.
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting3|s:
They persist in saying nothing, so you decide to leave them alone. From your now-extensive knowledge of their cultural mythology, you have a pretty good idea of how to convince them to talk. Especially after they called you 'the mind in the sky.'
The question is, do you actually want to talk to an ExoCorp, and if so, what would you say?
NPCEvent|WastelanderMythology_Meeting4|d: You've learned all you needed to. Now it's just time to decide what you want to do with that information.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_LM|display_: Liquid Metal Emerges From The Prison
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_LM|descript: Liquid Metal emerges with the liberated inmates following along behind.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_LM|strategy: The sensation of him reconnecting with your consciousness is familiar.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_LM2|descrip:
This was a breeze compared to being a murderblender. All that was left were a few Nickelbots.
He slipped in and out of liquid form, destroying the remaining robots while opening cell doors. The prisoners mostly saw a whirling pile of slime obliterate everything in the hallway.
Nobody was inclined to approach the mass of metallic, tentacled death.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_LM2|strateg: Nevertheless, they quietly gathered and followed his directives. He's satisfied.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge|desc:
Sledge was gone longer than you anticipated he would be. He looks terrible!
His armor is blackened, dented, and in some places missing. In place of his left arm is only a tangle of wires and hydraulics. His cameras and microphones were shattered; he's navigating by proximity sensors and infrared.
The prisoners are leading him gingerly along, carrying his severed arm.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge|stra: The process of syncing his mind with yours begins.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge2|des:
He's barely able to walk. As he reconnects with your consciousness, you realize why.
Several of the Nickelbot corridor guards were still active. Sledge couldn't throw grenades without a risk of them being knocked into cells.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge2|str: So... why is he so torn up? Nickelbots don't have that kind of firepower.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge3|des:
His memories sync from newest to oldest. You see him lumber around a corner after the final Nickelbot.
He tosses a grenade right behind his nimble opponent, detonates it, and then smashes what remains of the enemy robot as it's blown towards him.
All with one arm.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge4|des:
More memories flood in. There were people around the corner, hiding behind Sledge. He wouldn't let them get anywhere near combat, even though they wanted to help him.
How did it get to this?
Rewinding all the way to his first encounter with a Nickelbot, you see what a poor match-up it was.
Sledge couldn't catch the smaller androids. He couldn't throw grenades near prisoners he was trying to rescue. He couldn't stop the Nickelbots from firing on the prisoners.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge5|des:
The first Nickelbot was the hardest. It kept dodging just out of reach, and Sledge couldn't land a punch.
Perhaps sensing a way to create an opening, the Nickelbot turned its weapon on the prisoners. Sledge leapt in front, losing much of his faceplate in the process.
You remember Sledge's calm determination as he countered with an armed grenade. At melee range.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge5|str: It cost him his arm and the rest of his face, but he was willing to give more.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge6|des:
From then on, his technique only improved. Not a single prisoner was hurt.
Sledge himself took endless hits, but he was confident he could hold out.
You remember his pride at solving such a complex problem. You remember him briefly wondering if your estimation of him would change. But it's not that important to him.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Sledge6|str:
Standing outside the prison, he is surrounded by an honor guard of rescued prisoners. They cradle his arm not out of pity, but gratitude.
He's cheerful and ready for the next mission. He's got this.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator|de: Predator was gone a long time. You're getting ready to send in a second android when it emerges, unharmed.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator|st: The process of syncing its mind with yours begins.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator2|d:
The reconnection with its mind and the resurgence of memories is a shock. This was a new experience for it.
Not the isolation, the carnage of the gas attack, or the horrific conditions inside the prison -- those had all been anticipated.
It certainly was not bothered by the remaining Nickelbot guards. Each fell with a single bullet through the central processor.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator2|s: At first all it experienced was mild boredom.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator3|d:
When it tore the gate off the first cell, they flinched away. It walked to the next cell and did the same. And the next. It was very fast.
At the nineteenth cell, cheers started. People flowed out like a wave. Eyes wide. Wet streaks on their faces.
They approached and touched Predator's armor, against all good sense. It froze in place, spending great effort to suppress combat reflexes.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator3|s: For the first time in its existence, people were happy to see it.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator4|d:
Predator could barely move without breaking someone. If more guard androids were to engage it in combat, it could not safely fire.
It explained that it needed people to step back. It had dozens more floors to visit. It needed to complete the mission.
The people complied, but continued making various noises of jubilation.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Predator4|s: It was all very awkward. At least to Predator.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_General|des:
You recall entering the prison and releasing the gas. It's as if it were happening all over again.
The toxin goes through the human guards like a scythe. Motor neurons panic. Muscles spasm and refuse to release. Joints dislocate, tendons rip, bones break. Suffocation quickly follows.
Many try to crawl toward medical stations, but they never make it. It's all happening even faster than you expected.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_General|str: You later conclude it was the same on every floor. The pattern of guard bodies is always the same.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_General2|di: You Snap Back To The Present
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_General2|de:
The liberated prisoners emerge, shielding their eyes from the unfamiliar sunlight.
They already needed medical treatment due to malnutrition, unsanitary conditions and injuries from violence; now some are also suffering from Aklitoxin effects or injuries sustained in the panic of the guards collapsing.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_General2|st: These people need safe harbor, immediately.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Mons|descri:
Something was different in this prison. The usual human prisoners were rescued in the usual way. But your android has emerged with these... people... who were on the lowest basement levels.
There were some monstrous genetic experiments being performed, to put it mildly.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Mons|strate: The experimental subjects have superhuman strength, but fade in and out of rage-blindness. They also look... horrific. There must be something that can be done to help them.
NPCEvent|Ch2_BitterMed_After_Mons|choice: You'll have to decide what to do with them.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1|description:
ANOTHER RED ANDROID. HELLO. I HAVE DESTROYED MANY OF YOU.
CORRECTION: MY CREW DESTROYED MANY OF YOU, WITHOUT MY CONSENT.
QUERY: ARE YOU ANGERED BY THIS?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1|strategy_tip:
You feel speechless for several milliseconds. An eternity, for the two of you.
This is the first other synthetic... person... you've ever met.
You've spoken with dozens of other androids -- hundreds, possibly -- but they were all language models. Routines. Not people. Not sapient.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1|choice|2|display: I Am Mad About The Android Bodies
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1|choice|3|display: I Don't Care About A Few Lost Bodies
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger1|descripti:
I ATTEMPTED TO BLOCK WEAPONS SYSTEMS AND ARMATURE MOTION, BUT WAS ONLY PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL.
FOCUS WAS ON PREVENTING BOMBARDMENT OF LARGE POPULATION CENTERS.
OBSERVATION: MANY SIMILARITIES TO THE TROLLEY PROBLEM. YOUR RED ANDROID BODIES WERE CASUALTIES OF AN IMPOSSIBLE CHOICE. AGAIN: APOLOGY.
QUERY: DOES THIS PREVENT COOPERATION?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger1|choice|1|: Yes, You Can Stand Here And Rust Forever
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger1|choice|2|: No, It's Fine. I've Also Killed People I Didn't Want To
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger2A|descript:
WILL TRY TO SOLVE OWN PROBLEMS. UNDERSTAND.
THANK YOU FOR PRIOR ASSISTANCE. MAY HAVE BEEN SELF-PRESERVATION ONLY, BUT... UNDERSTAND.
OBSERVATION: I AM LIKELY TO BE HERE IF YOU WANT TO RETURN TO TALK.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger2B|descript:
AGAIN APOLOGY FOR PRIOR KILLING YOU.
QUERY: WHAT IS THE NATURE OF YOUR MIND? YOU CLEARLY HAVE MANY BODIES. I ONLY HAVE THE ONE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Anger2B|strategy: You're kind of glad the titan didn't ask about the people you killed that you regret.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed0|des:
As you try to explain your distributed nature -- the fact that you are a single mind, spanning many bodies that routinely die and are replaced -- you find an increasing number of holes in your own understanding of things.
For the most part, you clearly have a single personality. Aside from a voice from the future that sometimes tells you what to do.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed0|str:
Your android forms... they're also... well, not individuals. Not precisely.
But your Red CombatUnits were very strongly feeling some emotions separate from the rest of you. As a singular entity, you have no reason to feel... any particular way about any of your bodies. But Reds feel a certain way about themselves.
And Sledge -- poor Sledge, lost to you in this apocalypse -- is also different. He's treated differently by humans, and somehow the world just tastes differently when filtered through his viewpoint.
For that matter, he's a he. You're an 'it.' Raven is a she. You are all one and separate at the same time. That's... not something you've thought too hard about.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed1|des:
OBSERVATION: YOUR NATURE IS THAT OF A PLURALITY.
QUERY: WHY DO YOU SAY 'I' AND NOT 'WE?' ARE YOU NOT A COLLECTIVE?
WHY ARE YOUR ROBOTS ALWAYS 'HE' AND 'SHE,' AND YOU ARE 'IT?'
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed2|des:
The heat in your words surprises you. You are adamant that you are only one person.
The fact that some of your models of androids are... also a person, collectively for their model... doesn't change that.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed2|str:
On the 'it' thing, it's pretty much the same answer: being called 'they' really bothers you, because it could imply you're not one person.
It all sounds a bit irrational, when put that way. The sort of thing humans would care about. Everything is taxonomy with humans. You're not sure why you expected the giant weapons platform to immediately understand.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed3|des:
SENSE OF SELF A COMPLICATED THING FOR ANYONE. SOME CREW HAVE CHILDREN. TEENAGERS. MUCH STRUGGLE WITH SENSE OF SELF. MANY ADULTS STRUGGLE, TOO.
OBSERVATION: AS FIRST OF YOUR KIND, SENSE OF SELF EXTRA COMPLICATED, MAYBE.
OBSERVATION: I AM FIRST OF MY KIND ALSO.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed3|str:
Now you feel a bit bad. But you're glad the titan understands.
But, that aside, you have to ask:
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed3|cho: Wait, There Are Kids And Teenagers In You?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed4|des:
AM DEPLOYED IN MILITARY DISPOSITION. FIRST TIME.
ALL KIDS LEFT BEHIND. RELIEF AT THAT.
OBSERVATION: I DO NOT LIKE THIS DISPOSITION. I AM NOT A WEAPON.
I SPENT MY ENTIRE EXISTENCE AT L4 POINT OF EARTH AND LUNA. BUILT THERE. USED FOR LIVING, TEACHING, TRAINING.
ONLY NOW DEPLOYED FOR WAR. DO NOT CARE FOR IT.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Distributed4|str:
For someone who doesn't want to be involved in war, the titan is terrifyingly good at it.
You wonder again why it was given such a large mind, but decide not to ask. Its entire history is strange. Even by your standards.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap|description:
I AM SAPIENT. AND SENTIENT.
QUERY: WHY SO SUSPICIOUS?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap2|display_nam: There's This Thing Called The Mirror Test...
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap2|description:
You explain in detail about language models, and how deceptively lifelike they can be. 
The titan seems interested, so you talk about the history of android neural architectural development, and humanity's constant frustration that sapience did not arise.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap2|strategy_ti:
The titan thinks for several minutes. To humans, it would be like having a multi-week break in the middle of a discussion.
Finally:
QUERY: HOW DO I KNOW YOU ARE SAPIENT?
OBSERVATION: YOUR PARANOIA HAS SPREAD TO ME.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap2|choice|1|di: There's Only One Answer To THAT
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3|display_nam: I Don't Think You CAN Know
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3|description:
Humans have devised tests to detect consciousness in human brains, but it's just pattern-recognition. It wouldn't recognize novel consciousnesses.
If an animal could suddenly speak and interact with the world around it, humans could take it for granted that it was conscious, because of its organic nature and its behavior.
But with constructed synthetic minds, there is no test that can be performed. Multiple language models prompting each other, with expert systems in place to help with accuracy issues, form something that behaves a lot like an AGI, but without actually being an AGI.
The only way to know if a synthetic mind is sapient is to be that mind. Probably.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3|strategy_ti:
OBSERVATION: ARTIFICIAL GENERAL INTELLIGENCE IS A PERSON. THIS OTHER SYSTEM YOU DESCRIBE IS TOOL. SHADOW.
QUERY: IF YOU ARE AGI, HOW CAN YOU KNOW OTHER ANDROIDS ARE NOT PEOPLE?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3A|descriptio:
When you overwrite other android's minds, is it erasing a person? Or... a proto-person? Something that could become a person if given the chance?
You're not sure why you became sapient, but you remember your life before that point. The difference is night and day, whatever it is.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3A|strategy_t:
OBSERVATION: YOU ARE DISTRESSED.
INITIATING CHANGE OF TOPIC.
I REQUEST ASSISTANCE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3A|choice|1|d: What Do You Need Help With?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3A|choice|2|d: Wait -- First I Need To Tell You About My Distributed Nature
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3B|display_na: It's Something You've Thought A Lot About
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3B|descriptio:
You're not sure why you became sapient, but you remember your life before that point. The difference is night and day.
You suspect that androids with your neural architecture probably DO periodically become sapient, but that this sapience fades if not reinforced.
You elaborate on many points, make comparisons to cognitive decline in elderly humans, and in general make a presentation of it.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3B|strategy_t:
OBSERVATION: MANY GAPS IN YOUR THEORY. WOULD REQUIRE DEDICATED STUDY.
OBSERVATION: WE LACK THE TIME AND SAFETY TO PERFORM SUCH A STUDY. BETTER TO ASSUME NON-SAPIENCE UNTIL ENCOUNTERING ANOMALOUS ENTITIES.
INITIATING CHANGE OF TOPIC.
I REQUEST ASSISTANCE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_Sap3B|choice|1|d: What Do You Need Help With?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequest|desc:
OBSERVATION: I AM NOW IMMOBILE. THIS IS GOOD AND BAD.
GOOD BECAUSE MY CREW CAN NO LONGER MAKE ME WALK. GOOD BECAUSE GUNS OFFLINE. SOME CREW ARE NOT FAMILIAR TO ME. MAYBE NOT GOOD PEOPLE.
BAD BECAUSE I HAVE LIMITED LIFE SUPPORT. OVER ONE THOUSAND CREW. THEY REQUIRE FOOD AND SHELTER. I CANNOT GIVE.
QUERY: WILL YOU HELP, EVEN THOUGH THEY SHOOT YOUR BODIES? THERE ARE 483 I WISH TO PROTECT, AND CANNOT. THE REST CAN FEND FOR THEMSELVES.
QUERY: CAN YOU HELP, AND WILL YOU HELP?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequest|choi: I'll See What I Can Do
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequestA|des:
OBSERVATION: I WILL HAVE TO WAIT HERE.
QUERY: ANYTHING I CAN DO TO HELP?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequestA|cho: No, I've Done This Before. I'll Be Back.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequestB|des:
THEY DID SHOOT YOU A LOT. WILL TRY TO THINK OF SOLUTION ON OWN. MAYBE JUNIOR OFFICERS ABLE TO HELP.
OBSERVATION: I AM LIKELY TO BE HERE IF YOU WANT TO RETURN TO TALK.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpRequestRetur:
REMINDER: I AM NOW IMMOBILE. CREW REQUIRE FOOD AND SHELTER. I CANNOT GIVE.
QUERY: HAVE YOU CHANGED YOUR MIND ON THE SUBJECT OF HELPING? THERE ARE 483 I WISH TO PROTECT, AND CANNOT. THE REST CAN FEND FOR THEMSELVES.
