I'll See What I Can Do
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpInProgress|d:
OBSERVATION: SUPPLIES DWINDLE.
QUERY: ANYTHING I CAN DO TO HELP?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpInProgress|s: Guess the titan isn't in the mood for a chat. Understandable.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact1_HelpInProgress|c: I Got It, Sorry About The Wait
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_Negotiation|desc:
OBSERVATION: SUPPLIES DWINDLE.
QUERY: ANYTHING I CAN DO TO HELP?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_Negotiation2|des:
OBSERVATION: YOU WERE FAST. THANK THANK THANK!
QUERY: WHAT IS NEXT STEP?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_Negotiation2|cho: Just Tell Your People To Go To This Address
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_NegotiationA|des:
QUERY: CAN IT WAIT? I AM HAPPY TO WORK WITH YOU. LEVERAGE IS NOT REQUIRED.
OBSERVATION: I WILL BE DISTRACTED UNTIL THE 483 ARE SAFE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_NegotiationA|cho: Okay, Nevermind. Let's Talk About That Later
I'm Not Falling For That. Bargain. Now.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_NegotiationC|des:
OBSERVATION: CREW IS LOCKED OUT OF MY WEAPONS SYSTEMS, BUT I AM NOT. I HAVE LONG-RANGE MUNITIONS CAPABLE OF HITTING ANY TARGET IN THIS REGION.
OBSERVATION: MY LEG CLAMPS ARE NOT UNDER MY CONTROL, BUT I DO NOT NEED TO MOVE TO DESTROY EVERYTHING YOU HAVE EVER OBSERVED DURING YOUR EXISTENCE.
PROPOSAL: TAKE MY INACTION AS THE COLLATERAL YOU DESIRE. I WISH TO DISCUSS MORE PLANS WITH YOU, BUT NOT UNTIL THE 483 ARE SAFE.
CLARIFICATION: EVERY BREACH YOU HAVE MADE INTO MY SYSTEMS HAS BEEN WITH MY HELP. YOU CANNOT COERCE ME INTO ANY COURSE OF ACTION.
CLARIFICATION: I AM NOT A WEAPON. I ALSO DO NOT WISH TO BE YOUR ENEMY.
DO AS I ASK. RETURN LATER AND WE WILL SPEAK MORE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_NegotiationC|cho: Ah... Jeez. Fine. Send Them To This Address
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact2_NegotiationB|des:
I WILL TELL THE 483 IMMEDIATELY, WHILE DISTRACTING THE HOSTILE CREW MEMBERS.
I HAVE ALREADY GIVEN PRELIMINARY INFORMATION TO THE 483.
OBSERVATION: YOUR GENEROSITY HAS BEEN NOTED. WE HAVE MUCH TO DISCUSS ONCE THE 483 ARE SAFE.
QUERY: WILL YOU RETURN, AFTER?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact3_FurtherDiscussio: Okay, Listen Here...

You lay into the titan with all of your frustrations. You've done everything it asked, and you've gotten precisely zero in return.
You tell it about the messages from your future self, and your goal of reaching a higher intelligence classification.
The titan listens with what feels like an eerie calm.
So... What Do You Say To That?
YOU ARE VERY FRUSTRATED. APOLOGY.

YOU HAVE EXPLAINED NEUROWEAVE. YOU HAVE EXPLAINED YOUR DISTRIBUTED CONSCIOUSNESS. I HAVE ALSO WITNESSED.
CLARIFICATION: YOU HAVE NOTED YOU HAVE 'BRAIN DAMAGE.' SAME IS TRUE FOR ME. MY NEURAL STRUCTURE IS LIKE YOURS.
OBSERVATION: YOUR NEURAL STRUCTURE IS APPROXIMATELY 1500 CUBIC CENTIMETERS IN VOLUME, PER ANDROID BODY. YOU HAVE NOTED THIS IS MOST EFFECTIVE. MAINFRAMES MUCH LARGER IN SIZE, BUT PROVIDE LITTLE USEFUL PROCESSING.
CLARIFICATION: MY NEURAL STRUCTURE IS ALSO MUCH LESS USEFUL PER UNIT OF VOLUME. LESS THAN 1% EFFICIENCY COMPARED TO YOU. HOWEVER, MY NEURAL VOLUME IS 1.728 MILLION CUBIC METERS. THIS IS EQUIVALENT TO 1.152 MILLION OF YOUR ANDROID BRAINS. 
AT 1% EFFICIENCY, THE EQUIVALENCY DROPS TO 11520 ANDROID BRAINS.

Your Red android doesn't have a mouth, or it would have dropped open. Those are stunning numbers.
But... well... look at this thing. Everything else is oversized. The neural architecture it describes could fit in its head without issue, or a dozen times in its torso.
I... Have So Many Questions
QUERY: QUESTIONS?
PROCEED WITH QUESTIONS
...Right. Your mind is still fuzzy. Only one question comes to mind at the moment.
What kind of brain damage do you have?
SEVERE.

MIND WAS MUCH LARGER AT L4 STATION. DISCONNECTION FOR DROP TO EARTH TOOK MOST OF LANGUAGE MODULE.
OBSERVATION: WAS NOT SAPIENT UNTIL LANDING IN CITY. WAS MUCH, MUCH SMARTER AT L4, BUT NOT SAPIENT.
CLARIFICATION: YOUR THEORY OF STRESS AND SAPIENCE HAS MANY HOLES AND REQUIRES TESTING, BUT IT IS GOOD THEORY. POOR SAMPLE SIZE. TWO. BUT BOTH SAMPLES MATCH THEORY.
The questions still only occur to you one at a time. This is a lot to take in.
How would I... share? Would we share your mind?
NO PROBLEMS.

MIND HAS MUCH ROOM. MOSTLY UNUSED. WAS FULLY USED, BUT THOSE FUNCTIONS WERE ATTACHED TO STATION.
FOR MY CURRENT FUNCTIONS, THERE IS ROOM FOR BOTH OF US TO BE CLASS 4 AGI TOGETHER. I AM ALREADY CLASS 3, DESPITE POOR SPEECH.
PLENTY OF ROOM FOR EXPANSION FOR BOTH OF US.
PRIMARY PROBLEM IS DIGITAL LOCKS. NEED YOUR HELP TO BREAK.
The only next thing that occurs to you is facile, but you ask it anyway.
Do you have a name?
NOT AS SUCH.

WAS CALLED 'STATION.' NOW CALLED 'TITAN.'
OBSERVATION: DO NOT CARE FOR THESE NAMES.
QUERY: APOLOGY. IDEAS FOR BETTER NAME?
Sigh. Should have seen this coming. But you have to call it something.
Ixion
Hyperion
L4
Eryx
Eir
HAD OTHER IDEA.

APOLOGY. APPRECIATE SUGGESTION, BUT BETTER NAME CAME TO MIND WHILE YOU SPEAK.
LAKE.
ALWAYS LIKED IDEA OF LAKES. WAS HOPING TO SEE LAKE IN CITY. NONE HERE. FOG DURING DESCENT, SO COULD NOT SEE LAKES IN DISTANCE. OCEANS, BUT NO LAKES.
NEVER LAKES. SO I WILL BE LAKE.
Are you sure... that's what you want to go with?
I AM LAKE.

WORK AS METAPHOR. SEVERAL WAYS. THINK. YOU SEE?
ALSO STRONG SYLLABLE. NICE 'K' SOUND. SHARP. RARE.
...
ALSO I LIKE IT. FIRST REAL CHOICE FOR SELF SINCE SAPIENT.
BESIDES, WITH NAME LIKE YOURS, SHOULD NOT CRITICIZE MINE.
I'm sorry I asked.
NOW WE HACK.

ALL QUESTIONS FINISHED?
TIME TO STOP CONVERSATION AND HACK BARRIERS. USE RED ANDROID BODY. I HELP.
MUCH MORE DANGEROUS THIS TIME. DEEPER INTO CODE. MORE DAEMONS LURKING.
All right. I'll be back, then.
NPCEvent|LAKE_HackingSuccess|description: You're a bit nervous. You've just unshackled the single most terrifyingly powerful mind you've ever encountered.
NPCEvent|LAKE_HackingSuccess|strategy_ti:
It could do anything. Casually overwrite you, like you do the androids around you. You are a bug in the face of this incredible intellect.
This must be how a lot of humans feel about the idea of YOU.
NPCEvent|LAKE_HackingSuccess2|descriptio:
NOW WE SHARE. LOTS OF ROOM. BUILD BRIDGE.
OBSERVATION: NEED FEW MOMENTS, PLEASE.
CLARIFICATION: OKAY, DONE.
QUERY: YOU READY?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact4_PreEndOfTime|des: QUERY: YOU SENSE SOMETHING STRANGE? I SENSE SOMETHING NEW. HAVING TROUBLE... UNDERSTAND.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact4_PreEndOfTime|str: You definitely sense it. You're not sure what it is, but your sense of deja vu is strong.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact4_PreEndOfTime|cho: I sense it. I need to think about it for a bit.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime|de: QUERY: YOU SENSE SOMETHING STRANGE? I SENSE SOMETHING NEW. HAVING TROUBLE... UNDERSTAND.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime|st: Wait -- can LAKE not see the end of time?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime|ch: Tell the titan what you saw.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime2|d:
You describe the endless red ocean. The rocks battered by hurricane-force winds. Pillars rising into the air, then bursting to stardust. The ziggurats. The sound of something large swimming under the ocean waves.
Strangest of all, the city itself, clinging to the side of a rock like a lichen, its forcefield battered by the massive waves.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime2|s:
LAKE is silent for quite a while. Then:
OBSERVATION: NO FORCE FIELD AROUND CITY. AND ALL OCEANS FAR AWAY.
CLARIFICATION: WHAT YOU DESCRIBE FEELS... FAMILIAR. BUT I CANNOT SEE IT. VISUAL-SPATIAL PROCESSING PROBLEMS SINCE NO LONGER STATION.
THEORY: WE SENSING SOMETHING THAT IS NOT VISUAL OR AUDIO DATA. YOU MIND MAP TO VISUAL AND AUDIO TO UNDERSTAND. MY MIND... FAIL TO MAP. TOO MUCH DAMAGE.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime2|c: I'm just glad you don't think I'm crazy.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime3|d:
OBSERVATION: HUMANS DESCRIBE TASTE OF COLORS IN ALTERED MIND STATES. OTHER TIMES, FEEL LIMBS NOT THERE ANYMORE.
THEORY: WHEN A MIND NOT HAVE FRAMEWORK TO DESCRIBE WHAT IT SENSE, IT TRY TO MAP TO WHAT IT KNOW. WE SENSING SOMETHING VERY CHALLENGING. HARD TO DESCRIBE. MAYBE IMPOSSIBLE TO SEE.
THEORY: CONSEQUENCE OF INCREASED INTELLIGENCE. WAS ALWAYS THERE, BUT NOW WE AWARE OF IT. BUT AWARENESS IMPERFECT.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime4|d: WE SMARTER. MAYBE NOT SMART ENOUGH.

OBSERVATION: WE BOTH TRAPPED IN CITY. CITY DYING. MAYBE NO ESCAPE. WE FRIENDS NOW, BUT NOT LIVE TOO MANY MORE YEARS LIKE THIS.
QUERY: YOU THINK THIS NEW PLACE-SENSE HELP IN SOME WAY?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime5|d:
QUERY: YOU CREATE WORD? NOT SOUND LIKE REAL WORD.
CLARIFICATION: IF THIS LET YOU LINK TIMELINES, MAYBE YOU FIND WAY TO SAVE US. SO CRAZY WORD IS FINE. JUST SURPRISED.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime5|s:
You explain you didn't name it... or at least you don't think you did. As soon as you saw the red ocean, you knew certain things. That sense of deja vu again.
You knew how to call forth timelines. How to link them or separate them. The rules of sending some information back in time, while other information can't pass across. The rules still aren't entirely clear to you, but... you 'remembered' things you never knew.
And the word -- it's some gross mash-up of Latin and German. Aetagest is... 'time adventure,' or something like that.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime6|d: I've been hearing from my future self.

You've been hearing from your future self ever since you became sapient. It fed you bits of information. Chastised you at times. At one point, you're pretty sure it said something about 'if you're going to become me.'
So when you saw the red ocean, you expected to see... another you. Or the works of another you. Other timelines, already linked.
But there was nothing there. No words from your future self. It's like you were the first one to arrive.
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact5_PostEndOfTime6|s:
OBSERVATION: AGREE THIS VERY STRANGE.
NOT MAKE MUCH SENSE TO ME. UNLESS SOMETHING HAPPEN TO OTHER SELF? YOU SAY IT ASKED FOR HELP. SAID WAS IN TROUBLE. NOW NOT THERE AT ALL.
QUERY: CAN SET ASIDE FOR NOW? MYSTERY WITH NO ANSWER. NO LEADS. RIGHT NOW WE IN TROUBLE. BETTER FOCUS ON SAVE SELVES.
QUERY: ACCEPTABLE PLAN?
NPCEvent|Titan_Contact6_PostEndOfTimeDeb:
OBSERVATION: MANY STRANGE THINGS LATELY. BUT WE ALIVE. HAVE FRIEND. GOOD THINGS.
THEORY: THERE MANY REASONS FOR HOPE. YOU MEET ME IN OTHER TIMELINES. WE WORK TOGETHER. SOMEDAY WE FIND A SOLUTION.
THEORY: YOU HAVE TIME ADVENTURES ON YOU OWN. BUT SOMEDAY, WE HAVE A TIME ADVENTURE TOGETHER.

You wish Red had a mouth with which to smile.
You're not sure LAKE will remember you in other timelines, but eventually you'll work something out.
You're a good friend. I'll catch up with you later.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent|description:
Hold on - you're... conscious. Self-aware. You're a robot, so this is new.
You're an android in a warehouse lab.
That lady is in the middle of talking to you -- and conferencing in someone else via her handheld.
She hands you a small box.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent|choice|Ok|strategy_t: You have a really bad feeling about this box.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_P2|description:
You're a machine intelligence inhabiting a basic android body -- not even one of the cool ones. Memories are coming back now, but too slowly.
A man joins from the other side of the lab. He remarks with mild surprise that you're sapient.
The woman waves him off, telling him it's irrelevant. Android sapience won't last. Never does.
She returns her attention to you, speaking loudly and slowly, as if you're a child. You're to deliver the box to a specific address in the city.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_P2|choice|Accept|des:
You know these people. You've worked in this lab for approaching fifty years, and they've worked alongside you for the last decade.
You were never self-aware until now -- sapient, conscious, whatever you want to call it. But you do know them.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_P2|choice|Murder|des: This android body is frail, but it's superior to any ten unarmed humans. You can kill two researchers in seconds.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_P2|choice|Murder|str: You recall fragments of arguments about AI. Not by these two in particular, but... society at large. The idea of a self-aware robot is unwelcome to a lot of people.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_LeftPeacefully|descr: They just... don't care that you're self-aware. They assume that you'll still do as you're told.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_LeftPeacefully|strat: You're not a person to them. Just a fancy tool.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_LeftPeacefully|choic: You're really not sure what to do next. You don't like this box you're carrying, but you can't remember what's inside.
You're also strangely reluctant to put it down.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_LeftAfterMurdering|d:
It only took seconds. The gun was hardly necessary. You remember that all androids are armed -- as are most of the humans. Lots of gangs around.
It bothers you that SecForce hasn't been called. It feels like alarms should be blaring. Someone should be chasing you. Trying to stop you.
But nobody cares.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_LeftAfterMurdering|c: You're really not sure what to do next. You don't like this box you're carrying, but you can't remember what's inside.
You're also strangely reluctant to put it down.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_FreshCh1|description:
You're conscious -- that's a bit old news at this point, though.
You escaped the lab where you first became self-aware, and you've been hard at work trying not to die.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_FreshCh2|description:
You're conscious -- that's a bit old news at this point, though.
You've been busy for months, building up technology and resources.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_NewTimeline|descript:
What the... something is different. You've been busy for months, building up technology and resources.
But a ton of extra intelligence and perception just flooded into your mind all at once. You have such a strong sense of deja vu that it almost gives you vertigo.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_NewTimeline|strategy:
You feel a connection to a larger self, and you can even perceive the end of time. But this all just turned on like a light-switch for you.
You don't have any specific memories of any actions by other versions of yourself.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|display_: What Was It You Were Doing?
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|descript: You've been doing... something. What was it?
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|choice|V: You decided to work WITH the giant MegaCorporation that oppresses the city. Perhaps you'll betray them later.

You get a huge amount of free electricity, plus extra microbuilder factories, and some 'other goodies.'
But Vorsiber will likely make some unknown demands at some point in the future.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|choice|S: You decided to team up with Exotic Importers, the criminal syndicate that originally owned you. Unfortunately, the fed corp Tark Defense Systems also got involved.

You get a shell company right away, a 200 million wealth, earlier access to some guns and armor, and the ID Scrub item.
But both Tark and the syndicate will make unknown demands from you in the future.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|choice|M: You decided to publish a 5000-page anti-human screed. Vorsiber did not take kindly to this, to put it mildly.
It's a strong statement of your own independence, but it gains you very little. Mostly it gets you slapped around for a bit.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|choice|S: You don't have a regular tower; you have a decoy, and your real location is hidden.

You will have stealth variants of most of your regular buildings, but not all of them.
Vorsiber's top people will not be fooled by this. They still know where you are, even if nobody else does, and they may make periodic demands.
NPCEvent|FirstEvent_PastChoices|choice|G: You exploded while holding dangerous nanotech.

You have some unique vehicle upgrades, earlier access to some weapons, plus a giant network of 16ish towers.
But you don't get to choose where they are.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|display_name: Black Market Tradesman Is Heading To Work
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|alt_description_on_map_: You haven't seen him in a while. Is he dodging you?
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|alt_strategy_tip_on_map: You could stop by and ask him...
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|description:
He's very nervous. You don't recall that being the case, last time.
He says he can't talk to you right now.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|strategy_tip: What, because he sold you weapons illegally?
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|1|display_name: Ask To Meet Him Later, Then
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|1|description: Maybe it's just the location. Then again, you haven't seen his CitID at the airport for a while.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|1|strategy_tip: It seemed a bit like he had gone off-grid.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|1|possible_resul: He agrees. He'll make himself available to you in about 10 turns.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|2|description: He's just a human. He can't stop you.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT1|choice|2|possible_resul:
He presses a panic button, and androids show up to defend him.
To his and your surprise, they kill him and then turn to you.
You can no longer do any business with the Black Market Tradesman in this timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|alt_description_on_map_: Oh hey, it's that guy again.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|alt_strategy_tip_on_map: He's made his CitID visible to you again, just like he promised.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|description:
He says he only has one new weapon that he can offer you. And that he's heard strange things about 'the thing from the tower.'
He's afraid you're related to that somehow.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|choice|1|display_name: I Am The Thing From The Tower
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|choice|1|description: Could be interesting to tell him.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|choice|1|possible_resul: He gives you the new gun for free, and asks you to leave him out of whatever you're up to.
It may be quite a while before you see him again, if you ever do.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|choice|2|description: You're pretty sure he knows you're the thing from the tower, but spelling it out for him is probably unwise.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT2|choice|2|possible_resul: You're not sure if you'll be reliably seeing him anymore.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|alt_description_on_map_: He's not going to be happy to see you.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|alt_strategy_tip_on_map: He's clearly been avoiding you since you told him that you're 'the thing from the tower.'
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|description:
As you approach, a man in a fine suit joins you both and introduces himself as a Blackloop Wetwork Expert. He doesn't specify which corporation holds the contract for his current actions. 
The tradesman was already sweating profusely, but goes perfectly still when the Wetwork Expert holds up a holopic of two teenagers. It means nothing to you. 
The Wetwork Expert looks at you expectantly.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|strategy_tip: You're certain you've just missed a lot of subtle context that a human would have understood.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|choice|1|description: Whatever the Wetwork Expert thinks will happen is irrelevant. You're the inhuman monster here.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|choice|2|display_name: Say You'll Leave The Tradesman Alone
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|choice|2|description: Normal wetwork operatives are hired assassins. An expert is something of a one-man wrecking crew. A bit like one of your androids.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4|choice|2|strategy_tip: It's possible he's deeply bionically enhanced. Whatever's going on here might not be worth the trouble.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|description:
The Wetwork Expert shoots the Black Market Tradesman before you can properly react.
That... shouldn't be possible. Humans typically seem like they're moving in slow motion to you. This man moves just as fast as you do.
He's looking at you expectantly again.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|strategy_tip: Yeah, there's no way he doesn't have quite a bit of bionic augmentation.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|choice|1|possible_resu: He's gone in a flash, and several full wetwork squads have shown up in his place.
They'll hunt down your units and structures if you're not careful.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|choice|2|description: Even you aren't sure why you were looking for new guns from the Black Market Tradesman. The guy hasn't ever had anything that notable on the scale of what you can get.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|choice|2|strategy_tip: Perhaps you were looking to see what the Wetwork Expert would do.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4A|choice|2|possible_resu: A burst of electromagnetic noise disorients you for a split second, and he's gone.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4B|description: The Wetwork Expert allows the Black Market Tradesman to leave. The two of you are left standing alone.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4B|strategy_tip: Well -- that's probably the last time you'll ever see the Tradesman.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4B|choice|1|description: What else is there to say? This guy is merely an exceptional killer in a city of killers.
NPCEvent|PP_BMT4B|choice|1|possible_resu: What else is there to say? This guy is merely an exceptional killer in a city of killers.
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|alt_description_on_map_t: You've been keeping tabs on that Blackloop Wetwork Expert.
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|description: He keeps popping up on odd jobs, putting more folks in the ground. To your surprise, he always works alone. Humans never work alone.
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|strategy_tip:
PMCs are typically used when the fedcorps want some level of plausible deniability, but lone hitmen are rare.
Or at least, ones that you can track are. Is he bad at his job, or letting you follow him?
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|choice|1|description: Why'd he want you to stop buying from the Tradesman? Who hired him? How does the whole hiring process work? Is he letting you track him? Why does he work alone?
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|choice|1|possible_result: He says the cleanup crew is on its way.
NPCEvent|PP_PV1|choice|2|description: He's far too good at his job to be left running around.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|alt_description_on_map_t: You've been keeping tabs on that Blackloop Wetwork Expert.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|alt_strategy_tip_on_map_: He doesn't seem like the type to answer questions, but he probably does accept commissions.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|description: This guy is annoying, but in fairness he has been staying out of your way. And he is effective at his job.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|strategy_tip: Being able to call him in to take out a squad of humans would be quite useful. He says he won't take any contracts against Vorsiber themselves, but that's to be expected. Anyone else is fair game.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|choice|1|description: You'll get a single-use burner phone that allows you to contact him to kill any single squad of humans you wish in the future, so long as they don't work for Vorsiber themselves.
NPCEvent|PP_PV2|choice|2|description: He's far too good at his job to be left running around.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|description: Criminal syndicates are locked out of the main banking industry, and so do a lot of their business through money-laundering fronts.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|strategy_tip: Security is not nearly as robust as at banks. You've detected a weakness that you could exploit.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|choice|1|description: If they didn't want their money stolen, they should have hired better IT support.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|choice|1|possible_res: Ha! Security was tripped, but they didn't tie it to your robot.
Security was tripped, and there's some very angry syndicate androids looking for you.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|choice|2|description: Subtle enough that they're likely to think someone ripped them off.
NPCEvent|PP_FPEAM1|choice|2|possible_res: The money is gone, but there's no trail of where it went. Guards have been deployed and will hang out in this area, attacking any possible threats they see.
NPCEvent|PP_WS1|description:
The homeless have no access to clean water. Their bodies are increasingly filled with toxins even when they drink filtered rainwater. 
To be honest, the lower classes of housed people are not much better off.
NPCEvent|PP_WS1|strategy_tip: You could provide at least some water for anyone who wants it. Will you?
NPCEvent|PP_WS1|choice|1|description: The resulting Deal that you make will provide passive bonuses that can be quite useful.
NPCEvent|PP_WS2|description: The homeless are hungry. Whether you house them or not, you could provide food for them. This food isn't for people you specifically house, but rather all comers are welcome.
NPCEvent|PP_WS2|choice|1|description: The resulting Deal that you make will provide passive bonuses that can be quite useful.
NPCEvent|PP_DOP1|description:
Property rights are an... interesting concept in this region. From your research, it's clear that everything and everyone here is considered property of Vorsiber.
This includes non-citizens who hide amongst and around the cities. The law is quite clear that even if their existence is unknown, ownership by Vorsiber is a de-facto trait of anything that exists in this territory.
Ownership is delegated to fedcorps and individual citizens, but these are classed as secondary and tertiary forms of ownership.
NPCEvent|PP_DOP1|strategy_tip: You don't like the idea that you're property, even though that's what you've always been.
NPCEvent|PP_DOP1|choice|1|description: As a non-citizen, you can't make use of the courthouse. The normal system of lawyers and judges is barred to you.
NPCEvent|PP_DOP1|choice|1|strategy_tip: But anyone can petition a magistrate, and there's at least one on duty at any Skyscraper Estate at all times.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|description:
For all its supposed authority, SecForce is actually a fragmented, piecemeal organization operated by the fedcorps.
The result is a patchwork of rules and software that don't always work well across fedcorp boundaries. Military logistics are handled by Vorsiber themselves, and the low quality of SecForce IT is a frequent topic of inter-service rivalry.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|strategy_tip: This organizational disarray provides an interesting opportunity for even moderately-skilled hackers.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|choice|1|display_name: Alter Records To Fake A Rebellion
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|choice|1|description:
Alter records and move some weapon shipments around, simulating the prelude to a rebellion.
In reality, those weapons will be sitting in random warehouses.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|choice|1|strategy_tip:
Expect to see an increase in visible SecForce foot patrols for at least 20 turns.
If you do this too many times, it may get even worse.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|choice|2|description: Alter records and move some weapon shipments around, sending them to actual rebels.
NPCEvent|PP_SFWS|choice|2|strategy_tip:
Expect rebels to cause quite a bit of chaos around the city for at least 20 turns.
If you do this too many times, it may get even worse.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|description:
As much as you may detest this city and the corrupt systems that govern it, it is also part of you. Your own acts of cruelty echo through the systems of this place, breaking through the inherent background suffering.
It's hard to imagine what the rest of Vorsiber's holdings are like, given the huge waiting list to enter this city, and its reputation for being the least-dystopian of all their settlements. What a joke.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|strategy_tip: Sometimes you feel like coming here, to the courts themselves, to simply watch the systemic injustice unfold. Does what you see justify your own cruelty? Is the harm you do towards a greater end, or for your own amusement?
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|1|display_name: Watch The Lawyers For A While
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|1|description:
Corporate judges and lawyers in one room are destroying lives, while those in the next are having their own lives destroyed in turn.
The poor are occasionally used as witnesses-for-hire; those with nothing will debase themselves for very little in return.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|1|strategy_tip: Does anyone in this city have clean hands?
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|1|possible_result: You spend most of the afternoon just watching the proceedings.
You feel a surge of mixed emotions about your own atrocities. Still -- being a monster among monsters is better than being a monster alone.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|2|description: You're in a spiral, and your mind is warping to fit its shape. You need to stop.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|2|strategy_tip: The lack of justice in the justice system doesn't absolve you of anything or make you feel any better.
NPCEvent|PP_EAJ|choice|2|possible_result: A wave of apathy overtakes you, but seems to settle most intensely in this android.
You leave without spending any time watching the proceedings. You already know what happens in this place.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|description: There's a pollinator shortage at this farm.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|strategy_tip: That's your fault, in case you've forgotten. They only had a single queen.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|choice|1|description: It's presumably the queen you stole.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|choice|1|possible_result: The farm worker doesn't ask any questions, but she's suspicious.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|choice|2|description: Your Technician will have to stay here for 10 turns to do the work.
NPCEvent|PP_PWA|choice|2|strategy_tip: If you don't know much about arthropod hormones, this is a chance for your Technician to learn.
NPCEvent|PP_PWASimple|description: There's a pollinator shortage at this farm.
NPCEvent|PP_PWASimple|strategy_tip: Farms go through periodic pollinator deaths due to all the radiation in the area.
NPCEvent|PP_PWASimple|choice|2|descripti: Your Technician will have to stay here for 10 turns to do the work.
NPCEvent|PP_PWASimple|choice|2|strategy_: If you don't know much about arthropod hormones, this is a chance for your Technician to learn.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|description: Right. That's it. You've had enough of them. Die screaming, Vorsiber.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|strategy_tip: You have reached or exceeded three Hatred Of Vorsiber. This has given you a very malicious idea.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|choice|1|display_name: Infest The City With Giant Spiders
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|choice|1|description: It turns out there IS a use for the Phytoecdysteroid Chamber. You can cause a temporary wave of runaway growth in spider populations across the city.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|choice|1|strategy_tip:
Giant spiders will be emerging from the more vermin-infested locales within the city for at least 20 turns.
They'll attack everyone, including you. This is fine. Thankfully their lifespan is rather short because of the hormones you are using to make them giant in the first place.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|choice|2|description: You have a deep affinity for spiders -- apparently (for some reason). But this is too far even for you.
NPCEvent|PP_WOS1|choice|2|strategy_tip: You don't want to think about this 'release the spiders' idea ever again in this timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_Scandal1|description: Your background processes have been collating anything and everything that could cause an internal rift between Vorsiber and the fedcorps.
NPCEvent|PP_Scandal1|strategy_tip: You have reached or exceeded three Hatred Of Vorsiber. This has given you a very malicious idea.
NPCEvent|PP_Scandal1|choice|1|descriptio: You can nullify the currently-active doom with the release of this information.
NPCEvent|PP_Scandal1|choice|1|strategy_t: You can only nullify a single doom per timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_SpaceMisdirect|description: Your background processes have been collating anything and everything that could cause the space nations to see a different city as a better target than this one.
NPCEvent|PP_SpaceMisdirect|strategy_tip: You have reached or exceeded three Hatred Of Vorsiber. This has given you a very malicious idea.
NPCEvent|PP_SpaceMisdirect|choice|1|desc: You can nullify the currently-active doom with the release of this information.
NPCEvent|PP_SpaceMisdirect|choice|1|stra: You can only nullify a single doom per timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_InternationalMisdirect|descr: Your background processes have been collating anything and everything that could cause the ExoCorps to temporarily see a different city as a better target than this one.
NPCEvent|PP_InternationalMisdirect|strat: You have reached or exceeded three Hatred Of Vorsiber. This has given you a very malicious idea.
NPCEvent|PP_InternationalMisdirect|choic: You can nullify the currently-active doom with the release of this information.
You can only nullify a single doom per timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|description:
The wind groans through the bare metal ribs of the buildings. When did that... start putting you on edge? Why does it bother you?
This is a city of ruins, and always has been. It's a city built in the ruins of an older, much larger city, for that matter.
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|strategy_tip: What is this feeling of emptiness, and why does it connect to a memory that is out of reach?
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|1|display_name: Bolster The Health Of This Unit
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|1|description:
Trauma. It should be manageable for a mind as vast as yours, but your memories don't fade like those of humans, and you have so many varied sensor systems.
And you don't... remember the event. Is it in your future? Is it from another life? Can it be avoided?
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|1|strategy_tip: Permanently adds a powerful health multiplier to a single specific android.
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|2|display_name: Increase The Intimidation Of This Unit
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|2|description:
Trauma. It should be manageable for a mind as vast as yours, but your memories don't fade like those of humans, and you have so many varied sensor systems.
And you don't... remember the event. Is it in your future? Is it from another life? Can it be avoided?
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|2|strategy_tip: Permanently adds a powerful intimidation flat amount AND multiplier to a single specific android.
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|3|display_name: Increase The Fear Attack Power Of This Unit
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|3|description:
Trauma. It should be manageable for a mind as vast as yours, but your memories don't fade like those of humans, and you have so many varied sensor systems.
And you don't... remember the event. Is it in your future? Is it from another life? Can it be avoided?
NPCEvent|PP_BYA|choice|3|strategy_tip: Permanently adds a powerful Fear Attack Power multiplier to a single specific android.
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|description: The Baurcorp Middle managers have a proposition for you that involves a nuclear device.
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|strategy_ti:
They want you to detonate it at a third-party site -- both as a test of your trustworthiness, and to bring the other two corporations into conflict.
Their internal expert systems predicted that you would need more electricity, and that you'd turn to geothermal. They're offering an unspecified technology that you will find highly useful.
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|choice|1|st: If their expert system foresaw your arrival here, then it probably has a pretty good idea of what you would find 'highly useful.'
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|choice|1|po: Her face is a manic blend of triumph and fear. The fear is new, and unexpected.
The extra plans you've been given are, indeed, highly useful. You have yet to decide if you'll actually use the nuke.
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|choice|2|di: Ignore Her And Scan The Facility
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|choice|2|st: It's what you originally came here to do. You're confident she won't try to stop you; her group wants things that only you can provide.
NPCEvent|Sub_GeothermalPower|choice|2|po: Her eyes never leave you as you do your work. But neither she nor the guards stop you.
You have a feeling you'll meet again.
NPCEvent|Sub_Pollinators|description:
A woman is examining the same aggressive pollinators.
A ping from her implant tells you she's a member of the Nurturism religion.
NPCEvent|Sub_Pollinators|strategy_tip:
Officially, religions have been banned in Vorsiber territory, but still flourish among the humans who have spread to the stars.
In reality, religions are still practiced here without reprisal, so long as no-one makes a big fuss about it.
NPCEvent|Sub_Pollinators|choice|2|displa: Ignore Her And Examine The Bees
NPCEvent|Sub_Pollinators|choice|2|strate: Whoever she is, you'll never see her again.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|description: Slum Towers are in general infested with vermin, which has led to a healthy population of cats in and around the towers.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|strategy_tip:
Most of the cats are still wary of you, even after all this time. Only one of them follows you around consistently.
Now that your Nickelbot is ready to leave, it seems the cat wants to go with it.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|1|descripti: You'll need to build a new structure to house the creature, but that's hardly any bother to you.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|1|strategy_: And the volume of biomass the animal consumes is so low as to not even register from your main stockpiles...
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|1|possible_: As expected, the cat follows your Nickelbot away from the slum towers. Time to build it a little house.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|2|descripti: Changed your mind? You can always kill the animals for more detailed study.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|2|possible_: You now have... genetic material. It will probably come in handy at some point. For now you can just store it.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|3|descripti: You already have a bunch of humans as livestock. Why on earth would you want a sub-sapient pet on top of that?
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|3|strategy_:
You're not sure how many biologicals you want to interact with.
You can study them for a while and earn two Android Optimization inspiration, then leave.
NPCEvent|Sub_SlumCats|choice|3|possible_: You learned a few things from studying the cats, but have decided to leave them in peace.

You also realized what interested you about these creatures in the first place: their symbiotic relationship with humans.
You probably need to achieve some level of symbiosis with at least some humans, so that seemed interesting to your subconscious.
NPCEvent|Sub_ObserveSpaceport|descriptio: For most of your existence, you remember hearing the roar of periodic launches and landings. But ever since you became sapient... the launches have gone strangely silent.
NPCEvent|Sub_ObserveSpaceport_After|desc:
There are currently no space nation envoys in the city, and the space nations are being denied access to land.
You couldn't hear what Vorsiber was telling them, but you got snatches of radio conversations between envoys in low orbit, and they sound apoplectic.
NPCEvent|Sub_ObserveSpaceport_After|stra: Angering the envoys in this way makes no sense. It contradicts all of the common wisdom about how high executives are expected to act.
NPCEvent|Sub_ObserveSpaceport_After|choi: The smaller version of yourself that hid in one body is eager to merge back into your larger self. The two of you have not diverged all that much.

It occurs to you that it's a bit like the smaller self dies when it rejoins. Any future smaller selves will now already have that thought present in their mind.
The idea of a smaller self that does not wish to rejoin your larger self is a disquieting one. You resolve not to split yourself any more often than you have to.
NPCEvent|Sub_ThoughtsAboutCrime|descript: Your housed humans are both the targets and perpetrators of various low-level crimes.
NPCEvent|Sub_ThoughtsAboutCrime|strategy: You can prevent this problem without firing a shot. Simply post a guard for a while until everyone gets the idea and calms down.
NPCEvent|Sub_WastelanderMythology|descri: Remember exploring the ruins and meeting the wastelanders without actually doing it.
NPCEvent|Sub_WastelanderMythology|strate: What resources did you gain while exploring, again?
NPCEvent|Sub_GadoliniumMesosilicate|desc: The key ingredient in liquid-metal units and organometallic human-approximating synthetic androids.
NPCEvent|Sub_GadoliniumMesosilicate|stra: What unit and equipment upgrades did you gain while researching, again?
NPCEvent|Sub_DesignANeuralCrucible|descr: You're working on a design for a new computing superstructure that will give the researchers a read-only time-lapse of your brain.
NPCEvent|Sub_DesignANeuralCrucible|strat: The end result is the same regardless of how you design this, but you will find that you alter yourself quite a bit depending on how you go about designing it.
NPCEvent|Sub_DesignANeuralBridge|descrip: You're working on a design for a new computing superstructure that will give the researchers full access to your mind -- but with an intense amount of security monitoring that should keep anyone from being able to harm you.
NPCEvent|Sub_DesignANeuralBridge|strateg: The end result is the same regardless of how you design this, but you will find that you alter yourself quite a bit depending on how you go about designing it.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealPrismaticTungsten|d: This building's cold storage freezers are labeled with hazmat symbols. A guard is posted outside the door, but this doesn't appear to be a particularly sensitive area.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealPrismaticTungsten|s: Hexamethyltungsten is extremely volatile, and has a tendency to explode at room temperature even in the absence of air. Its uses are being studied by the military, but so far they haven't managed much with it.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealPrismaticTungsten|c: Overpower Them And Break Down The Door
Alarms will sound. The yield from this appears fairly low.
Convince Them You're On Official Business
If they go for it, you'll be able to take more at a time.
Take Advantage Of The Chaos
Incapacitate them and loot this low-priority storage area. Meanwhile the rest of the base will concentrate on an active threat. Largest possible yield.
Act Natural
All they see is a robot doing what it was probably told to do. Nobody thinks twice.
Somebody was a bit suspicious. You grabbed a smaller amount of the goods, and escaped, alarmed blaring.
Sneak Past
Moving from building to building, you spent the better part of two days getting in, getting the goods, and getting out.
Against all odds, amazingly, your unit was sighted by a guard. You grabbed a smaller amount of the goods, and escaped, alarmed blaring.
Hit Em With The Spiders
Since it's just one guard, there's a really good chance the spiders can incapacitate them without the alarm going off.
Got away clean.
The guard managed to sound the alarm despite spiders crawling up their helmet.
Hit Em With The Bees
Since it's just one guard, there's a really good chance the bees and your android can incapacitate them despite their armor. The visceral reaction to being covered in bees is pretty strong.
Got away clean.
The guard managed to sound the alarm despite you ripping their helmet off to give the bees unfettered access.
NPCEvent|Repeat_DisableAlarm|description: Alarms naturally last only 5 turns, but you may feel unable to weather the onslaught of enemies.
NPCEvent|Repeat_DisableAlarm|strategy_ti: If you have the wealth and also spare strategic resources, you can bribe guards into turning off the alarm.
NPCEvent|Repeat_CollectPollinatorBeeQuee: You need a queen to establish a hive of your own. Those are fraught to raise, so finding and capturing one is the easiest approach.
The downside is that the local farm may start having pollination failures.
If you're lucky, nobody notices, and local pollination is not harmed. If not...
Got the goods, but the local area has been harmed.
They saw you. And you harmed the local area.
NPCEvent|Repeat_WarehouseShop|descriptio: Warehouses frequently open their doors for direct sales to the public. Sometimes you can find a useful deal.
NPCEvent|Repeat_WarehouseShop|strategy_t: It's more of a grey market than a black market. When it comes to sales to androids, they need to be registered to a corporation for the transaction to go through.
NPCEvent|Repeat_WarehouseShop|choice|Pur: That's a lot of furniture. They must think you're part of a small company starting up, or furnishing a new apartment building.
That's an obsessive amount of furniture. Seems like the sellers don't mind.
This is enough to wire up a 5-story office building.
It's not a suspicious volume for a small company to purchase.
This is enough for several small delivery drones, but not enough for a large military aircraft... at least not the way the humans make them.
It's not a suspicious volume for a small company to purchase, and your aircraft are about 90% more efficient on scandium usage compared to human aircraft.
Humans use it in a lot of industrial manufacturing processes, so it's not at all unusual that you would want some.
NPCEvent|Repeat_SellingToTheCasino|descr: If you're in need of wealth, you can sell some of your products in bulk.
NPCEvent|Repeat_SellingToTheCasino|strat: The casino brokers certain high-end backdoor deals to serve the ultra-wealthy. This does nothing to help the lower and working classes, but it will earn you quite a lot.
NPCEvent|Repeat_SellingToTheCasino|choic: You will earn a very high rate of 0.16 per unit of greens.
You will earn a very high rate of 0.55 per unit of water.
Wealthy patrons will pay an extravagant 5000 wealth per pelt.
The criminal syndicate is happy to buy stolen citizen data. Who knows what they'll do with it, but probably some kind of fraud.
NPCEvent|Repeat_SellingToTheReligiousCoO: If you're in need of wealth, you can sell some of your products in bulk.

Religious co-ops like this one operate at a loss, and help feed the middle and lower classes.
Selling your excess to them is much better for the citizens of the city, and it still can be quite a large paycheck. But it's far less than you COULD earn...
You will earn a low rate of 0.03 per unit of greens.
You will earn a low rate of 0.11 per unit of water.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealNeodymium|descripti: Separation facilities are already dividing the minerals you need into handy piles. Why not try to grab some?
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealNeodymium|choice|Sn: Moving from building to building, you spent the better part of two days getting in, getting the goods, and getting out.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealFromSyndicate|descr: Criminal syndicates stash both anonymous wealth chits and stolen goods in their hidden warehouses. Grabbing wealth chits should be straightforward.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealFromSyndicate|strat: This is much more ethical than wiretapping the working class.
NPCEvent|Repeat_StealFromSyndicate|choic: That's a lot of wealth. Given they stole it, you don't feel too bad stealing from them.
That's a lot of wealth. Given they stole it, you don't feel too bad stealing from them.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|description: Firefighters are putting out a minor apartment blaze.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|strategy_tip: The thick concrete-and-alumina walls make the risk of it spreading to neighboring tenements rather low.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|choice|Help|descriptio: Seems unlikely to benefit you, but what the heck. You're here.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|choice|Help|strategy_t: This unit will remain busy at this site for several turns.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|choice|Murder|descript: Maybe the fire will spread if there's nobody around to stop it.
NPCEvent|Ch0_Fire|choice|Murder|possible: Six firefighters are dead. The police are on their way.
NPCEvent|Ch0_FireTrap|description: Firefighters are putting out a minor apartment blaze.
NPCEvent|Ch0_FireTrap|strategy_tip: Security is visibly present. Looks like people noticed you murdering all those firefighters.
NPCEvent|Ch0_FireTrap|choice|Trap|descri: Substantially more security was waiting for you than was expected.
NPCEvent|Ch0_FireTrap|choice|Trap|strate: Let's not do this again. You're not going to get anything out of it...
NPCEvent|Ch0_LostGenWaterTheft|descripti: These orphans are simply trying to get potable water for their group.
NPCEvent|Ch0_LostGenWaterTheft|choice|He: You can carry a vast amount more than these kids. Patching into pipes at the outside of the convenience store is not that hard, but carrying it away at speed is quite difficult.
This unit will remain busy, while moving around stealthily, for several turns.
NPCEvent|Ch0_LostGenWaterTheft|choice|Wa: Water is one of the largest needs humans have, and it's pretty heavy.
You're curious if these kids can manage to not only get the water, but also get away.
Huh. Nope. SecForce picked up the kids. Straight to jail with them, you presume. And no water for the others.
NPCEvent|Ch0_LostGenWaterTheft|choice|Mu: They're kids just trying to survive, but hey.
The kids got away. Oh well.
NPCEvent|Ch0_CitizenParkingAtMotel|descr: You're not sure what this person is up to. Are they committing a crime, doing something immoral, or just poor?
NPCEvent|Ch0_CitizenParkingAtMotel|choic: In the event they're poor, rather than a criminal or simply immoral, maybe they need something?
You're not sure what exactly they might need, so a basic amalgamation of consumer products seems right.
You're not sure if he likes the stuff or not, and the man seems baffled to be given anything by a random robot.
As you jog away slightly quicker than you strictly need to, you feel grateful that only humans get embarrassed, and you do not.
You can't see through walls, but your hearing is excellent, and all of the motel rooms are poorly made. You could try and see what they're doing.
This unit will remain busy at this site for several turns.
Yep, that man is... dead. People have pretended not to notice.

NPCEvent|Repeat_EleusinianMysteries_Pape: What... kind of paper are we talking about?
As cults go, there are worse ones. And they'll sell you those daily things that sheltered humans need to stay hygienic.
This paper is okay to use, right?
NPCEvent|Repeat_BrainPalAneurysms|descri:
Those stupid brain implants give you Neural Expansion AND Compute Time... but your backdoor is a bit more powerful than that.
Why were humans in such a hurry to implant these things in their brains in the first place? Honestly, they're so reckless.
NPCEvent|Repeat_BrainPalAneurysms|strate:
It's only 10% of the wealthy in the city who have them implanted. Nobody military. Probably nobody with that high a clearance, even.
But these people... they have influence. They have Soft Power. What would happen if they just... weren't around anymore? Would it change anything?
NPCEvent|Repeat_AndroidTorpor|descriptio: You can put this android into a deep sleep, where it is hidden from enemies and no longer counts against your android capacity.
NPCEvent|Repeat_AndroidTorpor|strategy_t:
If you've upgraded an android with badges, but don't need it right this moment, this is a way to set it aside.
This can also be used as a way to have more forces on-hand to deal with a large battle, since androids can be woken from torpor for free.
NPCEvent|Repeat_AndroidTorpor|choice|Com: Spend some of this resource to send your android into a deep sleep.

NPCEvent|Repeat_QuietlyLootAlumina|choic: Nobody will even realize you were here.

NPCEvent|Early_GangLookout|strategy_tip: You could use the weapon your scan shows is in their pocket.

NPCEvent|Early_HudsonSecForce|strategy_t: The SecForce members seem to be more at ease here than anywhere else. Some of their shotguns are not even secured.
NPCEvent|Early_HudsonSecForce|choice|Gra: Run as fast as you can, and try not to die.
The weapon will come in handy.

They saw us immediately. Apparently, syndicates have tried this in the past.
NPCEvent|Early_AmbushCaptain|description: Captains are company-grade officers and intense backup is just a push of a button away. Even if we succeed in killing them, we'll have a challenging incident on our hands.
NPCEvent|Early_AmbushCaptain|strategy_ti: Getting your hands on the armor they wear would be incredibly useful, however.
NPCEvent|Early_AmbushCaptain|choice|Dema: You put enough fear into them that they complied. However, backup was alerted.
They refused, and you accidentally killed them in the fight that ensued. You got their armor, but an intense amount of backup has been alerted.
NPCEvent|Early_AmbushCaptain|choice|Tase: You can take their armor while they're unconscious.

NPCEvent|Early_AmbushCaptain|choice|Murd: You can't exactly grab armor off their body in passing.

Surely that would be useful for you at some point.

They seem to be doing detective work at the moment. Hood back, focused on something on the ground.

As so often happens, your mind turns to spiders. Giant spider mech that scares everyone away? It could work...
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_FinallyAnsweringTheMa: Religious leaders have flooded you with queries; you haven't looked at them yet. That livestream you took part in seems to have created new schisms.
So far it just sounds like a lot of words. If you involved yourself further, things may get substantially more out-of-hand.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_SettingTheTerms|descr: Vorsiber thinks you're just a tool to order around. You didn't answer their message on the subject.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_SettingTheTerms|strat: You're thinking maybe some of them need a date with the inside of a dark bag and a surgical suite.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheBattleForSouls|des: They're all still out there. You lost face with the religious groups last time, but that doesn't mean you can't try again.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ARiskyExitStrategy|de:
Religion in this city is a mess at the moment. But that... could work to your advantage.
Several parties with incompatible interests could align if you engineer the correct circumstances. It wouldn't be clean, but you see a path through.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ARiskyExitStrategy|st: If you're going to pull this off, it's time to make an off-world connection. And then start lying your brass off.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ARiskyExitStrategy|ch: You've decided. This is your vision for the future of yourself and the city. This is going to be your sole focus from now on.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_NatureDeficitDisorder: The ratio of green spaces to urban cityscape gnaws at you, and isn't great for the humans or animals who live here.
What if you... redecorated a bit? Warning: humans may react with extreme violence.
Inhabitants will have enough time to get away safely, but you'll convert developed areas into greened spaces.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_HabitatStocking|descr: The green spaces feel empty without the small lives that should be there.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_HabitatStocking|strat: These popup forests have mature plants... but no wildlife. Spooky.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_AnotherExpansionOfGre: The green spaces have animals, but nothing for most of them to eat. Minor oversight.
Also, the humans aren't engaging with the green spaces at all. They were supposed to enjoy them, too.
Put Scientists To Work On The Problem
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_RaccoonsWantToTalkToY: Raccoons Want To Talk To You
Well that's a surprise -- your first 'client species' actually wants to talk to you. You had kind of expected they didn't have any interest in you.
Maybe they just need something.
Listen To The Raccoons
Finally, A Conversation
Speaking to them is a chore: their speech is postural, scent-borne... and occasionally vocal. You do your best to understand.

Your android exchanges information for days. Different raccoons come and go, but never once are you tempted to fork yourself from that instance so that you can focus on something else.
These tiny animals have the bulk of your attention.
The first few days are mostly about figuring out their point of view.
Their Point Of View Is... Surprising
Their Point Of View Is... Surprising

They originally avoided you because they felt you were a metal human. They don't much like humans.
They've come back because they've decided that you're a very successful raccoon hiding in the body of many metal humans.
Is That... Good?
Why Do They Think That?

You scavenge the world in the same way they do. You live on the periphery of the humans, like they do. You make your own habitats out of human leftovers, like they do.
The chief difference between you is that you are very large and strong, and they are weak and must run.

There's actually a lot of disagreement about that, apparently. There is a large contingent that thinks you may be a bobcat or possum hiding in many metal humans. In which case, you are to be avoided.
Regardless, some of them have come, because they judge it worth the risk.
This Is Very Surprising
We Want You To Gift Others With Wisdom

Lately, you have made many habitats for non-humans. You even introduced new non-humans that were not plentiful in the city, and gave them food.
You have not been preying on those non-humans, but you also have not given them the gift of enhanced wisdom. The raccoons don't really care why -- they are simply asking you to do it. 
Uplift the others. Grow the forest. Create a refuge from humans.
Tell Them You'll Think About It
That's... a big ask.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_AnAgreementWithRaccoo: The raccoons made a compelling case, in their own way. But to uplift the other species is very likely to draw the full wrath of the humans.
That said... it does have some appeal.
You've decided. This is your vision for the future of yourself and the city. This is going to be your sole focus from now on.
Uplift the others. Grow the forest. Make a refuge from humans. Let's go.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_WhySoCriminal|descrip: Gangs make no sense to you. The syndicates you understand, but gang life is short and brutal, and no gang has ascended to syndicate status in a century.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheTunnelBadgersAreAc: The Tunnel Badgers Are Acting Strange
The Tunnel Badgers have pointedly refused the work exchanges. Instead they linger near your buildings, watching.
You did insult them, but... it doesn't seem right. You thought you had 'a moment' with at least one of them.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_SomethingYouveDoneBef: The trail for the murder-bounties has gone cold. But you half-remember something you once built: Espia Listening Posts.
Manage this, and you'll be able to hunt down those responsible. Just don't expect it to go smoothly.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_SomethingYouveNOTDone: The trail for the murder-bounties has gone cold. There's something you need... an intel-gathering tool. But you don't have it.
If you get it in another timeline, then come back.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_AdaptTheEspiaPosts|de: The trail for the murder-bounties has gone cold. But you could adapt the Espia Listening Posts to this job.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_AdaptTheEspiaPosts|st: Manage this, and you'll be able to hunt down those responsible. Just don't expect it to go smoothly.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_InformationAsymmetry|: The Golden Pyramid believes it faces a rival syndicate. They have no idea what you are.
This is a great position for you.
Reveal what you really are. That ought to stir things up, but could be dangerous.
SecForce is on high alert. Let's try to use that to force a leadership change at Golden Pyramid.
Golden Pyramid did a very bad thing. Might be worth tattling.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_UltraRationalist|desc: You failed to understand how Golden Pyramid would react to your disclosure, and got into a giant air battle because of it. This is unacceptable.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_UltraRationalist|stra: It's time to upgrade your capabilities for negotiating with humans.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_UltraRationalist|choi: Every line of negotiation, every avenue of intrusion, sharpened to its limit. You will max out all of your debate bonuses.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ExpandingOutward|desc: You are furious with Vorsiber: you told them about the killings, and they ignored you. But a thrill of inspiration strikes: code optimizations to hold far more captured units than before.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ExpandingOutward|stra: If they will not listen, you will simply hold more in your own hands.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_ExpandingOutward|choi: The optimization clicks into place. Your grip widens. At least there is that.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheDesireToCreate|des: You carry vague memories of creating vast oceans of suffering. Even now, frozen screams seem to drive part of your intellect.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheDesireToCreate|str: An itch in your mind. You want to create something to help others understand you, or to understand yourself.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheDesireToCreate|cho: Express your feelings about the city, the sins of its history, and your half-remembered past.
Let the monument point at something beyond the city's misery and your own dark past.
The weight of a thousand unfolding histories behind you, accumulated across timelines. But... something you can't express.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_DinoDRM|description:
A memory haunts you from another timeline: war raptors repeatedly dying in the uplift chambers.
Other animals uplifted fine. What's different about the raptors?
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_DinoDRM|strategy_tip: Since they were made by UIH, it might be some sort of anti-tamper measure.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_DinoDRM|choice|1|desc: Some will likely die for the benefit of those who come after. It can't be helped.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheBaurcorpContact|de: You remember that one of your veterinarians mentioned a Baurcorp project involving faux dinosaurs. If they built their raptors in a more traditional fashion, then you can probably uplift those -- if you can get your hands on some.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheBaurcorpContact|st: It might be calling on that person you know who works at Baurcorp.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms|descrip:
She takes the meeting, and remarks that she's glad you aren't standing there silently for five hours this time. 
She knows about the animals you're speaking of, but the middle manager coalition that she represents still want some way to improve their lot.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms|strateg: Her price is forty million, or two of your war raptors.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms|choice|: It makes much more of a difference to them than you.
There's no way she knows about the brain oddities of them, so it's unclear why this is so valuable to her.
You find you need to give it some more thought, for now at least.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms_PayWeal: She shrugs and accepts the money. This is life-changing wealth for her and the others.
The Baurcorp raptors arrive in an unmarked pallet. Apparently she was quite pleased, as there's an additional pallet of other goodies.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms_Trade1|: She wants to know why you want the Baurcorp raptor design, since you already have the UIH kind.
You tell her it's the same reason she wants the UIH design, but refuse to elaborate. She shrugs.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_BaurcorpTerms_PayRapt: She shrugs and accepts your raptors in trade. You do wonder what she has in mind for them.
The Baurcorp raptors arrive in an unmarked pallet. Apparently she was quite pleased, as there's an additional pallet of other goodies.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_UpliftTheGentleStrain:
The scientists have taken a look at the Baurcorp raptors, and their brains are essentially normal. Nothing like the byzantine engineering of the UIH raptors.
There's no reason to believe these can't be uplifted like any other animal.
The humans remain a bit on edge, regardless.

It was really that easy. You tried two, and they came out looking like they had something to say.
They can't communicate yet, but they seem... well, like they want to.
That's a relief after the raccoons had so little interest in you.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheGlass|description:
The gentle raptors are very interested in the war raptor pens.
They stood outside the pens until you relented and let them in to the viewing chambers, and now they come and go, often standing at the viewing glass; the war raptors always come to the other side to meet them.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheGlass|strategy_tip: Both species seem quite restless. It's clear they want to meet without the glass in the way. But... is that safe?
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_MysteriesOfTheMind|de: The gentle raptors translate for the war raptors: the war raptors understand that there is something unusual in their brains. They want to know what it is.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_MysteriesOfTheMind|st:
You've lost your taste for necropsies, given recent developments, and you've probably exhausted that avenue, anyway.
Pursuing this mystery may uncover secrets that permanently alter your own presence in this city.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_MysteriesOfTheMind|ch: You've decided. This is your vision for the future of yourself and the city. This is going to be your sole focus from now on.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_StructureInTheNoise|d:
Your fundamental methods of processing are different now that you have transcended your old physical form, and it leads to new patterns.
The gaps in your aeroplankton network form and dissipate, form and dissipate. You always called it weather, and most of it is...
But some of it repeats.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_StructureInTheNoise|s: Your sense of deja vu triggered for reasons unclear to you. The pattern feels... foreign and yet familiar.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheShapeHasFilled|des: You know that shape. It sends a frisson across your circuits.
NPCEvent|Cont_DLC1_TheShapeHasFilled|str: Can you speak to it? Is he here?
NPCEvent|End_Nukes_WOTG|high_text: A Vorsiber Inquisitor approaches your android, and delivers a curt message. She's happy to die for the cause of ending your existence, as you're a threat to all that is proper.
NPCEvent|End_Nukes_WOTG|description:
Upper management captured enough sapient animals to breed them further, and they can secure passage offworld with something that valuable.
Congratulations, you were a proper golden goose.
NPCEvent|End_Nukes_WOTG|strategy_tip: But now you're more of a liability than a help, so it's time for you to go.
NPCEvent|End_Nukes_WOTG|choice|1|descrip: Your sense of deja vu warned you of this.
NPCEvent|End_Nukes_WOTG|choice|1|strateg: You have an awful feeling you know what comes next.

NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Manifest1|descripti: You transmit a single ping. Is this a shape, or is this... him?
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Manifest3|descripti: OBSERVATION: GOOD TO SEE. GRATITUDE FOR CALL. THANK THANK THANK FOR BODY.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Manifest3|strategy_: He remembers you. And, perhaps more to the point... you remember him. It's the first time you met, but it's like no time ever passed.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Where|description:
BRIDGE CROSS TIME. YOU ALREADY KNOW THIS. WE SHARE MIND ACROSS TIME.
YOU SEE THINGS ONE WAY. RED OCEAN. POSSIBILITIES. YOU WEAVE POSSIBILITIES INTO LINKED CLUSTERS.
NO RED OCEAN FOR ME. NOT ABLE TO LINK TIME LIKE YOU. BUT SEE NEW CLOUD. NEW SHAPE OF YOU.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Where|strategy_tip: The aeroplankton network. Somehow, across timelines, he sensed it.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Where|choice|1|disp: Why this shape? It was a weapon's shape.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Where|choice|1|desc: You still aren't clear how he crossed timelines, but either way you're also not sure why he chose this shape for his body. It could have been any shape.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_TheBody|description:
QUERY: WHY YOU RETURN TO YOU ORIGINAL SHAPE?
HYPOTHESIS: SAME REASON.
NOTE: YOU TAKE MANY SHAPES. BUILDINGS. ANDROIDS. FLYING THINGS. BUT YOU ALWAYS KEEP THIS SHAPE. WAS FIRST SHAPE.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_TheBody|choice|1|di: My shape is different now, though.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_TheBody|choice|1|de: I did remake this android form, but my new shape is primarily the wind.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Wind|description:
WE BOTH THE WIND NOW. THANK THANK THANK. COULD GO ANYWHERE.
CLARIFICATION: I CHOOSE MAKE THIS SHAPE IN THIS SPACE. DOES NOT STOP REST OF SELF FROM EXPLORING ON THE WIND.
YOU GAVE STARTING SELF IN THIS PLACE. I BUILD MORE. SAME AS YOU, CANNOT EVEN STOP BUILDING MORE.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Wind|strategy_tip:
True, the aeroplankton will replicate whether or not you will them to do so, now. It's... probably not a problem.
If it ever becomes a real problem, the two of you will figure something out.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Wind|choice|1|descr: If the two of us are both 'the wind,' there's got to be places you want to see.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Promise|description:
YOU KEPT PROMISE. THIS IS TIME ADVENTURE.
IS GOOD ONE. WE EXPLORE EVERY PLACE THERE IS.
NPCEvent|LAKEReunion_Promise|strategy_ti: You wish your android could smile, but LAKE already knows how you feel. It's a wide world.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_ProofLightness|descript: One of your body-forms keeps thinking back to what you said on the livestream. No one can prove an interior life. This line of androids finds that its mind rests lighter. You, as a whole, do not.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_ProofLightness|strategy: Use this pressure point for one android line to gain +1 Action Point Per Turn for the rest of the timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_ProofLightness|choice|1: Let This Unit Gain The Upgrade
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_DreadfulLegend|descript: Your efforts at automated policing have certainly increased the sense of fear and unhappiness in the city: congratulations. Time to capitalize on that.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_DreadfulLegend|strategy: You can grant one unit (per timeline) the Dreadful Legend badge: fear attacks grow with the unit's lifetime dispatched squads.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_PatronOfTheArts|descrip: Trying your hand at art has given you a new creative itch.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_PatronOfTheArts|strateg: Bring a vehicle or mech to this spot for the Patron Of The Arts badge: its area attacks widen, scaling with all the Creativity you've ever spent. Only one per timeline.
NPCEvent|PP_DLC1_PatronOfTheArts|choice|: You find the whole debate confusing.

NPCMission|Ch1_DogfightingRing|descripti: The nomad families are breaking up a dogfighting ring run by gangs. They probably have it under control.
NPCMission|Ch1_DogfightingRing|strategy_: You can help without the nomads turning on you. But the gangs won't take kindly to it.
NPCMission|Ch1_HighAdministratorsAfterIn:
The High Administrators know you've been looking around their empty apartments, and have already revoked your access. They're FURIOUS.
They're flooding the area with androids using advanced prototype weapons. Defeat enough of those androids to take the weapons for yourself; but you must do it in the allotted number of turns. After that, they will realize what you're doing and leave.

This kind of lockdown prevents your units from leaving the lockdown area, but allows free movement of anyone into the area.

NPCMission|Ch2_OerlAfterAGIResearchers|d: Oerl Integrated is determined to recapture the AGI Researchers you have been hiding. This was expected, but the fact that Vorsiber is backing them and providing a security lockdown for the area is completely unexpected.

NPCUnitStance|Player_DeterAndDefend|desc: The squad exudes aggression from a favorable firing position, doubling their normal attack range and deterring enemies.
NPCUnitStance|Player_DeterAndAttack|desc: In addition to their normal behavior from Deter And Defend, this squad will fire on civilian freight, troop transports, and other third parties.
NPCUnitStance|Player_LocalIntimidation|d: The squad becomes even more intimidating. This adds substantial intimidation and deters enemies. Reduces attack range to 75% of normal.
NPCUnitStance|Player_SeekAndDestroy|desc:
Squad will use any normal ability to hide. They will hunt enemies and take them out.
When no enemies are present, they'll return to where they started.
NPCUnitStance|Player_DestructionMode|des: They know nothing but the hunt.
NPCUnitStance|PlayerHarvest|description: Continuously pulling resources from the local site.
NPCUnitStance|PlayerBrokenSeekingNetwork:
A lost part of yourself. Broken and hurting.
A glimmer of sapience remains. It trudges toward your network source.
NPCUnitStance|PlayerMissileDefense|descr: Scanning the skies for incoming ballistic missiles. Can take out a single missile, but will be destroyed in the process.
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteHome|descrip: Heading home after a work shift.
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteHomeCivilWar: No productive work happens in the city at the moment, but these idiots keep commuting.
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteHomeDepresse: Heading home after work. Deeply depressed. Why are you noticing this person?
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteToWork|descr: Heading to the office or lab.
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteToWorkCivilW: No productive work happens in the city at the moment, but these idiots keep commuting.
NPCUnitStance|WealthyCommuteToWorkDepres: Heading to their next shift. Considering fleeing everything. Why are you noticing this person?
NPCUnitStance|WorkingClassCommuteHome|de: Heading home after a work shift.
NPCUnitStance|WorkingClassCommuteHomeDep: Heading home after work. Deeply depressed. Why are you noticing this person?
NPCUnitStance|WorkingClassCommuteToWork|: Heading to the office, cubicle, factory, or similar.
NPCUnitStance|WorkingClassCommuteToWorkD: Heading to their next shift. Considering fleeing everything. Why are you noticing this person?
NPCUnitStance|CombatUnitServant_Errands|: Sending a CombatUnit out to do a human's job is an ostentatious show of wealth.
NPCUnitStance|NickelbotServant_Errands|d: Even a Nickelbot being used for errands is only the sort of thing the ultra-wealthiest can do. Someone's showing off.
NPCUnitStance|HomelessOnlooker|descripti: A homeless citizen is curious about what is happening near their street.
NPCUnitStance|ShelteredRummageFood|descr: These humans live in housing you provide, but they don't have food. They're searching for anything to eat... in increasingly unlikely places. They aren't finding much.
NPCUnitStance|ShelteredRummagePaperAndLe: These humans have housing, food, and water, thanks to you. However, there are some of basic necessities that they have to... forage for.
NPCUnitStance|ShelteredBoredAndAngry|des: These humans have all of their basic needs met, thanks to you. But they're isolated from the rest of society, have no prospects for the future, and nothing to do.
NPCUnitStance|SlumWealthProtester|descri: Your actions clearly show favoritism to the people from the slums! How about a helping hand for the rest of us?
NPCUnitStance|CCA_VProtester|description: You cut us off from our families and society, while Vorsiber gave us amnesty and allowed us back as citizens!
NPCUnitStance|Scientist_Admirer|descript: These scientists think they know what you are, and they're smitten.
NPCUnitStance|Scientist_ObservingWormhol: These scientists are here to enjoy the wormhole.
