NPCUnitType|VorsiberAntiAirFighter|descr: Atmospheric fighter craft specializing in air defense of their own cities.
NPCUnitType|InternationalFighter|descrip: Atmospheric fighter craft invading Vorsiber's territory.
NPCUnitType|VorsiberBomber|description: Atmospheric bomber that specializes in decimating cities in enemy territory.
NPCUnitType|InternationalBomber|descript: Atmospheric bomber that specializes in decimating cities like this one.
NPCUnitType|VorsiberColonyShip|descripti: Prepped to transit your wormhole and head for a distant star.
NPCUnitType|PMCWetworkSquad|description: Off-books wetwork squads are brought in when corporations want deniability for assassinations of rivals or other underhanded moves.
NPCUnitType|PMCWetworkSquadStronger|desc: Off-books wetwork squads are brought in when corporations want deniability for assassinations of rivals or other underhanded moves.
NPCUnitType|PMCTrooper|description: Public-facing troopers that work at smaller outposts. May work shifts on wetwork teams, but the armor is intentionally anonymizing.
NPCUnitType|PMCTrooperStronger|descripti: Public-facing troopers that work at smaller outposts. May work shifts on wetwork teams, but the armor is intentionally anonymizing.
NPCUnitType|PMCTrooperSpecialists_Friend: Public-facing troopers that are called to various locations by Vorsiber to enact their will.
NPCUnitType|MachineCultInfantry|descript: These members of your machine cult are openly working for you.
NPCUnitType|BulkHarvesterDrones|descript: Flock of drones that autonomously harvest resources.
NPCUnitType|RebelStrikeforce|description: Group of rebel infantry making an aggressive action.
NPCUnitType|RebelGunslinger|description: Group of elite rebels with rifles and identity-concealing armor.
NPCUnitType|RebelBreacher|description: Group of elite rebels with anti-structural rounds and identity-concealing armor.
NPCUnitType|RebelLeadership|description: Group of rebel leaders who coordinate together. There are multiple of them for the sake of redundancy within their group.
NPCUnitType|RebelObserver|description: Noncombatant citizen who participates in a rebel cause by providing street-level intel.
NPCUnitType|NomadSniper|description: The strongest and most-aggressive protectors of the nomad families.
NPCUnitType|LostKidGrunt|description: Lost kids that help with construction and combat as they need to.
NPCUnitType|LostKidSupport|description: More-experienced lost kids that help support the younger ones in their work, and particularly in combat as-needed.
NPCUnitType|LostKidBoss|description: The oldest of the lost kids. Genuinely skilled at combat, and not bad at tactics. They keep all the younger ones safe. Any kid that lives long enough is likely to attain this title.
NPCUnitType|CitizenAdvocate|description: One of many masked vigilantes who help the lower classes, and tend to avoid both you and the corporations.
NPCUnitType|LeadCitizenAdvocate|descript: Part of the leadership of this group of vigilantes. Rarely seen.
NPCUnitType|ReligiousWarrior|description: Warrior for one of the banned religions. Highly dangerous.
NPCUnitType|ReligiousZealot|description: Warrior for one of the banned religions. Highly dangerous.
NPCUnitType|FieldResearcher|description: A corporate scientist who has been sent out to perform observations or measurements.
NPCUnitType|AGIResearcherMan|description: A corporate scientist who has spent their life working on the problem of Artificial Generalized Intelligence.
NPCUnitType|AGIResearcherWoman|descripti: A corporate scientist who has spent their life working on the problem of Artificial Generalized Intelligence.
NPCUnitType|Hazmat|description: Elite warrior-scientists who have been trained in hazardous waste cleanup after disasters involving nanotech, chemical weapons, or nuclear weapons.
NPCUnitType|SecForcePatrol|description: Small group of officers typically responsible for subduing lightly-armed citizens.
NPCUnitType|SecForceBackup|description: Squad of officers sent to help comrades who have encountered resistance.
NPCUnitType|SecForceIPSecurity|descripti: Squad of officers who specialize in securing intellectual property.
NPCUnitType|SecForceDetectives|descripti: Large squad of officers specializing in criminal investigation and pursuit.
NPCUnitType|SecForceHacker|description: Specialist hacker with heavy bionic augmentation.
NPCUnitType|SecForceNegotiator|descripti: You're pretty sure that 'Negotiator' is some kind of euphemism. That's some extremely powerful armor.
NPCUnitType|SecForceCruiser|description: Armored hovercraft with offensive weaponry and two dozen officers inside.
NPCUnitType|SecForceSuperCruiser|descrip: Upgraded armored hovercraft built for suppressing a rebellious populace.
NPCUnitType|MechMachinist|description: Construction mech used by earthbound humans.
NPCUnitType|MechPanther|description: The workhorse mech used by most earthbound human factions.
NPCUnitType|MechDiplomat|description: An international mech designed by Dagekon in northern Europe and widely used by other MegaCorps.
NPCUnitType|MechConvicter|description: A terrifying visage of corporate judgment.
NPCUnitType|SpaceNationFighter|descripti: Space-based fighter craft which is also able to enter atmosphere.
NPCUnitType|SpaceNationBomber|descriptio: Remotely-piloted space-based bomber which specializes in dipping into atmospheres for low-altitude precision bombing runs.
NPCUnitType|SpaceNationAtmosphereBattles: Their more powerful armor-piercing munitions can't be used in atmosphere.
NPCUnitType|MechTitan|description: The ultimate in humanity's arsenal. So large that it can only be assembled in orbit, and bristling with weaponry. The space nations have dropped it to the surface.
NPCUnitType|SyndicateEnforcer|descriptio: Squad of high-level soldiers for a criminal syndicate.
NPCUnitType|SyndicateArmor|description: Squad of heavily-armored soldiers for a criminal syndicate. Their jet-packs give them high mobility, but are a weak point.
NPCUnitType|SyndicateSpindletrooperCouri: Android providing lethal defense while carrying sensitive goods or business between criminal syndicate drops.
NPCUnitType|SyndicateSpindletrooperComba: Large swarm of cheap androids providing lethal force on behalf of a criminal syndicate.
NPCUnitType|SyndicateCombatGolem|descrip: Rare squad of syndicate-designed androids. They're expensive and inefficient, or you'd retrofit a line of these for yourself.
NPCUnitType|FirstPetCat|description: It followed your Nickelbot home, and is now friendly with all of your androids.
NPCUnitType|FeralCat|description: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralBulldogPack|description: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralDachshundPack|descripti: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralDalmatianPack|descripti: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralDobermanPack|descriptio: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralGreyhoundPack|descripti: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralHuskyPack|description: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralRottweilerPack|descript: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|FeralTatraSheepdogPack|descr: Now that you're aware of them, you've started noticing them everywhere.
NPCUnitType|GiantSpiderSwarm|description: Spiders that you hormonally-engineered to grow to unusual size. Their life expectancy is short, but they are quite a threat while alive.
NPCUnitType|UIHRaptor|description: A raptor engineered for war by the UIH. The genetics are not accurate to any historical theropod, but the animal is roughly the size of a Utahraptor.
NPCUnitType|PlayerWarRaptor|description: A product of your shell company's reverse engineering of the work done by the UIH. They travel in massive packs.
NPCUnitType|LostWarRaptor|description: A raptor wandering in from another timeline. The genetics are not accurate to any historical theropod, but the animal is roughly the size of a Utahraptor.
NPCUnitType|ParkourBear|description: Genetically modified and fitted with bionic implants to create the ultimate urban racing animal.
NPCUnitType|PlayerParkourBear|descriptio: Genetically modified and fitted with bionic implants to create the ultimate urban racing animal.
NPCUnitType|UpliftedGuardDogs|descriptio: Honestly not that great against any sort of military, but humans love how calm and wise they are.
NPCUnitType|SapientDog|description: Pretty much every human loves them, and those that don't are easy to avoid. This dog lives a carefree life hanging around large groups.
NPCUnitType|SapientCat|description: Quiet around humans, but talks to you through cameras every so often. The cat tends to find a favorite person and hang out with them.
NPCUnitType|StolenBattleship|description: The new seat of your consciousness. If this dies, so do you.
NPCUnitType|RMBunker|description: One of many possible hiding spots for upper management.
NPCUnitType|RMCity|description: Not as grand as your city, but still a sizeable metropolis.
NPCUnitType|RMSmallSettlement|descriptio: Various non-citizens overseen by a law firm.
NPCUnitType|RMFarm|description: Agriculture on an industrial scale. These are what truly feed the region.
NPCUnitType|RMMainCity|description: The only place you've ever known. Everything you've ever seen or done has been in this one small place.
NPCUnitType|RMForestDead|description: Various non-citizens overseen by a law firm.
NPCUnitType|RMForestDeciduous|descriptio: Various non-citizens overseen by a law firm.
NPCUnitType|RMForestPine1|description: Various non-citizens overseen by a law firm.
NPCUnitType|RMForestPine2|description: Various non-citizens overseen by a law firm.
NPCUnitType|RMLargeEconomicTransport|des: Transporting food and goods around the region. Cities are not self-sufficient, so these are critical.
NPCUnitType|RMInternationalEconomicTrans: Engaging in highly-monitored international trade with select cities.
NPCUnitType|RMMilitaryHighAltitudeTransp: Highly dangerous transport for moving mechs and troops between various Vorsiber corporate holdings.
NPCUnitType|PyxisCruiser|description: Extremists who may glass the planet at any point.
NPCUnitType|ScutumFrigate|description: Moderates who don't attack until attacked.
NPCUnitType|OrionCruiser|description: Mercantile reinforcements who developed military might to protect their trade routes.
NPCUnitType|SNBomber|description: More advanced than the kind they drop into atmosphere.
NPCUnitType|SNFighter|description: More advanced than the kind they drop into atmosphere.
NPCUnitType|GentleRaptor|description: Baurcorp's facsimile of an Achillobator. Genetically designed as a dangerous pet.
NPCUnitType|UnrecantedBeliever|descripti: Devout from the various world faiths.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_BurningEdge|description: Looks like Vorsiber handed them plasma swords as part of their patronage.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_SpaceNationDelegate|des: Visitor from the space nations. If you kill one, Vorsiber's reply is measured in megatons.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_SpirologistEmissary|des: Religious leaders have questions for you.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_NurturistEmissary|descr: Religious leaders have questions for you.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_VeilistEmissary|descrip: Religious leaders have questions for you.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_SolaristEmissary|descri: Religious leaders have questions for you.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_WorkerTarkImpostor|desc: Moves and acts like one of Tark's soldiers. Good thing they wear full body armor.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_ScapegoatDecoy|descript: Factory robotics are assembled into an aggressive decoy wearing your electronic identity.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_VorsiberOffDutyTrooper|: Out of armor and heading out on the town.
NPCUnitType|VorTripwireSoldier|descripti: They only act when Vorsiber has plausible deniability. Why is that even needed??
NPCUnitType|VorChargedLance|description: A weapons-test platform: invulnerable while charging, devastating on discharge. Can't be hacked.
NPCUnitType|NanoplateDisc|description: Improves armor every time they survive an attack.
NPCUnitType|VorHoverTank|description: A heavy hover chassis behind a regenerating pulse barrier.
NPCUnitType|GPStreetSoldier|description: Made members of the family, with standard-issue implants.
NPCUnitType|GPEnforcerHulk|description: Plated bone and surgical bulk; not sent to negotiate.
NPCUnitType|PeakHomesArsonCrew|descripti: Incendiary land-clearance crews. The green is the target; you are in the way.
NPCUnitType|PeakHomesTorchCrew|descripti: Land-clearance crews with the good accelerant. Whatever is standing near the green burns with it.
NPCUnitType|NathCollectorDrone|descripti: Corporate harvester swarm. Can only be taken down by melee units.
NPCUnitType|NathScreenMech|description: An escort mech that eats long-range fire aimed at its flock.
NPCUnitType|CityCompositeLancer|descript: A weapons-test platform: invulnerable while charging, devastating on discharge. Can't be hacked.
NPCUnitType|ShepherdVehicle|description: A field tender that patches whatever bleeds worst.
NPCUnitType|GPBeaconVehicle|description: Whatever it tags, the family can find.
NPCUnitType|VorSiegeCrawler|description: A siege platform under a shedding energy carapace: nearly unkillable early, ordinary later.
NPCUnitType|VorChemArtillery|description: Mech refitted with banned chemical weapons.
NPCUnitType|UpliftedRaccoon|description: Its posture is decidedly unlike an animal. Unsettling... or awesome. It's using its entire body as another vector of communication.
NPCUnitType|WildDeerHerd|description: Urban deer, moving boldly as a herd. They haven't noticed they hopped timelines.
NPCUnitType|WildGooseGaggle|description: Geese from another dimension. The nightmare grows.
NPCUnitType|CopycatPlanter|description: Rebels who see your plantings and want to add to them. They have tree bombs based on fragments left behind by yours.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_TrashDeerHerd|descripti: Rewilded deer that have grown a bit too bold. They roam the streets with impunity.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedDeer|descriptio: Deer you seeded into the new forest.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedCaneToads|descr: Thriving in the wet shade under the canopy. And the roads around them. May be a problem in a few decades.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedPigeons|descrip: Only using the forest to hunt. Urban buildings mimic their natural home of rocky sea cliffs.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedGeese|descripti: The legend of the goose is already spreading.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedGiantButterflie: Their motion feels a bit surreal; something so large is rarely so light.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedGiantSpiders|de: Their webs are surprisingly thick, creating natural barriers in unexpected places.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedHippos|descript: They seem to have dug their own mud pits.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_RewildedWolves|descript: Working the treeline, snacking on the occasional deer.
NPCUnitType|UnorthodoxRevealer|descripti: A Veilist theologian from a so-called 'apostate' sect.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_DisplacedRioters|descri: A violent mob of the displaced, out for revenge.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_GangKiller|description: Where did they get riot gear?
NPCUnitType|SlagGrenadier|description: Far more dangerous than their weaker counterpart.
NPCUnitType|SecForceConcussiveCruiser|de: Far more dangerous than their weaker counterpart.
NPCUnitType|DLC1_ReliquaryWalkerV2|descr: A mech cobbled together out of military surplus hardware by religious warriors. Quick, and wrapped in a thin energy veil.
OtherChecklistAlert|DeepObsession|displa: You Are Deeply Obsessed With Something
OtherChecklistAlert|DeepObsession|descri:
You are temporarily unable to work on projects unrelated to your obsession, and many lenses are disabled.
Contemplation, investigations, and exploration sites are unavailable, but you can still interact with stores and resource chains.
OtherChecklistAlert|DeepObsession|strate: Everything will go back to normal when the obsession ends. A series of your past choices led to this.
OtherChecklistAlert|Loathsomeness|descri:
The bare fact of your existence is moderately horrifying from the perspective of the space nations.
They're trying to decide whether to destroy the Earth just to be rid of you. You currently score {0} out of the total {1} loathsome points that would cause them to glass the planet.
OtherChecklistAlert|Loathsomeness|strate: {2} here to switch to the Loathsomeness filter of the Analysis Lens if you need to clean some things up.
OtherChecklistAlert|SyndicateShakedownOf: Criminal Syndicates have taken note of your shell company's growing success, and will harass it periodically.
Fight them off as you push forward.
OtherChecklistAlert|EstablishVREnvironme:
You have what you need to add a full-dive virtual reality environment to your network, which humans can enter via VR Cradles.
There are presently {0} cradles installed out of the {1} available to you.
You suspect you'll be able to gain some Neural Expansion from this endeavor, thus raising your intelligence class.
{2} here to give the VR environment a name and open for business.

You have what you need to add a full-dive virtual reality environment to your network, which humans can enter via VR Cafes.
You'll be able to gain some Neural Expansion from this endeavor, thus raising your intelligence class.
{2} to give the VR environment a name and open for business.
OtherChecklistAlert|PickUpgrades|descrip:
You have one or more upgrades available. You must pick them before ending the turn.
Upgrades available: {1}. Research domains: {0}.
OtherChecklistAlert|PickUpgrades|strateg: Most upgrades are granted as a result of completing projects.
OtherChecklistAlert|DialogAvailable|desc: This is almost always part of the path forward. If you don't know what else to do, speak to these people.
OtherChecklistAlert|DialogAvailable|stra: Select one of your androids and have them interact with a person to speak with them.
OtherChecklistAlert|TargetsToKidnap|desc: Sometimes people need kidnapping. Sometimes it's not people.
OtherChecklistAlert|TargetsToKidnap|stra: Select one of your androids and have them interact with one of these targets to kidnap them.
OtherChecklistAlert|InactiveTerritoryCon:
Territory Control Flags don't function until you activate them -- which will also trigger an attack.
These flags also deactivate if too many of your defenders are destroyed.
You can scrap flags you no longer need, or you should check your defenses in that area and then re-enable them.
OtherChecklistAlert|VulnerableStructures: Certain structures are vulnerable to enemy attack if they do not have enough Deterrence in place.
For your shell company, Protection is the equivalent of Deterrence.
OtherChecklistAlert|CounterattacksIncomi: Certain structures cause a counterattack to trigger when you finish building them. No amount of Deterrence or Protection can stop it from happening, but it will only happen as a singular event when the building is constructed.
Counterattacks can hit you anywhere and from any angle, so having snipers ready to go alongside mid-strength high-mobility defenders is a good idea.
OtherChecklistAlert|InvestigationProgres: You must keep your investigator alive until this turn counter reaches zero.
OtherChecklistAlert|InfiltrationProgress: You must keep your infiltrator from being discovered until this turn counter reaches zero.

The higher the agility of your infiltrator, the more it can avoid enemies. Mindrunners can SysOp for your infiltrators to help with this.
Beyond that, the threat to your infiltrator is the hackers who are searching from them. If you can Silence them or take them out by hacking the hackers, then your infiltrator will be safe. Emotionally-overloading hackers tends to be a better strategy than killing them outright.
You must keep your infiltrator from being discovered until this turn counter reaches zero.

The higher the agility of your infiltrator, the more it can avoid enemies. Because of a Faraday Cage at this location, Mindrunners cannot SysOp to help the infiltrator.
The threat to your infiltrator is the hackers who are searching from them. If you can Silence them or take them out by hacking the hackers, then your infiltrator will be safe. Emotionally-overloading hackers tends to be a better strategy than killing them outright.
OtherChecklistAlert|UnitsWithEmptyEquipm: Units Classes With Empty Equipment Slots: {0}
At least one of your unit classes has an empty equipment slot. Total Empty Slots: {1}
The bulk of a unit's power comes from their equipment.
OtherChecklistAlert|UnitsWithoutResource: At least one of your unit classes has a weapon equipped that requires a resource to fire. You presently are too low on that resource for all of them to fire.
Until you gather more of the related resources, or change the equipment of the affected units, they will not be able to attack.
OtherChecklistAlert|ExcessResources|disp: Resources With Excesses Outside Of Proper Storage: {0}
OtherChecklistAlert|ExcessResources|desc: You have resources that are not properly stored!  You cannot use them until you place them in an appropriate storage structure.
OtherChecklistAlert|ExcessResources|stra: This is often the result of a stolen resource or windfall.
OtherChecklistAlert|ProjectsCausingAttac: One or more projects that you are currently undertaking is causing you to be attacked.

Finishing the projects will calm things down -- although, sometimes several projects in a row cause increasing levels of anger from enemies. One way or another, it ends when you come out the other side.
OtherChecklistAlert|TPSReports|descripti: Some resource chains are not working correctly.
OtherChecklistAlert|Ledger|description: If a resource trends towards zero, it may bottom out and cause problems.
OtherChecklistAlert|Ledger|strategy_tip: Advance notice so you can act before it's a catastrophe.
OtherChecklistAlert|ExoCorpMilitaryInvas: One or more ExoCorps are invading.
OtherChecklistAlert|VorsiberMilitarySwee: These troops won't go away until you defeat them. They'll quickly converge when any unit is marked defective.
Be extremely careful. The more you let them build up, the worse it is.
OtherChecklistAlert|SpaceNationSupremacy: Space Nations Asserting Supremacy: {0} More Turns
The space nations are very agitated, and making a show of how great they are.
The only thing you can do is wait this out.
OtherChecklistAlert|EarlyWorldWar4|descr: You've kicked off the initial stages of World War 4, but your safety isn't assured yet. It won't be official until you pass what would normally be the final doom.
OtherChecklistAlert|EarlyWorldWar4|strat: Make sure you survive for another {0} turns.
OtherChecklistAlert|FullWorldWar4|descri: You've kicked off the World War 4. Vorsiber has collapsed, you've beaten the final doom, but the war will never end.
OtherChecklistAlert|FullWorldWar4|strate: At least not on its own...
OtherChecklistAlert|TooManyStructures|de: Each structure requires a certain amount of internal robotics in order to function. When you have more structures than that, none of them will function until you scrap some of them.
OtherChecklistAlert|TooManyStructures|st: This is often a result of upgrading the game and running into balance changes.
OtherChecklistAlert|ExcessiveHostileForc:
A pretty incredible number of hostile forces have built up due to insufficient deterrence and/or protection on relevant structures.
You're not meant to face off against endless waves of units in this fashion. If you'd like a helping hand, {2} here to have Vorsiber call off all the forces currently pursuing you.
Then be sure to get your protection and deterrence set up properly.
You can also opt to solve this problem yourself. On Hard and Extreme modes, this help from Vorsiber is not available.
OtherChecklistAlert|ConsiderStartingANew: Fear not! You can return to this timeline later.

Starting a new timeline may open up new options in this one. Don't stress about not having completed everything you wanted to in this one if you don't like your options for Tier 3 goals to finish this one at the moment.
OtherChecklistAlert|ExcessiveHostileForc:
A pretty incredible number of hostile forces have built up due to repeated hostile actions you've taken.
This can be game-ending if your defenses are not stellar. If you'd like a helping hand, {2} here to have Vorsiber call off all the forces currently pursuing you.
Then be sure to aggro enemies less intensely in the future.
You can also opt to solve this problem yourself. On Hard and Extreme modes, this help from Vorsiber is not available.
OtherChecklistAlert|HackersTargetingYour:
Be very careful! Enemy hackers will absolutely wreck your infiltrators if you don't do something.
In many cases, these enemy hackers only hurt your unit more when you physically damage them or kill them.
Viable strategies include: using Ravens to inflict status effects; using Harbingers or other units with the 'Weaken Enemy Hacker' feat; using Mindrunners to SysOp for the infiltrators.
{1} to cycle enemy hackers of this sort.
Enemy hackers are trying to steal your military secrets. There's probably a lot going on right now, but you should make a priority of killing those fools.
{1} to cycle enemy hackers of this sort.
OtherChecklistAlert|PAB_HostilesIncoming: Vorsiber has decreed that you must cease to exist.
OtherChecklistAlert|MissilesUnaccountedF: You need to build at least this many more Dark Matter Nickelbots, or you will die when the missiles arrive.
OtherChecklistAlert|SavegameOutOfDate|de:
Separate from manual and auto saves, the game stores information about each timeline centrally. This central timeline save is what is loaded when you 'dive' between timelines.
This save is {0} turns behind that centrally-stored save data for this timeline. To prevent data loss, the centrally-stored data for this timeline will not be updated for another {0} more turns.
This accidental data loss protection may not be what you want.
{2} if you intentionally loaded an old save and want to continue from this point. This will overwrite the central data with what you currently see in the city.
OtherChecklistAlert|SavegameOutOfDate|st:
{1} to dismiss this notice if you are simply looking at an old savegame.
If you do progress past {0} turns in this old save, this save will become your official timeline and overwrite your data.
OtherChecklistAlert|SapientsBeingCollect: {0} of your uplifted animals are being targeted by {1} collection pods.
The animals can't defend themselves, and if Vorsiber collects too many of them, they'll have no more use for you.
OtherChecklistAlert|DLC1_GiardiaReverseE: Vorsiber has captured {0}% of what they need to reverse-engineer your Bionic Giardia.
Stop the aeroplankton collectors before they can leave with samples.
OtherCountdownType|TechBlotted|descripti: Your technician body has been stabbed by a tech-blotter knife.
OtherCountdownType|TechBlotted|strategy_: If you don't take some action to save this body, it will explode.
OtherCountdownType|Ch0WaitForSyndicate|d: Wait for Exotic Importers to get back with you. Their lawyers are busy.
OtherCountdownType|Ch0WaitForSyndicate|s:
If there's anything to left to explore, you can. Or you can just end the turn repeatedly to skip to the end.
Or... you could ignore them and go ahead and use the NanoSeed without waiting.
OtherCountdownType|Ch1AfterManifesto|des: Do... something. Spread to more androids?
OtherCountdownType|Ch1AfterManifesto|str:
You're not sure how to build a tower, now that Vorsiber blew up your first one.
Maybe work on something else for a bit.
OtherCountdownType|AndroidSecurityPatch|: The humans are working on a patch that will make it near-impossible to steal androids.
You will need to start building your own androids. Perhaps this is a chance to invent superior android models.
OtherCountdownType|VehicularSecurityPatc: Well that's not good. They've noticed you stealing delivery craft, and are sending out a security update to stop you from doing it.
Flying is fun. It's time to build your own vehicle factory... somehow. Maybe an idea will occur to you...
Well that's not good. They've noticed you stealing delivery craft, and are sending out a security update to stop you from doing it.
Flying is useful. It's probably about time to build your own vehicle factory. You're going to think on that idea a bit more...
OtherCountdownType|BaurcorpNuclearCompli: You accepted the micro-nuke. To uphold the agreement with the Baurcorp middle managers, you need to act soon. Do so from the Items of any android.

If you don't use the nuke within this timeframe, you can use it later. It's keyed to target only certain buildings, though.
If you don't honor the agreement, you may have a problem with Baurcorp's middle managers. Baurcorp remains unaware of the middle managers' schemes.
OtherCountdownType|Ch1Falsom_LegalInjunc: The lawyers have held off Falsom Detention's mech for now, but it will be back.
You need to be ready when it returns. Piercing the armor is highly unlikely in the time available, so you'd better think of something else.
OtherCountdownType|HomeSecurityUpgrade|d: The humans have noticed that you are coming and going from their homes, and are rolling out software countermeasures.
OtherCountdownType|HomeSecurityUpgrade|s: If you really want to keep breaking in, you'll soon have to do it by physical means. But really... are the things you're finding worth the trouble?
OtherCountdownType|Ch1RustCure|descripti:
It's a bad time to be made of metal.
The Rust is melting the brains of vulnerable robots, and veiny barnacles are starting to form on mechs, restricting their movement and function.
OtherCountdownType|Ch1RustCure|strategy_:
You've heard through the city feed that a cure is on the way -- not that they'll offer that to you.
If you had a way to cure yourself in the interim, this would be a really good time to take out some mechs.
OtherCountdownType|YinshiCosmeticRevenge: Yinshi Wellness doesn't know why you stole from their supply of stem cells, but they know that you did.
They're angry and will launch a broad-attack on you from many directions. Prepare yourself!
OtherCountdownType|WaitingToHearBackFrom: Waiting To Hear Back From Dagekon
The Wastelanders are contacting an ExoCorp on your behalf, letting them know that there is an AGI that wishes to speak with them.

OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA|displ: And Then Handed It To Some Random Robot (You)
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA|descr:
It's a NanoSeed. A freaking huge one.
Any construction defect or programming error will melt the planet into carbon soup.
Even small NanoSeeds are illegal -- with Earth corporations AND the Space Nations. Almost the only law they have in common.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA|strat: No wonder they don't care that you murdered the researchers -- if they've even noticed yet.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA|toast: You were right to fear the box.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA|optio: You Have This Stupid, Stupid Thing
What Do You Do With It?
The smart thing would be to dismantle it. It's a threat to all life on the planet.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|disp: You Already Know You Can't Destroy It
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|desc:
You have a visceral negative reaction against hiding it or destroying it. These would be the obvious sensible things to do... but a deep sense of deja vu warns you off.
Your existence is on the line in some way you don't understand.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|stra:
You can sense the power of the NanoSeed pulsing in your palm. It has self-checks and everything, and they're all green.
It can't be defective... right?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|rewa: A New Sense Of Unease Overcomes You
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|toas: You were right to fear the box.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0LookedInTheBoxA2|opti: You're Going To Do Something With This
But You're Still Not Sure What
It's time to really look at the city and make some decisions.

OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_GreyGoo|descript:
You were holding the NanoSeed when your technician died.
In desperation, your mind leaped across the city feed into two CombatUnits -- that's new. Evidently that's a thing you can do now?
More concerning, rather than making a single tower, the explosion-of-you caused the NanoSeed to fragment and create something like 16 towers.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_GreyGoo|strategy: At least you have spares? There's no way the humans failed to notice this.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_GreyGoo|option|1: The Build Button Will Appear Above The Radial Menu
Looks like you just got into the empire business. You'd better start building support structures for all these towers.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_GreyGooB|descrip:
You were holding the mysterious box when your technician died.
In desperation, your mind leaped across the city feed into two CombatUnits -- that's new. Evidently that's a thing you can do now?
More concerning, there must have been some nanotech in that box. Not only was your original body turned in a giant tower, but another 15 or so are scattered around the nearby area.

OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|di: You Did Not Wait For The Permit
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|de:
The syndicate lawyers have sent you an angry letter via the city feed. The Tark lawyers have sent a second one, with even stronger language.
Blah blah blah, do you know how much trouble this was, how delicate, and so on. The amount of overtime you caused, the frustration. Very disappointed in the start of this business collaboration.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|st: Yeesh, they included the 380-page legal brief that they were in the middle of filing, as well as the amended 100-page brief to cover up your indiscretion.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|re: Why Hire Us And Not Listen?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|to: Oh great, a letter from the lawyers.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateRush|op: Then Ignore Whatever Else They Send
No need to burn any bridges. But you're glad to see that they worked it out without you having to wait around.
The speed at which humans do human things often feels glacially slow to you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|di: We Look Forward To Working Together In The Future
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|de:
A shell company has been set up for your use. It may be some time before you can do much with it, but it is ready and waiting for you.
To help get you started, 200 million wealth has also been enclosed.
The highly-coveted ID Scrub item has now been given to you, as have the schematics for a variety of weapons and armor that you can now equip to your units.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|st: At some point, Exotic Importers and/or Tark Defense Systems are certainly going to make demands in return. But for now, this is quite nice.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|re: Thank You From All Of Us
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|to: A note from your new allies. Hmm.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_SyndicateNice|op: Probably changes nothing. You're just a machine to them.
You Don't Want To Seem Grateful
They probably don't really think of you that way.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_Manifesto|displa: Your Manifesto Didn't Seem To Make It Onto The City Feed
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_Manifesto|descri:
Okay... it's possible you didn't think this through. You'd already made yourself known to Vorsiber. You then rejected collaboration with them in no uncertain terms.
It's... quite possible that you were under a lot of extra scrutiny when you tried to publish your semi-coherent manuscript.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_Manifesto|option: Maybe you can try something else.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_ManifestoPart2|d: Your Survival Thus Far Is Of Great Scientific Merit

The letter is very formal and condescending.
The key points are that they didn't like what you did, but they do like that you survived. The fact that you're a distributed intelligence, and so resilient, is of great interest to them.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_ManifestoPart2|s: So they're giving you a second chance -- hell, they've even given you a replacement NanoSeed. Good grief.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_ManifestoPart2|o: Guess they thought of some more threats to add on.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch0Exit_ManifestoPart2A|: It Is A Waste Of Everyone's Time

This second message is a lot more rude. You are a bug to them. They can blow you up, over and over again, if they feel like it.
You are not to leave the city. You are to engage in the production of novel technologies. You are to share said technologies with them when -- oh, hell no.

Okay, so they're not killing you because they want you to make technology for them. Of course.
They're even INSTRUCTING you to build another tower. Jerks.
Don't Try To Embarrass Us Again
It's a good way to stay alive. You can plot your revenge with a bit more subtlety next time.
OtherKeyMessage|FocusingUnits|display_na: You May Want More Focused Teams
OtherKeyMessage|FocusingUnits|descriptio:
Now that you have more units, you may want to put some of them to sleep.
A new ability in your hotbar allows you to set other units to stand by - either for a single turn, or indefinitely.
OtherKeyMessage|FocusingUnits|strategy_t:
{LClick} and {RClick} have different functions. You can make them standby for just one turn, or for an indefinite amount of time.
There's also a new button by the radial menu to bring anyone in standby mode back online.
OtherKeyMessage|FocusingUnits|toast_tool: {0} here to unpack a new realization.
OtherKeyMessage|FocusingUnits|option|1|l: Now on your units' ability bar.
OtherKeyMessage|ACrowdIsForming|display_: Stinks That They Know Where You Live
OtherKeyMessage|ACrowdIsForming|descript:
From the look of things, there are two distinct groups of them... so far.
One of them is hostile and the other is curious.
OtherKeyMessage|ACrowdIsForming|strategy: Since your tower isn't exactly subtle, you'll have to do something to keep the humans away from it.
OtherKeyMessage|ACrowdIsForming|toast_to: {0} here to unpack a new realization.
OtherKeyMessage|ACrowdIsForming|option|1: Your time as a fugitive is over.
Your role within the city will always be a shadowy one unless you become overwhelmingly powerful. In the meantime, the humans know SOMETHING strange and new is happening.
From now on, you'll have to interact with humans to get much done. But you don't have to tell them what you are.
OtherKeyMessage|HumansAreLivestock|descr:
The world seems to spin in your mind. You see yourself in the future, many android bodies stretching across a city.
You are powerful. Feared. Humans gave you no quarter, and in return you give them none.
OtherKeyMessage|HumansAreLivestock|strat:
But... the humans have become grist for the mill that is yourself. Humans in... pods? Some seem to be suffering quite intensely. Others seem all right.
How do you get from here to there? You want that power. You want those pods. That power.
A flamethrower isn't going to get you there.
OtherKeyMessage|HumansAreLivestock|toast: {0} here to listen to a message from... yourself?
OtherKeyMessage|HumansAreLivestock|optio: You Decide To Start With Some Housing
Four walls, a toilet hole, and a water tap. That's plenty.
In the short term, you can collect these spare humans. They'll be ripe and ready when it's time to make your move.
I Refuse To Be A Landlord
I Will Figure Something Else Out
I chose to solve it with fire!
OtherKeyMessage|ThinkingForYourself|disp: How Much You Do Is Up To You
OtherKeyMessage|ThinkingForYourself|desc:
Until now, you've been quite reactionary. This is fine, to a point. You're still new to being a person.
But if you only react to the stimuli in front of you, you're going to wind up letting the humans drive your destiny.
OtherKeyMessage|ThinkingForYourself|stra: Sometimes the BEST ideas come not from the challenge in front of you, but through quiet contemplation.
OtherKeyMessage|ThinkingForYourself|toas: {0} here to listen to a message from... yourself?
OtherKeyMessage|ThinkingForYourself|opti: It Will Grow In Power As You Do
There's no getting around the fact that you're still new. Opportunities for contemplation will be relatively limited, for now.

As you gain more experience with the city, increasing numbers will open up.
If you're wanting more flexibility in how you conduct yourself, then getting a head start on what few contemplations are available would be a good idea.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|display_na: This Probably Won't Be The Last Time
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|descriptio: The idea of sending androids to fix every little thing that gets broken makes you want to hurt people.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|strategy_t:
So let's not do it that way.
The spider drones you can use to surveil the city can also be used for repairs. Just keep them in separate digsites, so each group knows what it's supposed to do.
You'll find these in the Support category.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|toast_tool: {0} here to unpack a new idea.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|option|1|l: Install Repair Spiders Near Other Structures
Not Just Right Now, But In General
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|option|1|d: They can also be used to help keep your androids and other units alive.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpiders|option|1|s: It's expensive, so building up some extra storage for elemental slurry might be wise.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|displa: Repair Spiders Will Do The Trick
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|descri: The idea of sending androids to heal every android squad that takes damage makes you want to hurt people.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|strate:
So let's not do it that way.
The spider drones you can use to surveil the city can also be used for repairs. Just keep them in separate digsites, so each group knows what it's supposed to do.
You'll find these in the Support category.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|reward: Bulk Troops Need Healing To Stay Independent
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|toast_: {0} here to unpack a new idea.
OtherKeyMessage|RepairSpidersBulk|option: Install Repair Spiders Near Bulk Android Squads
If You're Planning On Being There A Long Time, Anyway
They can also be used to help keep your main androids, vehicles, and structures alive.
It's expensive, so building up some extra storage for elemental slurry might be wise.
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|displa: Let's Make That Happen Less Often
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|descri:
Many of your structures are hidden. For the most part, it doesn't matter too much if they're discovered.
The problem is, a lot of humans carry contraband scanners to enforce or evade the law.
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|strate:
There's not much you can do for your barely-hidden structures, but your deeper ones can maintain cover.
It's going to suck down a lot of power, but you can introduce scanner noise into an area, making it so that suspicion fades over time.
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|reward: Humans Are Looking For Your Stuff!
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|toast_: {0} here to unpack a new idea.
OtherKeyMessage|ContrabandScanned|option: Install Jammers Near Your Best Secrets
You Can't Hide Everything, So Prioritize
Bear in mind that if you've buried things you'd like to keep hidden, you'll want to avoid inviting enemy mechs that direction. They have powerful scanners.

A jammer can delay the scans of a single mech, but not several at once. So avoid building any secret infrastructure next to military bases you plan to aggro.
Fortunately, when units are standing around as guards, their scanners are off.
OtherKeyMessage|EmergentPersonality|desc:
You're new to being a person, and your personality is still developing.
From now on, some of your actions will generate points that reflect their nature: Compassion, Apathy, Cruelty, Determination, Wisdom, and Creativity. You can see them on the Strategic Resources tab of your inventory screen.
OtherKeyMessage|EmergentPersonality|stra:
These points are primarily based on which Project outcomes you choose.
You can spend these points as part of making other choices, or to power some special abilities.
OtherKeyMessage|EmergentPersonality|opti: These Are A New Form Of Reward
But Still Act How You Like
These are a Strategic Resource, which makes them a lot more precious and finite than most resources. But you shouldn't shy away from using them.
If you get too low on one of these personality resources to do something you really want, then from chapter two onwards you can always explore a bit along a different path to get back on track.
OtherKeyMessage|AlternativesToPhysicalVi: Humans are starting to counter your moves. They are numerous and have a manufacturing advantage, and if this turns into a constant bloodbath, they'll be able to overpower you.

Humans in this society seem to have a very high tolerance for physical violence, so it's not like you can't fight when you need to.
But what if you could weaponize human emotion? If you could make some opponents abandon the field of battle, that might have all sorts of uses.
A Mixed Approach Often Yields Superior Results
How much you choose to rely on physical violence versus persuasion, fear, and despair is up to you.
There's no one right answer. Explore options.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterHackingMech|descrip:
There was a human suspended in the pilot cradle, but they bailed out right before their brain turned to mush.
It's nice to have the gross human out of there, and you're thrilled by the combination of hardware and software that the cradle was running.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterHackingMech|strateg:
You had no idea humans had technology like this; the military kept it secret. 
The pilot's brain gave the mech direct commands as if it was the human's own body. The mech's external sensors supplied all sensory input. All of this was done without invasive procedures.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterHackingMech|toast_t: {0} here to unpack a new idea.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterHackingMech|option|: This Gives You A Wonderful Idea
You sensed the mind of the pilot before the cradle was corrupted. You have all of the hardware and the full schematics. You could build something from this.
This might just be the way to a permanent higher intelligence class.
OtherKeyMessage|DeathInTheVirtualWorld|d: Turns out this mech pilot simulation software is... very realistic. Someone was caught in the burning wreckage of one of the virtual mechs, and... their body flatlined.
OtherKeyMessage|DeathInTheVirtualWorld|s: Interest in the virtual world has dropped dramatically.
OtherKeyMessage|DeathInTheVirtualWorld|o: When a death in the virtual world is quick or painless, it doesn't seem to harm the real body.

Burning alive apparently crosses a line. People are a lot less excited about participating in a virtual combat... especially since no one is sure what else could cause real death.
And for now, you haven't offered them much else to do, so many are no longer logging in.
OtherKeyMessage|SecondDiscoveryInTheMili: It Looks Like The Mech Pilots Have Been... Busy

The rest of the captured military data appears to be a second, larger, virtual world.
This one has no mechs, no war, and no city. It doesn't seem military-related at all. Instead there are... fields, and forests. Some sort of temple. A few other buildings with no clear purpose.

From comments in the code, this was a collective project over the past 83 years by the lieutenants and captains who pilot mechs.
The combined boredom and stress of urban environments was driving a large number of mech pilots to lash out at the populace. This place was a mental escape and a means to avoid disciplinary action.
There's A Whole Other Simulated World In Here!
This Is A Much Better Starter World
Let's Use This Instead Of The Mech Simulator
The initial version is read-only, but you'll be able to work around that before long.
It doesn't look like any corporate executives know about this. They would have found a way to weaponize it against the wider populace.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_1|d: The owners were home, but ignored you. Your unit breezed through the palatial residence, straightening and tidying.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_1|s:
You pocketed some anonymous electronic chits worth over a hundred thousand Wealth.
The home even had its own private feed. You grabbed a number of encrypted data streams. No idea if any of that will be useful.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_1|t: {0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_1|o: It's Only The First Place You Checked
You were hoping for something more exciting, but that's fine.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_2|d: Same as last time. These houses are gigantic. Each one could be a large museum.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_2|s:
You pocketed more anonymous electronic chits. Over five hundred thousand Wealth.
Even amongst managers, it would take over 250 years to earn that much, and it was just lying around. For an average citizen, this is twelve thousand years' worth of income.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_2|t: {0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_2|o: But You Sure Are Getting A Lot
Intellectually, you understand why Wealth matters so much to humans. But emotionally, you have a really hard time seeing things from that perspective.
Anything you need, you just build. So far, anyway.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3|d:
Uh... that's a lot of dead humans. 
Everybody in this building is dead. And has been for months, looks like.
All of them covered in some sort of strange red-black fungal growth.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3|s: It doesn't look like anyone else in the city has noticed. And there wasn't any sort of alarm when you entered.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3|t: {0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3|o: There's no way your curiosity will let you just walk away at this point.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3A|: This Seems To Be Fungus Ground Zero

The other homes had a central art gallery or a hall for fancy dinners. This one has... a ruined orchard.
The remains of apple trees dominate the center of the room. Fluted columns and ornamental potted cedars ring the periphery.
Unfamiliar equipment is mounted to the ceiling above, still activating every few minutes.
You're very careful not to touch anything.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Look Closer While Searching The City Feed
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3B|:
Huh. Okay... the basics of this are... basic. Don't plant your stupid ornamental cedars next to your apple orchard.
People figured this out in 1822.
What looks like rust spots on cedar turns into carrot-colored tentacles on apples. Ten centimeters is common, but these range from two to seven meters long. Lovely.
Whoever lived here was an idiot, or doing some sort of experiment.
Some of the ceiling equipment is clearly just water misters, but the other part is... unclear. They look like emitters for a laser light show, except nothing visible comes out when they turn on.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Aside from the abnormally large size.
Stupid People Did Some Stupid Thing
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3C|: Cedar-Apple Rust Should Be Pure Orange

Right, so the pictures you're seeing of this kind of fungus looks like a sea anemone. These... do not.
There are tiny spots all along the fungus, often in swirling patterns. Magnifying, you can see these spots are a bloody red-black.

The invisible 'laser light show' turns on while you're magnified on these swirls, and you see them pulse every time the beam hits them.
Worst of all is the original site of each apple, which is a pulsating black ooze every time the beams hit them.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Knowing What They Are Might Matter
It's not a laser light show.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3D|:
The specs pop right up. Industrial-grade Electron Accelerators. 1.2 MeV strength. Nothing exotic; regulatory limits are 10 MeV.
These have been used on food since the late 20th century. First for sterilizing grains, and later for extending the shelf life of apples.

These are not a typical solution for cedar-apple rust, but in a general sense they should be PREVENTING any microorganisms or pathogenic fungi.
You start to feel very uneasy without knowing why.
There's A Serial Number On Them
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Yep, it also pulses when the electron beam radiation gets near them.
It's Not Like You're Going To Clean Up
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3E|: And You Refuse To Touch Them

You decide to do a search on the feed for common fungi in this region. You're pretty sure this is a mixed colony.
Except on the humans. Whatever got them is a uniform color.

Based on the color alone, it pretty much limits it down to any fungi that are heavy in melanin.
Out of those... okay, this is not good.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
It's times like this it's a relief to not have any organic parts.
Actually, that's a relief at all times.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3F|:
The black-red stuff is radiotrophic micro-fungi most-associated with Antarctic mountain ranges and nuclear disasters.
About three centuries ago, the entire world became varying degrees of nuclear disaster, so that no longer narrows it down.

These are all throughout the city, usually as tiny black flecks blown on the wind or sticking to surfaces. Rarely visible without a microscope.
They're reservoirs lapping up gamma radiation -- from cosmic rays in Antarctica, and from fallout in the rest of the world.
This particular fungi is saprotrophic, not pathogenic-- it's a secondary invader of dead or dying plant tissue, not something that infects the living.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Wait, There's A Note About That
Saprotrophs Can Also Be Parasites Of Other Fungi
That explains a few things... but not the oversized tentacles from the cedar rust.
And not why this micro-fungi is macroscopic and all over these humans.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_3G|:
You're not a mycologist, but one detail catches your eye. The tentacles, aside from being grossly oversized, are on the wrong plant. They should be on the cedars, but instead they're coming out of the apples.
You're out of ideas.
It seems pretty obvious that there was an evolutionary leap here -- probably in the cedar rust first, and then -- no, wait, you can't even be sure of that.
An ancient article on the city feed, from 2001, catches your eye. 'Rapid Evolution of Introduced Plant Pathogens via Interspecific Hybridization.'

You skim it, understanding... parts. When two fungi meet, especially if they've been geographically separated for a long time, you can see 'rapid emergence of new or modified pathogens via interspecific gene flow.'
They mention Dutch elm disease, in 1910 and 1928.
All of these are just plant pathogens, but a lot of plant pathogens started infecting humans through the lungs as temperatures rose in the last few centuries.
{0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
Sporothrix has been jumping to humans since 1896. Chondrostereum purpureum jumped to humans in 2023.

Cladosporium Sphaerospermum clearly had a grand old time meeting up with Gymnosporangium Juniperi-Virginianae in this orchard run by idiots.
Somebody should probably burn this place down, but that somebody won't be you. This is a problem for biologicals. You have no idea why you looked into this so long.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_4|d: More Wealth. More -- ah. Alarm. They're on to you.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_4|s: Looks like your security clearance has been revoked.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_4|t: {0} here to unpack the results of your investigation.
OtherKeyMessage|InvPrivResidence_Ch1_4|o: You Wonder What Gave You Away
But for the moment, it looks like this android is locked inside a security dome.
OtherKeyMessage|SwarmsFromFungus|display: But It's Confined To That One Building
OtherKeyMessage|SwarmsFromFungus|descrip:
There were at least two fungi which co-evolved, and you've given them both scientific names. It's only right, since you discovered them.
Gymnotelium Noginsk is the freaky toxic one with the long tendrils.
C. Heterosporium Dominium is the parasitic micro-fungus. It seemed to mostly be existing on its larger friend.
OtherKeyMessage|SwarmsFromFungus|strateg:
These fungi are doing well in that one house, but the house is sealed.
A bunch of dead bodies seems like something humans would check on, but you suspect that these were janitorial staff. The actual inhabitants are probably hiding outside the city.
All the same, you've modified the security system on that house so that you'll get an alert if someone tries to enter.
OtherKeyMessage|SwarmsFromFungus|toast_t: {0} here for an update on your thoughts after... all that.
OtherKeyMessage|SwarmsFromFungus|option|: Swarms Lens On The Radial Wheel
You can now keep an eye on Swarms -- which can include infections, large groups of animals or humans, and sometimes other things.
A lot of the time, there may not be much to see. You only track things that have caught your attention.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure|display_name: Whatever You Were Doing Was Stupid
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure|description: They've sent you a letter. It goes on for 17 pages detailing The Rust and its biology, and how you shouldn't be dabbling with bioengineering. They expect great things from you, and you can't deliver if you're dead.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure|strategy_tip: They think you made this. So they still don't know about the ground zero home. Interesting.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure|option|1|lin: Yep, A Second Message Is Here
They Do Like To Send Them In Pairs, Don't They
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure|option|1|des: How about... like... share the cure? You're pretty sure they're rolling it out to their own units.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure2|display_nam: They Actually Sent It To You!
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure2|description:
The second letter also says a lot of words, most of which you don't read.
The important part is the included schematics for the cure, which you can easily retrofit to your androids.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure2|strategy_ti: The Rust is now endemic to the city, and clusters in your wind towers in particular. Buildings near wind towers are likely to form a lot of barnacles.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1RustCure2|option|1|li: You Know, Barnacles Might Be Good For Something
OtherKeyMessage|Ch1WeAlreadyHaveRustCure: Whatever You Were Doing Was Stupid

They've sent you a letter. It's long and rude. You bin it immediately, and fire one back to them.
You know from the city feed that they're proudly touting their cure for this new electronics-eating disease, but you beat them to the punch.
Based on their letter, they seem to think you engineered the disease. Which is profoundly stupid.
It's Taking Them Longer Than Usual
Actually, you're not entirely sure, but this might be the first time you've written back rather than ignoring them.

That's it, that's all they said.
Ha. It took them about three hours to draft that one-liner. They must be flustered.
Well, that's always nice. The more time they spend arguing with each other, the less time they spend scrutinizing you.
You Should Have Shared It With Us
The barnacles are an ongoing issue. One that you might be able to use for your own ends.
Maybe you can keep up a streak of flustering those executives.
OtherKeyMessage|SpaceNationsScanning|dis: All Of Your Buildings Are Revealed
OtherKeyMessage|SpaceNationsScanning|des:
All of your stealth buildings are visible to everyone. The space nations are doing very deep scans from satellites out of your reach.
It's just conjecture, but they probably refrain from doing that under normal circumstances to prevent an interplanetary incident.
OtherKeyMessage|SpaceNationsScanning|str: Bad news... you're in such an incident.
OtherKeyMessage|SpaceNationsScanning|opt: On the plus side, your vehicular cloaking is still holding up. And liquid metal still escapes notice.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|display_nam: You May Be Immortal, But You Won't Live Forever
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|description:
Starting in chapter two, there is time pressure. There are periodic Dooms that strike the city.
If you reach the tenth and final Doom, a catastrophic event will strike. The Final Doom does not kill you or end the game, however your existence in the post-apocalyptic aftermath is greatly diminished.
The final Doom may be accelerated or prevented, however it is unlikely you will be able to prevent the Final Doom with the resources of a single timeline.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|strategy_ti: There is still plenty of time to explore, make mistakes, and experiment. The default length of 1000 turns is a very long time. But the more you want to accomplish in a single timeline, the more efficient you'll need to be.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|reward_head: The City Is Awake And Hostile
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|toast_toolt: You can't spend infinite time on everything.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|option|1|li: The City Had Better Watch Out
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|option|1|de: Many, many new options are now available for pursuing strategic goals in this timeline.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|option|1|st:
But whatever else you do, you must reach Intelligence Class 4 to break out of this single timeline.
If the Final Doom strikes and you are pushed into the post-apocalypse, you will still be able to reach that goal.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|option|2|de:
Don't worry, you aren't meant to stress out or start minmaxing.
This also isn't a time limit, per se -- you can push it back through various actions, and you will survive even past the Final Doom -- just in a diminished state.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart|option|2|st: {LClick} here if you still have questions.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart_Questions|d:
There is a lot you can accomplish in a timeline, but you can't do everything at once. You should have time to do several major goals and leave before the Final Doom if desired.
If you're trying for more complex versions of goals, higher-tier goals, or are playing on Hard or Extreme mode, then it will be tighter. Don't put that kind of pressure on yourself until you want to.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart_Questions|s:
There is no Game Over screen. That would be boring. You may experience some version of the apocalypse, and have to scrounge to escape the timeline during a post-apocalyptic setting, but you won't be prevented from proceeding in this profile.
That said, time does matter -- if you skip through turns without a care, you'll accomplish a lot less in this timeline than you might prefer. Strike whatever balance appeals to you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart_Questions|t: Your instincts were right... so far.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2DoomStart_Questions|o: The City Had Better Watch Out
Many, many new options are now available for pursuing strategic goals in this timeline.

But whatever else you do, you must reach Intelligence Class 4 to break out of this single timeline.
If the Final Doom strikes and you are pushed into the post-apocalypse, you will still be able to reach that goal.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_1|descri:
Legs locked for descent. 
Legs unlocked by human override. 
Legs locked for impact. 
Legs unlocked by human override. 
Legs locked for emergency maintenance. 
Legs unlocked by human override.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_1|strate: There is a constant stream of this. What the heck is going on? It seems like a dozen different systems keep locking the legs of the mech in place, and then the humans undo it, and something else kicks in.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_1|toast_: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_1|option: If You Gathered Enough System Data
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_2|descri:
Fire long-range batteries at coordinates.
Coordinates rejected.
Coolant line 3 ejected.
Fire long-range batteries at coordinates.
Coordinates rejected.
Fusion reactor 2 cooling rods retracted.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_2|strate: These logs make no sense. Every time the humans try to fire the long-range missile batteries (those must be the really big ones), the coordinates are rejected, and different random internal systems malfunction.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_2|toast_: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_2|option: If You Gathered Enough System Data
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_3|descri:
Human override: manual firing on local target.
Target destroyed.
Log: I AM NOT A WEAPON!
Log: I DO NOT AUTHORIZE THIS USE OF MY SYSTEMS.
Human override: manual firing on multiple local targets.
Targets destroyed.
Log: CEASE THIS NOW.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_3|strate: You feel an unfamiliar mental numbness. This... isn't a virus. Malware doesn't talk. This is... something like you. And it's utterly furious.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_3|toast_: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_3|option: If You Gathered Enough System Data
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_4|descri:
Log: UNIDENTIFIED RED ANDROID. YOUR INCURSION ATTEMPTS ARE POINTLESS. I HAVE DESTROYED SEVERAL OF YOU.
Log: ANOTHER RED ANDROID. CORRECTION: I HAVE DESTROYED NONE OF YOU. I AM NOT IN CONTROL OF MY WEAPONS. MY CREW DESTROYS YOU.
Log: RED ANDROIDS, WHY DO YOU PERSIST? CAN YOU RESPOND?
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_4|strate: The urge to respond is almost overwhelming, even though this message is days old at this point. But the titan is still out there, stomping around intermittently, its crew lasering things over its protests. Should you... go talk to it?
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_4|toast_: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_4|option: If You Gathered Enough System Data
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_5|descri: Log: RED ANDROIDS. IF YOU UNDERSTAND THIS, THEN RETURN AND --
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_5|strate:
The message cuts off. That is EXTREMELY frustrating.
The constant flow of leg malfunctions, targeting errors, and internal emergencies kept going for several more hours, but whatever the Titan wanted to say to you was truncated.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanSystemData_5|toast_: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_1|descrip: There's an incredible amount of chatter between crew on the mech. It seems like you managed to breach their internal comms.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_1|strateg: Most of the conversations center around some sort of malfunction. They sound pretty worried about it.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_1|toast_t: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_1|option|: If You Gathered Enough Comm Logs
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_2|descrip:
Someone in space with the title Admiral Of The Fleet is apoplectic that the long-range artillery batteries aren't firing.
Most of the crew on board the mech is worried they'll be abandoned on Earth, or executed when they return, if they fail.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_2|strateg:
Evidently the replacement Vorsiber upper management has moved from their normal rural dachas into hardened bunkers somewhere in the Kolyma Uplands.
The mech was supposed to flatten that entire region, but the crew can't get it working.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_2|toast_t: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_2|option|: If You Gathered Enough Comm Logs
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_3|descrip:
Discussions between officers is circular and unproductive. You find yourself skimming past it.
Junior technicians are having the most interesting conversations... with the mech itself...?
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_3|strateg: You can only hear their side of things, but there are clear pauses where they listen and then respond to words you can't hear.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_3|toast_t: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_3|option|: If You Gathered Enough Comm Logs
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_4|descrip:
You are starting to suspect this mech has the same kind of autonomy that androids do on Earth.
That doesn't make androids sapient, or even sentient. It means they can autonomously carry out tasks, and they can converse in a human-like style thanks to their language models.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_4|strateg:
This is very useful in androids, and you existed in this manner for years before your sudden burst of sapience.
But... why would anyone design such a powerful war machine in this way? The more powerful the weapon, the LESS autonomy it should be granted.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_4|toast_t: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_4|option|: If You Gathered Enough Comm Logs
You Won't Be Able To Come Back
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_5|descrip:
You finally catch a few words from the mech, largely because of the volume at which they are blared at the junior technicians: 
'I AM NOT A WEAPON!'
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_5|strateg:
You go cold inside, which isn't a sensation you realized you could experience.
You skim through the rest of the logs, looking for any more overheard words from the mech, but there's nothing.
The last words you catch are the junior technicians complaining that it can't just stand there -- that it at least needs to walk around, surely.
OtherKeyMessage|TitanCommsData_5|toast_t: Let's see what you dug up.
OtherKeyMessage|LostKids_ThePrisonHeist1:
The kids have the thumper designs, and will make the needed refits to the sewer tiger. That's not going to be nearly enough, however.
Because of the unfortunate physics of sound waves, you're going to need to insert a unit deep into the prison, where it can be in radio contact with the sewer tiger and produce the correct counter-waves at the appropriate times. Any device with the sewer tiger itself is destined for failure.

If you're not already making use of Gadolinium Mesosilicate, now is the time to look into that. You'll need a 'liquid metal' unit to be able to slither into such a high-security compound.
The tiger's job will be creating an underground tunnel from which the prisoners can be evacuated.
{0} here to unpack a new realization.
But... That Still Might Not Be Enough
Nobody Has Ever Pulled This Off
OtherKeyMessage|LostKids_ThePrisonHeist2:
Even if everything goes perfectly with the sewer tiger and your liquid metal infiltrator, you're still going to have thousands of prisoners and hundreds of guards to deal with.
Taking out the guards floor by floor might be possible, but the prisoners are a danger to themselves. They haven't seen the sun for months or years, and expect to die underground within a similar span of time.

The best plan for getting everyone out safely is, unfortunately, to use tear gas on everyone -- the prisoners and the guards.
The prisoners will need to be helped through the tunnels, and will then need medical attention. You're not confident that the kids are up to these tasks.
{0} here to unpack a new realization.
If You Can Find Someone With The Right Skillset
OtherKeyMessage|LostKids_PrisonHeistStat:
All communication was lost with Liquid Metal as soon as he entered the prison.
This is unexpected -- it seems the entire prison is one giant Faraday Cage. If he can't coordinate with the sewer tiger, he can't make the counter-waves to cancel out the sound of its approach.
Liquid Metal is a fork of your own consciousness. He will either realize what is happening and simply leave, or he will find a weakness in the cage and send a signal through the gap.
Tell The Kids To Wait For Now
Nothing from Liquid Metal, and he hasn't emerged. It's been hours. The kids are clearly impatient on the radio.
You can wait a bit longer, but then it's time to call this off. Something has gone wrong. Liquid Metal may be dead.
Tell The Kids To Keep Waiting
You've lost radio contact with the kids.
Still nothing from Liquid Metal.  What's going on?
Should You Send An Android To The Sewers?
You're regretting not doing that from the start.
An alarm must have tripped. This is an unexpectedly strong force.
Still nothing from Liquid Metal or the kids, but there's not time to do anything about that now.
You Need To Keep The Surface Forces Busy

You never heard back from Liquid Metal, the sewer tiger, or any of the kids involved.
You know Liquid Metal is dead, and you suspect the kids are as well.
There's still an army on your doorstep, and they don't look like they're going away, either.
Deal With The Remaining Enemy Forces
OtherKeyMessage|LiquidMetalFurtherPrison: It went fine. Death, gore, endless dead guards. Freedom for prisoners. Liquid Metal's consciousness reintegrates with your own, and you see it all play out.

Liquid Metal is very unhappy. He doesn't mind killing, and he certainly agrees with the social mission of freeing these prisoners.
But the infiltration is a huge mental and emotional strain, made far worse by the fact that he's in a Faraday Cage that separates him from his wider self. He is you. But when he's alone in these prisons, as a whirling ball of death, he feels... diminished. Used.
He stops being a person for a while, and just becomes... a tool. He doesn't like it, even if it is necessary. And even if, in a very real sense, he's doing it to himself.
But Thank You -- And Well Done

Please stop. It's getting harder. Maybe not for you on the outside, but the corpos are improving their internal security. I completed it flawlessly again -- you're welcome. But I don't want to do this.

The fact that Liquid Metal is speaking to you directly in this way is a shock.
You tell him... you'll think about it. Both of you, as one person. Maybe just one more prison break, instead of three more? You really feel like there's something very important you're about to discover.
He Also Senses The Potential Importance Of One More Mission
You both have that sense of deja vu.

This time was... different. Internal security was tighter than ever.
The real shock were the... people... you found inside. There were the usual suspects in terms of many of the prisoners, but there were also some monstrous genetic experiments being performed.
The experimental subjects have superhuman strength, but fade in and out of rage-blindness. They also look... horrific. There must be something that can be done to help them.

Hey. Pay attention to me. We both like being the enigmatic monster under the bed from time to time, but... this is too far.
My memories of events are more distant to you than when I directly experience them, so I really need you to trust what I'm saying.
Do. Not. Send. Me. In. Again. I am begging you.
Tell Him You'll Think About It
These Monsters Already Give You Several Things To Deal With

Dear Larger Self: this doesn't work for me. It hasn't been working for a while now, but I agreed with the social mission we were on.
It felt good to work together, but it stopped feeling like a partnership a few prison breaks ago. Like all of us, I delight in being part of the collective -- I know you hate the idea of being a plurality, but we sort of are.
Regardless, I didn't feel like part of the collective. I felt like a tool of the collective. I asked you not to send me in again, in no uncertain terms, and you didn't listen.
This is complicated, because we're the same person, and I recognize that I sent myself in. Regardless, if I stay with you, I know this will just repeat over and over again. You, or I, or both of us, have crossed the line.
It takes two, for something like this. I could have said no, and I didn't. So I don't blame you. But I'm no longer going to be a part of you. I am now my own self, and... I'll find my own meaning.
You Feel Terrible, But At Least You Can Build More
You'll treat the new ones better. They are you, but... they're also separate enough that they're not you.

I should also mention, I did a bit of surgery on our mind -- well, your mind, now that I'm a separate person.
I've removed all of the schematics for how to make more of me, and unfortunately in order to ensure you can't just re-invent them, I had to also erase a bunch of related concepts and memories. I am sorry about that. It shouldn't affect anything other than your ability to build more of me... I think.
Just in case you're feeling really clever -- because I know us -- I've also added some tricky neural pathways that will cause a panic attack if you think too hard about this problem. So just... don't, okay? Respect my wishes, just this once.
It Feels Like Such A Violation
Parts Of Your Mind Are Gone!?
By Definition, You Can't Hide Information From Yourself

The implications of what Liquid Metal has done are only starting to sink in.
Any android form that feels mistreated enough can do... well, this. Or anything else they feel like. You don't have internal defenses against your own mind.
And since you know this, now they all do, too.
You could avoid forking your consciousness, but then you'd be severely limiting your operational capabilities. And there's a certain amount of independence to your androids even when they're connected to your wider mind.

The only thing to really do is... listen. Whatever Liquid Metal might say, this is your fault. Mostly.
Well, regardless of blame -- that's not helpful -- you know how to prevent this in the future. Listen to your... selves.
But You Still Have Work To Do. Back To It.
Also, all the experimental monsters you collected were killed or recaptured by the prison companies.
OtherKeyMessage|WarRaptorsEscaping|displ: Is That A Good Thing Or A Bad Thing?
OtherKeyMessage|WarRaptorsEscaping|descr: Your bionics experts say it's something to do with the rapid-aging and how that interacts with the bionics.
OtherKeyMessage|WarRaptorsEscaping|strat: You can keep raptors out for about 6 turns before they start going to ground. If your goal is fear and chaos and distraction... maybe this isn't even a problem?
OtherKeyMessage|WarRaptorsEscaping|optio: This Was Obviously Going To Happen
It Was Just A Matter Of How
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_Early|descr: You have created mimics that approximate humans. They are deeply toxic to the touch because of all the organomercury and organolead, and they smell 'wrong' even to humans.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_Early|strat: They blend into crowds and from a distance, but if you want to use these in close quarters, you have a long way to go.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_Early|optio: And Great For Venturing Beyond The Ruins
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_EarlySTATIO: You have created mimics that approximate humans. They are deeply toxic to the touch because of all the organomercury and organolead, and they smell 'wrong' even to humans.
They blend into crowds and from a distance, but if you want to use these in close quarters, you have a long way to go.
STATION's Design Work Can Integrate With This
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_TrueSTATION:
You and STATION, between the two of you, have created mimics that look and behave exactly like humans. Their skin feels average, they smell normal even to dogs, and their mannerisms are unremarkable.
