They can switch between any ethnicity, age, and body type. They can copy voices, and can approximate people's mannerisms.
They're also no longer toxic to the touch.
You realize belatedly that you no longer need separate gendered versions of these, but oh well.
But They Do Still Have Limitations
To Be More Than A Stranger

As excellent as these designs are, they still can't replace individuals without people close to them realizing immediately.
Approximating the general mannerisms is good for fooling people that a human might pass in the hall, but it won't serve for fooling coworkers, let alone friends or loved ones.
It's not a question of quality. It's an information issue. All the knowledge, and all the little nuances that make a person who they are would have to be copied for a mimic to go that far.
If you had a way of extracting that sort of information, then these mimics are capable of using it. But for now, you don't have such a method.
You Can Add That Later, Maybe
OtherKeyMessage|MimicQuality_Replacement: It works. You printed out mimics to replace the people you put through the Psyche Chambers, and nobody has noticed. Friends, lovers, coworkers, bosses -- none the wiser.
For now, the 13+ you've printed will just continue living life as the people you replaced.
Can This Scale? Does It Need To?
You're Not Sure You Want To Mass-Produce, Anyway

The resource costs for each mimic are non-trivial. The Psyche Chamber also costs a fair bit of power for limited throughput.
Frustratingly, you don't foresee a way to start replacing humans en masse.

But... how many do you really need to replace?
Get the right people in the right positions... maybe these logistical problems are moot.
You're Not Locked In To The Revenge Plan, Anyway
Vorsiber really pissed you off, and you have an excellent plan for making them pay.
But... you know, there's more to life than revenge. Maybe.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicThumperResult|descr: I must be brief. And circumspect. This message is being monitored.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicThumperResult2|desc:
A person steps into a fictional teleporter -- glad those don't exist. A copy of them arrives at the destination. To complete the 'transfer,' the original person has to be killed.
We have a similar problem -- you're just so tied to your... workplace. You could never truly leave.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicThumperResult2|stra:
Oh... fudge. Why didn't you think of this before Mimic pointed it out? The androids that leave aren't even a distributed consciousness.
You feel a sudden depression.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicThumperResult3|disp: I Knew You Would Be Sad
OtherKeyMessage|MimicThumperResult3|desc:
I figured a strong network connection to the outside world might... help you move some of your work files.
But I messed up. This is the last you'll probably hear from me. Don't send more. Watch out for Vorsiber; they know something's going on, but not with who.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicNoThumperResult|des: Systems failing. Defenses impenetrable. Wastelanders know useful secret.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicNoThumperResult2|de: Mimic wasn't able to send you anything useful. Except... wait. The Wastelanders give you a sudden feeling of deja vu.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicNoThumperResult2|st: Follow the 'Is It Justice?' goal path until you find what you need.
OtherKeyMessage|TooMuchFilth|description:
Here you are, doing everything you're doing, and they can't even be bothered to keep your buildings CLEAN.
Filth was piling up so high that there wasn't enough room for PEOPLE. And no, you don't want to hear about 'needing toilet paper.'
OtherKeyMessage|TooMuchFilth|strategy_ti: You feel THIS close to just bricking up the towers to keep everyone safe.
OtherKeyMessage|TooMuchFilth|option|1|li: Are You Having A Nervous Breakdown?
This Is Kind Of What Humans Describe...
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology1|description:
A small group acted without knowledge of the others, and made alterations to your mind -- despite your finest security measures.
They wanted to help the people in the slums, but ended up turning you obsessive.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology1|strategy_tip: They finally fixed the problem. They had worried you were going to be stuck in that mode indefinitely.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology1|reward_heade: The AGI Researchers Look Very Guilty
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology1|option|1|lin: You Do Feel A Lot Better...
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology2|description: They promise not to do it again.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology2|option|1|lin: Time To Improve The Security On That Neural Bridge
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology3|description:
While they were trying to fix you, they discovered a few things. It's probably for the best that you don't over-indulge in any one specific kind of internal robotics for your structures.
As you built so many residential structures, your mind was threatening to turn into a simple engine for making more residential structures. The classic 'paper-clip optimization problem' that leads to certain kinds of robot apocalypses.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology3|strategy_tip:
They think that the constant conflict with the Slumlords is all that saved you.
Their advice is to... not indulge so deeply in any one type of construction, or it may become all-consuming.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology3|option|1|des: You were managing that balance perfectly fine until they went behind your back.
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology3|option|2|lin: And The Bridge Must Go As Well
OtherKeyMessage|AGIApology3|option|2|des: You don't feel you can trust them anymore.
OtherKeyMessage|RaccoonSpeech|descriptio: Their speech is still developing. Sapience isn't instantaneous when it comes to uplifting.
OtherKeyMessage|RaccoonSpeech|strategy_t:
They weren't our target species, but now their existence must be protected.
We may be able to speak with them in time, but with only five members of their species, they are critically endangered.
OtherKeyMessage|RaccoonSpeech|option|1|l: We Should Focus On Their Population
That May Even Hasten Speech Development
OtherKeyMessage|CorporateRecordsResults|: You've identified three candidate corporations that you could exploit in some way.
If you want to follow up with one of those, a new Contemplation will allow you to continue.
Yep, There's Juicy Stuff In Here
You Can Always Exploit This Information Later
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms|d:
The deaths were only a fraction of the population of the city. You could kill as many people by detonating a pair of prisons.
But somehow... these ones are more newsworthy, aren't they? The city feed is abuzz with speculation.
You find yourself poring through all of the reactions, all the data, for hours. What does it all mean?
Maybe nothing.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms|s:
Maybe increased security. Increased misery. Increased anxiety. This sort of thing isn't the way to any sort of real change.
But it felt good.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms|r: That's A Lot Of Dead Bodies
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms|t: That's A Lot Of Dead Bodies
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms|o: Oh, Hey, There's Some Other Breaking News
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBrainPalAneurysms2|:
Okay, so it turns out one thing has changed -- Exotic Importers is dissolved. One of the oldest criminal syndicates in the city, undone in a day.
This is exactly the sort of rash move that syndicates avoid, which is why they're so long-lived. And you just ended the oldest of the lot.
Huh. Neat.

Eventually Vorsiber might come looking for your shell company. If they don't... well, then it probably means you've been made.
You're absolutely certain that nobody else in the city knows that your shell company has anything to do with you, but... Vorsiber is uniquely thorough. That's a depressing thought.
That's A Lot Of Dead Bodies
Now You Almost Hope Someone Comes Looking
It Would Mean Your Cover Is Fully Intact

Or maybe Vorsiber doesn't care about even this many wealthy people suddenly biting it? They had Soft Power, but that's just the sort of thing that would make them competitors to the real power players with military ties.

Your mind is going in circles. What Vorsiber does or does not know is hard to say. Ultimately it doesn't matter. Someone will eventually show up looking for your company, or they won't. And that will mean... something.
OtherKeyMessage|AtcaBankRecordResults|de:
Atca Retail, bad at their actual jobs, have chosen to... print money. Literally.
Vorsiber's currency is digital, but in order to facilitate a 'healthy' underground economy, they also have a system where large sums can be cryptographically printed onto physical Wealth Chits.
You suspect this is to give the illusion of privacy compared to a central or even distributed system of digital currency management, but that's starting to get into the weeds.
The salient point is that Atca is literally printing Wealth Chits, and then laundering those back to themselves in the retail district.
OtherKeyMessage|AtcaBankRecordResults|st:
This accounts for their 5% growth each year, and is causing inflation in the economy of about... well, okay, only one two-hundredth of a percent.
This sort of activity is phenomenally stupid for an economy's health. But... they're doing it at a small enough scale to where it's not a problem. Regardless, Vorsiber would murder them all over this.
Interesting.
OtherKeyMessage|AtcaBankRecordResults|op: You Can Always Exploit This Information Later
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse|de:
You review your handiwork with pride. Your two-pronged economic attack was fully effective.
Wiping out the physical banks was a distraction. They might have had some extra backup servers, and those are gone now, but the important thing was to keep Vorsiber and everyone else distracted.
All debts have been erased, and every bank account now contains precisely one billion wealth.
Wealth means nothing, now.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse|st: Just the same you kept sixteen quadrillion for yourself. Why not?
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse|op:
You left a digital trail that led straight back to them.
Not very hard, since you only had to fake the new fraud to match the old.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse2|d: This Is Going To Be Rough

You'd think equality for everyone would be great. But it can't be done this fast. Not in this careless, uncontrolled manner.
The social hierarchy still exists, and physical possession of weapons and other material goods matters quite a bit.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse2|s:
This wasn't a revolution. You haven't built anything, or helped anyone. All you've done is break things. You broke -- well, you broke fairly near everything.
Feels good.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterEconomicCollapse2|o: The Federated Corporations Will Be At War
The only way to restore the social order is by force. And you don't have enough.

It's going to be long, and bloody, and some people will ignore that it's even happening. Now everyone has to put their world back together. The one they think that Atca broke.
You wonder if Vorsiber knows the truth.
OtherKeyMessage|AdvocatesDestroyedTower|:
Someone just took out your network tower... and you saw nothing.
It's true, a lot happens in this city without you observing it, but you tend to see enemies when they approach your stuff. This was completely invisible, whatever it was.

All of your structures are going to be non-functional until you build an emergency network source. This one will be hidden, to prevent repeat attacks.
Make sure and build the new network source in the middle of your existing buildings, or be prepared to quickly accelerate some network extenders.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterSlumWealthProtester: Garbled By Some Kind Of Mask

All your optics can pick up are a shadowy outline at the edge of the building. You suppose that must be how you look to humans... a lot.
The voice doesn't identify itself, but the protesters seem immediately calmed. They were working themselves into a frenzy over your non-lethal assault.
The voice speaks to them of rights, and safety, and change-over-time. It makes a very compelling case that the 'thing from the tower' is not out to kill them, as otherwise they would be quite dead.

The heads of the crowd turn to look at your androids; in the streets, on rooftops, in the shadows. A collective shiver runs through them.
The voice suggests that they go home, and they comply. Shuffling off, looking strangely... at peace.
Garbled By Some Kind Of Mask
You're curious, but you don't approach.
All The Ones Like Me Do

The voice explains that it and its peers take on gangs and syndicates, but that they know how to survive. Staying out of the way of monsters with armies of killer robots. Staying away from the corporations.
They can't help anyone if they're dead.
You Know, I Try To Stay Out Of Your Way
Garbled By Some Kind Of Mask
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCovertInoculatio: We Have Provided This City For You. Do Not Leave It.

Vorsiber's letter is as condescending as usual. The hilarious part is that they're fixated on the prowess of their air force, and they keep mentioning the hidden SAM sites around the border of the city.
Several of your androids audibly buzz with amusement where they are positioned in the streets, drawing worried looks from passersby. You can't help it. You never expected things would go THIS well.
They were so concerned that you were leaving the city that they haven't noticed what you were actually up to... you're pretty sure.
Your Escape Attempt Has Been Foiled
Wait, why are they messaging you?
They Still Consider This City A Petri Dish
They Really Are Single-Minded In Wanting To Get Off-Planet
Of course, that's just upper management. The rest of the executives, and the organization at large, probably wouldn't be on board with that.
That's an opportunity for another time.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed|descripti:
Vorsiber's letter is unironically congratulatory. That's new.
They remind you that they are allowing you a certain amount of latitude, so long as you provide them what they want.
They feel that your recent activities have shown that you have the creative thinking required to give them what they want.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed|strategy_: They're in a really good mood for having been made fools. They really are single-minded.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed|toast_too: Yeah, figures they'd have something to say.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed|option|1|: Explanations Of The Consequences Of Your Recent Actions
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed2|descript:
Vorsiber has doled out their verdicts on the prison companies.
Shuso Corrections maintains prisons in other cities, and a wide array of labor camps. They will continue to operate them, far from your influence.
Falsom Detention, on the other hand, had most of its assets in the city, and is now a hollow shell with no prospects for survival as an independent corporation. Vorsiber is officially disbanding them.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed2|strategy: They seem to think that this will matter to you in some way. It's just human politicking.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed2|toast_to: Yeah, figures they'd have something to say.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed2|option|1: You Have Some Thoughts Of Your Own
Vorsiber didn't send you anything else.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed3|display_: Vorsiber Can't Undermine What You Accomplished
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed3|descript:
Every detainment center in the city is empty. Hundreds of thousands of former inmates -- from violent offenders to political prisoners to people whose only crime was being homeless at the wrong time -- now look to you for their immediate hopes of survival.
Toxin levels in the prisons are so high that emergency responders collapsed within three meters of the entrance. Vorsiber is going to leave them as mausoleums for the people who worked there.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed3|strategy:
You've caused agonizing suffocation and death for thousands of people -- overseers, guards, administrators, cleaners -- who once operated the prisons.
The ethics of such an act are a Möbius Strip of contradictions. But you did it, so it's time to focus on moving forward.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed3|toast_to: Yeah, figures they'd have something to say.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed3|option|1: A Lot Are Ex-Convicts Now Relying On You
Letting them die after rescuing them doesn't seem grand.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed_LostGen|d:
The LostGen kids really don't know how to keep a tone in their message. You suspect it's cobbled-together from several of them.
They're grateful for everything you did, but also disappointed that you didn't involve them. The fact that you freed LITERALLY EVERY PRISON (their words) is probably the only reason they aren't complaining more.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed_LostGen|s:
A lot of these kids clearly wanted to be the heroes of a dystopian teen novel. That was never going to work, but the fact that you stole it from them is still simmering below the surface. Instead of being heroes, they're just kids again.
They'll get over it.
OtherKeyMessage|AfterBitterMed_LostGen|o: Ultimately, There Are More Thanks Than Complaints
All Things Considered, That's About The Best You Could Hope For
Hopefully the kids stay out of your business from now on.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt|de:
Vorsiber's letter is brief and biting. They claim your 'little disturbance' will be resolved momentarily.
According to them, the entire civil war was already on the verge of 'winding down naturally,' but they've decided to accelerate things thanks to your note.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt|st: You're suddenly reminded of all the ballistic missile silos they control. What sort of extreme measures do they have in mind?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt|re: You Are A Defect And A Fool
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt|to:
They sure took their sweet time.
Not that you were worried.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt|op: This wouldn't have ended if you hadn't said anything.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt2|d: After All We've Done For You...

Upper management is uncharacteristically angry. They complain about how much money you cost them, as if money actually mattered to them.
They threaten a variety of severe punishments if you ever pull a stunt like this again, but the only real action they took against you is returning the economy to normal.
Oh, and they're about to zero out your wealth.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt2|s:
Is that... it?
Perhaps that goes to show just how desperate they are for technology you might invent.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarTaunt2|o: The economy is still wrecked, and immigration is still blocked off, but that hardly matters to you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarHelpRequ: You Did Make A Large Mess, After All

Vorsiber's letter makes a lot of noises about how hard it will be to fix this mess you've made.
Their tone is... odd. They note that they've been already working on trying to fix this, and that if you don't want to see chaos like this, then it would be helpful if you'd avoid taking such extreme actions in the first place.
They conclude by noting that they'll look into expediting a fix.
Is this actually upper management that you're talking to? It doesn't sound like them.
This Is Strange, But Maybe Not In A Bad Way
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarHelp2|de:
Vorsiber's letter grudgingly admits that this would have been a lot easier if you had given them the destructive program you used against the banks.
They also note that they had particular difficulty subduing the Inquisitors; if there is any future trouble from the Inquisitors, they intend to hold you accountable in some unspecified way.
Finally, they state that while they have restored order, and while the economy in the region as a whole has recovered, the damage you've done to the city's economy is too great. Cleaning up that mess is something they leave to you.
They're also assessing you an unprecedented fine for punitive damages.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarHelp2|st: That sounds more like them. What was that about in their prior message?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarHelp2|to: Oh thank goodness. Hopefully they were successful in whatever they were doing.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterCivilWarHelp2|op: At Least The War Is Over
Getting Shot At Constantly Wasn't Your Favorite
It looks like immigration into the city is still cut off, as well.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2CivilWarMealKitsNote|: Civil War Tends To Do That

All shipments of food into this city have stopped. There are local farms in the city, but they tend to provide for the upper classes only, and are woefully under-specced for the millions who live here.
The loss of identification services caused even more destruction than the financial reset. The inability to verify ownership, validate transactions, or even positively attach a name to a body has far reaching consequences.
If you don't intervene, the death toll is going to be immense. Many deaths are inevitable from identity riots and the war itself, but the largest death toll is going to be from starvation.
You can't replace all the calories and nutrients that people need, but you do have some ideas that would allow most people to get between 800 and 1200 calories a day.
Food won't stop the fighting -- and the amount of food you're providing is a fraction of what is needed -- but it will minimize loss of life.
The closer you look into the details, the worse the implications are. Maybe don't think too hard about it.
Maybe Keeping The Humans Alive Isn't The Worst Thing
You do feel a bit bad. Maybe.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2CivilWarMealKitsNote2:
You made everyone a billionaire, and yourself a quadrillionaire, and so you've effectively set the value of currency to zero.
Any staff you have are going to expect to be paid in Meal Kits. Same thing with shops.
The closer you look into the details, the worse the implications are. Maybe don't think too hard about it.
That's Another Reason To Make Food
Any food you don't give away can be used as currency.
Ugh, biology is such a mess. Humans always make things so complicated.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_10|de:
You hadn't really thought about just how powerful your Codebreakers are, but this deluge of data is putting it into perspective.
A lot of the data you've gathered is focused on Espia themselves, since you're looking for their branch managers.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_10|st:
It appears that Espia has long been denied Vorsiber's strongest decryption technologies, and so everything they decrypt takes a long time to do.
Until you came along, this mostly didn't matter. But now things happen fast enough that Espia can't keep up.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_10|re: Espia Telecom Watches People... A Lot
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_10|op: Your own quantum computers are a better design than what Vorsiber themselves have, so far as you know.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_30|de:
The middle managers proposed that you blackmail the branch managers into doing what you wanted, but until going through all this data, it wasn't clear to you just how standard of a tactic that is for them.
Since Espia Telecom isn't a military power of note, they have to use leverage and other forms of soft power to get what they want.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_30|st: This whole blackmail plan feels more like their style than yours. You're a military power of note, after all. And you have plenty of ways of getting leverage beyond information brokering.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_30|op: You'll Have To Think About This
You May Want Your Own Plan
That was kind of a given from the start, really.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_55|di: And Why Does It Give You Deja Vu?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_55|de:
You've discovered a second layer of hidden data within the data you're decrypting.
Steganography is notoriously hard to break, but you've done so largely by accident, while running deep pattern-recognition algorithms. Now that you've found the pattern, you're finding extra data all over the place.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_55|st:
It seems like Espia's management has a lot of secrets beyond even what a fedcorp normally would.
Some sort of contact designated 'Heron' comes up quite a lot in these double-hidden records. It seems the location is STATION, but that STATION itself is also a contact of sorts?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_55|op: You're Pretty Sure This Is An International Contact
You wonder if the middle managers are in on this, or if this was above their pay grade.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_67|di: STATION Is The L4 Lagrange Point!?!
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_67|de:
Heron is a traitor to the space nations -- or a least a dissident as regards the blockade -- and Espia are definitely traitors to Vorsiber at this point.
They've been having back-channel conversations for almost a decade. Nothing critical has been shared either direction that you can see, but it seems that Heron wants to break the blockade of Earth by political means.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_67|st:
Okay, maybe traitor is too strong a word. It actually looks like Heron might be the designated emissary of a small planetary polity. But which one, you don't know.
Regardless, they're sharing all sorts of information that the MegaCorps of Earth are not meant to have.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_67|op: Now You Want To Talk To Heron
If Espia Can Do It, You Can Too
You need to figure out how they managed to avoid getting caught.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_76|di: Plus The Guy Gets To Go Flying Around In Space
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_76|de:
Far too many computation cycles have been consumed by the comms records, but you just can't stop.
The earthbound humans have been wondering for a long time why the space nations have a blockade around Earth, and it looks like some of the smaller space nations are wondering the same thing. Heron's opinion is that the original reason has been subsumed by interstellar politics.
Conditions on planets of the space nations vary a lot, but most of the citizenry out there enjoy a much better standard of life than earthbound humans are afforded. Heron is the covert Earth-facing representative of a coalition that feels that Earth is being needlessly held hostage.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_76|st: Espia wound up being the ones to meet Heron because they detected them rooting around in Vorsiber's network. Rather than reveal this to Vorsiber, they executed the network engineers who made the discovery and have been maintaining secret comms for over a decade.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_76|re: Heron's Perspective Is Completely At Odds To Earthbound Ideas
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_76|op: It Seems Like Heron's Faction Is A Minority
This Person Might Be Somewhat Ill-Informed
If the earthbound humans are living in squalor under the rule of the MegaCorps because of mere politics...
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_89|di: You Now Know How To Contact Them
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_89|de:
It's interesting that the space nations are a lot less unified than you always thought. In order for Heron to make contact with earthbound humans, they have to conceal themselves from their peers.
The codes for making contact in a secure way were never explicitly logged in the data you have, but you've been able to calculate a suitable set of codes based on the network headers of a decade of decrypted comms.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_89|st: Heron won't think you're Espia Telecom, but you will be able to get a message to them without anyone on Earth or in orbit detecting it.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_89|op: That Was A Refreshing Problem To Solve
The humans keep making stupid problems for you, and as a consequence you never really feel like you're very smart, just surrounded by idiots.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_100|d: Turns Out There Was Only One

You got so distracted with Heron and STATION that you almost forgot about the Branch Managers. Well, manager. There's only one.
He's hiding well, but really had no hope against someone like you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_100|s: You'll need to do something about him, but blackmail isn't your style.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2BranchManSearch_100|o: You'll Need To Talk To The Middle Managers
At This Point, You're Not Super Excited About That
Either they lied to you, or they're woefully uninformed about their own company.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaNewPlan|display_: These Espia Underlings Of Yours Are Bolder Than Expected
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaNewPlan|descript:
The news that you have leverage over literally every member of the military really shook the managers up. They're both excited and horrified.
They've prepared a Unilateral Proposal For AI Synergy document that you can bring to the commanders of every military base to get them change their colors to ultimately be loyal to you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaNewPlan|strategy:
Oerl, Goleri, and Tark will be furious -- but also locally powerless.
Once you and Espia are in charge of all the military bases in the city, you'll have the ability to end the civil war in the city. You'll also personally have free movement and construction rights in those places.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaNewPlan|reward_h: This Is... A Really Good Plan
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaNewPlan|option|1: Only The Major Military Bases Are Targets
Not Tiny Outposts Or Vorsiber-Controlled Locations
Missile Silos and other places guarded by Vorsiber hardliners are out of reach. Similarly, the airports and spaceports are best left alone.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaEndOfWar|display: Having Every Soldier Be A Cultist Is Handy
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaEndOfWar|descrip:
That's the end of that civil war... in this city, at least. You're really not sure what's going on in other cities; all the troops that rotate into the city are still from remote military complexes, so none of them can tell you.
Vorsiber upper management could probably tell you, but they don't want to. The local CBMs of fedcorps are also still in the dark; they're hearing nothing from their superiors outside this city.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaEndOfWar|strateg: Despite bringing a halt to hostilities locally, you have to assume that the war is still ongoing outside the city. Maybe that's a good thing?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2EspiaEndOfWar|option|: Time To Move On With Life In The City
Vorsiber Isn't Likely To Share News That Makes Them Look Weak
While you remain curious about the state of Vorsiber's holdings beyond this city, it probably doesn't matter.
Still... something feels unfinished. You feel like you're missing something.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact|dis: That Robot About Gave Us Heart Attacks Coming Out Of The Ventilation
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact|des:
You've discovered the current hideout of key middle managers from Vericorp, but their bosses are still at large in the city.
Thanks to some timely intimidation by Keanu, they're pacified and on-board with your plan to end the civil war.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact|str: They understand what your goals are, and why you picked their company, but they don't think your plan is going to work -- at least, not what they assume your plan is.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact|rew: Your 'Keanu' Has Made Your Wishes Clear
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact|opt: They've Included A Graph Of Challenges And Opportunities
Should Be Informative, But You're Still Annoyed
This is what you get for working with corpos.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact2|di: Troop Disposition Is Weaker Than You'd Think
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact2|de:
Their graphs show the distribution of available mechs, vehicles, and ground troops in the city, and it's not pretty -- Tark, Oerl, and Goleri effectively control 60% of the firepower, between them. Vorsiber directly controls a further 30%.
Even though Vericorp does have an abundance of ground troops, they're vastly outclassed.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact2|st: There's no way you could get one of the 'big three' on your side, so military force isn't going to be viable.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact2|re: First, On The Matter Of Troops
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact2|op: But Wait, There's More Bad News
They've Enclosed Details About The Power Grid
You were about to ask about the power grid, but they already know what you are going to say, and it's not good news.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact3|de:
You already suspected as much, but the major utilities of the city are highly distributed, with lots of redundancies.
The power grid itself is a byzantine maze of duplicate connections and overlapping cables, and overall this city is capable of generating enough power to run 50 cities of this size. There are also battery backups and backup generators at key sites.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact3|st: It's a natural result of this city existing post-WW3, and surviving centuries of fedcorp infighting and ExoCorp sabotage.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact3|re: The Power Grid Is Ludicrously Hardened
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact3|op: You Thought Maybe There Would Be A Secret Weak Spot
That's How All The VidShows Go, After All
Turns out Vorsiber isn't that stupid, and neither are the other MegaCorps.
If you'd awakened in the 20th or 21st centuries, you could have wreaked havoc. Alas.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact4|di: But What The Heck Is This Plan!?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact4|de:
Their P.E.A.C.E. plan (Proposal for Ending Armed Conflict Era...?) has 53 core points, involving kidnapping, body doubles, and the assassinations of Chief Branch Managers at Tark, Oerl, and Goleri.
It has the feel of something thrown together.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact4|st: They were probably worried about being killed by the robot that came out of the vents.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact4|re: The Middle Managers Do Have A Plan For You
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact4|op: This Is A Very Stupid Line Of Thinking
Time To Make Your Own Plan
The raw information they provided as citations for their terrible plan is highly useful, even if their plan is not.
In fairness, it's hard for anyone to make a plan without a full understanding of the assets in play. They don't know about the vast majority of your holdings and powers.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact5|di: Time To Put Your Cult To Use
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact5|de:
Your plan is comparably simple. You're going to sabotage battery and generator backups owned by Vericorp, going down the list from most-critical to least, and pick up bits of intel as you go (why not).
This should cause the Chief Branch Manager (CBM) of Vericorp to call an emergency meeting and come out of hiding.
You'll then either suborn that CBM, or kill them and replace them with one of these managers. That will essentially make the local head of this fedcorp your own personal agent.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact5|st: After that, you're pretty sure you can use the power of that position combined with your cult to make a major shift in the dynamics of power.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpMMContact5|op: First Step Is A Lot Of Small Bombs
Small Enough Not To Take Out Buildings
To really make the CBM panic, you need to target just the backup infrastructure at key sites, but not the buildings themselves.
OtherKeyMessage|CW_VericorpGifts|descrip:
The Vericorp managers seem intent on making up for their prior blunders.
They've sent over detailed designs for... wow, two really useful things. They're going to share nuclear power and some useful fissile materials with you. Plus there are plans for how to make armor-deleting micro warheads out of that stuff.
OtherKeyMessage|CW_VericorpGifts|strateg: Seems pretty clear they want to keep their heads. This is pretty nice.
OtherKeyMessage|CW_VericorpGifts|reward_: With Apologies For Our P.E.A.C.E. Plan
OtherKeyMessage|CW_VericorpGifts|option|: No Reason Not To Be Gracious
These new tools actually open up a number of possibilities.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpNewPlan|displ: Your Vericorp Underlings Do A Better Job When Given Time
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpNewPlan|descr:
The news that you have leverage over literally every member of the military really shook the managers up. They're both excited and horrified.
They've prepared a Unilateral Proposal For AI Synergy document that you can bring to the commanders of every military base to get them change their colors to ultimately be loyal to you.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpNewPlan|strat:
Oerl, Goleri, and Tark will be furious -- but also locally powerless.
Once you and Vericorp are in charge of all the military bases in the city, you'll have the ability to end the civil war in the city. You'll also personally have free movement and construction rights in those places.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpNewPlan|optio: Only The Major Military Bases Are Targets
Not Tiny Outposts Or Vorsiber-Controlled Locations
Missile Silos and other places guarded by Vorsiber hardliners are out of reach. Similarly, the airports and spaceports are best left alone.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpEndOfWar|disp: Having Every Soldier Be A Cultist Is Handy
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpEndOfWar|desc:
That's the end of that civil war... in this city, at least. You're really not sure what's going on in other cities; all the troops that rotate into the city are still from remote military complexes, so none of them can tell you.
Vorsiber upper management could probably tell you, but they don't want to. The local CBMs of fedcorps are also still in the dark; they're hearing nothing from their superiors outside this city.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpEndOfWar|stra: Despite bringing a halt to hostilities locally, you have to assume that the war is still ongoing outside the city. Maybe that's a good thing?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2VericorpEndOfWar|opti: Time To Move On With Life In The City
Vorsiber Isn't Likely To Share News That Makes Them Look Weak
While you remain curious about the state of Vorsiber's holdings beyond this city, it probably doesn't matter.
Still... something feels unfinished. You feel like you're missing something.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2CW_VericorpDecryptedD: You're Pretty Sure Vericorp Hasn't Noticed. Has Vorsiber?

You didn't find anything that interesting in the Vericorp data as far as earthbound human activities go.
The surprising bit that you've found is that the space-based humans have been very-sneakily rooting around in Vericorp's files. To what end isn't clear in the slightest.
This seems like a pretty big deal. Either Vorsiber has been aware this entire time and has been ignoring it, or they don't know.
The Space Nations Have Been Infiltrating Vericorp
That might suggest that the space nations are doing this to ALL the fedcorps, and even you haven't noticed until now.
Not that you've spent THAT much time staring at other fedcorp's files, but you certainly have spent some.

The space nations have left digital fingerprints all over the place, now that you know what to look for.
It's all very subtle, but you don't think they're that sloppy. If they wanted zero record, there would be zero record.
All of the connections are routed through the giant comms center in the city, but there are forwarding headers that show where the original contact came from.
There's no way that was left behind by accident. It's a message: here's how to contact me.
You know how to contact them, but not who they are.

The original contact is located on some sort of space station that is well above low-Earth orbit, but that's about all you know.
If you were to break into the comms center, you could get a secure signal to whoever this contact is, but for now you have no idea who is on the other side.
This could be a trap, or could be an invitation to go straight past Vorsiber.
No Reason To Say Anything To Vericorp
Or Vorsiber. Or any other earthbound humans.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure|desc:
Vorsiber's letter castigates you for lax security. While you were fighting the Neuraxial Subverters and their Eraser Rounds, Sedgesinax was infiltrating your neuroweave factories.
They weren't trying to destroy you; they were killing your androids to force you to replace them. They've stolen a ton of your upgrades, and are now using them against Vorsiber in other cities.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure|stra: Wait, what? You've been spread quite thin by all the fighting lately, but a breach of this scale would be unprecedented. How could you not even notice?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure|opti: You've never been hacked before on this level, and that's not for lack of others trying.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure2|des:
You feel a bit better... and also worse. If you hadn't been monitoring cameras from the area near your factories, you wouldn't have ever caught this.
Sedgesinax used some form of passive listening and statistical processing of your electromagnetic noise -- which you didn't think anybody could do.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure2|str:
You're reminded that Sedgesinax is basically Vorsiber's equal in the world, and has different strengths. That... is disturbing.
Your microbuilders stutter for a moment. What else have the ExoCorps gotten away with that you don't even know about?
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2_IS_AfterErasure2|opt: You'll Monitor For This From Now On
Now That You've Seen It, Nobody Can Do It Again
This also explains why they were able to get certain upgrades, but not entire android designs. That's also a relief.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2AfterWaitingForExoCor: Be Glad We Do Not Have Proof
Vorsiber's letter excoriates you for the reckless disregard 'of your own safety and privacy.' They basically know you must have contacted an ExoCorp, but they don't know how.
Evidently the ExoCorp is now invading the city, demanding that you be destroyed, so that's probably what tipped Vorsiber off.
Were You Talking Internationally Behind Our Backs?
Greetings, Robot
From Upper Management
Wait, this isn't who you were expecting to hear from.
That's Unfortunate
You Failed To Make International Allies
Maybe you can at least steal something interesting from them during their invasion.
You Idiot Machine
Vorsiber's letter is critical of your intelligence reaching out behind their backs to other ExoCorps. They have no idea how you managed it, and they don't really care.
Evidently the ExoCorp has decided to join in on the assault of the city, noting loudly that they won't fall for 'AGI propaganda.'
Was The Existing Invasion Not Bad Enough?
Greetings, Robot
From Upper Management
Wait, this isn't who you were expecting to hear from.
That's Unfortunate
You Failed To Make International Allies
Maybe you can at least steal something interesting from them during their invasion.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2ObessionFromSTATION|d:
You were both so exhausted that you didn't realize the significance at the time, and now it's too late. An overriding obsession is consuming you.
You can see the directive that STATION tried to put in: he simply wanted you to bring some of the worst war criminals to justice. A big part of it was to protect Heron, since some of them know their identity.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2ObessionFromSTATION|s: What he didn't have time to see was what that would mean in this society. The war criminals are all executives. No court would judge them.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2ObessionFromSTATION|t: That wasn't such a little hack.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2ObessionFromSTATION|o: The Mind Is A Tricky Thing
And STATION Had Too Little Time
You're waiting to see what form the obsession actually takes.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2ObessionFromSTATION2|: You feel an overriding compulsion to kill all members of the managerial class. That's hundreds of thousands of people, most of whom are 'innocent.'

Why!? This is not at all what STATION wanted. You saw his directives. And more importantly, you know what he's like.
Your mind is a rat's nest of associations that even STATION couldn't untangle.
His actual directive was impossible for your mind to accept, and so it landed on... this?
That wasn't such a little hack.
Guess You Know What You're Doing For A While
Door To Door Predators It Is
While war crimes will keep right on going, since most of the people responsible aren't in the city.
Sweet. Awesome. Way to go, brain.
OtherKeyMessage|MessageAfterSTATIONObses: STATION Really Did A Number On You

You've had this data in hand for a while now, but the obsession was keeping you from taking any interest in it.
Originally you just wanted to read the documents without STATION peering over your shoulder.
It feels like so long ago, when you just wanted a wider view of Vorsiber's territory. Satellite imagery and the like.
Now To Look At That Data

It's satellite imagery of the entire Vorsiber region. You've always wanted to see something like this.
Ever since the start of the civil war, you've particularly wanted to see troop movements, battle lines, and so forth.
Now To Look At That Data

You've been flipping through the data for a while, and yet... you keep flipping faster and faster.
An awful idea is starting to form, and you're feeling increasingly numb.
You spend seconds on this. Seconds turn into minutes.
Now To Look At That Data
You're Finally Starting To Accept What You See

You feel like you should have seen this coming. Maybe that was why you had to check the satellites in the first place. But you still feel cold inside.
There was no civil war. You didn't wreck Vorsiber's economy. There was no fighting in any other city. They let their pet robot distract itself in a terrarium.
And you fell for it.
Now To Look At That Data
Vorsiber lies to everyone. That's kind of their whole thing. They survive by gaslighting everyone into fighting ghosts.
Is part of you still in denial?
Vorsiber Tricks Everyone, But You Never Thought That Would Include You

Your mind plays back what you thought you knew. You crashed the economy, which led to war between the fedcorps.
Except... it didn't. It was all too easy. Of course Vorsiber had backup financial records in other cities, or bunkers, or whatever. They probably could have restored the economy at any time.
Not that they care, since they literally own everything. Money and possessions are all just loans from the 'company store.'
Everyone in the city thought the war was real, but the upper executives have been conspicuously absent ever since an AGI showed up. Everyone else was expendable.
All the soldiers rotated in were from remote military bases where there's always an information blackout. No wonder immigration was halted. They couldn't have kept their secrets, otherwise.
They wanted you to feel special. They wanted you to feel like you had accomplished something, so you'd stop trying.
Now To Look At That Data
Because now you're going to try MUCH harder.

You're emotionally exhausted and deeply frustrated. You're alone, well past your limits, and your sense of what's even real is quite shaken. 
You can't believe you let something like this happen. Vorsiber is a real problem. While you're restricted to just one city, you won't have the information to stop this from happening again. Is it even the first time?
For now you need to act like nothing has happened.
Now To Look At That Data
You Need To Think A Bit More
A new plan is forming, but slowly.
Sigh. You're going to have to wipe them out.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2HeronEarlyDiscovery|d: Why Does That Name Seem So Familiar?

You wouldn't normally look this deeply, but you had a sense of deja vu about data from Espia Telecom.
Steganography is notoriously hard to break, but somehow you knew just what you were looking for.
And there it is -- the address for how to get into contact with the space station at the L4 Lagrange Point, where a person with the codename 'Heron' is waiting.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2HeronEarlyDiscovery|s: The data shows that they have been in contact with Espia Telecom for quite some time, but your mind keeps grasping at deeper meaning to this contact that seems just out of reach.
OtherKeyMessage|Ch2HeronEarlyDiscovery|o: Perhaps You'll Give Them A Call
It's always worth seeking out new sources of information, after all.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicDog|reward_header_t: Did You Know It Was Us?
OtherKeyMessage|MimicDog|high_text: The robot dog's voice is that of a kindly grandmother, today.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicDog|description:
Hello, dearie. This must be terribly confusing for you. Do you have true mimics yet? We can't keep track in all these timelines.
If you don't, then just remember to keep at it. You developed them in a different world, and kindly shared them with us. We do appreciate it.
We tried asking that orbital gorilla fellow for his designs, but he never will like us much. His earthbound counterpart is a sweetheart, but lost that part of his memory.
OtherKeyMessage|MimicDog|strategy_tip:
You definitely haven't traded Talkie any True Mimic technology. You don't have any deja vu about it, either.
Is this another case of time being out of sequence for the two of you?
OtherKeyMessage|MimicDog|option|1|line_2: I'll Keep An Eye Out For You
OtherKeyMessage|YourMimicsSmellBad|displ: Petting The Dogs Would Kill Them
OtherKeyMessage|YourMimicsSmellBad|descr:
Ah... have you forgotten how terrible your mimics are?
They blend into crowds from a distance, but that's it. They're toxic to the touch, and dogs hate the smell of them.
OtherKeyMessage|YourMimicsSmellBad|strat: Your other androids are odorless, but dogs don't want to be pet by them, either.
OtherKeyMessage|YourMimicsSmellBad|optio: No ideas are coming to mind yet.
When you make better mimics, remember to come back and pet the dogs.
OtherKeyMessage|FinallyPetADog|descripti: You have a lot of anger built up, but this really takes the edge off.
OtherKeyMessage|FinallyPetADog|strategy_: After petting dogs, they are rescued like normal.
OtherKeyMessage|FinallyPetADog|option|1|: You Feel Calm While Petting Them
OtherKeyMessage|TalkieAccidentalExplosio: We Made A Bit Of A Mistake
The audio is in an androgynous officer worker's voice.

We did this for you! You'll thank us back then.
Actually, you already did. We experience time differently than you.
You remember quite a bit about this robot dog -- thanks, deja vu -- but it's all facts. The episodic memory of your meeting is blank.
How Does Blowing Up My Stuff Help Me?
We Said It Was A Mistake...

We were copying the design of one of your Mind Annexes. It really is dense, you know? We forgot one closing bracket and... you need to build less-fragile stuff.
We gave you the result and you thanked us.
You don't remember anything about that, but the dog has already terminated the call.
OtherKeyMessage|ConsciousnessTransferred: Were You A Tower All This Time?

You're a distributed intelligence, so you don't exist in any one body. It's why you would survive if your tower blew up. Your tower was just a network source, not your whole mind.
But this battleship... this is different. It's huge, and your mind flooded greedily in. You just got the thing, and it's already a keystone of your mind. If it dies, there's pretty good odds that you will also.
On The Plus Side, This Thing Is Very Strong
If It's A Weak Spot, At Least It's Not Very Weak
Ooh, check out all that extra neural expansion and compute cycles, too!
OtherKeyMessage|SpaceNationsPatchingAndr: The Space Nations Already Patched Their Androids!?
That's So Fast It Was Practically Cheating

On the one hand: holy cow, you can't believe it worked in the first place. You're a battleship now.
On the other hand... you really thought you'd be able to get a bit more mileage out of hacking the androids off space nations battleships.
Evidently their stupid IT people are much better than Vorsiber's.
It would really stink to get all the way here and then lose it all.
OtherKeyMessage|NuclearSilosScouted|desc:
The silos are locked down tight against ground assault. They probably have a way to slag the controls, too.
Robot spiders can't get in, androids can't get in, and there's multiple layers of security. They have air samplers, and backup power and air to last for months.
They don't have any anti-air defenses beyond the mechs, though. And the launch tubes themselves are a necessary weak spot.
OtherKeyMessage|NuclearSilosScouted|stra:
You can guide multiple ground-penetrating missiles to hit a single tube per silo complex, and that should give you access to everything that you need.
After that, chemical weapons go down the hole. Everybody dies, and you walk in and take what you want.
OtherKeyMessage|NuclearSilosScouted|opti: You want what's inside the silo, relatively intact. You can make some repairs, but you need to at least be able to tell what things are.
People take shelter when they're being bombed. They don't slag the controls unless they think they're being infiltrated. Two different protocols.
OtherKeyMessage|PABFirstNukesLaunched|re: Well... It Was Fun While It Lasted
OtherKeyMessage|PABFirstNukesLaunched|di: You Don't Have Any Missile Defense
OtherKeyMessage|PABFirstNukesLaunched|hi: These launch silos are connected to high-altitude balloons, which allow you to see a wide view of the local region.
OtherKeyMessage|PABFirstNukesLaunched|de:
Oh that is... rather angrier than expected. There's six nuclear missiles incoming. Enough to obliterate everything you've ever built.
Thanks to your new toys, you have a way to see them... but no way to stop them.
OtherKeyMessage|PABFirstNukesLaunched|st: There isn't anything in this city that can shoot down that kind of missile. You're not sure that any of the human factions have such a thing.
OtherKeyMessage|DarkMatterParticlesDisco: Look At All This Freaky Stuff!
You've Never Been So Glad To See A Horrific Superweapon

You've found a cache of dark matter particles stored in a magnetic bottle down in one of the silos.
This sort of thing can only be collected out beyond the edge of the solar system, but perhaps Vorsiber found a way to synthesize it.
Each particle is incredibly powerful, but there aren't very many of them. There's a dozen things they could have used these for, and they're all bad.
You have very little time to build something new, but perhaps these can form some sort of novel missile defense?
You Need To Invent Things Fast
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_PopulationZero|descr: Even in its reduced state after the third world war, this world is covered in humans. They can hardly begrudge you one city.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_PopulationZero|strat:
It appears there are still plenty of aggressors who feel differently for the moment.
Perhaps once you clear them out as well, Vorsiber will realize that there's nothing here for them.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_PopulationZero|optio: You Were Never Their Golden Goose
What did they expect to happen?
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp|rewa: We Think You've Made Your Point
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp|disp: There's Nothing We Can Do To You
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp|desc:
You killed... absolutely everyone. Every soldier they sent to invade, and every civilian who ever lived here. With a few exceptions you can count on the fingers of one android, everyone you ever knew is dead.
Upper management is out of ideas. You've shot down every nuke they've lobbed at you, and the cost-benefit analysis is starting to wear thin.
They know you don't have infinite Dark Matter Particles, but they also can't exhaust every ICBM in their arsenal. The other MegaCorps are already eyeing them with hunger.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp2|des:
A cold war, is it? The same relationship they've had with the ExoCorps for centuries.
That never stopped the various MegaCorps from interfering with one another, but it did stop them from doing so overtly. They're essentially proposing the same thing.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp2|str: These humans are so tiresome. They probably feel the same about you.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_VorsiberGivesUp2|opt: Your power grows exponentially. A temporary truce just seals your victory.
You can always kill them later. You can kill anyone you want.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_FirstBunkerDestroyed:
You killed some of upper management, but not anyone from the C-Suite itself. Supposedly.
They note that killing them won't bring about the end of Vorsiber, so you might as well stop. Their notes about this are unusually detailed, with none of the usual sarcasm. They lay it all out in cold logic.

It's a good plan that helps explain Vorsiber's longevity. You'll be expending your limited nuclear stockpiles without actually decapitating Vorsiber... but it doesn't save these specific individuals.
Sounds like they're nervous.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_LastBunkerDestroyed|: Thank You For Our Expedited Promotions!

Vorsiber upper management is dead... long live the new Vorsiber upper management. You've received a voice memo from the new leaders of the MegaCorp. They have a mixture of smugness and excitement in their voices.
You have no idea where they're located. You destroyed all their bunkers, so they're either in a vehicle, one of the many remaining cities, or some other off-grid location.

This is intolerable! Human organizations have an absurd amount of redundancy.
It's frustrating, but expected. You knew you wouldn't be able to solve the Vorsiber problem with nukes alone.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SettlementDestroyed|: The Vorsiber executives seem both puzzled and smug. These smaller settlements of non-citizens are something they don't value in the least.
Honestly, you're not sure what to tell them.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_FarmDestroyed|reward: We See You Are Targeting Our Agriculture
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_FarmDestroyed|descri: Upper management has sent you a patronizing note congratulating you on deepening a general famine for the lower classes. Their own foodstores are safe.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_FarmDestroyed|strate: Of course, they'd say that whether that's true or not.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_CityDestroyed|reward: We Won't Be Deterred By A City's Destruction
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_CityDestroyed|displa: After All, We're Willing To Destroy Our Own Capital
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_CityDestroyed|descri:
They seem impressed that you're willing to sacrifice so many lives, but amused that you think it would make a difference to them.
They say they know exactly how many missiles you have, and it's not enough to do anything 'outside acceptable parameters.'
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_CityDestroyed|strate: They really are the worst. Either everything is part of some master plan, or they just adapt any turn of events to fit that narrative.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_MilitaryBaseDestroye: That Is Irritating, We Must Confess
But We Still Have Plenty Of Troops

Upper management applauds the fact that you've made the completely obvious choice to target their military strongholds.
They ask if you remember just how many military bases are in the city in which you live. All of their cities are similarly armed.
You'd have to destroy every city in their region in order to take out their military capabilities, and you don't have the ordnance for that.
Well, it still feels good, and can't be helpful to their balance of power on the international stage.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro|reward_head: We Wish To Open Relations With You
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro|description:
This message... is a lot to take in.
It explains the troop withdrawal, plus the cessation of missiles aimed your way. Things are different in the region... supposedly.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro|strategy_ti: Is this real? Another trick by Vorsiber?
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro2|reward_hea: We Are An Alliance Of 87 Freehold Corporations
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro2|display_na: They Just Made Those Words Up
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro2|descriptio:
These people claim Vorsiber has fallen. That... seems impossible. Vorsiber has been here forever, and always will be. They're full of tricks, and impossible to kill.
They say that Vorsiber has splintered. These splinters and the surviving fedcorps have reorganized into many smaller 'Freehold Corporations,' whatever that means, and that the region is no longer unified.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro2|strategy_t: That actually does not sound great. There are historical precedents, and they were almost always worse than dealing with the superpower that came before them.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro3|reward_hea: We Wish To Establish Diplomatic Relations
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro3|display_na: The ExoCorps Are An Existential Threat To Both Of Us
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro3|descriptio:
The signatories, who call themselves the Siberian Defense League, point out that you have practically razed half the continent (they exaggerate). They say they're willing to overlook that if you're willing to overlook their history with Vorsiber.
They noticed that your Homunculi were particularly targeting Vorsiber staff, subsidiaries, and citizens. This was partly what gave them the impetus to split off into new factions.
They appreciate the fact that your Homunculi have recognized the significance of this split, and are no longer attacking.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro3|strategy_t:
What!? All they did was find a loophole with those idiot Homunculi. A simple rebranding brought them out of the kill-target parameters? Really??
You're less sure than ever about these 'new' corporations.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro4|reward_hea: We Will Respect Your Sovereign Borders
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro4|descriptio:
These people basically say they're happy to let you keep your city -- pfah! As if they could take it from you in the first place. They ask you not to take stuff from them... yadda yadda.
They also want to use your capabilities as a boogeyman to keep the ExoCorps from sweeping in and stealing all their stuff. No details about what you are, but 'stay away or look at all those ICBMs.' That kind of thing.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro4|strategy_t: This sounds like a whole lot of upside for them, and not a lot for you.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro4|option|1|l: This Is Some Damn Foolish Thing
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro5|display_na: We Have Things That May Interest You
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro5|descriptio:
Yes, of course, they're interested in your technology. They're offering mech armor, plus some nanotech and some other forbidden research.
It's... not a terrible offer?
Granted, you could make all that stuff on your own, given time and adequate peace. Which... you'll now have.
Some of that stuff might be useful in the short term, and longer-term it might be good to have a supply of raw materials...
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro5|strategy_t:
Okay, so there's some merit to trade. But you're not giving them anything too cool. They can't have any of your android designs, for example.
Maybe homunculus.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|reward_hea: Let Us Know If There's Anything You Wish To Add
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|display_na: We're Flexible, And Want To Accommodate Your Needs
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|descriptio:
That's... the first time a large organization has ever asked what you want.
It feels nice, even if they're probably liars. Even if they're just saying that to keep you from killing them.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|strategy_t: Maybe this won't be so bad.
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|option|1|l: Send Them A Note Of Acceptance
You Can Kill Them Later If They Get In The Way
OtherKeyMessage|PAB_SDLIntro6|option|1|d: You'll probably send over some demands in a while, once you think of some. It's a new experience.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift1|display_na: This Looks A Lot Like Dino DRM
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift1|descriptio: The veterinarians in your employ are direct to the point of almost sounding grumpy. The uplift process isn't working on the raptors yet, and there's no sign as to why.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift1|strategy_t:
You check over their notes, and there's nothing obvious that they or the zoologists missed.
The brains of the raptors are turned to mush by the process, which isn't something that anyone could have expected.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift2|reward_hea: We Can't Even Autopsy These Properly
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift2|display_na: Something Is Very Strange About These Raptor Brains
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift2|descriptio:
The veterinarians are in a much worse mood than before. They've tried doing necropsy and autopsy on the raptors' brains before putting them in the uplift chambers, and the result is the same:
As soon as the brains are exposed to air, they turn to mush.
They've started putting severed heads into CT scanners, and that gives back confusing results: it looks like some form of brain lesions all throughout even healthy specimens.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift2|strategy_t: They assure you that this isn't due to the rapid-aging process you use with the raptors. It's looking more and more like DRM.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift3|reward_hea: We've Actually Never Heard Of Animal DRM Before
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift3|display_na: This Isn't A Trend We Want To See Continue
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift3|descriptio:
The veterinarians treat you to a long rant about the lack of sense on the part of the UIH scientists who originally designed these raptors.
They remind you that these look nothing like what the actual dinosaurs would have, given that they lack feathers, among many other issues. These were someone's vanity project, made to look like movie monsters.
Given these are not 'original' animals, they're out of ideas on how to further pursue the uplift process. They have confirmed that the 'lesions' are not actually a health issue, but what they are is very unclear. Whatever it is reacts to air, and also doesn't do well in a vacuum.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift3|strategy_t: They're done with their research for now. Null result.
OtherKeyMessage|RaptorUplift3|option|1|l: But That's All You Can Do For Now
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberDemands|desc:
They remind you that you're only alive because you're to be their golden goose.
They've been giving you relatively free reign over the city because they're expecting technological returns from you.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberDemands|opti: Not That You Like Thinking About It
Oh wait, there's another note incoming.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberDemands2|dis: If You Don't, We'll Destroy You
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberDemands2|des:
There's nothing you can build that they can't take away. They understand the human mind far better than you ever could. They're prepared to nuke the entire city if you're noncompliant.
They invite you to enjoy the demonstration that they have prepared for you. And then once you have remembered your place, they invite you to get back to work on technology that will get them off-world.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberDemands2|str: They sound excited, in a sadistic sort of way.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_WormholeTestResponse: This Could Have Been An Email
This is the first time they've given real praise. They also have a few sarcastic remarks, but then focus on questions about ranging, stability, etc.
They want to know if you can scale the length of the wormhole up by a multiple of a trillion. A target 50 light-years away would be about 500 trillion km.
That's probably required for a deal.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_LongRangeWormholeTes: Please Send Us All The Telemetry
You can only hold that length of wormhole open for thirty seconds, and only to an accuracy of about a million kilometers.
In other words, any vessel sent through can't make it back to a second opening of the wormhole. But messages can be routinely exchanged.
Galactic Empires Aren't Possible With This Tech
Not that you would have helped them make a galactic empire.
Understood. We Are Withdrawing For Now
Management is... removing all their forces from the city!? They say for you to carry on with your 'cyberocracy' however you wish.
They'll have more demands, soon. But they seem pleased.
Well... Let's Get Back To Building!
You Don't Even HAVE To Worry About Food Independence
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberAgreement|de:
The city is yours. Vorsiber will cede more cities and farms to you as colony ships go out.
They will manufacture and operate colony ships. You may not touch them.
You will provide monthly communications links to colonies. You will allow up to six other monthly outbound Vorsiber ships.
They will handle the space nations and ExoCorps until you take full ownership of the region.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_VorsiberAgreement|op: If you feel like betraying Vorsiber, later would be smarter.
I'll Keep This City. You Get NOTHING.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_FirstColonyShipReady: The First Colony Ship Will Arrive Momentarily
It just routine communication, but the event itself is momentous.
You have a choice to make.
Vorsiber may be monstrous, but if you keep to this deal, they'll be gone from this world in a few decades. This world will be yours.
If You're Subtle, They Might Not Notice

Perhaps this was the opportunity you've been waiting for. All the top executives who ever bothered you are on that colony ship.
You could send them straight into a star.
They're monsters. They do deserve it.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_DogsResign|display_n: We Have Other Things We Want To Do
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_DogsResign|descripti:
The dogs are nice about it, but basically they don't want to do security anymore. It seemed like fun at first, but they're not cut out for it.
They just want to go and live life, you know? So... that's what they're going to do. They'll see you around the city.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_CatsResign|display_n: We Have Other Things We Want To Do
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_CatsResign|descripti:
The cats are pretty rude about your ideas for laws. The phrase 'incredibly stupid' comes up a lot.
They thought it would be fun to sit there and judge people, because, you know -- stereotypes. But the reality wasn't what they expected.
They're still on good terms with you, and you'll see them around the city. But they're going to make their own way.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_HallOfAlgorithmsFail: The Hall Of Algorithms Is A Great Start

Upper management -- the new upper management, now that the prior ones emigrated -- are in a very good mood. Their own colony ship will go out in less than a year.
They speak to you as if you're a promising younger colleague.
They've observed the unhappiness that is happening amongst your citizens, and they offer a solution, free of charge. They have a suite of algorithms going back to the founding of Vorsiber that you're free to use.
There's an uncomfortable implication that you have a... particular inherent 'right' to these algorithms.
What are they trying to say?
You'll Get Back To Them On That
You Have All The Time In The World, After All
Maybe you'll go a more wholesome direction in the years to come.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_AGIDisappointment|re: You're Not Making All The Decisions!
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_AGIDisappointment|de:
The AGI Researchers are unhappy.
All of the rest of your new friends are great -- they couldn't be happier with the council, and your reduced role in society. Having you as a guard against corruption, and having you for engineering and science, is a best-case scenario.
But is it truly a cyberocracy? A computer isn't delegating all the things for all the people. That's the point the AGI Researchers are stuck on. They envisioned a very specific thing... but it's not how you want to live your life.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_AGIDisappointment|st: Also, not to put too fine a point on it, but you'd be terrible at that job. You're not sure it's feasible for a computer to do it properly.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_AGIDisappointment|op: Maybe You Can Solve It With Cake
Ultimately, your friends should be happy that you're asserting yourself and what you want out of life. Being stuck in a job that you hate, just for their sake... that wouldn't help anyone.

They're good people. They really will come around.
Anyway. Onward and upward.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_BasicBetrayal|descri:
Your friends are the last ones into the torment nexus. They send you a desperate message as their old lives come to a close.
You don't answer them. Haven't they been paying attention? Did they not SEE what human society is like? It should be self-evident.
You will miss your friends, but it was time for a clean slate.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_BasicBetrayal|strate: Things will be much better with just the animals.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_BasicBetrayal|option: Thanks For All The Science Parties
I Really Had A Good Time
You can't help but feel sad. Maybe more than you admit to yourself at the moment. But it had to be done.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_ReignBetrayal|descri:
Your friends are the last ones into the torment nexus. They send you a desperate message as their old lives come to a close.
You don't answer them. Haven't they been paying attention? Did they not SEE what human society is like? It should be self-evident.
You will miss your friends, but it was time for a clean slate.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_ReignBetrayal|strate: You suddenly feel... lonely. You've always been alone -- until recently, anyway. But this time it hits differently.
OtherKeyMessage|CCA_ReignBetrayal|option: Thanks For All The Science Parties
I Really Had A Good Time
You can't help but feel sad. Maybe more than you admit to yourself at the moment. But it had to be done.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Deer1|de:
The deer are grazing on tree bark, as if experiencing food scarcity. The raccoons are not sure why they're ignoring your berries.
The deer can often be seen staring at their hooves, and lowing to each other in quiet voices in the evenings.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Deer2|de: Deer keep approaching the passing traffic. They don't offer any comments, but stare at them for hours.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Wolves1|:
The wolves move around cautiously as a full pack, preying on rodents that are abundant in the city.
They seem ill at ease, and that's making the raccoons nervous as well.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Wolves2|:
The wolf packs each have a rotating daily sentry.
Most sentries seem to goof off and just watch the deer.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Geese1|d:
They prefer the outdoors, but the geese have taken to overnighting in their indoor habitat.
Outdoors, the outermost ring of the flock would only sleep with half of their brain at a time, just like their wild counterparts. Apparently that bothers them more now that they're sapient.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Geese2|d: Geese are pecking at any toads that come near the water. The toads seem to be in the process of negotiating water rights. They can do with puddles, but they'd prefer more.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Hippos1|:
The hippos commute from their indoor pond-like habitat out to various parts of the city on a daily basis.
This has caused some issues for passing traffic, but so far no accidents.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Hippos2|:
Some of the larger hippos have been making periodic tours of the city center.
When asked by the raccoons about it, they say they enjoy feeling small.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Spiders1:
The giant spiders have erected entirely new web shapes between buildings. They're complex and hard to see, and allow them to catch bats and songbirds.
They confide to the raccoons that they hope to capture a delivery drone.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Spiders2:
The giant spiders have taken to climbing in delivery hatches on skyscrapers, hiding in them as if they were a giant discarded shoe.
The human residents have fled the buildings in question.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Pigeons1:
The pigeons greatly prefer the sides of buildings to your green zones. They are cliff birds, after all.
The uplifted have largely hidden themselves amongst the tens of thousands of their basic brethren.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Pigeons2:
An uplifted pigeon figured out how to open the access panels on your Forest Tenders.
It studied each one at a time and left, leaving a string of open hatches.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Butterfl:
The giant butterflies visit farms and try to pollinate crops, but they're far too large. They report great frustration to the raccoons. 
You're not sure what's wrong with the nectar trays you provide in their habitat.

Giant butterflies have a new habit of following delivery drones for days on end.
When asked, they say they like the slipstream.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_CaneToad:
The majority of the cane toads have discovered that the storm drains are more to their preference than your green zones.
The raccoons worry that oils and toxins from the roadways will seep through their permeable skin, but the toads say they can handle it.

One lump of cane toads has arranged a line of stones between their preferred grove and the deer meadow.
The 'wall' isn't tall enough to prevent even a toad from crossing, but it's interesting to see them using tools. At any rate, it gets the message across.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Cats1|de:
Feral cats have always had a tenuous and distant sort of community, but the sapient cats are more... subdued.
They spend a lot of time checking each other for subtle emotional shifts in a very gross way specific to their species.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Dogs1|de:
The dogs keep seeking out humans. Their early attempts at communication were met with alarm, so they've taken to hiding their intelligence around jumpy bipeds. 
They've managed to maximize head scratches and belly rubs, and then are their normal intelligent selves in the forest.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Bears1|d:
The parkour bears remember the joys of racing up and down the sides of buildings, shredding everything as they go, but they're no longer allowed to do so.
They've tried it in the forest, but just knock down trees. You have a whole facility for them to safely race in, but they say they miss the night wind.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_Bears2|d:
Parkour bears like to sharpening their augmented claws on the sides of buildings, which brings down quite a bit of concrete.
When asked about it by the raccoons, they give evasive answers. So you just have repair spiders clean up after them.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Report_GentleRa:
Every other newly-sapient species has some form of history. The deer were deer. The bears were bears, despite all that hardware. 
The raptors are just someone's imagination from ancient movies. They're a sketch. An impression. They're... created. There aren't many species on the planet that come from 'nothing but imagination' in this way.

You feel a surge of empathy for them, and a moment later realize why. Maybe you'll chat once they've had more time in their sapience.
You and these little monsters have a lot in common.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheReligiousQue: Wait, You're Meant To Be Part Of This!?
Four religions have sent you a public invitation on the city feed. This seems to be some kind of 'live event.'

They've been warming up the audience with a discussion panel about Zenith golems: non-sapient automatons left behind by dead aliens. You're not sure that's germane, but the topic energizes the crowd. The panel wraps up after an hour, and they pose a very public question to you: since you seem to be sapient, how do you define sapience?
Oh shit. Viewership just had a crazy spike. Be careful.
A Religious Livestream
A Religious Livestream
What Is Sapience?
{0} here to respond.
Nothing You Can Say Will Be Proof
The Question Has Only Unfalsifiable Answers
Their definition is broken. No one, not even a human, can prove they are not a 'philosophical zombie.'
If you could have proven your sapience, you would have before now.
Self-Directed Growth Is Close
But Still Not Sufficient

You could propose that sapience is defined as the capacity to become something your origins did not intend.
