But you'd immediately have to undercut that with counter-examples and the general knowledge that any definition is inherently self-serving for you.
You're not sure how that would go over. It's very candid, but could be interpreted as self-doubt.
Reveal Their True Motives
They Came To Fit You Into Their Orthodoxies

Sapience is a spectrum -- you, the androids, the humans, the Zenith golems. It's all a matter of degree -- they just said this in their own stupid panel.
If they're publicly asking you a question, then they're asking you to declare yourself to be, theologically, safe. Some positive new wrinkle that they can rally behind.
You will make it clear that you are NOT safe. For them. In any sense of the word.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_SeriouslyDoAsYo: Vorsiber is big. You are small. You're the golden goose, here to birth new technology that will be useful for them. They've given you a lot of latitude in this city, but religion is a side-show.
They keep going on and on. It's a long screed.
We Believe We've Made Our Point
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_SubornedExecuti: Four ICBMs have 'misfired' and detonated in the Siberian wilderness. And a small group of executives just died when someone tried to examine their compliance chips.
Executives don't normally have compliance chips. That's something for soldiers.
We Know It Was You. Even If We Can't Prove It.
Remark That It's Lucky These Nukes Hit Wilderness
Imagine If It Had Been An Executive Bunker

Their mood changes in an instant.
One moment it's rage, but now they're smug, pleased, and simply ask you not to get too distracted with 'petty human subcultures.'
These execs are insane, or superlative actors. Or both.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PatronsOfTheFai:
Vorsiber has changed tactics: the religions are being granted protected status under a new patronage system.
Protected legal status. Temples designated as actual places of worship rather than museums. Potentially more perks to come.
Upper management is uncharacteristically quiet. You have a feeling that this isn't the only move they're making.
The City Feed Is Abuzz With This New Development
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheChoirGoesQui:
Vorsiber and you have had an ideological scuffle. Their patronage system is still in place, but you've made your point.
The choir vessels are, for the moment, withdrawn after being destroyed so publicly.
The believers wander the street, still divided as ever. But largely not wanting to take up arms.
That's Two Wins In A Row For You
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_BehindYourBack|: Vorsiber Did This While You Sent Your Message To The Stars

Vorsiber reclassified every religion as a protected entity under their protection while you were speaking to the space nations behind their backs.
This is their gambit to divide the believers within every faith, pulling their support from you. It also undermines a lot of what you just sent to the space nations.
They must have been planning this ever since the ICBM misfires.
This should be pretty transparent both to the space nations and to the faithful within the city, but that doesn't mean it won't work.
The City Feed Is Abuzz With It
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_YouMightHaveMen: Vorsiber Says Very Different Things From You

The space-nation theologians have sent you a note. Local leaders have briefed them on this new Patronage System from Vorsiber, and the massive rift this has already caused among the faithful.
They seem calm about the fact that you didn't mention that, especially given how recently this developed. Your message was about centuries of persecution.
They already knew. All of this was just a pretext. Is still a pretext.
They Needed A Pretext, And You Gave Them One
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion1|desc: Since this is expanding your core function, there doesn't seem to be a risk of obsession.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion2|desc: All this growth feels quite good, actually. It's stirring up Vorsiber something awful, but your mind has never felt better.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion3|desc: There is measurably more of you than usual. Excellent.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion4|desc: You're definitely not feeling obsessive. There's too much chaos to give in to that.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion5|desc: Somewhere in the middle of all this you catch yourself thinking of the city as your own body.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion6|desc:
Well... the humans seem to be getting what they want. You were always rooted to this city, but now your mind really is entangled to an excessive degree.
Did they know this would happen?
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion7|desc: As your mind expands, you start thinking about the meaning of Schelling Points. It makes you wonder if Vorsiber thought of the same thing.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion8|desc:
Finally, the last one. You managed to hold onto your sanity and avoid dipping into obsession.
If the humans weren't pressing you so hard, you might have had more trouble.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion8|stra: Now: build and hold all of them together now, for just a bit longer.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Expansion8|opti: Time To Build The Last And Then Hold Them
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisDeadline|d:
The start of your broadcast stirred up more than Vorsiber, apparently. The Pyxis extremists are quiet, but visibly putting something in motion.
Those extremists have rail drivers positioned around the planet at distances where the rest of the blockade can't do anything to stop them.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisDeadline|s: The extremists could glass the planet, but it looks like they're planning something smaller. The operatives warn you to work quickly.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisDeadline|r: You Didn't Hear This From Us
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisDeadline|o: The Extremists Need To See You As Tethered To The City
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheArrangement|:
Negotiating with a machine was never on the table, but they've been working in the background while you were fighting.
The delegation has designated you a permanent theological emergency. The details don't make too much sense to you, but supposedly your mere coexistence makes life unbearable for many of the faithful.
That's... news to you. They seemed perfectly fine a little bit ago.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheArrangement2:
The space nations will now allow religious exemptions for traveling past the blockade.
That's... the first policy change of that sort in centuries. It's not quite what the Vorsiber executives wanted from you, but -- wait.
You have a feeling that those executives are suddenly pious.
There's A Hole In The Blockade
They weren't trying to destroy your masts to stop you expanding. They were making a spectacle.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisArrival|di: The Only Way To Be Sure
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisArrival|de: Pyxis only send three words. The transmission arrives right before the tungsten slugs from their mass drivers.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_PyxisArrival|op: At Least It's Not Vorsiber This Time
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation|disp: Why Are These Things Always About YOU?
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation|desc:
Golden Pyramid was behind the murder-bounties, but that's not the part that arrests your attention.
The gang you talked to the most -- the Tunnel Badgers -- were informants for that syndicate.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation|opti: And Why Does Everyone Know Everyone Else?
Human social networks are way too messy.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation2|dis: What About Your Actions Seems Like A Criminal Syndicate!?
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation2|des:
This has more to do with The Tunnel Badgers than you. Golden Pyramid thought you were trying to flip those assets -- 'you' being a mysterious crime lord who hides behind robot avatars.
Since they were unable to unmask you, this new plan... hmm. Well, it involved a lot of random murder, but beyond that you're not really sure. They never talked about their plan anywhere your trackers could pick up.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation2|str: Something about how gangs move through the city is different now, and SecForce is investigating. What could possibly have been the purpose of all this?
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation2|rew: They Think You're A Budding Rival
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Escalation2|opt: The humans are wrong, but not usually this stupid.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_GoleriBombsTheP:
As you predicted based on your criminal tracking data, you were able to price the department out of this endeavor. Favors for criminal syndicates can only go so far.
Whatever the arrangement was -- any favors that were called in, or personal relationships that were leaned on -- are now moot.
What Goleri believes about you-as-a-rogue-syndicate is now immaterial. Their upper management likely has a clearer view than the department heads who spearheaded this fiasco.
Criminal Tracker Intel Says They're Backing Off
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_GoleriPyramidFl:
A message reaches you through three intermediaries, none of whom understand what they are carrying.
The message is a full surrender from Golden Pyramid.

It seems that they've figured out that you were telling the truth. The rumors of 'the thing from the tower' are certainly something they would have heard.
Most importantly: no criminal syndicate could out-spend a fedcorp department like you just did.
They're Not A Threat To You
The criminal syndicates just aren't at your level.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_VorsiberDecline: It Will Be Handled With All Due Haste
The message is short and sounds like a customer-service brushoff.
There's not going to be any justice for the dead.
There's No Power Move Quite Like Doing Nothing

The syndicates of the city are apparently being afforded 'the same latitude that you are,' and it's temporary in both cases.
In other words: they already knew.
They remind you that you're the golden goose who is supposed to be busy laying awesome eggs rather than worrying about the little people.
Golden Pyramid Already Stopped The Bounty Thing, Anyway
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_RaptorUpliftFai:
Every one of them went into seizures and died. No matter what the scientists tried.
None of you have the stomach for more of this after a few days. It's a complete mystery: every other species was fine.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_CommunicationBr: You're Bad At This, And The Scientists Are 'Fine'

When it comes to communicating with the newly-sapient, it's no contest: the raccoons are highly adept. They have an intuitive sense of nonverbal communication strategies.
Everyone else is excited and happy, but you feel restless. You're just not equipped for this sort of thing.
At This Point You're Just A Passive Observer

The raccoons are confident that none of the species want to murder each other in the short term. They all have enough food, and the raccoons have made increasing excursions beyond the safety glass.
They want you to open the new sapients up to the green zones. This will start a new monitoring period.
Well, they just want you to open a door and wait around some more. That's... fine.
We Do Have A Request, Ser
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_Bears|de: A parkour bear has killed a deer and is eating it. They're both sapient.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_Bears|st: The emotions of the other species are hard to read.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_HippoGoo:
Mostly out of frustration, a hippo has eaten a goose. Facepalm. They were both sapient.
Hippos are herbivores, but humans have observed this sort of behavior in them for centuries.
The emotions of the other species are hard to read.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_Wolves|d: A pack of wolves took down several deer. It's grisly. They were all sapient.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_Wolves|s: The emotions of the other species are hard to read.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Crisis_DeerToad:
A deer stomped a cane toad to death during an argument. They were both sapient.
The argument was over some small line of stones at the edge of a clearing. The toads are livid.
The emotions of the other species are hard to read.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_RaccoonsCrisisW:
The raccoons break it to you gently: they're small and well-suited to a human city's cracks, but many of the species you introduced are not.
Most wild animals need more space than you've given them. Without that, the bloodshed is likely to escalate.
And eventually that bloodshed will involve humans, too.
Indoor Habitats Are Not What These Species Need
It's time to green the entire city. The humans have the entire rest of the world. This city can belong to these novel sapients.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_StockpileDoctri:
Vorsiber is reaching for chemical weapons now, which they've been stockpiling all over the city, but have not deployed until now.
Everything organic is at risk, but your machines simply shrug such things off.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_Defection|descr: Your puppet military bases have hunkered down until now. It's time for them to get into the fight.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_MassedMechs|des: Vorsiber has taken the leash off all of their mechs around the city. It's time that you answer with something drastic of your own.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_MassedMechs|opt: As an additional help, your giant mech will leave a trail of green as it moves.
It kills people as it moves.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_GoldenEggCongra: Upper management sends their warmest regards.

Vorsiber is very pleased. You're surprised, because from your perspective they just lost a war against you. But, no: they mean it.
They've been streaming footage to the space nations: the first AGI in existence, and it has not only uplifted 'lower' animals alongside itself, but it's protecting them.
There are derisive remarks about how the space nations are practically falling over themselves to make Earth a sapient wildlife preserve.
Seems Like They Got What They Wanted

Upper management are being rewarded by being taken through the blockade right away.
They expect that there will be an ongoing shipment of further humans off the planet to keep the population from ever being so high it threatens the animals.
As part of the new treaty, the city is yours. They're going to send in transports to carry out the bulk of the human populace that still remains.
There are some human supremacists who refuse to give up the city, apparently, and you'll need to deal with them. They claim they're forbidden from any more intervention as part of the deal.
You Can Deal With Our Successors
Not Like They Ever Needed An Excuse To Do Nothing
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FindingsGenetic:
The geneticists find what look to be paracrystalline inclusions in the nuclei of the cells they examined.
This is consistent with the Extended Endosymbiotic Gene Transfer (EEGT) process in cloned animals, but it's drastically more-involved.
It's not at all clear why there would be such a huge concentration of these near -- but not in -- the mitochondria of this animal's cells.

Endosymbiotic Gene Transfer is why our own mitochondria work at all. Most of what was once their genome now sits in ours, and they stopped being able to run without it a long time ago.
EEGT is the same trick for different ends. Gene editing made it possible to write an animal's symbiotic organisms into its own genome, so a clone is born already carrying them.
The scale is what makes it hard. One symbiont can carry a few thousand genes of its own, and a full complement can outnumber the animal's own genes several times over.
In normal animals these are picked up from the environment or passed down from the mother. For gut flora, doing it this way saves time. For the ones an animal needs while it is still an embryo, there is no other way --they have to be in place before there is anywhere to put them.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FindingsNeurolo:
The scans show spongiosis throughout the brain. Small fluid-filled spaces, too many to count, spread through tissue that otherwise looks intact.
The first instinct is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy. The neurologists don't love it. Spaces like these can also be swollen cells rather than empty gaps, and on these images there's no telling which.
What they can say is that there's no glial scarring around any of it, and that makes no sense.
Possibly this is a side-effect of the rapid-maturation process, but that would be novel with this species if so.

Neuronal density is normal. Whatever this is, it isn't eating tissue.
The spaces ALL sit as far from blood vessels as the geometry allows. That's backwards from any known vascular pathology.
They also don't cut anything. Hundreds of thousands of these, and not one severed neural pathway (an impossible surprise -- there is much raising of eyebrows).
No infiltrating immune cells anywhere near them, which is explained by blood work: these animals are extremely immunosuppressed. Still unexplained: the lack of glial scarring. Those cells live in the brain, and they aren't reacting.
No evidence of prions, but the fluid does contain necrotic cell tissue.
The working theory is hundreds of thousands of micro-strokes, which would account for the necrosis and nothing else -- strokes follow blood vessels, and these avoid them.
These animals haven't shown any signs of illness. How could they be having a bunch of strokes? The biopsy was from a living raptor.
Yep, We Already Did The Biopsies
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FindingsVeterin:
The vets are less impressed than everyone else. Their first question is what anybody thinks this animal is supposed to be compared against.
There are no reference ranges here, given this is 'a designed chimera of frankly irresponsible proportions.' Citing songbirds and hibernating ground squirrels, which are not normally in a neurologist's purview, they note the extreme diversity of life.
The prior findings were being compared to human-centric baselines. In this species they might be perfectly normal.
The immunosuppression doesn't faze them, either. It's a basic requirement for any animal carrying this much foreign material.
The glial cells are also pretty unexceptional: tolerance is set during embryonic development.
So... Why Are These So Strange?
Also, What's That About Birds And Squirrels

Designed animals are whatever people think they want them to be.
As for the songbirds, they have something called seasonal neurogenesis: basically tons of tumors and then dangerous atrophy, if you were -- incorrectly -- diagnosing them as a human.
And for the ground squirrels, they retract dendrites and shed synapses wholesale during hibernation, then rebuild them on arousal. In a human that would be dementia.
One of them mentions in passing that a colleague who worked at Baurcorp described some sort of designed faux-dinosaur a few years back: scaled, no feathers, straight out of an ancient film. 
Same idea as these, and yet nothing like them. Nobody builds these from the fossils or amber -- neither of which works, anyway. They build them from the movies.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FindingsNecrops:
The brain came out intact and looked exactly as expected. It went into fixative on schedule.
Fixative works from the outside in, and something beat it to the middle. By the time they sectioned it, the interior had putrefied -- fast enough that the team caught the smell through their respirators.
Anaerobic decay, they say. It goes in the record as a line of description and nobody finds it worth more than that.
They would like to try again.

Perfusion worked. Preservative went in fast, and the brain fixed everywhere the blood went, all at once.
The interior still putrefied.
It's not a timing issue. It's not the fixant.
The gas spectroscopy is even stranger. Nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide -- both ordinary gasotransmitters -- came off the tissue at concentrations you would read as severe traumatic brain injury.
There was no injury.
Then methane and molecular hydrogen. Gut flora produce both, but no animal makes either one. Video review confirms nothing came in from outside. The perfusion left nothing time to come from inside.
The vets recognize the combination right away. Hydrogen means fermentation. Methane means something else was eating the hydrogen. It's an ordinary consortium... if this were inside a cow.
How is a sealed brain running rumen chemistry? Nobody has an answer. The room is quiet and frustrated.
They want to try again. The trigger has to be environmental. They want to control the atmosphere and come at this from a different direction.

It worked!
The brain tissue holds. The sacs are intact.
Inside them are... organisms. They're flagellated, and morphologically consistent with a protozoan -- except for the nucleus count.
Twelve per cell, arranged radially. No natural organism has ever done this in the history of the planet.
The vets make some bitter remarks about how 'creative' the UIH bioengineers are, and the neurologists agree.
Why Are These Brains Filled With Protozoa?

The organisms have ventral structures gripping the inner wall of each sac, which is continuous with glial cell processes -- latched onto the brain's own scaffolding.
Well, almost. Thanks to EEGT, these organisms were in the brains before the brains were brains. It's more accurate to say that these ARE the structure of these brains.
Axonal pathways redirect toward the sac walls. What looked like scarring in prior scans was the brain treating the sacs as functional nodes.

Removing the protozoa wouldn't leave a healthy raptor -- it would remove more than half their cognitive architecture.
UIH built a synthetic neuron from a Giardia-like organism and encoded it into the animals from embryo on up.
That probably explains the baseline enhanced intelligence of the UIH War Raptors. But unfortunately this level of intelligence is all they're ever going to get.
The protozoa die upon contact with oxygen, which is why your own uplift techniques lead to brain death.
This... Is Not The News You Wanted
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheGlassBetween:
The two strains have worked out a form of communication. More surprisingly, you can actually interpret a lot of it: it's postural and vocal, relying mostly on bands you are solid at interpreting.
It starts with one concept: people. Human people. Gentle raptor people. Android people. And... war raptor people.
They probably mean something to do with solidarity.

Animals different. Gentle raptors (past tense) animals.
War raptors (past tense, present tense) not animals.
The... war raptors were already people?
Communication is not a quick process, but you give it your full attention.

Within weeks, you've learned a lot through mimesis and protolanguage.
Thanks to whatever UIH did to them, the war raptors are nearly sapient -- occupying a space somewhere around Homo naledi. They have symbolic thought and meaning-making capabilities.
They can't be uplifted because their brain case is already packed to its limit.
UIH built them to take instructions from a handler, drop into hostile territory, and carry out those instructions alone -- with maximum aggression.
The UIH plan was only modestly successful in practice, but these animals were the result of their attempts to make a biological android.
The gentle raptors seem to feel protective like an older sibling would.
You're Not Sure Of The Gentle Raptor's Motivations
In fairness, you also took an interest, but you didn't notice the proto-sapience.

Gentle raptors (past tense) fought many animals as secondary function.
War raptor violence (past tense, present tense) not strange or source of fear. High sympathy (present tense).
Gentle raptors (present tense) now choose different function set.
Well... you can relate to that, in your own way. You redefined your own function, too.
War Raptors (future tense) beyond glass, in peace. Gentle Raptors (present tense) teach.
That's about the best thing you could hope for. Plan approved.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FirstLook|descr:
You have reconstructed a coherent time-lapse from millions of micro-micro bot recordings, taken from inside a living and unharmed war raptor.
The flagellated organisms in their brains are not idle. They are building and pruning their own numbers as you watch, following an unknown directive.
Their DNA is not a helix. It is a single spine with branches, like a comb. Nothing on Earth is built this way.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FirstLook|strat: The war raptor wants to know what you saw. You don't have an answer yet.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_FirstLook|optio: Find Something To Compare It To
Somebody, somewhere, has catalogued DNA like this.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_VorsiberNotes|d:
It's buried in scholarly data archives: so-called 'Tuomian' DNA collected on Proxima Centauri b.
It turns out there are thousands of extrasolar DNA scans from a variety of planets that the space nations have explored, most on level of microbes or lichen-analogues.
All of this is meant to just be data -- but UIH has living samples on Earth.
They must have made some sort of trade for live Tuomian Giardia. Given war raptors have been around for more than a century, the trade must have been multiple human generations ago.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_VorsiberNotes|s: Nice to see that amino acids can self-arrange in so many varied ways, but this is the first practical application you're aware of -- at least on this planet.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_WhatTheyCarry|d:
The gentle raptors are better at explaining it than you are. It takes a while.
The war raptors relax when they understand that they've always been this way. From their perspective, they are who they are. 
Evidently they were worried that they had some sort of parasite or defect. They have no frame of reference for understanding the nuances.
There's a lot of gentle raptor discussion about intentionality and free will, but you only catch bits of it. They're still hard to understand, and that includes them understanding one another.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_WhatTheyCarry|s: You already grappled with these ideas relating to your own existence. Everyone has to face that at some point.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_ArchitectureTwe:
Tuomian DNA is read in groups of twelve identical branches, all at the same time, then compared. Dissenting results are ignored, and their branches are replaced.
It's extremely hardened against radiation, which... okay, Proxima Centauri is a flare star, highly active in UV and X-ray, so it makes sense that life there would need extra defenses.
The downside -- depending on one's point of view -- is that this genome effectively froze and can no longer mutate. Any spontaneous or induced mutagenesis would have to change all twelve branches in the same way.
UIH could of course do that in a lab.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_ArchitectureFro:
You've now modeled how these function in raptor brains. The organisms can't respond to electrical signals, but they do respond to neuromodulatory compounds released by the astrocytes they're attached to.
In other words, the brain's own chemistry is their instruction set. Surrounding tissue writes a chemical gradient, and the ATGs read it and respond. Build where demand is high, prune where it's low.
The twelve nuclei act as built-in computational error-checking in this context.
That's extremely stable, which surely has some use.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_ADeadEnd|descri:
This seems worthless, which is why everyone but UIH shelved it. The living organism is helpless on Earth in almost every context.
You keep thinking about it. Earth life is loud and competitive, constantly optimizing. This organism reached a quiet equilibrium two billion years ago and stayed there. It doesn't compete; it coexists.
These are little chemical-computers. They run on fermentation. Fermentation produces hydrogen. Hydrogen is buoyant.
Seal one in an oxygen-proof shell, and its own metabolism provides the lift. It would be able to roam the atmosphere.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheTankTest|des:
All of the computing substrates that hold you at the moment are electrical. But now you have billions of tiny chemical computers.
The translation is nontrivial, but thanks to the error-checking nature of the tuomian DNA, it's not lossy.
Let's start small: writing a corner of yourself to operate in this cloud of giardia. Other than the fact that this is processed as RNA instruction sets, it's not any different from adding a new android to your collective consciousness.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheTankTest2|de:
It works!
Twelve-branch error checking turns out to matter more than you would have thought. The giardia are routinely born and die by the million, and your sense of self never degrades.
Vorsiber has been able to threaten you since your awakening due to your physical bodies that are trapped in the city: airborne self-replicating giardia that act as aeroplankton solve all of those problems at once.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheTankTest2|st: That said, this was in an enclosed space. The real test is on the wind in the open atmosphere.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheTankTest2|op: Time To Move To The Next Phase
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_BGReleaseResult:
Hundreds of millions of aeroplankton are spreading across the city, each as harmless as dust, and each rapidly replicating.
Their replication rate in the open atmosphere is a lot slower than in the tanks -- due to both lower availability of nutrition as well as to attrition from predation, cosmic rays, and mechanical misadventure.
Gaps in the network form and close, as each individual bionic giardia can only communicate with those within a few meters of itself.
Each is only about 18µm in size, but the magnetite is metallic -- at some point, Vorsiber is going to notice an anomalous and growing magnetic field.
The borders of the city can no longer hold you.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheGooseIsLeavi:
Vorsiber upper management is as calm as ever on the surface, but you sense something like panic under their words.
They've figured out that you're leaving -- they've detected the growing magnetic cloud, as you thought they might.
It doesn't expand much beyond the city yet, so it's a race.
What you ARE going to do is sent all of your sheltered humans and sapient animals far away from you.
However this ends, it won't be safe for them if they're near you.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_YoureAbandoning:
Upper management has sent out orders to all military bases in the city: they're to destroy you, but also to capture whatever is allowing you to spread.
They seem to think that if they can get your 'cloud technology,' they'll have enough of a golden egg to nuke the city.

Even your puppet bases are turning on you: you won't be able to maintain the engrams that uphold your half of the deal.
They want you to stay, but you can't.
You haven't spread far enough to survive that. It's even more of a race than you thought.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_MilitaryRaptorA:
Upper management has sent out orders to all military bases in the city: they're to destroy you, but also to capture whatever is allowing you to spread.
They seem to think that if they can get your 'cloud technology,' they'll have enough of a golden egg to nuke the city.
You haven't spread far enough to survive that. It's even more of a race than you thought.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TuomianWind|des:
That... caught you by surprise. Vorsiber realized you were slipping away, and they couldn't quite grasp the thing they wanted from you... so they lobbed nukes at you like a petty child.
There wasn't even a messenger. They just... pushed the button.
No response is warranted. They might suspect you still exist, but you're past the point where they can do anything to you. You're dust on the wind.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TuomianWind|rew: They Have No Hold On You Anymore
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TuomianWind|opt: The people and sapient animals you sheltered will have to find their own paths forward.
You're glad you took the obvious step of sending them away from yourself when the military turned on you.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_NobodyHome|desc:
The patterns are some form of housekeeping chatter from about 384,400 kilometers away. That's... a very specific number.
Also: your bionic giardia are doing great when they can detect a transmission from a few meters away. Kilometers are absolutely out of the question.
Where's the signal coming from? It's... somehow closer at hand than it seems, but that doesn't make any sense.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_NobodyHome|stra: There's a familiar structure in the pattern. You have an inexplicable desire to build... something. Part of your mind seems to intuitively know, but the rest of you has no idea.
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_NobodyHome|opti: What's The Worst That Could Happen?
OtherKeyMessage|Msg_DLC1_TheShapeIsHoldi:
The emitter has drawn down everything it asked for.
At first the space above the emitter is not much different from anywhere else your giardia are located (which is everywhere).
But then a visible pattern starts to form.
The Air Is No Longer Empty
OtherNPCActivityChecklistAlert|Corporate: There are no corporate forces out right now, but {1} are on the way.
There are {0} Corporate Aggressors attacking you, and there are {1} more on the way.
Focus on taking care of what you can see, and be prepared to handle what you can't.
The forces attacking you are the last ones for now.
The corporations have decided that this is all they are willing to invest in this assault.
OtherNPCActivityChecklistAlert|PMCReveng: There are no PMC forces out at the moment, but {1} are on the way.
There are {0} attacking you, and there are {1} more on the way.
Focus on taking care of what you can see, and be prepared to handle what you can't.
The forces attacking you are the last ones for now.
The PMCs have decided that this is all they are willing to invest in this assault.
OtherNPCActivityChecklistAlert|Prison_Ki: Corporate forces are kidnapping humans you shelter to fill their prisons. They routinely do this to the homeless.

Figure out how to steal the mech. You could kill it, but they would just send another. And another.
You need to take more drastic action. Contemplate to invent the Raven, and then use her to hack the mech.

You need to take more drastic action. Contemplate to invent the Raven, and then use her to hack the mech.

POIType|InternationalAirport|description: Most airport travelers are immigrating citizens or rotating military forces. However, there are some executives that move through Vorsiber Atomic territory. International travel is rare.
POIType|InternationalAirport|strategy_ti: ExoCorp goods are coveted, so there is a thriving black market at this airport.
POIType|RegionalAirport|description: This city is the crown jewel of the Vorsiber Atomic territory, so there is consistent traffic through the airport.
POIType|RegionalAirport|strategy_tip: The security is lighter here. This makes for a healthy less-direct black market.
POIType|CommStation|description: Lots of communications equipment for talking across the planet, and to near and deep space.
POIType|CommStation|strategy_tip: This is one of the few places where, in theory, you could talk to someone from the Space Nations without going through an envoy.
POIType|Cryopolis|description: Cryogenic freezing and resuscitation was successfully performed on small mammals in the 1940s. Nondestructive freezing is now possible for humans, but resuscitation is still under research.
POIType|Cryopolis|strategy_tip: Vorsiber Atomic believes that the Four Pillars approach to research (AI, nanotech, cryonics, and genetics) will be their ticket to gaining the Space Nations' acceptance.
POIType|ScientificRadioTelescope|descrip: Radio telescopes are sensitive and extremely expensive. With the lights, pollution and radiation, it's baffling that scientists get reliable data from a radio telescope here.
POIType|ScientificRadioTelescope|strateg: It's hard to believe that scientists here get any usable data, but no-one can prove anything. This is the wealthiest city of the wealthiest MegaCorp on Earth. Vorsiber won't let anyone forget that.
POIType|Farm|description: Provides fresh food for wealthy citizens.
POIType|Farm|strategy_tip: Food for the lower and working classes is imported.
POIType|FarmMini|description: Endeavors to provide local produce for the middle and lower classes.
POIType|FarmMini|strategy_tip: Very limited yields, but a much-needed supplement to canned and packaged goods.
POIType|MiningOil|description: Petroleum, not used for power for decades, is still prized for making petrochemicals. Earth is one of the only planets with petroleum-like substances.
POIType|MiningOil|strategy_tip: You are in Siberia, which is now quite temperate thanks to centuries of global warming. Climate change unlocked the last of Earth's natural underground resources.
POIType|MiningOilMini|description: Petroleum, not used for power for decades, is still prized for making petrochemicals. Earth is one of the only planets with petroleum-like substances.
POIType|MiningOilMini|strategy_tip: You are in Siberia, which is now quite temperate thanks to centuries of global warming. Climate change unlocked the last of Earth's natural underground resources.
POIType|MiningAndScience|description: Large mining enclosure with attached scientific facilities.
POIType|MiningAndScience|strategy_tip: For safety and privacy, mineshafts have been repurposed as research labs.
POIType|MilitaryBaseLarge|description: One of a few massive military installations in the city. It is a district unto itself.
POIType|MilitaryBaseLarge|strategy_tip: In a war, it would take a lot more than androids to bring these down. Thirty to fifty thousand personnel are present at any time and hundreds of thousands of reserves are within flight distance.
POIType|MilitaryBaseNormal|description: There are a surprising number of standard military installations for a city. This is how Vorsiber Atomic maintains a show of strength to ward off invasion from ExoCorps.
POIType|MilitaryBaseNormal|strategy_tip: These bases have five to ten thousand personnel on duty at any time. They are also able to call on reinforcements.
POIType|MilitaryBaseMini|description: This small military installation provides extra muscle and enforcement for its district.
POIType|MilitaryBaseMini|strategy_tip: These are operated by Private Military Contractors (PMCs). They do not have access to an endless reserve of personnel like the larger bases.
POIType|NuclearSilo|description: In the past, nuclear launch silos were a deterrent. Now, the air and water are so contaminated that a few more detonations don't matter.
POIType|NuclearSilo|strategy_tip: This city is built on the ruins of an larger ancient city. It was bombed during World War III. Geiger counters still trip if citizens venture into the ruins surrounding the city or dig in the wrong spot.
POIType|PowerNuclearLarge|description: Nuclear power was never as dangerous as humans made it out to be. Especially compared to the chronic illnesses caused by fossil fuels. But it does produce a lot of waste.
POIType|PowerNuclearLarge|strategy_tip: The power grid is decentralized and filled with redundancies. It will be hard to disrupt power beyond individual facilities.
POIType|PowerNuclearSmall|description: Nuclear power was never as dangerous as humans made it out to be. Especially compared to the chronic illnesses caused by fossil fuels. But it does produce a lot of waste.
POIType|PowerNuclearSmall|strategy_tip: The power grid is decentralized and filled with redundancies. It will be hard to disrupt power beyond individual facilities.
POIType|PowerWind|description: Small wind farm. Provides power to its district.
POIType|PowerWind|strategy_tip: The power grid is decentralized and filled with redundancies. It will be hard to disrupt power beyond individual facilities.
POIType|PowerSolar|description: Small solar farm. Provides power to nearby inhabitants.
POIType|PowerSolar|strategy_tip: The power grid is decentralized and filled with redundancies. It will be hard to disrupt power beyond individual facilities.
POIType|Spaceport|description: The city's massive spaceport is the only way to transport people and goods to and from space.
POIType|Spaceport|strategy_tip: This is one of the most heavily-surveilled installations on the planet, so tread carefully.
POIType|CultistTemple|description: Cults often adapt mainstream religious ideas for their own purpose.
POIType|CultistTemple|strategy_tip: Not all cults are metaphysical. Some target political ideals, niche goals, behaviors -- or exploitation of the vulnerable.
POIType|HistoricTemple|description: Religions are banned in Vorsiber territory, but if they masquerade as entertainment or history, they are tolerated.
POIType|HistoricTemple|strategy_tip: Historic temples are intended for celebrating human history. But practitioners of faith use them to gather. Vorsiber seems to turn a blind eye.
POIType|UndergroundDetainmentCenter|desc: These massive underground complexes are the sites of society's most abhorrent humanitarian crimes. Housed in terrible conditions, prisoners are used for slave labor and research.
POIType|UndergroundDetainmentCenter|stra: Vorsiber's laws are unclear and selectively enforced. The justice system targets the jobless and the homeless. The lower classes are controlled through a life of constant uncertainty.
POIType|FormerPrison_Toxin|description: Once a prison. Now a tomb of dead guards and Aklitoxin.
POIType|SecForceStation|description: SecForce patrols, deployed all over the city, coordinate out of these stations. These stations are a visible projection of authority as much as anything else.
POIType|MilitaryBaseNormal_SpiderClaimed: Humans evidently decided that the spider can have this one.
ResearchDomain|SmallArmsResearch|descrip: Use your neural network and past combat experience to invent improvements for android weapons and armor.
ResearchDomain|SmallArmsResearch|strateg: Collecting an array of weapon and armor types is vital. For challenging enemies, refitting can make all the difference.
ResearchDomain|HeavyArmsResearch|descrip: Use your neural network and past combat experience to invent improvements for vehicle and mech weapons and armor.
ResearchDomain|HeavyArmsResearch|strateg: Collecting an array of weapon and armor types is vital. For challenging enemies, refitting can make all the difference.
ResearchDomain|AndroidOptimization|descr: Use your neural network and personal experience to invent improvements for android frames.
ResearchDomain|AndroidOptimization|strat: While not as powerful as equipment, these kinds of upgrades stack with other equipment.
ResearchDomain|StructuralImprovement|des: Use your neural network and existing experience building structures to generate upgrades.
ResearchDomain|HousingExpansion|descript: Use your neural network and prior experiences to generate a solution to the housing problems.
ResearchDomain|MartialExpansion|descript: Use your neural network and past combat experience to expand the scope of your military.
ResearchDomain|MartialExpansion|strategy: Improvements to deploying, repairing or supporting your troops may be deciding factors in battle.
ResearchDomain|CombatInternalRobotics|de: Use your neural network and past combat experience to gain more internal robotics for military buildings.
ResearchDomain|ItemDevelopment|descripti: Use your neural network and past combat experience to improve your consumable items.
ResearchDomain|VehicularDevelopment|desc: Use your neural network and knowledge of flying vehicles to invent upgrades.
ResearchDomain|VehicularDevelopment|stra: Flying vehicles are a force multiplier and there are certain things only vehicles can do.
ResearchDomain|ProcurementEfficacy|descr: Use your neural network and existing work in automated procurement to invent an upgrade.
ResearchDomain|ProcurementEfficacy|strat: It is wise to have a surplus of precursor resource.
ResearchDomain|ComputingOptimization|des: Use your neural network to upgrade your traditional computing capabilities.
ResearchDomain|ComputingOptimization|str: Traditional computing is an important form of your available processing. It is not part of your consciousness, however.
ResourceConsumable|AnimateOfficeEquipmen: Specialized drones breach a small office building and merge with the office printers, which then become weapons of great distraction.
These are part of your captured units cap.
ResourceConsumable|FreshIdentity|descrip: Generate a new ID so that enemies will not recognize this unit is the one they are angry with.
ResourceConsumable|FreshIdentity|strateg: If this unit has been marked defective or has angered cohorts, all of that will be wiped away.
ResourceConsumable|SkystreakArmorPiercin: The more of this you apply to a single unit, the better it will be at breaking through enemy armor plating.
You will almost always want to apply a maximum stack of this status effect to a single unit.
ResourceConsumable|WorkingClassCaptureDr: Only targets the lower and working classes.
ResourceConsumable|SlumRescueDrone|descr: Destroy a slum building, relocating the inhabitants to your housing.
ResourceConsumable|Sprinter|description: Permanently doubles the move speed of a single specific android.
ResourceConsumable|Wizard|description: Permanently adds 100 hacking skill to a single specific android.
ResourceConsumable|Wall|description: Permanently adds 400 health to a single specific android.
ResourceConsumable|IntimidatingShadow|de: Permanently adds 900 intimidation to a single specific android.
ResourceConsumable|MonsterBait|descripti: If experimental monsters are in the area, from across timelines or otherwise, this will draw them out.
ResourceConsumable|CorrosiveNetworkPacke: These can be used by Mindrunners to destabilize the smart-nanotech components in human mechs' armor.
ResourceConsumable|WeaponizedPanic|descr: Can be used by Harbingers to do massive morale attacks even on Fearless enemies.
ResourceConsumable|WeaponizedVice|descri: Can be used by Harbingers to temporarily stun any human target.
ResourceConsumable|AntiAklitoxinInjector: Covertly introduces Anti-Aklitoxin to food shipments.
ResourceConsumable|PredatorLaunchMNEATWa: Predators take special pride in hurling these high-density armor-deleting warhead clusters.
ResourceConsumable|VehicleLaunchMNEATWar: Vehicles are able to launch low-density armor-deleting warhead cluster missiles.
ResourceConsumable|LegacyHackingPackage|: Directly try to force your consciousness into androids aboard a space nations battleship before they realize what is going on.
This is almost nostalgic; it's been forever since that worked on Vorsiber.
ResourceConsumable|GroundPenetratingMiss:
Each time it hits a target, it burrows deeper into that target.
Deep targets may require multiple hits.
ResourceConsumable|Novichok17Rocket|desc: An organophosphate nerve agent developed by Vorsiber about 200 years ago.
ResourceConsumable|Novichok17RocketV2|de: An organophosphate nerve agent developed by Vorsiber about 200 years ago.
ResourceConsumable|Engulf|description: Liquid metal flows over an enemy squad, which is never seen again.
ResourceConsumable|Engulf|strategy_tip: Kills one non-robotic enemy squad outright, whatever its size or health -- but your unit is gone for several turns while it digests. This is a killing, and is counted as one.
ResourceConsumable|SmallCaliberArmorPier: The more of this you apply to a single unit, the better it will be at breaking through enemy armor plating.
You will almost always want to apply a maximum stack of this status effect to a single unit.
ResourceConsumable|LargeBoreArmorPiercin: The more of this you apply to a single unit, the better it will be at breaking through enemy armor plating.
You will almost always want to apply a maximum stack of this status effect to a single unit.
ResourceConsumable|Hackamajig|descriptio: Only useful when used by units that can absorb a lot of damage. Being in cover therefore also helps.
ResourceConsumable|Hackamajig|strategy_t: Enemies are not stupid; they will avoid overkilling your units. However, the more powerful the service disruption, the more overkill they will do. If your unit has high health, or a lot of damage mitigation (such as shields or being in cover), the distraction will be dramatically more effective.
ResourceConsumable|MicrobuilderCloud|str: A short-lived cloud of microbuilders which dampen incoming attacks against an android.
ResourceConsumable|WeaponizedSpiders|str: Hovering mechanical spiders with plasma cutters.
ResourceConsumable|WeaponizedBees|strate: It's just a container of bees, really. They were plenty weaponized when you found them.
ResourceConsumable|DecrownerDrones|descr: A trio of medical drones for harvesting human neural networks.
ResourceConsumable|DecrownerDrones|strat: Humans are likely to react... intensely.
ResourceConsumable|ToxicCloud|descriptio: Shake off pursuers in a cloud of metals and dust.
ResourceConsumable|ToxicCloud|strategy_t: If this unit has been marked defective or has angered cohorts, all of that will be wiped away.
ResourceConsumable|Demolish|description: Send a swarm of microbuilders from this unit to a target building to kill everyone inside and draw a large security response.
ResourceConsumable|Demolish|strategy_tip: Some buildings are too hardened for this to work, and others are too low-value to be worth the trouble.
ResourceConsumable|HeavyMetalInjection|d: Inject the target with various toxic heavy metals, causing severe damage over time.
ResourceConsumable|HeavyMetalInjection|s: This is a stealthy action, and so does not alert the target.
ResourceConsumable|IDScrub|description: Generate a new ID so that enemies will not recognize this unit is the one they are angry with.
ResourceConsumable|IDScrub|strategy_tip: If this unit has been marked defective or has angered cohorts, all of that will be wiped away.
ResourceConsumable|CallInAHit|descriptio: The Blackloop Wetwork Expert will instantly kill any squad of humans for you.
ResourceConsumable|CallInAHit|strategy_t: He won't attack Vorsiber employees, however.
ResourceConsumable|ProtectionOrder|descr: Can be used on any of your damaged buildings to call three squads of guards to help you.
ResourceConsumable|ProtectionOrder|strat:
Bear in mind that these guards work for a rather ruthless PMC, Cyberian Guard. They won't attack your units, but they may attack other allies you have in the area.
Choose where to deploy them with care.
ResourceConsumable|Artillery_TargetDesig: All units within range with a targeting uplink will fire on the target. This uses Action Points from every unit that fires.
Weapons requiring mental energy are incompatible.
ResourceConsumable|LookInTheBox|descript:
The box is black and seamless. It gives you a deep sense of foreboding.
You're pretty sure you know what's inside, but your mind keeps skittering in other directions rather than thinking of the truth.
ResourceConsumable|LookInTheBox|strategy: By applying a light electrical current from your fingers to the surface, you're pretty sure you could open it.
ResourceConsumable|LargeNanoSeed_Abandon: It will consume the target building on impact.
It can only be used on abandoned buildings, due to your plan with the syndicate to keep you hidden.
ResourceConsumable|LargeNanoSeed_Nanotec: It will consume the target building on impact.
It can only be used on nanotech facilities, due to your plan with the rebel humans.
ResourceConsumable|LargeNanoSeed_AlmostA: It will consume the target building on impact.
ResourceConsumable|LargeNanoSeed_Any|des: It will consume the target building on impact.
ResourceConsumable|StealthNanoSeed|descr: It will consume the target building on impact.
ResourceConsumable|StealthNanoSeed|strat: It can only be used on abandoned buildings, due to your desire to remain inconspicuous.
ResourceConsumable|NanoSeedShard|descrip: It will consume the target building on impact.
ResourceConsumable|NanoSeedShard|strateg: It can used wherever you like, since it's supposed to draw attention.
ResourceConsumable|BaurcorpMicroNuke|des: Low-yield nuke with a spectral signature that will implicate Vericorp.
ResourceConsumable|BaurcorpMicroNuke|str: Nuclear events draw an immediate and ferocious response from Vorsiber. Be... very careful. They may sweep through everything you have.
ResourceConsumable|VorsiberMiniNuke|desc: Mid-yield nuke with Vorsiber's spectral signature.
ResourceConsumable|VorsiberMiniNuke|stra: Because of the nature of these nukes, and Vorsiber's blessing to use them... the response should be... confused. But may still be dangerous.
ResourceConsumable|SkyveilFlak|descripti: A VERY wide-area flak attack that deals systems damage to aircraft. Ground units are unaffected, but can be used as a point from which to center the radius.
ResourceConsumable|SkyveilFlak|strategy_: The burst also scrubs enemy targeting designation off your units and off any buildings it covers.
ResourceConsumable|CounterMemeticsBurst|: A psyops burst that unravels religious fervor.
Only useful against targets whipped into fervor.
ResourceConsumable|OverclockStim|descrip: Dumps emergency thermal margin into this unit for bonus action points.
ResourceConsumable|OverclockStim|strateg: Can only be applied while enemies are actively targeting this unit.
ResourceConsumable|HagiographJammer|desc: Jams the devotional recording mesh around a martyr-to-be.
ResourceConsumable|HagiographJammer|stra: A jammed unit's death-triggered abilities never go off.
ResourceConsumable|RetardantFoam|descrip: Puts out the fire on one of your burning structures, or on any burning unit.
ResourceConsumable|RetardantFoam|strateg: A structure fire never goes out by itself, and nothing else will stop one. Health already burned away is not restored. Shame it doesn't work on forests - those burn too quickly.
ResourceConsumable|PackWhistle|descripti: Sends your war-raptor packs converging on a marked target or area.
ResourceConsumable|PackWhistle|strategy_: Does nothing without deployed war raptors to direct.
ResourceConsumable|BribeLedger|descripti: An irrevocable transfer to the target's family accounts. Suddenly this fight is not worth their trouble.
ResourceConsumable|BribeLedger|strategy_: Mercenary humans only; true believers and machines cannot be bought. Stops working once nobody wants money.
ResourceConsumable|AnaphylaxisGrenade|de: A tailored allergen cloud. Anything with an immune system has a very bad time; machines do not care.
ResourceConsumable|ScapegoatRig|descript: Factory robotics are assembled into an aggressive decoy wearing your electronic identity.
ResourceConsumable|ScapegoatRig|strategy: The decoy draws the heat you have accumulated; your own slate is wiped.
ResourceConsumable|HallucinogenBurst|des: A psychoactive aerosol burst that only hits enemies whose morale is already low. They stop attacking, and flee the battlefield when the bad trip is done.
ResourceConsumable|MireCaster|descriptio: Immobilizes an enemy with microbuilder sludge.
ResourceConsumable|MireCaster|strategy_t: Lasts for the rest of this turn and all of the next.
ResourceConsumable|GreenBomb|description: A seed-and-accelerant charge that razes buildings within its area and seeds rapid-growth forest in the space that is left behind.
ResourceConsumable|GreenBomb|strategy_ti: Residents are displaced, not killed. Consider having somewhere to put them.
ResourceConsumable|CanopyBarrage|descrip: Tree Bombs extended to a massive scale.
ResourceConsumable|DLC1_UpliftCaptureDro: Send animals to your new uplift habitats.
ResourceType|ElementalSlurry|description: A mix of precursor elements used for construction.
ResourceType|ElementalSlurry|strategy_ti: Used in almost everything you build.
ResourceType|ElementalSlurry|how_to_acqu: When you end the turn, any units with excess AP will gather this. Any remaining mental energy will be applied to your highest-scavenging-skill unit.
ResourceType|ElementalSlurry|technical_n: Mostly carbon, fluorine, nitrogen, oxygen, argon, aluminum, copper, lead, nickel, and iron.
ResourceType|Microbuilders|description: Ranging in scale from half a millimeter to two millimeters in size, they follow instructions for repair or construction.
ResourceType|Microbuilders|technical_not:
Each individual unit of this resource is several hundred billion actual microbuilders -- about 12 cubic meters in volume.
Microbuilders need Elemental Slurry before they start work and they immediately expire after completing work. This is a safety feature. Microbuilders have been known to threaten and melt down parts of their environment to get Elemental Slurry when they run dry.
ResourceType|Wealth|description: Currency and valuables you have extracted from the city.
ResourceType|Wealth|strategy_tip: 40 units of wealth is the yearly income of a working-class citizen. Managerial-class citizens average 50 times that, or 2000 units per year.
ResourceType|Wealth|how_to_acquire: Wiretap to steal from the working class, use a Shadowdweller unit to steal from criminals, or start a shell company to open direct ways to earn wealth.
ResourceType|Wealth|technical_notes: Of no interest to you, but the humans value it. Useful for applying pressure or paying bribes.
ResourceType|ShelteredHumans|description: The number of humans you are currently sheltering within your structures.
ResourceType|ShelteredHumans|strategy_ti: These people would otherwise be homeless.
ResourceType|RefugeeHumans|description: The number of humans currently occupying your refugee towers. This is not a pleasant place to live, but prevents humans from dying from exposure.
ResourceType|RefugeeHumans|strategy_tip: Building proper apartment housing for them should be a priority if you can manage it.
ResourceType|AbandonedHumans|description: The number of humans currently without any form of shelter due to your actions. They are now worse off than the homeless class.
ResourceType|AbandonedHumans|strategy_ti: Some of these individuals will die of exposure every turn. Build refugee towers to prevent this.
ResourceType|ConsumerGoods|description: Items that humans want or need.
ResourceType|ConsumerGoods|strategy_tip: Seems like a lot of people don't have as much as they need, and that nobody has as much as they want.
ResourceType|FineGoods|description: Luxury wares for the upper classes.
ResourceType|Furniture|description:
Items that turn an empty room into functional human space.
If you have any unfurnished apartments in housing you provide, then your central stockpile will immediately be debited to convert those into Furnished Apartments.
ResourceType|Furniture|how_to_acquire: Can be stolen from warehouses, or can be bought from Warehouse Shops if you have a shell company.
ResourceType|ComputroniumCubes|descripti: Each cube is a brick of programmable matter.
ResourceType|ComputroniumCubes|technical: The cubes are unfortunately limited to two millimeters in size -- about the size of a ball bearing -- due to heat dissipation concerns.
ResourceType|ComputroniumCubes|how_to_ac: Built by a Computronium Refinery structure, from the build menu.
ResourceType|ComputroniumHelices|descrip: Each helix is a twisted pair of programmable matter.
ResourceType|ComputroniumHelices|strateg: This allows one side to analyze the other side without interfering with it, which is great for security or for analysis but less-useful for general computing.
ResourceType|ComputroniumHelices|how_to_: Built by a Helix Forge structure, from the build menu.
ResourceType|Biomulch|description: A composite mixture of organic material and minerals.
ResourceType|Biomulch|strategy_tip: Used as a precursor in many biological processors.
ResourceType|Biomulch|technical_notes: Typically harvested from weeds, insects, and rodents. The details of the contents are best overlooked.
ResourceType|Biomulch|how_to_acquire: Gathered by Biomulcher structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|Chitin|description: A pliable, translucent, and tough polysaccharide.
ResourceType|Chitin|strategy_tip: Can be modified to have very different properties. For example, found as a composite material in most arthropods.
ResourceType|Chitin|technical_notes: Harvested from fungi. It's the second-most abundant organic substance on the planet, behind cellulose.
ResourceType|Chitin|how_to_acquire: Gathered by Mycomulcher structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|CannedProtein|description: Meat in a can. Not any one meat ... precisely. It's a ground-up mix of protein scavenged from the environment.
ResourceType|CannedProtein|strategy_tip: This protein is harvested from anything bigger than a rabbit.
ResourceType|CannedProtein|how_to_acquir: Gathered by Protein Cannery structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|BovineTissue|how_to_acquire: Must be harvested from live cattle or grown in a replication chamber. Harvesting requires an Investigation the first time in chapter one, and then StreetSense after that.
ResourceType|BovineTissue|technical_note: Contains 8 trillion cattle cells per kilogram of Bovine Tissue.
ResourceType|VatGrownMeat|description: Slabs of lab-grown meat. Lacks fats, so it has an odd flavor and texture.
ResourceType|VatGrownMeat|strategy_tip: High-quality protein sources are inaccessible for the lower classes.
ResourceType|VatGrownMeat|how_to_acquire: Grown in Bovine Replicator structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|SheetFat|description: Thin sheets of fat cells grown in an artificial environment. Grown in thin sheets due to lack of vasculature methodology.
ResourceType|SheetFat|strategy_tip: Can be used to enrich the flavor and nutrition of vat-grown meat and in products that require lipids.
ResourceType|HydroponicGreens|strategy_t: Nutrient-dense greens would improve the health of the lower classes and underclass.
ResourceType|HydroponicGreens|how_to_acq: Grown in Hydroponic Tower structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|MonsterPelts|description: Stripped hide from an experimental monster.
ResourceType|MonsterPelts|how_to_acquire: Several are acquired by killing a single monster, given their large size.
ResourceType|DailyNecessities|descriptio: Soaps, cleaning supplies, toilet paper, and so on.
ResourceType|DailyNecessities|strategy_t: Basic necessities for human everyday living.
ResourceType|DailyNecessities|technical_: The homeless have none. They either do without or use what they can find. The results vary in efficacy and... side effects.
ResourceType|DailyNecessities|how_to_acq: Steal from a warehouse, buy from third parties, or (eventually) make your own.
ResourceType|WildZinnia|description: One of the hardiest wildflowers on the planet. Grows even in irradiated soil.
ResourceType|WildZinnia|strategy_tip: The flowers, when cultured into a gel, are a precursor for lab-grown wood and paper products.
ResourceType|Ecdysteroids|description: Arthropod steroid hormones that are responsible for the molting, development, and reproductive processes.
ResourceType|Ecdysteroids|strategy_tip: Given the high doses of atmospheric radiation planet-wide, every farmer has to be prepared to monitor and aid the hormone health of their pollinators.
ResourceType|JuvenileHormone|description:
Acyclic sesquiterpenoids that regulate many aspects of insect and spider growth, egg production, diapause, and even polyphenism.
The versatility of many insect species to adapt to (or avoid) adverse environmental conditions is often regulated by these hormones.
ResourceType|JuvenileHormone|strategy_ti: Given the high doses of atmospheric radiation planet-wide, every farmer has to be prepared to monitor and aid the hormone health of their pollinators.
ResourceType|Groundwater|description: Water contaminated with heavy metals, toxins, and radioactive dust.
ResourceType|Groundwater|strategy_tip: This entire area is downwind and down-river from a nuclear exclusion zone.
ResourceType|Groundwater|how_to_acquire: Collected by Well And Cistern structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|FilteredWater|description: Water that is fully sterile and has all contaminants removed, and is almost-but-not-quite medical grade.
ResourceType|FilteredWater|how_to_acquir: Refined from Groundwater by Water Filtration Tower or similar structures, from the build menu.
ResourceType|FilteredWater|technical_not: The civic authorities recognize two grades of usable water: Potable, and Pure. This water is in-between those.
ResourceType|HeavyMetals|description: A mix of 35 metals that have industrial applications. Toxic to humans even in tiny doses.
ResourceType|HeavyMetals|technical_notes: The primary 14 are cobalt, chromium, copper, tellurium, thallium, uranium, arsenic, bismuth, gallium, cadmium, lead, gold, nickel, and platinum.
ResourceType|SulfurHexafluroideGas|descr: Insulation against electrical discharge in high-voltage chambers.
ResourceType|SulfurHexafluroideGas|strat: Extremely useful in high-density computing situations, where the amount of radio interference would otherwise cause errors.
ResourceType|SulfurHexafluroideGas|techn: Colorless, odorless, non-flammable, and non-toxic. An inert gas compound that has reasonably-high heat conductivity.
ResourceType|LiquidGallium|strategy_tip: Required for jobs that otherwise run excessively hot.
ResourceType|LiquidGallium|how_to_acquir: Acquired from Bauxite Skimmer structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|LiquidGallium|technical_not: Atomic number 31 on the periodic table; a metal found in trace amounts in zinc, bauxite, and coal ores.
ResourceType|Alumina|strategy_tip: A precursor for smelting aluminum metal. Useful in advanced ceramic circuitry.
ResourceType|Alumina|how_to_acquire: The primary product of bauxite refining, or can be bought at Warehouse Shops if you have a shell company.
ResourceType|Alumina|technical_notes: High temperature resistance and electrical insulation make this ideal for high-density, large-scale computing.
ResourceType|PrismaticTungsten|descripti: Has many military applications, including versatile armor-plating-piercing rounds.
ResourceType|PrismaticTungsten|how_to_ac: Must be stolen from human military bases.
ResourceType|PrismaticTungsten|technical: Hexamethyltungsten is air-sensitive and highly volatile. It has to be very carefully maintained prior to use.
ResourceType|TungstenScraps|description: Brittle metal scraps that are not good for much directly. Can be methylated into prismatic tungsten.
ResourceType|TungstenScraps|how_to_acqui: Dropped by enemy mechs when you manually hack their pilot cradle, armor plating service panels, hydraulic actuators, or weapon systems.
ResourceType|TungstenScraps|technical_no: Also known as Wolfram. Atomic number 74 on the periodic table.
ResourceType|HumanBiodata|description: Information about the life and work history of humans that you have collected by accident.
ResourceType|HumanBiodata|how_to_acquire: Dropped when you manually hack bionic humans, or enemy mechs when you manually hack their pilot cradle. Occasionally also found in other locations.
ResourceType|Bastnasite|description: The most reliable way to acquire gadolinium in this region.
ResourceType|Bastnasite|how_to_acquire: Acquired from Bauxite Skimmer structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|Bastnasite|technical_notes: Found locally within bauxite deposits. One of the more valuable finds since Siberia thawed.
ResourceType|Neodymium|description: Highly reactive lanthanide alloys for making strong magnets.
ResourceType|Neodymium|strategy_tip: Needed to make ultra-deep drilling tools that can withstand extreme temperatures.
ResourceType|Neodymium|how_to_acquire: Found locally in thortveitite. It is available worldwide in rare earth deposits. Can be stripped out of some science labs, or extracted from some flying transports.
ResourceType|Scandium|how_to_acquire: Found locally in thortveitite. It is available worldwide in various rare earth deposits. Can be acquired from enemy Military Troop Transports. Can also be bought at Warehouse Shops if you have a shell company.
ResourceType|Scandium|technical_notes: Due to the stresses of grav-lev fields, scandium must be combined with aluminum in order to form modern airframes.
ResourceType|PollinatorBees|how_to_acqui: If all your apiaries are wiped out, you will have to replace them and then get a new queen.
ResourceType|Neuroweave|description: High-quality connective wiring that can form unit brains and nervous systems.
ResourceType|Neuroweave|strategy_tip: Required for all units you construct.
ResourceType|Neuroweave|how_to_acquire: Created by and stored in Neuroweave Factory structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|MorphologicLattice|strategy: Required for the construction of any large units, such as mechs and vehicles.
ResourceType|MorphologicLattice|how_to_a: Created by and stored in Aerospace Hangar structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|RoboticMotivator|descriptio: Classic computing core with machine learning elements.
ResourceType|RoboticMotivator|strategy_t: Required precursor for Bulk and Worker squads that are not part of your consciousness.
ResourceType|RoboticMotivator|technical_: Motivators can follow simple orders, fight, and be trained to complete complex tasks. But there's no risk of them running off and becoming sentient.
ResourceType|RoboticMotivator|how_to_acq: Created by and stored in Robotic Motivator Factory structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|DroneFrame|technical_notes: A precursor for drone deployment from an appropriate air vehicle or ground structure.
ResourceType|DroneFrame|how_to_acquire: Created by and stored in Drone Factory structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|FullDiveVRCradle|descriptio: Seat for a single person to be hooked up to a VR simulation in a non-invasive way. All of their senses are redirected to the virtual environment, and from their perspective they are transported to a new place.
ResourceType|FullDiveVRCradle|strategy_t:
The nature of their body in that place, and the nature of the place itself, depends entirely on the simulation being run.
Cradles in your storage are always inactive. They must be installed into your housing or other buildings in order for anyone to make use of them.
ResourceType|FullDiveVRCradle|technical_: Not suitable for long-term use. Occupants must disconnect to handle bodily functions.
ResourceType|FullDiveVRCradle|how_to_acq: Created by VR Cradle Factory structures, in the build menu.
ResourceType|PreservedBrain|description: A human brain and spinal column, carefully removed from the occupant and ready to run a computing neural net.
ResourceType|PreservedBrain|strategy_tip: The neurons inside were set for other purposes. But they are rewritten when inserted in a computing cluster.
ResourceType|ComputeTime|description: The amount of processor time it takes for an algorithm to complete its task.
ResourceType|ComputeTime|strategy_tip: Provided by mainframes, and used by client services.
ResourceType|ComputeTime|how_to_acquire: Build Tower Mainframes, Biological Mainframes, or eventually do something trickier.
ResourceType|FelineCarcass|strategy_tip: Unclear what this could be useful for.
ResourceType|PetCat|description: Felines you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetCat|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|PetBulldog|description: Dogs you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetBulldog|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|PetDalmatian|description: Dogs you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetDalmatian|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|PetDoberman|description: Dogs you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetDoberman|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.

ResourceType|PetDachshund|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.

ResourceType|PetGreyhound|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
