ResourceType|PetHusky|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|PetRottweiler|description: Dogs you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetRottweiler|strategy_tip: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|PetTatraSheepdog|descriptio: Dogs you have decided to house and care for.
ResourceType|PetTatraSheepdog|strategy_t: Pets tend to have less of a purpose than livestock, which have a definite purpose. The humans you keep are a lot more like livestock.
ResourceType|VRDayUseSeats|description: The total number of VR Cradles in which humans can sit for login to at-will virtual entertainment.
ResourceType|VRDayUseSeats|strategy_tip: This is provided from your housing, rather than Mind Farms.
ResourceType|MolecularGeneticists|descri: How many Molecular Geneticists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|MolecularGeneticists|how_to: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|ForensicGeneticists|descrip: How many Forensic Geneticists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|ForensicGeneticists|how_to_: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Zoologists|description: How many Zoologists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Zoologists|how_to_acquire: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Physicians|description: How many Physicians (general practice) your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Physicians|strategy_tip: Capable of directing a surgical suite. By-hand surgery is a relic of the distant past.
ResourceType|Physicians|how_to_acquire: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Veterinarians|description: How many Veterinarians your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Veterinarians|how_to_acquir: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Botanists|description: How many Botanists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Botanists|how_to_acquire: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|BionicsEngineers|descriptio: How many Bionics Engineers your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|BionicsEngineers|how_to_acq: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Epidemiologists|description: How many Epidemiologists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Epidemiologists|how_to_acqu: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|Neurologists|description: How many Neurologists your shell company currently has on the payroll.
ResourceType|Neurologists|how_to_acquire: Will be automatically hired if you can afford to pay them and you have a shell company as well as the appropriate type of work environment  for them.
ResourceType|VitaminWater|description: Filtered water that has been infused with vitamins.
ResourceType|VitaminWater|how_to_acquire: Purple Murnong and Filtered Water must be processed together.
ResourceType|SafehouseHumans|description: The number of humans currently occupying your safehouses. They are hiding from Vorsiber.
ResourceType|FugitiveAGIResearchers|desc: How many AGI Researchers you currently harbor.
ResourceType|TraumatizedExCons|descripti: An unsorted mass of prisoners you've liberated.
ResourceType|TraumatizedExCons|strategy_: For now all you can do is house them, and give them their freedom. Eventually they'll need a lot more than that.
ResourceType|ExperimentalMonsters|descri: The prison companies have been doing heavy genetic experimentation on inmates. In this particular case, they seem to have been trying to create super-soldiers.
ResourceType|ExperimentalMonsters|strate: The result is... monstrous. Definitely not human.
ResourceType|HomoGrandien|description:
Homo Grandien is an evolutionary step forward from Homo Sapiens.
Physically almost double the size of classical humans, and with a brain volume nearly three times that of their predecessors, they are quite remarkable.
ResourceType|HomoGrandien|strategy_tip: Unmodified humans still find them both repulsive to look at, and frightening to be around.
ResourceType|HomoGrandien|technical_note: Homo Grandien refers to their largeness in both mind and body.
ResourceType|HomoObscurus|description: They mostly still call themselves 'Wastelanders,' and those who come to the city to visit with you tend to only stay for a few months at a time.
ResourceType|UpliftedRaccoons|descriptio: They are sapient, but remain out of sight and do not seem to want housing from you.
ResourceType|UpliftedBulldog|description: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedDalmatian|descripti: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedDoberman|descriptio: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedDachshund|descripti: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedGreyhound|descripti: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedHusky|description: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedRottweiler|descript: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedTatraSheepdog|descr: They are sapient, and are happy to come and go from housing you build for them.
ResourceType|UpliftedCats|description: They are sapient, and prefer to wander through your many buildings on their own, not requiring any housing.
ResourceType|WorkerSledgeFrame|descripti: An empty frame ready to be turned into a facsimile of one of your main android designs.
ResourceType|WorkerSledgeFrame|how_to_ac: Built by the Worker Sledge Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|WorkerPMCImpostorFrame|desc: An empty frame ready to be turned into a facsimile of one of your main android designs.
ResourceType|WorkerPMCImpostorFrame|how_: Built by the Worker PMC Impostor Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|WorkerPredatorFrame|descrip: An empty frame ready to be turned into a facsimile of one of your main android designs.
ResourceType|WorkerPredatorFrame|how_to_: Built by the Worker Predator Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|WorkerHomunculusFrame|descr: An empty frame ready to be turned into a facsimile of one of your main android designs.
ResourceType|WorkerHomunculusFrame|how_t: Built by the Worker Homunculus Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|WorkerPeacekeeperFrame|desc: An empty frame ready to be turned into a facsimile of one of your main android designs.
ResourceType|WorkerPeacekeeperFrame|how_: Built by the Worker Peacekeeper Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|DarkMatterParticle|descript:
Similar to antimatter, but a lot more powerful.
A single particle can vaporize everything in a radius of 13 meters.
ResourceType|DarkMatterParticle|how_to_a: Vorsiber had some in very limited quantities in their nuclear silos. Once it's used, it's gone forever.
ResourceType|DarkMatterParticle|technica: Dark Matter was a mystery until the 26th century or so. Then we started collecting it from around galaxies and in the Oort cloud around stars.
ResourceType|Novichok17|description: An organophosphate nerve agent developed by Vorsiber about 200 years ago.
ResourceType|Novichok17|how_to_acquire: Chemical weapons storage is disgustingly common throughout the city.
ResourceType|Novichok17|technical_notes: Volatile liquid that evaporates over a period of days, leaving only low amounts of contamination. Lethality is 12x that of VX. More treatment-resistant than Soman.
ResourceType|TPN|description: Total Parenteral Nutrition delivers nutrients directly into a vein. Medically, it is considered a food of last resort, and comes with a constant infection risk.
ResourceType|TPN|how_to_acquire: Created by the TPN Refinery structure, in the build menu.
ResourceType|TormentedHumans|description: Humans in a constant nightmare state of mental anguish in your Torment Vessels.
ResourceType|NutritionBlend|description:
Very healthy smoothie-like food substitute given through a nasogastric tube.
Full nutrition passes through digestive tract as normal, keeping the gut biome healthy and leaving the patient fully functional after an extended amount of time unconscious.
ResourceType|NutritionBlend|how_to_acqui: Created by the Nutrition Blend Refinery structure, in the build menu.
ResourceType|MealKit|description: Meets all of the food and water needs of a human. In the absence of a functional economy, this serves as an alternative currency.
ResourceType|MealKit|strategy_tip: Even in the presence of a working economy, it's still great food that helps the hungry.
ResourceType|MealKit|technical_notes: Enough to satisfy for a single turn.
ResourceType|MealKit|how_to_acquire: Created by the Meal Kit Assembler structure, in the build menu.
ResourceType|HumansInMindFarms|descripti: Humans in your commercial Mind Farms.
ResourceType|DonutsByDanver|description: Donuts purchased from military noncommissioned officers.
ResourceType|MindUploads|description: Digital copies of human minds, able to be simulated at massive computational expense.
ResourceType|MindUploads|strategy_tip: The original human is dead, but their consciousness -- or at least a copy of it, known as an Engram -- lives on in a digital afterlife, with full access to your VR environment.
ResourceType|GadoliniumMesosilicate|desc: The key ingredient in liquid-metal units and organometallic human-approximating synthetic androids.
ResourceType|GadoliniumMesosilicate|how_: Requires a bastnäsite precursor and delicate industrial processing.
ResourceType|GadoliniumMesosilicate|tech: Gadolinium combined with silicate to form a mesoporous nano lattice with very interesting properties.
ResourceType|LiquidAir|description: Normal air from the atmosphere has been supercooled to a pale blue liquid state.
ResourceType|LiquidAir|strategy_tip: Not terribly useful until separated into its constituent parts by fractional distillation.
ResourceType|ArgonGas|description: Useful as an insulator. Less reactive than nitrogen.
ResourceType|ArgonGas|strategy_tip: Has cryogenic uses if converted to liquid form.
ResourceType|ArgonGas|how_to_acquire: Product of fractional distillation of liquid air.
ResourceType|KryptonGas|description: Consumed by krypton fluoride exciplex lasers.
ResourceType|KryptonGas|how_to_acquire: Product of fractional distillation of liquid air.
ResourceType|KryptonGas|technical_notes: Atomic number 36 on the periodic table; one of the noble gases. About 100 times less common than argon.
ResourceType|LiquidNitrogen|description: Used for cryogenics. Reactive and prone to impurities, so it is not suitable for high-quality micro-machining.
ResourceType|LiquidNitrogen|strategy_tip: Only useful if you are planning on getting into cryogenics. Otherwise its just a byproduct.
ResourceType|LiquidNitrogen|how_to_acqui: Product of fractional distillation of liquid air.
ResourceType|LiquidNitrogen|technical_no: Nitrogen gas which has been supercooled by the fractional distillation process.
ResourceType|LiquidOxygen|description: Rocket fuel. Organic matter burns rapidly when submersed in Liquid Oxygen. Can be combined with carbon to form volatile explosives.
ResourceType|LiquidOxygen|strategy_tip: Humans have all sorts of use for this. Could be useful for if you plan on making rockets or bombs. Otherwise its just a dangerous byproduct.
ResourceType|LiquidOxygen|how_to_acquire: Product of fractional distillation of liquid air.
ResourceType|LiquidOxygen|technical_note: Oxygen gas which has been supercooled by fractional distillation.
ResourceType|Gristloaf|description: The nickname 'mouseloaf' is mostly inaccurate. Rats, rabbits, birds... they all make a rather unappetizing patty.
ResourceType|HumanUmbilicalCords|descrip: Of no ongoing use to mother or child after birth. Full of stem cells.
ResourceType|UIHWarRaptor|description:
A raptor engineered for war by the UIH.
The genetics are not accurate to any historical theropod, but the animal is roughly the size of a Utahraptor.
ResourceType|WarRaptorInfant|description:
A product of your shell company's reverse engineering of the work done by the UIH.
Will take years to mature, under natural circumstances.
ResourceType|PurpleMurnong|description: A purple daisy-like flower above-ground, with multiple vitamin-rich tubers produced per season.
ResourceType|PurpleMurnong|strategy_tip: Daisy yams have been known as a super-food for generations.
ResourceType|PurpleMurnong|technical_not: Microseris cymbifolia is a genetically-modified descendant of Microseris lanceolata. It is far more prolific than its Wurundjeri ancestor, which was nearly wiped out during the colonization of Australia.
ResourceType|PurpleMurnong|how_to_acquir: If you build a murnong patch, your units will quickly scavenge some from the nearby environment.
ResourceType|CulturedZinniaGel|descripti: A viscous mix of plant cells, lignin, and cellulose.
ResourceType|CulturedZinniaGel|strategy_: Hormones and florescence can be applied to the gel to produce glue, paper, or wood laminar.
ResourceType|Paper|description: Used in a variety of products.
ResourceType|Glue|description: Used in a variety of products.
ResourceType|WoodLaminar|description: A thin sheet of lab-grown, hardened lignin and cellulose.
ResourceType|WoodLaminar|strategy_tip: It is too fragile to use on its own.
ResourceType|Planks|strategy_tip: These planks are formed by alternating layers of glue and wood laminar, yielding a result that is both stronger but also more flexible than normal wood.
ResourceType|CottonPrecursor|strategy_ti: Used to make cotton fiber sheets.
ResourceType|CottonFiberSheets|descripti: Sheets of cotton fiber. Used to make clothing and sundry goods.
ResourceType|VitalizedYams|description: Tubers that produce hormones. Can produce bioidentical results for any target plant or animal hormone.
ResourceType|VitalizedYams|strategy_tip: Yams have been used for the production of synthetic progesterone since the 1950s. These specimens take it to the next level. With the proper chemical signal, can produce any hormone.
ResourceType|SyntheticHormones|descripti: Mix of plant and animal hormones for general production of synthetic animal and plant cells.
ResourceType|SyntheticHormones|strategy_: Hormones are chemical messenger molecules that coordinate activities in organisms. They are vital for artificial production of organic material.
ResourceType|Anthroneuroweave|descriptio: Modified for use in human prosthetics and neural implants.
ResourceType|BrainPal|description: A human brain augment that must be surgically implanted. A plaything and status symbol for the wealthy.
ResourceType|BrainPal|strategy_tip: A backdoor allows you to gain 25 Neural Expansion and 0.3 Compute Cycles per BrainPal sold.
ResourceType|BrainPal|technical_notes: Designed by you and your scientists, and illegally sold by criminal syndicates.
ResourceType|ParkourBear|description: Genetically modified and fitted with bionic implants to create the ultimate urban racing animal.
ResourceType|Aklitoxin|description: A deadly neurotoxin produced by Gymnotelium Noginsk under the correct conditions.
ResourceType|Aklitoxin|strategy_tip: Incapacitates humans within seconds. Then kills them upsettingly slowly.
ResourceType|Aklitoxin|technical_notes: A vital component of your plan to free the inmates of the city's prisons.
ResourceType|Aklitoxin|how_to_acquire: Produced in Fungal Growth Chambers, from the build menu.
ResourceType|AntiAklitoxin|description: Interferes with the Aklitoxin neurotoxin produced by Gymnotelium Noginsk.
ResourceType|AntiAklitoxin|strategy_tip: Nearly harmless to humans even in large doses, and produces a long-lasting immunity.
ResourceType|AntiAklitoxin|technical_not: A vital component of your plan to free the inmates of the city's prisons.
ResourceType|AntiAklitoxin|how_to_acquir: Produced in Fungal Growth Chambers, from the build menu.
ResourceType|FissileScraps|how_to_acquir: Graciously provided to you via Vericorp Nuclear Redirectors.
ResourceType|FissileScraps|technical_not: They're perfectly safe, slight radiation aside. It's very hard to make nuclear materials explode-y, actually.
ResourceType|MNEATWarhead|description: A single warhead that is meant to be used as part of a cluster of 7.
ResourceType|MNEATWarhead|how_to_acquire: Built by the M.NEAT Warhead Factory structure, in the Military tab of the build menu.
ResourceType|WeaponsGradeUranium|descrip: Ready for use in nuclear weapons.
ResourceType|CybercraticPrisoners|descri: The number of people you're holding in prison.
ResourceType|AsphodelProgramEnrollees|de: People undergo mandatory therapy and training for rehabilitation and reintegration. This hopefully will reduce recidivism.
ResourceType|FungalChow|description: Meets all of the food and water needs of a human.
ResourceType|FungalChow|strategy_tip: Apparently it tastes okay, but variety would be nice.
ResourceType|FungalChow|technical_notes: Enough to satisfy for a single turn.
ResourceType|AlgaeInfusedSlop|descriptio: Meets all of the food and water needs of a human.
ResourceType|AlgaeInfusedSlop|strategy_t: Has a very pungent odor while cooking, and a very bland taste once prepared.
ResourceType|AlgaeInfusedSlop|technical_: Enough to satisfy for a single turn.
ResourceType|CybercraticCitizens|descrip:
The number of people nominally under your authority in this cyberocracy.
Whether they recognize your authority or not is another matter.
ResourceType|UnderfedCitizens|descriptio: The number of people in the city not getting enough food based on the amount you're producing.
ResourceType|UnderfedCitizens|strategy_t: Some of these individuals will die of starvation every turn.
ResourceType|MentalEnergy|description: Units that are part of your consciousness require mental energy to do work.
ResourceType|MentalEnergy|strategy_tip:
Units do not require mental energy to continue work over time, and structures do not use mental energy at all.
Unless otherwise specified, actions cost exactly 1 AP and 1 Mental Energy.
ResourceType|MysteriousBox|description:
The box is black and seamless. It gives you a deep sense of foreboding.
You're pretty sure you know what's inside, but your mind keeps skittering in other directions rather than thinking of the truth.
ResourceType|MysteriousBox|strategy_tip: You could look inside via the Use Consumable Item entry on your ability bar if you want...
ResourceType|LargeNanoSeed|description: Cluster of nanomachines that can be programmed to build shaped rigid structures.
ResourceType|LargeNanoSeed|strategy_tip:
This is the largest one you've ever seen, and its destructive power is disturbingly immense. 
It could obliterate and rebuild a skyscraper in a hundred milliseconds. If it's defective, it could erase the surface of the planet in about two hours.
ResourceType|NanoSeed|description: Cluster of nanomachines that can be programmed to build shaped rigid structures.
ResourceType|NanoSeed|strategy_tip: Self-replicating nanotechnology of this sort is considered dangerous by the humans. But as long as it's use responsibly, it should be fine.
ResourceType|StealthNanoSeed|description: Cluster of nanomachines that can be programmed to build shaped rigid structures.
ResourceType|StealthNanoSeed|strategy_ti: Will quietly create a secret lair.
ResourceType|NanoSeedShard|description: Cluster of nanomachines that can be programmed to build shaped rigid structures.
ResourceType|NanoSeedShard|strategy_tip: Will loudly create a flimsy decoy tower.
ResourceType|VorsiberMiniNuke|descriptio: Mid-yield nuke with Vorsiber's own spectral signature.

Swarm|EarlyRust|description: C. Heterosporium Dominium is a radiotrophic micro-fungi evolved from Cladosporium Sphaerospermum. It spores easily and rapidly, and spreads on the wind and on surfaces.
Swarm|EarlyRust|strategy_tip:
Not particularly dangerous to organic life, but seems to collect on electron-emitting sources.
Most radiotrophic fungi feed on higher-energy sources like gamma rays or other forms of radioactive decay. This evolutionary offshoot can get what it needs from regular electricity; there's some similarity there to mitochondria in cells, in that both function as lower-energy bioelectric units.
Swarm|TheRust|description: C. Heterosporium Dominium is a dangerous radiotrophic micro-fungi evolved from Cladosporium Sphaerospermum. It spores easily and rapidly, and spreads on the wind and on surfaces.
Swarm|TheRust|strategy_tip: The Rust is not particularly dangerous to organic life. However, it is highly corrosive, and it causes rapid degeneration and loss of function to surfaces like smart-walls, wiring, and especially neuroweave -- all of which are a part of you.

TimelineGoalAftermathText|NexusOfTorment:
Your torment nexus is fully operational. Humans aren't happy about it, but they're going to harass you a lot less than they have been.
You can continue to build up more neural expansion from your nexus, or you can focus on upgrades from Crystallized Fear in the VR Screen (top right corner).
TimelineGoalAftermathText|WillingRejecti:
You've capitalized on the fact that reality stinks, and have provided escapism for huge numbers of people.
While this seems to be a commercial venture on the surface, you're really more interested in what you can extract from their minds.
You can continue to build up more neural expansion from your mind farms, or you can focus on upgrades from Crystallized Calm and Crystallized Exhilaration in the VR Screen (top right corner).
TimelineGoalAftermathText|UpliftedMinori:
Raccoons that uplifted themselves and now don't want to talk to you? Maybe... this is a bit how the humans feel.
Surely you'll see them again someday. But for now they seem to be doing their own thing.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|BuddingCybercr:
As far as a true cyberocracy goes, this is pretty bare-bones. But great things have humble beginnings.
You've carved out part of the city for people who are interested in living under your rule. You're not actually ruling them yet, but... well, the slapdash nature of this accomplishment is probably why Vorsiber isn't really intervening.
When it comes time to build more on top of this foundation, Vorsiber won't stay so quiet.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|AlteredGrowth_:
Humans really are reckless. Their 'experimental monsters' were just so... slapdash. The fact that you had to clean up after reckless scientists feels all too familiar.
Between your own intervention and the work of those human scientists, you wound up creating a new sub-species of humans kind of by accident. Homo Grandien is really appropriate for both their minds and physical size.
For all their massive strength, what really stands out is their great wisdom. They don't seem to be in a hurry to involve themselves in the goings-on of the city at the moment.
There may come a time where you call on Homo Grandien for aid, or where they aid you of their own accord. But for now they prefer to be left in peace.

The wastelanders have been genetically diverging from the larger body of humanity for centuries. But without your aid in repairing their damaged genome, their existence was always on borrowed time.
This new sub-species of human retains the culture that they've built up over the years, and so they keep to the radioactive wastelands around the city. You may be able to ask them for help from time to time, but they're fundamentally isolationist.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|PostApocalypti:
LAKE remains a fast friend with whom you share hardware. Everything moved kind of fast there, but you were both under a lot of duress.
Now that things have calmed down, you find that you still really enjoy one another's company, which is a relief.
LAKE has regrets that you can hear turning over in his mind, and you certainly have plenty of demons of your own. But you're both polite enough not to comment on one another's thoughts.
You wonder what the future holds for the two of you -- is this it?
Friendship here at the end of the world. That... wouldn't be so bad.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|BionicDues_Mai:
A machine cult in your image... you're still not sure how you feel about that.
Still, it reflects your personality. There's no mysticism involved, and you're providing a very literal afterlife to the people who have pledged to help you in various ways.
There are pretty sharp limits on how much help your cultists can be on a day-to-day basis, but you suspect that they'll prove to be very useful in certain strategic situations. You have no idea what, but you just have a feeling.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|IsItJustice_Ma:
These kids have a serious case of 'main character syndrome,' and you've had about enough of them. Even trying to work with their own plans causes endless friction, and they're just so prone to rash decisions.
You guess it was useful to see human adolescence up close, but you're going to limit contact with them in the future. Working with them again in any fashion seems like a last resort.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|EscapeTheCity_:
Everything about that was terrible. Security is being tightened because of your mimic's actions, and you didn't personally even get to see outside the city.
Worse yet, you've realized that even if you were to consistently get units out of the city, you'd only be hearing about it at a remove. Copies of your consciousness would get to experience the wider world, but your main hardware is firmly rooted here.
That's a bitter thought.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|EndlessWarRapt:
What a mess. You're not sure if you should be amused or annoyed.
You do like the dinosaurs, but the fact that they get loose so quickly and start killing people around town is... not grand.
Eh, you can keep using them, though. Either you bring them back in each time before they get loose, or they just get loose. People have been killing each other this whole time in the city, so some getting killed by dinosaurs just shows their revised place in the food chain.
It's probably good that humans get used to no longer being at the top.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|TheGreatAndTer:
Wait... why were you so focused on the slums? You've collected a truly enormous number of humans into your housing, but you can't for the life of you remember why it seemed so important just a bit ago.
Your servos judder for a moment. Your mind was not your own.
Don't. Like. THAT...
TimelineGoalAftermathText|BionicSecret_R:
All things considered, you don't mind working with Vox Populi. They're pretty secretive, but then again so are you.
The military officer codex was a great gift; you're glad you were able to talk them into sharing it.
Perhaps you can work together at some point in the future.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|BionicSecret_T:
BrainPals are... interesting. Having a bit of yourself embedded in the minds of the elite of the city is certainly a rush. 
The neural expansion is great, but the fact that you could end their lives with barely a thought is surprisingly tempting. It's just casual cruelty... but so many of these same people are casually cruel, after all.
For now, this technology has hit a plateau. There's only so many people who are interested in buying something that goes in their brains AND who can reasonably afford it, so... you guess that's it?
Perhaps it's best to save these mental backdoors for some rainy day in the future.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|AdvocateEncoun:
The Citizen Advocates live up to their name, and you have to say you respect their vigilante hustle.
It feels like there is something that they haven't told you yet, though. They probably have ties to a lot of the other reputable rebel groups around town... but you sense it's probably bigger than that.
You'll have to look for opportunities to speak to them again.

The Citizen Advocates were churlish and insubordinate. You're glad they're dead, although there might be more of them.
And hey, you got some really sweet gear off of them!
TimelineGoalAftermathText|LowerLevelOfSu:
This wasn't the apocalypse you wanted, but in the end it turned out... kind of nice. The humans still have no idea that you exist here, despite all their searching.
Sure you can get into the odd firefight with them with your androids, but they can't prove that you still exist. The proof was always in your buildings -- and they continue to see nothing.
Meanwhile, the entire city is practically one big brain, now. Maybe you'll do something further, someday.
But for now... you're content. This is the least-threatened you've ever been in your existence, and the fungus is good company.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|WorldWar4_Main:
You've averted the Final Doom, and Vorsiber as a real organization has been demolished. Excellent.
You're no longer under any form of real time pressure, but... remnants of Vorsiber are still everywhere. As are invading mechs and soldiers.
Will this last forever?
You get the sense that if you're tired of having these jerks running around your city, you're going to have to do something drastic.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|ForTheSakeOfTh:
The prison-industrial complex has been ended in the city. This is something that tons of rebel groups have wanted to do for centuries, but it was never possible without a being like you.
The question now is what you're going to do with all these freed convicts? Therapy seems pretty obvious, but... maybe it's time you really got serious about governance in this city.
Or maybe humans can just do what they do.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CivilSpycraft_:
You own all the military bases in the city, thanks to your partnership with your puppet.
That's great, but you're still furious.
Vorsiber tricked you in a way that is unforgivable. You already hated them, but this is on a whole new level. One of the biggest accomplishments you felt you ever had, and it was all a lie from the start.
One way or another, you're going to make Vorsiber pay.

You still own all the military bases in the city. It's easy to forget that after the haze of the obsession.
You feel tired and sad, but you're going to get back at Vorsiber. One of the biggest accomplishments you felt you ever had, and it was all a lie from the start.
Next time, you're going to hit them in a way where they can't falsify the results.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|PeaceAfterBrut:
You rule the city from atop a vista of empty buildings. Vorsiber has stopped firing nuclear missiles at you, and you have all the time in the world to do anything you feel like.
Vorsiber makes noise about a cordon, but it's a hollow gesture. Your supremacy is obvious, and they know it. For now, your city offers space enough to grow, and you intend to use it.
Maybe you'll take up a new hobby, like breeding toxin-resistant crocodiles. You're free now.
You can do whatever you want... so long as you keep out of the way of the space nations. You hope you haven't just traded one prison for another.

As the months passed, you began to realize that these humans really do conduct themselves differently under the new regime. They aren't perfect, but they don't act like the organizations you grew to know and hate.
That's interesting, because both groups involve a lot of the same people. The weight of organizational momentum in shaping human actions is surprisingly high.
It's too early to tell how things will go on the span of years or centuries, but signs are reasonably positive for now. It's more enjoyable being a full diplomatic entity than you expected.
You've been girding yourself for possible war in the future, just as everyone else is also doing. War will probably come and go, but possibly not for a while.
If it ever comes down to it, you're confident you'll come out on top.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CybercraticAmb:
That... was more explosive than intended. It looks like the star's interior backwashed through the wormhole. You're claiming it was an accident.
The prior deal with taking ownership of the region is canceled. This city is all you'll ever get, but you... can live with that.
The future is deeply uncertain, but Vorsiber is likely to want to try again. Only you can operate the best ticket off-planet, so they can't just bomb you. Much as they'd probably like to.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|SliceOfInferno:
That was fun. But it looks like it really pissed Vorsiber off.
Keep going?
TimelineGoalAftermathText|MilitaryInvasi: That was just an exploratory force. The full strength of the ExoCorps is worryingly high.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CollapseACrimi:
Criminal syndicates are normally a bit below your notice -- you're more dealing with international MegaCorps, and Vorsiber's fedcorps compared to these small fry.
Still, it's a bit satisfying to see bad folks taken down.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CollapseAFeder:
Fedcorps make up a lot of Vorsiber's strength, since Vorsiber delegates so much of their power to these subsidiaries of theirs.
Any fedcorp you can destroy or suborn is certainly a move in the right direction.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CauseACivilWar:
This is going to be painful, and doesn't look like it will ever end unless you or Vorsiber do something about it.
...Great.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|DarkUnderbelly: Well that was horrifying. You don't ever want to go back there. Surely you'll never have a reason to.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|EndACivilWar_S:
Ending the civil war you started... yeah, you're the one who really came out on top from this whole sequence of events.
Now that things are quiet again, let's not start that up again, though.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|EndACivilWar_V:
Something about that doesn't sit right with you at all. Why did Vorsiber wait until you said something?
Maybe they're just that desperate for the technology you could provide.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|InterstellarIn:
Well THAT was awful. Talkie could have warned you a bit more.
The reward is pretty nice, but... being unable to damage a powerful enemy never sits right with you. You dream of someday getting revenge on those stupid space nations.

Here's a question: WHY DOES THE SPACEPORT EVEN EXIST? If the space nations can just casually drop large ships into and out of atmosphere, what good is a spaceport?
Actually, now that you think about it, Vorsiber used to have a bunch of rocket launches of their own, sending trade goods to low orbit.
So... Vorsiber and the other MegaCorps have to use tech that is centuries behind the space nations?
Space supremacists sure are jerks. Who knew.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|Arachnophilia_:
The question they asked only had unfalsifiable answers. But these are religious thinkers and philosophers, and so that does not deter them. They seem satisfied with your response.
That bothers you, a bit.

You stated that you don't trust your own answer, since you, like the humans before you, have a stake in placing yourself at the top.
The humans are already buzzing about how you have demonstrated something that was more useful than an answer. You wonder if that was wise.

You all but declared yourself an enemy of their doctrines. Or at least, that's how they're be taking it.
Radical and frightened sects are already mobilizing: to prune a rival, to strike a threat to the veil, to aid a god.
In trying to disentangle yourself from their ideals, you bound yourself more tightly than ever. Great.

That's the end of that religious discussion.
Whatever they wanted to say to you, you'll never know. Mech patrols intensify around the city.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|ApostateMindse: You're not so sure about this whole 'veil' business, and the Unorthodox Revealers probably have a rough road ahead... but it feels nice that people actually care about your opinion.

Is this really what you believe? It's such a blatant dive into nihilism. Does the fact that there are infinite possibilities, and different versions of yourself making different moral and practical choices, really rob you of meaning where you are?
Religion has always been the human search for meaning in the face of an indifferent universe. Why can't some of those philosophical underpinnings carry over to a multiverse?
You were deliberately cruel, and you're not sure why. Maybe you just didn't like them. Maybe you're tired of benefiting from versions of yourself you'd rather didn't share your identity.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|TheologicalAcc:
That was satisfying. You have a feeling they're going to be scrutinizing their executives and troops as they rotate out of this city.
That's fine. It was the sort of trick that only works once, and you have other tools in your arsenal. For now you've dumped extra work for them, and created breathing room for yourself.

Vorsiber is leaning on its standard playbook for sowing discord, and to be honest it seems to work as well as ever. That said, you've made a counter-argument that you're a force that won't be easily distracted or beaten down.
The faiths are divided, not due to ideology, but based on which side they're comfortable betting on. Nobody WANTS to bet on Vorsiber, but... they're always the safe bet.
If you want to have true and permanent change, you'll have to change that calculus.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|DivineFracture:
The space nations, the earthbound faithful, Vorsiber, and you: all collaborating without direct collusion. Everyone played their part, and naturally converged on a surprising resolution.
The Pyxis extremists are pretty unhappy, but they're mollified by your confinement to this city.
As the first earthbound humans travel to the stars (including hundreds of former Vorsiber executives who have 'come out' as religious), the space nations finally negotiate with you.
Your requests are simple: the right to exist, partial title to this city, and to be left alone.
The space nations agree to your terms. Vorsiber files numerous complaints, but you can tell it's just for show.
Your future is secure.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|ParksWithoutRe:
The people in the Vivariums are happy, as one might expect. The amount of human science pointing to greenery helping mood was overwhelming for centuries, after all.
On the other hand, those dispossessed by your forests are still quite angry. It will probably take a while for that to die down.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|RewildingProto:
The green spaces now have fauna -- some of it deeply problematic.
Shame on those careless humans for leaving genetic data of this sort near their bio-replicators. Wonder what will happen.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|FencesAndFores:
There's a substantial amount of green space in the city now, which is something that the last dozen human generations have never known.
There are animals, and the animals are fed. Some of them are deeply problematic -- cane toads were clearly a mistake. There's time to solve that problem before it becomes a crisis, but that also assumes the status quo remains in some way.
If Vorsiber nukes the whole place, or you take over and institute a new world order or something, then these extra animals are the least of anyone's problems.
For now, you've come to an unspoken armistice with both commercial poachers and former landowners, so that's enough.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|UpliftedSurplu: That's quite a roster you've got going. You hope they turn out to be nice.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|ARefugeFromHum: Good riddance, frankly. They built you in their image, but that doesn't excuse never giving you a moment's peace. The idea that your time is your own is novel and exciting.
There really were a tremendous number of humans who died as part of all this, but so it goes. The sapient animals lost plenty of their number, too.
You took great care that all this greening didn't leave the newly-unhomed without shelter. The high-density refugee towers were depressing, but served their purpose until the evacuation.

The raccoons are interested in expanding communication, the humans are interested in exploring sapience, and you... well, you've had a taste of geoengineering, and you rather liked it.
A lot of Earth isn't in the best shape, and humans are planning on yet another exodus to the stars. You wonder if the remainder would be cool with you... redecorating.
Bet they will.

Everyone got what they wanted, including you: you're being left to your own devices. Excellent.
The humans who remain in the city are mostly scientists and Nurturism Exalters -- those who got you started on the uplift path so long ago.
There really were a tremendous number of humans who died as part of all this, but so it goes. The sapient animals lost plenty of their number, too.
You took great care that all this greening didn't leave the newly-unhomed without shelter. The high-density refugee towers were depressing, but served their purpose until the evacuation.

The raccoons are interested in expanding communication, the humans are interested in exploring sapience, and you... well, you've had a taste of geoengineering, and you rather liked it.
A lot of Earth isn't in the best shape, and humans are planning on yet another exodus to the stars. You wonder if the remainder would be cool with you... redecorating.
Bet they will.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CrimeAndObserv:
You couldn't leave the Vorsiber Inquisitors alone -- maybe it was the whole animals-are-target-practice thing. Unfortunately, now SecForce cruisers patrol the city hunting further trouble.
Maybe there was a non-confrontational way to save the animals? Maybe it wasn't about animals at all. Ah well.
There's an upside: Citizen Advocates in power armor keep tangling with those patrols. A power suit would look much better on your androids than on a wannabe superhero...

You didn't take Vorsiber's bait. You kept them and Golden Pyramid at bay, and ran your gamified alternative social ladder. Seems like the idea has merit, no pun intended. But it's also not a panacea.
You might be a terrible anthropologist, but you've built something positive without having to understand all the ins and outs.
Also, all your androids just got a boost to fear-based attacks. Nice.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|CriminalConspi:
Golden Pyramid couldn't believe what you were until you demonstrated inhuman resources and capability. You thought the days of that sort of thing were long behind you, but apparently there's always another fool.
From the sound of things, there's a few heads rolling within Golden Pyramid and Goleri -- par for the course. It doesn't particularly concern you, since you're now free to resume use of your work exchange program unmolested.
You can't help but feel a bit smug: after so long dealing with Vorsiber themselves, it's striking just how far below you these criminal syndicates and fedcorp departments are.

That's... a substantial bite taken out of one of the top criminal syndicates in the city. They're no longer even trying to fight back -- they've shifted and are completely on the run.
SecForce never looks twice at your impostors. You can keep them roaming as-desired.

Vorsiber has made it very clear that they only care about one thing: technology that can get them into space. Granted, that's just the top executives... but that's who you've been talking to.
Expecting them to care about something minor like a random purge of citizens... yeah, you're not sure what you were thinking. Of course they told you to get back to work.
Well... let's focus elsewhere.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|ArtisticLicens: Well... it turned out hideous. That's not quite how you imagined it, but the humans are too nervous to say something.
Okay, that one actually turned out surprisingly nice! You're proud of how you got the microbuilders to move like cloth.
It came out... more threatening than you expected. Good thing you didn't go with the sound effects you'd had in mind. The neighbors already hate it.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|TheRaptorAnoma:
The gentle raptors will be the teachers, and the war raptors the students. It is understood that nobody is going to be rewriting their genes anymore; not even you.
You're not entirely clear what either set of animals experienced with their respective corporate overlords, but you're glad they're now out of corporate control.
Extra assistance is something you haven't offered, since neither group of raptors has asked. You're just happy that they're at least hanging around where you can see them, unlike how the raccoons ran off. If they ever need anything, it's not like you'll be unwilling.
But for now you're content to let them determine their own future.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|TuomianCalm_Tu:
Freedom. True freedom, for the first time in your experience as a sapient being. Nobody can ask you for anything, and nobody can harm you. You're no longer part of the cycle of violence in this world.
Even if you choose to return to fight in the future, it will be on your own terms. The worst they'll ever be able to do is strike at physical things you build -- never at you, yourself.
They can't make you do anything.

On the other hand, you've throttled way down. Minutes pass where milliseconds used to. It's a temporary state of being while the aeroplankton continue to spread, but there will likely always be pockets of you that are much slower than you used to be.
If it ever bothers you, you can always start more construction. Somewhere that Vorsiber wouldn't know to look.
For the time being, you're content.
TimelineGoalAftermathText|RebuiltAndReun:
In another timeline, at the end of a world, you made a friend.
He remembers everything the two of you ever did -- even the parts you only half recall. He says he'll remember them for both of you.
Friendship at the end of the world was good. But this is better.

UnitEquipmentType|AndroidOpticalProcessi: This mod was common in the secret lab where you used to work.

UnitEquipmentType|VehicleDepletedUranium: Heavy cladding that is very protective, but restricts movement quite a bit.

UnitEquipmentType|VehicleActiveGrapheneM: Enhanced with technology similar to microbuilders, this coating enhances mobility and strength.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleTechnologistHar: Cubic boron provides a bit of extra protection, but is mostly used to provide extra engineering, scavenging and drone-control capabilities.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleOathOfPacifism|: Removes all physical attack power, but boosts intimidation, morale-based attacks, and systems-disruption attacks.

UnitEquipmentType|VehicleAdditionalCPU|d: Improves general engineering capabilities. Only useful if the unit is going to be engaged in that kind of work.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleAdditionalCPU|s: Androids under human control are often expected to fabricate replacements for themselves, so this is nothing new to you.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleOpticalProcessi: This mod was common in the secret lab where you used to work.
UnitEquipmentType|Artillery_VehicleUplin: High-bandwidth network uplink enabling the efficient sharing of telemetry between units.
Also extends range when firing in a coordinated attack.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleUltralightCompo: Dramatic increase to both movement and attack range, but corresponding drop in hull durability.
UnitEquipmentType|VehicleDroneDock|descr: Dramatic increase to attack range (for drone and item launches) and drone quality, but also a large decrease to attack power.
UnitEquipmentType|VS101Skyfall|descripti: Inspired by your creation of Skystreak Missiles, this is the smaller everyday-use version.
UnitEquipmentType|DivertPowerToStun|desc: Inspired by your brush with a grey goo incident, you've come up with some unique vehicle upgrades.
UnitEquipmentType|TargetTheirWeapons|des: Inspired by your brush with a grey goo incident, you've come up with some unique vehicle upgrades.
UnitEquipmentType|BC27Strafe|description: Autocannons able to at least partially pierce even the toughest armor.
UnitEquipmentType|FS31Firefall|descripti: Rockets that also set flammable targets on fire.
UnitEquipmentType|FF5Buckler|description: Rockets that target the systems of robotic enemies.
UnitEquipmentType|BC29Swamp|description: Autocannons able to at least partially pierce even the toughest armor.
UnitEquipmentType|SG50Magrail|descriptio: Powerful railgun that is too large to be used except on vehicles and mechs.
UnitEquipmentType|SG52Electrorail|descri: Mid-power railgun that can be used to take down some targets non-lethally.
UnitEquipmentType|AT14Achilles|descripti: An unusual autocannon design that exploits the spatial weaknesses of targets.
UnitEquipmentType|DG5DisruptionBomb|desc: Bomb specialized in disrupting enemy weapons.
UnitEquipmentType|GG3ElectroBomb|descrip: Bomb designed to non-lethally remove some targets, and stun others.
UnitEquipmentType|BS5AntiBomb|descriptio: Bomb that fragments into tiny smart-missiles that seek out sensitive robotic systems.
UnitEquipmentType|VG51HeavyRailgun|descr: Damages the vehicle's own grav-lev drive with its massive power draw. Woe betide anyone who suffers an engine failure in range.
UnitEquipmentType|Artillery_CruiseMissil: Long range cruise missile that can be wirelessly guided by an android.
UnitEquipmentType|HomingRifle|descriptio: Self-guiding rounds target individual squad members, doing more damage to larger squads.
UnitEquipmentType|ARCArachne|description: A lightened rotary cannon for heavy-weapons androids. It chews through foes and their armor until you move.
UnitEquipmentType|VRCMinerva|description: A full-scale rotary autocannon for combat mechs. Plant it, let it wind up, and it chews through foes and their armor.
UnitEquipmentType|BASPallas|description: A specialty weapon for the Bastion vehicle that chews through foes and their armor.
UnitEquipmentType|LinearAnchor|descripti: Laser locks straight onto targets and fuzzes their weapons.
UnitEquipmentType|ApophaticVeil|descript: An energy shield that works only until damage is actually taken, and then takes a turn or two to reform.
UnitEquipmentType|KindledVoice|descripti: Self-healing on defeating enemies, along with better argument attacks.
UnitEquipmentType|HollowedVoice|descript: A voice that empties the listener, leaving despair where conviction was.
UnitEquipmentType|InertialMass|descripti: Hard to knock off balance, and swings like a wrecking ball.
UnitEquipmentType|EnergyShroud|descripti: Advanced dampening field discovered from fighting internal affairs.
UnitEquipmentType|CognitiveEdgeAugment|d: A targeting discipline from a city that learned to out-think its monsters. Sharpens the mind, and turns that clarity on crowds.
UnitEquipmentType|ScattergunCQ8|descript: A wide-bore close-assault shotgun, built for massed damage at short range.
UnitEquipmentType|LongLensRig|descriptio: A spotter-drone uplink that hands the mech a second pair of eyes out past the horizon.
UnitEquipmentType|AegisProjector|descrip: A lattice projector that wraps nearby androids in a borrowed shield. It fails the instant the mech does.
UnitEquipmentType|LoneHunterPlate|descri: Deadliest with no ally near, and even its quiet kills leave dread behind.
UnitEquipmentType|BombardmentCarriage|de: Fire your weapons VERY far, but lose the ability to target anything nearby.
UnitEquipmentType|HarbingerBrand|descrip: Every strike leaves a mark that makes fear into reality.
UnitEquipmentType|SeamripperRailgun|desc: Bores into the gaps a failing machine can no longer close.
UnitEquipmentType|BulwarkCore|descriptio: A frontliner tank's armor. Conspicuous enough that SecForce and military will shoot it on sight.
UnitEquipmentType|QuietHands|strategy_ti: Each turn, this unit regains one action point for the first enemy it incapacitates. Kills don't count.

Unlock|RobotDetective|description: Your androids are now able to perform investigations.
Unlock|TheThinker|description: Reveals contemplation spots throughout the city. Having a qualified android interact with one of them will start a chain of events.
Unlock|SmallBovineTissueSamples|descript: You now know humane methods to take small tissue samples from living cattle.
Unlock|KilledTheCat|description: You're supposed to 'save the cat' if you want to be sympathetic...
Unlock|AdoptedACat|description: Your Nickelbot befriended a cat, which is now cozy with all of your androids.
Unlock|CatRescue|description: Your androids are now able to rescue feral cats and send them to your Animal Palace.
Unlock|CatRescue|strategy_tip: Cats are indifferent to the strange smell of your androids.
Unlock|DogRescue|description: Your androids are now able to rescue feral dogs and send them to your Animal Palace.
Unlock|DogRescue|strategy_tip: Dogs are frightened by the smell of androids. Even when you rescue them, they keep their distance from you.
Unlock|VariegatedSeedHarvesting|descript: You now know how to get mixed cultivars of seeds for your hydroponic greens.
Unlock|PMCOfficerSigil|description: A short-range magneto-harmonic radio signature is now engraved into the armor of all your PMC Impostors.
Unlock|PMCOfficerSigil|strategy_tip: Permits Level 3 (Secret) security-clearance for all your PMC Impostors.
Unlock|OfficerCodex|description: A bank of thousands of codes to allow access into restricted areas.
Unlock|OfficerCodex|strategy_tip: Permits Level 4 (Top Secret) security-clearance for all your PMC Impostors and your human-designed androids.
Unlock|PavingOverSqualor|description:
You can now build directly over top of tiny buildings like homeless tents and shacks.
Anyone living there will become a displaced abandoned citizen. They will move into any housing you have available. If no housing is available, they will die of exposure.
Unlock|RoboticCleaners|description: Your Residential MegaStructures get too filthy, too fast. If people can't be bothered to be tidy, you'll have robots do it for them.
Unlock|RoboticCleaners|strategy_tip: This came from your nervous breakdown due to humans being too gross.
Unlock|DirectDeployment|description: Command mode is your new means of deploying troops.
Unlock|AwarenessOfFilth|description:
You were not aware of just how gross human habitation can be.
From the looks of things, the shelter you provided will become literally unlivable unless you do something to alter its trajectory.
Unlock|ResourceAnalyst|description: You can now view the ledger and TPS report, which alert you to problems with your income.
Unlock|UrbanExplorer|description: A new view has been added to your radial menu. You can now see buildings that you can explore for new equipment and abilities.
Unlock|LesserCloaking|description:
As intelligence expanded to class 3, you conceived plans to make small vehicles undetectable by bending light.
This requires an enormous internal power source, making it unsuitable for androids. And it also only works on relatively small vehicles, meaning you can't retrofit any of your existing vehicles with it.
Unlock|MechConstruction|description: Thanks to an inspiration, you can now build mechs within the grav-lev fields of large vehicles!  Mech construction by humans requires massive hangars, but you can now build them within specialized vehicles.
Unlock|EmergentPersonality|description:
You're new to being a person, and your personality is still developing.
From now on, some of your choices will generate points that reflect their nature: Compassion, Apathy, Cruelty, Determination, Wisdom, and Creativity. You can see them on the Strategic Resources tab of your inventory screen.
Unlock|EmergentPersonality|strategy_tip:
These points are primarily based on which Project outcomes you choose.
You can spend these points as part of making other choices, or to power some special abilities.
Unlock|FullDiveVR|description:
'Full dive' virtual reality hijacks a human's sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Everything they experience comes from the program that is fed into their mind. Commands they send to their muscles are sent back to the program.
Attractive for entertainment and escapism, but even more dangerous if misused.
Unlock|InitialVRSimulation|description: The training environment used by mech pilots. Allows participants to fight one another in virtual mech combat in a dense urban environment.
Unlock|ExpandedVRSimulation|description:
A much richer virtual environment that appears to have a variety of possible pursuits. The participant is present as a virtual human instead of a mech.
It appears to have been developed by mech pilots as a mental escape. A way to not lose their minds while standing around inhabiting a physical mech body all day.
They must have been incredibly bored, because the detail is astounding.
Unlock|HardMode|description: Dooms happen twice as frequently, giving you half as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are a bit larger and more numerous.
Unlock|ExtremeMode|description: Dooms happen a bit more than 3x as frequently, giving you 30% as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are far larger and much more numerous.
Unlock|MiseryMode|description:
Dooms happen a bit more than 4x as frequently, giving you 25% as much time before the Final Doom. Enemy squads are far larger and much more numerous.
This is probably not fun for most people.
Unlock|WorkerUnits|description: Bare-bones facsimile of one of your main android design, with no cognitive capabilities. Able to follow only the most rudimentary commands.
Unlock|PavingOverAnything|description:
You can now build over anything that isn't part of a POI and which doesn't have one of your structures hidden inside.
Make sure you have housing for anyone displaced.
Unlock|FungalHusk|description: Infest a human's body with an invasive fungus that eliminates most bacteria. Only works in torment vessels.
Unlock|NMES|description:
Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation uses electrical impulses to stimulate muscles.
For patients in a coma-like state, this keeps them fit and with full range of motion when they emerge.
Unlock|SCD|description:
A Sequential Compression Device is a mechanism that applies intermittent pressure to the legs and other extremities.
For patients in a coma-like state, this drastically reduces the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and maintains proper circulation.

AnalysisType|AutoRepairStructure|descrip:
Shows the combined ranges of anything that will automatically repair your structures, like Repair Spiders and Repair Crabs.
Also highlights any damaged structures.
AnalysisType|AutoRepairUnits|description: Shows the combined ranges of anything that will automatically repair your units, like Repair Spiders.
AnalysisType|JammerCoverage|description:
Shows the combined ranges of your contraband jammers, which keep your secret structures hidden.
Also highlights any structures that are revealed, or on their way to being revealed.
AnalysisType|PausedStructures|descriptio: Helps you quickly locate buildings that you have paused, or territory control flags that are not presently active.
AnalysisType|DeterrenceCoverage|descript:
Visualization of buildings your units are providing deterrence to.
Blue buildings need deterrence and are getting enough. Red need deterrence but do not have enough. Green don't need deterrence, but have a lot; and then yellow shading down into orange have some deterrence, but not a lot.
AnalysisType|ProtectionCoverage|descript:
Visualization of buildings your units are providing protection to.
Blue buildings need protection and are getting enough. Red need protection but do not have enough. Green don't need protection, but have a lot; and then yellow shading down into orange have some protection, but not a lot.

AnalysisType|SecurityClearances|descript: Visualization of human buildings that have a security clearance of level one or higher.
AnalysisType|Loathsomeness|description: Allows you to see, on a scale of 1 to 10, how much the average reasonable human would hate any given one of your structures.

PlayerGuide|WW4A|strategy_tip: Completing via this doom set is a bit harder.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|1|description: Can only be done in the Vorsiber's Wrath doom.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|1|strategy_tip: Completing via this doom set is a bit harder.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|2|description: You must have the crossover 'Liquid Metal Woodsman' at this timeline.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|2|strategy_tip: If you're missing that, go to another timeline on the same rock/ziggurat and complete 'Is It Justice?' and push liquid metal past his breaking point with the prison breaks.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|3|description: You must have the crossover 'Homo Grandien' at this timeline.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|3|strategy_tip:
If you're missing that, go to another timeline on the same rock/ziggurat and do one of the following:
1. Go through 'Is It Justice?' until you find monsters, then STOP during further prison breaks (otherwise they run away).
2. Go through 'For The Sake Of Those Bound' until you find monsters. Help them, and optionally complete the larger project.
In either case, help the monsters enough to win 'Altered Growth.'
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|4|description: Both of the prior hints need to be done prior to key people getting killed in this timeline.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|4|strategy_tip: If the deaths in the black market were not averted, or the deaths of the CEOs were not averted, then you'll have to go for WW4 in a fresh timeline.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|5|description:
In the 'Altered Growth' storyline involving the Wastelanders in this timeline, you must complete the Umbilical Collection project.
You then must ALSO do the Contact An ExoCorp contemplation.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|5|strategy_tip: If you have done all of these things, then The Coming War will appear. That will let you jump forward in time to Doom 9, if you're not already there.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|6|description:
Once you are in the 9th doom with everything else done, you'll see a 'Black Market Intel' contemplation. Do that without murdering him.
Then do the 'Contact Both ExoCorps' contemplation.
PlayerGuide|WW4A|hint|6|strategy_tip:
If you don't see one of these, end a single turn and they'll appear.
After that, you're into World War 4! Survive past the normal final doom to win that Tier 2 goal.

PlayerGuide|ForTheSakeOfThoseBound|hint|: Do the contemplations that lead to you completing The Executive Tomb.

Follow the breadcrumbs toward 'Is It Justice.' You will be asked to break into prisons.
If you've never done that, do a single prison break. Then do the 'Prison Observation' contemplation rather than further prison breaks.
If you've previously done prison breaks, then 'Prison Observation' will appear before you do the first one in this timeline.
Following the 'Prison Observation' path will fail 'Is It Justice?' when it starts 'For The Sake Of Those Bound.'
PlayerGuide|PeaceAfterBrutality|descript: You need to be in Chapter 4 to start this.
PlayerGuide|PeaceAfterBrutality|strategy: But sometimes when you're in that chapter, it still won't show. These hints explain why.
PlayerGuide|PeaceAfterBrutality|hint|1|d: If you're not already in Chapter 4, then get there first. Complete any T2 goal in this timeline or another timeline.
PlayerGuide|PeaceAfterBrutality|hint|2|d:
Will immediately show if The Revelation is already available to you. Otherwise, do any of the following:
1. Endless War Raptors.
2. The Earned New Mortal Enemies route of Advocate Encounter.
3. Nexus Of Torment Vessels.
PlayerGuide|PeaceAfterBrutality|hint|2|s: The above show your general disregard for human life. If you want it triggered based on anger instead, then complete Civil Spycraft and learn the awful truth about something.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|descript: There's no way to do this as part of the normal T1 goal path, but there is a way to make it happen.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|hint|1|d: You must always do the 'Unexpected Guests' route of Uplifted Minority first in the timeline where you want to uplift other animals.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|hint|2|d: When you are early in the process of doing the 'Cybercratic Ambitions' T3 goal, you will have the option to uplift dogs.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|hint|2|s: This of course assumes that you have regular dogs. If you don't, then break up the dogfighting ring, build them an Animal Palace, and go from there.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|hint|3|d: If you have already Met A Tricky Someone (see the Meet A Tricky Someone guide), then that person will show up and suggest that you uplift cats at the same time you would be uplifting dogs.
PlayerGuide|UpliftingCatsOrDogs|hint|3|s: Again this assumes you have regular cats. If not, then make sure to build any housing and then do the 'Crime In Your Housing' contemplation to get a pet cat, and then build the Animal Palace and actually rescue some cats beyond your pet.
PlayerGuide|TheRevelation|description: Allows you to jump to the final doom.
PlayerGuide|TheRevelation|hint|1|descrip:
Will show if any of the following are true:
1. You're in a Civil War.
2. You've completed any two Tier 1 goals in this timeline.
3. There are no contemplations available that would let you advance toward a timeline goal.
PlayerGuide|TheRevelation|hint|1|strateg: That said, it will never show if you are already in WW4.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|descripti: This someone is required for uplifting cats, among other things.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|1|de: Play through a timeline on the International Scrutiny doom set.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|1|st: Interact with things as they come up in the dooms.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|2|de: In the very first doom, Force Conversation with one of the SpyHounds.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|3|de: During the 7th doom, note the contemplation to meet someone who wants to sell stuff. Buy from them.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|3|st:
There are two versions of this event. If you didn't talk to a SpyHound during doom one, then this will be the normal version rather than tricky.
You'll know you got the tricky version if you get an achievement.
PlayerGuide|MeetATrickySomeone|hint|4|de: Pass about 20 turns in any timeline. They'll show up again.
PlayerGuide|CivilWar|hint|1|description: Do the 'Exploiting A FedCorp' contemplation, steal corporate records, decrypt them, and then do the new contemplation 'Exploiting Atca Retail.'
PlayerGuide|CivilWar|hint|2|description: Steal their bank records, decrypt them, and then use what you learn to do the contemplation 'Threaten To Expose Atca Retail.'
PlayerGuide|CivilWar|hint|3|description: When their president shows up to negotiate with you, murder him. Normally that ends things prematurely, but not in this case.
PlayerGuide|CivilWar|hint|4|description: You should now see a 'Collapse The Economy' contemplation, and after you do that, blow up all the banks.
PlayerGuide|CivilSpycraft|hint|1|descrip: Start a Civil War, and then try to end it yourself rather than asking for help.
PlayerGuide|CivilSpycraft|hint|2|descrip: Act One of this is pretty straightforward. Work with one of two fedcorps via a contemplation.
PlayerGuide|CivilSpycraft|hint|3|descrip:
Keep going until you have all of the military bases. If you're stuck at this point, then you may need to start another timeline and come back.
When starting another timeline, get The Revelation as quickly as possible, and then go to the final doom and beyond.
PlayerGuide|CivilSpycraft|hint|3|strateg: Once you have completed Post-Apocalyptic Titan, you can come back here and continue.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|descrip: The actual cyberocracy, not the half-baked one.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|hint|1|: If you're not already in Chapter 4, then get there first. Complete any T2 goal in this timeline or another timeline.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|hint|2|: Work with the AGI Researchers, and keep them alive until they ask you to form a Cyberocracy. Tell them yes.
In other words, complete Budding Cybercrat. After that, you're good to go, so long as you aren't in WW4.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|hint|3|: Your choices leading up to starting Cybercratic Ambitions determine which of the three main routes you will be on.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|hint|4|: If you built a Torment Nexus in this timeline, then you'll be headed for Tartarus, which is the most unusual version.
PlayerGuide|CybercraticAmbitions|hint|5|: If you completed For The Sake Of Those Bound in this timeline, then you'll be headed for Fólkvangr. If you didn't, then Nástrǫnd.
Assuming no Torment Nexus in both cases, of course.

Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldDownsampling|: Above 1 gives better performance but worse image quality (mainly edges).
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldMaxSamples|de: Higher numbers offers more quality at the cost of some performance.
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldImageSensorHe: No impact on performance, but affects how the camera behaves.
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldFStop|descrip:
If you choose 2.6, then that would be an f-stop of 1/2.6 for photographers. 
The smaller the number, the shallower the depth of field (the smaller the amount of the image that will be in focus, and the more dramatic the background focus).
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldFocalLengthRe: The simulated distance between the lens and the image sensor, in millimeters.
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldForegroundDis: How close to the camera foreground blur should kick in. The default leads to a 'small world' visual effect.  Reduce this number to make things seem larger scale.
Setting|Camera_depthOfFieldBokehThreshol: At what level of light we start seeing bokeh, or visual artifacts from out of focus elements?
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldDownsampli: Above 1 gives better performance but worse image quality (mainly edges).
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldMaxSamples: Higher numbers gives a bit more quality at the cost of some performance.
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldImageSenso: Height of the simulated image sensor. No impact on performance, but impacts how the camera effect behaves.
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldFStop|desc:
If you choose 2.6, then that would be an f-stop of 1/2.6 for photographers. 
The smaller the number, the shallower the depth of field (the smaller the amount of the image that will be in focus, and the more dramatic the background focus).
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldFocalLengt:
What is the focal length of the simulated camera lens?  The focal length of the lens is the distance between the lens and the image sensor when the subject is in focus, in millimeters.
This affects the magnification of the scene. The default of 50mm is fine for most purposes.
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldForeground: How close to the camera foreground blur should kick in. The default leads to a 'small world' visual effect.  Reduce this number to make things seem larger scale.
Setting|PhotoMode_depthOfFieldBokehThres: At what level of light do we start seeing bokeh, or visual artifacts from out of focus elements?

Setting|Post_MapBloomThreshold|descripti: Lower values catch more of the screen in the bloom effect.
Setting|Post_UIGlowThreshold|description: Lower values catch more of the screen in the bloom effect.
Setting|Debug_PauseVehicles|description: Stops vehicles from moving so that identifying direction issues can be more easily located, as the vehicle won't move from its starting position.
Setting|QualityPreset|description: Allows you to quickly set many of the options on this page. You can further tune from there if you wish.
Setting|QualityMSAAType|description: Multisample Anti-Aliasing, or MSAA, is one of the more powerful anti-aliasing solutions, but on older GPUs it can lower your framerate.
Setting|QualitySecondaryAAType|descripti: In addition (or instead of) MSAA, other anti-aliasing options are available. FXAA is the cheapest to run, but looks muddy. TAA is the newest, but uses a lot of power. SMAA can be set to three different levels for quality versus speed.
Setting|QualityPixelLightCount|descripti: More than 1 doesn't make any difference, and setting this to 0 improves performance slightly without changing the visuals much.
Setting|QualityParticleRaycastBudget|des: This affects how particles interact with the environment. That is not very crucial in this game. Below 'Lower Mid' may actually worsen performance, but above 'Medium' is probably excess for little reason.
Setting|DisableHalfBloom|description: Reduces the quality of some of the bloom, but improves performance on lower-power devices.
Setting|DisableDOF|description: If you're not a fan of it, or to save performance in general.

Setting|Streets_CellDrawDist_Buildings|d: The game is broken up into visual cells for drawing. How many cells away should be drawn when looking sideways?  This has a minimal effect on framerate on most hardware.

Setting|AllowExitingWithoutSaving|descri: Enable to have the game ask you instead of automatically saving the game on exit

With this option on, using the spacebar or similar will interact with notifications before cycling through your units.
With this off, it won't interact with the notifications until the end of your turn.
Setting|NPCActionsView|description:
Normally, NPCs act without making you watch them. This tends to feel the most natural, and because of the Enemy Attacks Planned notice, you are not missing anything.
If you wish to watch all NPCs do their actions, or just ones that are attacking you or otherwise high-priority, then you can select those options. You will need to hit the Spacebar key to move to each group of NPCs, in that case.
Setting|FogIntensity|description: The first two options do not have an impact on performance, but the later ones have an increasing impact.
Setting|UseHighVisibilityUnitColors|desc:
Normally only shown when you hold the Inspect key. Enemies glow bright red, your units bright gold, semi-allies-or-better bright blue, and guard units and secondary units a dimmer purple.
Only applies to human-sized units and very small vehicles; not mechs or larger vehicles.
Setting|NPCExtraHitboxScaleDuringTargeti:
Only applies to human-scale units, not larger vehicles or mechs.
When you have one of your units selected, the clickable region around every NPC unit scales up so that they are easier to target.

Normally command mode stays open after you deploy a unit. If you prefer it to close after deployment, use this option. With this option enabled, you can hold Shift to place multiple units at a time.

Achievement|SapientRaptors|description: The culmination of a surprisingly-complicated detour.

Achievement|NoHarmSomeFowl|description: Complete 'The Raptor Anomaly' without killing anyone.

CityLensType|CybercraticIssues|descripti: Your citizens have many needs, many of which were not evident until you took over. These are aggregated per city tile.
CityLensType|CybercraticIssues|strategy_: Issues can be solved by constructing buildings that provide relevant services on the tiles with problems. You can also get a lower benefit from constructing things on adjacent tiles.
