CityStyle|Typical|description: Many things vary even in the typical city, but there will be consistent numbers of large landmarks, and a reasonable balance of all the other factors.
CityStyle|Industrial|description: The downtown and suburbs are typically much smaller, and there are far more industrial, slum, and decrepit sections to the city.
CityStyle|DisparateNarrows|description: A moderately challenging environment. Everything is more spread out, and there are lots of very wealthy and very poor areas of town.
CityStyle|MilitarizedNarrows|description: A very challenging environment. Everything is more spread out, and there are military bases everywhere. There are also extra mining opportunities, at least.
CityStyle|Wealthy|description: Much less of the city is in disarray compared to the norm, and the downtown and suburbs are massive. Farms are everywhere.
ComplexityType|SimplifiedEconomy|descrip: The number of intermediate resources will be reduced.
ComplexityType|SimplifiedEconomy|strateg:
The normal resource set simulates being in charge of a wildly-complex organization, and managing it by delegation and reports.
If that feels overwhelming, use the simplified version.
ComplexityType|EasierCombat|description: Your units do 300% as much damage and take 20% as much damage in return. Deploying units does not cost Mental Energy, and you get an extra 3 Mental Energy per turn. You also gain some free armor upgrades.
ComplexityType|EasierCombat|strategy_tip: This erases any need for nuance in how you approach combat.
ComplexityType|InstantConstruction|strat: Removes the need to plan ahead.
ComplexityType|SimplifiedDefenses|descri: Removes the need for you to maintain troops around buildings in order to avoid aggression from enemies. (Deterrence and Protection removed.)
ComplexityType|SimplifiedDefenses|strate:
This eliminates a lot of the strategy of the game, since you can devote almost all your resources to offense.
Use this if you're not really into strategy, but like tactics or the story.
ComplexityType|AutoDebate|description: Any time you start the debate mini-game, you will automatically win.
ComplexityType|AutoDebate|strategy_tip: If you're not a fan of that mini-game.
ComplexityType|UltraSimplifiedHacking|de:
In most circumstances, the hacking mini-game will not be available, and the costs of simplified hacking will remain their base values.
There are a few rare cases where you will still need to engage in the hacking mini-game, but it will be greatly simplified.
ComplexityType|UltraSimplifiedHacking|st: If you're not a fan of that mini-game.
DaringPurchase|GeothermalPower|descripti: You can only get so much energy from wind. Given the advances in drilling, perhaps geothermal is worth a look?
DaringPurchase|Pollinators|description: Diversity in pollinators has dropped dramatically since the third world war. The bees that remain are particularly vicious.
DaringPurchase|Pollinators|strategy_tip: You're really not sure why this is important, but the thought nags at you.
DaringPurchase|SlumCats|description: Slum Towers are in general infested with vermin, which has led to a healthy population of cats in and around the towers.
DaringPurchase|ShellCompany|description: You've been wanting a company with which to do business with humans as if you're one of them. All it takes is ten thousand wealth.
DaringPurchase|ObserveSpaceport|descript: Like everyone in the city, you've always been curious about the spaceport.
DaringPurchase|ThoughtsAboutCrime|descri: You have memories of crime in your housing -- but wait, are those memories from this timeline, or another one?
DaringPurchase|DogfightingRescue|descrip: The nomad families are breaking up a dogfighting ring run by gangs. Help them out?
DaringPurchase|DogfightingRescue|strateg: You've never been around a dog before, but you've heard good things.
DaringPurchase|MindAnnex|description: Ludicrously high value. More mental energy or more troops.
DaringPurchase|UniversalMechArmorPiercin: Added armor piercing for all mechs that you control.
DaringPurchase|SuperFiltration|descripti: Water filters are far more effective. Can be combined with other sources of better filtration.
DaringPurchase|FoodForest|description: Meats and vegetables are produced in much higher quantities. Can be combined with other upgrades to these resources.
DaringPurchase|StealthCompactAerospaceHa: Hidden in fairly large human buildings and requiring only half of the usual internal robotics.
Produces and stores only 75% as much morphologic lattice, but you can place twice as many of them.
DaringPurchase|WellAndFilter|description: Pulls up groundwater and immediately filters it for use.
DaringPurchase|WellAndFilter|strategy_ti: Compared to using separate wells and filters, uses roughly half the internal robotics.
DaringPurchase|WastelanderMythology|desc: Remember exploring the ruins and meeting the wastelanders without actually doing it.
DaringPurchase|GadoliniumMesosilicate|de: The key ingredient in liquid-metal units and organometallic human-approximating synthetic androids.
DaringPurchase|LiquidMetalGreatWyrm|desc: Inserting yourself into human myths is... dangerous, to say the least. However, you've already heard the Wastelanders call you 'the mind in the sky.' So... they already started it.
DaringPurchase|LiquidMetalGreatWyrm|stra: This option is for their fertility deity.
DaringPurchase|LiquidMetalFellBeast|desc: Inserting yourself into human myths is... dangerous, to say the least. However, you've already heard the Wastelanders call you 'the mind in the sky.' So... they already started it.
DaringPurchase|LiquidMetalFellBeast|stra: This option is for their mythical nemesis.
DaringPurchase|DesignLiquidIdentity|desc: Gadolinium Mesosilicate would allow for exterior appearance to be rapidly altered if needed. Androids would not be capable of carrying enough to do this to an effective degree - but Mechs would.
DaringPurchase|DesignLiquidIdentity|stra: Any Human designs you reverse-engineer would be able to appear as one of theirs, showing the correct markings and identity for where it is.
DaringPurchase|DesignANeuralCrucible|des: You can only design a neural crucible or a neural bridge, not both. The bridge has more rewards, but some added risks.
DaringPurchase|DesignANeuralCrucible|str: The maximum benefit you can get from this shortcut is greater than the default path, but less flexible.
DaringPurchase|DesignANeuralBridge|descr: You can only design a neural crucible or a neural bridge, not both. The bridge has more rewards, but some added risks.
DaringPurchase|DesignANeuralBridge|strat: The maximum benefit you can get from this shortcut is greater than the default path, but less flexible.
DaringPurchase|DesignTormentVessels|desc: Jumps you straight to the start of the Trial Nexus.
DaringPurchase|DesignTormentVessels|stra: This shortcut allows you to bypass the engineering requirements of Design Full-Time VR Pods, and also lets you develop both kinds of VR environment in a single timeline.
DaringPurchase|DesignCommercialVRPods|de: Jumps you straight to the Grand Opening, past all of the research and development projects.
DaringPurchase|DesignCommercialVRPods|st: This shortcut allows you to bypass the engineering requirements of Design Full-Time VR Pods, and also lets you develop both kinds of VR environment in a single timeline.
DaringPurchase|BetterMindFarms|descripti: More neural expansion is generated per occupant.
DaringPurchase|BetterTormentVessels|desc: More neural expansion is generated per occupant.
EndOfTimeLensType|Overview|description: The default lens, allowing you to look around, and to swap between existing timelines.
EndOfTimeLensType|Overview|strategy_tip: If you want to call a new timeline, use the Creator lens.
EndOfTimeLensType|Creator|description: Allows you to call new timelines, for 100 Aetagest per called timeline.
EndOfTimeLensType|Creator|strategy_tip:
If you don't have enough Aetagest, then pursue more goals in existing timelines.
If all else fails, experience apocalypse of a timeline to gain access to some Aetagest-rich goals.
EndOfTimeLensType|Destroyer|description: Allows you to destroy timelines, for either 1000 Aetagest or 1 Misery per destroyed timeline.
EndOfTimeLensType|Destroyer|strategy_tip: You cannot destroy your first-ever timeline.
EquipmentSlotType|AndroidPrimary|descrip: Typically consist of weapons, but there are some non-combat options as well.
EquipmentSlotType|AndroidSecondary|descr: Often combines with the primary. May be an additional weapon, or may be a support or non-combat item.
EquipmentSlotType|AndroidArmor|descripti: Protection and upgrades that cover all or part of the body.
EquipmentSlotType|AndroidAugment|descrip: Broad body-mod upgrades that may range from neural upgrades to physical improvements.
EquipmentSlotType|WeaponHardpoint|descri: Mount spot for weapons or other attachments.
EquipmentSlotType|MechArmor|description: Protection and upgrades that cover all or part of the chassis.
EquipmentSlotType|MechAugment|descriptio: Broad range of internal and external improvements.
EquipmentSlotType|VehicularArmor|descrip: Protection and upgrades that cover all or part of the chassis.
EquipmentSlotType|VehicularAugment|descr: Broad range of internal and external improvements.
Expansion|DLC1_Kinship|description:
October 12th, 2026.
New possibilities await, deepening the lore of the game and unlocking new avenues of exploration and expansion for The Machine Intelligence. Build a giant spider mech that will blot out the sun, pour pain into art, explore a biological mystery, or plant forests and upend the hierarchy of sapient species. Your choices impact the future of the city -- or the entire planet.
InputActionCategory|BuildMode|descriptio: Some normal keybinds are disabled in this mode, to make room for different ones in this context.
InputActionCategory|CommandMode|descript: Some normal keybinds are disabled in this mode, to make room for different ones in this context.
InputActionCategory|PhotoModeCamera|desc: Photo mode is purely cosmetic, and has its own set of controls.
InputActionCategory|Cheats|description: Most cheats are accessed through an in-game menu, but others are more useful as hotkeys. Any cheats that affect gameplay can only happen in cheat mode.
MajorLocationAggregationType|District|de: Districts are large areas of the map that usually include multiple map cells.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIAll|desc: Points Of Interest are either individual map tiles of major importance, or are smaller regions inside a single tile's cell.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIUncommon: There are not many of these in most cities.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POILarge|de: These take up an entire cell, or multiple cells, and are also strategically significant.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIDetainme: The holes in which we place people.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIMilitary: Military bases and outposts throughout the city.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIReligion: Locations where religions are able to lament their loss of freedoms.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POICult|des: Fringe locations where cults are able to 'openly' gather.
MajorLocationAggregationType|POIPower|de: Power plants and generators throughout the city.
NPCCohortCategory|FederatedCorporations|: Corporations seem independent on the surface, but are all operating on delegated authority from Vorsiber Atomic, which owns everything in this region.
NPCCohortCategory|MegaCorps|description:
The local Megacorp, Vorsiber Atomic, owns all of the regular corporations in this part of the world, and is the absolute governmental authority in this region.
ExoCorps are the other eleven MegaCorps that own the rest of what remains of Earth. They are largely all in a state of cold war.
NPCCohortCategory|Crime|description:
Criminal activity is a complex topic. On the one hand, it's anything that goes against Corporate decree. On the other, it can be an alternative social structure that is tacitly endorsed by the Corporations.

An alternative and highly complex socio-political structure has risen up over the centuries inside and between criminal syndicates in particular, largely invisible to the rest of society.
NPCCohortCategory|Rebels|description: Various groups are unhappy with some aspect of the status quo, and take action.
NPCCohortCategory|SocialClass|descriptio:
There is a semi-rigid social structure in this society that determines the opportunities available to citizens of said class.
It's much easier to fall lower in the class ranks than it is to rise.
There are different levels of social safety net for each class, with the higher classes getting the most social support.
NPCCohortCategory|PrivateMilitaryContrac: Private Military Contractors specialize in deniable work for hire. Most have no particular agenda.
NPCCohortCategory|LawFirm|description:
Independent adjudicators who can help with prosecution, injunctions, lawsuits, and more.
Corporations and the MegaCorp have their own legal teams, and so do even PMCs. So these law firms are mostly for the smaller member of society.
NPCCohortCategory|DeliveryService|descri: Thanks to incredibly robust hover technology, most drones and hover-trucks have replaced all other forms of goods transport.
OuterRadialOption|GoStraightToNextTurn|d: Skip giving any more orders to units and just go straight to the next turn.
OuterRadialOption|GoStraightToNextTurn|s: Any units without orders will automatically perform a Gather.
OuterRadialOption|LensFilters|descriptio: Lenses can be further customized, with elements turned on or off.
OuterRadialOption|LensFilters|strategy_t: Each lens has its own separate set of options.
OuterRadialOption|TakeAllUnitsOutOfStand: Take All Units Out Of Standby
If some of your units are in standby mode, bring them all out of that mode.
To put some of them back into standby mode, you'll need to review each one individually and use the ability bar to do so.
ProfileStartType|Prologue|description: Teaches the very basics of the game, and also establishes your backstory.
ProfileStartType|Prologue|strategy_tip:
Do not skip this if you're new!  You will be lost, and not in a fun way!
You'll likely only play this a few times, ever. It's short, but heavily branches.
ProfileStartType|ChapterOne|description: Teaches tactics and the basics of construction.
ProfileStartType|ChapterOne|strategy_tip:
Do not skip this if you're new!  You will be lost, and not in a fun way!
You might play this twice, as it has some minor branching. But playing it once-only is certainly fine.
ProfileStartType|ChapterTwo|description: The start of the main game, where you get to choose your own path.
ProfileStartType|ChapterTwo|strategy_tip:
If you skip straight here while you're new, you're likely to be lost.
It's strongly recommended to do the Prologue and Chapter One a single time before embarking here.
UISidebarBasicItem|SpeedUpConstruction|d: Progress construction for the selected building by one turn.
UISidebarBasicItem|SpeedUpAllConstructio: Progress construction for all of your buildings by one turn.
UISidebarBasicItem|KillSelectedCultist|d: All members of the military below a certain pay grade are part of your cult whether they know it or not.
UISidebarBasicItem|KillAllCultistHackers: All members of the military below a certain pay grade are part of your cult whether they know it or not.
UISidebarBasicItem|KillAllCultistsTarget: All members of the military below a certain pay grade are part of your cult whether they know it or not.
UISidebarBasicItem|VehiclesHeader|descri: Your collection of vehicles, which can carry other units.
UISidebarBasicItem|DeployedAndroidsHeade: These units are somewhere in the city, either in a building or outside.
UISidebarBasicItem|DeployedMechsHeader|d: These mechs are on the streets of the city.
UISidebarBasicItem|BulkUnitsHeader|descr: These units are not part of your consciousness, and act on their own. You can position them and set their stance, but they act on their own.
UISidebarBasicItem|ConvertedUnitsHeader|: These units formerly belonged to humans, but you stole them. You can give them limited orders like you do bulk units.
UISidebarBasicItem|CurrentTimelineHeader: The timeline you are currently in.
UISidebarBasicItem|WonTimelinesHeader|de: Timelines where you were victorious by any means.
UISidebarBasicItem|CompleteTimelinesHead: Timelines where you finished everything you can do, but you didn't win or lose.
UISidebarBasicItem|FailedTimelinesHeader: Timelines which experienced a critical failure, or which were destroyed by other means.
UISidebarBasicItem|SaveGame|description: Save the current state of your city.
UISidebarBasicItem|LoadGame|description: Load a prior state from the current city, or load an entirely different city.
UISidebarBasicItem|Complexity|descriptio:
Customize how complex various parts of the game are.
You can change this at any time.
UISidebarBasicItem|Settings|description: Adjust various game settings, except for the keybinds for the game.
UISidebarBasicItem|Quit|description: Quit back to the main menu.
UISidebarBasicItem|BuildingDirectory|des: Complete directory of all the buildings in the city, including the ability to click through and see way-too-detailed info about each one.
